### Example（取自子主题 Introduction to firmware commands › Firmware view）

As the following example shows, the `VECD?` query returns vector data from the sequencer memory in the range between 0 and 8, for the S0_1 pin.

Add the $ prefix to the query command to retrieve the binary data in a readable format.

 !`Executing the firmware command in the Firmware view`（raw: `../../../../raw/111040.png`）

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APDV -  APpenD Vectors）

```
APDV {cmd_No}, {vect_length}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APDV -  APpenD Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

A number that identifies the command within the sequencer area of the port to which the label belongs. Enter the command number of a GENV or RPTV instruction within the selected label.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The number of vectors you wish to append. Enter an integer in the range 0 to the maximum vector length.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APDV -  APpenD Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,520,,,(@)
< ...
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> APDV 2,25
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,34,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,544,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example appends 25 vectors to the end of the sequencer construct with the command number 2. Note the change of the start address in command line 4.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APRM -  Activate PRiMary sets）

```
APRM {mode}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APRM -  Activate PRiMary sets）

| mode  | Selects the activation mode: |
 | FRC  | Forced activation. Primary sets are always activated. |
 | CNL  | Conditional activation, depends on previous activation performed by APRM or by any of the commands in the second list above. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APRM -  Activate PRiMary sets）

```
APRM CNL
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

```
APTS {"label"}, {type}, {base_wf_set|"wavetable"|specset_id|"multiport_spec"} [,(port)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

|

label

 |

Defines the name of the new label. Enter an alphanumeric string in double quotes containing 1 to 128 characters.

 |
 |

type

 |

The label type. It has the following options:

 |
 |

MAIN

 |

The MAIN program. You can make calls to both types of subroutine (SJMP and SVEC), execute commands and sequencer instructions, generate vectors and use SSRC and SRCV instructions.

 |
 |

SVEC

 |

Vector subroutine. A subroutine where you can execute commands and sequencer instructions and generate vectors. You can nest SVEC subroutines up to 7 levels deep.

 |
 |

DSRC

 |

The digital source label. A type of label used only by SSRC and SRCV (see `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）). A DSRC label is not executable. The contents of the DSRC label are determined by the DVCU command. See `DVCU, DVCU? - (Define Vector variable Configuration Usage)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.96_DVCU__DVCU__-__Define_Vector_variable_Configuration_Usage.md`）

 |
 |

base_wf_set

 |

Defines a base waveform set. Enter an integer in the range of 1 to the number of used waveform sets as defined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

wavetable

 |

The name of the base wavetable. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *` equation_set_no `+ ` specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_

spec

 |

In a multiport setup, you can also specify the name of a multiport specification.

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter fulfills two functions. It primarily determines the port with which the label is to be associated. If you do not specify a port, the label is associated with the default port @.

If you have entered a multiport specification as the third parameter, the parameter also serves to identify uniquely the base wavetable for the label.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

```
> APTS "test_2",MAIN,"gross_func_wtb"
> SQLB? ALL,ALL,(@)
< SQLB "test_1",MAIN,0,3,"gross_func_wtb"
< SQLB "test_2",MAIN,4,6,"gross_func_wtb"
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,12,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,520,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
```

This example appends a label to the sequencer area of the default port @. The label has the name `test_2`, is of type MAIN and is configured with the base wavetable `gross_func_wtb`. The following two queries display the result of the call. The STVA instruction of the new label points to the actual end of the vector areas.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

```
APTS "NEW",MAIN,"spec_port_1_port_2",(port_1)
```

This example appends the label `NEW` to the sequencer area of port `port_1`. The base wavetable is identified uniquely by specifying the multi-port specification `spec_port_1_port_2` and the port `port_1`, which belongs to `spec_port_1_port_2`.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ASWE  ASWE  -  Auto SWing Enable）

|

waveform_set

 |

Specifies the number of a waveform set for non-equation based testing. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, ALL for all waveform sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Specifies a spec set ID for equation based testing. The specset_id is derived as follows:

`100 *` equation_set_no `+ ` specset_no

 |
 |

enable_status

 |

Enter ON to switch automatic swing modification on. Enter OFF to switch automatic swing modification off.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ASWE  ASWE  -  Auto SWing Enable）

```
ASWE 1,ON
```

This example enables the automatic swing adjustment for waveform set 1.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ASWM  ASWM  -  Auto SWing Mode）

|

command

 |

This parameter is used to set the specified mode:

 |
 |

SET

 |

Sets the mode specified regardless of the previous mode.

 |
 |

MIN

 |

Sets the 'minimum' mode of either the mode specified or the previous mode. Minimum refers to minimum time consumption.

The following order applies:

FREEZE, SEARCH, AUTO. For example, SEARCH is the minimum mode of the two modes SEARCH and AUTO.

 |
 |

MAX

 |

Sets the 'maximum' mode of either the mode specified or the previous mode. Maximum refers to maximum time consumption.

The following order applies:

AUTO, SEARCH, FREEZE. For example, SEARCH is the maximum mode of the two modes SEARCH and FREEZE.

 |
 |

mode

 |

The mode can take one of the following values:

 |
 |

AUTO

 |

Automatic level swing adjustment is done for all waveform sets. Any change of waveforms or levels triggers an automatic swing adjustment.

 |
 |

FREEZE

 |

No swing adjustment is performed. The actual swing adjustment settings are used. As soon as primary sets change, the mode is switched back to AUTO.

 |
 |

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ASWM  ASWM  -  Auto SWing Mode）

```
ASWM SET,AUTO
```

This example sets the swing adjustment mode AUTO.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BCMD  BCMD  - Binding CoMmanD）

|

InstanceName

 |

User-defined unique name to identify what type of binding instance is being controlled. It is a string without a ".".

 |
 |

Set

Reset

Action

 |

Set is the function used to assign values to the runtime properties of an object.

Reset is the function used to restore the runtime properties of the resource, which is the current focus of the binding, to their initial values.

Action is the function used to drive the hardware associated with a binding instance.

 |
 |

parameter

 |

This is a case-sensitive, predefined keyword. The available types are Configuration settings and Initial Runtime settings.

Configuration: Configurations used to define the resource.

Initial Runtime: Initial Runtime settings are the default values the binding should be set to at the start of a DUT test. These values can be changed at runtime with the BCMD command.

 |
 |

value

 |

This can be a list of elements separated by a space or spaces, or a predefined function. All functions must be placed in quotes.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BCMT  BCMT  -  Binary CoMmenT）

```
> BCMT?
< BCMT 0,49,#9000000078&!This is the first vector
  of test_2&0This is the first vector of test_3
```

This call of BCMT? displays the comments of the default port. The `&` character (with the decimal ASCII value 38) indicates the (identical) length of the two comments. The first comment is at vector 33 (decimal ASCII value of the ! character), the second at vector 48 (decimal ASCII value of the 0 character).

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BLUP -  BLock UP to date）

|

name

 |

The name of a label.

 |
 |

type

 |

The only allowed option is:

 |
 |

 |

LBL

 |

This comprises labels of types MAIN, BRST, SVEC, and MPBU.

 |
 |

state

 |

This parameter defines the status and can be one of the following:

 |
 |

 |

UPTD

 |

Label is up to date.

 |
 |

 |

CHNG

 |

Label was changed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BLUP -  BLock UP to date）

```
BLUP "test",LBL,UPDT,
```

This example sets the state of label `test` to up to date.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BSVE -  Bulk Set Value Evaluation）

```
BSVE {spec_value_set_no}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BSVE -  Bulk Set Value Evaluation）

|

spec_value_set_no

 |

Number of a spec value set.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BSVE -  Bulk Set Value Evaluation）

```
> BSVE 11
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BSVR  BSVR   Bulk Set Value at Runtime）

|

spec_value_set_no

 |

Number of a spec value set. The set must have been defined with DSVS.

 |
 |

number

 |

Variable number in a given range. One of two possible options for the second, optional parameter.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

The name of a spec (base) variable. The variable must have been declared in the equation set of the specification to which the spec value set belongs. Note however that this is not checked by BSVR, but only by BSVE.

 |
 |

spec_name`@`port_name

 |

If the spec value set is associated with a multi-port timing specification, and the variable is declared in the equation sets of several ports, you can restrict the value change to one port by adding the port name. Note that this has a bearing on the scope of the variable (see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）).

 |
 |

value

 |

The new value of the variable.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BSVR  BSVR   Bulk Set Value at Runtime）

```
> DSVS 11, "per", TIM,1,1
> BSVR 11,"per1",30
> BSVR 11,"per2",60
> BSVR? 11
< BSVR 11,"per1",30
< BSVR 11,"per2",60
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BWDF  BWDF  -  Break Waveform DeFinition）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter ALL for all waveform sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *` equation_set_no `+ ` specset_no

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

a1..a6

 |

Edge action. The actions you can define are:

 |
 |

N

 |

no action

 |
 |

F0N

 |

drive 0, no tri-state action

 |
 |

F1N

 |

drive 1, no tri-state action

 |
 |

FN0

 |

no drive action, tri-state off

 |
 |

FNZ

 |

no drive action, tri-state on

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which break waveform definitions are to be made or read back. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured input and IO pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BWDF  BWDF  -  Break Waveform DeFinition）

```
BWDF 1,N,N,N,F1N,F0N,N,(D0,D1,D2,D3)
```

This example defines a pulse for waveform set 1, and for pins D0 to D3, driving to 1 at edge action 4 and to 0 at edge action 5. The tri-state formatter is not used.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › BWDS  BWDS  -  Break Waveform Definition String）

```
> BWDS? 1,,,(@)
< BWDS 1,,,"",(io)
< BWDS 1,,,"d1:F00 d5:F10",(clk)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

```
CDCP? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {strt_disp}, {disp_length}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CDCP {cycle}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}, {DD1}, {DD2}, {ED1}, {ED2}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle to be analyzed. The range of values for this parameter depends on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

cycle

 |

In the query, the consecutive number of the displayed cycle.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles to be analyzed. The range for this parameter is 0 to 1000.

 |
 |

strt_disp

 |

This parameter defines the offset of your range of interest from start_cycle. The actual display starts with the last device cycle that does not begin before start_cycle and does not end before start_cycle + strt_disp.

The purpose of this construction is to enable a correct device cycle reconstruction even if the first cycle you are interested in does not lie at a device cycle boundary (a device cycle can generate up to 16 cycles).

 |
 |

disp_length

 |

Specifies the display length in cycles. This parameter determines the end of your range of interest. The actual display stops with the last device cycle that starts before start_cycle + strt_disp + disp_length.

If this parameter is larger than no_of_cycles, it is ignored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which a device cycle data transfer is to be made. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to download data for all configured pins.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

A reply parameter, giving the name of the reconstructed device cycle.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

A reply parameter, giving the length of the reconstructed device cycle. For SmarTest 7.10 this is always 1.

 |
 |

DD1 and DD2

 |

Drive Data parameters. They contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values the system returns are:

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

N

 |

Not used. Returned if no drive data parameter is set to a drive and tri-state value.

 |
 |

UC

 |

Unclear. The system may return this value to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle.

 |
 |

ED1 and ED2

 |

Expected Data Parameters. The values the system returns are:

 |
 |

F0

 |

compare to 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

compare to 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

compare to intermediate

 |
 |

FX

 |

compare to mask

 |
 |

FU

 |

compare to unstable

 |
 |

N

 |

Not used. Returned if no expected data parameter is set to a compare value.

 |
 |

UC

 |

Unclear. The system may return this value to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

```
> CDCP? 0,8,0,8,(S0_1)
< CDCP 0,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 1,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 2,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 3,"MYDC",2,F00,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 5,"MYDC",2,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
> CDCP? 2,6,4,2,(S0_1)
< CDCP 5,"MYDC",2,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
```

In the second call of CDCP? (the first call just serves to display the underlying situation) the range of interest starts at vector 6. Note that the reply starts with vector 5, and that the first occurrence of MYDC, which lies between vector 2 and vector 6, is not displayed.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFCF  CFCF  -  Clock Forwarding ConFiguration）

|

cf_name

 |

Specifies the name of a clock forwarding set that must have been defined with CFDF.

 |
 |

source_pin

 |

Specifies the pin whose tracking behavior is to be transferred.

 |
 |

sink_pins

 |

Specifies the pins that are to make use of the tracking behavior of the source pin.

 |
 |

speed

 |

Defines the maximum expected shift per ns. This can be used to determine the maximum supported shift. See `Implementation details of clock forwarding`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.05.01_Implementation_details_of_clock_forwarding.md`）.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This query parameter specifies the pins whose role in the specified clock forwarding set is to be retrieved.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFCF  CFCF  -  Clock Forwarding ConFiguration）

```
> CFCF? "cf_set1",(@)
< CFCF "cf_set1",(Pin1),(Pin3, Pin2)
< CFCF "cf_set1",(Pin4),(Pin5)
> CFCF "cf_set1",(Pin1),(Pin6, Pin3)
> CFCF "cf_set1",(Pin7),(Pin4)
> CFCF? "cf_set1",(@)
> CFCF "cf_set1",(Pin1),(Pin6, Pin3)
> CFCF "cf_set1",(Pin7),(Pin4)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFDF  CFDF  -  Clock Forwarding Set DeFinition）

|

cf_set_name

 |

In the command, this is the name of a new clock forwarding set. In the query, it is a name of an existing clock forwarding set. If you omit this parameter in the query, CFDF? will return the names of all user defined clock forwarding sets.

 |
 |

mode_context

 |

The mode context with which the clock forwarding set is associated. If this parameter is omitted, the DEFAULT context is assumed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFDF  CFDF  -  Clock Forwarding Set DeFinition）

```
> CFDF   "cf_set1"
> CFDF   "cf_set2"
> CFDF   "cf_set3"

> CFDF?
< CFDF   "cf_set1"
< CFDF   "cf_set2"
< CFDF   "cf_set3"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFPR  CFPR  -  Clock Forwarding PRimary set）

|

cf_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing clock forwarding set. Specify an empty string to inactivate the current primary set and thus to disable clock forwarding.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFPR  CFPR  -  Clock Forwarding PRimary set）

```
> CFPR   "cf_set1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFUD -  Clock Forwarding set UnDefine）

```
CFUD {"cf_set_name"}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFUD -  Clock Forwarding set UnDefine）

|

cf_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing clock forwarding set.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Remove all existing transition tests sets

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CFUD -  Clock Forwarding set UnDefine）

```
> CFUD   "cf_set1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHER  -  CHeck ERrors）

```
CHER? [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CHER {res_flag}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHER  -  CHeck ERrors）

|

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the result returned for this Pin Scale pin will be combined from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to the HXA pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Results will be provided only for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO pins.

 |
 |

res_flag

 |

The result flag is returned by the system. It can be:

 |
 |

F

 |

The last functional test performed on the specified pins failed.

 |
 |

P

 |

The last functional test performed on the specified pins passed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHER  -  CHeck ERrors）

After a functional test has been performed, sending CHER? returns the result for each pin in pinlist.

```
CHER? (@)
```

returns:

```
CHER F,(Q0,Q1)
CHER P,(Q2)
CHER F,(Q3)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHFA  -  CHannel FAil flag）

```
CHFA? [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CHFA {res_flag}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHFA  -  CHannel FAil flag）

|

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the combined result from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to the HXA pin will be used to determine the answer.

 |
 |

res_flag

 |

The result flag can be:

 |
 |

F

 |

The pin failed in the last match loop cycle.

 |
 |

P

 |

The pin passed in the last match loop cycle.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of pins. If more than one pin is included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be of O or IO type.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHFA  -  CHannel FAil flag）

```
CHFA? (D1)
```

returns:

```
CHFA F, (D1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHIN  -  CHannel INformation）

```
CHIN? {channel_nr|ALL}
```

returns:

CHIN {channel_nr}, {channel_type}, [phys_location], {board_no}, [clk_board], [chan_info_1], [chan_info_2]

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHIN  -  CHannel INformation）

|

channel_nr

 |

The number that identifies the channel.

Specify ALL if you want information about all channels.

For a digital channel, specify it with the test system channel number, which is five digits (see `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name) for the number)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`）.

For a DPS channel, specify it with the test system channel number, which is two digits (see `DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） for the number).

 |
 |

channel_type

 |

Returns the type of the channel. It can be:

 |
 |

CPIO

 |

Pin Scale 1600 digital channel

 |
 | PYIO  | Pin Scale 5000 digital channel |
 |

WZ_FDIFF_I

 |

Fast differential input channel

 |
 |

WZ_FDIFF_O

 |

Fast differential output channel

 |
 |

PPS

 |

Precision Parallel Source channel

 |
 |

HVP

 |

High Voltage PMU

 |
 |

DPS128HC

 |

DC Scale DPS128-HC or DPS64-HC

 |
 | XPS256  | DC Scale XPS256 |
 |  UHC4T  | DC Scale UHC4T |
 |

phys_location

 |

The channel's physical location.

NOTE: For PS1600 and DPS128 SmarTest returns always "-1"!

This format is TCSSPP.

Where:

 |
 |

T

 |

test head (1)

 |
 |

C

 |

card cage (1 - 8)

 |
 |

SS

 |

slot (01 - 18) in the card cage

 |
 |

PP

 |

hardware pin number of the digital channel

For DPS, this is the channel number in the DPS board.

 |
 |

board_no

 |

Board number of the board to which the channel belongs. For the DPS, this is the DPS board number. For details, see the board_no parameter in `*OPT? - (hardware OPTions)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md`）.

 |
 |

clk_board

 |

Board number of the clock board in the card cage to which the channel belongs.

 |
 |

chan_info_1

 |

First information of the channel.

 |
 |

For digital channels:

Sequencer memory (SM) depth in blocks of 128k vectors (or 0.125M vectors).

DC Scale DPS channels behave like a digital channel and return the sequencer memory depth.

 |
 |

For PPS channels:

Pattern memory depth in blocks of 1k words (16 bit).

 |
 |

For HVP channels:

DAC/ADC RAM depth in blocks of 1k words (16 bit).

 |
 |

chan_info_2

 |

Second information of the channel.

 |
 |

For digital channels:

Sequencer memory (SM) depth in blocks of 128k vectors (or 0.125M vectors).

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHIN  -  CHannel INformation）

```
CHIN? 10901
```

returns:

```
CHIN 10901,PSIO,120601,109,21,512,0
```

```
CHIN? ALL
```

  Return (for example):

```
CHIN 10101,PYIO,110301,101,11,3551,0
CHIN 10102,PYIO,110302,101,11,3551,0

CHIN 21701,DPS128HC,-1,217,31,191,0
CHIN 21702,DPS128HC,-1,217,31,191,0

```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CHRS  CHRS  -  CHeck Routing Set globally）

|

OFF

 |

SmarTest tries to fulfill an inconsistent request as well as possible. This is the default.

 |
 |

ON

 |

SmarTest issues an error message when a routing request is inconsistent, and retains the previous routing status

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CLKR  CLKR  -  CLocK Resolution）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To set or query the resolution of a multi-port timing specification, specify the name of the specification.

 |
 |

ref_period

 |

Not used. (Ignored)

 |
 |

period_res

 |

The period resolution (in ns) for the specified specification or waveform set.

If necessary, period_res is rounded to nine digits after the decimal point. The allowable maximum period resolution is the maximum tester period value. The minimum period resolution is determined by the hardware (see `Automatic calculation of period resolution for single-port setups`（raw: `02.06.06.01.04.01.02.01_Automatic_calculation_of_period_resolution_for_single-port_setups.md`）).

 |
 |

type

 |

In the query, the type parameter specifies which resolution is queried. The allowed values are:

VIRTUAL: The period resolution (period_res) is queried. This is the default.

EXACT: The clock resolution (clock_res) is queried.

 |
 |

clock_res

 |

In the answer to the query, the clock resolution is returned if type is set to EXACT in the query.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CLKR  CLKR  -  CLocK Resolution）

```
> CLKR 1,,10
> CLKR? 1
< CLKR 1,1000,10

```

This example sets and queries the period resolution (10 ns) for waveform set 1. Ignore the returned value of the ref_period parameter.

```
> CLKR? "spec_port_1_port_2"
< CLKR "spec_port_1_port_2",50,5.555555556
```

This example queries the period resolution for the multi-port specification `spec_port_1_port_2`.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CLKC）

```
CLKC? <specset | specificationName>, (portName)
```

returns:

```
CLKC <spscset | specificationName>, mater_clock_ns, edge_clock_ns, (portName)
```

Parameters
 |

specset

 |

The required specification set.

 |
 |

specificationName

 |

The name of the required specification.

 |
 |

portName

 |

The port name. This can be either a specific port, or all ports. For all ports, you can use @@ if this is a multiport, or only @ to specify all pins if this is not a multiport.

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CLMP  CLMP  -  CLaMP level）

|

level_set

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by the DSCP command). Specifying ALL sets the clamp levels for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Specifying PRM sets the clamp levels for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number > 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for the high-Z state of digital pins. For more information see `Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF`（raw: `02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md`）.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

 |
 |

clamp_mode

 |

ON | OFF

For the Pin Scale 3600, the clamps can be set to ON when std/fast mode is set to std, and termination mode is set to OFF or A (active load).

Pin Scale 9G cards do not have clamps. Setting clamp levels will be ignored.

For termination mode, see `TERM, TERM? - (TERMination mode)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.257_TERM__TERM__-__TERMination_mode.md`）.

 |
 |

low_clamp_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the low clamp level.

For the Pin Scale 800, the range is -1800 to 6800. At power-on this parameter assumes a default value of -250.

 |
 |

high_clamp_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the high clamp level. For the Pin Scale 800, the range is -1800 to 6800, and the difference of high_clamp_level - low_clamp_level must be in the range 0 to 8.6 V.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pins for which the clamp levels are to be set. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the DFGP (DeFine GrouP) command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. The symbol @ refers to all pins. You can include O and IO pin types in pinlist.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CLMP  CLMP  -  CLaMP level）

```
CLMP 1,ON,-10,5100,(Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

This example sets the clamp levels for level set 1 for pins Q0, Q1, Q2 and Q3. The low clamp level is set to -10 mV, and the high clamp level is set to 5100 mV.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CMNT  CMNT  -  CoMmeNT）

|

act_vect_of_port

 |

Specifies the active vector of the referenced port at which the comment is to be inserted, or, in the query, the first vector of which the comment is to be displayed.

Note that you must count the active vectors of the port consecutively across all of its labels, starting from 0. Suppose, for example, that two labels, test_1 and test_2, are associated with the port, where test_1 has 8 active vectors, and test_2 has 3. Then, to insert a comment at the second vector of test_2, you must enter 9.

 |
 |

text

 |

A string of up to 250 characters. The string must be enclosed with double quotes.

Comments can contain any characters with ASCII codes from 32 to 126, that is, all printable ASCII characters. To put a double quote character (", ASCII 34) into a comment, enter two double quote characters.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

In the query, the range of active vectors to be displayed, starting from act_vect_of_port. It can cross label boundaries.

 |
 |

port

 |

Specifies the port to which the active vectors associated with the comments belong. If you do not specify a port, the comments to the active vectors of the default port @ are set or read.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CMNT  CMNT  -  CoMmeNT）

Display the sequencer area of the default port:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,528,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 7,GENV,12,,,(@)
< SQPG 8,STOP,,,,(@)
```

Add the comment "Start of test_2" to the active vector 15 of the default port @, that is, to the first active vector of the second label:

```
> CMNT 15,"Start of test_2"
```

Activate test_2 for editing and display the comments for its vectors with the label specific TCMT? query:

```
> TSTL "test_2",(@)
> TCMT? 0,11
< TCMT 0,"Start of test_2"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CMVC -  Clear and MoVe Comments）

CMVC {src_vec_No}, {dst_vec_No}, {vect_length}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CMVC -  Clear and MoVe Comments）

|

src_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the source range.

 |
 |

dst_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the destination range.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The vector range from which comments are to be moved. Specify 0 in order to simply delete the vectors between the source and the destination number.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CMVC -  Clear and MoVe Comments）

```
> CMNT? 0,6
< CMNT 0,"0"
< CMNT 1,"1"
< CMNT 2,"2"
< CMNT 3,"3"
< CMNT 4,"4"
< CMNT 5,"5"
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> CMVC 0,4,2
> CMNT? 0,6
< CMNT 4,"0"
< CMNT 5,"1"
```

This example moves comments in the vector range 0 to 1 to the range 4 to 5. The previous comments for vectors 4 and 5 are overwritten, the comments for vector 2 and 3 are cleared.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CNCT - CoNneCT disCoNneCT）

| mode |

OFF: Disconnects all pins in the specified modules.

CNCT? always returns OFF as mode.

 |
 | pinlist |

Pin names.

Multiple pin names must be separated with a comma.

The @ symbol specifies all modules that have a pin for which a pin name has been defined.

You do not need to specify more than one pin in one PPS module.

 |

CNCT disconnects the pins immediately.

The following rules apply if the CNCT command is used in conjunction with PPS cards:

- CNCT disconnects all 16 output pins in the PPS module, even in multisite testing.
- CNCT does not change the output voltage of the PPS core when disconnecting the pins.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CNCT - CoNneCT disCoNneCT）

To set all defined PPS pins to 0 V and disconnect all output pins of the PPS modules:

```
FORC 0,(@)
CNCT OFF,(@)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CNGV -  CoNnect Generate Vectors）

```
CNGV {(cmd_No)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CNGV -  CoNnect Generate Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number which references the first of the two consecutive GENV sequencer constructs.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CNGV -  CoNnect Generate Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,8,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> CNGV 2
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,17,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CONF  CONF  -  CONFiguration）

| context |

This extra parameter specifies a mode context. If it is omitted, the default mode context DEFAULT is set or read. If DEFAULT is the only context defined, the parameter is omitted in the query reply.

The default mode context is predefined. All other mode contexts must be defined with the CTXT command.

If you specify ALL in the query, CONF? will display all mode contexts.

 |
 | pin_type |

The mandatory parameter assigns channel resources to the pin. This can be:

 | I  | Configures a drive pin. |
 | O  | Configures a receive pin. |
 | IO  | Configures a bidirectional pin. |
 | DC |

Configures a pin for DC measurements. The pin is only connected to the PMU, and no driver or receiver resources are allocated to it.

For DC Scale channels (power or signal pins) the mode is always DC.

This option is not allowed for Smart Scale pins.

 |
 | OFF  | The pin is not available for measurements.  | |
 |

pin_oper_mode

 |

The mandatory parameter defines or indicates the operating mode of the pins in pinlist. The operation mode can be:

 | DCSIGNAL  | In the query this indicates that the pin is associated with a DC Scale channel and has been configured in PMU mode with DFPN. |
 | POWER  | In the query this indicates that the pin is associated with a DC Scale channel and has been configured in DPS mode with DFPS. |
 | CMON  | Configures the pin as current monitor output. For more information, refer to `XPS256 current monitor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.03.02_XPS256_current_monitor.md`）. |
 | F160 |

Specifies Standard operating mode. This is the default. It must be selected for pins on PS1600 boards.

 |
 | F330  | Not valid. |
 | FAST |

This operation mode must be selected for fast pins. Note that no pin can be set to FAST in the default mode context DEFAULT, and that no IO pin can be set to FAST.

For Smart Scale pins this mode will be mapped to F160.

   | |
 | pinlist |

The name of the pin or pins to be configured or listed. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

The symbol @ can be used in the query to list all pins that were previously either explicitly configured with the CONF command, or (in the case of DC Scale pins) implicitly with the DFPN or DFPS command.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CONF  CONF  -  CONFiguration）

```
> CONF IO,F160,(D0,D1)
```

This example configures pins `D0` and `D1` as bidirectional pins operating in Standard Mode for the default mode context.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CONF  CONF  -  CONFiguration）

```
> CONF? (sdd,vdd)
< CONF DC,DCSIGNAL,(sdd)
< CONF DC,POWER,(vdd)
```

This example queries the DC Scale channels `sdd` and `vdd`, which were set with `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） to PMU mode (`DCSIGNAL`) and with `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） to DPS mode (`POWER`), respectively.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CPYV -  CopY Vectors）

```
CPYV {src_vec_No}, {dst_vec_No}, {vect_length}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

src_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the source range.

 |
 |

dst_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the destination range.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The length of the vector range to be copied.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins for which vectors are to be copied. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to modify the vectors of all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CPYV -  CopY Vectors）

```
> SQPG? all,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> $VECD? PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1)
< VECD PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1),
  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0001
  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000
  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000
```

The first three active vectors of the RPTV instruction (with the logical vector numbers 9 to 11) are set to 0 for pin S0_1. Now activate the label for editing and copy vectors 12 to 14 to position 9 for S0_1:

```
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> CPYV 12,9,3,(S0_1)
```

Display the result:

```
> $VECD? PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1)
< VECD PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1),
  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0001
  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000
  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

```
CSAS? [msMode,] {mask}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CSAS {status}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

| msMode  | The extra parameter controls how the return value is created.

The value of the parameter can be PQFC:

- PQFC specified: The current query focus is respected and allows status query per site without affecting status bits of other sites.
- PQFC not specified: The command reads (and clears) status bits of all enabled and active sites at a glance, ignoring the actual query focus.
The parameter applies only to use of parameter mask as integer value. |
 |

mask

   | Integer bit mask or ALL.

-

Integer bit mask: Integer value is used to mask out individual status bits. Each bit of mask is logically AND-ed with the corresponding bit of the DPS status. If one of the resulting bits is set, then F (Fail) is returned, otherwise P (Pass).

It is used to check for an error condition. All bit positions of the status flags that should be checked, must be set to 1 in mask. If one of the selected status bits is set, then CSAS? returns F.

- ALL: Hex value (hexadecimal representation of all status bits) is returned.
For setting the integer bit mask or interpreting a returned hex value, refer to the `status`（raw: `02.06.02.02.33_CSAS__-__Channel_Slot_Accumulated_Status.md#_144688__r_status`） parameter below. |
 |

pinlist

 |

Comma separated list of DPS128/64 or XPS256 pins. The @ character can be used to read the status for all DPS pins.

 |
 |

status

   | If mask is ALL, you need to translate the hex value (hexadecimal representation of the status bits) to its binary form as follows:

 | Bit 0:  | High voltage or current of surge tracker exceeded |
 | Bit 1:  | Low voltage or current of surge tracker exceeded |
 | Bit 2:  | 0 |
 | Bit 3:  | Measurement range change failed |
 | Bit 4:  | Clamp current correction failed |
 | Bit 5:  | Battery full |
 | Bit 6:  | Power budget 1 |
 | Bit 7:  | Power budget 2 |
 | Bit 8:  | Power budget 3 |
 | Bit 9:  | High voltage of surge tracker reached |
 | Bit 10:  | Low voltage of surge tracker reached |
 | Bit 11:  | High current of surge tracker reached |
 | Bit 12:  | Low current of surge tracker reached |

If mask is specified as an integer bit-mask:

- Pass: P
- Fail: F
 |

### Example 1:（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

```
CSAS? 3,(VCC)
```

returns either

```
CSAS P,(VCC)
```

or

```
CSAS F,(VCC)
```

The example uses the integer bitmask and checks whether a spike on the `VCC` pin exceeded the low or high limit.

- P = Pass

No spike occurred since the last CSAS? query.

- F = Fail

Either the low or high limit or both were exceeded.

### Example 2:（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

```
CSAS? ALL,(Vaux)
```

returns

```
CSAS #H10,(Vaux)
```

The example uses the ALL specifier and checks for an error condition on the `Vaux` pin.

- Bit 3 = 0

No "Measurement range change failed" error. All set current measurement range requests were successful.

- Bit 4 = 1

The "Clamp current correction failed". A high-accuracy clamp current correction for a DCVH setup with execution mode SER_HAC or PAR_HAC was not successful.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CTST  -  Continuity TeST）

```
CTST? {mode}
```

returns:

```
CTST {result},{(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CTST  -  Continuity TeST）

|

mode

 |

The mode is:

 |
 |

GPF - Global Pass/Fail. Returns a single pass/fail result that includes all pins in the pin list.

 |
 |

PPF - Per pin Pass/Fail. Returns a pass/fail result for each pin in the pin list.

 |
 |

result

 |

This parameter returns the result of the test.

 |
 |

F - If at least one pin fails.

 |
 |

P - If all pins pass.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Must contain the names of pins previously defined by the DFCT command. If more than one pin is specified, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CTST  -  Continuity TeST）

```
DFCT
10.000,1700.000,200.000,700.000,SPOL,(p1,p2,p3,p4)
CTST? GPF
```

This example uses the command to set up the parameters needed to execute a continuity test on pins p1 to p4. The parameters are as follows:

- Force current = 10 mA
- Commutation voltage = 1.7 V
- Voltage minimum pass value = 200 mV
- Voltage maximum pass value = 700 mV
- Single polarity measurement selected.

It then executes the test with the CTST command using the global pass/fail mode.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CTXT  CTXT  -  ConTeXT）

|

action

 |

Specifies the action. Possible values are:

 |
 |

DEFINE

 |

Defines a new mode context

 |
 |

DELETE

 |

Deletes a mode context

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Displays all existing mode contexts (only in the query).

 |
 |

name

 |

The name of the mode context. If the action parameter is set to DELETE, you can also specify ALL to delete all mode contexts.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CTXT  CTXT  -  ConTeXT）

```
> CTXT? ALL
< CTXT DEFINE,"DEFAULT"
< CTXT DEFINE,"differential"
< CTXT DEFINE,"PdrvNPrcv"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYCI  -  get CYCle Information）

CYCI? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {resolution_mode} [,MUX] [,(port)]

returns:

CYCI {cycle}, [res_mode] [, (port)], {vector_number}, [label], [type], [seq_status], [comment], [no_of_waveforms] [,MUX], {#spec(data)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYCI  -  get CYCle Information）

|

start_cycle

 |

The start cycle is an integer that defines the first cycle to be reported. The start cycle is in the range 0 to 2^48 when the sequencer runs in the Start Analysis mode, and -2^48 to -1 when the sequencer is in the Stop Analysis mode. If a positive number is entered, cycles are counted from 0 upwards. If a negative number is entered, the cycles are counted from the end of the test to -1. In both cases the reported start cycles are in Start Analysis mode.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

Defines the number of cycles to be reported. The integer must be in the range 0 to 256.

 |
 |

resolution_mode

 |

Defines the answer format of the binary data.

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the default value.

 |
 |

CYRM

 |

This option lets the result granularity depend on the CYRM command. If CYRM is set to EDGE, then CYCI? will supply information on the edge level (receive events).

 |
 |

port

 |

If you specify a port, information is returned for this port. If you do not specify any port, the default port @, to which all pins belong, is reported.

 |
 |

cycle

 |

In the reply, this is the consecutive number of the reported cycle. The numbering starts with the value of start_cycle.

 |
 |

res_mode

 |

This has the same values as defined in the CYRM mode parameter.

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the answer if the CYRM command mode is CYCL.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

If CYRM is set to EDGE and resolution_mode was set to CYRM, then EDGE will be returned for this parameter.

 |
 |

vector_number

 |

Returns the logical number of the first vector of the instruction that generated the cycle. The logical vector number counts the active vectors within one label, starting from 0. If the vectors generated by the instruction are break vectors, then -1 is returned.

 |
 |

label

 |

Returns the label name. It references the label to which the reported cycle belongs.

 |
 |

type

 |

Returns the label type. The following types are reported:

 |
 |

MAIN

 |

The MAIN program.

 |
 |

SJMP

 |

A JuMP Subroutine.

 |
 |

SVEC

 |

A VECtor Subroutine.

 |
 |

BRST

 |

BuRST mode.

 |
 |

 |

MPBU

 |

Multi-Port BUrst mode

 |
 |

seq_status

 |

Returns the current sequencer status. The status is expressed on most occasions in the form of the sequencer instruction that was used to generate the vectors in the requested cycle range. Otherwise it is expressed in terms of the current sequencer activity. Note that seq_status is not the same as the sequencer state determined by `SQST, SQST? - (SeQuencer STate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.241_SQST__SQST__-__SeQuencer_STate.md`）. Sequencer instructions are parameters to `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）. For additional information on sequencer programming see also see `Vector Setup Commands`（raw: `02.06.07_Vector_Setup_Commands.md`）.

The seq_status parameter is required for the reconstruction of received data. Some of the values it returns signify that vectors are being generated, others inform of sequencer status changes, which cause some or no break vectors to be generated.

 |
 |

GENV

 |

This is returned if GENV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vector for the reported cycle.

 |
 |

SRCV

 |

This is returned if SRCV is the sequencer instruction that generates vectors in the reported cycle range.

For "non-source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the parallel vectors exactly the same way as RPTV. That means "no_of_vectors" parallel vectors are repeated for a repeating count (equal to no_of_cycles divided by no_of_vectors) to generate "no_of_cycles" cycles on the test system.

For "source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the vectors stored in the source memory. It means "no_of_cycles" vectors are generated from the source memory to produce "no_of_cycles" cycle on the test system, and the information of "no_of_vectors" has no meaning to "source pin".

 |
 |

RPTV

 |

This is returned if RPTV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vector for the reported cycle.

 |
 |

JPPS

 |

This keyword indicates that a per pin subroutine is executed that cannot be reconstructed because it is too complex. In this case, PP is returned for the drive data and expected data parameters in the result data (#spec(data) parameter).

 |
 |

CTIM

 |

This is returned if a change timing instruction has been issued in the queried cycle range. Each timing change generates break vectors.

The real number of break cycles depends on the test system period and will not be shown in the cycle reconstruction.

Between 0 to 7 break cycles will be recorded during a CTIM instruction, the exact number depends on the number of vectors loaded previously. For instance, if the previous number of cycles was a multiple of 8, then no break vectors are issued during the reload.

 |
 |

CLEV

 |

The CLEV (change levels) parameter indicates that unrecorded break cycles, due to a change of level set, exist in the specified cycle range.

 |
 |

BRK

 |

This is returned if break cycles are being generated during the reported cycle range - for example, if a timed match loop is in progress. Between 0 and 7 break cycles will be recorded.

Additionally, the following sequencer instructions also generate break vectors:

 |
 |

 |

Sequencer instruction

 |

reported as

 |
 |

 |

CTIM

 |

CTIM

 |
 |

 |

CLEV

 |

CLEV

 |
 |

 |

WTER

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

FLQU

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

MEAS

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

STOP

 |

BRK

 |
 |

MTCH

 |

This is returned if

- the test contains a counted match loop,
- the test has been executed online, and
- the last cycle of the match loop is not the last cycle of a 8-cycle block.

In this case the last match loop cycles belonging to this block (up to 7) are recorded in the Error Map and reported by CYCI?. For details see `Adjusting the junctions between match loop and surrounding label`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01.01_Adjusting_the_junctions_between_match_loop_and_surrounding_label.md`）.

 |
 |

comment

 |

Returns the comment text inserted at vector_number. (See also `TCMT, TCMT? - (Test CoMment Transfer)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.254_TCMT__TCMT__-__Test_CoMment_Transfer.md`）)

 |
 |

no_of_waveforms

 |

This parameter will always be 1.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the Pin Scale pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Returns result data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the data for each pin. The pins are ordered by ascending channel numbers from the first site.

The format of the pin specific output data is controlled by the res_mode parameter: Cycle resolution format is used if res_mode was set to CYCL, edge resolution format is used if res_mode was set to CYRM. Both formats agree for the first 23 bytes, which contain the following information:

 |
 |

 |

byte 0-16:

 |

Device cycle name or 'BREAK' in case of break cycles, zero terminated. The reserved device cycle name 'JPPS' can be returned if the reconstructed data belongs to a Per-Pin subroutine.

 |
 |

 |

byte 17:

 |

HXA information

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 0-3: NOT USED (always 0).

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 4-5: channel selector for pins mapped to a HXA pin. Indicates the logical position of the pin in the multiplexing order. Set to 0 for standard pins.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 6-7: pin multiplexing factor for HXA pins. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

 |

0

 |

Pin not mapped to HXA pin

 |
 |

 |

 |

1

 |

One of two Pin Scale pins that are mapped to HXA pin

 |
 |

 |

 |

3

 |

One of 4 Pin Scale pins that are mapped to HXA pin

 |
 |

 |

 |

Information relating to HXA multiplexing is only returned if the MUX flag is set.

 |
 |

 |

byte 18, 19:

 |

NOT USED (always set to 4).

 |
 |

 |

byte 20, 21:

 |

NOT USED (always set to 15).

 |
 |

 |

byte 22:

 |

Received data. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

 |

0

 |

No error

 |
 |

 |

 |

FF

 |

This means that an error has occurred, but that it is not reconstructible for one of the following reasons:

- The waveform contains more than 1 edge.
- The waveform contains a window compare.
- Only 1 bit results are recorded.
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bits 0-2 contain the received value:

 |
 |

 |

 |

1

 |

Received high

 |
 |

 |

 |

2

 |

Received intermediate

 |
 |

 |

 |

4

 |

Received low

 |
 |

 |

 |

5

 |

Received unstable

 |
 |

 |

 |

7

 |

Failed but not reconstructible

This value will be returned for single-ended standard mode if only one bit results are recorded and the edge failed.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 3 - 5: number of failing compare edge or failing window close. If the edge was not reconstructible (bits 6-7 set to 3) the value is set to 7.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 6-7:

 |
 |

 |

 |

0

 |

This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

 |

3

 |

The failing edge is not reconstructible.

 |
 |

 |

The cycle resolution format consists of the 23 bytes described above. If the data is returned in edge resolution format, CYCI? provides additional information about receive events.

 |
 |

 |

byte 23:

 |

Number of the following receive events. Note that only used receive events will be reported.

Every receive event consists of three bytes (A, B, C), that are to be read as follows:

 |
 |

 |

byte A:

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED (Always 0).

 |
 |

 |

byte B:

 |

Receive event index

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 0-2: edge index (0 through 7)

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 3-4: channel selector for HXA pins.

If the multiplexing factor in byte 17 is > 0, and the channel selector in byte 17 is set to 0, then CYCI? will add the edges of all the other channels for the same HXA pin to the binary data. This field indicates to which of these channels the edge belongs. It specifies the position number of the respective channel in the logical multiplexing order.

 |
 |

 |

 |

Information relating to HXA multiplexing is only returned if the MUX flag is set.

 |
 |

 |

byte C:

 |

Receive data

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 0 - 3: compare method

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 4 - 6: received value

 |
 |

 |

For details see the tables below.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYCI  -  get CYCle Information）

CYCI? 20,2,CYCL

returns:

CYCI 20,11,"TEST1",SVEC,RPTV,"comment",1,

#9000000046

 dvc_01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x04\x99

 dvc_02\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x04\x0F\x0F\x00

CYCI 21,12,"TEST1",SVEC,GENV,,1,

#9000000046

 dvc_03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x04\x04\x05\x0F\x6C

 dvc_04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x04\x04\x0F\x0F\x0D

This example returns result information (on the cycle level) for 2 cycles and 2 output pins of the label `TEST1`, which is of type SVEC. The first cycle was generated by a RPTV instruction from logical vector 11 and has an associated comment, the second cycle was generated by a GENV instruction for logical vector 12.

The binary data reports the device cycle names, which in this example are different for each pin and cycle. The waveform offsets are zero. The reported drive/expected/received data are:

 |

dvc_01:

 |

DD1 = F00, DD2 = F10, ED1 = FX, ED2 = F0

error: high received on edge 3 (param E2)

 |
 |

dvc_02:

 |

DD1 = F00, DD2 = N, ED1 = N, ED2 = N

no error

 |
 |

dvc_03:

 |

DD1 = N, DD2 = N, ED1 = FU, ED2 = N

error: high received on edge 5 (param E1)

 |
 |

dvc_04:

 |

DD1 = N, DD2 = N, ED1 = N, ED2 = N

error: unstable received on edge 1 (FIX)

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRM  CYRM  -  CYcle Resolution Mode）

|

resolution_mode

 |

Defines the resolution mode. This can be:

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the normal operation mode. In spite of its name (which was coined at a time when the normal operation mode was one result per cycle), it simply means that the result resolution as defined with DCRM is to be applied. This is the default.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

This option

- activates a mechanism by which a test that failed on the cycle level is re-executed in order to enable error map recording on the edge level. For details see `Retrieving edge information by repeating the test`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.02.01_Retrieving_edge_information_by_repeating_the_test.md`）.

Note also that re-execution of the test can be blocked with the CYRP command.

- prevents acceptance of any DCRM configuration that combines more than one edge result into one recorded result, except DCRM 1,PFC.

Note that the EDGE option is not available for pins which take part in a match loop.

 |
 |

error_limit

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin or pins to which this mode will be applied. You can also specify one or more pin groups or ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRM  CYRM  -  CYcle Resolution Mode）

```
CYRM CYCL,,(@)
CYRM CYCL,,(MatchLoopPin)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRP  -  CYcle Resolution Parameter）

```
CYRP [recovery],[shots]
CYRP?
```

returns:

```
CYRP {recovery},{shots}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRP  -  CYcle Resolution Parameter）

|

recovery

 |

Specifies whether the test is repeated with all receive edges enabled after the last fine granularity shot. This serves to reset the hardware registers into the state in which they were before the first fine granularity shot. Possible values are:

 |
 |

RCRY

 |

The test is repeated at the end with all receive edges enabled. This is the default.

 |
 |

NRCR

 |

The test is not repeated.

 |
 |

shots

 |

Specifies whether additional shots are allowed. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ONE

 |

No additional shots are allowed. This option allows execution of a test only if CYRM is set to CYCLE, or the mode parameter of DCRM is set to 8.

ONE can be used to prevent execution of a test in fine granularity mode (EDGE option of CYRM) with several shots if this would lead to erroneous results.

 |
 |

MULT

 |

Additional shots are allowed. This is the default.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRP  -  CYcle Resolution Parameter）

```
CYRP NRCR,ONE
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRS  -  CYcle Resolution State）

```
CYRS? {(pinlist)}
CYRS {result_state}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRS  -  CYcle Resolution State）

|

result_state

 |

Specifies the result state of the selected pins. Possible values are:

 |
 |

INVL

 |

No functional test has been executed, so that no test results are available.

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

Test results are available for all selected pins, but they are not edge specific for at least one of them.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

Edge specific test results are available for all selected pins.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin or pin list for which the result state is to be returned. Only O or IO pins will be taken into consideration.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › CYRS  -  CYcle Resolution State）

```
CYRS? (Out1,Out2)
CYRS CYCL,(Out1,Out2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCCH -  DC Current measurement High precision pmu）

```
DCCH {`setNr`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_setNr`）}, `[prechargeVoltage`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_prechargeVoltage`）], `[forceMode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_forceMode`）,] `[forceValue`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_forceValue`）], `[clampValue`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_clampValue`）], `[voltageDrop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_voltageDrop`）,]
            `[lowThreshold`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_lowThreshold`）], `[highThreshold`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_highThreshold`）], `[forceRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_forceRange`）,] `[compareMode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_compareMode`）], `[settlingTime`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_settlingTime`）],
            `[clampRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_clampRange`）,] `[relayAction`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_relayAction`）], `[measureCurrentRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_measureCurrentRange`）,] `[executionMode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_executionMode`）],
            `[connectState`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_connectState`）,] `[samples`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_samples`）,] {(`pinlist`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_pinList`）)} `, ([refPinList`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_refPinList`）)]
```

Parameters
 | setNr |

The DC set identification number, starting with 1.

 |
 | prechargeVoltage |

Defines a precharge voltage (in mV).

This is an optional parameter.

 |
 | forceMode  | This extra parameter specifies the force mode:

 |   | I  | Specifies the force current mode.

Parameter forceValue is to be defined in 碌A (Microampere).

 |
 |   | V  | Specifies the force voltage mode.

Parameter forceValue is to be defined in mV (Millivolt).

This is the default force mode.

 |

The force current mode is currently supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | forceValue  | The force value parameter specifies the force current in 碌A (Microampere) or the force voltage mV (Millivolt).

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The force value is to be specified as current in 碌A (Microampere). |
 |   | V  | The force value is to be specified as voltage in mV (Millivolt).  |  The valid range for the force value depends on the hardware. |
 | clampValue  | The optional clamp value parameter specifies the output clamp voltage in mV (Millivolt) or the output clamp current in 碌A (Microampere).

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The clamp value is to be specified as output clamp voltage in mV (Millivolt).

This is the default mode.

 |
 |   | V  | The clamp value is to be specified as output clamp current in 碌A (Microampere).  |  The parameter may be defined as floating-point number or as string.

The string format supports different values for the upper (or positive) clamp value and the lower (or negative) clamp value.

The string must be defined with pairs of properties and values in the format "property1:value1 property2:value2 ...":

 | Property  | Value type  | Description |
 | lowLimit  | float  | The lower (or negative) clamp value. The value must be less than 0.0. |
 | highLimit  | float  | The upper (or positive) clamp value. The value must be higher than 0.0.  |  In the query answer the lower clamp value is returned only if it is not symmetrical to the upper clamp value.

Example:

`...,"lowLimit:-2000 highLimit:15000",...`

The valid range for the clamp value depends on the hardware.

 |
 | voltageDrop  | The extra parameter specifies the following values:

- Maximum allowed force voltage in mV (Millivolt)
- Maximum allowed return voltage drop in mV (Millivolt)
- Warning threshold for force/return voltage drop in mV (Millivolt)
- Delay time before a current clamp alarm is raised in ms (Millisecond)
- Delay time before a disconnect is performed, after the clamp current is reached in ms (Millisecond)

The extra parameter is to be defined as string and is supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

The string format supports different values for the force drop and for the return drop.

The string must be defined with pairs of properties and values in the format "property1:value1 property2:value2":

 | Property  | Value type  | Description |
 | forceDrop  | integer |

The maximum voltage drop on the force line or return line in mV (Millivolt).

For the specification, refer to `Voltage drop protection / measurement`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.05.03.07_XPS256_other_performance_characteristics.md#_350739__s_Voltage_drop_protection`） in `XPS256 other performance characteristics`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.05.03.07_XPS256_other_performance_characteristics.md`）.

The programmable range is 0.0 鈥?nbsp;1.0 V for the force line and for the return line but, the total for the two lines must not exceed 1.0 V.

The related power supply bits are set if the limits are hit: Bit 6 (Voltage drop force) or bit 7 (Voltage drop return). For more information, refer to `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`）.

For a maximum voltage drop > 0.5 V, the OPEN_LOOP_PROT property of the `connectState`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_connectState`） parameter must be set to OFF and in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`） the `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON.

 |
 | returnDrop  | integer |
 | warnForceDrop  | integer |

The warning levels for the voltage drop on the force line or return line in mV (Millivolt).

The related power supply bits are set if the limits are hit: bit 15 (Voltage drop force warning) or bit 16 (Voltage drop return warning). For more information, refer to `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`） |
 | warnReturnDrop |
 | currClampTimeToAlarm  | integer  | Specifies the delay time before an alarm is raised or a disconnect is performed, after the clamp current is reached.

Unit is milliseconds.

 |
 | currClampTimeToDisconnect  | integer |

Example:

`...,"forceDrop:5000 returnDrop:4000",...`

 |
 | lowThreshold  | The low threshold is used for evaluating the Pass/Fail result. It's specified in 碌A. |
 | highThreshold  | The high threshold is used for evaluating the Pass/Fail result. It's specified in 碌A. |
 | forceRange  | This extra parameter specifies the force range.

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The force current range is to be specified in 碌A (Microampere). |
 |   | V  | The force voltage range is to be specified in mV (Millivolt).  | |
 | compareMode  | This optional string parameter defines how the measured value is compared against the lowThreshold and the highThreshold.

The parameter may be defined as follows:

 | Value  | Mode  | Description |
 | L  | Low  | The Pass/Fail result is set to PASS if the measured value is lower than the lowThreshold. |
 | H  | High  | The Pass/Fail result is set to PASS if the measured value is higher than the highThreshold. |
 | I  | Intermediate  | The Pass/Fail result is set to PASS if the measured value is between lowThreshold and highThreshold.  | |
 | settlingTime  | The settling time specifies the additional time between the setup and the measurement being performed.

The valid range is 0 ms to 2000 ms. The specified settling time is added to the internal settling time of the test system.

 |
 | clampRange  | This extra parameter specifies the clamp range.

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The clamp voltage range is to be specified in mV (Millivolt). |
 |   | V  | The clamp current range is to be specified in 碌A (Microampere).  | |
 | relayAction  | This parameter defines the termination mode of the measurement. The mode can be:

 | |

NTBBM

 |

No-Termination-Break-Before-Measure.

Relay action:

- For digital DC pins:

Non-terminated measurement: Causes all pins in the pin list to be disconnected from the pin electronics (AC relay open).

 |
 |   | NTMBB |

No-Termination-Measure-Before-Break.

Relay action:

- For digital DC pins:

Non-terminated measurement: Causes all pins in the pin list to be disconnected from the pin electronics (AC relay open). Relay switching order is changed to MBB.

 |
 |   | TERM  | Relay action:

- For digital DC pins:

Terminated Measurement: Causes all pins in the pin list, which are already connected to the pin electronics (AC relay closed) to remain connected during measurement. The state of the AC relay is not changed.

 |
 |   | NO |

NO relay action: No relays are switched during the measurement.

 |
 | |

NT

 |

Not terminated.

- For DC Scale pins:

Supported only in PMU operating mode. For more information, see `SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay()`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.234.01.28_SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay.md`）.

 |

See also `SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay()`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.234.01.28_SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay.md`）.

 |
 | measureCurrentRange  | This extra parameter defines the current measurement range. |
 | executionMode  | Measurements belonging to the same DC Set must have the same execution mode. The measurement defined first defines the execution mode of the DC set:

 |   | SER  | Serial measurement (all pins of a site are measured sequentially) |
 |   | PAR  | Parallel measurement (clock board parallel measurement) |
 |   | SER_UNG  | Serial measurement (all pins of a site are measured sequentially). Ganged pins are unganged during the measurement as far as possible.

Only supported for DC Scale channels in PMU mode. Ignored for unganged pins.

 |
 |   | PAR_UNG  | Parallel measurement (clock board parallel measurement). Ganged pins are unganged during the measurement as far as possible.

Only supported for DC Scale channels in PMU mode. Ignored for unganged pins.

 |
 |   | HV_PPMU_BADC_VAL  | The measurement is set up using the pin PMU and performed using the board ADC.

This mode is not supported

 |
 |   | HV_PPMU_GPF  | A global pass/fail measurement is performed using the pin PMU (not the system PMU).

This mode is not supported

 |
 |   | HV_PPMU_PPF  | A pass/fail measurement for each pin is performed using the pin PMU (not the system PMU).

This mode is not supported

  | |
 | connectState  | The combination of the parameters executionMode and connectState defines the behavior of the selected channel.

This parameter is currently supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

This parameter must be defined as string, containing pairs of properties and values in the format "property1:value1 property2:value2 ...".

 | Property  | Value  | Description |
 | SAFE_CON |

ON

OFF

 |

Enables or disables the Smart Connect feature: The voltage at the DUT is sensed and the PMU is automatically set to the measured voltage before a channel is connected.

Default property is OFF.

Note: Parameter prechargeVoltage will be ignored if the Smart Connect is enabled.

 |
 | OPEN_LOOP_PROT  | ON

OFF

 |

The property selects the internal connection from the force output line (P# pin) and the high sense output line (PS# pin).

One of the following specifiers can be set:

- ON

The internal connection is made via two anti-parallel diodes.

This is the default state if the property is not defined.

This is the recommended setting if both the forceDrop propery and the returnDrop property of the `voltageDrop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_voltageDrop`） parameter are set to a value < 0.5 V.

- OFF

The internal connection is open. The output stage no longer has any feedback if the force to sense connection on the DUT or the DUT board is (unintentionally) open.

The following rules apply to this option:
