  - The `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`）.
  - This is the required setting if the forceDrop propery or the returnDrop property of the `voltageDrop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98518__r_voltageDrop`） parameter is set to a value 鈮?nbsp;0.5 V.

See also `XPS256 programming - Voltage drop measurement`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.19_XPS256_programming_-_Voltage_drop_measurement.md`）. |
 | PULLDOWN  | ON

OFF

 |

Enables/disables the pulldown resistor at disconnect.

Default property is ON. |
 | HIGH_ACCURACY  | ON |

Enables usage of High Accuracy mode if possible. If this connection state is defined, the setup can use the 1.5V high accuracy range, see `XPS256 measure voltages`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.06.02_XPS256_measure_voltages.md`）. If HIGH_ACCURACY is specified in a setup but the license is missing, an error message will be generated.

   | |
 | samples |

The number of samples must be a power of 2 (2n).

This limitation does not apply for XPS256.

 |
 | pinList  | The previously defined parameters are applied to all pins specified with the pinList parameter. If more than one pin is specified, pin names must be separated by commas. The pinList can contain pins configured as O, I, IO, or DC pin types. |
 | refPinList |

The reference pin is currently not supported.

The connection state HC_AWG requires a reference pin. This extra parameter defines a single pin or a list of pins that are used as reference pin for the pins defined by pinList.

The reference pin defines always the low force or low sense pin(s). These pins are the LF pin of the floating high-current unit or the LS pin of the differential voltmeter.

Each pin in the refPinList corresponds to a pin in the pinList. Both lists must have the same number of pins defined. The first pin in refPinList belongs to the first pin in pinList.

The refPinList cannot be defined if pinList defines all pins or more than the half of the available pins that support a reference pin based connection state.

A "single-ended" connection mode will be selected if refPinList is omitted and no reference pin is defined: The low force pin and the low sense pin of the floating resource are connected to the common ground and the channel specific ground sense input.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCCH -  DC Current measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCCH 1,,1000,6000,-4170,-3830,I,0,NO,SER,(pin1,pin2,pin3)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, MEAS_VAL
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, VAL
DCRE P, -4103.3, (pin1)
DCRE F, 200.1, (pin2)
DCRE P, -3908.4, (pin3)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCCH -  DC Current measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCCH 1,,I,100000,"lowLimit:-1000 highLimit:10000",0,100000,I,0,NT,PAR,"HC_AWG:ON",(pin1, pin2),(refPin1,refPin2)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, FORCE_ON
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCCH -  DC Current measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCCH 1,,V,10000,"lowLimit:-100000 highLimit:200000",0,100000,I,0,NT,PAR,(pin1, pin2)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, FORCE_ON
```

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCDT  DCDT  -  Device Cycle DefaulT）

```
DCDT 1,"HOLD"
```

This example defines the default device cycle name HOLD for Waveform Set 1.

```
DCDT? "fast_ARM",(ARMPort)
DCDT "fast_ARM","Cycle",(ARMPort)
```

This example queries the default device cycle name for the ARMPort port in the multi-port specification fast_ARM.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCEL  DCEL  -  Digital Compare Exception List）

| DCRT  | The command for which an exception list is to be created. Currently, DCRT is the only allowed command. |
 | TP   | The option of the command specified in the first parameter. Currently TP is the only allowed value. |
 | parameter  | This query parameter can be TP or ALL. |
 | action  | This can be one of the following: |
 | SET  | Add the specified pins to the exception list related to the command in the first parameter. |
 | DEL  | Delete the specified pins from the exception list related to the command in the first parameter. |
 | pinlist  | In the command, these are the pins that are to be added to or deleted from the exception list. In the query, DCEL? returns the subset of the specified pins that is included in the exception list. Instead of a pin list, you can also specify one or more pin groups. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCEL  DCEL  -  Digital Compare Exception List）

```
> DCRT RAM,(portA)
> DFPT? (portA)
< DFPT (p1,p2,p3),(portA)
> DCEL DCRT,TP,(p2)
> DCEL? DCRT,TP,(portA)
< DCEL DCRT,TP,SET,(p2)
> DCEL DCRT,TP,(p1,p3)
> DCEL? DCRT,TP,(portA)
< DCEL DCRT,TP,SET,(p1,p2,p3)
> DCRT? (portA)
< DCRT RAM,(portA)
```

Note that you can add further pins to the exception list, and that the settings of DCRT are not changed even if all three pins of `portA` are in the exception list.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCEX -  DC set EXecute）

```
DCEX {setNr}, [mode]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCEX -  DC set EXecute）

| setNr  | The DC Set Identification number, starting with 1. |
 | mode   | MEAS_VAL  | Value measurement per pin (including P/F result) is executed as defined with `DCCH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`） or `DCVH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`）. |
 |   | MEAS_GPF  | Global pass/fail measurement as defined with `DCCH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`） or `DCVH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`）. |
 |   | MEAS_PPF  | Per-pin pass/fail measurement as defined with `DCCH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`） or `DCVH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`）. |
 |   | FORCE_ON  | The parameters of the DC Set are applied to the HPMU to use the HPMU as source, no measurement is executed.

This mode is not supported for HV pins.

 |
 |   | FORCE_OFF  | The relays are re-opened, so that the HPMU is no longer used as source.

This mode is not supported for HV pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCEX -  DC set EXecute）

Precondition:

```
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1,pin2,pin3)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, MEAS_VAL
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1,
DCRE P, 10.3, (pin1)
DCRE F, 200.1, (pin2)
DCRE P, 20.4, (pin3)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCGM  DCGM  -  Digital Compare Global Mode）

|

acqu_mode

 |

Specifies the recording mode for the detailed Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All cycles are recorded (cycle oriented mode). In this mode, recording will wrap around to the start when the error map is full before the specified stop position or the end of the test.

In this mode, the response time of the result queries EMAP? and ERMP? will be better than in the FAIL mode.

 |
 |

FAIL

 |

Only failed cycles are recorded (failure acquire mode). In this mode, recording for the detailed Error Map will always stop when the map is full. Note that this may happen before the area of interest is reached.

In this mode, more data can be stored in the detailed Error Map.

 |
 |

STRD

 |

SmarTest is to decide whether ALL or FAIL is selected.

 |
 |

emap_pos_int

 |

Specifies how the Error Map position, as set with `DCRP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.47_DCRP__DCRP__-__Digital_Compare_Result_Positioning.md`） or `SQGB`（raw: `02.06.02.02.232_SQGB__SQGB__-__SeQuencer_GloBal.md`）, is interpreted for the detailed Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

STRT

 |

The Error Map position is interpreted as a start value. If the start position is greater than the total number of test cycles, no data will be recorded.

 |
 |

HALT

 |

The Error Map position is interpreted as a stop value. Recording will stop at this position at the latest. If the stop position is greater than the total number of test cycles, recording will stop at the end of the test.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

The Error Map position is ignored. Recording will stop at the end of the test or (if the recording mode is FAIL) when the Error Map is full.

 |
 |

Note that the options STRT and HALT cannot be used with the sequencer modes EL, SE, SEEL, STSQ, and STSV (as set with `SQGB`（raw: `02.06.02.02.232_SQGB__SQGB__-__SeQuencer_GloBal.md`）). If one of these sequencer modes is active, DCGM will issue a warning, and `FTST?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.127_FTST__-__Functional_TeST.md`） will refuse to run.

 |
 |

ovem_pos_int

 |

Specifies how the Error Map position is interpreted for the overview Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

HALT

 |

The Error Map position is interpreted as a stop value. Recording will stop at this position. When the error map is full before this position is reached, recording will wrap around. If the stop position is greater than the total number of test cycles, recording will stop at the end of the test.

This value is only allowed if the emap_pos parameter is also set to HALT.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

The Error Map position is ignored. Recording will stop at the end of the test.When the error map is full before the test ends, recording will wrap around.

 |
 |

answer_type

 |

This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |
 |

exec_context

 |

An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） . This parameter is only accepted when answer_type is set to EXEC.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCGM  DCGM  -  Digital Compare Global Mode）

```
DCGM FAIL,STRT,NONE
```

This example sets the error map into acquire failure mode and specifies that the error map position is to be interpreted as a start value for the detailed error map, and to be ignored for the overview error map.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRE  -  DC set REsult）

```
DCRE? setNr,[resultMode]
```

Parameters
 |

setNr

 |

The DC set identification number, starting with 1.

 |
 | resultMode  | The optional parameter defines the result mode:

 |   | GPF |

A single result, which includes the pass/fail result of the pins, specified in the DC set. A pass is only returned if all pins passed the test.

 |
 |   | PPF  | Returns the pass/fail result for each specified pin of the DC Set. |
 |   | VAL  | Returns for each pin of the DC set the pass/fail result and the measured value.  | |

If the resultMode is not specified for DCRE?, the result mode given to `DCEX`（raw: `02.06.02.02.43_DCEX_-__DC_set_EXecute.md`） is returned.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRE  -  DC set REsult）

Preconditions:

```
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1, pin2, pin3)
DCEX 1, MEAS_VAL
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, VAL
DCRE 1,P, 10.3, (pin1)
DCRE 1,F, 200.1, (pin2)
DCRE 1,P, 20.4, (pin3)
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, GPF
DCRE 1,F,, ()
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, PPF
DCRE 1,P,, (pin1,pin3)
DCRE 1,F,, (pin2)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRE  -  DC set REsult）

Preconditions:

```
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1, pin2, pin3)
DCEX 1, MEAS_VAL
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1,
DCRE 1,P, 10.3, (pin1)
DCRE 1,F, 200.1, (pin2)
DCRE 1,P, 20.4, (pin3)
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, GPF
DCRE 1,F,, ()
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, PPF
DCRE 1,P,, (pin1,pin3)
DCRE 1,F,, (pin2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

DCRM

```
DCRM {map},{mode},[bits],["sub_cycles",] {(port_list)}
```

 DCRM?

```
DCRM? [answer_type,] {map},{(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
DCRM {map},{mode},[bits],[sub_cycles,] {(port)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

| map  | Specifies which error map will be configured. Possible values are: |
 | EMAP  | Detailed Error Map |
 | OVEM  | Overview Error Map |
 | mode  | The meaning of this parameter depends on the map parameter.

- map is set to EMAP:

In this case mode specifies the maximum number of results that are recorded per cycle. The possible values are 1, 2, 4, 6, 8; 6 is only supported by Smart Scale cards. 1 is the default.

Note that not all these values are supported on all hardware types. Furthermore certain of these values are only available with one option of the bits parameter. The details can be found in `Possible combinations of CYRM, CYRP, and DCRM`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.01.02.05_Possible_combinations_of_CYRM__CYRP__and_DCRM.md`）.

The number of results can be reduced with the sub_cycles parameter, but not for mode values of 6 and 8.

- map is set to OVEM:

In this case the mode parameter controls the compression mode and the compression factor. The following values are allowed:

 | FCM  | A fixed number of cycles is combined into one result. The number can be defined by a second call of DCRM, where the number is specified as the mode parameter. |
 | LMAP  | All cycles of one pattern in a (single-port or multi-port) burst are combined into one result. Note that with this option, 8 鈥?nbsp;15 break cycles are inserted between the patterns of the burst. In the error map, 0 .. 7 additional cycles are recorded.Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 | BFLM  | All cycles of one pattern in a (single-port or multi-port) burst are combined into one result. With this option, which is only available for Smart Scale, no break cycles are inserted between the patterns of the burst. Note In BFLM mode, each pattern in the burst must generate 8 or more cycles. |
 | cycles |

The number of cycles to be compressed in FCM mode. It must be divisible by 16.

Note that this number is not affected by a switch to LMAP. If you switch back to FCM the compression factor will be the same as before the switch to LMAP.

The default is 4096.

 |
 |
 | bits  |  Only valid if map is set to EMAP. Specifies how detailed the recorded error code is to be in case of failure. Possible values are: |
 | PF  | Only a one bit Pass/Fail result will be returned. |
 | PFC  | In case of failure, a more detailed two bit code will be recorded. This is the default. |
 | The meaning of the 2 bit error codes depends on the expected result as follows:

 |   | Received |
 | Expected  | L  | I  | H  | U |
 | L  | 00  | 01  | 10  | 11 |
 | I  | 10  | 00  | 01  | 11 |
 | H  | 01  | 10  | 00  | 11 |
 | U  | 01  | 10  | 11  | 00 |

"I" stands for "Intermediate", and "U" stands for "Unstable". Note that you can reconstruct the received result from the expected result and the error code.

 |
 | Note that only one error code format is supported for some result granularities. See `Possible combinations of CYRM, CYRP, and DCRM`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.01.02.05_Possible_combinations_of_CYRM__CYRP__and_DCRM.md`）. |
 | sub_cycles |

This parameter, which is only valid if map is set to EMAP, defines the sub-cycles. The format is

c1: edge_list1 [c2: edge_list2 [c3: edge_list3 [c4: edge_list4]]]

where every edge list is a comma separated list of edge numbers.

The number of sub-cycles must not be larger than the number specified with the mode parameter. A sub-cycle can contain only one edge, numbering gaps are allowed, and the same edge may occur in more than one sub-cycle.

User defined sub-cycle definitions are not supported for all combinations of mode and bits, and some combinations are only supported for certain recording modes and certain hardware types. For details see `Possible combinations of CYRM, CYRP, and DCRM`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.01.02.05_Possible_combinations_of_CYRM__CYRP__and_DCRM.md`）.

The default with mode set to 2 is:

```
"c1:1,2,3,4 c2:5,6,7,8"
```

The default with mode set to 4 is:

```
"c1:1,2 c2:3,4 c3:5,6 c4:7,8"
```

 |
 | port_list  | Specifies the ports for which the recording mode is to be defined. If you specify @@, DCRM will set the recording mode, or return the current settings, for all ports. |
 | answer_type  | This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are: |
 | CONF  | The current configuration is returned. This is the default. |
 | EXEC  | The configuration of the last executed test is returned. |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

```
DCRM EMAP,4,PF,"c1:1,3 c2:5,7 c3:2,4 c4:6,8",(P1,P2)
```

This example configures the detailed Error Map of port `P1` and `P2` to record 1 bit results for 4 sub-cycles, each of which combines two different edges.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

```
DCRM EMAP,1,PFC,(P1,P2)
```

This example configures the Error Map to record one global detailed two bit result combining all edges of a cycle at every test execution.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

```
DCRM OVEM,6000,,(@)
```

This example defines that 6000 cycles will be compressed into one Overview Error Map bit when the next test will be executed.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRP  DCRP  -  Digital Compare Result Positioning）

|

error_map_pos

 |

Specifies the start or stop position for Error Map recording. The interpretation of the value is determined by DCGM independently for both error maps:

- If the current interpretation mode is STRT, the value specifies the first cycle to be recorded. This applies only to the detailed Error Map.
- If the current interpretation mode is HALT, the value specifies the first cycle that will not be recorded any more.
- If the current interpretation mode is NONE, the value can also be specified, but it is ignored until the interpretation mode is changed.

The range of the value must be between 0 and 2^48 - 1

If the value is interpreted as a start (stop) value, recording will start (stop) at the largest multiple of 8 smaller than error_map_pos.

 |
 |

ref_port

 |

This parameter specifies the single port which is used for counting the cycles specified with the error_map_pos parameter. When this reference port has completed the specified number of cycles, cycle recording will be started or stopped for all ports. Note that the reference port must belong to the start label. In particular, you must specify the default @ for single port start labels.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

In the query, you can specify a port list. For the ports that are not used as the reference port, the reply will return the calculated Error Map positions. These are derived from the Error Map position of the reference port and the ratio between the period lengths of the reference port and the other port in the primary timing setup. If you specify @@, DCRM? will return the settings for all ports of the current start label.

 |
 |

answer_type

 |

This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRP  DCRP  -  Digital Compare Result Positioning）

```
> PCLK? "mu_burst",1,(@@)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,20,(P1)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,10,(P2)
> DCGM ALL,STRT,NONE
> DCRP 20,(P2)
> DCRP? (@@)
< DCRP 10,(P1)
< DCRP 20,(P2)
```

This example illustrates the calculation of the cycle numbers for the ports that are not used as the reference port. For interpretation mode STRT, recording will start for the reference port `P2` with cycle 16 (largest multiple of 8 smaller than 20). Since the period length for `P1` is twice the period length of `P2`, recording for `P1` will start with cycle 8 (largest multiple of 8 smaller than 10).

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRP  DCRP  -  Digital Compare Result Positioning）

```
> SQGB STSQ,14,(P2)
> DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE
> DCRP 20,(P2)
> DCRP? (@@)
< DCRP 7,(P1)
< DCRP 14,(P2)
> SQGB STRD,
> DCRP? (@@)
< DCRP 10,(P1)
< DCRP 20,(P2)
```

This example shows that a definition of the Error Map position with DCRP is ignored when the sequencer mode is STSQ, but that it can subsequently be activated. Note that the DCGM command only serves to make the initial ineffectiveness of the definition visible. It is not possible to execute a functional test with these settings when the sequencer mode is STSQ.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRS  -  Digital Compare Result Size）

```
DCRS? [answer_type,] {map},[mode],[bits],{(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
DCRS {map},{x-mode},{bits},{no_of_cycles},{(port)}
```

Parameters
 |

answer_type

 |

This parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |
 |

map

 |

The only allowed value is EMAP (for the detailed error map).

 |
 |

mode

 |

Specifies the level of granularity with which the receive edges of one cycle are recorded. The allowed values are 1, 2, 4, and 8; for Smart Scale, 6 is also possible. If you omit this parameter, the mode set with DCRM is used.

 |
 |

bits

 |

Specifies how detailed the recorded error code is to be in case of failure. If you omit this parameter, the value set with DCRM is used. Possible values are:

 |
 |

PF

 |

Only a one bit Pass/Fail result will be returned. This value is not allowed for Pin Scale cards if mode is set to 1.

 |
 |

PFC

 |

In case of failure, a more detailed two bit code will be returned. PFC is not allowed if mode is set to 8.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

Returns the number of test system cycles that can be stored in the Error Map.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

Specifies the ports for which the capacity of the Error Map is to be returned. If you specify @@, DCRS? will return the capacity for all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRS  -  Digital Compare Result Size）

```
> DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE
> DCRT TP,(P1)
> DCRM EMAP,8,PF,(P1)
> CYRM CYCL,,(P1)
> DCRS? EMAP,,,(P1)
< DCRS EMAP,8,PF,2048,(P1)
> DCRP 3360,(P1)
> FTST?
> EMAP? PPIN,1312,2048,EDGE,8,PF,ALL,BYTE,(P1)
```

This example shows how to get hold of the first cycles of your area of interest under the following conditions:

- The area of interest is greater than the capacity of the error map.
- The acquire mode is set to ALL with DCGM, so that the first recorded cycles will be overwritten when the error map is full before the end of the test.

The solution is to interpret the error map position defined with DCRP as a stop value (by setting the second parameter of DCGM to HALT), and to calculate the last cycle to be recorded as:

```
first_cycle_of_interest + capacity_of_the_Error_Map
```

In the example, the first addend is 1312. The second addend is determined with the DCRS? query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRT  DCRT  -  Digital Compare Result Target）

|

target

 |

Specifies the target area for the error map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

TP

 |

The error map data is stored within the test processor. This is the default.

 |
 |

RAM

 |

The error map data is stored in the external memory as the vector memory.

Note that if you select the external memory as the location of the detailed error map on a P/Ce system, the parallel vector areas must be located in the Sequencer Memory.

 |
 |

port_list

   | Specifies the ports for which the target is to be defined:

- If you specify @@ (all ports, multi-port label), the DCRT command will set the specified target area for all configured ports.
- If you specify @ (all pins, non-multiport label), the DCRT command will set the specified target area for the default port (all pins).
- If you specify the name of a specific port (multi-port label), the DCRT command will set the specified target area for that port only.
 |
 |

answer_type

 |

This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCRT  DCRT  -  Digital Compare Result Target）

### Querying the location of the error map for all ports and setting it for specific ones (multi-port label)

This example queries the location of the error map for all ports. Then, it sets the location of the error map in the test processor for port `P2`, and in RDRAM for `P1`:

```
DCRT? (@@) // Note: this is equivalent to specifying DCRT? CONF,(@@)
DCRT RAM,(P1) // Set location of error map for port P1 in RDRAM
DCRT TP,(P2) // Set location of error map for port P2 in Test Processor
```

### Querying and setting the location of the result map for the default port (non multi-port label)

To query or set the location of the error map for the default port, you need to specify @ as the port_list of the DCRT? and DCRT commands, respectively:

```
DCRT? (@) // Query location of error map for the default port
DCRT TP,(@) // Set location of error map for the default port to Test Processor
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCST  -  DC SeT）

```
DCST? {setNr}
DCST? ALL
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCST  -  DC SeT）

|

setNr

 |

The DC set identification number, starting with 1.

 |
 | ALL  | Selects all available DC sets. |

The query returns the DC set definition with the syntax as described for `DCCH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.40_DCCH_-__DC_Current_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`） and `DCVH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md`）.

### Example 1: Read a specific setup（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCST  -  DC SeT）

Precondition

```
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1, pin3)
DCCH 1,,4000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin2)
DCVH 3,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin4)
DCCH 2,,7000,3000,100,2000,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin5)
```

  Execution

```
Task>  DCST? 1
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1,pin3)
DCCH 1,,4000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin2)
```

  The example works in offline mode for five PS1600 pins.

### Example 2: Read all setups（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCST  -  DC SeT）

Precondition

```
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1, pin3)
DCCH 1,,4000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin2)
DCVH 3,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin4)
DCCH 2,,7000,3000,100,2000,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin5)
```

  Execution

```
Task>  DCST? ALL
DCVH 1,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin1,pin3)
DCCH 1,,4000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin2)
DCCH 2,,7000,3000,100,2000,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin5)
DCVH 3,,20000,200,-100,100,I,25,NTBBM,PAR,(pin4)
```

All defined DC sets are returned. The sort order is defined by the DC set identification number. The example works in offline mode for five PS1600 pins.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCUD -  Device Cycle UnDefine）

```
DCUD {waveform_set},{"dev_cyc_name"},{(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCUD -  Device Cycle UnDefine）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes. Enter ALL for the removal of all device cycles from the device cycle table.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which device cycle definitions are to be deleted. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCUD -  Device Cycle UnDefine）

```
DCUD 1,"WRITE"
```

This example deletes the device cycle `WRITE` for waveform set 1 from the device cycle table.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCVH -  DC Voltage measurement High precision pmu）

```
DCVH {`setNr`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_setNr`）}, `[prechargeVoltage`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_prechargeVoltage`）], `[forceMode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_forceMode`）,] `[forceValue`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_forceValue`）], `[clampValue`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_clampValue`）], `[voltageDrop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_voltageDrop`）,]
            `lowThreshold`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_lowThreshold`）], `[highThreshold`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_highThreshold`）], `[forceRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_forceRange`）,] `[compareMode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_compareMode`）], `[settlingTime`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_settlingTime`）],
            `[clampRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_clampRange`）,] `[relayAction`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_relayAction`）], `[measureVoltageRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_measureVoltageRange`）,] `[executionMode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_executionMode`）],
            `[connectState`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_connectState`）,] `[samples`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_samples`）,] {(`pinList`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_pinList`）)} `, ([refPinList`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_refPinList`）)]
```

Parameters
 | setNr  | The DC set identification number, starting with 1. |
 | prechargeVoltage |

Defines a precharge voltage (in mV).

This is an optional parameter.

 |
 | forceMode  | This extra parameter specifies the force mode:

 |   | I |

Specifies the force current mode.

Parameter forceValue is to be defined in 碌A (Microampere).

This is the default force mode.

 |
 |   | V |

Specifies the force voltage mode.

Parameter forceValue is to be defined in mV (Millivolt).

 |

The force current mode is only supported by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | forceValue |

The force value parameter specifies the force current in 碌A (Microampere) or the force voltage mV (Millivolt).

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The force value is to be specified as current in 碌A (Microampere). |
 |   | V  | The force value is to be specified as voltage in mV (Millivolt). |

The valid range for the force value depends on the hardware.

HPMU force current value: -200mA ... +200mA

 |
 | clampValue |

The optional clamp value parameter specifies the output clamp voltage in mV (Millivolt) or the output clamp current in 碌A (Microampere).

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I |

The clamp value is to be specified as output clamp voltage in mV (Millivolt).

This is the default mode.

 |
 |   | V  | The clamp value is to be specified as output clamp current in 碌A (Microampere). |

The parameter may be defined as floating-point number or as string.

The string format supports different values for the upper (or positive) clamp value and the lower (or negative) clamp value.

The string must be defined with pairs of properties and values in the format "property1:value1 property2:value2 ...":

 | Property  | Value type  | Description |
 | lowLimit  | float  | The lower (or negative) clamp value. The value must be less than 0.0. |
 | highLimit  | float  | The upper (or positive) clamp value. The value must be higher than 0.0. |

In the query answer the lower clamp value is returned only if it is not symmetrical to the upper clamp value.

Example:

`...,"lowLimit:-2000 highLimit:15000",...`

The valid range for the clamp value depends on the hardware.

HPMU clamp voltage value: -5V ... +8V

 |
 | voltageDrop  |  The extra parameter specifies the following values:

- Maximum allowed force voltage in mV (Millivolt)
- Maximum allowed return voltage drop in mV (Millivolt)
- Warning threshold for force/return voltage drop in mV (Millivolt)
- Delay time before a current clamp alarm is raised in ms (Millisecond)
- Delay time before a disconnect is performed, after the clamp current is reached in ms (Millisecond)

The extra parameter is to be defined as string and is supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

The string format supports different values for the force drop and for the return drop.

The string must be defined with pairs of properties and values in the format "property1:value1 property2:value2":

 | Property  | Value type  | Description |
 | forceDrop  | integer |

The maximum voltage drop on the force line or return line in mV (Millivolt).

For the specification, refer to `Voltage drop protection / measurement`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.05.03.07_XPS256_other_performance_characteristics.md#_350739__s_Voltage_drop_protection`） in `XPS256 other performance characteristics`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.05.03.07_XPS256_other_performance_characteristics.md`）.

The programmable range is 0.0 鈥?nbsp;1.0 V for the force line and for the return line but, the total for the two lines must not exceed 1.0 V.

The related power supply bits are set if the limits are hit: Bit 6 (Voltage drop force) or bit 7 (Voltage drop return). For more information, refer to `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`）.

For a maximum voltage drop > 0.5 V, the OPEN_LOOP_PROT property of the `connectState`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_connectState`） parameter must be set to OFF and in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`） the `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON.

 |
 | returnDrop  | integer |
 | warnForceDrop  | integer |

The warning levels for the voltage drop on the force line or return line in mV (Millivolt).

The related power supply bits are set if the limits are hit: bit 15 (Voltage drop force warning) or bit 16 (Voltage drop return warning). For more information, refer to `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`） |
 | warnReturnDrop |
 | currClampTimeToAlarm  | integer  | Specifies the delay time before an alarm is raised or a disconnect is performed, after the clamp current is reached.

Unit is milliseconds.

 |
 | currClampTimeToDisconnect  | integer |

Example:

`...,"forceDrop:5000 returnDrop:4000",...`

 |
 | lowThreshold |

The low threshold is used for evaluating the Pass/Fail result. It is specified in mV.

 |
 | highThreshold |

The high threshold is used for evaluating the Pass/Fail result. It is specified in mV.

 |
 | forceRange |

This extra parameter specifies the force range.

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The force current range is to be specified in 碌A (Microampere). |
 |   | V  | The force voltage range is to be specified in mV (Millivolt).  | |
 | compareMode |

This optional string parameter defines how the measured value is compared against the lowThreshold and the highThreshold.

The parameter may be defined as follows:

 | Value  | Mode  | Description |
 | L  | Low  | The Pass/Fail result is set to PASS if the measured value is lower than the lowThreshold. |
 | H  | High  | The Pass/Fail result is set to PASS if the measured value is higher than the highThreshold. |
 | I  | Intermediate  | The Pass/Fail result is set to PASS if the measured value is between lowThreshold and highThreshold.  | |
 | settlingTime |

The settling time specifies the additional time between the setup and the measurement being performed.

The valid range is 0 ms to 2000 ms. The specified settling time is added to the internal settling time of the test system.

 |
 | clampRange |

This extra parameter specifies the clamp range.

The type and unit of the value depends on the value of the forceMode parameter:

 |   | I  | The clamp voltage range is to be specified in mV (Millivolt). |
 |   | V  | The clamp current range is to be specified in 碌A (Microampere).  | |
 | relayAction  | This parameter defines the termination mode of the measurement. The mode can be:

 |   | NTBBM |

No-Termination-Break-Before-Measure.

Relay action:

- For digital DC pins:

Non-terminated measurement: Causes all pins in the pin list to be disconnected from the pin electronics (AC relay open).

 |
 |   | NTMBB |

No-Termination-Measure-Before-Break.

Relay action:

- For digital DC pins:

Non-terminated measurement: Causes all pins in the pin list to be disconnected from the pin electronics (AC relay open). Relay switching order is changed to MBB.

 |
 |   | TERM  | Relay action:

- For digital DC pins:

Terminated Measurement: Causes all pins in the pin list, which are already connected to the pin electronics (AC relay closed) to remain connected during measurement. The state of the AC relay is not changed.

 |
 |   | NO |

NO relay action: No relays are switched during the measurement.

 |
 |   | NT |

Not terminated.

- For DC Scale pins:

Supported only in PMU operating mode. For more information, see `SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay()`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.234.01.28_SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay.md`）.

 |

See also `SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay()`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.234.01.28_SPMU_PIN_TASK.relay.md`）.

 |
 | measureVoltageRange  | This extra parameter defines voltage measurement range. |
 | executionMode |

Measurements belonging to the same DC Set must have the same execution mode. The measurement defined first defines the execution mode of the DC set:

 |   | SER  | Serial measurement (all pins of a site are measured sequentially). |
 |   | SER_HAC |

Serial measurement with high accuracy force current (all pins of a site are measured sequentially).

This execution mode cannot be used for ganged channels.

 |
 |   | PAR  | Parallel measurement (clock board parallel measurement). |
 |   | PAR_HAC |

Parallel measurement with high accuracy force current (all pins are measured in parallel).

This execution mode cannot be used for ganged channels.

 |
 |   | PAR_UNG  | Parallel measurement (clock board parallel measurement). Ganged channels are unganged during the measurement as far as possible.

Only supported for DC Scale channels in PMU mode. Ignored for unganged channels.

 |
 |   | HIZ  | High impedance measurement. Supported for DC Scale channels in PMU mode, and digital DC pins. |
 |   | HV_PPMU_BADC_VAL  | The measurement is set up using the pin PMU and performed using the board ADC.

This mode is currently not supported.

 |
 |   | HV_PPMU_GPF  | A global pass/fail measurement is performed using the pin PMU (not the system PMU).

This mode is currently not supported.

 |
 |   | HV_PPMU_PPF  | A pass/fail measurement for each pin is performed using the pin PMU (not the system PMU).

This mode is currently not supported.

  | |
 | connectState |

The combination of the parameters executionMode and connectState defines the behavior of the selected channel.

This parameter must be defined as string, containing pairs of properties and values in the format "property1:value1 property2:value2 ...".

 | Property  | Value  | Description |
 |   | |

An empty string defines the normal mode.

This is the default value.

 |
 | KELVIN_FORCE |

ON

OFF

   | Selects a measurement of the voltage drop on the force (HF#) line.

Default property is OFF.

Supported only by the HC variant of DPS128 and by XPS256.

For more information on DPS128 kelvin measurements, refer to `Voltage drop measurement`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01.03_DPS128____PS64_functionality_and_features.md#_140638__s_Voltage_drop_measurement`） in `DPS128鈥?鈥奃PS64 functionality and features`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01.03_DPS128____PS64_functionality_and_features.md`）.

 |
 | KELVIN_RETURN |

ON

OFF

   | Selects a measurement of the voltage drop on the return (LF#) line.

Default property is OFF.

Supported only by the HC variant of DPS128 and by XPS256.

For more information on DPS128-HC kelvin measurements, refer to `Voltage drop measurement`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01.03_DPS128____PS64_functionality_and_features.md#_140638__s_Voltage_drop_measurement`） in `DPS128鈥?鈥奃PS64 functionality and features`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01.03_DPS128____PS64_functionality_and_features.md`）.

For more information on XPS256 kelvin measurements, refer to `XPS256 programming - Kelvin test / sense connection test`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.12_XPS256_programming_-_Kelvin_test___sense_connection_test.md`）.

 |
 | SAFE_CON |

ON

OFF

 |

Enables or disables the Smart Connect feature: The voltage at the DUT is sensed and the PMU is automatically set to the measured voltage before a channel is connected.

Default property is OFF.

Supported only by XPS256.

Note: Parameter prechargeVoltage will be ignored if the Smart Connect is enabled.

 |
 | OPEN_LOOP_PROT  | ON

OFF

 |

The property selects the internal connection from the force output line (P# pin) and the high sense output line (PS# pin).

One of the following specifiers can be set:

- ON

The internal connection is made via two anti-parallel diodes.

This is the default state if the property is not defined.

This is the recommended setting if both the forceDrop propery and the returnDrop property of the `voltageDrop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_voltageDrop`） parameter are set to a value < 0.5 V.

- OFF

The internal connection is open. The output stage no longer has any feedback if the force to sense connection on the DUT or the DUT board is (unintentionally) open.

The following rules apply to this option:

  - The `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`）.
  - This is the required setting if the forceDrop propery or the returnDrop property of the `voltageDrop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.52_DCVH_-__DC_Voltage_measurement_High_precision_pmu.md#_98530__r_voltageDrop`） parameter is set to a value 鈮?nbsp;0.5 V.

See also `XPS256 programming - Voltage drop measurement`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.19_XPS256_programming_-_Voltage_drop_measurement.md`）. |
 | PULLDOWN  | ON

OFF

 |

Enables/disables the pulldown resistor at disconnect.

Default property is ON.

Supported only by XPS256.

 |
 | HIGH_ACCURACY  | ON |

Enables usage of High Accuracy mode if possible. If this connection state is defined, the setup can use the 1.5V high accuracy range, see `XPS256 measure voltages`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.06.02_XPS256_measure_voltages.md`）. If HIGH_ACCURACY is specified in a setup but the license is missing, an error message will be generated.

Supported only by XPS256.

 |

Example:

`...,"SAFE_CON:ON",...`

Instruments that do not support the parameter connectState will show an error when a pin or pin group is used without an XPS256 pin.

Some restrictions must be respected for the combinations of the parameters:

- The combination of executionMode = HIZ and (connectState = SENSE_ONLY:ON or KELVIN_REVERSE:ON or SAFE_CON:ON) is not supported.
- The combination connectState = SAFE_CON:ON and (connectState = SENSE_ONLY:ON or KELVIN_REVERSE:ON or FORCE_ONLY:ON) is not supported.
 |
 | samples |

The number of samples must be a power of 2 (2n).

This limitation does not apply for XPS256.

 |
 | pinList |

The previously defined parameters are applied to all pins, which are specified with the pinList parameter. If more than one pin is specified, pin names must be separated by commas. pinList can contain pins configured as O, I, IO, or DC pin types.

 |
 | refPinList |

Some connection states (HC_AWG, DIFF_VM) require a reference pin. This extra parameter defines a single pin or a list of pins that are used as reference pin for the pins defined by pinList.

The reference pin defines always the low force or low sense pin(s). These pins are the LF pin of the floating high-current unit or the LS pin of the differential voltmeter.

Each pin in the refPinList corresponds to a pin in the pinList. Both lists must have the same number of pins defined. The first pin in refPinList belongs to the first pin in pinList.

The refPinList cannot be defined if pinList defines all pins or more than the half of the available pins that support a reference pin based connection state.

A "single-ended" connection mode will be selected if refPinList is omitted and no reference pin is defined: The low force pin and the low sense pin of the floating resource are connected to the common ground and the channel specific ground sense input.

The reference pin is currently not supported.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCVH -  DC Voltage measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCVH 1,,1,1000,4820,5180,i,0,no,ser,(pin1, pin2, pin3)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, MEAS_VAL
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 1, VAL
DCRE P, 4903.3, (pin1)
DCRE F, 200.1, (pin2)
DCRE P, 5108.4, (pin3)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCVH -  DC Voltage measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCVH 2,,,,100,200,i,0,TERM,HIZ,(pin1)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 2, MEAS_VAL
```

Result:

```
DCRE? 2, VAL
DCRE F, 4903.3, (pin1)
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCVH -  DC Voltage measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCVH 1,,I,200000,"lowLimit:-1000 highLimit:5000",-500,4700,I,0,NT,PAR,"DIFF_VM:ON",(pin1, pin2),(refPin1,refPin2)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, FORCE_ON
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DCVH -  DC Voltage measurement High precision pmu）

Precondition:

```
DCVH 1,,V,10000,"lowLimit:-100000 highLimit:200000",-500,9000,I,0,NT,PAR,(pin1, pin2)
```

Execution:

```
DCEX 1, FORCE_ON
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DDIC  DDIC  -  Define DUT Interface Connection）

|

connectionSet

 |

This parameter is currently not used.

This extra string parameter adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC Scale channel in PMU mode. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as single pin or in ganging groups. Note: The documentation for supported DC Scale cards knows this feature also as "Ganging on the fly".

Default connection set: The default connection set is defined if this extra parameter is not used or if an empty string is programmed. A DC Scale pin can be defined in only one default connection set.

It's possible to specify several DDIC commands which differ in the name parameter, but have identical (cp1, cp2) combination.

 |
 |

circuitry_type

 |

The following circuitry types are supported:

 |
 |

CONN

 |

A simple direct connection between the given pogo pins.

Two pogo pins on one or two DC Scale cards (UHC4T) must be given: One GANG_IN (pppGI) pogo and one GANG_OUT pogo (pppGO).

 |
 |

CLR

 |

Clears all previously defined circuitry.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Only for queries:

Returns all previously defined circuitry.

 |
 |

cp1,cp2

 |

The parameters define the ganging or stacking connections:

- Format pppxx defines a pogo block and a ganging connection.

Only pogo pin in/out pairs are allowed as connection points.

 |
 |

ppp

 |

The three digits specify the pogo block number.

 |
 |

xx

 |

Alpha numeric code for specifying the ganging connections:

 |
 |

GO

 |

Ganging Output

 |
 |

GI

 |

Ganging Input

 |
 | cc  | The two digits define the channel number from 01 to 16. |
 | -  | Low force (LF#) / Return of the upper channel |
 | +  | High force (HF#) / Force of the lower channel |
 |  CAUTION "Upper channel" in this context means towards the DUT while the "lower channel" means towards a stable reference like ground or the supply voltage of the DUT. This applies to both positive and negative voltages. |

### Example 1: Ganging（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DDIC  DDIC  -  Define DUT Interface Connection）

```
DDIC CONN, (207GO,209GI)
DDIC? ALL
```

returns

```
DDIC CONN, (207GO,209GI)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DELI -  DELete Instruction）

```
DELI {cmd_No}, {count}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DELI -  DELete Instruction）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number which references the first sequencer instruction to be deleted.

 |
 |

count

 |

This parameter defines the total number of instructions to be deleted.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DELI -  DELete Instruction）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,27,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,7,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,544,,,(@)
< ...
> DELI 2,1
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,7,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,544,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example deletes the sequencer instruction with command number 2 from the sequencer area of the default port @. Note that since the vectors of the instruction are not deleted, the start address of the following label (STVA instruction at command number 4) does not change.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DELV -  DELete Vectors）

```
DELV {cmd_No}, {vect_length}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DELV -  DELete Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number which references the sequencer construct where vectors are to be deleted. The instruction of the construct must be GENV (GENerate Vectors) or RPTV (RePeaT Vectors)

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The number of active vectors to be deleted at the end of the referenced sequencer construct.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DELV -  DELete Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,34,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,544,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> DELV 2,25
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,520,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
```

This example deletes 25 vectors from the end of the sequencer construct referenced by command number 2. Three memory words become inactive in the process and are deleted. The start address of the following label (command line 4) is adjusted.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFCR  DFCR  -  DeFine Clock Routing）

|

source_group

 |

specifies the hardware group whose local clock is to be routed to dest_group. The format is Gx, where x is the group number.

 |
 |

dest_group

 |

specifies the hardware group whose inherited clock is to be changed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFCR  DFCR  -  DeFine Clock Routing）

```
> DFCR?
<
> DFCR G1,G8
> DFCR?
< DFCR G4,G3
< DFCR G4,G1
< DFCR G4,G5
< DFCR G1,G6
< DFCR G1,G2
< DFCR G1,G8
< DFCR G1,G7
```

This example changes the default routing (DFCR? gives an empty reply). Note that the inherited clocks of G6 and of all successors of G6 are also changed.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFCT -  DeFine Continuity Test）

|

force_current

 |

The force_current parameter specifies the current (in [micro ]A) that the active load sources or sinks. The range is 0 to 35 mA for the Pin Scale 800 and P-/Ce- channel boards. The direction of the current is determined by the polarity of the commutation voltage and the pass range.

 |
 |

commutation_voltage

 |

This parameter defines the commutation voltage (in mV) that the active load requires to source/sink the force_current. For the Pin Scale 800, the range is -1.5 V to 5.5 V. For the P-/Ce-channel boards, the range is -2 V to +6 V.

 |

 |

pass_volt_min

 |

This parameter specifies (in mV) the minimum pass value of the test. It defines the low level threshold for the comparator during the measurement.

 |
 |

pass_volt_max

 |

This parameter specifies (in mV) the maximum pass value of the test. It defines the high level threshold for the comparator during the measurement.

   | Note If pass_volt_min > pass_volt_max, the two parameters are swapped around internally.

 |

polarity

 |

The polarity is as follows:

 |
 |

SPOL

 |

Selecting the SPOL (single polarity) option causes the measurement to be taken with the specified polarity. The specified polarities are set for the commutation voltage and the pass limits.

 |
 |

BPOL

 |

Selecting the BPOL (both polarities) option causes measurements to be taken with both polarities; a pass result is returned if the pin passes the test in both directions.

For using this option, the range of commutation_voltage is -1.5 V to +1.5 V for the Pin Scale 800, and -2 V to +2 V for the P-/Ce-channel boards.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The parameters defined by the DFCT command are applied to all the pins named in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pinlist can contain pins configured as O, I, IO, or DC pin types. The @ character can be used to specify all relevant pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFCT -  DeFine Continuity Test）

```
DFCT 10000,1700,200,700,SPOL,(p1,p2,p3,p4)
CTST? GPF
```

This example sets up the parameters needed to execute a continuity test on pins `p1` to `p4`. The parameters are as follows:

-  Force current = 10 mA
-  Commutation voltage = 1.7 V
-  Voltage minimum pass value = 200 mV
-  Voltage maximum pass value = 700 mV
-  Single polarity measurement selected

The example also includes the CTST? (Continuity TeST) query used to execute the test.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFGE  DFGE  -  DeFine Group by Expressions）

|

group_type

 |

Defines the type of pins in the group. This can be:

 |
 |

I

 |

Identifies a group of device input pins.

 |
 |

O

 |

Identifies a group of device output pins.

 |
 |

IO

 |

Identifies a group of bidirectional pins.

 |
 |

DC

 |

Identifies a group of DC type pins.

 |
 |

group_expression

 |

The expression that describes the pins to be included in the group. The expression must be built up from pin or pin group names which serve as arguments for the following operators:

 |
 |

 |

+

 |

returns the union of its arguments, that is, all pins that are contained in one of its arguments.

 |
 |

 |

*

 |

returns the intersection of its arguments, that is, all pins that are contained in both of its arguments.

 |
 |

 |

-

 |

returns the difference of its arguments, that is, all pins that are contained in the first argument, but not in the second.

 |
 |

 |

You can also use parentheses to force a certain processing order.

 |
 |

pin_group

 |

The name assigned to the pin group. You can use the same name for groups of different type.

The symbol @ can be used with the DFGE? query to list all groups previously defined using the DFGP and DFGE command. If you query a non-existent group, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFGE  DFGE  -  DeFine Group by Expressions）

```
> DFGP? (SCAN)
< DFGP X,(SI1,SI2,SO1,SO2),(SCAN)
> DFGP? (OUT)
< DFGP O,(O1,SO1,SO2),(OUT)
> DFGE O,"SCAN * OUT",(SCAN_OUT)
> DFGE? (SCAN_OUT)
< DFGE O,"SCAN * OUT",(SCAN_OUT)
> DFGP? (SCAN_OUT)
< DFGP O,(SO1,SO2),(SCAN_OUT)
```

This example defines a group called SCAN_OUT which contains the pins that occur both in pin groups OUT and SCAN. Note that you must use the DFGP? query to display the pins of SCAN_OUT. DFGE? returns the group definition.

The same result would be obtained with the definition

```
> DFGE O,"OUT - O1",(SCAN_OUT)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFGP  DFGP  -  DeFine GrouP）

|

pin_type

 |

Defines the type of pins in the group. This can be:

 |
 |

I

 |

Identifies a group of device input pins.

 |
 |

O

 |

Identifies a group of device output pins.

 |
 |

DC

 |

Identifies a group of DC type pins.

 |
 |

X

 |

Identifies a group that may contain pins of any type.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The names of the pins to be included in the group. All pin names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

pin_group

 |

The name assigned to the pin group. You can use the same name for groups of different type.

The symbol @ can be used with the DFGP? query to list all groups previously defined using the DFGP command. If you query a non-existent group, the system returns nothing.

Maximum number of characters is 16 for 32-bit SmarTest and 64 for 64-bit SmarTest.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFGP  DFGP  -  DeFine GrouP）

```
DFGP O,(Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3),(outputs)
```

This example defines a group called outputs which contains pins Q0, Q1, Q2 and Q3.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

| resourceSpecifier |

The extra parameter specifies the resource to be set or queried.

The following resources are supported:

 | Resource specifier  | Description |
 | VIL and VIH  | Input (drive) voltage definition for I and I/O pins. |
 | VIHH  | High voltage level definition for I and I/O pins. |
 | VOL and VOH  | Output threshold voltage definition for O and I/O pins. |
 | VOL_DIFF and VOH_DIFF  | Output threshold voltage definition for O and I/O pins in differential mode. |
 | VT  | Termination voltage definition. |
 | VCOM  | Commutation voltage of the active load. |
 | REC_SWING  | The receiver swing for a differential comparator. |
 | REC_OFFSET  | The receiver offset for a differential comparator. |
 | ALL  | Keyword ALL selects all resources.  | |
 | mode |

The extra parameter specifies for which operation mode parameter value should be applied or queried.

Supported operation modes:

- STD
- ALL

Keyword ALL selects all operating modes.

Extra parameter resourceSpecifier must also be defined if mode is specified.

If the parameter is not defined, mode STD is taken as default value. In this case the specified value is applied to STD values only and default values used in STDDIFF mode will not be affected.

Note: There is an exception when setting parameter value to RESET. In this case, an omitted mode parameter will be counted as ALL.

 |
 | value |

The mandatory parameter defines the default value for the selected resource and operating mode.

 This parameter is to be defined as

- voltage (in mV) or
- as keyword RESET.

With the parameter set to RESET, the affected values will be set to the system-defined default values of the selected cmos or ecl device technology.

 |

### Example 1: Resource and mode specified（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV VIL,STD,100

```

This example sets the default value for the VIL resource in STD mode to 100 mV. Other default values are not modified.

### Example 2: Resource specified, mode omitted（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV VIL,100
DFLV VIH,200
```

This example sets the default value for the VIL resource to 100 mV, and VIH to 200 mV. As no operating mode is specified, the values are applied only for the STD mode.

### Example 3: Reset single resource（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV VIL, RESET
```

Sets the default value for the VIL resources to the technology defined default value for all operating modes. This overwrites potential user-defined values by the initial system value.

### Example 4: Reset all default values to the technology defined values and query all values（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV RESET
DFLV? ALL, ALL
```

returns

```
DFLV VIL,STD,2250
DFLV VIH,STD,2500
DFLV VIHH,STD,0
DFLV VOL,STD,2250
DFLV VOH,STD,2500
DFLV VOL_DIFF,STD,0
DFLV VOH_DIFF,STD,0
DFLV VT,STD,2500
DFLV VCOM,STD,2500
DFLV REC_OFFSET,STD,1200
DFLV REC_SWING,STD,3200
```

for the cmos technology.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPC  DFPC  -  DeFine Pin Comment）

|

pin

 |

In the command, this is the pin to which a comment is to be added. In the query reply, it is the pin whose comment is returned.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

A query parameter that specifies the pins for which the comments are to be returned. You can also specify @ for all configured pins.

Pins for which no comments have been defined are ignored.

 |
 |

comment

 |

The comment to the pin. The maximal length of the comment string is 2048 characters.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPC  DFPC  -  DeFine Pin Comment）

```
> DFPC (pin1), "This is a comment to pin1"
> DFPC? (pin1,pin2)
< DFPC (pin1), "This is a comment to pin1"
```

Since no comment has been defined for pin `pin2`, it is ignored in the reply.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPN  DFPN  -  DeFine Pin Name）

|

connectionSet

 |

This parameter is currently not used.

This extra string parameter adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC Scale channel in PMU mode. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as single pin or in ganging groups. Note: The documentation for supported DC Scale cards knows this feature also as "Ganging on the fly".

Default connection set: The default connection set is defined if this extra parameter is not used or if an empty string is programmed. A DC Scale pin can be defined in only one default connection set.

All traces that are needed for a cross-card ganging group and are defined by the `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`） command and the DFPN command must have the same connectionSet defined. Recommendation: If the DUT trace can be activated by utility lines, name it like the utility line (see DFUP command).

There can be several pin definitions containing the same channel:

Adding a different ganging combination (new pin), does not invalidate the setups for the existing pins.

The different pins containing the same channel must be part of the same ports.

The patterns, events and DC-setups of these pins do not overlap.

 |
 | channelNo_1 |

The test system channel number of the channel to which the specified device pin is connected (five digits), or the utility block number of the specified card cage (three digit).

Digital or DC Scale channel

For a digital channel this is a five digit number. The first three digits specify the pogo block number, and the fourth and fifth digits specify the pin number in the pogo block. The first digit is 1 to 4, the second and third digits is 01 to 32, and the final two digits is 01 to 16. For example, 10105 is the digital channel whose pogo pin number is 05 in the pogo block 101.

Each pogo block contains 16 digital channels. The pogo block numbers are determined by the slots in which the channel boards are installed.

The first three digits are also called the board number of the logical channel board, and the last two digits are a channel number in the logical channel board, where each logical channel board contains 16 channels

Utility DC channel

For the utility DC pins, this is a three digit number, specifying the utility block of the card cage. The referenced utility pogo must be one which can be connected to the DC rail of the card-cage. To get the utility block number, add 164 (264 for the second utility line card on EXA Scale test systems) to the desired utility line block, such that for example utility block 4 has number 168. For compatibility with SmarTest 7.6x, "HPMU1" now maps to "UTIDC165" and so on (for Smart Scale test systems only).

For more information, see subtopics in `Pogo pin assignment - Utility pogo blocks`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08_Pogo_pin_assignment_-_Utility_pogo_blocks.md`）.

The hardware knows 4 Utility DC channels (pogo pins): DC-force, DC-sense, ground-sense, and guard. But because they are referenced as a group, one pin name is sufficient to reflect all 4 channels.

 |
 |

DC_channel_list

 |

You can define ganging for a set of DC Scale channels in PMU mode by specifying a list of DC Scale channels, separated by commas and enclosed by parentheses. The channels must be physically adjacent on the same board.

Before cross-card ganging can be used, the connection must be enabled by command `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`）.

 |
 |

pinNo

 |

This is the device pin number which is allocated to the specified channel. The number must be enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

pinName

 |

The name to be allocated to the pin. Maximum number of characters is 16 for 32-bit SmarTest and 64 for 64-bit SmarTest.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This query parameter specifies the pins whose definitions are to be retrieved. The symbol @ can be used with the DFPN? query to list all pins previously defined by the DFPN command. If a list of more than one pin is required, the pin names must be separated by a comma. If you query a non-existent pin, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPN  DFPN  -  DeFine Pin Name）

```
> DFPN 10101,"1",(Clock)
> DFPN 10102,"2",(D0)
> DFPN? (@)
< DFPN 10101,"1",(Clock)
< DFPN 10102,"2",(CD0)
```

The above example allocates the `Clock` pin to channel 10101 and allocates pin `D0` to channel 10102, and then queries these definitions. The device pin numbers allocated are 1 and 2 respectively.

```
DFPN (11901, 11902),,(vee)
```

This example defines ganging for DC Scale channels in PMU mode.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

|

alias_set_name

 |

The alias set name.

If you assign a pair of pin alias and package pin name to a nonexistent alias set, an alias set is created named with this parameter.

In the query, you can define multiple alias sets or use the symbol @ to list all the defined pin alias sets.

 |
 |

pin_alias

 |

The pin alias.

 |
 |

package_pin_name

 |

The package pin name.

 |
 |

DEF|ALL

 |

If you select `ALL` in the query, for the pins without aliases, the package pin names are returned.

If `DEF` is chosen in the query, only the defined pin aliases are returned.

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

### Generic case

The pin configuration file includes three pins: `CP`, `S0`, and `S1`. There are two alias sets, `FUNC` and `TRANS.`

FUNC

 |

Alias

 |

Pin

 |
 |

CLK

 |

CP

 |

TRANS

 |

Alias

 |

Pin

 |
 |

Read

 |

S0

 |
 |

Write

 |

S1

 |

The following examples are the operations of these sets.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

```
DFPR? DEF,(@)
```

returns

```
DFPR "FUNC","CLK",(CP)
DFPR "TRANS","Read",(S0)
DFPR "TRANS","Write",(S1)
```

This example returns the names of all defined alias sets together with their defined pin aliases. This query will not return the pins without aliases.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

```
DFPR? ALL,(FUNC,TRANS)
```

returns

```
DFPR "FUNC","CLK",(CP)
DFPR "FUNC", "S0",(S0)
DFPR "FUNC", "S1",(S1)
DFPR "TRANS","CP",(CP)
DFPR "TRANS","Read",(S0)
DFPR "TRANS","Write",(S1)
```

This example returns the pin aliases for all pins in the alias sets `FUNC` and `TRANS`. For the pins without aliases, the package pin names are returned.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

```
DFPR? DEF,(TRANS)
```

returns

```
DFPR "TRANS","Read",(S0)
DFPR "TRANS","Write",(S1)
```

This example returns the defined pin aliases in the alias set `TRANS`. This query will not return the pins without aliases.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

```
DFPR? DEF,(FUNC::CLK)
```

returns

```
DFPR "FUNC","CLK",(CP)
```

This example returns the package pin name `CP` which is related to the pin alias `CLK` in the alias set `FUNC`.

### Example 5（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPR  DFPR  -  DeFine Pin Role）

```
DFPR "TRANS","CLK",(CP)
```

This example adds the package pin `CP` and its alias `CLK` to the alias set `TRANS`. Now the alias set `TRANS` is as the following.

Alias

 |

Pin

Read

S0

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

|

dps_channel

 |

The test system channel number of the DPS channel to be configured.

The channel is to be defined as follows:

- For `external device power supplies`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.06_External_device_power_supply__external_GPIB_DPS.md`）, this is a three鈥慸igit or four鈥慸igit integer.

The first one or two digits define an external supply. To avoid a conflict with the internal supplies, we recommend using values above 8. The maximum supported value is 16.

The last two digits define the channel number of the DPS. If the channel number is less than 10, a leading "0" must be used.

-

For DC Scale channels (in DPS mode) this is a five digit number in the same format as for digital I/O channels.

 |
 |

DC_scale_channel_list

 |

To gang DC Scale channels, you must specify a consecutive number of channels enclosed by parentheses, either as comma separated list or as range, for example 10105-10106.

- DPS128/64: Ganging is possible for any number of successive channels within a card, but not across cards.

DPS128/DPS64 channels must be of the same type (HC or HV).

The maximum number of ganging groups per DPS128/64 is half the number of channels. The maximum current per card cannot be exceeded.

- XPS256: Only channels on the same HLA can be ganged.
- UHC4, UHC4T: For UHC4 or UHC4T ganging is possible for any number of successive channels within a card and any number of cards within a test head. The combination of UHC4 and UHC4T within the same ganging group is not supported. The maximum current per card cannot be exceeded.

Before cross-card ganging can be used, the connection must be enabled by command `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`）.

 |
 |

polarity

 |

Gives the polarity of the DPS which has to be applied to the selected channel.

 |
 |

POS

 |

Enter POS only if the DPS connections on the DUT board are as follows: The force is connected to power; the sink is connected to ground. The voltage supplied to the device will then be exactly as entered in the Level Setup, but the entry made there must be positive, otherwise the system returns an error.

For DC scale channels, only POS is allowed.

 |
 |

NEG

 |

NEG is not allowed for DC Scale channels.

 |
 |

pin

 |

Defines the pin name for the DPS channel.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names of those power supply outputs which have already been defined. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured power supply pins.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DFPS 11,POS,(Vee)
```

This example connects device pin Vee to channel 1 of DPS board 1. The DPS output polarity is positive.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

|

```
DFPS (10101, 10102),POS,(vee)
```

 |
 |

```
DFPS (10101-10102),POS,(vee)
```

 |

Both lines define the same master/slave configuration for DC Scale channels in DPS mode. They just use different notations. Note the five digit channel numbers.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DDIC CONN, (104GO, 105GI)
DFPS (10403, 10404, 10501, 10502),POS,(vee)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale UHC4 channels in DPS mode across two boards.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DDIC CONN, (104GO, 105GI, 105GO, 106GI)
DFPS (10403, 10404, 10502, 10503, 10504, 10601),POS,(vee)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale UHC4 channels in DPS mode across three boards.

### Example 5（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DDIC CONN,(230GO, 227GI)
DFPS (23004, 22701),POS,(VDDCI)
```

This example specifies the ganging of channels across two DC Scale UHC4 cards.

|

pinlist

 |

Pin name or names. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to refer to all configured pins. The pin list can contain digital or DC Scale pins, or a combination of both.

 |
 |

port

 |

The name of the port to which the pins are associated. The maximum number of characters is 16 for 32-bit SmarTest and 64 for 64-bit SmarTest.

 |

portlist

Q0_1,S1_1,S0_1,_MR_1),(port_1)
DFPT (CP_2,DS7_2,DS0_2,I/O7_2,...,I/O0_2,Q7_2,
