### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFSP  DFSP  -  DeFine Sampling Profile）

| meas_resource  | The measurement resource. It can be:

- PMU - The default value
 |
 | measure_type  | The measurement type. It can be:

- VOLT - for voltage measurements, or
- CURR - for current measurements.
 |
 | measure_range  | This parameter corresponds to the voltage/current measure range. |
 | sampling_rate  | Specifies the sampling rate in microseconds. |
 | average_factor  | The number of measurements per sample. |
 | keep_range  | Specifies whether the range used by current profiling should be kept. Default is to restore last measure range before doing the profiling. |
 | pinlist  | This parameter specifies the pins to be used for the measurements. |

### Example 1: Current measurements（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFSP  DFSP  -  DeFine Sampling Profile）


or

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFTD  DFTD   DeFine Test Data）

| testdata_name |

A mandatory name that identifies a collection of test data elements (td).

If the collection contains DC sets, the name is freely definable. Note that all test data elements that are to be used with one label (as defined with the TPSE command) must belong to the same collection.

If the collection contains DC waveforms, the name must be the name of the sub-pattern by which the DC waveforms are to be executed.

 |   | ALL  | Returns all test data collections (only in the query).  | |
 | edit_mode |

The mandatory parameter specifies the editing mode for the test data elements.

 |   | REPLACE  | Replaces all existing td elements with the new definitions. |
 |   | UPDATE |

Modifies operation elements of existing td elements, or adds new operation elements to an existing td element.

Note the UPDATE mode is restricted for DC waveforms: their vectorDistance attribute, and also the number of values of their values attribute cannot be modified.

 |
 |   | INSERT |

Defines additional td elements. Existing td elements remain unchanged.

 |
 |   | DELETE  | Removes all specified td elements.  |  The DFTD? query responds with UPDATE if an element_id was specified, otherwise it responds with REPLACE. |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory parameter defines the pin or pins on which this command is applied. To specify multiple pins, separate the names with a comma, or use @ to specify all pins. You can also use pin groups.

If the collection contains DC sets, only pins that are associated with DC Scale channels are taken into account.

If the collection contains DC waveforms all pins must be digital pins. If this requirement is not satisfied, DFTD will issue an error message. Furthermore, the specified pins must be exactly the pins that belong to the port of the sub-pattern specified as testdata_name.

 |
 | category |

The mandatory parameter is for queries only. The admitted values are:

 |   | ALL  | returns all elements of all categories. |
 |   | LEV  | returns all elements of all types within the LEV category. The possible types are dcset and dcWaveform.  | |
 | element_id |

The mandatory parameter selects a test data element that is to be returned by the query. This parameter does not occur in the command because it corresponds to the id attribute of the td element (see the #spec(data) parameter).

 |
 | ALL |

Returns all test data elements of the specified collection.

 |
 | #spec(data) |

The binary data stream that contains the test data. The general format is:

#Nn1n2...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 = i = N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The format of the data stream itself depends on the edit mode:

- For edit mode DELETE, the td elements of the testdata collection must not contain any operation elements.
- For all other edit modes, the td elements should contain one or more operation elements.

Currently, two types of td elements are supported, dcset and dcWaveform.

 |
 |

dcset

td elements of type dcset can contain one or more of the following operation elements:

- `lastMeasure`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_lastMeasure`）
- `matchCmp`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_matchCmp`）
- `measure`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_measure`）
- `restoreMeasureRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_restoreMeasureRange`）
- `setCompliance`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setCompliance`）
- `setFilterValue`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setFilterValue`）
- `setForceRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setForceRange`）
- `setForceValue`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setForceValue`）
- `setMeasureRange`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setMeasureRange`）
- `setTmuArming`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setTmuArming`）
- `setTmuConfigure`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setTmuConfigure`）
- `setTmuMeasure`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md#_100076__t_setTmuMeasure`）

The setForceValue and the measure elements can be combined in one td element. The following tables show the attributes of the operation types and their possible values.

Note that you can specify the name of a base or derived variable instead of a constant for all double or integer attributes. The format is

LEV:<variable_name>

These references will be resolved from the primary level set with which the element is executed.

dcWaveform

td elements of type dcWaveform can only contain the following operation element:

- setForceWaveform

The following table shows the attributes of this operation element and their possible values. Note that spec variables cannot be used with the attributes of setForceWaveform.

Attributes for element "setForceWaveform":
 | Attribute  | Type  | Value  | Comment |
 | type  | enum  | voltage, current  | |
 | vectorDistance  | int  | |

The number of break vectors to be executed while the values are programmed. This must be a multiple of 8 = 16.

Note that this parameter must have the same value on all pins of the specified pattern for which DC waveforms are defined.

 |
 | iRange  | double  | |

Optional. If it is not specified, the largest current range of the hardware that fits for all given pins and values is taken. If it specified, the value must be within the range of hardware specification.

Note that this range is used for compensating the waveform values. It is not applied to the PMU hardware. This must have been done previously by the user, when he prepares the system for waveform generation with the PMU (setup PMU, close relays).

 |
 | vRange  | double  | |

Optional. If it is not specified, the largest voltage range of the hardware that fits for all given pins and values is taken. If it specified, the value must be within the range of hardware specification.

Note that this range is used for compensating the waveform values. It is not applied to the PMU hardware. This must have been done previously by the user, when he prepares the system for waveform generation with the PMU (setup PMU, close relays).

 |
 | values  | list[double]  | |

Comma separated list of values for the waveform in Volt or Ampere.

Note that number of list items must have the same value on all pins of the specified pattern for which DC waveforms are defined.

   | |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFTD  DFTD   DeFine Test Data）

```
# For pin vdd, define dc test data:
DFTD "DCTasks",REPLACE,(vdd),#3237<?xml version="1.0"?>
<testdata>
 <td id="0" type="dcset">
 <setMeasureRange type="voltage" minValue="0" maxValue="3"/>
 </td>
 <td id="1" type="dcset">
 <measure type="current" failOnLowClamp="true" failOnHighClamp="true"/>
 </td>
</testdata>
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFTD  DFTD   DeFine Test Data）

```
DFTD "DCTasks",REPLACE,(vdd),#3233<?xml version="1.0"?>
<testdata>
 <td id="maxVoltage" type="dcset">
 <setForceValue type="voltage" value="LEV:maxVoltage"/>
 </td>
 <td id="derivedVoltage" type="dcset">
 <setForceValue type="voltage" value="LEV:derivedVoltage"/>
</td>
</testdata>
```

This example shows how base and derived variables can be referenced within a test event. A test in which this setForceValue element is executed must be run with a primary level equation set where these variables are declared, for example:

```
EQNSET 1 "level1"
 SPECS
 maxVoltage [V]
 EQUATIONS
 derivedVoltage = maxVoltage/2
 ...
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFTD  DFTD   DeFine Test Data）

The following example shows a test data collection of DC waveforms, and how an element of this collection is referenced in a SVEC pattern:

```
DFTD "dcSubLabel",INSERT,(pmuPort),#9000000352<?xml version="1.0"?>
<testdata>
<td id="force1V" type="dcWaveform">
<setForceWaveform type="voltage" vectorDistance = "16" iRange="0.01" values="0,0.5,1"/>
</td>
<td id="force0V" type="dcWaveform">
<setForceWaveform type="voltage" vectorDistance = "16" iRange="0.01"
values="1,0.75,0.5,0.25,0"/>
</td>
</testdata>

SQLB "dcSubLabel",SVEC,0,2,"functional_MP",(pmuPort)
...
SQPG 0,STVA,,0,SM,(pmuPort)
SQPG 1,XACT,,"force1V",SM,(pmuPort) # execute ramp to force 1V
SQPG 2,RSUB,,,,(pmuPort)
```

The subpattern named `dcSubLabel` executes the first of the two DC waveforms that are contained in the test data collection of the same name.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFUP  DFUP  -  DeFine Utility Purpose）

| ch_No_list |

Utility line channel numbers to be defined as the members of a utility purpose and specified with five digits. The channels must be separated with a comma.

In the five鈥慸igit format, the first three digits of the channel numbers specify the utility pogo block. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy three鈥慸igit format is also supported: The first digit (1 ... 8) specifies the utility pogo block UTIL鈥? ... UTIL鈥?.

The last two digits specify the channel number 01 ... 32 of the utility line.

On the utility pogo blocks, an offset of -1 is to be considered and the channel number is URW00 ... URW31.

When reading the defined utility lines with the DFUP? command, the data returned always have the five鈥慸igit format. The same applies to the `PALS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.173_PALS__PALS__-__Pin_ALlocation_for_multiple_Sites.md`） command.

The channel numbers 16515 and 16516 should not be used. They should only be accessed with the `I2CA`（raw: `02.06.02.02.142_I2CA__I2CA__-__I2CA_bus.md`）or the `BDID`（raw: `02.06.02.02.09_BDID__BDID__-__BoarD_ID.md`）firmware command.

 |
 | setting |

Output states for each channel in the ch_No_list. Specify the setting of each utility line with the following specifiers:

- 0: sets the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)
- 1: sets the corresponding (write) channel to low
- X (x): no action

Specify the setting values corresponding to the definition order of the ch_No_list parameter.

The number of characters must be equal to the number of the utility line channels in the ch_No_list parameter.

Note that the settings must be explicitly activated with `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`）.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of the utility purpose. In the query you can use the symbol @ to list all defined utility purposes.

This parameter can have up to 16 alphanumeric characters and must not contain blank spaces, or any of the following characters: `# ; ( ' ' ) ? @ ,`

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFUP  DFUP  -  DeFine Utility Purpose）

```
> DFUP (16501,16502,16503,16504),"0110",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "0110",(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example defines a utility purpose AWG_CNCT and activates its standard settings.

The members and the setting values are as follows:

```
Member:      16501  16502  16503  16504
---------------------------------------
Setting:     0      1      1      0
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFUT  DFUT  -  DeFine UTility line）

| ch_No |

Channel number of the utility line specified with five or three digits.

In the five鈥慸igit format, the first three digits specify the utility pogo block. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

In the legacy three鈥慸igit format, the first digit (1 ... 8) specifies the utility pogo block UTIL鈥? ... UTIL鈥?.

The last two digits specify the channel number 01 ... 32 of the utility line.

On the utility pogo blocks, an offset of -1 is to be considered and the channel number is URW00 ... URW31.

When reading the defined utility lines with the DFUT? command, the data returned always have the five鈥慸igit format. The same applies to the `PALS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.173_PALS__PALS__-__Pin_ALlocation_for_multiple_Sites.md`） command.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）

 |
 | type |

Specifies the operating mode of the utility line with the following specifiers:

- W: Write-Only
- R: Read-Only
- RW: Read-Write

Utility lines of the optional `Utility Card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.04_Utility_Card.md`） can also be configured as safety lines or as global shutdown line for hardware鈥慶ontrolled shutdown of XPS256 pins:

- TRIGGER_IF_HIGH: Safety line
- TRIGGER_IF_LOW: Safety line
- TRIGGER_SITE_IF_HIGH: Global shutdown line
- TRIGGER_SITE_IF_LOW: Global shutdown line

For more information, refer to `XPS256 safety line and DUT board disconnect`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.03.06_XPS256_safety_line_and_DUT_board_disconnect.md`）.

 |
 | util_name |

Name of the utility line. For the query, it specifies the utility line name to be retrieved. @ can be used to list all defined utility lines.

This parameter can have up to 16 alphanumeric characters and must not contain blank spaces, or any of the following characters: `# ; ( ' ' ) ? @ ,`

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DFUT  DFUT  -  DeFine UTility line）

```
DFUT 16504,w,(filter)
```

This example assigns the name `filter` and operating mode w to utility line 4 of the first utility pogo block.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DGCM  -  DiGital Capture Mode）

|

vector_label

 |

Vector main label. Must be enclosed in double quotes

 |
 |

capt_mode

 |

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DGCM  -  DiGital Capture Mode）

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DGCS  DGCC   DiGital Capture aSynchronous）

```
DGCS
SQST RUN
DGCC?
```

returns:

```
DGCC {result_flag}
```

Parameters
 |

result_flag

 |

The result returned by DGCC?.

P (for Pass) is returned if received and expected data match.

F (for Fail) is returned if received and expected data do not match.

F (for Fail) is returned if In a standard digital capture test a high is received, which means it does not match the functional test result (refer to `Combining selective digital capture with a functional test`（raw: `02.06.06.01.03.01.03_Combining_selective_digital_capture_with_a_functional_test.md`） to learn about using the HRPF keyword).

Note that the result flag refers to the functional test, and does not say anything about the success of the digital capture. Rather, when the functional test returns P, this may imply that something went wrong with digital capture. Thus, if the received values are compared against 0, which is recommended, P can indicate that no data was captured.

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DGCS  DGCC   DiGital Capture aSynchronous）

### Generic example

```
> DGCS
> SQST RUN
> DGCC?
< DGCC F
```

### Application

This command performs hardware activation and clean-up on pins configured for digital capture.

 |
 | -2  | Stops the logging of the issued firmware commands/queries to a file /var/opt/hp93000/soc/MCDLog. |
 | 44  | Suppresses the error and warning messages to the report window.

The default state for this function is OFF (-44).

 |
 | -44  | Starts to display the error and warning messages to the report window. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DIAG -  DIAGnostics）

```
DIAG 44
```

This example stops to display the error and warning messages to the report window.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DIDT  DIDT  -  upload DIgital DaTa）

```
DIDT {"var_name"}, [code_format], [code_input_mode], [byte_order], [code_width], [offset], [nr_vectors], [comment], {data}
DIDT? {"var_name"}, ["area-id",][code_format], [code_input_mode], [byte_order], [code_width], [offset], [nr_vectors]
```

returns:

```
DIDT {"var_name"}, [code_format], [code_input_mode], [byte_order], [code_width], [offset], [nr_vectors], [comment], {data}
```

To return only parameters and comments:

```
DIDT?ALL,,,,,0,0
```

Returns all vector variable parameters.

```
DIDT? "var_name",,,,,0,0
```

Returns only the parameters of the specific vector variable var_name:

```
DIDT {"var_name"}, [code_format], [code_input_mode], [byte_order], [code_width], [offset], [nr_vectors], ["comment"], #9000000000
```

Parameters
 |

var_name

 |

This is a unique name string for the vector variable that defines the filtering conditions.

 |
 |

area-id

 |

Selects a specific result retention area by ID to upload from. The corresponding result retention configuration must have been configured and valid results must have been recorded into the area by a previously executed digital capture test.

 |
 |

code_format

 |

Output format of the DUT, which is the input format for DIDT?. The possible values are:

- BIN
- COMP1
- COMP2
- MOD_COMP1
- GRAY
- BCD
- SYMM
- MOD_SYMM
- ALAW
- MOD_ALAW
- MSB

The default value is BIN. If you specify another DUT format, DIDT? takes an end segment of the sample with length code_width (see below) to be a code in that format and converts it into binary format before the sample is returned.

MSB causes the bit order of the sample segment to be reversed, that is, if the segment length is m, then the nth input bit will be the (m-n+1)th output bit. The maximum segment length is 32.

For example, 010011 will become 110010.

 |
 |

code_input_mode

 |

Defines the input mode of the data.

Code formats specified by the code_format and code_input_mode parameters determine how the data will be decoded for digital source memory downloads with the DIDT command or encoded during digital capture uploads with the DIDT? query.

The possible modes are:

- NORM (normal)
- COMP (complementary)

The default is NORM (assumed if not specified).

For details, see `Code Format Tables`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.04_Code_Format_Tables.md`） from the related VECTOR test method API `inputMode()`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.269_VECTOR.md#_29830__dle_inputMode`） and `getInputMode()`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.269_VECTOR.md#_29830__dle_getInputMode`）.

 |
 |

byte_order

 |

Specifies the byte order of the device. Allowed values are:

- BIG_ENDIAN: The high-order byte is most significant.
- LITTLE_ENDIAN: The low-order byte is most significant.
 |
 |

code_width

 |

The width of that end segment of the sample that is considered as a code. It is this segment which is converted. The default width for Digital Capture variable type is determined as follows:

- If the xfer_mode parameter of the specified vector variable has been set to PARA, the default value of code_width is the number of pins that are associated with the vector variable.
- If xfer_mode is set to SERI, the default width is the value of the nr_vec_per_sample parameter of the vector variable.
 |
 |

offset

 |

This parameter can be used to further reduce the size of the data returned. This offset starts from the position specified by the init_discard parameter of the vector variable. The default is 0. This usage of offset is only supported for Digital Capture variables (defined with DVVA).

 |
 |

nr_vectors

 |

The number of vectors that are to be downloaded or uploaded, starting from offset. The Digital Capture variable type default is

nr_of_ frames 脳 nr_vec_per_frame

where nr_of_ frames and nr_vec_per_frame are parameters of the vector variable.

This parameter determines the number n of samples that are returned when uploading. n will be

nr_vectors / nr_vec_per_sample [+1],

where 1 is added if nr_vectors is not an integer multiple of the vector variable parameter nr_vec_per_sample.

 |
 |

comment

 |

String that can be used for equation algorithm of the downloaded arbitrary waveform. For example, sin(x)+sin(2x). This is not needed for Digital Capture upload.

 |
 |

data

 |

The waveform data described by using the binary data standard format. It consists of a standard header followed by the actual data (32 bit integer format). The format is:

#Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

 |

### Example 1 - Digital capture（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DIDT  DIDT  -  upload DIgital DaTa）

```
> DVVA? ALL
< DVVA "par_var",DIGCAPT,"MYTEST",PARA,,,,0,3,1,1,2,2,(PAR3,PAR2,PAR1)
> DIDT? "par_var",,,,,,
< DIDT "par_var",BIN,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,3,0,6,,#9000000024,,,,,,
```

or, alternatively:

```
> $DIDT? "par_var",,,,,,2
< DIDT "par_var",BIN,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,3,0,2,,
       0000  0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000  0110
       0000  0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000  0101
```

In the preceding call of $DIDT? it was assumed that the output format of the DUT is BIN. Accordingly, no conversion was performed. If the output format is GRAY, call and reply will look like this:

```
> $DIDT? "par_var",GRAY,,,,,2
< DIDT "par_var",GRAY,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,3,0,2,,
       0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0100
       0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0110
```

### Example 2 - Digital Source Memory（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DIDT  DIDT  -  upload DIgital DaTa）

```
> DIDT? ALL,,,,,0,0
```

returns:

```
DIDT "LEFT",BCD,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,16,0,10,"download comment LEFT",#9000000000
DIDT "L1",BIN,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,32,0,0,"download sin wave",#9000000000
DIDT "L11",BIN,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,32,0,0,"", #9000000000
DIDT "L2",BIN,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,32,0,0,"",#9000000000
DIDT "LF",BIN,NORM,BIG_ENDIAN,16,0,20,"download comment Flat",#9000000000
```

Note To query the comments or download parameters of DIDT, you must specify that offset and nr_vectors be 0. Omitting nr_vectors means that you upload the number of frames defined in the vector variable configuration usage, using all the other default download parameters.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLPP -  DeLete Per Pin Subroutine）

```
DLPP {label}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLPP -  DeLete Per Pin Subroutine）

|

label

 |

Specifies the name of the per-pin subroutine to be deleted.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLPP -  DeLete Per Pin Subroutine）

```
DLPP "summer"
```

This command deletes the per-pin subroutine referenced by the label "summer".

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLSO  Driver Level Switch Off）

```
DLSO{(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLSO  Driver Level Switch Off）

|

pinlist

 |

Pin or pins for which the channels are to be set to high impedance as defined by level set 0. You can specify @ for all pins, and @NONSHARED@ for the resources that are not shared between configured sites in a multi-site test.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLSO  Driver Level Switch Off）

DLSO can be used in a customized disconnect sequence (disconnect.user_def in the testfunc directory) as follows:

```
DLSO(@)
RLYC IDLE,OFF,(@)
...
PSST OFF
```

Executing this file instead of the standard disconnect sequence has the advantage that only the sequencers of the sites that are in setup focus are switched off. DLSO also ensures that this is done without hot switching. The standard sequence uses the SQST OFF command, which switches all sequencers off, not only those in setup focus.

 Note The goal is to ensure that the AC relay is not open while there is current flowing through it nor close the AC relay when there is a difference in potential across the two AC relay terminals. That is, we want to minimize the di/dt when we open or close the AC relay or PPMU relay. The clamps only help to limit the voltage excursion transient from L*di/dt. So it's best if di/dt is zero or near zero so clamps are not needed. This is the theory behind how to eliminate hot switching damage to both the DUT as well as the tester's pin electronics. We need the device connect and disconnect sequences to minimize di/dt during the switching of any relay or FET between the tester pin electronics and the DUT due to the long inductive cable between the pin electronics and DUT. This applies to all cards.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLTS -  DeLete TeSt）

```
DLTS {"label"}[, (port)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLTS -  DeLete TeSt）

|

label

 |

Specifies the label to be deleted.

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter is only relevant for multi-port burst labels. If you call DLTS with a multi-port burst label and you do not specify a port, the label is deleted for all ports. If you specify a port, the label is only deleted for this port.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DLTS -  DeLete TeSt）

```
DLTS "MPBU_port_1_port_2",(port_1)
```

This example deletes the label referenced by `MPBU_port_1_port_2` from the port `port_1`.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DMAS  DMAS  -  Define Memory Area Size）

|

area

 |

The area parameter specifies the type of data for which a memory area is to be set or read. It can be one of the following:

 |
 |

 |

PARA

 |

Only the DMAS? PARA (PARAllel vector area) query is supported. It returns the current end of the vector areas for the different memory types. Note that in case of a multiport setup, values are only returned if the PER_PORT option is explicitly set as the third parameter.

 |
 |

 |

PPSQ

 |

Only the DMAS? PPSQ (Per Pin SeQuencer subroutine) query is supported. It returns the space currently used for per pin sequencer subroutines. It can only be applied to the default port @.

 |
 |

 |

RSLT

 |

The DMAS? RSLT(ReSuLT area) query returns how much memory is available for result data (Error Map in the external memory or digital capture data).

 |
 |

 |

SAVE

 |

The DMAS? SAVE query returns the size of the currently used memory for the area types PARA, PPSQ, and SQPG.

Note that in case of a multiport setup, PARA values are only returned if the PER_PORT option is set explicitly as the third parameter.

 |
 |

 |

SQPG

 |

The SQPG (Sequencer ProGramming area) option allocates memory for a number of sequencer instructions. The allocated command lines are filled with NOP instructions.

The DMAS? SQPG query returns the current end of the sequencer areas for the specified ports.

 |
 |

 |

MFRE

 |

The MFRE (Memory Free RangE) option can only be used in the query. It reports the actual maximum number of vectors that can be added to each of the specified ports, pins or channels.

 |
 |

 |

MFRP

 |

The MFRP (Memory Free Range per Pool) option can only be used in the query. It reports the free memory space for the specified ports from the pool (test processor, channel group) perspective.

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

The ALL (ALL areas) option can only be used in a query. It returns the size of the currently used memory for the area types PARA, PPSQ, and SQPG, and in addition also the space that is free for result data (area type RSLT).

Note that in case of a multiport setup, PARA values are only returned if the PER_PORT option is set explicitly as the third parameter.

 |
 |

size

 |

In the command, the size parameter defines the number of sequencer instructions for which memory is to be allocated on the specified port (area type SQPG). One sequencer instruction requires the space of 8 vectors. Enter a number of instructions between 0 and MAX_FREE_MEM/ 8 vectors.

In the query replies, this parameter either specifies the used space (for example, with area type PARA) or the available free space (with area types RSLT, MFRE, and MFRP).

 |
 |

size_1

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the amount of free vector memory at the end of a specified channel for the PER_CHANNEL option of MFRE and MFRP.

 |
 |

size_2

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the largest block of free vector memory on a specified channel for the PER_CHANNEL option of MFRE and MFRP.

 |
 |

size_3

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the total amount of free vector memory on a specified channel for the PER_CHANNEL option of MFRE and MFRP.

 |
 |

pool_size

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the total amount of free vector memory on a pool (channel group, test processor) which shares a channel with a specified port for the PER_POOL option of MFRP.

 |
 |

memory

 |

Specifies the type of memory which is acted upon:

 |
 |

 |

SM

 |

Sequencer memory. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

SHMEM

 |

A special kind of SM for memory sharing in multisite setups. For details see `Selecting the memory type`（raw: `02.06.07.01.04.01_Selecting_the_memory_type.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

HSER

 |

A special kind of SM for patterns used in SmartLoop testing. For details see `Defining a compliance pattern for pattern鈥慴ased SmartLoop testing`（raw: `02.06.17.04.01_Defining_a_compliance_pattern_for_pattern__ased_SmartLoop_testing.md`）.

 |
 |   | SMEXT  | A special kind of memory for vectors, used only when himem is enabled in the .technology file. See `Technology file for a device - himem`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.07.02.01.02_Technology_file_for_a_device.md#_49363__row_himem`） for details. This option can only be used in the query with MFRE or MFRP. |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

All types of memory. This option can only be used in the query.

 |
 |

PER_PORT

 |

This query option requires the answer to be given per port. This is the default.

Note however that this option must be specified for area type PARA; otherwise DMAS? will return no answer. This also applies to the PARA values for area types SAVE and ALL.

 |
 |

PER_PIN

 |

This query option is only supported by area types MFRE and RSLT, Its point is that the amount of free vector space or result space can be different for different pins of the same port.

 |
 |

PER_CHANNEL

 |

This option is only supported by the MFRE and the MFRP area types. With area type MFRE, it causes DMAS? to return three values for each specified channel in the following order:

- size_1: The amount of memory that is available at the end of the vector memory
- size_2: The size of the largest free vector memory block
- size_3: The sum of all free blocks

With area type MFRP, the same three values are returned, but for all channels of any pool that supplies channels to one of the specified ports.

 |
 |

PER_POOL

 |

This option is only supported by the MFRP area type. It causes DMAS? to return the total free space of all pools (channel groups, test processors) that supply channels for the specified ports.

 |
 |

port

 |

The port for which areas are to be defined or for which information is requested. The default port, to which all pins belong, is denoted by the @ character.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

The ports for which information is to be retrieved.

 |
 |

pin, pin_list

 |

The pins for which information is requested or returned.

 |
 |

channel, channel_list

 |

The channels for which information is requested or returned.

 |
 |

pool_channels

 |

The channels of the pool to which the channels of those ports belong that are specified in the query.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DMAS  DMAS  -  Define Memory Area Size）

The following example illustrates the various options of the MFRE and MFRP queries. First, the free memory range of the `port12` port is queried on the port level:

```
> DMAS? MFRE,,(port12)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,84288,(port12)
```

On the pin level, the corresponding query and reply look as follows:

```
> DMAS? MFRE,,PER_PIN,(port12)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,84288,(Pin1)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,88288,(Pin2)
```

Note that the query per port returns the smaller of the two values.

`Pin1` is mapped to channel 10101, `Pin2` to channel 10102. Thus the corresponding channel related query and its reply are

```
> DMAS? MFRE,,PER_CHANNEL,(10101,10102)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,84212,84312,84640,(10101)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,88312,88312,88640,(10102)
```

The figures are slightly different, because the query per channel only considers the hardware.

Finally, the two possible options for MFRP, applied to `port12`, produce

```
> DMAS? MFRP,,PER_CHANNEL,(port12)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,84212,84312,84640,(10101)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,88312,88312,88640,(10102)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,84212,84312,84640,(10103)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,90464,90464,90736,(10104)
```

 for the PS9G pool 10101 through 10104, and

```
> DMAS? MFRP,,PER_POOL,(port12)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,347400,(10101,10102,10103,10104)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPPC -  Define Per Pin subroutine Configuration）

|

name

Name of the Pin-Per Sequencer Subroutine label. For the query, you can enter ALL to return all PPSS labels.

parameter

SMLEN

RELOC

MWAIT

MAXLEN

Used internally.

ALL

In the query, to display information about all parameters.

value

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPPS  DPPS  -  Define Per Pin Subroutine label）

level_set

dps_set

screen_select

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPRT  DPRT  -  Default PRimary Timing sets）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + spec_set_no

Note that the spec set ID identifies the primary wavetable in equation based testing.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, a primary multiport specification can be specified.

 |

timing_set

The identification number of the timing set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets (of the selected waveform set or timing specification). The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of timing sets allowed (as defined by DSCP).

In a multiport setup, the timing set number applies to all ports of the specification if no port is specified. Otherwise, the number applies to the specified port.

timing_set_list

In a multi-port setup, you can specify primary timing sets for all ports of the specification by entering a list of numbers separated by commas.

In the query, the numbers of the primary timing sets are returned in a list for all ports of the primary specification unless the numbers are identical for all ports or a port has been specified in the query.

 |

port

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSA  DPSA  -  Define per Pin Subroutine Address）

|

name

 |

Per-pin Subroutine name. This parameter can be used to call the subroutine from a parallel sequencer program.

address
