### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

|

setnr

 |

This number defines the set number for the measurement. The number must be an integer from 1 to 256.

In the query, you can specify ALL to retrieve the data of all sets.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This parameter specifies the pins to be used for the measurements.

 |
 |

binary_data

 |

This is a binary data string. The string starts with the '#' character, followed by a digit in the range 1 to 9 which stipulates how many digits are used in the data length specifier. The data length specifier is next: up to 9 digits determine how many bytes of data will follow. The actual data string follows last.

 Note If the binary data string is empty, the definition for the pins specified in pinlist will be deleted from the set.

The first character or value of the data stream determines the format for the remainder of the data stream (characters '0' through '3' are for current measurements, '4' through '11' for voltage measurements):

 | 0: Waveform template |
 | |

If the first character is a '0', it is followed by a waveform template. The values are given first for the low value and then for the high value. The values are separated by a ',' (comma).

This template is for the PASS/FAIL results from the `PSER?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） query. The current range in which the measurements will be executed is determined by the maximum/ minimum value of the template. The values have the unit Amps [A].

This option can only be combined with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 1: Number of measurement points followed by low and high values |
 |   | If the first character is a '1', a number and two values follow. The first number gives the number of measurement points. The second and third define the low and high values. These are separated by a "," (comma). The current range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Amps [A].

This option can only be combined with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 2: Low and high value |
 |   | If the first character is a '2', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The current range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Amps [A]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 3: Low and high value |
 |   | If the first character is a '3', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The current range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Amps [A]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option can only be selected for DC Scale channel DPS's and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command. If the channels belong to a Master/Slave configuration, they are unganged during the measurement as far as possible, that is, as far this can be done without affecting the goal of the measurement.

 |
 | 4: Waveform template |
 |   | If the first character is a '4', it is followed by a waveform template. The values are given first for the low value and then for the high value. The values are separated by a ',' (comma). This template is for the PASS/FAIL results from the `PSER?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） query. The voltage range in which the measurements will be executed is determined by the maximum/ minimum value of the template. The values have the unit Volt [V].

This option can only be selected for DC Scale channel DPS's and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 5: Number of measurement points followed by the low and high values |
 |   | If the first character is a '5', a number and two values follow. The first number gives the number of measurement points. The second and third define the low and high values. These are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V].

This option can only be selected for DC Scale channel DPS's and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 6: Low and high value |
 |   | If the first character is a '6', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 7: Voltage waveform template for the high speed digitizer |
 |   | If the first character is a '7', it is followed by a voltage waveform template for the high speed digitizer (connect state *HDIG). An error message occurs if another connect state is used. The values are given first for the low value and then for the high value. The values are separated by a ',' (comma). This template is for the PASS/FAIL results from the `PSER?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） query. The voltage range in which the measurements will be executed, is determined by the maximum/ minimum value of the template. The values have the unit Volt [V]. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command. See also `DPS_PIN_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.50.01_DPS_PIN_TASK.md`）. |
 | 8: Number of measurement points followed by the low and high values for high speed digitizer measurements |
 |   | If the first character is an '8', a number and two values follow. The first number gives the number of measurement points. The second and third define the low and high values. These are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. This template is for high speed digitizer measurements only, that means connect state *HDIG. An error message occurs if another connect state is used. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command. See also `DPS_PIN_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.50.01_DPS_PIN_TASK.md`）. |
 | 9: Low and high value for high speed digitizer measurements |
 |   | If the first character is a '9', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1. This template is for high speed digitizer measurements only, that means connect state *HDIG. An error message occurs if another connect state is used. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command. See also `DPS_PIN_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.50.01_DPS_PIN_TASK.md`）. |
 | 10: Force voltage-drop measurement |
 | |

If the first value is a '10', two values follow. They define the low/high P/F limits of a force (voltage-)drop measurement and are separated by a "," (comma). The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option can be selected only for the HC variant of `DC Scale DPS128`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01_DC_Scale_DPS128_DPS64_cards.md`） channels and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 11: Return voltage-drop measurement |
 | |

If the first value is an '11', two values follow. They define the low/high P/F limits of a return (voltage-)drop measurement and are separated by a "," (comma). The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option can be selected only for the HC variant of `DC Scale DPS128`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01_DC_Scale_DPS128_DPS64_cards.md`） channels and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

   | |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000170,0.1,0.2,0.2,0.3
```

This example defines a template which consists of 2 points (0.1, 0.2) and (0.2, 0.3). If the first measured value is in the range (0.1, 0.2) and the second value is in the range (0.2, 0.3), then the result will be a pass.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000121,15,0.1,0.2
```

This example defines a template which is 15 points long and is constant.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DFPS 11,pos,(Vcc)
DFPS 12,pos,(Vdd)
DPSE 1,(@),#10 <- Delete set 1
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#152,1,2 <- Vcc min=1A, max=2A
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#152,2,3 <- Vdd min=2A, max=3A
PSST ON <- Measurement requires connect state
PSIE 1,,,(@) <- Measure both pins in parallel
PSER? 1,pval
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000006,1.501 <- value within range
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000006,3.173 <- value outside range
PSER? 1,ppf
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000000
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000000
PSER? 1,gpf
PSER 1,F,(),#9000000000
```

This example performs a measurement with format 2 and PSIE for two different pins in parallel.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DFPS (10101),pos,(Vcc) <- DC Scale pin
DFPS (10102,10103),pos,(Vdd) <- DC Scale pin (Gang of two channels)
DPSE 1,(@),#10 <- Delete set 1
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#153,0.5,1.5 <- Vcc min=0.5A, max=1.5A
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#153,20,30 <- Vdd min=20A, max=30A
PSST ON <- Measurement requires connect state
PSIE 1,,,(@) <- Measure both pins in parallel
 Vcc: High Precision Mode is used
 Vdd: Only one channel of the gang is used
PSER? 1,pval
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000006,1.301 <- value within range
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000006,31.73 <- value outside range
PSER? 1,ppf
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000000
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000000
PSER? 1,gpf
PSER 1,F,(),#9000000000
```

This example performs a measurement with format 3 and PSIE for two different pins in parallel.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DPSR  DPSR  -  Define Parallel SeaRch）

```
> PSFC ALL
> DPSR 3,,,FUNC,#219,TIM,"f",B,30,130,,
> PSFC 2
> DPSR 3,(IN1),,FUNC,#220,TIM,"del",B,0,110,,
> PQFC 1
> DPSR? 3,(@)
< DPSR 3,(@),(@),FUNC,#9000000019,TIM,"f",B,30,130,,
> PQFC 2
> DPSR? 3,(@)
< DPSR 3,(OUT1),(@),FUNC,#9000000019,TIM,"f",B,30,130,,
< DPSR 3,(IN1),(@),FUNC,#9000000020,TIM,"del",B,0,110,,
```

This example illustrates:

- How the same search can be defined differently for different sites.
- How an existing condition is partially overwritten when a new condition is partially inconsistent with it.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DQUE  -  show Data QUEue low level）

```
DQUE?{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
DQUE {dqueue_level}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DQUE  -  show Data QUEue low level）

|

dqueue_level

 |

A reply parameter specifying the smallest number of 8-vector blocks that was left in the data queue during the last sequencer run for the specified pins

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the lowest data queue level is queried or returned.

Use the @ character to query all pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DQUE  -  show Data QUEue low level）

```
> DQUE? (p1)
< DQUE 26,(p1)
```

This example queries the low level of the data queue for pin p1.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

```
DRLS? {test}, {pass_value}, [limit], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
DRLS {value_specifier}, {result_value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

|

test

 |

This parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

H

 |

This parameter must be entered to determine the high input voltage threshold (VIH,min). VIH,min is the minimum input level which is recognized as logic 1 by the DUT.

 |
 |

L

 |

This parameter must be entered to determine the low input voltage threshold (VIL,max). VIL,max is the maximum input level which is recognized as logic 0 by the DUT.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

For a simple pass or fail test (limit parameter omitted), the pass value defines the expected pass level (in mV) for the test. For value measurements, this parameter defines the start value of the measurement window; set it to a value that ensures a pass result for the functional test. pass_value must be in the range of the drive level in the channel board (see `DRLV, DRLV? - (DRive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.89_DRLV__DRLV__-__DRive_LeVel.md`）).

 |
 |

limit

 |

The limit parameter is an integer which defines the upper (for a low level search) and lower (for a high level search) limits for the measurement window of a value measurement. The limit must be specified in mV. This parameter must be omitted if only a pass/fail result for the test is required. The range limitations for this parameter are as follows:

- when checking the high threshold, the limit parameter must be between the minimum drive level of the channel board (see `DRLV, DRLV? - (DRive LeVel`（raw: `02.06.02.02.89_DRLV__DRLV__-__DRive_LeVel.md`）) and the specified pass value;
- when checking the low level threshold, the limit parameter must be between the specified pass value and the maximum drive level of the channel board.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins that you want to test. This parameter may also include groups previously created using the DFGP command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. pinlist must only contain pins configured as inputs.

 |
 |

value_specifier

 |

This reply parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned if a VIL,max measurement was performed and already the first test (with the pass_value parameter) failed.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned if a VIH,min measurement was performed and all the functional tests performed within the measurement window passed.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

(equal to) is returned if a value measurement was performed and the first failed functional test occurred within the measurement window.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned if a VIL,max measurement was performed and all tests performed within the measurement window passed.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned if a VIH,min measurement has been performed and the first functional test performed within the measurement window failed.

 |
 |

P

 |

This indicates that the functional test performed passed. This is only returned if the limit parameter is omitted.

 |
 |

F

 |

This indicates that the functional test performed failed. This is only returned if the limit parameter is omitted.

 |
 |

result_value

 |

The result value is the level (in mV) of the last passed test.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

```
DRLS? H,5000,,(Q0_1)
```

returns:

```
DRLS P,5000
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

```
DRLS? H,5000,-1000,(Q0_1)
```

returns:

```
DRLS EQ,-490
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLV  DRLV  -  DRive LeVel）

|

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set (fixed levels) in which you want the levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command). Typing ALL in this field sets the levels for all existing level sets. Typing PRM sets the drive voltage levels for the primary level set.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

 |
 |

logic_0_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the low level voltage for the drive amplifier.

 |
 |

logic_1_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the high level voltage for the drive amplifier.

 |
 |

v3h_level

 |

Input (drive) 3rd level definition (high level voltage shift). The expression of this extra parameter must define a value in millivolts (mV).

This parameter is no longer used.

 |
 |

range

 |

This extra parameter selects the drive range in mV:

- -8000.0 ... 8000.0 selects the 8 V range
- -30000.0 ... 30000.0 selects the 30 V range
- all other values select the -40 V ... +80 V range

If not specified the best fit range will be selected based on logic_0_level and logic_1_level.

This parameter is currently not available.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose levels you want to set. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） (DeFine GrouP) command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ sets or reads the drive levels of all input pins in the level set. You can include I and IO pin types in pinlist.

 |

For card specifications, like level ranges, see `Digital Cards`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04_Digital_Cards.md`）, for example:

- `Pin Scale 1600`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.01.03_PS1600_driver.md`）
- `Pins Scale 5000`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.03.04_Pin_Scale_5000_driver.md`）

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLV  DRLV  -  DRive LeVel）

```
DRLV 1,-1750,-850,(Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

This example sets the driver levels for level set 1 for pins Q0, Q1, Q2 and Q3. The logic 0 level is set to -1750 mV and the logic 1 level to -850 mV.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DRLV  DRLV  -  DRive LeVel）

```
DRLV 1,-1750,-850,8000,(avi64Pin1)
```

This example shows how the 8 V drive range of an AVI64 pin is selected.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

| device_cycle  | The device_cycle parameter is an integer that defines the absolute maximum number of device cycles that you can create for one pin.

Default: 256

Maximum: 16384

Note that the total number of device cycles gets evenly divided between the combined number of waveform sets and wavetables. If you use the default values, then 256 device cycles divides into the total number of 32 `waveform sets and wavetables`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） to give you 8 device cycles per waveform set/wavetable. If you choose values that do not divide evenly, then the number of device cycles will be rounded up to the next multiple of the `waveform_set`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） parameter.

 |
 | devicecycle_set |

The devicecycle_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of device cycle sets that you can create. Device cycle sets are needed for selective digital capture.

Default: 1

Maximum: 128

 |
 | dps_set |

The dps_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of DPS sets you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | level_set |

The level_set parameter is an integer that defines the combined total of level sets for fixed and equation based levels that you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | period_res_prec |

This parameter defines the precision with which the period resolution is calculated by the system. It has no effect on a user defined period resolution (using, for example, the period_res keyword in the equation set).

The default is 4, if the .technology file does not contain this parameter.

If it does, the value of the .technology file is the default.

This value is set to 9, the greatest possible value, when a device is created.

 |
 |

pmu_set

 |

The pmu_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of actions that can be contained in all measurement sets of all PPMU DC sets.

Default: 1024

Maximum: 12800

 |
 | routing_set |

Defines the number of routing sets managed by the firmware, provided by the MCD.

Default: 256

Maximum: 512

 |
 | timing_set |

The timing_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum combined total of timing sets for fixed and equation based timing you can create.

Default: 256

Maximum: 999

The number of timing sets must be equal to or greater than the number of waveform sets, as there must be at least one timing set per waveform set.

 |
 | waveform_set |

The waveform_set parameter defines the maximum combined total of waveform sets (fixed timing) and wavetables (equation based timing) you can create. Thus, if you specify a value of 32, you could, for example, create 10 waveform sets and 22 wavetables.

Default: 32

Maximum: 128

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

```
DSCP 256,16,256,32,32,1024,16,1,256,
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DSUS  DSUS  -  Dps Sets USed）

|

ds_No

 |

DPS Set Number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a DPS set, or the highest number of set you want to load. The number you type must not exceed the maximum number of DPS sets allowed (defined by the DSCP command).

This number is automatically updated to include any new DPS set as it is created. At power-on only one DPS set (containing the default values) is available.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DSUS  DSUS  -  Dps Sets USed）

```
DSUS 2
```

This example defines a maximum of 2 DPS sets.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DSVS  DSVS  -  Define Spec Value Set）

|

spec_value_set_id

 |

This must be an integer between 1 and 2^16-1.

 |
 |

description

 |

A description of the spec value set.

 |
 |

spec_type

 |

The specification type. Possible values are:

- TIM: Timing specification
- LEV: Level specification
 |
 |

equ_set_no

 |

An equation set number, which together with a spec set number identifies a (single-port) specification.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

Instead of an equation set number, you can also specify the keyword PRM, which refers to the current (single- or multi-port) primary specification.

If the primary specification is not equation based, equation set 1 and spec set 1 are used.

 |
 |

spec_set_no

 |

A spec set number, which together with an equation set number identifies a (single-port) specification.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

Instead of a spec set number, you can also specify the name of a multi-port timing specification. In this case the equ_set_no parameter must be left empty.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DSVS  DSVS  -  Define Spec Value Set）

```
> DSVS 1, "per", TIM,PRM,
> DSVS? 1
< DSVS 1,"per",TIM,1,1
> DSVS 1, "per", TIM,1,2
< Error: Failed to execute firmware command: DSVS 1, "per", TIM,1,2
> DSVS 1,,,,
> DSVS 1, "per", TIM,1,2
> DSVS? 1
< DSVS 1,"per",TIM,1,2
```

This example shows how to redefine a spec value set. Note that you must delete the set before you can change the specification.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DTCP  DTCP  -  Define Technology Control Parameters）

| key  | The string specifies the system control parameter.

Currently, the only supported control parameters are testpoints and extended_dram_factor.

For more information, refer to `testpoints`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.07.02.01.02_Technology_file_for_a_device.md#_49363__row_testpoints`） and `extended_dram_factor`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.07.02.01.02_Technology_file_for_a_device.md#_49363__row_extended_dram_factor`） in `Technology file for a device`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.07.02.01.02_Technology_file_for_a_device.md`）.

 |
 | value   | The value to be set as string. |

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DTCP  DTCP  -  Define Technology Control Parameters）

```
> DTCP? "testpoints"
< DTCP "testpoints", "0"
> DTCP "testpoints", "100"
> DTCP? "testpoints"
< DTCP "testpoints", "100"
> *RST
> DTCP? "testpoints"
< DTCP "testpoints", "100"
```

```
> DTCP "extended_dram_factor","90"
> *RST
> DTCP? "extended_dram_factor"
< DTCP "extended_dram_factor","90"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DVVA  DVVA  -  Define Vector VAriable）

|

name

 |

Name of the vector variable to be defined. The name must be unique across vector labels. If the identifier ALL is used in the query, all those vector variables will be returned that were defined for vector labels of the specified ports.

 |
 |

type

 |

Type of vector variable. Currently, only the type DIGCAPT is supported.

 |
 |

vector_label

 |

Name of a vector label. Only main vector labels are supported.

 |
 |

xfer_mode

 |

Optional parameter that determines the transfer mode. The options available are:

PARA Parallel. This is the default.

SERI Serial

Note that you cannot select SERI if the vector variable is associated with more than one pin.

 |
 |

device_cycle

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED.

 |
 |

start_vector_nr

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED.

 |
 |

capt_label

 |

This parameter describes a label reference to a capture block within a vector label which has been set aside for digital capture. If this parameter is specified, the vector variable is defined with respect to this capture area. If it is not specified, the capture label references the entire pattern.

CURRENTLY NOT USED, DO NOT SPECIFY.

 |
 |

init_discard

 |

The offset relative to the start location of a capture block within the capture memory. The vectors before this offset will not be uploaded.

The default value is 0.

 |
 |

nr_vec_per_frame

 |

The number of relevant vectors within a frame.

 |
 |

nr_vec_per_sample

 |

The number of (relevant) vectors that are contained in one sample.

The suitable values for this parameter depend on the selected transfer mode (xfer_mode parameter).

- For transfer mode PARA, this parameter must be set to 1 (the default value).
- For SERI, the maximum number is 32. The bigger the number is, the faster the upload will be. For example, if one frame contains 5 relevant vectors, you could set nr_vec_per_sample to 30 in order to put 6 frames into one sample.
 |
 |

nr_vector_interdisc

 |

Defines the length of irrelevant vector blocks within a frame. These will be discarded in step 2 of the extraction process. If set to 2, for example, only the first and then every third vector will be extracted within a frame.

The default value is 0, in which case no vectors within a frame will be discarded.

 |
 |

nr_of_frames

 |

The number of frames that are to be extracted, starting from the first frame.

The default value is 1.

 |
 |

nr_frame_interdisc

 |

The number of irrelevant vectors between frames. These will be discarded in step 2 of the extraction process.

The default value is 0.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of pins for which the vector variable is defined. The pins specified here should also be associated with the vector label referenced by the vector_label parameter. Only then will the digital data of these pins be retrieved by DIDT?, if DIDT? is called with the actual vector variable.

If the list contains more than one element, the element names must be separated with a comma. Up to 32 pins can be associated with one vector variable.

If you have set the xfer_mode parameter to SERI, specify only one pin.

If you have set xfer_mode to PARA, the LSB of the sample will be assigned to the last pin of the pin list.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

If you specify ALL for name in the query, the vector variables of those vector labels will be returned that are associated with the ports specified here. The default for this parameter is the default port @ to which all pins belong.

Specify @@ to display all vector variables for all labels of all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DVVA  DVVA  -  Define Vector VAriable）

```
> DVVA "vec_1",DIGCAPT,"port2_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,\ 1,0,(I/O5_2)
> DVVA "vec_2",DIGCAPT,"port2_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,1,0,(I/O7_2,I/O6_2)
> DVVA "vec_3",DIGCAPT,"port1_B",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,\ 1,0,(Q7_1)
> DVVA? ALL,(port_1)
< DVVA "vec_3",DIGCAPT,"port1_B",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,1,0,(Q7_1)
> DVVA? ALL,(port_2)
< DVVA "vec_1",DIGCAPT,"port2_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,1,0,(I/O5_2)
< DVVA "vec_2",DIGCAPT,"port2_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,1,0,(I/O7_2,I/O6_2)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DVVC  DVVC  -  Define Vector Variable Configuration）

|

name

 |

The configuration name. This can also be ALL.

 |
 |

#data

 |

A configuration file in binary (BIN) format. This parameter allows you to define the length of the data (in bytes) and the data itself to be transferred. It has the following format:

- # to mark the start of the data block.
- One digit indicating how many digits make up the data length specifier.
- A number of digits indicate the length (in bytes) of the data to follow.
- A number of characters which make up the specified VVC based testing file. This stream of characters must be terminated with the @ character.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › DVCU  DVCU  -  Define Vector variable Configuration Usage）

The following example creates a usage for the label "src_ramp", using VVC "AC97", at offset 0.

VVC "AC97" looks like:

```
ATTR DIGDATA
VARIABLES LEFT,RIGHT
PINS ser_in
 SOURCE_DATA_TEMPLATE LEFT[0-19] ; RIGHT[0-19]
 MAPPING
 0 low
 1 high
```

This usage creates two vector variables, `LEFT_DATA` and `RIGHT_DATA`. It creates 1024 frames.

```
> DVCU "src_ramp","AC97",0,0,1024,"LEFT=LEFT_DATA,RIGHT=RIGHT_DATA",TRUE
> DVCU? ALL,ALL,ALL
< DVCU "src_ramp","AC97",0,0,1024,"LEFT=LEFT_DATA, RIGHT=RIGHT_DATA",TRUE
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EAEX  -  Edge Action EXpected data）

```
EAEX? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EAEX {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, [err_type], {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EAEX  -  Edge Action EXpected data）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. The scanning method and the range of values this parameter can take depend on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode, enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis mode, enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range. If the timing set was changed within the requested cycle range, more than one answer is returned.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. You can use the @ character to read the edge actions for all pins.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is optional and specifies what type of error information is available. It is always NOER since this query only reports expected data.

 |
 |

NOER

 |

Error information is not available. The reported range lies outside the range covered by the Error Map.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. Edges without action are not reported.

 |
 |

 |

The data is to be decoded as follows:

Each cycle of the reported cycle range is preceded by a two byte header information:

- First byte, bits 7, 6, 5, 4: Always zero, reserved for future use.
- First byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0: Always 1: number of waveforms contained in the device cycle.
- Second byte: Number of edge actions following (0 - 140)
 |
 |

 |

Each of the following edge actions is described by two bytes:

- First byte, bit 7: Channel selector for differential pins. The first channel has the value 0, the second the value 1.
- First byte, bits 6, 5, 4, 3: Waveform index (0 - 9)
- First byte, bits 2, 1, 0: Edge index (0 - 7)
- Second byte, bit 7: Error flag

0: No error on receive edge, or a drive edge

1: Cannot occur since only expected data are reported

- Second byte, bits 6, 5: Data parameter

00: Fixed value

10: Data parameter 1

11: Data parameter 2

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bit 4: Edge direction

0: Drive/tri-state edge

1: Receive edge

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 0, then drive/tri-state data:

Bits 3, 2: Tri-state data

00: Not used

10: Tri-state off

11: Tri-state on

01: Reserved for future use

Bits 1, 0: Drive data

00: Not used

10: Drive 0

11: Drive 1

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 1, then receive data compare method:

0001: Edge compare to intermediate

0010: Edge compare to 0

0011: Edge compare to 1

0100: Edge compare to mask

0101: Edge compare to unstable

1001: Window compare to intermediate

1010: Window compare to 0

1011: Window compare to 1

1100: Window compare to mask

1101: Window compare to unstable

1111: Window close

0000: Reserved for future use

0111: Reserved for future use

1000: Reserved for future use

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EAEX  -  Edge Action EXpected data）

```
EAEX? 0, 1, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
EAEX 0,1,3,,(pin1),#9000000010\x01\x04\x00\x0B\x01\x0A\x02\x19\x03\x1F\x0A
```

This example returns edge action drive and expected data (in hex notation) for one cycle. To decode the data, convert it into binary notation and use the lists above.

The data in binary format is:

```
0000 0001 0000 0100 0000 0000 0000 1011 0000 0001
0000 1010 0000 0010 0001 1001 0000 0011 0001 1111
```

The device cycle contains 1 waveform with 4 edge actions. The edge actions are RZ on the drive edges 1 and 2 and a window compare to intermediate on the receive edges 3 and 4.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

```
EARD? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {type}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EARD {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {type}, [err_type], {(pinlist)}, [MUX,] {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. You can enter a value between 0 and 2^48.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2^48.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

type

 |

This parameter specifies which actions will be reported. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

RCV

 |

Only receive edges are reported

 |
 |

 |

DRV

 |

Only drive edge actions are reported.

 |
 |

 |

BOTH

 |

Both drive and receive edge actions are reported. This is the default.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is used in the reply to inform about the recording mode, or if the specified cycle range is not included in the error map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

NOER

 |

Indicates that the part of the requested cycle range specified in the reply is outside the recorded error map.

 |
 |

 |

PF

 |

Indicates that the requested cycle range is included in the recorded error map, and that 1 bit results have been recorded.

 |
 |

 |

PFC

 |

Indicates that the requested cycle range is included in the recorded error map, and that 2 bit results have been recorded.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can use the @ character to read the error data for all pins.

For an HXA pin, specify one of the Pin Scale pins to which it is mapped.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. The format of the reconstructed data supports expanded device cycles with up to 10 waveforms and 16 edges per waveform. Edges without action are not reported.

 |
 |

 |

The data is to be decoded as follows:

 |
 |

 |

Byte 0:

 |

Contains multiplexing information for HXA pins. This byte is returned only once in the reply.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 7-4: Pin multiplexing factor. Specifies the number of Pin Scale pins that are mapped to one HXA pin or differential pin. 1 stands for differential pins or 2-multiplexed HXA pins, 3 for 4-multiplexed HXA pins.

The parameter is set to 0 for normal pins.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 3-0: Channel selector. If the pin multiplexing factor is > 0, this field specifies the logical position of the pin in the multiplexing order.

 |
 |

 |

 |

Information relating to HXA multiplexing is only returned if the MUX flag is set.

 |
 |

 |

Byte 1:

 |

Always 1. This byte is returned for every cycle.

 |
 |

 |

Byte 2,3:

 |

The number of actions to follow. The maximum, for an HXA pin mapped to 4 Pin Scale pins, is 640. This byte is returned for every cycle.

 |
 |

 |

Every edge action is described in 3 bytes.

 |
 |

 |

Byte A:

 |

Normal action or OOB action. Possible values are:

0: Normal action

1: OOB action

 |
 |

 |

Byte B:

 |

Edge index (0-7 for normal pins, up to 31 for HXA pins).

 |
 |

 |

Byte C:

 |

Action data

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 7: Action type. The following values can occur:

0: Drive action

1: Receive action

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 6-4: Received value, 0 for drive actions. For receive actions, the following codes can occur:

000: No error (expected = received)

001: Intermediate

010: 0

011: 1

101: Unstable

110: Reconstruction not possible

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 3-0: Expected compare/drive action.

The following values can occur for drive actions:

1010: Drive to 0, tri-state off

1011: Drive to 1, tri-state off

1110: Drive to 0, tri-state on

1111: Drive to 1, tri-state on

The following values can occur for receive actions:

0001: Edge compare to intermediate

0010: Edge compare to 0

0011: Edge compare to 1

0100: Edge compare to mask

0101: Edge compare to unstable

0110: Edge compare, reconstruction not possible

1001: Window compare to intermediate

1010: Window compare to 0

1011: Window compare to 1

1100: Window compare to mask

1101: Window compare to unstable

1110: Window compare, reconstruction not possible

1111: Window close

 |
 |

 |

 |

The codes for "reconstruction not possible" are only returned if the edge failed in single-ended standard mode with one bit results.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

```
> EARD? 2,1,BOTH,(TX1_d0)
< EARD 2,1,BOTH,PF,MUX,(TX1_d0),#9000000052
      \x10\x01\x00\x10
      \x00\x00\x82\x00\x01\x82\x00\x02\x82\x00\x03\x82\x00\x04\x82\x00\x05\x82\x00\x06\x82\x00\x07\x82
 \x00\x08\x82\x00\x09\x82\x00\x0a\x82\x00\x0b\x82\x00\x0c\x82\x00\x0d\x82\x00\x0e\x82\x00\x0f\x82
```

This example shows the results for a Pin Scale pin TX1_d0, which is multiplexed together with one other Pin Scale pin to an HXA pin. Since the MUX flag is set, the combined results of both these pins are returned in the reply.

Byte 0 indicates that TX1_d0 is one of two multiplexed Pin Scale pins, and that it has the logical position 0 in the multiplexing order. Byte 2 and 3 contain the information that the cycle contains 16 edges.

Byte A is the same for all edges and says that the edge is associated with a fixed value (not a data parameter), and that the waveform to which it belongs occupies position 0 in the device cycle. The edges of the two Pin Scale pins are interleaved according to the logical position in the multiplexing order. The edges of TX1_d0, which has position 0, are those with an even edge index (byte B), starting from 0. The edges of the other multiplexed Pin Scale pin (position 1) have an odd index. The actions (byte C) are also the same for all edges, namely an edge compare to 0 where expected = received value (that is, no error).

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

The EARD? answer will be split if the requested cycle range is greater than the available error map information, as shown below:

 !`Example`（raw: `../../../../raw/11910.png`）

```
> EARD? 0,15000, (pin1)
< EARD 0, 100, BOTH, NOER, (pin1), BinData        (a)
< EARD 100, 9900, BOTH, PF, (pin1), BinData       (b)
< EARD 10000, 5000, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData      (c)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARE  -  Edge Action REceived data）

```
EARE? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EARE? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, [err_type],{(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARE  -  Edge Action REceived data）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. You can enter a value between 0 and 2^48.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2^48.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can use the @ character to read the error data for all pins.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is optional and specifies what type of error information is available. The system returns a status only for O or IO pins:

 |
 |

ERON

 |

Error information is available. The cycle range where error information is available is reported by the query `VALD? - (VALid Data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.316_VALD__-__VALid_Data.md`）.

 |
 |

NOER

 |

Error information is not available. The reported range lies outside the range covered by the Error Map.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. The format of the reconstructed data supports expanded device cycles with up to 10 waveforms and 14 edges per waveform. Edges without action are not reported.

 |
 |

 |

The data is to be decoded as follows:

Each cycle of the reported cycle range is preceded by a two byte header information:

- First byte, bits 7, 6, 5, 4: Always zero, reserved for future use.
- First byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0: Always 1: number of waveforms contained in the device cycle.
- Second byte: Number of edge actions following (0 - 140)
 |
 |

 |

Each of the following edge actions is described by two bytes:

- First byte, bit 7: Channel selector for differential pins. The first channel has the value 0, the second the value 1.
- First byte, bits 6, 5, 4, 3: Waveform index (always 0)
- First byte, bits 2, 1, 0: Edge index (0 - 7)
- Second byte, bit 7: Error flag

0: No error on receive edge, or a drive edge

1: Error on receive edge. (The system returns this only if err_type is ERON.) In case of a failing window compare, both the window open edge and the window close edge are marked.

- Second byte, bits 6, 5: Data parameter

00: Fixed value

10: Data parameter 1

11: Data parameter 2

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bit 4: Edge direction

0: Drive/tri-state edge

1: Receive edge

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 0, then drive/tri-state data:

Bits 3, 2: Tri-state data

00: Not used

10: Tri-state off

11: Tri-state on

01: Reserved for future use

Bits 1, 0: Drive data

00: Not used

10: Drive 0

11: Drive 1

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 1, then receive data compare method:

0001: Edge compare to intermediate

0010: Edge compare to 0

0011: Edge compare to 1

0100: Edge compare to mask

0101: Edge compare to unstable

0110: Edge compare, reconstruction not possible

1001: Window compare to intermediate

1010: Window compare to 0

1011: Window compare to 1

1100: Window compare to mask

1101: Window compare to unstable

1110: Window compare, reconstruction not possible

1111: Window close

0000: Reserved for future use

0111: Reserved for future use

1000: Reserved for future use

 |

If reconstruction is not possible (code 110 on bits 2, 1, 0), there has been more than one edge or window compare within a single test system cycle.

If error bit 7 is set, an error has occurred on at least one of these edge or window compares.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EARE  -  Edge Action REceived data）

```
EARE? 0, 1, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
EARE 0,1,3,ERON,(pin1),#9000000010\x01\x04\x00\x0B\x01\x0A\x02\x9A\x03\x9F\x0A
```

This example returns edge action drive and received data (in hex notation) for one cycle. To decode the data, convert it into binary notation and use the lists above.

The data in binary format is:

```
0000 0001 0000 0100 0000 0000 0000 1011 0000 0001
0000 1010 0000 0010 1001 1010 0000 0011 0001 1111
```

The device cycle contains 1 waveform with 4 edge actions. The edge actions are RZ on the drive edges 1 and 2 and a failing window compare (received value: 0) on the receive edges 3 and 4.

The EARE? answer will be split if the requested cycle range is greater than the available error map information, as shown below:

 !`Example`（raw: `../../../../raw/11910.png`）

```
EARE? 0,15000, (pin1)
EARE 0, 100, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData (a)
EARE 100, 9900, 1, ERON, (pin1), BinData (b)
EARE 10000, 5000, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData (c)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EDDC  -  EDge in Device Cycle）

```
EDDC? [waveform_set], [timing_set], {edge_spec},
[dev_cyc_name], [dc_ref], [direction], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EDDC {edge_number}, {dev_cyc_name}, [reuse_flag], {(pinlist)}
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EDGE  -  EDGE errors）

```
EDGE? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EDGE {fail_string},{(pinlist)}
```

for each group of consecutive pins having the same result.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EDGE  -  EDGE errors）

|

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which edge direction definitions are to be read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the DFGP (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

fail_string

 |

One character per edge. F means failed and . means not failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EDGE  -  EDGE errors）

```
> EDGE? (pin1, pin2, pin3, pin4)
< EDGE ...F.... (pin1,pin2)
< EDGE .F..F... (pin3)
< EDGE ..F..... (pin4)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

```
EMAP? {pin_res},{start_cycle},{no_of_cycles},{resolution_mode},[results_per_cycle],[bits],{rep_mode},{results_align},[byte_max], [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EMAP {pin_res},{start_cycle},{no_of_cycles},{resolution_mode},{results_per_cycle},{bits},{rep_mode},{results_align},[byte_max],{(pinlist)}, [MUX,] {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

pin_res

 |

Specifies the pin granularity. Possible values are:

 |
 |

PPIN

 |

Separate results will be reported for every pin of the pin list.

 |
 |

COMB

 |

Only one global result will be reported for all pins of the pin list.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

In the query, this is an integer that defines the first test cycle to be reported.

In the reply, this is the first cycle that is returned. If the requested cycle range exceeds the capacity of the Error Map, the index of the first returned cycle may be greater than that of the first requested cycle.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of test cycles to be reported. The range for this parameter is 0 to2^48 - 1. In the reply, this parameter indicates the number of cycles which have been read. If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the requested range.

 |
 |

resolution_mode

 |

Defines how the recorded results are combined. Possible values are:

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

In this mode all recorded results are combined into one result per cycle.

 |
 |

SCYC

 |

In this mode the results are reported as they were recorded.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

This mode requests error information for each recorded receive edge. If the results_per_cycle parameter is omitted, the reply will return all 8 edges, even if only 2 or 4 edges were recorded; the edges that were not recorded will be represented as passed. In this way, the edge number of the failing recorded edges will be indicated by their position within the result data stream.

The EDGE option requires one of the following two sets of conditions to be satisfied:

- The mode parameter of DCRM is > 1.
- No result combination, as specified with the sub_cycles parameter of DCRM, contains more than 1 edge.

Note that this requires that result combinations are specified with DCRM.

- The edges in the sub_cycles string are in ascending order.

or (see `Retrieving edge information by repeating the test`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.02.01_Retrieving_edge_information_by_repeating_the_test.md`）):

- DCRM is set to 1,PFC.
- CYRM is set to EDGE.
- CYRP is set to MULT (the default).
 |
 |

results_per_cycle

 |

This parameter is only relevant for resolution mode EDGE. If you are only interested in an initial segment of the 8 edge sequence that is returned by default, you can specify the length of this segment here. In certain situations, this allows you to reduce the size of the reply.

If the MUX flag is set, and one of the specified PS (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the edges of the PS pins that are multiplexed to this HXA pin will be returned interleaved as follows:

r1 of PS pin 1, ..., r1 of PS pin n, r2 of PS pin 1, ..., r2 of PS pin n,...,

r8 of PS pin 1, ..., r8 of PS pin n

Here, n is 2 or 4, and the PS pins are ordered as defined in the BOARDCONF section of the model file.

Accordingly, if the multiplexing factor of the HXA pin is 4, and 5 edges per cycle are requested, then the first edge of every PS pin plus the second edge of the first PS pin will be returned.

 |
 |

bits

 |

Specifies how detailed the reported error code is to be in case of failure. Possible values are:

 |
 |

PF

 |

Only a 1 bit Pass/Fail result will be returned.

 |
 |

PFC

 |

In case of failure, a more detailed two bit code will be returned.

The received data can be reconstructed from the expected data and the error code as follows:

  !`Parameters`（raw: `../../../../raw/57171.png`）

"I" stands for "Intermediate" and "U" for "Unstable".

Note that 2 bit codes can only be reported if 2 bit codes were recorded (bits parameter of `DCRM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.46_DCRM__DCRM__-__Digital_Compare_Result_Mode.md`） set to PFC).

 |
 |

rep_mode

 |

Specifies the reporting mode for the Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All cycles within the selected area are reported. If the data was recorded in acquire failure mode, EMAP? will expand the reply accordingly.

 |
 |

EOLY

 |

As far as is feasible, only failed cycles are reported.

 |
 |

results_align

 |

Specifies how the results, as defined by the resolution_mode, results_per_cycle and bits parameters, are aligned within the returned data stream. The supported values are:

 |
 |

BYTE

 |

By this option, no byte will contain results of more than one cycle. If the results returned per cycle do not make up exactly one or two bytes, they will be padded accordingly.

Note that if two bit codes are requested for resolution mode EDGE, and results_per_cycle is set to a value < 8, the results will always be padded to two bytes, even if results_per_cycle is 鈮?4.

 |
 |

 |

PACK

 |

This option is mainly relevant for resolution modes CYCL and SCYC. It will have the effect that the results are not padded, but follow one another immediately. Thus, the results of 8 or 4 cycles (depending on the bits setting) will be packed into one byte in CYCL mode, and the results of 4 or 2 cycles (depending on the bits setting) will be packed into one byte in SCYC mode.

PACK will have an effect on resolution mode EDGE only, if the initial segment defined with results_per_cycle already makes up a complete byte. This would be the case, for example, if two bit codes are recorded for all 8 edges, and results_per_cycle is set to 4.

 |
 |

byte_max

 |

In the query, this parameter specifies the maximum number of bytes that may be returned. This option is primarily intended for the reporting mode EOLY, where the size of the data that will be returned cannot be calculated beforehand.

In the answer, the following codes can be returned:

 |
 |

EOB

 |

The cycle range of the query exceeds the specified maximum number of bytes.

 |
 |

EOF

 |

The cycle range of the query exceeds the cycle range to be recorded (as defined with `DCGM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.44_DCGM__DCGM__-__Digital_Compare_Global_Mode.md`） and `DCRP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.47_DCRP__DCRP__-__Digital_Compare_Result_Positioning.md`）).

 |
 |

EOM

 |

The cycle range of the query exceeds the actual content of the Error Map.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

In particular, if information on the edge level is requested, then the edges of all multiplexed Pin Scale pins will be returned interleaved as follows:

r1 of PS pin 1, ..., r1 of PS pin n,

r2 of PS pin 1, ..., r2 of PS pin n,

...

r8 of PS pin 1, ..., r8 of PS pin n

Here, n is 2 or 4, and the order of the PS pins is that defined in the BOARDCONF section of the model file.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins or pin groups for which information is returned. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in the pin list must have type O or IO. They must also all belong to the same port in the current start label.

If the MUX flag is set, then each pin in the pin list should represent a different HXA pin, and all HXA pins should have the same multiplexing factor.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

Nn1n2...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The data stream itself consists of blocks each of which contains result data for every cycle (passed as well as failed) within a contiguous cycle range. Every block has a header that specifies

- the number of the first cycle of the block (8 bytes, big-endian encoded), and
- the block size in bytes (4 bytes, big-endian encoded).

The result data is also big-endian encoded.

If the rep_mode parameter has been set to ALL, only one block is returned, which contains the whole selected result range.

If rep_mode has been set to EOLY, then EMAP? will close a block after a failed cycle, and start a new block at the next failed cycle, if the passed cycles in-between occupy at least as much space as a block header (12 bytes). See the first example below.

If you are working with HXA pins note that the block size specifies bytes, not cycles. Thus, a block of size 32 contains 4 cycles of a HXA pin with 4 multiplexed Pin Scale pins.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

```
> EMAP? COMB,0,42,EDGE,8,,EOLY,BYTE,,(dut_tx3)
< EMAP COMB,0,42,EDGE,8,PF,EOLY,BYTE,,(dut_tx3),#9000000038
  \x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x0F
  \x00\x00\x00\x03
  \x03\x00\x80
  \x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x1F
  \x00\x00\x00\x0B
  \x80\x00\x00\x80\xA0\x00\x80\xA0\x00\x00\x0A
```

This example shows the format of the binary data that is returned by EMAP?. The data stream has been broken up to make it more readable. Two data blocks are returned. The information is to be decoded as follows:

 |

Block

 |

Start cycle

 |

Number of cycles

 |

Failing edges

 |
 |

 |

Hex

 |

Dec

 |

Hex

 |

Dec

 |

 |
 |

1. block

 |

0F

 |

15

 |

3

 |

3

 |

edges 7,8 (03 = 00000011) in cycle 15

edge 1 (80 = 1000000) in cycle 17

 |
 |

2. block

 |

1F

 |

31

 |

0B

 |

11

 |

For example:

edge 1 (80 = 10000000) in cycle 31

edges 1,3 (A0 = 10100000) in cycle 35

 |

For each cycle, all 8 edges are reported. The first block is closed because 13 passing cycles (= 13 bytes) lie between the failed cycle 17 and the next failed cycle 31.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

```
> FTST?
< FTST F
> EMAP? COMB,0,50000000,EDGE,8,PF,EOLY,BYTE,3500000,(O1,O2)
< EMAP COMB,0,12000000,EDGE,8,PF,EOLY,BYTE,EOB,(O1,O2),#90003500000
```

This example illustrates the use of the byte_max parameter. The test comprises 50 million cycles. The Error Map is located in the RDRAM. If the number of errors exceeds 0.5% of the cycles, that is, as soon as more than 250,000 errors have been found, the device is to be rejected offhand. Therefore, EMAP? is called with the EOLY option, so that only failed cycles are returned, and the maximum length of the reply is restricted to 3,500,000. This is based on the worst case assumption that every error occupies 13 bytes. The answer indicates that in fact more than 0.5% of the cycles have failed. Note that only 7% of the 50 million test cycles have to be uploaded to the system controller.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

The following example illustrates the difference between the resolution modes EDGE and SCYC.

```
> DCRM? EMAP,(@)
< DCRM EMAP,4,PFC,"c1:1 c2:2 c3:7 c4:8",(@)
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,EDGE,,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,12,EDGE,8,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out),#224
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00001100   11000011   10000011   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000011   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000

> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,SCYC,,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,12,SCYC,4,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out),#224
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00001100   11110000   10110000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00110000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
```

The first failing cycle is cycle 0 (fifth byte in the second line of the EMAP? reply); in this cycle, edges 1,2,7,8 have failed. In addition, cycle 1 (edges 1,3,4) and 7 (edges 3,4) contain errors. With the PACK option, resolution mode SCYC compresses 12 bytes into 6:

```
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,SCYC,,PF,ALL,PACK,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,12,SCYC,4,PF,ALL,PACK,,(out),#218
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000110   11111011   00000000   00000000   00000011
     00000000   00000000
```

But the following call of EMAP? will produce an error message:

```
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,EDGE,4,PF,ALL,PACK,,(out)
```

The reason for this is that the results per cycle are only 4 bits long.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

The following example shows the expanded format for 2 bit error codes (2 bytes per cycle):

```
> DCRM? EMAP,(@)
< DCRM EMAP,4,PFC,"c1:1 c2:2 c3:3 c4:4",(@)
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,7,EDGE,,PFC,ALL,BYTE,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,7,EDGE,8,PFC,ALL,BYTE,,(out),#228
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00001110   11110011   00000000   00001111   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00001100   00000000
```

In cycle 0, edges 1, 2, and 4 have failed. In cycle 1, edges 3 and 4 have failed. In cycle 6, edge 3 has failed.

```
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,7,EDGE,4,PFC,ALL,PACK,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,7,EDGE,4,PFC,ALL,PACK,,(out),#220
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000111   11110011   00001111   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00001100
```

In this case, the PACK option is accepted because the initial segment of 4 two bit codes already makes up one byte.

|

no_of_vectors
