### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCC  -  ERror in Cycle range Count）

ERCC? {type}, {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}

returns:

ERCC {type}, {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles} [, granularity], {valid_code}, {no_of_errors}, [map_mode], [MUX,] {(pin)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCC  -  ERror in Cycle range Count）

|

type

 |

The type parameter can be:

 |
 |

ERCP

 |

Error count per pin. Each pin returns a separate answer.

 |
 |

ERCG

 |

Error count global, which requests the sum of all error counts reported by ERCP. Only one answer is generated.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

An integer that defines the cycle following which failures are to be counted. If the queried range starts before the analyze delay (see SQGB command) then the returned value will be corrected to a later cycle number.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

An integer that defines the cycle range in which failures are to be counted. If the queried start_cycle has to be corrected or the amount of failures causes an overflow of the error map then the returned value will be corrected to a smaller number of cycles.

 |
 |

granularity

 |

This parameter specifies how errors are condensed. Possible values are:

 |
 |

CYCL

   | The number of failing cycles is returned. |
 |

EDGE

   | The number of failing edges is returned. |
 |

valid_code

 |

This parameter tells you if the error count that the system returns is valid. The system may return:

 |
 |

VALD

 |

The error count is valid. This reply is always returned in offline mode.

 |
 |

OVFL

 |

This signifies an Error Map overflow. no_of_errors contains the number of errors that occurred until this happened.

 |
 |

LESS

 |

Either the start of the cycle range was before the error map error acquisition started or the end was after the test has ended or both. If an overflow condition and the less condition are both true, LESS is reported.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the errors from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to this HXA pin will be used to calculate the total number of errors.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which errors are to be counted. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to retrieve the data for all configured pins.

 |
 |

no_of_errors

 |

An integer that contains the number of errors found in the queried range of cycles. If the reported range of cycles is smaller than the queried range then this value represents only the number of errors in the reported range and not in the requested range. It should be regarded as the minimum number of errors in the requested range, and could be higher.

 |
 |

map_mode

 |

The system returns the current Error Map mode. This is:

 |
 |

F160

 |

The pin operating mode is Standard mode

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCC  -  ERror in Cycle range Count）

```
> ERCC? ERCP, 1000, 200, (pin1,pin2)
< ERCC ERCP, 1000, 200, VALD, 5, F160, (pin1)
< ERCC ERCP, 1000, 200, VALD, 1, F160, (pin2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCE  -  Expected and Received Cycle data of Events）

```
ERCE? {type},{start_cycle},{no_of_cycles},{data_format},{rep_mode}, [byte_max], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERCE  {type}, {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {data_format}, {rep_mode}, [error_status], {(pin)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCE  -  Expected and Received Cycle data of Events）

| type |

The supported types are:

 | RCV |

Requests received data only.

Can only be requested if a test point pattern has been executed for DC Scale pins.

 |
 | EXP  | Requests expected or setup data of all test point events, not only those that generate a result. |
 | ALL |

Requests both expected and received data of events that generate a result.

This option can only be requested if a test point pattern has been executed for DC Scale pins.

  | |
 | start_cycle  | The start cycle of the area from which event data is to be reported. Cycles are counted from 0. |
 | no_of_cycles  | The length of the cycle area from which event data is to be reported. |
 | data_format  | Specifies the binary data format of #spec(data). The DC Scale cards DPS32, VI32, and UHC4 / UHC4T support both formats.

 | 0  | This format contains PASS/FAIL and status information for every cycle. It can be used for status analysis where expected data and measurement values are not required. This format is only available for type RCV. |
 | 1 |

This format can return both received and expected data.

The received data of format 1 not only contains PASS/FAIL and status information for every measurement, but also the measurement type and value.

The expected data contains all the setup information of the respective event.

Format 1 is available for all three types RCV, EXP, and ALL).

   | |
 | rep_mode  | Specifies the reporting mode. Possible values are:

 | ALL  | Reports all results within the selected area. |
 | EOLY  | Reports only failed results including measurement errors (that is, too small a distance between two measurements, or type mismatch between measurement and range). This mode is not available for type EXP.  | |
 | byte_max |

In the query, this parameter specifies the maximum number of bytes that may be returned. This option can be used for the reporting mode EOLY, where the size of the data that will be returned cannot be calculated beforehand.

In the reply, this parameter is used to indicate the reason in case that not all the requested results can be returned:

 |
 |   | EOB  | The number of requested results exceeds the maximum buffer length specified with byte_max. |
 |   | EOF  | The result range of the query exceeds the length of the test. |
 |   | EOM  | This code is returned if the size of the answer exceeds the available storage capacity. |
 | pinlist  | Only DC Scale pins are considered. |
 | #spec(data) |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

#Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream

The N digit defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The data stream itself consists of a stream header and one or more answers (only one answer for data formats 0 and 1), where every answer contains the same number of data blocks.

The stream header defines

- the number of answers (4 long bytes, big-endian encoded)
- the number of data blocks per answer (4 long bytes, big-endian encoded).

Every data block consists of a block header and one data unit which contains the data of one event (td element).

The block header specifies the cycle number of the event anchor (defined with TPSE) (8 long bytes, big-endian encoded). The cycle number can be different from the event anchor, which is a vector number.

The length of the data units depends on the selected format and on the selected type. If type is set to ALL, each data unit consists of the expected data and the received data in this order.

Graphically, the structure can be illustrated by a simple example with a cycle range from 100 through 500 as follows:

 |
 |   !`ERCE? binary data`（raw: `../../../../raw/118685.png`） |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCE  -  Expected and Received Cycle data of Events）

The following example shows a query for expected data only in the cycle range from 0 through 60000.

```
> ERCE? EXP,0,60000,1,ALL,,(dpsPinMea)
< ERCE EXP,0,60000,1,ALL,,(dpsPinMea),#9000000405
    /x00/x00/x00/x01/x00/x00/x00/x0F
    /x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x46
    /x00/x1D
    /x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00
    /x40/x10/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00
    /x00
    /x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00/x00
    . . .
```

The data stream has been broken up to make it more readable. The answer contains 15 (`/x0F`) data blocks, of which only the first is displayed in the example. Its cycle number is 70 (`/x46`). The event is a voltage range definition (`x1D`) which is defined by DFTD as follows

```
DFTD "myNamespace",INSERT,(dpsPinMea),#2473<?xml version="1.0"?>
<testdata>
  <td id="setMeasVoltRange" type="dcset">
    <setMeasureRange type="voltage" minValue="0" maxValue="4"/>
 . . .
```

Since this is not a measurement event, the result check byte is set to 0. Note that the cycle number and the two range limits are big endian coded. The event contains no setForceValue operation.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCT  -  ERror CounT）

```
ERCT? {type}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERCT {type}, {valid_code}, {no_of_errors}, [map_mode], [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCT  -  ERror CounT）

|

type

 |

The type parameter can be:

 |
 |

ERCP

 |

Error count per pin, as delivered by the hardware error counter. The map_mode is always F160. For differential pins, the maximum of the specified pin and its counterpart is returned.

 |
 |

ERCG

 |

Error count global, which requests a sum of all error counts reported by ERCP. No map_mode information is returned.

 |
 |

EOLY

 |

The Errors OnLY option delivers the numbers of failed cycles per pin from the detailed Error Map. The map_mode is F160. For differential pins, the numbers of those cycles will be returned where at least one of the pins produced an error.

 |
 |

valid_code

 |

This parameter tells you if the error count the system returns is valid. The system may return:

 |
 |

VALD

 |

The error count is valid. (This reply is always returned in offline mode.)

 |
 |

OVFL

 |

Signifies error counter overflow. The hardware error counter has a range of 2^31.

 |
 |

no_of_errors

 |

This parameter returns the total number of results containing errors for one of the specified pins. For the ERCG type, it returns the sum of all the error counts for the individual pins.

 |
 |

map_mode

 |

The system returns the Error Map mode. The only possible value is:

 |
 |

F160

 |

The pin is operating in standard mode

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the errors from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to this HXA pin will be used to calculate the total number of errors.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The command returns the error count only for pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCT  -  ERror CounT）

```
> ERCT? ERCP, (Q0)
< ERCT ERCP, VALD, 1, F160, (Q0)
```

This example requests the error count for pin Q0. The system returns one error, the error count is valid, the map mode is F160.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCY  -  ERror CYcle）

```
ERCY? {type}, {start_cyc_no}, [no_of_cycles], [no_of_errors], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERCY {type}, {cycle_no}, [window_len], [expected_data], [received_data], [data_type], {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

type

 |

Selects the type of error data to be returned. The parameter can be:

 |
 |

CYC

 |

Only Error Cycles are returned.

 |
 |

EXP

 |

Error Cycles with expected data is returned.

 |
 |

REC

 |

Error Cycles with received data is returned.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Error Cycles with expected and received data is returned.

 |
 |

start_cyc_no

 |

An integer that defines the cycle following which failures are to be returned.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

An integer that defines the cycle range in which failures are to be reported. This parameter must be entered if the no_of_errors parameter has not been included.

 |
 |

no_of_errors

 |

This parameter determines how many cycles containing errors are to be returned for every pin, starting from start_cycle. This parameter must be entered if the no_of_cycles parameter has not been included.

 |
 |

cycle_no

 |

Specifies the cycle where an error has occurred.

 |
 |

window_len

 |

Window length is an optional parameter returned only if you have specified the error type EXP, REC or ALL and the cycle containing an error occurred during a window compare. The parameter window_len delivers the length of the compare window. A length of one test system cycle returns a 0. A length of two cycles returns a -1, and so on. An error occurring during a window compare is reported in the cycle where the compare window closes. The number of cycles making up the window is therefore negative.

In cases where cycle-boundary crossing takes place, the window_len parameter is useful when re-constructing in which cycle the error actually occurred.

 |
 |

expected_data

 |

Expected Data optional parameter. Returned only if the selected data type is EXP or ALL. The values returned can be:

 |
 |

F0

 |

expected data is 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

expected data is 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

expected data is intermediate

 |
 |

FU

 |

expected data is unstable

 |
 |

FN

 |

No reconstruction possible due to multiple compare edges in a single cycle. This will usually be the case when testing in X mode.

 |
 |

received_data

 |

Received Data optional parameter. Returned only if the selected data type is REC or ALL. The values returned can be:

 |
 |

F0

 |

received data is 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

received data is 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

received data is intermediate

 |
 |

FU

 |

received data is unstable

 |
 |

FN

 |

No reconstruction possible due to multiple compare edges in a single cycle. This will usually be the case when testing in X mode.

 |
 |

data_type

 |

Data Type optional parameter. Returned only if the selected data type is EXP, REC or ALL. The values returned can be:

 |
 |

FIX

 |

The edge or window compare was made to a fixed state.

 |
 |

E1

 |

The edge or window compare was made to the E1 parameter.

 |
 |

E2

 |

The edge or window compare was made to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

FE1

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to a fixed state, and one edge or window compare to the E1 parameter.

 |
 |

FE2

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to a fixed state, and one edge or window compare to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

E1E2

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to the E1 parameter and one edge or window compare to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

FE1E2

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to a fixed state, one edge or window compare to the E1 parameter and one edge or window compare to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

See also the `WAVE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.333_WAVE__WAVE__-__WAVEform.md`） command for an explanation of the expected data parameters.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which error cycles are to be retrieved. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to retrieve the data for all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERCY  -  ERror CYcle）

```
> ERCY? ALL,0,,2,(pin1,pin2)
< ERCY ALL,215,-2,F1,F0,E1,(pin1)
< ERCY ALL,240,,F0,FI,FIX,(pin1)
< ERCY ALL,17,,F0,F1,FIX,(pin2)
```

This example queries the system for the first two error cycles of pin1 and of pin2, starting from cycle 0. Expected and received data are also to be returned. The system returns the first two error cycles of pin1. For pin2 only one error cycle exists, therefore only one cycle can be returned.

There is an error on pin1 in cycle 215 which was a window compare 3 cycles long. The expected data was a 1, the receive data was a 0. The window compare was made to the E1 parameter.

There is an error on pin1 in cycle 240 which was an edge compare to a fixed state. The expected data was a 0, the received data was intermediate.

There is an error on pin2 in cycle 17 which was an edge compare to a fixed state. The expected data was 0, the received data was 1.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERMP  -  ERror MaP）

```
ERMP? {map_id}, {start_unit}, {no_of_units}, [map_mode],[edges,] [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERMP {map_id}, {start_unit}, {no_of_units}, {map_mode},[edges,] [MUX,] {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

map_id

 |

Determines the type of Error Map for which data is to be read out. Note that the allowed values depend on the settings of the DCRM command. Options that request two bit values can only be specified if the bits parameter of DCRM is set to PFC.

The possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

DERR

 |

This option provides per pin pass/fail results and full error codes per test cycle for all pins in the pinlist. The system returns values for the error codes PASS, FAIL1, FAIL2 and FAIL3 using a two-bit code as follows:

PASS 00

FAIL1 01

FAIL2 10

FAIL3 11

The received data can be reconstructed from the expected data and from the error code values in the following table:

 |
 |

 |

 |

 |

Expected Data

 |

FAIL1

 |

FAIL2

 |

FAIL3

 |
 |

Low

 |

Intermediate

 |

High

 |

Unstable

 |
 |

Intermediate

 |

High

 |

Low

 |

Unstable

 |
 |

High

 |

Low

 |

Intermediate

 |

Unstable

 |
 |

Unstable

 |

Low

 |

Intermediate

 |

High

   | |

 |
 |

 |

 |

Note that this mode requires that the DCRM command has been set to 1,PFC, and that the map_mode parameter of ERMP? is set to F160.

 |
 |

 |

EDGE

 |

This option reads the error map and returns an overall one bit Pass/Fail result (combining the results of all selected pins) of the edges selected by DCRM. The reply will not only return the results, but will also indicate the numbers of the recorded edges.

Note that this mode is only applicable if

- no result combination, as specified with the sub_cycles parameter of DCRM, contains more than 1 edge,
- the edges parameter is omitted or set to 8.
 |
 |

 |

EOLY

 |

The errors only error map delivers errors per pin. With this option, a two bit error code and the address of all those cycles will be returned at which errors have occurred. For more information on the error codes see the DERR option.

Note that this mode requires that the DCRM command has been set to 1,PFC.

 |
 |

 |

ERRM

 |

The error map option reads the Error Map and provides a single one-bit result per test system cycle for all pins in the pinlist. The result is:

0: Pass

1: Fail

 |
 |

 |

OVEM

 |

This option reads the Overview Error Map and provides a single result according to the compression factor set with DCRM. The returned pass/fail result is of the same type as for the ERRM option (one bit pass/fail). This option is only allowed if if the over view Error Map was set to FCM with DCRM in the last executed test.

 |
 |

 |

LMAP

 |

This option returns the results for the specified range of label calls within a burst. It is only allowed if the overview Error Map was set to LMAP with DCRM in the last executed test.

 Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 |

 |

RECD

 |

The receive data option reads the Error Map and provides per pin pass/fail result per test cycle for all pins in the pinlist. The returned pass/fail information is of the same type as for the ERRM option (one bit pass/fail).

 |
 |

start_unit

 |

For most values of map_id, this parameter defines the first recorded cycle that is to be reported. Note that depending on the selected map_id, the returned start cycle can be an earlier cycle than the requested start cycle.

If map_id is set to LMAP, then start_unit specifies the first label call of a burst that is to be reported. For this map_id option, only positive numbers are allowed.

 |
 |

no_of_units

 |

For most values of map_id, this parameter defines the number of cycles to be reported. The range for this parameter depends on the compression factor if OVEM has been selected. The specified number of cycles is adjusted to the existing cycles. If no existing cycle is included in the specified range, an error message is issued. It is recommended that you first determine the available cycle range with the VALD? query.

Note that depending on the selected map_id, the returned number of cycles can be greater than the requested number.

If map_id is set to LMAP, then no_of_units specifies the number of label calls within a burst that are to be reported.

 |
 |

map_mode

 |

Specifies how detailed the displayed error code is to be in case of failure. Note that the parameter is ignored for all values of map_id except EDGE. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

PF

 |

A one bit Pass/Fail result will be returned. This value is only allowed if DCRM has been set to 8,PF.

 |
 |

 |

F160

 |

This is equivalent to PF for the map_id value EDGE.

 |
 |

edges

 |

Specifies the number of edges for the EDGE option of the map_id parameter.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

In particular, if information on the edge level is requested, then the edges of all multiplexed Pin Scale pins will be returned interleaved as follows:

r1 of PS pin 1, ..., r1 of PS pin n, r2 of PS pin 1, ..., r2 of PS pin n, ..., r8 of PS pin 1, ..., r8 of PS pin n

Here, n is 2 or 4, and the order of the PS pins is that defined in the BOARDCONF section of the model file.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO pin types. They must also all belong to the same port of the current start label.

If the MUX flag is set, then each pin in the pin list should represent a different HXA pin, and all HXA pins should have the same multiplexing factor.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that is returned. The general format is:

#Nn1n2...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The structure of the data stream depends on the selected map_id value.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERMP  -  ERror MaP）

```
> ERMP? OVEM, 0, 16, F160,(Q0)
< ERMP OVEM,0,16,F160,(Q0),#9000000001 0x80
```

This example requests Overview Error Map data for the output pin Q0 in the Start Analysis mode between vectors 0 and 15.

```
> $ERMP? EDGE,0,7,F160,3,(Q0,Q7)
< ERMP EDGE,0,7,F160,3,(Q0,Q7),
  1100 0000  0000 0000  0010 0000  1100 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000 0000 0000
```

This example uses the "$" prefix, by which the binary data stream is represented bitwise by an ASCII "1" or "0" (see `Storing and Retrieving Binary Data`（raw: `02.06.01.03.04_Storing_and_Retrieving_Binary_Data.md`）). The call requests edge specific data for the output pins Q0, Q7. The first three receive edges of each of the first 7 cycles are queried. One byte is returned for every cycle. The result is that there are errors at edges 1 and 2 in cycle 0 and cycle 3, and an error at edge 3 in cycle 2. The other cycles contain no errors at the first three edges.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERRE  -  Expected and Received Results of Events）

```
ERRE? {type}, {resultIndex}, {numResults}, {data_format}, {rep_mode}, [byte_max] [,gang_index], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERRE {type}, {resultIndex}, {numResults}, {data_format}, {rep_mode}, [error_status] [, gang_index], {(pin)}, {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

type

 |

The supported types are:

- RCV

Requests received data only.

Can only be requested if a test point pattern has been executed for DC Scale pins, or a DC pattern was executed for digital pins.

- EXP

Requests expected data of only those test point events that generate a result.

This type is only allowed for test point patterns, not for DC patterns.

- ALL

Requests both expected and received data.

This type is only allowed for test points patterns, not for DC patterns.

 |
 |

resultIndex

 |

The index of the first result to be read. Only test point operations (MEAS instructions) that provide a result are counted, starting from 0.

 |
 |

numResults

 |

The number of results to be retrieved.

 |
 |

data_format

 |

Specifies the binary data format of #spec(data). The DC Scale cards DPS32, VI32, and UHC4 / UHC4T, as well as DC patterns, support both formats.

- `0`

This format contains PASS/FAIL and status information for every measurement. It can be used for status analysis where expected data and measurement values are not required. This format is only available for type RCV.

- `1`

For test point events, this format can return both received and expected data. Expected data are not available for DC patterns.

The received data of format 1 not only contains PASS/FAIL and status information for every measurement, but also the measurement type and value.

The expected data contains all the setup information of an event (td element) that contains a Measure operation.

Format 1 is available for all three types.

 |
 |

rep_mode

 |

Specifies the reporting mode. Possible values are:

- ALL:Reports all results within the selected area.
- EOLY: Reports only failed results including measurement errors (that is, too small a distance between two measurements, or type mismatch between measurement and range). This mode is not available for type EXP.
 |
 |

byte_max

 |

In the query, this parameter specifies the maximum number of bytes that may be returned. This option can be used for the reporting mode EOLY, where the size of the data that will be returned cannot be calculated beforehand.

In the reply, this parameter is used to indicate the reason in case that not all the requested results can be returned:

- EOB

The number of requested results exceeds the maximum buffer length specified with byte_max.

- EOF

The result range of the query exceeds the length of the test.

- EOM

This code is returned if the size of the answer exceeds the available storage capacity.

 |
 |

gang_index

 |

The index within the ganged channels for which data will be

answered. If this parameter is used, the connect_state (set with `PSLR`（raw: `02.06.02.02.194_PSLR__PSLR__-__Power_Supply_Level_Ranges.md`）) must be hdig or norm_hdig.

This only applies to test point measurements.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

DC Scale pins for which no test point pattern has been executed and digital pins for which no DC pattern has been executed will be ignored.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

#Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream

The N digit defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮? i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The data stream itself consists of a stream header and one or more answers (only one answer for data formats 0 and 1), where every answer contains the same number of data blocks.

The stream header defines

- the number of answers (4 long bytes, big-endian encoded)
- the number of data blocks per answer (4 long bytes, big-endian encoded).

Every data block consists of a block header and one or more data units each of which contains the result of one test point measurement or MEAS instruction (DC pattern).

The block header defines

- the index of the first result (4 long bytes, big-endian encoded)
- the number of successive results (4 long bytes, big-endian encoded).

If rep_mode is set to ALL, there will be only one block; if it is set to EOLY, there can be more than one.

The length of the data units depends on the selected format and on the selected type. If type is set to ALL, each data unit consists of the expected data and the received data in this order.

Graphically, the structure can be illustrated by a simple example of the EOLY reporting mode with type RCV as follows:

 |
 |  !`Format of data stream`（raw: `../../../../raw/101276.png`）

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ERRE  -  Expected and Received Results of Events）

```
# Get the number of available results
> VALR? (dpsPin)
< VALR CONS,10,(dpsPin)

# upload the first 5 received results in format 0
> ERRE? RCV,0,5,0,ALL,,,(dpsPin)
< ERRE RCV,0,5,0,ALL,(dpsPin),#9000000021
  \x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x01
  \x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x05
  \x00\x02\x00\x00\x0C
```

The data stream has been broken up to make it more readable. The first test point measurement failed because of a low limit violation, the fourth because of a low clamp violation.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ESGB  ESGB  -  Edge Search GloBal）

|

lin_step

 |

The lin_step parameter defines the step width (in ns) to be used for the linear searches which can be initiated by the TTRS? query. Any negative number entered in this parameter results in tests only being performed at the specified start and stop values. The default value for the linear_step is -1.000.

 |
 |

lin_bin_step

 |

The lin_bin_step parameter defines the step width (in ns) to be used for the combined linear and binary searches which can be initiated by the TTRS?, and TSUP? command queries. Any negative number entered in this parameter results in tests only being performed at the specified start and stop values. The default value for the lin_bin_step is 0.500.

 |
 |

min_pulse

 |

The min_pulse parameter defines the minimum pulse width (in ns) which can be used for the input pin searches initiated by the TSUP? and THLD? queries. The default value for the min_pulse is 0.000.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ESGB  ESGB  -  Edge Search GloBal）

```
ESGB 20,30,0
```

This example defines a 20 ns step width for linear search and a 30 ns step width for the combined linear/binary search. The minimum allowed pulse width is 0 ns.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ETDS  ETDS  -  Edge Timing Definition String）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query, you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *`equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

For a multi-port setup, specify the name of a multi-port specification.

Note that the multi-port specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multi-port specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Timing Set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by TSUS.

 |
 |

mode

 |

The operating mode. For the query, you can enter ALL for all modes or BIDIR for bidirectional mode, that is, for edges that serve both as drive and receive edges.

With fast pins, you can specify the mode DELTA for both the command and the query. In this mode, the delays specified for edges with an index > 1 are interpreted as offsets from the calculated default values.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

The definition string consists of a sequence of items each of which associates a delay with a drive or compare edge. On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, drive edges are denoted by dn. On Pin Scale 9G boards, there are two kinds of drive edges, which are denoted by fn and sn, respectively; for details see `Defining waveforms for Pin Scale 9G pins`（raw: `02.06.06.01.03.02_Defining_waveform_shapes_for_Smart_Scale_pins.md`）. You can also use the dn notation for Pin Scale 9G channels, but mixing both notations in one string is not allowed. Receive edges are always denoted by rn.

Unless you employ the pdiv statement for fast pins (see below), all edges which are not explicitly set remain unchanged.

The range of the edge delay is -8000 ns to +24000 ns (or -4 to +12 test system periods) for the Pin Scale 3600/800.

On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, the restrictions for edge ordering must be observed both in fixed and equation based timing. For example, you cannot assign a greater delay to d1 than to d3 if d1 precedes d3 in a waveform definition. For more information, see `Selecting and ordering edges`（raw: `02.06.06.01.03.01.02_Selecting_and_ordering_edges.md`）.

Note that with equation based timing, ETDS returns no error message when the edge order restrictions are violated.

On Pin Scale 9G boards, ordering of drive edges is not restricted in any way.

 |
 |

 |

Special Rules for Fast Pins:

If a pin is configured as a fast pin in the context of the specification given by the first parameter, you can specify the period divider at the start of the definition string. The format is pdiv:n, where n must be the same value as the period_div value of the pins in pinlist within the timing set specified by the timing_set parameter.

If you specify pdiv:nand a delay for the first edge, ETDS calculates delays for the following n-1 edges except those that are specified explicitly in the string. Note that for n = 3, the edges with index 1, 3, 5 are used for internal reasons.

If you omit either pdiv or the first edge, only the specified edges are modified. However, with receive edges this is only possible for r1.

The calculated delays are determined for the ith edge by the following formula:

 1st_edge_delay + (i-1) * (period/pdiv)

1st_edge_delay is the delay specified for the first edge (d1 or r1; the generic notation e1 is not allowed for fast pins). If the first edge is not specified in the string, its delay is set to 0. An example for the calculation will be given below.

Note that when both the period divider and a delay for the first edge are present in the definition string, then the delays for all the edges required by the period divider will be overwritten.

When a delay is explicitly specified for one of the edges, this delay overrides the calculated default. There are two formats to specify overrides. You can either define absolute delays or the offsets from the default delays.

If you want to use the second, relative format, you must specify DELTA for the modeparameter. Note that you can also specify negative offsets in the DELTA mode.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which edge delays are to be set or read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the DFGP (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

In a multi-port setup, every pin must belong to a port of the specified specification.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ETDS  ETDS  -  Edge Timing Definition String）

```
> ETDS 1,1,,"e1:0 e2:2 e3:6 e4:4",(io)
> ETDS 1,1,,"d1:0 d2:1 d3:2 d4:3 d5:4 d6:5 d7:6 d8:7",(clk)
> ETDS? 1,1,,(@)
< ETDS 1,1,,"d1:0 d2:2 d3:6 d4:4 r1:0 r2:2 r3:6 r4:4",(io)
< ETDS 1,1,,"d1:0 d2:1 d3:2 d4:3 d5:4 d6:5 d7:6 d8:7",(clk)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ETDS  ETDS  -  Edge Timing Definition String）

The following example shows the various possibilities for using ETDS with fast pins:

```
> ETDS? 401,1,,(CP)
< ETDS 401,1,,"pdiv:4 d1:0 d2:5 d3:10 d4:15",(CP)
> ETDS 401,1,,"d2:5.5",(CP)
> ETDS? 401,1,,(CP)
< ETDS 401,1,,"pdiv:4 d1:0 d2:5.5 d3:10 d4:15",(CP)
> ETDS 401,1,,"pdiv:4 d1:3 d3:14",(CP)
> ETDS? 401,1,,(CP)
< ETDS 401,1,,"pdiv:4 d1:3 d2:8 d3:14 d4:18",(CP)
> ETDS 401,1,DELTA,"d3:-1",(CP)
> ETDS? 401,1,,(CP)
< ETDS 401,1,,"pdiv:4 d1:3 d2:8 d3:12 d4:18",(CP)
> ETDS 401,1,DELTA,"pdiv:4 d1:0 d2:1 d4:-1",(CP)
> ETDS? 401,1,,(CP)
< ETDS 401,1,,"pdiv:4 d1:0 d2:6 d3:10 d4:14",(CP)
```

Note in particular the effect of the first instance of the command in DELTA mode. The negative offset is not applied to the actual value of d3, which is 14, but to the calculated default value, which is 13.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ETDS  ETDS  -  Edge Timing Definition String）

This example shows how to set and retrieve a delay of a multi-port specification:

```
> ETDS? "mu_timing",2,,(In1)
< ETDS ETDS "mu_timing",2,,"d1:0",(In1)
> ETDS "mu_timing",2,,"d1:0.5",(In1)
> ETDS? "mu_timing",2,,(In1)
< ETDS "mu_timing",2,,"d1:0.5",(In1)
```

The specification name and the pin name identify the port (no pin may occur in more than one port within the same specification). Then the port and the specification identify the equation set.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › ETIM  ETIM  -  Edge TIMing）

```
ETIM 1,1,2,4,8,6,10,,(DATA)
```

This example sets the edge delays for the pin group DATA specified for waveform set 1 and timing set 1. Edges 1 to 5 are set to 2,4,8,6 and 10 ns respectively, edge 6 is unused. If no previous setting for edge 6 exists in waveform set 1 and timing set 1, then its delay remains at 0.0 ns.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EUDS  -  Edge Usage Definition String）

```
EUDS? {waveform_set}, [mode], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EUDS {waveform_set}, {definition_string}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EUDS  -  Edge Usage Definition String）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter ALL for all defined waveform sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The waveform set must have previously been defined. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. Enter PRM to select the primary waveform set. Equation specs (101 to 9999) can be used for queries.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Not used.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

 |
 |

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

Thus, the specset ID consists of 3 or 4 digits, where the first two digits specify the equation set number, and the following two digits the spec set number.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The name of the wavetable. It must be enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

Edge usage definition string which consists of a list of all used edges. These are given as d1 through d8 (f1 through f8 and s1 through s8 on Smart Scale cards), and r1 through r8.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which edge usage definitions are to be read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the DFGP (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EUDS  -  Edge Usage Definition String）

```
EUDS? 1,,(@)
EUDS 1,"d1 d2 d3 r4",(io)
EUDS 1,"d1 d2 d3 d4 d5 d6 d7 d8",(clk)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EVCK  -  EVent ClocK）

```
EVCK? {"multi-port_spec"}, {(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
EVCK {"multi-port_spec"}, event_clock_per, {(port)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EVCK  -  EVent ClocK）

|

multi-port_spec

 |

Name of a multi-port timing specification.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

This query parameter specifies a list of ports that belong to the respective multi-port timing specification.

 |
 |

port

 |

This reply parameter specifies a port that belongs to the respective multi-port timing specification.

 |
 |

event_clock_per

 |

This reply parameter returns the event clock period of the respective port.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EVCK  -  EVent ClocK）

```
>  SCLK? "mu_burst"
<  SCLK "mu_burst",480
>  EVCK? "mu_burst",(@@)
<  EVCK "mu_burst",2448,(PortA)
<  EVCK "mu_burst",2448,(PortB)
<  EVCK "mu_burst",480,(PortD)
<  EVCK "mu_burst",480,(PortE)
```

This example returns the system clock period and the event clock periods for the multi-port timing specification `mu_burst`. The event clock periods of `PortD` and `PortE` equal the system clock period, those of `PortA` and `PortB` are different.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › EXSR -  EXecute SeaRch）
