### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

```
FFCI? {(no_ffcyc)} [,(port)]
```

returns:

```
FFCI {(no_ffcyc)}, {no_pins}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

| no_ffcyc  | Number of first failed cycles to be reported. |
 | port  | Specifies the port for the pins for which information is to be returned. If you omit this parameter information will be returned for the default port @ to which all configured pins belong. |
 | no_pins  | The number of O and IO pins. |
 | #spec(data) |

Prefix and pin error data in binary format:

- The prefix is defined as follows:

  - The number sign # marks the start of the data block.
  - One digit follows, indicating how many digits make up the following data length specifier.
  - A number of digits indicating the length (in bytes) of the data to follow.

- Binary data are available per reported cycle. The data for each cycle consists of two parts, the number of the failing cycle and the pin data, which indicates the failing pins of that cycle:

  - Cycle number:

The length of the cycle number is always 8 bytes.

  - Pin data:

The pin data consists of one byte per eight pins that belong to the specified port:

    - Each pin is represented by one bit.
    - An error on a particular pin is denoted by a 1, an error free pin by a 0.
    - Bits of the pin data are filled starting from the left (MSB) side.
    - If the number of configured channels of the specified port is not divisible by 8, the last byte of pin data contains unused bits on the right (LSB) side.

Mapping of the bits in the pin data block to the individual pins:

- The I / IO pins are sorted based on their pogo number defined for the first site.
- The sorted pins are mapped starting on the left (MSB) side of the first byte of the pin data block.
- The information how the pins are mapped can be read by command `FFPM? (First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping)`（raw: `02.06.11.02.24_FFPM___First_Failing_cycle_information_Pin_Mapping.md`）.
 |

### Example 1: Firmware view（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

```
$FFCI? 2
FFCI 2,7,#218
  00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000011
  01100000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  00010000 00010000
```

This example for `Firmware view`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.08.08_Firmware_view.md`） queries the first two cycles where failures have occurred on an output pin of the default port, that is, on any configured output pin. Note: For the query, you must use the prefix $ so that the binary data are represented by ASCII 1 or 0.

The answer is to be interpreted as follows:

- `FFCI 2,7` means that 2 cycles are reported and 7 output pins are configured. Since this entails that one byte is sufficient for the pin data, the binary data needs only one byte for the pin data consists of 2 * 9 bytes.
- `#218` defines the size of the following binary data: 2 digits for the length specifier followed by the length specifier itself that indicates a length of 18 for the binary data.
- The Firmware view displays the cycle numbers and pin data as groups of eight bytes that must be evaluated as follows:

  - Failed cycle # 3:

    - The cycle number 3 is defined by the first eight address bytes `0000000` 鈥? `00000011`.
    - The 9th byte `01100000` shows failures on the 2nd and 3rd pin: Value 0 of the MSB on the left represents the passing 1st pin.

  - Failed cycle # 16:

    - The next eight bytes 10 鈥?17 (`00000000` 鈥? `00010000`) define the cycle number 16.
    - The last byte 18 (`00010000`) shows that the fourth pin failed.

For the assignment from bits of the pin data bytes to the configured pins, refer to `#spec(data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__r_specData`）, the `following example`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__d_Example_2`） and to firmware command `FFPM? (First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping)`（raw: `02.06.11.02.24_FFPM___First_Failing_cycle_information_Pin_Mapping.md`）.

The FFCI? command can also be executed using API `FW_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.77_FW_TASK.md`）. You must use the syntax `FWTASK_STATUS FW_TASK(const STRING& command, FW_ResultData & resultdata);` to retrieve the binary data.

### Example 2: Sort order of pins（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

The pogo numbers of the following example setup are assigned in descending order to emphasize that the order of the pogo numbers and not the order of the definition by `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） matters.

```
DFPN 11105,"",(pinA)
DFPN 11104,"",(pinB)
DFPN 11103,"",(pinC)
DFPN 11102,"",(pinD)
DFPN 11101,"",(pinE)
CONF IO,F160,(pinA)
CONF I,F160,(pinB,pinC)
CONF O,F160,(pinD,pinE)
```

The FFCI? command will sort I / IO pins based on their pogo number defined for the first site resulting in the pin list pinE, pinD, pinA. The two pins pinB and pinC have no output capability and, therefore, will not be included in the FFCI? answer.

Assuming a test has been executed where pinA passes, but pinD and pinE fail for every cycle, the FFCI? answer for the first two failing cycles now would look like this:

```
FFCI? 2
FFCI 2,3,#218
  00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  11000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  00000001 11000000
```

 The binary data of the answer is to be interpreted as follows:

- Byte 1 鈥?8: Address of the first cycle (`00000000` 鈥? `00000000` = 0)
- Byte 9: Pin data `11000000`
- Byte 10 鈥?17: Address of the second cycle (`00000000` 鈥? `00000001` = 1)
- Byte 18: Pin data `11000000`

Byte 9 and 18 show that the first two pins on the left side (MSB) are failing. According to the sorting scheme that is defined in the FFCI parameter description for `#spec(data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__r_specData`）, the failed pins are pinE (Channel 11101 and pinD (Channel 11102).

The `FFPM?`（raw: `02.06.11.02.24_FFPM___First_Failing_cycle_information_Pin_Mapping.md`） firmware command will return `FFPM 3,(pinE,pinD,pinA)` as pinE, pinD and pinA are configured for the I / IO mode. The pin list is sorted by the pogo number defined for the first site.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FLBL  -  Failing LaBeLs）

```
FLBL? {cycle_info},[start_cycle]},[no_of_cycles],{(port)}
```

returns:

```
FLBL {index_of_call},{label_name},{cycle_info}, [ffc_abs],[ffc_rel],[ffv], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FLBL  -  Failing LaBeLs）

|

cycle_info

 |

This parameter specifies which information is to be retrieved about the first failing cycle of the labels. Possible values are:.

 |
 |

 |

AFFC

 |

Returns the first failing cycle relative to the start of the burst.

 |
 |

 |

RFFC

 |

Returns the first failing cycle relative to the start of the label.

 |
 |

 |

FFCS

 |

Both numbers, relative to the start of the burst and relative to the start of the label, are returned.

 |
 |

 |

FFV

 |

Returns the first failing vector and the first failing cycle relative to the start of the label.

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

Returns the first failing cycle relative to the start of the burst and relative to the start of the label, and the first failing vector relative to the start of the label

 |
 |

 |

NONE

 |

No information about first failing cycles is provided.

 |
 |

index_of_call

 |

This reply parameter specifies the index of the call for which the label name is returned.

 |
 |

label_name

 |

This reply parameter specifies the name of the label that was called at the position index_of_call.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

This reply parameter specifies the start cycle of the label within the burst. It is omitted if reconstruction of the label is not possible.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This reply parameter specifies the number of cycles of the label. It is omitted in the reply if reconstruction of the label is not possible.

If it is omitted in the query, the reply depends on the value for start_cycle:

- If both start_cycle and no_of_cycles are omitted, FLBL? returns information about the complete test.
- If no_of_cycles is omitted, but start_cycle is not, FLBL? returns information about the start cycle.

If you want to get information about an end segment of the test, simply specify a number which is certainly greater than the size of the end segment.

 |
 |

port

 |

Specifies the port for which label information is requested. The port is also returned in the reply if cycle_info is set to NONE.

 |
 |

ffc_abs

 |

The first failing cycle relative to the start of the burst.

There are two special return values:

 |
 |

 |

-1

 |

The label contains errors, but recording started too late.

 |
 |

 |

-2

 |

The label contains errors, but the detailed error map is already full.

 |
 |

ffc_rel

 |

The first failing cycle relative to the start of the label.

 |
 |

ffv

 |

The first failing vector relative to the start of the label.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This reply parameter specifies the pins of the port which fail for the first time in the same cycle within the specified label. A pinlist is returned if cycle_info is not NONE.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FLBL  -  Failing LaBeLs）

```
> FLBL? ALL,0,105,(@)
< FLBL 1,"MainFailures",ALL,26,10,10,(Read)
< FLBL 1,"MainFailures",ALL,25,9,9,(Write,RowAS)
< FLBL 1,"MainFailures",ALL,20,4,4,(Addr3)
< FLBL 1,"MainFailures",ALL,23,7,7,(Data0,Data1,Data2,Data3)
< FLBL 3,"MainRowAsFail",ALL,82,18,6,(RowAS)
< FLBL 4,"MainWriteFail",ALL,92,4,4,(Write)
< FLBL 5,"MainFailures",ALL,114,10,10,(Read)
< FLBL 5,"MainFailures",ALL,113,9,9,(Write,RowAS)
< FLBL 5,"MainFailures\",ALL,108,4,4,(Addr3)
```

This example returns all available information for a single-port burst from cycle 0 through 104. The first two replies for the first call of label MainFailures are to be read as follows: Pin Read fails at cycle 26, counted from the start of the burst, which is 10 counted from the start of the label. The pins Write and RoWAS already fail at cycle 25, respectively 9.

Note that the fifth call is included in the reply although none of its failing cycles is inside the requested cycle range. Every failing label which has at least one cycle in the specified range is reported.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FLSH -  FLuSH buffered commands）

```
FLSH {MUX}, {"init_flags"}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FLSH -  FLuSH buffered commands）

|

MUX

 |

The optional MUX parameter is designed to be used as an execution code of a testflow that is generated by the system software for disconnecting the particular sites (not for user programming).

Do not use this parameter for programming a user procedure or executing the FLSH command from the hpt.

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTCG  FTCG  -  Functional Test ConfiGure）

FTCG

```
FTCG {parameter}, {mode}, {(portlist)}
```

  FTCG?

```
FTCG? {parameter}, {(@@)}
```

returns:

```
FTCG {parameter}, {mode}, {(portlist)}
```

  Parameters

 |

parameter

 |

The parameter to be used is SKPR (SKip PRimaries).

 |
 |

mode

 |

Specifies different activation conditions. This option can take the following values:

 |
 |

ON

 |

Suppresses activation of all primary sets at the start of a functional test for the sequencing groups of the ports specified by the portlist parameter. This option serves to keep a PLL alive across functional tests.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Allows activation for the ports specified by the portlist parameter. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

NEVER

 |

By this option, the primary sets will always be loaded at the start of a test for all ports of the sequencing groups to which the ports specified by the portlist parameter belong.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

In the command, specify a list of ports, separated by commas. Note that the ports are treated as representatives of their sequencing groups. Activation will be suppressed, allowed, or enforced not only for the specified ports, but for all member ports of the sequencing groups to which the specified ports belong in the current setup.

In the query, specify @@, which stands for all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTCG  FTCG  -  Functional Test ConfiGure）

The following example illustrates the dependence of the FTCG command on the current sequencing group definitions.

```
> SQLB "MP_burst1",MPBU,28,31,"SG1",(clock)
> SQLB "MP_burst1",MPBU,28,29,"SG2",(data1)
> SQLB "MP_burst1",MPBU,31,32,"SG2",(data2)
> SQLB "MP_burst2",MPBU,32,33,"SG1",(clock)
> SQLB "MP_burst2",MPBU,30,31,"SG1",(data1)
> SQLB "MP_burst2",MPBU,33,34,"SG2",(data2)
> FTCG SKPR,ON,(clock)
> FTCG SKPR,NEVER,(data2)
> SPRM "cont_clock",,,
> SQSL "MP_burst1"
> SQGB ACQF,0
> FTST?
...
> SQSL "MP_burst2"
> FTST?
...
```

In the first functional test, sequencing group `SG1` only contains the port `clock`, and therefore activation of primary sets is suppressed at the start of `MP_burst1` only for `clock`, whereas it is enforced for ports `data1` and `data2`. In the second test, `SG1` contains both `clock` and `data1`, and therefore activation is suppressed for both these ports at the start of `MP_burst2`, and enforced only for `data2`.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTSM  FTSM  -  Functional Test Set Mask）

```
FTSM {mode}, [run_to], [mask_before], [mask_after][,(ref_port)]
FTSM?
FTSM?
```

returns:

```
FTSM CLEAR, , ,
```

or

```
FTSM SET, [run_to], [mask_before], [mask_after][,(ref_port)]
```

  Parameters

 | mode  | Lets you set the mode of the FTSM command. The mode can be: |
 | SET  | In this mode the parameters run_to, mask_before, and mask_after are set and used in the next sequencer run. The original SQGB values are saved and restored with the next FTSM CLEAR command. |
 | CLEAR  | The FTSM parameters run_to, mask_before, and mask_after will be ignored by subsequent sequencer runs. Instead, the original SQGB values are restored. Original values are the values that had been active before execution of the FTSM SET command to set a specific mask. |
 | run_to |

The pattern is executed up to the specified cycle, including this cycle. This parameter cannot be used together with the mask_before or mask_after parameter except for two cases:

- If the mask_before parameter is set to 0.
- If the run_to parameter is set to N and the mask_after parameter to N + 1.

The cycle number must be within the range [0 ... 2^48 - 2]

 |
 | mask_before |

All cycles before the specified cycle are masked and do not contribute to the pass/fail result. The specified cycle is not masked.

If mask_before is not a multiple of 8, cycles will be recorded starting from the next lowest multiple of 8, but those up to the specified cycle will be discarded afterwards.

 |
 | mask_after  | All cycles after the specified cycle are masked and do not contribute to the pass/fail result. The specified cycle is not masked. (Recording will run to the end of the test, but the cycles following the specified one will be discarded afterwards.) |
 | ref_port |

For a multi-port burst, this parameter specifies the reference port to which the cycle numbers of the run_to, mask_before, and mask_after parameters refer.

If you have set the run_to parameter, then the sequencers will be stopped for all ports after the reference port has completed the requested number of cycles. The mask_before, and mask_after parameters are only applied to the specified port. The other ports will not be masked,

Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

   |  Application Used in the parametric functional test. Errors and warnings

An error is generated if:

- A value (run_to, mask_before, mask_after) is not in the valid range of [0... 2^48 - 2].
- The run_to and mask_before parameters are specified, and run_to is equal or bigger than mask_before.
- The run_to and the mask_after parameters are specified, and run_to is bigger than mask_after.

A warning is generated if:

- The run_to parameter and the mask_before parameter are specified and run_to < mask_before. In this case the pattern executed will always pass as all cycles executed are masked out for result evaluation.
- The run_to parameter and the mask_after parameter are specified and run_to <= mask_after. In this case the entry for the mask_after parameter can be omitted as the sequencer will not even execute the cycles that are masked out.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTSM  FTSM  -  Functional Test Set Mask）

```
FTSM?
```

returns:

```
FTSM CLEAR, , ,
FTSM SET, ,10,20
```

The FTSM? query returns the current FTSM settings.

The FTSM SET command masks all cycles except for those in the range from cycle 10 to cycle 20.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

```
FTST? ["exec_context"]
```

returns:

```
FTST {result_flag}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

| exec_context  | An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`）. |
 | result_flag  | This is returned by the system when the functional test has finished. It can be:

 |   | P  | is returned if the functional test passes. |
 |   | F  | is returned if the functional test fails.  | |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

```
FTST?
```

returns:

```
FTST P
```

This example returns a pass result for the functional test.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FXDL  FXDL  -  FiXture DeLay）

|

channel

 |

The test system channel number of the digital channel. This is a five digit field. See `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for the number. You can type ALL to set the attributes for all installed channels. For the query, you can type CFG to query only configured channels.

 |
 |

fixture_delay

 |

The fixture_delay represents the delay (in ns) of the lines on the DUT board. The range of the admissible values depends on the test system type as follows:

- PS1600: Between -0.015 and +26.4 ns

The default value is 0. The maximum number of digits after the decimal point is 3.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › FXDL  FXDL  -  FiXture DeLay）

```
FXDL 10101,2.5
```

This example sets the fixture delay of channel 10101 to 2.5 ns.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GCTX  -  Get ConTeXt）

```
GCTX? {setup_type},[setup_comp]
```

returns:

GCTX {setup_type}{,setup_nr|"name"},"[context_name]"

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GCTX  -  Get ConTeXt）

|

setup_type

 |

The type of the setup component for which the mode context is queried. Possible values are:

 |
 |

TIM

 |

Timing equation set

 |
 |

LEV

 |

Level equation set

 |
 |

WAVE

 |

Wavetable

 |
 |

LBL

 |

Sequencer label

 |
 |

SPCF

 |

Multi-port specification

 |
 |

CURR

 |

The mode context for the current primary sets (as defined with the SPRM command) and the current start label (as defined with the SQSL command).

 |
 |

setup_nr

 |

The number of a setup component. This parameter is ignored for setup type CURR.

 |
 |

name

 |

The name of a wavetable, or the name of a multi-port specification. This parameter is ignored for setup type CURR.

 |
 |

context_name

 |

The name of the mode context. If you specified CURR for the setup_type parameter, and the current mode context is not correct, GCTX? returns an empty string.

The context is only correct when all primary sets (defined by SPRM) and the current start label (defined by SQSL) are associated with the same mode context. Furthermore, if there exists a primary multi-port specification, the mode context must be the same for all ports of this specification.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GCTX  -  Get ConTeXt）

```
> GCTX? TIM,101
< GCTX TIM,101,"High-Speed"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETA  -  GET vector memory Address information）

GETA? {type}, [param_1], {param_2}, {(pinlist)}

returns:

GETA {type}, {param_1}, {param_2}, {applic}, {start_addr}, {length}, {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETA  -  GET vector memory Address information）

|

type

 |

Specifies the type of test for which vector area address information is required. The only allowed value is VEC (for VECtors).

 |
 |

param_1

 |

param_1 requires a label name. The present implementation always takes the label currently activated with the TSTL command, so you must leave this parameter blank in the query. The reply specifies the currently activated label.

 |
 |

param_2

 |

param_2 requires a logical vector number.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to obtain data for all pins.

 |
 |

applic

 |

A reply parameter. Returns the type of the test application:

 |
 |

PARA

 |

Parallel test.

 |
 |

start_addr

 |

A reply parameter. It returns the absolute address of the queried vector in the vector area.

 |
 |

length

 |

A reply parameter. It returns an integer giving the remaining active vectors of the sequencer construct starting from the queried vector.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETA  -  GET vector memory Address information）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> GETA? VEC,,9,(S0_1)
< GETA VEC,"test_1",9,PARA,520,6,(S0_1)
```

This example queries the absolute address of the parallel vector with the logical vector number 9 (the first active vector of the RPTV instruction) in the label test_1 for pin S0_1. Note that 7 padding vectors exist between the last active vector of the GENV instruction and the first active vector of the RPTV instruction.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETC  -  GET Cycles）

```
GETC? {(vector_no)}
```

returns:

```
GETC {(cycle_no)}
```

Parameters
 |

vector_no

 |

The vector number for which you want to obtain the matching cycle number. vector_no must be a positive integer that does not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

cycle_no

 |

The number of the cycle that results when the vector at vector_no is executed. The cycle numbers do not always linearly follow the vector numbers. The relationship between the two depends on the sequencer program. The system returns a cycle_no in the range of 0 to 2^48.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETC  -  GET Cycles）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,103,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,7,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,MACT,256,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,GENV,1,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,MRPT,1,,,(@)
< SQPG 7,RPTV,1544,100,,(@)
< SQPG 8,GENV,1,,,(@)
< SQPG 9,STOP,,,,(@)
> GETC? 112
< GETC 104
> GETC? 1656
< GETC 154504
```

In this example, the cycle numbers are calculated from the expected values. Vector 112 is the first vector after the match loop. The last 6 vectors before the match loop are not recorded in the Error Map, because the sequencers consider them to be part of the match loop (see `Counted match loops`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01_Counted_match_loops.md`）). The two match loop vectors proper are also not recorded in the Error Map. Since no other loop has occurred before vector 112, the cycle number corresponding to vector 112 is calculated as 112 - 8 = 104.

The cycle number of vector 1656, the last vector of the label, is calculated as 104 + 100 * 1544 = 154504.

The calculation is more complicated if it is based on the received data, because the last match loop cycles may be recorded in the Error Map (see again `Counted match loops`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01_Counted_match_loops.md`）).

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETL  -  GET Label）

```
GETL? {index_first_call},[number_of_calls], {(pin_or_port)}
```

returns:

```
GETL {index_of_call},{label_name}, [start_cycle], [number_of_cycles], {(pin_or_port)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETL  -  GET Label）

|

index_first_call

 |

Specifies the index of the first label call within the burst for which the name is requested.

 |
 |

number_of_calls

 |

The number of label calls for which the name is requested.

 |
 |

index_of_call

 |

This reply parameter specifies the index of the call for which the label name is returned.

 |
 |

label_name

 |

This reply parameter specifies the name of the label that was called at the position index_of_call.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

This reply parameter specifies the start cycle of the label within the burst. It is omitted if reconstruction of the label is not possible.

 |
 |

number_of_cycles

 |

This reply parameter specifies the number of cycles of the label. It is omitted if reconstruction of the label is not possible.

 |
 |

pin_or_port

 |

Specifies the pin or port for which label information is requested.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETL  -  GET Label）

```
> GETL? 0,9,(@)
< GETL 0,"MainInit",0,16,(@)
< GETL 1,"MainFailures",16,24,(@)
< GETL 2,"MainPassing",40,24,(@)
< GETL 3,"MainFailures",64,24,(@)
< GETL 4,"MainPassing",88,24,(@)
< GETL 5,"MainFailures",112,24,(@)
< GETL 6,"MainPassing",136,24,(@)
< GETL 7,"MainFailures",160,24,(@)
< GETL 8,"MainDataFail",184,24,(@)
```

In this example, the label names are requested for the first 9 calls of the burst that was executed as the last test. Note that certain labels are called more than once.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETN  -  GEt Testdata Name）

```
GETN? {range_type}, {index}, {length}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns

```
GETN? {range_type}, {index}, {testdata_name}, {identifier}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETN  -  GEt Testdata Name）

|

range_type

 |

This parameter determines how the index and length parameters are to be interpreted. Possible options are:

CYCL index and length refer to cycles

RSLT index and length refer to results

 |
 |

start_index

 |

In the query, this parameter specifies the start of the range to be scanned. In the reply, it specifies the index of the event whose name is reported.

 Depending on the range_type parameter, this is a cycle or a result index.

 |
 |

length

 |

Specifies the length of the area to be scanned. Depending on the range_type parameter, this is a number of cycles or of results.

 |
 |

name_space

 |

This reply parameter specifies the name space of the respective event, as defined with DFTD.

 |
 |

identifier

 |

This reply parameter specifies the identifier of the respective event, as defined with DFTD.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Only DC Scale pins are taken into account.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETN  -  GEt Testdata Name）

```
> FTST?
< FTST P

> VALR? (Sdd)
< VALR CONS,10,(Sdd)

> GETN? RSLT,0,1,(Sdd)
< GETN RSLT,0,"powercycle","meaLimV_0.0_0.2",(Sdd)

> VALC? (Sdd)
< VALC CONS,0,50000,(Sdd)

> GETN? CYCL,0,41000,(Sdd)
< GETN CYCL,63,"powercycle","setRange7V",(Sdd)
< GETN CYCL,40199,"powercycle","meaLimV_0.0_0.2",(Sdd)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETS  -  GET Sets）

```
GETS? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
GETS {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, {level_set}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

start_cycle

 |

The start cycle is an integer that defines the first cycle to be reported. The start cycle is in the range 0 to 2^48 when the sequencer runs in the Start Analysis mode, or -2^48 to -1 when the sequencer runs in the Stop Analysis mode. If a positive number is entered, cycles are counted from 0 upwards. If a negative value is entered, the cycles are counted from the end of the test at -1. The start cycle returned by the system may be different from the start cycle entered for the query.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

In the command, this parameter defines the number of cycles to be reported. The integer must be in the range 0 to 2147483648.

In the reply, the parameter specifies the number of cycles that are generated with the timing and levels sets specified by the timing_set and level_set parameters. 0 is returned if a CLEV and a CTIM instruction follow each other immediately.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to return the sequencer instructions for all pins.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

level_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the level set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 *`equation_set_no `+ 1000 * `specset_no `+ `level_set_no

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETS  -  GET Sets）

```
GETS? 0,2000,(Q0)
```

This example requests the timing and level set information for the first 2000 test cycles of pin `Q0`. The response may be as follows:

```
GETS 0,160,2,1,(Q0)
GETS 160,704,1,1,(Q0)
GETS 864,1136,2,1,(Q0)
```

The first 160 cycles were generated with timing set 2 and level set 1, the next 704 cycles with timing set 1 and level set 1, and the last 1136 cycles with timing set 2 and level set 1 again.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETV  -  GET Vectors）

```
GETV? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
GETV {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {start_vector}, {no_of_vectors}, {seq_status}, {"label"|"scan_template"}, [instance], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETV  -  GET Vectors）

|

start_cycle

 |

An integer that defines the first cycle to be reported. It is in the range 0 to 2^48 when the sequencer runs in the Start Analysis mode, or -2^48 to -1 when the sequencer runs in the Stop Analysis mode. If a positive number is entered, cycles are counted from 0 upwards. If a negative value is entered, the cycles are counted from the end of the test at -1.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

Defines the number of cycles to be reported. The integer must be in the range 0 to 2147483648 (2^31).

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

start_vector

 |

Returns the logical number of the start vector for the instruction specified by the seq_status parameter within the test specified by the label parameter.

The logical vector number counts the active vectors within one label, starting from 0. If the vectors generated by the instruction are break vectors, then -1 is returned.

 |
 |

no_of_vectors

 |

Returns the vector length of the instruction specified by the seq_status parameter. If the vectors generated in the requested range are break vectors, then the parameter returns -1.

 |
 |

seq_status

 |

Returns the current sequencer status. The status is expressed on most occasions in the form of the sequencer instruction that was used to generate a segment of the vectors in the requested cycle range. Otherwise it is expressed in terms of the current sequencer activity. Note that seq_status is not the same as the sequencer state determined by `SQST, SQST? - (SeQuencer STate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.241_SQST__SQST__-__SeQuencer_STate.md`）. Sequencer instructions are parameters to `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）. For additional information on sequencer programming see also `Vector Setup Commands`（raw: `02.06.07_Vector_Setup_Commands.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

The seq_status parameter is required for the reconstruction of received data. Some of the values it returns signify that vectors are being generated, others inform of sequencer status changes, which cause some or no break vectors to be generated.

 |
 |

 |

GENV

 |

This is returned if GENV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range. The number of vectors generated equals the no_of_vectors.

 |
 |

 |

SRCV

 |

This is returned if SRCV is the sequencer instruction that generates vectors in the reported cycle range.

For "non-source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the parallel vectors exactly the same way as RPTV. That means "no_of_vectors" parallel vectors are repeated for a repeating count (equal to no_of_cycles divided by no_of_vectors) to generate "no_of_cycles" cycles on the test system.

For "source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the vectors stored in the source memory. It means "no_of_cycles" vectors are generated from the source memory to produce "no_of_cycles" cycle on the test system, and the information of "no_of_vectors" has no meaning to "source pin".

 |
 |

 |

RPTV

 |

This is returned if RPTV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range. In order to obtain the number of repetitions divide no_of_cycles by no_of_vectors.

You can stop a repeat loop by hitting BREAK in the user interface. The seq_status may then still be RPTV because the BREAK occurs asynchronously to the execution of the loop.

 |
 |

 |

JPPS

 |

This is returned if the parallel vectors for the reported cycles were generated by a per-pin subroutine.

 |
 |

 |

CTIM

 |

This is returned if a change timing instruction has been issued in the queried cycle range. Each timing change generates break vectors.

The actual number of break cycles depends on the test system period and will not be shown in the cycle reconstruction.

Between 0 to 7 break cycles will be recorded during a CTIM instruction, the exact number depends on the number of vectors loaded previously. For instance, if the previous number of cycles was a multiple of 8, then no break vectors are issued during the reload.

 |
 |

 |

CLEV

 |

The CLEV (change levels) parameter indicates that unrecorded break cycles, due to a change of level set, exist in the specified cycle range.

 |
 |

 |

BRK

 |

This is returned if break cycles are being generated during the reported cycle range - for example, if a timed match loop is in progress. Between 0 and 7 break cycles will be recorded.

Additionally, the following sequencer instructions also generate break vectors:

 |

sequencer instruction

 |

reported as

 |
 |

CTIM

 |

CTIM

 |
 |

CLEV

 |

CLEV

 |
 |

WTER

 |

BRK

 |
 |

FLQU

 |

BRK

 |
 |

MEAS

 |

BRK

 |
 |

STOP

 |

BRK

 |

 |
 |

 |

MTCH

 |

This is always returned if the test contains a counted match loop. The specified vectors are those that are associated with the MRPT instruction. The specified number of cycles is greater than 0 if the test has been executed online, and the last cycle that was generated from these vectors is not the last cycle of a block. For details see `Adjusting the junctions between match loop and surrounding label`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01.01_Adjusting_the_junctions_between_match_loop_and_surrounding_label.md`）.

MTCH is also returned for a timed match loop, but only if the test has been executed online, and the number of cycles will always be 0.

 |
 |

label

 |

This parameter returns the label to which the instruction belongs.

 |
 |

instance

 |

This parameter is blank for all sequencer instructions.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETV  -  GET Vectors）

```
> GETV? 0,50,(S0_1)
< GETV 0,9,0,9,GENV,"test_1",,(S0_1)
< GETV 9,30,9,6,RPTV,"test_1",,(S0_1)
< GETV 39,1,-1,-1,BRK,"test_1",,(S0_1)
```

The vectors for cycles 9 through 38 were generated by an RPTV instruction that generated 6 waveforms 5 times.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETX  -  GET eXtended vector information）

```
GETX? [type], [label], [vector], [cycle], [index], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
GETX {type}, {label}, {vector}, {cycle}, [index], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETX  -  GET eXtended vector information）

|

type

 |

The label type. You can supply one of the following options:

 |
 |

MAIN

 |

The MAIN program.

 |
 |

SJMP

 |

A JuMP Subroutine.

 |
 |

SVEC

 |

A VECtor Subroutine.

 |
 |

BRST

 |

BuRST mode.

 |
 |

MPBU

 |

Multi-Port BUrst mode

 |
 |

ALL

 |

reads the configurations for all label types (query only).

 |
 |

label

 |

The label name. It references the label for which you require vector information. Enter a string enclosed in double quotes. The string can have a length of between 1 and 128 alpha-numeric characters.

 |
 |

vector

 |

The logical number of a vector within the label specified by label. The logical vector number counts the active vectors within one label, starting from 0.

 |
 |

cycle

 |

A cycle number. If this parameter is specified, the label and vector parameters are ignored.

 |
 |

index

 |

This parameter is reserved for future use. In this implementation it must be left blank!

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to obtain data for all pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GETX  -  GET eXtended vector information）

```
> GETX? ,,,4,,(CP)
< GETX MAIN,"multi",4,4,,(CP)
```

This example asks for vector data at cycle 4 on pin CP. The system replies that cycle 4 was generated by vector 4 in a main label called multi.

Note that this type of query where only a cycle number is supplied is similar to the GETV? query requesting information on just a single cycle - see `GETV? - (GET Vectors)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.135_GETV__-__GET_Vectors.md`）.

```
> GETX? MAIN,"multi",10,,,(CP)
< GETX MAIN,"multi",10,10,,(CP)
```

This example requests the number of the cycle that was generated by vector 10 in the main label called multi. The system replies with cycle 10.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GNOS  -  GetNumberofOccupiedSets）

GNOS? {set_type}

returns:

GNOS {NumberOfOccupiedSets},{MaxNumberOfSets},{NrOfOccupiedMSetActions},{MaxNumberOfMSETActions}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GNOS  -  GetNumberofOccupiedSets）

|

set_type

 |

Must be MSET

 |
 |

NumberOfOccupiedSets

 |

Number of the current sets

 |
 |

MaxNumberOfSets

 |

Maximum allowed number of sets

 |
 |

NrOfOccupiedMSetActions

 |

Number ot the current set actions

 |
 |

MaxNumberOfMSETActions

 |

Maximum number of actions (pmu_set)

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › GNOS  -  GetNumberofOccupiedSets）

```
> DSCP 4096,16,256,32,32,12800,16,1,256,9
> GNOS? MSET
< GNOS MSET,1,3201,1,12800
```

Related firmware commands:

- Configure sets: `MSET`（raw: `02.06.02.02.164_MSET__MSET__-__definition_of_Measurement_SET.md`）
- Execute sets: `MEAS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.160_MEAS_-__execute_a_MEASurement_set.md`）
- Obtain results: `PMUR?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.179_PMUR___retrieve_PPMU_result.md`）

Define the maximum number of sets

- `Technology file for a device`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.07.02.01.02_Technology_file_for_a_device.md`）
- `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） (pmu_set parameter)

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HREX  -  High Resolution EXecution）

```
HREX? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
HREX {(pin)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HREX  -  High Resolution EXecution）

|

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins or pin groups for which the measurement is to be reported. A reply will be given for a pin only if the port to which it belongs is in the same sequencing group as the reference port of `HRIT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.139_HRIT__HRIT__-__High_Resolution_Interval_of_Time.md`）.

 |
 |

pin

 |

The pin for which an answer is given.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

Nn1n2...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The data stream itself is in principle a sequence of pairs each which consists of a repetition factor and a result value. The repetition factor indicates how often the following result value is measured before the result changes. A repetition factor of 1 is omitted.

The possible result values are:

L: Low

H: High

I: Intermediate

U: Unstable

An example is given below.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HREX  -  High Resolution EXecution）

```
> HRIT HRES,40,0,42,0,800,(A)
> HREX? (a1,a2,b1)
< HREX (a1),#9000000020199LI199HI199LI199HI
< HREX (a2),#9000000020199LI199HI199LI199HI
> HRIT END
```

In this example, a rising edge occurs exactly in the middle of every cycle, and a falling edge at the end of every cycle for all pins. Note that the total number of results 4 * (199 + 1) equals the number of samples requested with HRIT RES.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HRIT  HRIT  -  High Resolution Interval of Time）

|

HRES

 |

Indicates the start of a high resolution measurement sequence.

 |
 |

SCOP

 |

Indicates the start of a scope measurement sequence.

 |
 |

END

 |

Indicates the end of a measurement sequence.

 |
 |

task

 |

One of the three HRES, SCOP, or END.

 |
 |

start_cyc

 |

In the command, this is the first cycle of the reference port that is to be displayed.

In the query reply, the parameter contains the (defined or calculated) start cycle of the specified port.

 |
 |

start_offs

 |

In the command, this is a delay (specified in ns) relative to the start of the cycle defined by start_cyc. This allows you to start the measurement in the middle of a cycle of the reference port.

In the query reply, the parameter contains the (defined or calculated) start delay of the specified port.

 |
 |

stop_cyc

 |

In the command, this is the first cycle of the reference port that is to not to be displayed any more.

In the query reply, the parameter contains the (defined or calculated) stop cycle of the specified port.

 |
 |

stop_offs

 |

In the command, this is a delay (specified in ns) relative to the start of the cycle defined by stop_cyc. This allows you to stop the measurement in the middle of a cycle of the reference port.

In the query reply, the parameter contains the (defined or calculated) stop delay of the specified port.

 |
 |

samples

 |

Specifies the number of measurement points for the display interval.

 |
 |

ref_port

 |

Defines the port to which the start and stop cycle refer. The time interval to be displayed will be (if the offsets are 0)

 (stop_cyc - start_cyc) * ref_port-period.

For the other port of the same sequencing group, this may mean that the diagram starts or/and stops in the middle of a cycle.

 |
 |

port

 |

The port for which information is requested. If it is the reference port, the parameters specified in the command (HRES or SCOP) are returned. If it is another port of the same sequencing group, the answer will be how many cycles of this port fit into the display interval.

 |
 |

param

 |

This parameter is used in the answer for different purposes:

If the measurement sequence is active it will contain the start cycle of the specified port.

If the measurement sequence was terminated correctly or aborted because of an error, it will contain an error code as follows:

0: No closing action necessary

1: Error. Closing action (HRIT END) required

-1: Severe Error. Closing action required

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HRIT  HRIT  -  High Resolution Interval of Time）

```
> HRIT HRES,40,0,42,0,800,(A)
> HRIT? (B)
< HRIT HRES,50,0,52,2,800,(B)
> HREX? (a1,a2,b1)
< HREX (a1),#9000000020199LI199HI199LI199HI
< HREX (a2),#9000000020199LI199HI199LI199HI
< HREX (b1),#9000000025159LI159HI199LI159HI159LI
> HRIT END
> HRIT?
< HRIT 0
```

In this example, there are two ports A and B that belong to the same sequencing group. A is the reference port. The period length for port A is 5 ns, that for port B is 4 ns. It is assumed that a rising edge occurs exactly in the middle of every cycle, and a falling edge at the end of every cycle for all pins.

The display interval is 2 cycles for port A, and 2 1/2 cycles for port B. This is reflected by the offset of 2 in the answer to the first query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HROL  HROL  -  High Resolution Option and Level）

|

PINS

 |

Indicates that the result resolution and possibly the High/Low definition for differential pins will be given.

 |
 |

LEVP

 |

Indicates the level for a scope measurement will be defined. This option is only allowed after a HRITSCOP command.

 |
 |

param1

 |

The meaning of this parameter depends on the setting of the first parameter. If the first parameter is set to PINS, then param1 defines the result resolution (1 bit or 2 bits). The default depends on the capabilities of the respective pin.

If the first parameter is set to LEVP, then param1 defines the voltage level for a scope measurememnt in [mV].

 |
 |

param2

 |

If the first parameter is set to PINS, then param2 defines the method by which High and Low are determined for differential pins. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

NONE

 |

The only value for standard pins, not allowed for differential pins.

 |
 |

 |

Vdif

 |

The value that will be compared to the expected value is the difference between the positive and the negative pin. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

Vpos

 |

The value that will be compared to the expected value is the voltage of the positive pin.

 |
 |

 |

Vneg

 |

The value that will be compared to the expected value is the voltage of the negative pin.

 |
 |

 |

Vcom

 |

The value that will be compared to the expected value is the average of the positive and the negative pin.

 |
 |

 |

On the firmware level, the last three options are only available for HXA pins. In the timing diagram they are available for all differential pins.

You can use the `SPEC?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.225_SPEC__-__SPECification.md`） query to find out which options are available for a given pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins which are to be measured with the specified parameters. All these pins must be O or I/O pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HROL  HROL  -  High Resolution Option and Level）

```
> HRIT SCOP,135,0,175,0,800,(A)
> HROL PINS,1,,(HSClck)
> HROL LEVP,100,,(HSClck)
> HROL LEVP,1000,,(D0+,A0+,D0-,A0-)
> HREX? (HSClck,D0+,A0+,D0-,A0-)
> HROL LEVP,110,,(HSClck)
> HROL LEVP,1200,,(D0+,A0+,D0-,A0-)
> HREX? (HSClck,D0+,A0+,D0-,A0-)
> HRIT END
```

This example shows a measurement sequence for a scope measurement. First, the result resolution for the `HSClck` pin is set to 1. Then two measurements are taken. Before each measurement execution, the voltage levels are defined. After the second measurement, the measurement sequence is closed with HRIT END.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HWTY  -  HardWare TYpe）

```
HWTY?
```

returns:

```
HWTY {machine}, {testhead}, {dut_if}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HWTY  -  HardWare TYpe）

|

machine

 |

Returns PS

 |
 |

testhead

 |

Returns type of the test head. Options are:

TH_1CC for the A-test head or CX test head (containing one card cage)

TH_2CC for the compact test head or SX test head (containing two card cages)

TH_3CC for the LX test head (containing three card cages)

TH_4CC for the small test head (containing four card cages)

TH_8CC for the large test head (containing eight card cages).

 |
 |

dut_if

 |

Specifies the DUT interface type

 |
 |

SOC

 |

SOC

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › HWTY  -  HardWare TYpe）

```
> HWTY?
< HWTY VS,TH_4CC,SOC
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › I2CA  I2CA  -  I2CA bus）

|

address

 |

The mandatory parameter specifies the physical address of the EEPROM.

For the X24C04 EEPROM, this would be 160, 168, or 172 (164 is reserved for the DUT board interface EEPROM). The address 160 is the address of the DUT board EEPROM.

 |
 |

offset

 |

The mandatory parameter specifies the offset for the read or write operation.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data to be written from the EEPROM.

This parameter enables you to define the length of the data (in bytes) and the data itself to be transferred. It has the following format:

- A # to mark the start of the data block.
- One digit indicating how many digits make up the data length specifier.
- A number of digits indicating the length (in bytes) of the data to follow.
- A number of characters which make up the binary data.
 |
 |

size

 |

The size of data to be read from the EEPROM in bytes.

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › INGV -  INsert Generate Vectors）

```
INGV{cmd_No}, {num_vec}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › INGV -  INsert Generate Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number before which the GENV instruction is to be inserted.

 |
 |

num_vec

 |

The number of vectors that are to be generated by the GENV sequencer instruction.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › INGV -  INsert Generate Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,16,,,(@)
< ...
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> INGV 3,11
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,11,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,32,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example inserts a GENV instruction for 11 vectors before command 2. Note that the memory type is SM, as in command 0, and that the address of command 5 has been increased.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › INSI -  INsert Instructions）

```
INSI {cmd_No}, {count}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › INSI -  INsert Instructions）

|

cmd_No

The command number before which instructions are to be inserted.

 |

count

```
TSTL "test_1",(@)
```

```
forceCurrentHWLimitMax=1e+06 forceCurrentRangeMin=na forceCurrentRangeMax=na

measureCurrentHWLimitMax=1e+06 measureCurrentRangeMin=-1e+06 measureCurrentRangeMax=1e+06
voltageDropMaxForce=na voltageDropMaxReturn=na voltageClampFastLoad=na
voltageClampChannelOff=na slewV=na slewI=na filterV=OFF filterI=OFF measureFilter=na
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JRST -  Jitter modulator ReseT）

```
JRST {(pin_list)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JRST -  Jitter modulator ReseT）

|

pin_list

 |

The pins for which the jitter modulator is to be reset. Typically, this must be done for all configured pins, so that you will usually specify @ for the pin list.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JRST -  Jitter modulator ReseT）

```
JRST (@)
```

This example resets the jitter modulator of all configured pins to its default state OFF.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSCF  JSCF  -  Jitter Set ConFiguration）

|

jitter_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of a jitter set that must have been defined with JSDF.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the jitter set. For a list see the table below.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all jitter sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration of the current primary jitter set.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified property. The values that are admitted for the individual properties are listed in the table below.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which this configuration is to be applied.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSCF  JSCF  -  Jitter Set ConFiguration）

```
> JSCF? "my_J_SET",ALL,(Pin1)
< JSCF "my_J_SET",MODE,CONT,(Pin1)
< JSCF "my_J_SET",WAVEFORM,"-100,-50,0,50,100,50,0,-50",(Pin1)
< JSCF "my_J_SET",PERIODFACTOR,25,(Pin1)
```

This example defines a simple sawtooth waveform with a peak-to-peak value of 200ps for a STDDIFF or STD pin.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSDF  JSDF  -  Jitter Set DeFinition）

|

js_set_name

 |

In the command, this is the name of a new jitter set. In the query, it is a name of an existing jitter set. If you omit this parameter in the query, JSDF? will return the names of all user defined jitter sets.

 |
 |

mode_context

 |

The mode context with which the jitter set is associated. If this parameter is omitted, the DEFAULT context is assumed.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

With this parameter, the query returns all existing jitter sets.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSDF  JSDF  -  Jitter Set DeFinition）

```
> JSDF   "js_set1"
> JSDF   "js_set2"
> JSDF   "js_set3"

> JSDF?
< JSDF   "js_set1"
< JSDF   "js_set2"
< JSDF   "js_set3"

```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSPR  JSPR  -  Jitter Set PRimary set）

|

js_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing jitter set. Specify an empty string to inactivate the current primary set and thus to disable jitter injection.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSPR  JSPR  -  Jitter Set PRimary set）

```
> JSPR   "js_set1"
```


|

js_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing jitter set.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This option removes all defined jitter sets.

```
> JSUD   "js_set1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

```
JSWF? {"jitter_set_name"}, {clock_resolution}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
JSWF {"jitter_set_name"}, {"offset_sequence"}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

|

jitter_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of a jitter set that must have been defined with JSDF.

 |
 |

clock_resolution

 |

Specifies the clock resolution on which the calculation will be based. The admitted range is between 880 and 1750 ps.

You can retrieve the clock resolution for a specification with the CLKR? EXACT query.

Note that the unit is pico seconds, not nano seconds.

 |
 |

offset_sequence

 |

The list of the calculated offsets that is returned.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which the offset sequence is calculated.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

```
> jscf? "test",,(IO0)
< JSCF "test",WAVEFORM,SINUS,(IO0)
< JSCF "test",PERIOD,20,(IO0)
< JSCF "test",AMPLITUDE,100,(IO0)
> CLKR? EXACT,101,(@)
< CLKR 101,2.4,1.2,(@)
> jswf? "test",1200,(IO0)
< JSWF "test","0,29,47,47,29,0,-30,-48,-48,-30,-1,29,47,47,29,0,
  . . .
  -1,-30,-48,-48,-30,0,29,47,47,29,0,-30,-48,-48,-30",(IO0)
```

This example first queries the jitter waveform for pin `IO0`, and also the clock resolution for timing specification 101. It then calculates the offset sequence for this waveform and clock resolution. Note that CLKR? returns the clock resolution as nano seconds, but that JSWF? expects it to be specified as pico seconds. The reply is displayed in abbreviated form. The total length of the sequence is about 500 items.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

```
> JSCF? "test",WAVEFORM,(IO1)
< JSCF "test",WAVEFORM,"150,110,80,70,0"
> JSWF? "test",880,(IO1)
< JSWF "test","150,120,90,70,40",(IO1)
```

This example shows how JSWF? corrects the offset list if the second of two consecutive items is smaller than the first, and the maximum difference is exceeded.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LBMD  -  LoopBack MoDe）

LBMD? {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|PRM}, {(pinlist)}

returns:

LBMD {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|PRM}, {lpbk_mode}, {(pinlist)}

Parameters
 |

wvf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number (range 1 to maximum). Enter ALL for all waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

This option is needed by some GUIs that use this query. A SmartLoop鈩?test can only be defined in equation based timing.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case).

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

The SmartLoop鈩?configuration of the primary wavetable(s) is returned.

 |
 |

lpbk_mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

LOOP_I

 |

The pin is enabled for resending the received data to the DUT.

 |
 |

LOOP_O

 |

The pin is enabled for routing received data to the corresponding input pin.

 |
 |

LOOP_OFF

 |

The pin is not configured for SmartLoop鈩?testing.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the SmartLoop鈩?configuration is to be retrieved. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured input and IO pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LBMD  -  LoopBack MoDe）

```
> LBMD? PRM,(@)
< LBMD 101,LOOP_OFF,,(pin1,pin2)
> SPRM 103,1,1,1
> LBMD? PRM,(@)
< LBMD 103,LOOP_I,2,(pin1)
< LBMD 103,LOOP_O,8,(pin2)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LBMD  -  LoopBack MoDe）

```
> LBMD? "lpbk_1",(@)
< LBMD "lpbk_1",LOOP_O,(pin1,pin2)
```

This example queries a wavetable.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LBRT  -  LoopBack RouTing）

```
LBRT? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
LBRT {(pin1)}, {(pin2)}
```

Parameters
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which the partner pin is to be retrieved.

 |
 |

pin1

 |

Specifies a pin of pinlist.

 |
 |

pin2

 |

Specifies the pin which is mapped to the partner channel of the channel for pin1.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LBRT  -  LoopBack RouTing）

```
> LBRT? (@)
< LBRT (pin1),(pin2)
< LBRT (pin2),(pin1)
```

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LBUD  LBUD  -  LaBel User Data）

Attach user data example:

```
> LBUD "MD5Checksum", "Label1", DELETE_AT_EDIT, (port1), #214Checksum3457xx
```

This command attaches a MD5 checksum "214Checksum3457xx" to "Label1", at "port1". Attached data on demand will be deleted upon user editing the pattern.

Delete user data example:

```
> LBUD "MD5Checksum", "Label1", , (port1), #9000000000
```

This command detaches the MD5 checksum "214Checksum3457xx" from "Label1", at "port1".

Query user data example:

```
> LBUD? ALL,"LBL1",(port)
> LBUD? "MD5Checksum",ALL,(@@)
> LBUD? "MD5Checksum","LBL1",(port)
```

Each of these queries returns one matching result or multiple matching results. It can also return an empty result (instead of an error), if the given key does not exist.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LSUS  LSUS  -  Level Sets USed）

|

level_set_no

 |

Level Set Number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a level set or the highest number of set you want to load. The number you type must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command).

This number is automatically updated to include any new level set as it is created. At power-on only one level set (containing the default values) is available.

 |
 |

equation_set_no

 |

The level equation set number for which the number of currently defined level sets is to be determined. Enter an integer in the range 1 to 99. Valid for Equation based testing only.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LSUS  LSUS  -  Level Sets USed）

```
LSUS 4
```

This example defines a maximum of 4 level sets.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LSUX  LSUX  -  Level Sets Used eXtended）

|

level_set_no

 |

Level Set Number. If the number is smaller than the current value of LSUS then LSUX is set to this value. Otherwise it is set to the current value of LSUS.

 |
 |

SWAP

 |

This command parameter causes the values set by LSUS and LSUX to be switched, that is, LSUS is set to the current value of LSUX, and LSUX to that of LSUS.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

This command parameter sets the value of LSUX back to 1.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LSUX  LSUX  -  Level Sets Used eXtended）

```
LSUX 4
```

This example defines a maximum of 4 level sets.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LTDE  LTDE  -  Load Test Data Entity）

|

tde_name

 |

The name of the protocol test data entity (TDE) file. This is the file name including the extension that specifies the type of the TDE.

The file must be located at the path specified with the `PTDE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.200_PTDE__PTDE__-__Path_for_Test_Data_Entities.md`） command.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › LTDE  LTDE  -  Load Test Data Entity）

```
LTDE "test.prot_asg"
LTDE?
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MCNT  -  Match loop CouNT）

```
MCNT? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
MCNT {match_count},{(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MCNT  -  Match loop CouNT）

|

match_count

 |

Specifies the number of the pass after which the match condition was met.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Pin name or names. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MCNT  -  Match loop CouNT）

```
> MCNT? (CP)
< MCNT 16 (CP)
```

In this example, a match was obtained after 16 passes.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MEAR  retrieve MEAsurement Results）

```
MEAR{type}, [no_of_samples], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MEAR  retrieve MEAsurement Results）

|

type

 |

Data type to be measured. The following specifiers can be set:

VMUM: Per pin parallel value retrieval from PPMU measurement (successive approximation).

VAL: Per pin value measurement with BADC.

PF: Per pin pass fail result.

GPF: Global pass fail result.

 |
 |

no_of_samples

 |

Determines the number of samples that are taken if the type parameter is set to VAL. For the other types, it is ignored. The default is 1.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Target pin or pins to be measured

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MEAR  retrieve MEAsurement Results）

```
> PSFC ALL
> MEAR VAL,35,(p1,p2)
> PQFC 1
> PMUR? VAL,(p1,p2)
< PMUR P,,2,(p1)
< PMUR F,-2100,,(p2)
> PQFC 2
> PMUR? VAL,(p1,p2)
< PMUR P,,2.3,(p1)
< PMUR F,-2200,,(p2)
```

This example triggers a value measurement with 35 samples for p1 and p2 on all sites. It then retrieves the average of the samples for every pin separately for each site with PMUR?.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MEAS -  execute a MEASurement set）

```
MEAS {id_dc}, {id_mset}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MEAS -  execute a MEASurement set）

|

id_dc

 |

The DC set identification number to be executed.

 |
 |

id_mset

 |

The measurement set identification number to be executed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MEAS -  execute a MEASurement set）

```
MEAS 1,2
```

This example executes the measurement set 2 of the DC set 1.

See also an example in `MSET, MSET? - (definition of Measurement SET)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.164_MSET__MSET__-__definition_of_Measurement_SET.md`）.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MERL  MERL  -  Message ERror Limits）

| error_limit |

The maximum number of errors that will be logged. An integer in the range 1 to 30000.

Default value is 10.

 |
 | message_limit |

The maximum number of messages that will be logged. An integer in the range 1 to 30000.

Default value is 40.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MERL  MERL  -  Message ERror Limits）

MERL 30,30

This example sets both the error and the message limits to 30.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MSCF  MSCF  -  Modulation Set ConFiguration）

|

modulation_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of a modulation set that must have been defined with MSDF.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the modulation set. For a list see the table below.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all modulation sets.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified property. The values that are admitted for the individual properties are listed in the table below.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MSCF  MSCF  -  Modulation Set ConFiguration）

```
> MSCF? "mod1",ALL
< MSCF "mod1",SHAPE,SINE
< MSCF "mod1",PERIOD,250
< MSCF "mod1",PHASE,180
< MSCF "mod1",AMPLITUDE,305
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MSDF  MSDF  -  Modulation Set DeFinition）

|

ms_set_name

 |

In the command, this is the name of a new modulation set. In the query, it is a name of an existing modulation set. If you omit this parameter in the query, MSDF? will return the names of all user defined modulation sets.

 |
 |

modulation_type

 |

Currently, the only allowed modulation type is TIM (for "timing").

 |
 |

ALL

 |

With this parameter, the query returns all existing modulation sets.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MSDF  MSDF  -  Modulation Set DeFinition）

```
> MSDF   "ms_set1",TIM
> MSDF   "ms_set2",TIM
> MSDF   "ms_set3",TIM

> MSDF?
< MSDF   "ms_set1",TIM
< MSDF   "ms_set2",TIM
< MSDF   "ms_set3",TIM

```

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MSET  MSET  -  definition of Measurement SET）

Setting up PPMUs:

```
MSET 1,DC,1,LEN,6,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,1,WAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 1,DC,1,ACT,,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,1,SEL,0,CURR,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,SEL,0,VOLT,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,IRNG,1,IRA,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,IRNG,1,90,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,UFOR,2,500,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,IFOR,2,-40,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUL,3,-5,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUL,3,3000,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUH,4,5,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUH,4,3000,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,ACTI,5,,(p1,p2)
```

On PS5000:

```
MSET? 3,DC,1,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,LEN,7,,(@)
MSET 3,DC,1,WAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 3,DC,1,SWAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 3,DC,1,ACT,,,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,SEL,0,CURR,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,IRNG,1,10000,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,UFOR,2,3300,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,PMUL,3,-10,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,PMUH,4,30,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,ACTI,5,,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,SYNC,6,,(dig1)
```

Setting up the relays:

```
MSET 1,DC,2,LEN,2,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,2,WAIT,,1.3,(@)
MSET 1,DC,2,ACT,,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,2,OPM,0,ON,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,2,PPMU,0,ON,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,2,ACTI,1,,(p1,p2)
```

Setting up the measurement mode:

```
MSET 1,DC,3,LEN,1,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,3,WAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 1,DC,3,ACT,,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,3,PMUM,0,I,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,3,PMUM,0,H,(p2)
```

This example illustrates the internal structure of a measurement set as well as the requirement to define different measurement sets for different tasks. Note that no ACTI action is required (or even permitted) for measurement set 3 which contains only the PMUM action.

To execute this example, use the MEAS command as shown below:

```
MEAS 1,1
MEAS 1,2
MEAS 1,3
```

These commands sequentially execute measurement sets 1, 2 and 3 of DC set 1.

To retrieve the result of this measurement, use the `PMUR?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.179_PMUR___retrieve_PPMU_result.md`） command as shown below:

```
PMUR? GPF,(@)
```

This command retrieves the global pass/fail result of all pins.

Defining a DC set for value measurement

```
MSET 2,DC,1,VMUM,0,I,1,ADC,4000,0.0004,(p1)
```

In this example, 4000 measurements will be taken with the sampling period 400 us on the pin p1.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MVCU -  Modify Vector variable Configuration Usage）

```
MVCU {label name}, {VVC name}, {vector offset}, {Init Discard Frames}, {Number Of Frames}, {VarNameDef}, {InitStaticData}
```

Parameters
 |

label name

 |

Name of the label for which usage is to be modified.

 |
 |

VVC name

 |

Name of the Vector Variable configuration. Refer to `DVVC, DVVC? - (Define Vector Variable Configuration)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.95_DVVC__DVVC__-__Define_Vector_Variable_Configuration.md`） for more information.

 |
 |

Vector offset

 |

This is the offset in the label where usage needs to be modified. Vector offset is the logical vector number in the label. A usage with this combination of parameters {label name, VVC name, Vector offset} should already exist in the system, when defined by DVCU.

 |
 |

Init Discard Frames

 |

This is a reserved parameter. For future use.

 |
 |

Number Of Frames

 |

Number Of Frames to which this usage refers. If the label is DSRC, usage allocates this many frames. If the label is a main label, usage refers to this many frames.

 |
 |

VarNameDef

 |

This parameter specifies the vector variable names for the variable names defined in VVC. This parameter is a string.

Syntax:

`"VVC_NAME=VEC_VAR_NAME[,VVC_NAME=VEC_VAR_NAME[,.....]]"`

There is no need to have aliases (vector variable names) for all the variables in VVC.

 |
 |

InitStaticData

 |

This parameter is either TRUE or FALSE.

TRUE: Static data will be downloaded on definition of usage.

FALSE: Static data will not be downloaded.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MVCU -  Modify Vector variable Configuration Usage）

The following example modifies the usage to change vector variable names. This usage is defined for the label "src" using VVC "AC97" at offset 0.

VVC "AC97" looks like:

```
ATTR DIGDATA
  VARIABLES LEFT,RIGHT
  PINS ser_in
     SOURCE_DATA_TEMPLATE LEFT[0-19]; RIGHT[0-19]
     MAPPING
         0 low
         1 high
>MVCU"src_ramp","AC97",0,0,1024,"LEFT=Sine,
 RIGHT=Ramp",TRUE
>DVCU? ALL,ALL,ALL
<DVCU "src_ramp","AC97",0,0,1024,"LEFT=Sine,
 RIGHT=Ramp",TRUE
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MVVA -  Modify Vector VAriable）

```
MVVA {"name"}, {type}, {"vector_label"}, {xfer_mode}, [device_cycle], [start_vector_nr], [capt_label], [init_discard], [nr_vec_per_frame], [nr_vec_per_sample], [nr_vector_interdisc], [nr_of_frames], [nr_frame_interdisc], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MVVA -  Modify Vector VAriable）

| name |

Name of a vector variable.

 |
 | type |

Type of vector variable. Currently, only the type DIGCAPT is supported.

 |
 | vector_label |

Name of a vector label. Only main vector labels are supported.

 |
 | xfer_mode |

Mandatory parameter that determines the transfer mode. The options available are

-

PARA = Parallel. This is the default.

-

SERI = Serial

Note that you cannot select SERI if the vector variable is associated with more than one pin.

 |
 | device_cycle |

Optional parameter, currently not used.

 |
 | start_vector_nr |

Optional parameter, currently not used.

 |
 | capt_label |

This optional parameter describes a label reference to a capture block within a vector label which has been set aside for digital capture. If this parameter is specified, the vector variable is defined with respect to this capture area. If it is not specified, the capture label references the entire pattern.

 |
 | init_discard |

The optional parameter defines the offset relative to the start location of a capture block within the capture memory. The vectors before this offset will not be uploaded.

The default value is 0.

 |
 | nr_vec_per_frame |

The optional parameter defines the number of vectors that make up a frame.

 |
 | nr_vec_per_sample |

The optional number of vectors that are contained in one sample.

The suitable values for this parameter depend on the selected transfer mode (`xfer_mode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.166_MVVA_-__Modify_Vector_VAriable.md#_99063__r_xfer_mode`） parameter).

- For transfer mode PARA, this parameter must be set to 1 (the default value).
- For SERI, it should be set to the number of code bits (see the code_width parameter of `DIDT?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.75_DIDT__DIDT__-__upload_DIgital_DaTa.md`）). The maximum value is 32.
 |
 | nr_vector_interdisc |

The optional parameter defines how many vectors are discarded between two extracted vectors in step 2 of the extraction process. If set to 2, for example, the first and then every third vector will be extracted.

The default value is 0, in which case no vector will be discarded in step 2.

 |
 | nr_frames |

The optional number of frames that are to be extracted, starting from the first frame.

The default value is 1.

 |
 | frame_interdisc |

The optional number of irrelevant vectors between frames. These will be discarded in step 3 of the extraction process.

The default value is 0.

 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory List of pins for which the vector variable is defined. The pins specified here should be contained in the pin list that was associated with the referenced vector label (vector_label parameter) by the `SDGC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.219_SDGC__SDGC__-__Setup_DiGital_Capture.md`） command. Only then will the digital data of these pins be retrieved by `DIDT?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.75_DIDT__DIDT__-__upload_DIgital_DaTa.md`）, if DIDT? is called with the actual vector variable.

If the list contains more than one element, the element names must be separated with a comma.

If you have set `xfer_mode`（raw: `02.06.02.02.166_MVVA_-__Modify_Vector_VAriable.md#_99063__r_xfer_mode`） to SERI, specify only one pin.

The LSB of the uploaded vector variable data will be assigned to the last pin of the pin list.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › MVVA -  Modify Vector VAriable）

```
> DVVA "vec_var",DIGCAPT,"test_capt",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,1,0,(OUT_1)
> MVVA "vec_var",DIGCAPT,"test_capt",SERI,,,,,,,,,,(OUT_1)
> DVVA? "test_capt"
< DVVA "vecvar",DIGCAPT,"test_capt",SERI,,,,0,1,1,0,1,0,(OUT_1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NIFE  NIFE  -  Number of Independent Fast Error）
