```
NIFE {number}
```

```
NIFE?
```

returns:

```
NIFE {number}
```

`NIFE?` can be issued only if the number of independent Fast Sync ports already has been set by command `NIFE {number}`. Otherwise, the error message Failed to execute firmware command: NIFE? will be shown.

  Parameters

 | number  | Specifies the maximum number of independent Fast Sync ports. It can be [1,...,8]. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NIFE  NIFE  -  Number of Independent Fast Error）

```
>SQST OFF
>NIFE 2
>STME FAST,
>STME ON,
```

This example configures the Fast Sync feature, and sets two independent Fast Sync ports on each test processor.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NODV  -  Number Of Displayable Vectors）

```
NODV?
```

returns:

```
NODV {num_vec}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NODV  -  Number Of Displayable Vectors）

|

num_vec

 |

returns the number of active vectors.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NODV  -  Number Of Displayable Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> NODV?
< NODV 15
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NOOP  NOOP  -  NO OPeration）

|

string_1 to string_4

 |

A string of up to 128 characters

 |
 |

no_1 to no_4

 |

An integer

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › NOOP  NOOP  -  NO OPeration）

```
NOOP "TF1",,,
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › OUTS  -  OUTput Search）

```
OUTS? {vector_no_1}, [vector_no_2], {vector_type}, {level_type}, {(pinlist)} [, (port)]
```

returns:

```
OUTS {cycle_no}, {output_level}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › OUTS  -  OUTput Search）

|

vector_no_1

 |

This parameter is an absolute vector number or a range specifier depending on whether DPTH, SNGL, or RNG has been selected.

 |
 |

vector_no_2

 |

This parameter is an absolute vector number.

 |
 |

vector_type

 |

The vector_type is one of the following:

 |
 |

DPTH

 |

The depth option. The vector table is searched from the current start label (defined by the label parameter or by the SQSL command) for the number of vectors specified in the vector_no_1 parameter. The vector_no_2 parameter must be omitted.

 |
 |

SNGL

 |

The single option. Only the vectors specified in the vector_no_1 and vector_no_2 parameters are searched.

 |
 |

RNG

 |

The range option. The range of vectors between (and including) vector_no_1 and vector_no_2 are searched.

 |
 |

level_type

 |

The level_type is one of the following:

 |
 |

HIGH

 |

If HIGH is selected, the system looks for a high level (logic 1 state).

 |
 |

LOW

 |

If LOW is selected, the system looks for a low level (logic 0 state).

 |
 |

BOTH

 |

If BOTH is selected, the system looks for both levels.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pinlist can contain O, or IO pins. If all pins configured as outputs are to be searched, use the @ character. If more than one pin is included, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |
 |

port

 |

If you issue the query in a multi-port test, you must specify one of the pattern ports in order to determine the search range uniquely.

 |
 |

cycle_no

 |

The cycle number of the first occurrence of a logic 0 or logic 1 state.

 |
 |

output_level

 |

The output_level is one of the following:

 |
 |

LOW

 |

This indicates that a logic 0 occurs at the given cycle.

 |
 |

HIGH

 |

This indicates that a logic 1 occurs at the given cycle.

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PACT  PACT  -  Parallel ACTivities control）

|

control

 |

The control parameter is:

 |
 |

 |

ACTIVE

 |

When a site is ACTIVE it receives all test data, and generates results for the tests.

 |
 |

 |

MASKED

 |

When a site is MASKED, it receives all test data, as with the ACTIVE parameter. However, the receivers for the site are disabled and no result information is available.

 |
 |

site

 |

A single integer representing a site number.

 |
 |

site_string

 |

A string consisting of "0" and "1". One character must be given for every site that is configured in the pin configuration. "0" indicates that the respective site is (to be) masked. "1" indicates that the respective site is (to be) activated.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

means that all configured sites that are available for testing (that is, do not use a channel that is inactivated in the MCDIgnore file) are to be activated or masked.

For the MCDIgnore file see MCDIgnore usage and restrictions in Service Guide Part 1.

 |
 |

STR

 |

forces the query to return a site string instead of a single line for every site.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PACT  PACT  -  Parallel ACTivities control）

```
> PACT ACTIVE, 1
> PACT MASKED, 2
> PACT MASKED, 3
```

This example masks site 2 and site 3, and makes site 1 active.

```
> PACT?
< PACT ACTIVE,1
< PACT MASKED,2
< PACT MASKED,3
> PACT? STR
< PACT "100"
```

This example shows the impact of the optional STR parameter for the query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PADS  PADS  -  Pin Attributes Definition String）

|

mode

 |

Currently not used.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

Edge delay definition string which consists of delay adjustments for up to all available edges. The valid range (in ns) is from -8 to 8.

All edges which are not explicitly set are not changed but stay at the same value as before.

 |
 |

drv_adj

 |

The driver adjustment contains the sum of any additional driver offset delays that you want to include. The delay (in ns) must be between -5 and +5 and contain a maximum of three digits after the decimal point. The default value is 0.

 |
 |

rec_adj

 |

The receiver adjustment contains the sum of any additional receiver offset delays that you want to include. The delay (in ns) must be between -5 and +5 and contain a maximum of three digits after the decimal point. The default value is 0.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pinlist must include all pins to which the given attributes apply. If more than one pin is to be entered, the names must be separated with a comma. All pins in pinlist must be I, O, or IO pin types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PADS  PADS  -  Pin Attributes Definition String）

```
> PADS ,"d1:0.1 d2:0.2 d3:0.3 d4:0.1 d5:0.2 d6:0.3 d7:0.1 d8:0.2",2,,(clk)

> PADS? ,(@)
< PADS ,"d1:0.1 d2:0.2 d3:0.3 d4:0.1 r1:0.1 r2:0.2 r3:0.3 r4:0.1",,-1,(io)
< PADS ,"d1:0.1 d2:0.2 d3:0.3 d4:0.1 d5:0.2 d6:0.3 d7:0.1 d8:0.2",2,,(clk)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PALS  PALS  -  Pin ALlocation for multiple Sites）

|

site

 |

The site parameter is an integer that defines the number of the site where the channels are to be defined.

The integer must be greater than 1 (channels for site 1 are defined by the command `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`）.

When specified as part of the PALS? query, you can use the parameter ALL to read the channel allocation for all sites or the parameter PEND to read the pending channel allocation.

 |
 |

channel_1

 |

This parameter specifies the test system channel used in the specified site for the pin.

For a digital or DC Scale channel, specify it with the test system channel number, which is five digits.

See `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for the channel number.

For utility lines, see `DFUT, DFUT? - (DeFine UTility line)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.70_DFUT__DFUT__-__DeFine_UTility_line.md`） for the channel number.

 |
 |

DC_scale_channels_list

 |

You can define a Master/Slave configuration for DC Scale channels by specifying a list of DC Scale channels, separated by commas and enclosed by parentheses. The first channel is the master.

For UHC4 / UHC4T the channels must be physically adjacent on the same board, or be the last (the 4th) channel of a board and the first of another UHC4 / UHC4T board. You cannot gang UHC4 and UHC4T boards. Before ganging between boards can be used, the connection must be enabled by `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`）.

 |
 |

channel_2

 |

The optional parameter is currently not used.

 |
 |

pin

 |

This defines the name of the pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The names of the pins to be allocated to the pin.

The query returns the name of the pin allocated to each channel. The symbol @ can be used with the PALS? command to list all pins previously defined by the PALS command. If a list of more than one pin is required, the pin names must be separated with a comma. If you query a non-existent pinlist, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PALS  PALS  -  Pin ALlocation for multiple Sites）

```
PALS 2,10201,,(Clock)
PALS 2,10202,,(D0)
```

The above example allocates the Clock pin for site 2 to channel 10201 and allocates pin D0 for site 2 to channel 10202.

```
PALS 2,(10101, 10102),,(dc1)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale channels. The first channel is the master.

```
DDIC CONN, (104GO, 105GI)
DDIC CONN, (105GO, 107GI)
PALS 2,(10403, 10404, 10501, 10502, 10503, 10504, 10701, 10702),,(dc1)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale UHC4 channels across boards. The first channel is the master.

```
DFAN "MCE231,2,i","",(av8_bbrx_b+)
DFAN "MCE231,6,i","",(av8_bbrx_b-)
PALS 2,"MCE231,1,i",,(av8_bbrx_b+)
PALS 3,"MCE231,3,i",,(av8_bbrx_b+)
PALS 4,"MCE231,4,i",,(av8_bbrx_b+)
PALS 2,"MCE231,5,i",,(av8_bbrx_b-)
PALS 3,"MCE231,7,i",,(av8_bbrx_b-)
PALS 4,"MCE231,8,i",,(av8_bbrx_b-)
```

This example defines a pair of differential pins av8_bbrx_b+ and av8_bbrx_b- using the MCE card in 4 sites.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

```
PASS? {(pin_list)}
```

or

```
PASS? {(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
PASS {res_flag}, {(pin_list)}
```

or

```
PASS {res_flag}, {(port)}
```

respectively.

Note port_list mode returns the pass or fail result per port. This is different than the case when using pin_list mode.

To report the last test result per individual pin , the PPIN command is used.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

```
PASS?PPIN,{(pins)}
```

returns

```
PASS PPIN,{res_flag}, {(pin}
```

Note The result (pass or fail) is returned for each pin specified in pins individually.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

|

pin_list

 |

The last test result is provided for the pins specified in pin_list. If more than one pin list is included, the names must be separated by a comma.

Normally, only O or IO pins in the list are taken into account; I pins are ignored. However, if any sequencer program of the setup contains a`MEAS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.160_MEAS_-__execute_a_MEASurement_set.md`） instruction (see the `SQPG`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`） command), and the measurement set that is executed by this instruction is defined for an I pin, then the measurement result for this pin will be included in the reply of PASS? if the I pin is specified in pin_list.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

The last test result is provided for the pins of a port specified in port_list. If more than one port is included, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |
 |

Pins

 |

The last test result is provided per each pin specified in pins individually. If more than one pin is included , the names must be separated by a comma.

 |
 |

res_flag

 |

F

 |

If this result is returned, at least one pin in pin_list or port failed the last test. In the case of per pin query (using PPIN command), a fail is returned if the individual pin specified in pins failed the last test.

 |
 |

P

 |

If this result is returned, all pins in pin_list or port passed the last test. In the case of per pin query (using PPIN command) , a pass is returned if the individual pin specified in pins passed the last test.

 |

Application

Test results, see `Test Result Commands`（raw: `02.06.11_Test_Result_Commands.md`） and `Multi-Port Testing`（raw: `../../03_Use_cases_and_application_papers/03.03_How_to_use_Multiport_for_specific_Applications/03.03.01.02_General_Overview_of_Multi-Port_Testing__Cover.md`）.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

After a functional test has been performed, sending PASS? returns one result for the whole test.

```
PASS? (@)
```

returns:

```
PASS P, (@)
```

or

```
PASS F, (@)
```

for a passed or a failed test result respectively.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PCLK  PCLK  -  Pin CLocK）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Used for equation based timing. It is derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

Note that if you change the period for an equation based timing setup, PCLK will only change the runtime value, not the setup value specified in the timing set.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In the command, you cannot enter a multi-port specification unless the specification is associated with the default port, and no other ports are configured. This restriction does not apply to the query.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Timing Set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by `TSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

period

 |

Enter the test system period in ns. The period range depends on the model. For the Pin Scale 800, the range is 2.5 ns to 31250 ns. All values entered (or queried regardless of query_mode) are in ns and will be rounded to nine digits after the decimal point (atto-seconds) according to the accuracy of the firmware. The power-on default value for all configured pins also depends on the model.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose period you want to define or read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to set or read the periods for all configured pins. If you do not use @, the firmware assumes asynchronous operation.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

In the query, you must specify a list of ports, if you have specified a multi-port specification for the first parameter.

 |
 |

query_mode

 |

In the query, you can specify whether the period specified by the user or the corrected period calculated by the system is to be returned. The allowed values are:

WANT: The period defined by the user is returned. This is also the default.

EXACT: The period calculated by the system is returned.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PCLK  PCLK  -  Pin CLocK）

```
PCLK 101,1,20,(@)
```

This example sets the test system period for specification 101 to 20 ns.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PCLK  PCLK  -  Pin CLocK）

```
PCLK 101,1,40,(S1)
```

This example sets the test system period of pin S1 for specification 101 to 40 ns.

The `VCLK?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.319_VCLK__-__Verify_CLocK.md`） query checks whether a PCLK command with the specified parameter values was accepted with or without auto-correction.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDIV  -  Period DIVider）

```
PDIV? {specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|"wavetbl"} [,spec_type][,(pinlist)]
```

returns:

```
PDIV {specset_id|"multi-port_spec"}, {period_div}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDIV  -  Period DIVider）

|

specset_id

 |

Identifier of a timing specification, which is derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

wavetbl

 |

Name of a wavetable. This requires that spec_type is set to WFT.

 |
 |

period_div

 |

Possible values are -1 (for standard pins), 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 (only for fast pins).

 |
 |

spec_type

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

TIM

 |

Returns the period divider of the timing sets (fast pins). If not all timing sets have the same period divider for the same fast pin, PDIV? returns an error.

 |
 |

WFT

 |

Returns the implicit period divider of the wavetable specified as the first parameter.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This parameter is only applicable to fast pins. For standard pins,`-1` is returned.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDIV  -  Period DIVider）

```
> PDIV? "fast",WFT,(I1)
< PDIV "fast",WFT,6,(I1)
```

This example queries the implicit period divider of the fast pin I1 in the wavetable `fast`. The factor is 6.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? [PRLT,] {spec},[averages,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
PDMM {spec},, [ident], {result}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 | PRLT  | The extra parameter controls how the measurement is performed.

The value of the parameter can be: PRLT

 |
 | PRLT specified: |
 |   | The specified test is performed for all active sites and for all pins that are defined in the pinlist. The command returns individual results only for the site in focus.

The command additionally stores a global pass/fail result for all active sites. The global pass/fail result can be retrieved by a following `PRLT?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.183_PRLT__-__request_Parallel_ResuLTs.md`） query.

 |
 | PRLT not specified: |
 |   |   | If not specified, the measurement results are returned only for the site in result focus. The command returns individual results for the measurements defined by parameter spec and for the pins defined by pinlist. A following PRLT? query will return an error message. |
 | spec  | The mandatory parameter defines the test specification that can be: |
 | Fo_Se  | to check that the force/sense lines are correctly wired on your DUT board. This measurement must be made in disconnected state. |
 | Ma_S1  | to check the force connections on the ganging line. The force of master and all forces of slaves must be connected within a resistant of 20 惟. PASS is returned if pin is not in ganging mode.

Only supported with the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | averages |

The extra parameter defines the number of averaged measurements to be performed.

The valid range of the integer parameter is 1 鈥?128.

The default value is 1.

 |
 | pinlist  | pinlist must contain the names of DPS previously defined by the DFPS command (and used in DPS operating mode) or the names of DPS previously defined by the DFPN command (and used in PMU operating mode).

See `DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） and `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for more information.

If more than one pin is specified, the names must be separated by a comma. The character @ can be used to specify all DPS pins.

 |
 | ident  | The identifier is: |
 | POS  | for positive power lines |
 | NEG  | for negative power lines |
 | result  | The result is P (pass), or F (fail) for a Fo_Se specification. |

### Example 1: Test of the site in query focus（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? Fo_Se, (@)
```

returns:

```
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vee)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vee)
```

This example checks that the force/sense connections on the DUT board are correctly wired for positive and negative lines. For the pin Vee the master channel and the slave channel show a pass for both lines.

### Example 2: Test of all active sites（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? PRLT, Fo_Se, (Vcc,Vee)
PRLT? ALL
```

returns:

```
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vcc)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vcc)
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vee)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vee)

PRLT ALL,"PF0P"
```

The returned pass/fail result of PRLT? presumes that four sites are defined and sites 1, 2, and 4 are active. Sites 1 and 4 have passed the test. Site 2 shows the result for an open force to sense connection.

### Example 3: Averaging（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? Fo_Se, 10, (@)
```

returns:

```
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vee)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vee)
```

The returned go/no-go results are built from the average of ten measurements to improve the stability of the measurement in noisy environments.

### Example 4: Ganging（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? Ma_Sl,32,(@)
```

  returns:

```
PDMM Ma_Sl,,POS,P,(Vee1)
PDMM Ma_Sl,,POS,P,(Vee2)

```

This example checks the master and slave connections for ganged pins with an average of 32 measurements to improve the stability of the measurements in noisy environments.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PFND  -  Pin FiND）

```
PFND? [group_type,] {(pin)}
```

returns:

```
PFND {group_type}, {(list)}, {(pin)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PFND  -  Pin FiND）

|

group_type

 |

The group type can be PRT (for "port") or DIFF (for "differential pair"). PRT is the default.

 |
 |

pin

 |

The name of the pin about which information is to be retrieved.

 |
 |

list

 |

List of the ports that contain the pin, or the differential pair to which the specified pin belongs.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PFND  -  Pin FiND）

```
> PFND? (I/O1_1)
< PFND PRT,(port_1,port_1.CP_1),(I/O1_1)
> PFND? DIFF,(P+)
< PFND DIFF,(P+,P-),(P+)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

```
PMUR?{type}, [mode,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns

```
PMUR {judge}, [voltage], [current], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

|

type

 |

Data type to be retrieved. The following specifiers can be set:

VMUM: Returns the measurement value from the PPMU measurement (successive approximation) for the pins in pinlist.

VAL: Returns the per pin measurement value or values for the pins in pinlist.

PF: Per pin pass fail result for the pins in pinlist.

GPF: Global pass fail result for all tested pins. The pinlist is ignored.

 |
 |

mode

 |

This parameter controls the behavior of PMUR? if the type parameter is set to VAL. The allowed values are:

 |
 |

 |

FORCE_MEASURE

 |

PMUR? performs a value measurement for type VAL.

 |
 |

 |

USE_CACHE

 |

PMUR? performs a value measurement only if necessary, that is, if a result for the same measurement set is not present in the cache.

 |
 |

judge

 |

This parameter indicates a judgment of the pin with the following specifiers:

P: Pass

F: Fail

 |
 |

voltage

 |

Measured voltage in mV. This parameter is only returned when type = VAL.

 |
 |

current

 |

Measured current in uA. This parameter is only returned when type = VAL.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Target pin or pins to retrieve result

   | Note For the VAL type, either voltage or current will be returned depending on the measurement mode (I-force V-measure or V-force I-measure).

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

```
> PMUR? VAL,(p1,p2)
< PMUR P,,2,(p1)
< PMUR F,-2100,,(p2)
```

This example retrieves the measurement value of "p1" and "p2" for the site that has the query focus.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

```
> PMUR? GPF,(@)
< PMUR P,,,()
```

In this example, PMUR? returns the global pass/fail result for all tested pins of the site that has the query focus.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PQFC  PQFC  -  Parallel Query FoCus）

|

site

 |

The site parameter is single integer representing the number of the site that has or shall have the query focus.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PQFC  PQFC  -  Parallel Query FoCus）

```
PQFC 2
```

This example sets the query focus to site 2.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRCF  PRCF  -  Pseudo Random bit sequence ConFiguration）

|

PRBS_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of a PRBS set that must have been defined with PRDF.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the PRBS set. There are two properties to be configured:

 |
 |

POLYNOMIAL

 |

This property defines the connection polynomial of the LFSR. It is coded as a bit string where the position of the bit identifies the degree of the addend, and its value defines the coefficient of this addend. The constant term of the polynomial, which is always 1, must be omitted. The last bit is supposed to determine the degree n of the polynomial. Therefore, the length of the string must be n, and its last bit must be "1".

 |
 |

SEED

 |

This property defines the seed for the LFSR in the order in which it is output. This property is only required for PRBS generation. The seed for the PRBS check is taken from the received data.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all PRBS sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified to modify or retrieve the configuration of the current primary PRBS set.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specify a bit string for this parameter. Its meaning depends on the selected property. For POLYNOMIAL it encodes the connection polynomial. For SEED, it defines the initial state of the LFSR. The maximum length is 32 in both cases.

- The default for the polynomial is

11111110111010110011110000100101,

which is the polynomial

1+x+x2+x3+x4+x5+x6+x7+x9+x10+x11+x13+x15+x16+x19+x20+x21+x22+x27+x30+x32.

- The default for the seed is

00110010011011110001001101100111.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which pin this configuration is to be applied.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRCF  PRCF  -  Pseudo Random bit sequence ConFiguration）

```
> PRCF? "PRBS_1",ALL,(Pin1)
< PRCF "PRBS_1",POLYNOMIAL,"101",(Pin1)
< PRCF "PRBS_1",SEED,"100",(Pin1)
```

This example defines 1 + x1 + x3 as the connection polynomial, and 100 as the initial segment for Pin1. This is the example which is also used in `Overview of pseudo random bit sequences`（raw: `02.06.17.01_Overview_of_pseudo_random_bit_sequences.md`）.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRDF  PRDF  -  PRBS set DeFinition）

|

prbs_set_name

 |

In the command, this is the name of a new PRBS set. In the query, it is a name of an existing PRBS set. If you omit this parameter in the query, PRDF? will return the names of all user defined PRBS sets.

 |
 |

mode_context

 |

The mode context with which the PRBS set is associated. If this parameter is omitted, the DEFAULT context is assumed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRDF  PRDF  -  PRBS set DeFinition）

```
> PRDF   "prbs_set1"
> PRDF   "prbs_set2"
> PRDF   "prbs_set3"
```

```
> PRDF?
< PRDF   "prbs_set1"
< PRDF   "prbs_set2"
< PRDF   "prbs_set3"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRLT  -  request Parallel ResuLTs）

```
PRLT? ["exec_context",] {site}
```

returns:

```
PRLT {site}, {"result"}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRLT  -  request Parallel ResuLTs）

| exec_context  | An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`）. |
 | site  | The site parameter is number A single integer representing the site number. ALL Means that all the results of all configured sites are returned. |
 | result  | The result parameter is a string containing one character for every site. The nth character stands for site n. Possible characters are: P If the last test passed on all pins. F If the last test failed at any pin. 0 If the site was masked during the last test. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRLT  -  request Parallel ResuLTs）

```
PRLT? ALL
```

returns:

```
PRLT ALL, "PF0"
```

In this example, site 1 passed the last test, site 2 failed it, and site 3 was masked during the test.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

```
PRMD? {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi_port_spec"|PRM}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
PRMD {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi_port_spec"|PRM}, {prbs_mode}, [x_mode], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number (range 1 to maximum). Enter ALL for all waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

This option is needed by some GUI tools that use this query. A PRBS test can only be defined in equation based timing.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case).

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

The PRBS configuration of the primary wavetable(s) is returned.

 |
 |

prbs_mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

PRBS_I

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS generation.

 |
 |

PRBS_I_INV

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS generation and is the negative connection of a differential pair.

 |
 |

PRBS_O_INV

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS checking and is the negative connection of a differential pair.

 |
 |

PRBS_O

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS checking.

 |
 |

PRBS_OFF

 |

The pin is not configured for PRBS testing.

 |
 |

x_mode

 |

Specifies the x-mode for PRBS enabled pins. Left empty if prbs_mode is PRBS_OFF.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the PRBS configuration is to be retrieved. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured input and IO pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

```
> PRMD? PRM,(@)
< PRMD 101,PRBS_OFF,,(pin1,pin2)
> SPRM 103,1,1,1
> PRMD? PRM,(@)
< PRMD 103,PRBS_I,2,(pin1)
< PRMD 103,PRBS_O,8,(pin2)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

```
> PRMD? "prbs_2",(@)
< PRMD "prbs_2",PRBS_O,4,(pin1,pin2)
```

This example queries a wavetable.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRPR  PRPR  -  PRBS PRimary set）

|

prbs_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing PRBS set. If you specify "", the defaults will be restored.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRPR  PRPR  -  PRBS PRimary set）

```
> PRPR   "PRBS_set"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRUD -  PRBS set UnDefine）

PRUD {"prbs_set_name"|ALL}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRUD -  PRBS set UnDefine）

|

prbs_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing PRBS set.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Remove all existing transition tests sets

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PRUD -  PRBS set UnDefine）

```
> PRUD   "prbs_set1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

```
PSAS? [msMode ,] {mask}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns

```
PSAS {status}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 | msMode  | The extra parameter controls how the return value is created.

The value of the parameter can be PQFC:

- PQFC specified: The current query focus is respected and allows status query per site without affecting status bits of other sites.
- PQFC not specified: The command reads (and clears) status bits of all enabled and active sites at a glance, ignoring the actual query focus.
The parameter applies only to use of parameter mask as integer value. |
 | mask  | Integer bit mask or ALL.

-

Integer bit mask: Integer value is used to mask out individual status bits. Each bit of mask is logically AND-ed with the corresponding bit of the DPS status. If one of the resulting bits is set, then F (Fail) is returned, otherwise P (Pass).

It is used to check for an error condition. All bit positions of the status flags that should be checked, must be set to 1 in mask. If one of the selected status bits is set, then PSAS? returns F.

- ALL: Hex value (hexadecimal representation of all status bits) is returned.
For setting the integer bit mask or interpreting a returned hex value, refer to the `status`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md#_98691__r_status`） parameter below. |
 | pinlist  | Comma separated list of DPS128/64 or XPS256 pins. The @ character can be used to read the status for all DPS pins. |
 | status  | If parameter mask is ALL, you need to translate the hex value (hexadecimal representation of the status bits) to its binary form as follows:

 | Bit 0 (LSB):  | Constant voltage |
 | Bit 1:  | Constant current |
 | Bit 2:  | Unregulated |
 | Bit 3:  | Overvoltage |
 | Bit 4:  | Overpower / Overcurrent / Power budget exceeded |
 | Bit 5:  | Overtemperature |
 | Bit 6:  | Voltage drop force |
 | Bit 7:  | Voltage drop return |
 | Bit 8:  | DUT board disconnect  | For the special mapping of bit 9 and 8 on UHC4 and UHC4T, refer to table `DPS flag description`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md#_98691__s_DPS_flag_description`） below. |
 | Bit 9:  | Safety line |
 | Bit 10:  | Current limit disconnect |
 | Bit 11:  | Low headroom |
 | Bit 12:  | Current limiter protection detected |
 | Bit 13:  | Range overflow |
 | Bit 14 (MSB):  | Clamp distance too low |
 | Bit 15:  | Voltage drop force warning |
 | Bit 16:  | Voltage drop return warning  |  If parameter mask is specified as an integer bit-mask:

- Pass: P
- Fail: F

Refer to table `DPS flag implementation`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md#_98691__s_DPS_flag_implementation_710`） below for information regarding the card specific implementation of the bits or flags.

 |

### Description（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

For the following examples (1 to 4), the assumed binary value of the status of the UHC4 pin Vcc is 10000110 (Voltage drop return, Unregulated, Constant Current).

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To get all flags:

```
PSAS? ALL,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS #86,(Vcc)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To check if Unregulated (bit 2) is set:

```
PSAS? 4,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS F,(Vcc)
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To check if Constant Current (bit 1) or Overpower (bit 4) is set:

```
PSAS? 18,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS F,(Vcc)
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To check if Voltage Drop Force (bit 6) or DUT Board Disconnect (bit 8) is set:

```
PSAS? 320,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS P,(Vcc)
```

### Example 5（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

```
PSAS? ALL,(Vee)
```

returns

```
PSAS 2,(Vee)
```

This example for device pin Vee shows the DPS is working in constant current mode.

### Example 6（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

```
PSAS? ALL,(Vee)
```

returns

```
PSAS 64,(Vee)
```

This example for device pin Vee shows the DPS has hit the voltage drop force threshold.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSEE -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Execute）

```
PSEE [setnr], [current_range], [samples], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSEE -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Execute）

|

setnr

 |

The set number of the external trigger measurement. (The range is 1 to 256). When this parameter is specified the corresponding set must have already been defined.

 |
 |

current_range

 |

If the setnr parameter is specified, the range in which the executed measurement will be made will be determined from the maximum value of the limits defined with the `DPSE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.85_DPSE__DPSE__-__Define_Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement.md`） command, and this parameter will be ignored.

If the setnr parameter is not specified, you must specify the range with a value. In this case, the measurement will be executed in the smallest range that can measure the given value. The unit is Ampere [A].

 |
 |

samples

 |

This parameter specifies the number of measurements. After the measurements are completed, the average of the measurements will be calculated.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This parameter will be ignored if setnr is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSEE -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Execute）

```
DFPS 11,pos,(Vcc)
DFPS 12,pos,(Vdd)
DPSE 1,(@),#10          <- Delete set 1
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#150,1,2   <- Vcc min=1A, max=2A
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#150,2,3   <- Vdd min=2A, max=3A
PSST ON      <- Measurement requires connect state
PSEE 1,,,(@)   <- Measure both pins in parallel
PSER? 1,pval
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000006,1.501 <- value within range
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000006,3.173 <- value outside range
```

This example performs a measurement with format 2 and PSEE for two different pins in parallel.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? [setnr], {mode}
```

returns:

```
PSER [setnr], [result], {(pinlist)}, {binary_data}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

|

setnr

 |

The set number of the external trigger measurement. (The range is 1 to 256). If this parameter is omitted, this command returns the result of previous execution of the PSEE or PSIE command.

 |
 |

mode

 |

This parameter defines the type of result.

 |
 |

PVAL

 |

Binary data for each pin defined in the measurement will be returned.

 |
 |

PPF

 |

A per-pin pass/fail result will be returned. Only valid when a setnr is given.

 |
 |

BVAL

 |

Binary data mode.

4 Bytes header for the sample count

4 Byte for test points count

Test points (8 bytes per test point)

Sampler (channel count) is set to 1.

 |
 |

GPF

 |

A global pass/fail result will be returned. Only valid when a setnr is given. Data will be evaluated for all sites of a multi-site test.

 |
 |

result

 |

The result given when setnr is specified. The result parameter contains a P (pass) or an F (fail) if the GPF or PPF option has been selected.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Only DPS pins and DC Scale pins configured with `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） are supported.

 |
 |

binary_data

 |

The binary data result string. The string starts with the '#' character, followed by a digit in the range 1 to 9 which stipulates how many digits are used in the data length specifier. The data length specifier is next - up to 9 digits determine how many bytes of data will follow. Then comes the actual data string which appears as a list of values separated by a "," (comma). The first byte of data is an identifier which defines the format of the following data. For a waveform the first byte is '\x00' with the waveform represented as FLOAT64 values. Each value is in Amps [A].

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000170,0.1,0.2,0.2,0.3
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#90000000121,2,0.1,0.2
PSEE 1,,,()
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? 1,PVAL
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000010,0.15,0.25
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000010,0.3,0.3
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? 1,PPF
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000000
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000000
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? 1,GPF
PSER 1,F,(),#9000000000
PRLT? ALL // get multisite results
PRLT "FPP" // site 1 fail, sites 2 & 3 are pass
```

### Example 5（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSEE, I_300mA, 32, (Vee)
PSER? ,PVAL
```

returns:

```
PSER,,(Vee),#90000000120,0001923451
```

### Example 6（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000096,0.1,0.2
PSIE 1,,all_sampler,,,(Vcc)
PSER? ,PVAL
```

returns:

```
PSER ,,(Vcc),#90000000190.15,0.25,0.35,0.45
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSFC  PSFC  -  Parallel Setup FoCus）

|

site

 |

A single integer representing the site number.

 |
 |

site_string

 |

A string of characters ("0" or "1"). The length of the string corresponds to the number of the configured sites. The nth character of this string stands for site n.

-

1 means that the site is (to be) addressed by any subsequent commands that take the setup focus into account.

-

0 means that the site is not (to be) addressed by any subsequent commands.

If some of the sites that are required to get the setup focus are not available (because they use a channel that is inactivated in the MCDIgnore file) the setup status of these sites will not be changed.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

In the command, this means that all sites that are available for testing (that is, do not use a channel that is inactivated in the MCDIgnore file) are to be addressed by subsequent (setup focus aware) commands.

ALL is returned in the query reply, if the query is issued without the STR parameter, and if all available sites have the setup focus.

 |
 |

STR

 |

forces the query to return a site string even if all available sites have the setup focus. This can be used to check if some sites are not available.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSFC  PSFC  -  Parallel Setup FoCus）

```
PSFC "11111110"
```

In this example, 8 sites are defined. The PSFC command unsets the setup focus for the last site. The setup data of this site will not be changed by any subsequent command execution.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSIE -  Power Supply Internal trigger Execute）

PSIE [setnr], [current_range] [,{keep_range|"RSTO"}] [,{all_sampler|"CH_ALL"}] [,{primary_act|"NPRM"}], [samples] [,settl_time], {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSIE -  Power Supply Internal trigger Execute）

|

setnr

 |

The set number defined by the `DPSE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.85_DPSE__DPSE__-__Define_Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement.md`） command. (The range is 1 to 256). This set contains the limits of the measurement point for pass/fail judgment. When this parameter is specified, the corresponding set must already have been defined.

When the setnr parameter is omitted, the current and the pinlist parameters must be specified.

 |
 |

current_range

 |

If the setnr parameter is specified, this parameter will be ignored.

If the setnr parameter is not specified, you must specify the range with a value. In this case, the measurement will be executed in the smallest range that can measure the given value. The unit is Ampere [A].

 |
 |

keep_range

 |

No longer supported.

The measurement range is kept per default.

For DPS128 and XPS256, the parameter is silently ignored and the measurement range is restored to the force or clamp range.

 |
 |

all_sampler

 |

To upload the results of all channels in the gang with sampler connected, and store them, specify CH_ALL. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels.

If called without the all_sampler parameter, the command will upload only the value of the master channel, even if the measurement was done over the sampler, or if a voltage drop on DUT was measured.

 |
 |

primary_act

 |

The conditional primary activation is default.

To avoid the conditional primary activation, specify NPRM.

 |
 |

samples

 |

(Optional) This parameter specifies how often the measurement will be performed under the same test conditions. The default is 1.

For details see the table above.

The value that will be stored is the average of all these measurements.

This parameter can be used both for measurements defined with DPSE and for measurements defined directly with PSIE.

 |
 |

settl_time

 |

The system must wait the settling time before the measurement is executed. If the force range is switched, for example, "unganging during measurement", to avoid glitches the settling time is waited before the small force range is active.

The unit is milliseconds (ms).

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Names of pins to which this command is applied. The character @ can be used to specify all DPS pins. This parameter will be ignored if setnr is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSIE -  Power Supply Internal trigger Execute）

```
> DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000112,0.09,0.11
> PSIE 1,,,(Vcc)
> PSER? 1,PVAL
< PSER 1,F,(Vcc),#9000000006,0.155
```

In this example, the `DPSE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.85_DPSE__DPSE__-__Define_Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement.md`） command specifies a current limit of 0.9 A to 0.11 A for Vcc. Then the PSIE command starts measurements for the measurement set 1. In this case, the pin name is ignored because the set number is specified with the first parameter. After the measurement, the `PSER`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） command retrieves the measurement value for Vcc. In this case, the 300 mA range that is determined by using the specified limit value, is automatically selected for the measurement.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLC  PSLC  -  Power Supply Load Capacitance）

|

value

 |

The value of the load capacitor (capacitance) in 渭F in the range of 0.0 ... 214748364.6.

 |
 |

DCS_value

 |

Capacitance for DPS128 HC. This value must be set to 0, if there is no capacitance on the DUT board. Otherwise it must be set to the capacitance value of the DUT board.

The range is: `2147 渭F *` number_of_ganged_channels

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

pinlist contains the DPS pins whose capacitive load range you want to set or read. Note that pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command. If more than one pin is specified, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLC  PSLC  -  Power Supply Load Capacitance）

DC Scale DPS128/DPS64

```
PSLC ,4.7, (VDD)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLR  PSLR  -  Power Supply Level Ranges）

|

dps_No

 |

Needed for non-equation-based setup.

The identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify. The number must not exceed the maximum number allowed (as defined by the DSCP (Define System Control Parameter) command). Typing ALL modifies all the existing DPS sets. Typing PRM modifies the primary DPS set. Typing ACT (only for PSLV?) displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Needed for equation-based setup.

This parameter is derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + 1`

 |
 |

vout_frc_rng

 |

Specifies the upper limit of the voltage range for DC Scale channels in [V].

This is the maximum output voltage that can later be programmed by the `PSLV`（raw: `02.06.02.02.195_PSLV__PSLV__-__Power_Supply_LeVel.md`） command. The specified value is rounded up to the next higher range limit of the underlying hardware. The value also effects the number of required channels in case of connect_state = UNGANG (see below).

This parameter does not apply to DPS-slot DPS's and to DC Scale DPS's which provide only one range. Check the `DC Scale Device Power Supplies specifications`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.05_DC_Scale_Device_Power_Supplies_and_VI_Cards.md`） whether voltage force ranges are supported for your configuration. Use the (optional) parameter accordingly.

 DC Scale AVI64 and FVI16 The parameter can be changed in connected state and in disconnected state of the DPS. All other DPS The parameter may only be changed when `PSST, PSST? - (Power Supply STatus)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） is set to OFF for the specified pins.

When changing the range while in LOZ state (see `PSLV`（raw: `02.06.02.02.195_PSLV__PSLV__-__Power_Supply_LeVel.md`）), the system shortly opens the output relay and closes it afterwards.

 |
 |

iout_clamp_rng

 |

Specifies the maximum current for DC Scale channels in [A]. The parameter is ignored for DPS-slot DPS's.

  DC Scale AVI64 and FVI16 The parameter can be changed in connected state and in disconnected state of the DPS. All other DPS The parameter may only be changed when `PSST, PSST? - (Power Supply STatus)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） is set to OFF for the specified pins.

When changing the range while in LOZ state (see `PSLV`（raw: `02.06.02.02.195_PSLV__PSLV__-__Power_Supply_LeVel.md`）), the system shortly opens the output relay and closes it afterwards.

 |
 |

current_limiter

 |

Enables (= protected) or disables (= unprotected) a protection against a shutdown of the tester due to excessive current consumption (see also parameter hex_value, bit 12 of the `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`） query).

 |
 |

const_curr_check

 |

Defines whether constant current check is enabled. The parameter can be set for DPS-slot DPS's as well. Possible values are:

ON Current check is enabled

OFF Current check is disabled (this is the default)

 |
 |

connect_state

 |

Defines the connection state for DC Scale channels. This parameter may only be changed when PSST is set to OFF for the specified pins. Possible values are:

 |   | HIMP  | High Impedance Measurement Mode. This mode allows you to use a DC Scale card as a voltmeter. |
 |   | NORM |

Normal (default)

 |
 |   | HDIG |

Digitizer Mode

This parameter is for UHC4 / UHC4T only!

 |
 |   | NORM_HDIG |

Normal with Digitizer Mode

This parameter is for UHC4 / UHC4T only!

 |
 |   | UNGANG |

Specifies to connect only necessary channels

This parameter is for all DC Scale cards.

Note that on DPS128/64 and XPS256 you cannot execute a current compare on a ganged group of channels in unganged mode. Already activated comparators are silently disabled in unganged mode. A user notification (Error or warning) is omitted in this case, to avoid any interrupt in the testflow. The previous state of the comparators is automatically restored after the ganged group has been restored.

See also `Using UNGANG connect state with DC Scale DPS cards`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.06.01.03_Using_the_UNGANG_connect_state_with_DC_Scale_DPS_cards.md`）.

   | |
 |

pinlist

 |

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command. If a pin is associated with a DPS-slot DPS, it is ignored. @ refers to all pins that are associated with a DC Scale channel.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLR  PSLR  -  Power Supply Level Ranges）

```
PSLR PRM,4,0.5,OFF,NORM,(dps1)
```

This example sets the following parameters for device pin Vee:

- The current primary DPS set
- A voltage of 4 V
- A current of 0.5 A
- Current check is disabled
- The connect state is set to normal, and not high impedance measurement mode

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLR  PSLR  -  Power Supply Level Ranges）

```
PSLR PRM,,,,HDIG,(dps1)
```

This example uses the default parameters for device pin Vee, while the connect state is set to digitizer mode.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLV  PSLV  -  Power Supply LeVel）

Note The settling time parameter (setup_time) of the PSLV command and the rise_... and fall_... parameters of the `PSSR, PSSR? -(Power Supply Slew Rate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.197_PSSR__PSSR__-_Power_Supply_Slew_Rate.md`） command exclude each other. This also applies to the t_ms equation parameter (see `DPSPINS`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07_DPSPINS.md`） and `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）).

 |

dps_No

 |

Needed for non-equation-based setup.

 |
 |

dps_No

 |

The identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify. The number must not exceed the maximum number allowed (as defined by the DSCP (Define System Control Parameter) command.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Modifies all the existing fixed DPS sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

Modifies the primary DPS set.

 |
 |

ACT

 |

(Only for PSLV?) Displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Needed for equation-based setup.

This parameter is derived as follows:

`100000*equation_set_no + 1000*specset_no+1`

 |
 |

voltage

 |

The optional parameter voltage defines the output voltage (in V) of the DPS. Applicable value depends on the DPS type.

 |
 |

source_current

 |

The optional parameter defines the source current limit (ilimit_source) in [A]. The applicable value depends on the DPS type.

The parameter defines the source and the sink current limit if both values are equal.

The parameter defines only the source current limit if the sink_current parameter is used.

 |
 | sink_current |

The extra parameter defines the sink current limit (ilimit_sink) in [A].

The parameter is required only if the source and sink current limits are set to different values. This parameter defines then the sink current limit while the source current limit is defined by the above source_current parameter.

The parameter is not required if the current limits are programmed symmetrically to the same (absolute) value. Both, the source and the sink value are then defined by the source_current parameter.

The query answer shows the sink_current parameter only if the programmed sink current limit is not symmetrical to the source current limit.

 |
 |

impedance

 |

The optional parameter sets the DPS output impedance. You can select:

- LOZ sets the DPS output impedance to low when the test system is in the disconnect state. The current limit remains at the same level as in the active state, while the force voltage is set to 0 V.
- HIZ sets the DPS output to high impedance when the test system is in the disconnect state. This sets the channel to the minimum possible current limit. HIZ is the default state for DPS-slot types. If it is applied to DC Scale cards, HIZ_R is used instead of HIZ.
- HIZ_R sets the DPS output to high impedance by switching the output relay off when the test system is in the disconnect state.

Note that relay switching is slower than with HIZ.

- LOZ_HIZ combines LOZ with HIZ. First, the DPS is switched to 0 V with an unchanged current limit (just like in LOZ mode). After the output voltage has reached 0 V (卤50 mV) or after a timeout of 1 second, the DPS pin is switched to high impedance. This combines the advantages of both modes. A capacitor on the load board is quickly discharged and then the DPS pin is switched to high impedance. This is safer when changing the DUT or DUT board after a disconnect.
- LOZ_HIZ_R combines LOZ with HIZ_R. First, the DPS is switched to 0 V with an unchanged current limit (just like in LOZ mode). After the output voltage has reached 0 V (卤50mV) or after a timeout of 1 second, the DPS pin is switched to open. This combines the advantages of both modes. A capacitor on the DUT board is quickly discharged and then the DPS pin is switched to high impedance. This is safer when changing the DUT or the DUT board after a disconnect.
 |
 |

setup_time

 |

The optional parameter is an integer which specifies the settling time (in ms) of the DPS. All DPS's are synchronized so that they finish their settling periods at the same point in time. This is the point when the system is switched to the connect state. If there are, for example, two DPS's, one with a settling time of 10 ms, and the other with a settling time of 4 ms, then the second DPS will be started 6 ms after the first:

   !`Synchronizing Different DPS Settling Times`（raw: `../../../../raw/93235.png`）

The range is from -2147483647 up to 2147483646 ms.

 The default value is 0.Note setup_time has a resolution of ms (floating point values are rounded to nearest integer). |
 |

pinlist

 |

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command. If more than one pin is specified, the names must be separated by commas. The character @ can be used to set the levels for all DPS pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSLV  PSLV  -  Power Supply LeVel）

```
PSLV 1,5.2,0.5,HIZ,15,(Vee)
```

This example sets the following parameters for device pin Vee:

- DPS set 1
- A voltage of 5.2 V
- A current limit of 0.5 A
- Minimum current limit when the test system is disconnected
- A setup time of 15 ms

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSSL  PSSL   Power Supply Safety Limits）

|

min_voltage

 |

Lowest allowed voltage in V. Must be 鈮?0.

 |
 |

max_voltage

 |

Highest allowed voltage in V. Must be 鈮?0.

 |
 |

max_source_current

 |

Highest allowed source current in A. Must be > 0.

 |
 |

max_sink_current

 |

Highest allowed sink current in A. Must be > 0.

 |
 |

pin_list

 |

Comma separated list of DPS power pins, previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command, and of DC signal (PMU) pins defined by the `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） command.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSSL  PSSL   Power Supply Safety Limits）

```
PSSL OFF,OFF,OFF,OFF,(DPS_1)
PSSL -2,5,0.5,0.5,(DPS_2)
PSSL -1.5,3,0.5,0.5,(SIG_1A)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSSR  PSSR  - Power Supply Slew Rate）

Note The rise_... and fall_... parameters of the PSSR command and the settling time parameter (setup_time) of the `PSLV`（raw: `02.06.02.02.195_PSLV__PSLV__-__Power_Supply_LeVel.md`） command exclude each other. This also applies to the t_ms equation parameter (see `DPSPINS`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07_DPSPINS.md`） and `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）). Note All time values have a resolution of microseconds (floating point values are rounded to three decimal places).

 |

dps_No

 |

Needed for non-equation-based setup.

The identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify. The number must not exceed the maximum number allowed (as defined by the DSCP (Define System Control Parameter) command). Entering ALL modifies all the existing fixed DPS sets. Entering PRM modifies the primary DPS set. Entering ACT (only for PSSR?) displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Needed for equation-based setup.

This parameter is derived as follows:

`100000*equation_set_no + 1000*specset_no+1`

 |
 |

rise_tm_per_v

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the rising edge in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

 |
 |

rise_settm

 |

Sets the settling time for the rising edge in ms.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms.

 |
 |

fall_tm_per_v

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the falling edge in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

 |
 |

fall_settm

 |

Sets the settling time for the falling edge in ms.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms.

 |
 |

rise_t_per_v_c2c

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the rising edge. expression must define a value in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect-" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_rise_t_ms_per_volt parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

rise_setup_t_c2c

 |

Sets the settling time for the rising edge. expression must define a value in ms.

The allowed range is -10000 to 10000 ms.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect-" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_rise_settling_t_ms parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

fall_t_per_v_c2c

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the falling edge. expression must define a value in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect-" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_fall_t_ms_per_volt parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

fall_setup_t_c2c

 |

Sets the settling time for the falling edge. expression must define a value in ms.

The allowed range is -10000 to 10000 ms.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_fall_settling_t_ms parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command. If a pin is associated with a DPS-slot DPS, it is ignored. @ refers to all pins that are associated with a DC Scale channel.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSSR  PSSR  - Power Supply Slew Rate）

```
PSSR PRM,10,50,20,70,(Vcc)
```

This example sets the following parameters for the primary set of DPS pin Vcc:

- rise_tm_per_v = 10 ms/V
- rise_settm = 50 ms
- fall_tm_per_v = 20 ms/V
- fall_settm = 70 ms

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSST  PSST  -  Power Supply STatus）

|

state

 |

The device power supply state:

 |
 |

 |

ON

 |

Switches the DPS on.

 |
 |

 |

OFF

 |

Switches the DPS off.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which the DPS is switched on/off.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSST  PSST  -  Power Supply STatus）

```
PSST ON
```

This example turns the DPS on.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSST  PSST  -  Power Supply STatus）

The following example shows the use of the PSST command in conjunction with multisite:

```
PSFC ALL ; PSST ON   # turn on all supplies of all sites

PSFC "01"              # focus on one site only of the dual-site

PSST OFF,(vcc)         # turn off vcc of one site only!
PQFC 1 ; PSST? (vcc)   # these last two commands return different
PQFC 2 ; PSST? (vcc)   # answers, since one site should have vcc
                       # connected, whereas the other site does not
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSTE  PSTE  -  Parallel SiTe Enable）

| sites |

The sites parameter is an integer that specifies the number of sites (to be) configured. The maximum is 1024.

For more information, refer to `Number of sites`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits.md#_116532__r_numberOfSites`） in `SmarTest system parameters - default values and limits`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits.md`）.

 |
 | site_string |

A string consisting of "0" and "1". The length of the string corresponds to the number of the configured sites. The nth character of this string stands for site n.

"0" indicates that the respective site uses a channel that is listed in the MCDIgnore file, and that this site therefore cannot be used for testing. "1" indicates that the site can be used.

 |
 | STR |

If you specify this optional keyword in the query, PSTE? will return a site string.

If this parameter is omitted, PSTE? will return the number of sites that are configured in the pin configuration.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PSTE  PSTE  -  Parallel SiTe Enable）

```
> PSTE 3
```

This example configures three sites (site 1, site 2, and site 3).

```
> PSTE? STR
< PSTE "101"
```

This example says that three sites are configured, but that only two of them (site 1 and site 3) are available for testing. Site 2 uses a channel that is listed in the MCDIgnore file, and therefore cannot be used for testing.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PTDE  PTDE  -  Path for Test Data Entities）

|

device_directory

The path to the device directory in which the test data entities (TDEs) are located.

 |
 |

domain

The name of the domain in the specified device directory that contains the test data entities (TDE).

The domain is one of the subdirectories of the device directory. It bundles all related TDEs.

 |
 |

TDE_directory

The name of the directory in the domain that contains the test data entities (TDE).

This name is usually the name of the firmware command file to which the directory belongs, with a .files extension.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PTDS  PTDS  -  Pin attributes Tweaking Definition String）

|

channelNo

 |

This is a five digit field which defines the channel to which the pin is connected. See also the command `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for this parameter.

 |
 |

You can also enter:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Sets, or returns information on, all channels.

 |
 |

EBT_specifier

 |

The Equation Based Timing specifier can be:

 |
 |

eqn_set

 |

Equation Set number in the range of 1 to 256.

 |
 |

0

 |

Causes the next parameter (set_specifier) to be interpreted as waveform_set instead of spec_set.

 |
 |

If you specify the name of a multi-port specification for the set_specifier parameter, the EBT_specifier parameter will be ignored.

You can also enter:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Sets delay for, or returns information on, all Equation Sets.

 |
 |

set_specifier

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

1 to 256

 |

The number is interpreted as a waveform set number if EBT_specifier is set to 0. Otherwise, it is taken as a specset number.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multiport setup, you can specify the name of a multi-port specification in double quotes. In this case, the EBT_specifier parameter will be ignored. The pin attributes will be associated with the specified timing set (timing_set parameter) in every port of the specification.

 |
 |

You can also enter:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Sets delay for, or returns information on, all Spec Sets or Waveform Sets.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing Set number in the range of 1 to 256. You can also enter ALL to select information on all timing sets.

Note that ALL is the only allowed option if EBT_specifier or set_specifier is also set to ALL.

 |
 |

tweaking_set

 |

Tweaking Set number. Currently not used.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Currently not used.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

Definition string for the logical edges.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › PTDS  PTDS  -  Pin attributes Tweaking Definition String）

```
PTDS 10812,0,4,5,,1,1,"d1:2,d2:0.003, d8:5, r1:-1, r2:-2"
PTDS? 10101,,all,all,,
```

The following example defines pin attributes for timing sets of the multi-port specification spec_port_1_port_2.

```
> PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",1,,,"d1:1 d3:3"
> PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",2,,,"d1:2 d2:3"
> PTDS? 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,,
< PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",1,,,"d1:1 d3:3"
< PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",2,,,"d1:2 d2:3"
```
