### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

```
RCLS? {test}, {pass_value}, [limit], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
RCLS {value_specifier}, {result_value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

|

test

 |

This parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

H

 |

to determine the high level threshold for the DUT output pins.

 |
 |

L

 |

to determine the low level threshold for the DUT output pins.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The pass_value parameter defines the expected pass value (in mV) for the threshold measurement.

pass_value must be in the range of the comparator threshold level in the channel board (see `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`）).

 |
 |

limit

 |

The limit parameter specifies the limit (in mV) of the measurement window for value measurements. The range for this parameter is as follows:

- If you want to determine the high level threshold, the value entered must be between the maximum comparator threshold level of the channel board (see `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`）) and the specified pass value
- If you want to determine the low level threshold, the value entered must be between the pass value and the minimum comparator threshold level of the channel board.

If a pass/fail test is to be performed, this parameter must be omitted. For both high and low level threshold measurements, the search is performed by varying the comparator threshold from the limit you specify, to the hardware limit.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be tested. This parameter may also include groups previously created using the DFGP command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. pinlist must only contain pins configured as outputs.

 |
 |

value_specifier

 |

This parameter contains one of the following:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned after a high level test to indicate that the first functional test (performed at the value defined by the limit parameter) failed. LT is only returned after a value test.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned, after a low level test, if all the tests carried out within the window pass. LE is only returned during value measurements.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

Equal to is returned if the first failure of the level test occurs within the measurement window. EQ is only returned after a value measurement.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned, after a high level test, if all the tests carried out within the window pass. GE is only returned after a value measurement.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned after a low level test to indicate that the first functional test (performed at the value defined by the limit parameter) failed. GT is only returned after a value test.

 |
 |

P

 |

A P is returned if the functional test passes. A P can only be returned if the limit parameter has been omitted.

 |
 |

F

 |

An F is returned if the functional test fails. An F can only be returned if the limit parameter has been omitted.

 |
 |

result_value

 |

The result value is the level (in mV) of the last passed test.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

```
RCLS? H,3000,6000,(Q0)
```

returns:

```
RCLS EQ,5300
```

In this example a search was made to find the high level threshold between 3V and 6V. The pass/fail transition was located at 5.3V.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RCLV  RCLV  -  ReCeive LeVel）

|

level_set

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the low and high threshold levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP, DSCP? - (Define System Control Parameter)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）). If you enter a level set number that is outside the used range of sets defined by the LSUS command, a new level set is created. Typing ALL in this field sets the low and high threshold levels for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Typing PRM sets the low and high threshold levels for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number greater than 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for sequencer state OFF. For more information see `Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF`（raw: `02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md`）.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

 |
 |

vth

 |

Output threshold for FAST comparator (single threshold as opposed to high and low). The expression must define a value in millivolts (mV).

 |
 |

logic_0_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the logic 0 threshold level of the comparator. This parameter represents the point where the comparator distinguishes between logic 0 and an intermediate level.

 |
 |

logic_1_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the logic 1 threshold level of the comparator. This parameter represents the point where the comparator distinguishes between logic 1 and an intermediate level.

 |
 |

range

 |

This extra parameter selects the receive range in mV.

This parameter is currently not available.

Ranges of the high-speed voltage comparator:

- -8000.0 ... 8000.0 selects the 8 V range
- -40000.0 ... 80000.0 selects the -40 V ... +80 V range

Ranges of the high-resolution voltage comparator:

- -3000.0 ... 3000.0 selects the 3 V range
- -10000.0 ... 10000.0 selects the 10 V range
- -30000.0 ... 30000.0 selects the 30 V range
- -40000.0 ... 80000.0 selects the -40 V ... +80 V range

If not specified the best fit range will be selected based on logic_0_level and logic_1_level if a voltage comparator is selected.

Range of the high-resolution current comparator:

- A fixed range of 200 mA is set.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose threshold level you want to set. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the command `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ sets or reads the threshold levels for all output pins. You can include O or IO pins in pinlist.

 |

For card specifications, like level ranges, see `Digital Cards`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04_Digital_Cards.md`）, for example:

- `Pin Scale 1600`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.01.03_PS1600_driver.md`）
- `Pins Scale 5000`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.03.04_Pin_Scale_5000_driver.md`）

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RCLV  RCLV  -  ReCeive LeVel）

```
RCLV 1,-1300,-750,(Q0)
```

This example sets the low level compare threshold for pin Q0 to -1300 mV and the high level compare threshold to -750 mV.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RCLV  RCLV  -  ReCeive LeVel）

```
TERM 1,,,,,,HRV,(avi64Pin1)
RCLV 1,-1300,-750,3000,(avi64Pin1)
```

This example for an AVI64 pin sets the low level compare threshold to -1300 mV, the high level compare threshold to -750 mV, and the range to the 3 V range.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RDGC -  Reset DiGital Capture）

```
RDGC {"vector_label"|ALL}[,(portlist)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RDGC -  Reset DiGital Capture）

|

vector_label

 |

Vector main label. You can specify ALL to dissolve the associations for all vector labels of one or more ports.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

If you specify ALL for vector_label, the association is dissolved for all vector labels of the ports specified here. The default for this parameter is the default port @ to which all pins belong.

Specify @@ to remove the association for all label of all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RDGC -  Reset DiGital Capture）

```
> SDGC? ALL,(@@)
< SDGC "vec_lab_portA_1",STD,(I/O7_1,I/O6_1,I/O5_1)
< SDGC "vec_lab_portA_2",STD,(I/O2_1,I/O1_1,I/O0_1)
< SDGC "vec_lab_portB_1",STD,(I/O7_2,I/O6_2,I/O5_2)
< SDGC "vec_lab_portB_2",STD,(I/O3_2,I/O2_2,I/O1_2)
> RDGC ALL,(port_A)
> SDGC? ALL,(@@)
< SDGC "vec_lab_portB_1",STD,(I/O7_2,I/O6_2,I/O5_2)
< SDGC "vec_lab_portB_2",STD,(I/O3_2,I/O2_2,I/O1_2)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RLYC  RLYC  -  ReLaY Control）

| pin_mode |

This parameter controls per-pin relay resources. These are AC, DC and PPMU relays. pin_mode can take the following options:

 | IDLE  | Disconnects all relays |
 | AC  | Connects a DUT pin to its associated digital channel |
 | DC  | Closes the DC relay |
 | PPMU  | Closes the PPMU relay to connect the pin to the Pin-PMU |
 | ACDC  | Closes both the AC and DC relay |
 | BOTH  | Identical to ACDC |
 | ACPM |

Closes both the AC and the PPMU relay.

 |
 | DCPM  | Closes both the DC and PPMU relay |
 | ALL  | Closes all pin relays (AC, DC, PPMU) |
 | CNCT  | Special connect mode: for all I, O, IO pins AC relay closed, for all DC pins AC relay open |
 | X  | The settings of all relays remain unchanged  | |
 | dc_target |

The parameter lets you connect DC resources to the selected DUT pin. It controls the following relays:

- ISOL and GND relays on channel boards
- Pin PMU on channel boards

The dc_target parameter can be specified as an "enum" or a "string" value. The following keywords can be specified:

 | OFF  | Opens all channel board and clock board relays. |
 | PMU  | Closes the channel board PMU relay. This does not automatically connect the pin to the board ADC. |
 | EXT |

For digital DC pin:

Closes the external relays (EXT) on the clock board and ISOL and GND relays on the channel board.

For utility DC pin:

 Depends on the test system.

- Smart Scale test system: closes the EXT relay and the DUT relay on the clock board.
- EXA Scale test system: closes all relays on the utility-line card, card-cage, and test-head needed to establish a connection from the utility pogo to the external instrument.
 |
 | X  | The relays connecting the pins remain unchanged.  |   The keywords specify fixed combinations of relay settings, necessary to perform certain functions. As an alternative you can control the relays individually using the "string" entry. This has the format: "CCC", where each character "C" represents a relay on a channel board. Each character can take the value 0, 1, or X:

- 0: opens the relay
- 1: closes the relay
- X: leaves the relay unchanged

The functionality of the characters from the left to the right are as follows:

- ISOL relay on channel board
- GND relay on channel board
- PMU relay on channel board (BADC)
- EXT relay for utility lines (test system dependent)

This option, to control individual relays usin the "string" entry, is not supported for utility DC pins

 |
 | mux_setting |

This is an extra parameter that controls the input MUX of the board ADC (BADC). The following keywords can be specified:

 | MUX_VM_HIZ  | Switches the MUX to the high-impedance input of the BADC. |
 | MUX_PPMU  | Connects the BADC to the PPPMU in preparation for a dynamic pin PMU value measurement using the BADC.  | |
 | pin_list |

The pinlist parameter defines which pins are affected by the command. All pins must be configured as I, O, IO or DC pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by commas.

When some digital channels are configured for triggering analog modules that are shared by multiple sites in a multi-site test, you can use the special identifier @NONSHARED@ to disconnect just the resources that are not shared between configured sites. Also, you can use @SHARED@ to disconnect just the resources that are shared.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RLYC  RLYC  -  ReLaY Control）

### AC and DC examples

 |

```
RLYC IDLE,OFF,(pin)
```

   | Open all relays. |
 |

```
RLYC DC,OFF,MUX_VM_HIZ,(pin)
```

   | Close the DC relay, open all channel board relays, select the high impedance input of the board ADC. |
 |

```
RLYC ACPM,OFF,MUX_PPMU,(pin)
RLYC? (pin)
```

 |

Close both the AC and the PPMU relay, open all channel board relays, connect the board ADC to the PPMU and

 query the state of the relays. The returned state is

```
RLYC ACPM,OFF,(pin)
```

 |
 |

```
RLYC AC,,(pin)
RLYC? (pin)
```

 |

Close only the AC relay and

 query the state of the relays. The returned state is

```
RLYC AC,OFF,(pin)
```

 |
 |

```
RLYC DC,,(pin)
RLYC? (pin)
```

 |

Close only the DC relay and

 query the state of the relays. The returned state is

```
RLYC DC,OFF,(pin)
```

 |
 |

```
RLYC PPMU,,(pin)
RLYC? (pin)
```

 |

Close the PMU relay and

 query the state of the relays. The returned state is

```
RLYC PPMU,PMU,(pin)
```

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRDF -  Result Retention area DeFinition）

RRDF {area-id}, {size}[, (pinlist)]

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRDF -  Result Retention area DeFinition）

|

area-id

 |

A unique string for identifying the result retention area.

The area is referenced when being selected by its ID for result acquisition or upload.

The area ID must be globally unique - it is not allowed to define two result areas on different pin lists with the same ID.

Any number of areas may be added for the same pins until the available result memory is consumed. The required size is specified in bytes (analogous to `DMAS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.79_DMAS__DMAS__-__Define_Memory_Area_Size.md`）) but is internally rounded to a multiple of 1 KB.

 |
 |

size

 |

The required size of the result retention area in bytes.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

A list of pins for which to create the result area.

The pinlist must either match exactly one already defined result retention area or must be disjoint (may not overlap with any other pin list).

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRSC -  Result Retention area Select for Capture）

RRSC {area-id} | OFF

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRSC -  Result Retention area Select for Capture）

|

area-id

 |

A unique string identifying a specific result retention area.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Enumerated parameter to switch back to normal result acquisition.

Using OFF will return result acquisition to non-reserved memory or internal error map (as specified by DCRT).

   | Note The RRDF pin list must match the capture pins for a capture test. An error map test requires that all pins of the selected port (recording to RAM via DCRT) are included.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRUD -  Result Retention area UnDefine）

```
RRUD
```

If the result area is currently selected for recording or upload, it will be deactivated.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RSET -  ReSET）

```
RSET {specifier}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RSET -  ReSET）

|

specifier

 |

The specifier can be:

 |
 |

DPS

 |

Loads the default power supply setup for standard DPSs.

 |
 |

FCR

 |

Loads the default clock routing.

 |
 |

LEV

 |

Loads the default power supply setup for standard DPSs.

Level: 0 V

Current: 50 mA

Off state: minimum current

Setup time: 0 ms

This default states are:

UHC4T

- Connect state: normal
- Level: 0 V
- Range: 4 V
- Clamp: 4 A
- Clamp-Range: 40 A
- Disconnect state: HIZ
- Voltage drop force: 250 mV
- Voltage drop return: 250 mV
- Clamp mode: limit (see `UHCM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md`）)
- DUT capacitor mode: off

Fast preload: 0 ms

 |
 |

TIM

 |

Loads the default timing setup. The settings are:

Timing Sets

- Defined Timing Sets: 1
- Allowed Timing Sets: 256

Waveform Sets

- Defined Waveform Sets: 1
- Allowed Waveform Sets: 16

Waveforms: not defined

Breakwaveform: defined

Events

- Action: NOP
- Timing: 0 ns

Min Period: 4 ns

- This is dependent on the test system hardware configuration.

Device Cycles: not defined

Default Device Cycle: ""

 |
 |

VEC

 |

Loads the default vector setup. The Vector Memory contains:

No vectors

No tests (and therefore no labels)

No comments

No sequencer programs (no instructions)

 |
 |

ATR

 |

Loads the default edge attributes.

Pin attribute: set to 0

 |
 |

PDL

 |

Loads the default path delay attributes.

Cable assembly delay attribute: set to 0

Fixture delay attribute: set to 0

System attribute: set to 0

 |
 |

CAL

 |

Loads the default calibration data.

Level calibration data

Timing calibration data

 |
 |

MTPP

 |

Resets memory test and per-pin sequencer subroutine data.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RSET -  ReSET）

```
RSET TIM
```

This example resets all waveform sets and timing sets and loads the hardware with the default vector rate and edge placement values. Only waveform set 1 and timing set 1 in waveform set 1 is active.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RSSR  -  Retrieve Spec Search Results）

```
RSSR? {set_nr},[(setup_pinlist)]
```

returns:

```
RSSR {set_nr},(search_result),[pass_value],[fail_value],(setup_pinlist)
```

Parameters
 |

set_nr

 |

Specifies the number of the search set for which results are to be returned.

 |
 |

setup_pinlist

 |

The specified setup pins identify the search conditions for which the results are to be returned. For conditions with several setup pins, only one of them needs to be specified.

If this parameter is omitted, results are returned for all search conditions for which a valid result exists.

 |
 |

search_result

 |

Specifies whether a transition was found.

Possible values are:

 |
 |

P

 |

Transition found

 |
 |

 |

F

 |

No transition found

 |
 |

 |

E

 |

No result found for the specified pins. Search was not executed or had errors.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The last (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the first (in a FAIL/PASS transition) spec value or edge position where the test passed.

If only a pass value is returned, the test always passed.

 |
 |

fail_value

 |

The first (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the last (in a FAIL/PASS transition) spec value or edge position where the test failed.

If only a fail value is returned, the test always failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RSSR  -  Retrieve Spec Search Results）

```
> PQFC 2
> RSSR? 3,(@)
< RSSR 3,P,90.1,90.2,(OUT1)
< RSSR 3,P,33.1,33,(IN1)
```

In this example, RSSR? returns the results of all setup pins in search set 3 for site 2. For OUT1, a pass/fail transition was found, for IN1 a fail/pass transition.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRSU   Result Retention area Select for Upload）

RRSU {area-id} | OFF

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRSU   Result Retention area Select for Upload）

|

area-id

 |

Mandatory parameter consisting of a variable string. The quotes belong to the command language (not the syntax language) and must be specified in the call and also in the syntax description..

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Enumerated parameter to switch back to normal result upload focus.

Using OFF will return result retrieval to the default result area or internal error map (as specified by DCRT).

   | Note The result area selected for upload must contain valid results. That means the area must have been defined via RRDF, must have been selected as recording target prior to a test execution using RRSC.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RRSU   Result Retention area Select for Upload）

The following example defines a result area with the name "my_area" with a size of 128KB for all pins. This area is then selected as recording target for the subsequent functional test. The results in this area remain available even after execution of additional functional tests and can later be accessed by switching the upload forcus with 'RRSU 'my_area'' to it.

```
RRDF "my_area",128000,(@)
RRSC "my_area"
FTST?
RRSC OFF
RRSU "my_area"
ERMP? EDGE,0,8000,PF,8,(emap_pin)
RRSU OFF
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVCU -  Remove Vector variable Configuration Usage）

```
RVCU {label name}, {VVC name}, vector offset
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVCU -  Remove Vector variable Configuration Usage）

|

label name

 |

Name of the label for which usage is to be modified.

 |
 |

VVC name

 |

Name of the vector variable configuration. Refer to `DVVC, DVVC? - (Define Vector Variable Configuration)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.95_DVVC__DVVC__-__Define_Vector_Variable_Configuration.md`） for more information.

 |
 |

Vector offset

 |

This is the offset in the label where usage needs to be modified. Vector offset is the logical vector number in the label. A usage with this combination of parameters {label name, VVC name, Vector offset} should already exist in the system as defined by `DVCU`（raw: `02.06.02.02.96_DVCU__DVCU__-__Define_Vector_variable_Configuration_Usage.md`）. Refer to `DVCU, DVCU? - (Define Vector variable Configuration Usage)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.96_DVCU__DVCU__-__Define_Vector_variable_Configuration_Usage.md`）.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVCU -  Remove Vector variable Configuration Usage）

The following example removes the usage defined for label "src" using VVC "AC97" at offset 0.

```
> RVCU "src","AC97",0
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVVA -  Remove Vector VAriable）

RVVA {"name"|ALL}[, (portlist)]

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVVA -  Remove Vector VAriable）

|

name

 |

Name of the vector variable to be deleted. ALL can be used to remove all vector variables that are associated with the vector labels of one or more ports.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

This parameter is evaluated according to the following rules:

- If a vector variable is specified for name, the parameter is ignored.
- If you set name to ALL and specify a port list, all vector variables will be deleted that are associated with the vector labels of these ports.
- If you set name to ALL and do not specify a port list, all vector variables will be deleted that are associated with the vector labels of the default port.
- If you set name to ALL and specify @@, all vector variables of all ports will be deleted.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVVA -  Remove Vector VAriable）

```
> DVVA? ALL,(@@)
< DVVA "vec_3",DIGCAPT,"port1_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,
       1,0,(Q7_1)
< DVVA "vec_1",DIGCAPT,"port2_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,
       1,0,(I/O5_2)
< DVVA "vec_2",DIGCAPT,"port2_B",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,
       1,0,(I/O7_2,I/O6_2)
> RVVA ALL,(port_2)
> DVVA? ALL,(@@)
< DVVA "vec_3",DIGCAPT,"port1_A",PARA,,,,0,1,1,0,
       1,0,(Q7_1)
```

This example removes all vector variables that are defined for vector labels associated with port port_2.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVVC -  Remove Vector Variable Configuration）

```
RVVC {VVC name}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RVVC -  Remove Vector Variable Configuration）

|

VVC name

 |

Name of the vector variable configuration to be removed.

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SAOF  SAOF  -  Set Alternating Operation Features）

|

mode

 |

The operation mode which can take the following values:

 |
 |

ZERO

 |

Editing mode. This is the default.

 |
 |

APP

 |

This mode serves to append data to the sequencer and vector areas. In order to do that, you must first allocate memory for the respective area with the DMAS command. Now,in editing mode, the DMAS command defines the size of the area (it starts from address 0). If, however, the system is in APP mode, the existing area will be expanded by the size specified in the DMAS command.

Note that you cannot iterate this step. If you allocate memory in APP mode for a second time, the first expansion will be redefined. In order to further expand the area, you must first issue SAOFAPP again.

 |
 |

LOAD

 |

Load vectors. This mode improves performance of a vector download.

 |
 |

TMLD

 |

Load timing and/or pin attributes. This mode improves performance of a timing download.

 |
 |

EGRP

 |

Edit group definitions.

 |
 |

label

 |

If you call SAOF with a label name, you can generate a vector file for this label only.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SAOF  SAOF  -  Set Alternating Operation Features）

The following example illustrates the effects of the APP mode:

```
> SAOF?
< SAOF ZERO
> DMAS SQPG,SM,4,(@)
> DMAS SQPG,SM,3,(@)
> DMAS? SQPG,SM,(@)
< DMAS SQPG,SM,3,(@)
> SAOF APP
> DMAS SQPG,SM,4,(@)
> SAOF ZERO
> DMAS? SQPG,SM,(@)
< DMAS SQPG,SM,7,(@)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SATR  SATR  -  System ATtRibutes）

|

comm_rec_delay

 |

The common receiver delay represents the adjustment to the round-trip delay between the drivers and receivers. The delay is in [ns] and must be in the range -50 to +50. Three digits are allowed after the decimal point. The default value is 0.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SATR  SATR  -  System ATtRibutes）

```
SATR 20
```

This example sets the common receiver delay to 20 ns.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SCLK  -  System CLocK query）

```
SCLK? {wf_set|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|ALL|PRM}
```

returns:

```
SCLK {wf_set|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"} {sclk_val}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SCLK  -  System CLocK query）

|

wf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *`equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

sclk_val

 |

The SCLK period of the respective setup in ns.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Returns the SCLK values for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

Returns the value for the primary waveform set or specification (set by SPRM).

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SCLK  -  System CLocK query）

```
> SCLK? 401
< SCLK 401,480
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SDGC  SDGC  -  Setup DiGital Capture）

|

vector_label

 |

The vector label that is to be activated for digital capture. It must be a main label, and the sequencer memory must have been specified as the location of the input vectors.

For the query, you can type ALL to list all the activated vector labels of one or more ports.

 |
 |

res_mode

 |

Capture resolution mode. Valid modes are:

STD: standard mode

DBL: double high resolution mode

Note that the hardware will always operate in double high resolution mode. Therefore the resolution mode specified here is important only for data reconstruction. You will notice that this implies that only the high resolution comparator is used for the data capture action.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of pins that are to be activated for digital capture. If the list contains more than one element, the names must be separated with a comma.

All the specified pins must be contained in the port with which the specified vector label is associated.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

If you call the query for all vector labels (ALL for vector_label) and specify a port list, the settings will be returned for the specified ports. The default for this parameter is the default port @ to which all pins belong.

Specify @@ to display the activated labels of all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SDGC  SDGC  -  Setup DiGital Capture）

```
> SDGC? ALL
< SDGC "test_capt",STD,(OUT_1,OUT_2)
```

This example returns all the vector labels of the default port @ that are activated for digital capture.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SDSC  -  Set number DeSCriptions）

```
SDSC? {spec_type}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], [setup_comp_2], ["description"]
```

returns:

```
SDSC {spec_type}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], [setup_comp_2], {"description"}
```

Alternatively, for multiport specifications:

```
SDSC? {TIM}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], {"multi-port_spec"}, ["description"][, (portlist)]
```

returns:

```
SDSC {TIM}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], {"multi-port_spec"}, {"description"}, {(port)}
```

Parameters
 |

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use:

 |
 |

LEV

 |

to specify levels

 |
 |

TIM

 |

to specify timing. This is the only possible value for multi-port specifications.

 |
 |

ANA

 |

to specify analog setup

 |
 |

type

 |

The possible values and their meaning are as follows:

 |
 |

EQN

 |

equation sets

 |
 |

SPS

 |

specsets

 |
 |

WVT

 |

wavetables (equation based)

 |
 |

T

 |

timing sets (equation based)

 |
 |

L

 |

logical level sets (equation based)

 |
 |

WSET

 |

waveform sets (non-equation based)

 |
 |

TSET

 |

timing sets (non-equation based)

 |
 |

LSET

 |

level sets (non-equation based)

 |
 |

DSET

 |

digital sets

 |
 |

ASET

 |

analog sets (for analog setup)

 |
 |

RSET

 |

routing sets (for analog setup)

 |
 |

setup_comp_1

 |

An integer in the range 1 to 99 that refers to a setup component of a certain type (for example, an equation set or waveform set). The component type is determined by the values of spec_type and type according to the table below. If no value is specified, all components of the respective type are processed.

If you specify the name of a multi-port specification for the setup_comp_2 parameter, the setup_comp_1 parameter will be ignored.

 |
 |

setup_comp_2

 |

An integer that refers to a setup component of a certain type (for example, a timing set or spec set). The component type is determined by the values of spec_type and type according to the table below. If no value is specified, all components of the respective type are processed.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, enter the name of a specification instead of a component number, but only for spec_type TIM. In this case, the setup_comp_1 parameter will be ignored.

 |
 |

description

 |

Maximum 60 characters. Can be also a substring of a description, in which case all components containing this string in their description are returned.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

With multi-port specifications, you can specify a list of ports. If you do, only those components will be displayed that are associated with one of the specified ports.

If you specify a port list, the setup_comp_1 parameter will be ignored.

 |

The following table explains the interpretation of the setup_comp_1 and setup_comp_2 parameters for every accepted value pair of the spec_type and type parameters:

 |

spec_type

 |

type

 |

setup_comp_1

 |

setup_comp_2

 |
 |

TIM

 |

EQN

 |

equation set

 |

Not allowed

 |
 |

TIM

 |

WVT

 |

equation set timing specset

 combined into a specset_id

 |
 |

TIM

 |

SPS

 |

equation set

 |

timing specset

 |
 |

TIM

 |

T

 |

equation set

 |

timing set

 |
 |

TIM

 |

WSET

 |

waveform set

 |

Ignored

 |
 |

TIM

 |

TSET

 |

waveform set

 |

timing set

 |
 |

LEV

 |

EQN

 |

equation set

 |

Ignored

 |
 |

LEV

 |

SPS

 |

equation set

 |

level specset

 |
 |

LEV

 |

L

 |

equation set

 |

level set

 |
 |

LEV

 |

LSET

 |

level set

 |

Ignored

 |
 |

ANA

 |

ASET

 |

Not allowed

 |

analog set

 |
 |

ANA

 |

RSET

 |

Not allowed

 |

routing set

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SDSC  -  Set number DeSCriptions）

```
> SDSC? TIM,EQN,,,
< SDSC TIM,EQN,1,,"gross_func_eqn"
< SDSC TIM,EQN,2,,"specs_search_eqn"
< SDSC TIM,EQN,3,,"speed_eqn"
```

This example returns all defined equation sets.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SDSC  -  Set number DeSCriptions）

```
> SDSC? TIM,EQN,2,"spec_port_1_port_2",,(port_1)
< SDSC TIM,EQN,1,"spec_port_1_port_2",
     "gross_func_eqn",(port_1)
```

This example returns the equation set that is associated with port port_1 in the multiport specification

spec_port_1_port_2. Note that the setup_comp_1 parameter is ignored.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SHSP  SHSP  -  SHmoo SPecs）

```
> SHSP LEV, "aclk_vil",(aclkout), LEV, "adata_vil", (adata3)
> SHSP?
< SHSP LEV, "aclk_vil",(aclkout), LEV, "adata_vil", (adata3)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SHSP  SHSP  -  SHmoo SPecs）

In the following Pin Scale example, both spec variables occur in the period definitions associated with the two ports:

```
> CLKR? "MP_spec",(Port1)
< CLKR "MP_spec",17,3.4,(Port1)
> PRPT? "MP_spec","shmsp@Port1";
< PRPT "MP_spec",(Port2)
> SHSP TIM, "shmsp@Port1",,TIM,"shmsp@Port2",
> SHVL 17,30
> PRPT? "MP_spec","shmsp@Port1"
< PRPT "MP_spec",(Port1)
> CLKR? "MP_spec",(Port1)
< CLKR "MP_spec",17,4.25,(Port1)
```

Since `shmsp` is used in the period definitions for both port `Port1` and `Port2`, the one that is specified first in the SHSP command will be used to derive the period resolution. Note that the primary port is only changed after issuing the SHVL command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SHVL  SHVL  -  SHmoo spec VaLues）

|

value_1

 |

A double float defining the new value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

Or use RSTO to restore the original value.

 |
 |

value_2

 |

A double float defining the new value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

Or use RSTO to restore the original value.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SHVL  SHVL  -  SHmoo spec VaLues）

```
> SHSP TIM, "shmsp@Port1",, TIM, "shmsp@Port2",
> SHVL 2,3
> SHVL?
< SHVL 2,3
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SLDO -  Switch Level and Dps Order）

|

order

 |

This parameter sets the switching order mode:

 |
 |

FDSL

 |

First DPS, second levels. If this parameter is specified, the DPS voltage values are always switched before the voltage values of the levels.

 |
 |

CVDL

 |

There are three possibilities:

1. If DPS voltage values are increasing or stable, DPS voltages are switched before level voltages.

2. If DPS voltage values are decreasing or stable, level voltages are switched before DPS voltages.

3. If the voltages of some DPS pins are decreasing while the voltages of others are increasing (ambiguous case), DPS voltages are always switched first.

 |
 |

report

 |

This parameter sets the report mode, which can be one of the following:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Reports a change in the switching order from DPS voltages (first) to level voltages (first) and vice versa.

 |
 |

FLSD

 |

First levels, second DPS. Reports a change in the switching order to switching level voltages first.

 |
 |

AMBI

 |

Ambiguous case. Reports an ambiguous case.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

Nothing is reported. This is the default report mode.

 |
 |

operation

 |

This is the mode of operation. SAVE returns values for everything that can be set.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SLDO -  Switch Level and Dps Order）

```
SLDO CVDL, AMBI
```

This example switches either the DPS voltage values or the level voltage values first when changing from one DPS or level set to the next depending on which of the three above mentioned cases occur and reports any ambiguous case.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPCP  -  SPeCification Port list）

```
SPCP? {"multi-port_spec"|ALL}
```

returns:

```
SPCP {"multi-port_spec"}, {(portlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPCP  -  SPeCification Port list）

|

multi-port_spec

 |

Defines the multi-port specification for which the ports are to be queried. You can enter ALL in order to display the ports for all defined multi-port specifications.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

Displays the ports to which the specification applies.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPCP  -  SPeCification Port list）

```
> SPCP? ALL
< SPCP "spec_port_1_port_2",(port_1,port_2)
< SPCP "spec_ClkP_P1_P2",(ClockPort,p_CP_1,p_CP_2)
< SPCP "spec_ssearch_port_1_port_2",(port_1,port_2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPEC  -  SPECification）

```
SPEC? {"module:resource"},["details"],[context], [(pinlist)]
```

returns:

```
SPEC {"module:resource"},["details"],[context], {answer},[(pinlist)]
```

   Parameters

 | module:resource  | Specifies the module and the resource about which information is to be returned. Currently, the following values are allowed: |
 | Level:Term  | Queries the termination modes that can be specified with the `TERM, TERM? - (TERMination mode)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.257_TERM__TERM__-__TERMination_mode.md`） command for the specified pins and level setup. |
 | Level:Rcvrange  | Queries the minimum logic 0 threshold and the maximum logic 1 threshold that can be specified with the `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`） command for the specified pins and level setup. |
 | Level:UnterminatedModes  | Query returns unterminated termination modes for the given pin or pins, see pinList parameter (these modes have no leakage). |
 | Level:Pulldown  | Query the termination modes that support a pulldown resistor. |
 | Timing:FxdlRange  | Queries the range of the fixture delay, as defined by `FXDL, FXDL? - (FiXture DeLay)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.128_FXDL__FXDL__-__FiXture_DeLay.md`）, for the current system. |
 | HiRes:Mode  | Queries the possible options for determining High and Low of a differential pin. One of these options must be used for param2 of the `HROL, HROL? - (High Resolution Option and Level)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.140_HROL__HROL__-__High_Resolution_Option_and_Level.md`） command. |
 | pattern:testPoints |

Queries the minimum number of vectors that must be inserted between any of the following two points:

- Two test points,
- Vector 0 of the containing label and the first test point,
- A test point and the preceding instruction.

This applies only to testpoints defined with `TPSE, TPSE? - (Test Point SEquence)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.268_TPSE__TPSE__-__Test_Point_SEquence.md`）.

 |
 | Result:Xmodes  | Queries which x-modes are available to the result module on the current hardware. |
 | details |

Specifies a string containing a comma separated list. This parameter is required for the following module/resource combination

- Result:Mode: Specify `fail,8`
- HiRs:Mode: Specify ResultVerdictMode
 |
 | context |

Specifies further restrictions on the required information. This parameter is required for the following module/resource combinations:

- Level:Term and Level:Rcvrange to specify the level setup.

For a fixed level setup, enter a number from 1 to 99, or specify PRM to query the primary level set.

For an equation based level setup, specify a level setup ID. The level setup ID is derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no`

- Timing:FxdlRange

Global is currently the only allowed value.

 |
 | answer |

Returns the requested information. In the answer for Level:Rcvrange, the minimum 0 threshold precedes the maximum 1 threshold.

Note that the structure of the replies may change from release to release.

 |
 | pinlist  | A list of pins, separated by commas. This parameter is irrelevant for Result:Mode, but must be specified for the other queries.  |  Application Error map, level setup.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPEC  -  SPECification）

```
SPEC? "Result:Xmodes",,,(@)
```

returns

```
SPEC "Result:Xmodes",,,"1,2,4,6,8",(...)
```

This example queries which x-modes are possible for the result module on a Smart Scale system. On a Pin Scale system, x-mode 6 would be omitted in the reply.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPEC  -  SPECification）

The second example queries the termination modes that can be specified with the `TERM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.257_TERM__TERM__-__TERMination_mode.md`） command for pin "PS1600_pin" and level set 1:

```
SPEC? "Level:Term",,1,(PS1600_pin)
```

returns

```
SPEC "Level:Term",,1,"OFF,T,H,L,A,C,CT,HV,DIFHIZ",(PS1600_pin)
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPEC  -  SPECification）

The third example queries the range of the fixture delay:

```
SPEC? "Timing:FxdlRange",,"Global",
```

returns

```
SPEC "Timing:FxdlRange",,"Global","-0.015000,13.200000",()
```

The query returns the range for Pin Scale systems.

Note: Parameter pinlist is irrelevant for this query and may be omitted.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPGV -  SPlit Generate Vectors）

```
SPGV {vec_No}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPGV -  SPlit Generate Vectors）

|

vec_No

 |

The logical vector number at which a GENV sequencer construct is to be split.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPGV -  SPlit Generate Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,16,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,528,,,(@)
< ...
> SPGV 7
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> SQPG ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,7,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STVA,536,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example splits a GENV sequencer construct at command number 2 before vector 7. Note the adjustment of the start address in command 6.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPOP  SPOP  Set Performance Optimization Parameter）

|

keyword

 |

Specifies the parameter for which performance optimization is to be changed or queried. Currently, the only possible value is:

- SVLR_CACHE_DEPTH: Defines the number of timing sets which will be cached for searches and `SVLR`（raw: `02.06.02.02.252_SVLR__SVLR__-__Spec_VaLues_at_Runtime.md`） TIM commands.

For Pin Scale systems, the default is 10, the minmum is 1, and the maximum is 30. For P/C systems, the only possible value is 1.

 |
 |

value

 |

Specifies the value for the optimization parameter.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPOP  SPOP  Set Performance Optimization Parameter）

> SPOP SVLR_CACHE_DEPTH, 20

> SPOP? SVLR_CACHE_DEPTH

< SPOP SVLR_CACHE_DEPTH, 20

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPRM  SPRM  -  Set PRiMary sets）

|

waveform_set_no

 |

The identification number of the waveform set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of waveform sets allowed - as defined by `CONF, CONF? - (CONFiguration)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.31_CONF__CONF__-__CONFiguration.md`）.

 |
 |

timing_specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

Note that the spec set ID also identifies the primary wavetable in equation based testing.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

For a multi-port setup, specify a primary multi-port specification.

 |
 |

timing_set_no

 |

The identification number of the timing set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets (of the selected waveform set or timing specification). The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of timing sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）).

In a multiport setup, the timing set number applies to all ports of the specification if you do not specify a port. If you do, the number applies to the specified port.

 |
 |

timing_set_list

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can specify primary timing sets for all ports of the specification by entering a list of numbers separated by commas. The order of the timing sets must correspond to the order of the ports in the multi-port timing specification.

In the query, the numbers of the primary timing sets are returned in a list for all ports of the primary specification unless the numbers are identical for all ports or a port has been specified in the query.

 |
 |

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed level sets. The maximum number is determined by `LSUS, LSUS? - (Level Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.155_LSUS__LSUS__-__Level_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）).

 |
 |

dps_set_no

 |

The identification number of the DPS set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed DPS sets. The maximum number is determined by `DSUS, DSUS? - (Dps Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.91_DSUS__DSUS__-__Dps_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must be less than or equal to the maximum number of DPS sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）).

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no`

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + 1`

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multiport setup, you can specify a port of the specification that was entered as the first parameter. In this case, the timing set number specified as the second parameter will only be applied to the specified port. The port parameter is ignored if a timing set list is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPRM  SPRM  -  Set PRiMary sets）

The following example shows how to define and query primary timing sets for the multi-port specification spec_ClockP_P1_P2, which contains three ports:

```
> SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2","2,1,2",,
> SPRM?
< SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2","2,1,2",101002,101003
> SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2",2,,,(port_1.CP_1)
> SPRM?
< SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2",2,101002,101003
> SPRM? (port_1.CP_1)
< SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2",2,101002,101003,(port_1.CP_1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
SPST? {spec_type}, {equation_set_no}, {specset_no}
```

returns:

```
SPST {spec_type}, {equation_set_no}, {specset_no}, {status}
```

or, for multiport specifications:

```
SPST? {spec_type}, , {"multi-port_spec"}
```

or

```
SPST? {spec_type}, PRM,
```

returns:

```
SPST {spec_type},, {"multi-port_spec"}, {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

|

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use:

 |
 |

LEV

 |

to specify levels, or

 |
 |

TIM

 |

to specify timing.

 |
 |

equation_set_no

 |

Equation set number. An integer in the range 0 to 256.

Use ALL to refer to all defined equation sets. Use PRM to specify the primary equation set. In the latter case, the specset_no parameter is ignored.

Equation set 0 is used for compatibility with a non-equation based testing environment. In this case, when equation set 0 is used and spec_type is LEV, specset_no is meaningless, while when equation set 0 is used and spec_type is TIM, specset_no is interpreted as the number of a waveform set.

 |
 |

specset_no

 |

Spec set number. An integer in the range 1 to 99. Use ALL to refer to all defined spec sets.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, enter the name of a specification instead of a spec set number. In this case, the equation_set_no parameter must be left empty.

 |
 |

status

 |

An integer that indicates the settings of the status bits. Every set bit is represented by a power of 2, as described in the table below. The integer is the sum of these powers.

For example, if 768 = 512 + 256 is returned, then bits 8 and 9 are set, and all other bits are cleared.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
> SPST? lev,all,all
< SPST LEV,1,1,0
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
> SPST? tim,all,all
<  SPST TIM,1,1,0
< SPST TIM,2,22,0
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
> SPST? TIM,,"mu_burst"
< SPST TIM,,"mu_burst",6
```

In this last example, a multi-port specification is queried. The answer says that bits 1 and 2 have been set. This has the effect that a drive or receive period 1 limit violation will be ignored, and only a period 2 limit violation will be recorded.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQBV  SQBV  -  SeQuencer Break Vector insertion）

The following example synchronizes two ports RX and TX, each of which is the only port in its sequencing group. The RX port does not admit any changes of primary sets, the TX port must change its primary sets several times during the testflow. This is implemented by the `FTCG`（raw: `02.06.02.02.125_FTCG__FTCG__-__Functional_Test_ConfiGure.md`） command as follows:

```
> FTCG SKPR,OFF,(@@)
> FTCG SKPR,ON,(RX)
```

In order to synchronize both ports, the time span used up by the activation sequences in TX must be filled with break vectors in RX. If both ports operate with the same period length, and the PHASE flag is set for both of them in the multi-port timing specification, then the number of break vectors that compensates the different types of activation sequences will always be a multiple of 8. The exact number must be determined by empirical tests. The required numbers could then be passed to SQBV as follows:

```
> SQBV ,1504,TIM,(RX)
> SQBV ,22048,TIM_LEV,(RX)
> SQBV ,31784,ALL,(RX)
```

The reference port is TX. This is specified by

```
> SQRP (TX)
```

Finally, the timing changes in TX may include moving receive edges across cycle boundaries, and this in turn can (in rare cases) prolong the activation sequence for the next functional test. But this is not acceptable, because only one value can be passed to SQBV for every activation sequence type. In order to secure that the length of an activation sequence is not affected by the timing of the preceding test, break vectors can be inserted in TX before the last activation of the respective sequence type, so that the sequence as a whole has the extended length even if no cycle crossing takes place in the previous test.

The required number of break vectors must again be determined by measurements. The required number of vectors could then be defined as follows:

```
> SQBV 128,,TIM,(TX)
> SQBV 128,,TIM_LEV,(TX)
> SQBV 128,,ALL,(TX)
```

Note that in this case the insertion port is identical with the reference port.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQEC  SQEC  -  SeQuencer Execution Context）

|

context_name

 |

The name of the context. If a context with this name already exists, the previous definition will be overwritten.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

In the query, you can specify ALL in order to retrieve the definitions of all executuion contexts

 |
 |

port_list

 |

The list of the ports that are to run in this execution context.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQEC  SQEC  -  SeQuencer Execution Context）

```
> SQEC "c1",(P1,P2)
> SQEC? ALL
< SQEC "c1",(P1,P2)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

|

mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

ACQF

 |

ACQuire Failure mode. Only failed cycles are recorded, starting after analyze_delay cycles. If analyze_delay is not a multiple of 8, recording starts after the nearest smaller multiple of 8. In this mode the Error Map is called the Acquire Failure Map.

As the test proceeds the Acquire Failure Map is filled with failure data until the test stops or the map becomes completely full, whichever occurs first. If the map stops recording before the test has finished, the sequencer, which is in standard mode, continues executing the test until the end.

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of ACQF is reproduced by:

DCGM FAIL,STRT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

ACFF

 |

This mode is functionally identical to ACQF. It is obsolete and should not be used in new applications.

 |
 |

EL

 |

EndLess. The sequencer repeats the complete test, including primaries and multiport synchronization, in an endless loop and can only be stopped by Break.

The analyze_delay parameter is ignored. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented mode.

This mode is used for oscilloscope tests. The Error Map functions as a rolling buffer. After stopping the sequencer, the Error Map shows the last "buffer-full" of recorded cycles.

 |
 |

ELPT

 |

EndLess PaTtern. The sequencer repeats only the user program. This avoids critical holds during measurement.

In case of multiport testing, ports may run with different frequencies. Using the ELPT mode in this case, can lead to the situation, that for loop counts >1 the synchronization is no longer executed.

 |
 |

EMPS

 |

Error Map PoSitioning. The Error Map is in cycle oriented mode, the sequencer in default mode. The analyze_delay parameter specifies the end of the recorded area. If it is not a multiple of 8, the last cycle to be displayed is the largest multiple of 8 that is smaller than analyze_delay. The first cycle to be displayed is determined by the size of the Error Map (8k cycles).

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of EMPS is reproduced by:

DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

SE

 |

Stop on Error. The sequencer runs from the beginning of the test and stops when an error is encountered. If no errors occur, the sequencer runs to the end of the test and stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. The analyze_delay parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

SEEL

 |

Stop on Error and EndLess. The sequencer repeats the test in an endless loop, unless an error is encountered, whereupon it stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode. This mode is used to locate sporadic failures.

 |
 |

STSQ

 |

STop SeQuencer. Stops the sequencer after analyze_delay cycles. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. See also the query `GETC? - (GET Cycles)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.131_GETC__-__GET_Cycles.md`） for the analyze_delay count.

 |
 |

STRD

 |

In the query reply, this mode is displayed if the current combination of recording mode, as set with DCGM, and interpretation of the Error Map position, as set with DCRP, is different from all the other SQGB modes. For example, the Error Map can be in cycle oriented recording mode, and analyze_delay be interpreted as a start value.

In the command, this option leaves it to SmarTest to select the appropriate recording mode (cycle oriented or acquire failure), unless the recording mode has been explicitly set with DCGM.

 |
 |

STSV

 |

STop Sequencer on Vector. Stops the sequencer at the logical vector number specified in the analyze_delay parameter before executing the vector. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM.

Note that the STSV option cannot be used if no start label has been defined with SQSL, or if the start label is a burst or multi-port burst label.

 |
 |

analyze_delay

 |

Sets the analyze delay. This parameter is mandatory for the STSQ and STSV modes. Its interpretation depends on the selected mode parameter. The number must be between 1 (0 for ACQF) and 281,474,976,710,655 = 2^48 - 1 (2^48 - 2 for ACQF).

If the mode parameter is set to STSV, three cases must be distinguished:

- If analyze_delay is an existing logical vector number of the actual start label, the sequencer will be stopped at this logical vector before executing the vector.
- If analyze_delay specifies the total number of logical vectors (= greatest logical vector number of the test + 1) the sequencer stops at the last valid vector.
- If analyze_delay is greater than the total number of logical vectors, an error message is issued.
 |
 |

ref_port

 |

This parameter accepts a single port. It must be specified in the following situation:

- The selected mode requires an analyze delay (but is different from STSV), and
- the start label is a multi-port burst.

It specifies the port which is used for counting the cycles specified with the analyze_delay parameter. When this reference port has completed the specified number of cycles, the sequencers will be stopped, or cycle recording started or stopped, for all ports. Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

 |
 |

port_list

 |

If the current mode requires an analyze delay, you can specify a port list in the query. The reply will give the calculated analyze delays for those ports that are not used as the reference port. These delays are derived from the analyze delay of the reference port and the ratio between the period lengths of the reference port and the other port in the primary timing setup. If you specify @@, SQGB will return the settings for all ports of the current start label.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

```
> PCLK? "mu_burst",1,(@@)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,20,(P1)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,10,(P2)
> SPRM "mu_burst",1,,
> SQSL "mu_burst"
> SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
> SQGB? (@@)
< SQGB STSQ,15,(P1)
< SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
```

This example configures the sequencers to stop when port P2 has completed 30 cycles. Port P1, whose period length is twice the period length of P2, will be stopped after 15 cycles. Note that P1 and P2 must belong to the same sequencing group.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQIB  SQIB  -  SeQuencer Interrupt Behavior）

|

BANDWIDTH

 |

This refers to the behavior when the detailed error map is located in the external memory, and result recording was aborted due to a bandwidth overflow of the memory.

 |
 |

TIMEOUT

 |

This refers to the behavior in case of a sequencer timeout.

 |
 |

ERIM

 |

SmarTest issues an error message immediately after completion of the test. In case of a recording abort, this message reports the channels, pins, and sites of all channel groups on which recording was aborted.

In case of a sequencer timeout, a list of those channels is returned on which the timeout occurred.

 |
 |

FLIM

 |

This option is only allowed with TIMEOUT.

SmarTest reports the test as failed, that is, FTST? returns F. This is the default for TIMEOUT.

 |
 |

ERRQ

 |

This option is only allowed with BANDWIDTH.

SmarTest does not issue an error message immediately after completion of the test, but only if a channel which is involved in a recording abort is queried for result data. In this case again, the channels, pins, and sites of all channel groups on which recording was aborted will be reported. This is the default for BANDWIDTH.

 |
 |

FLRQ

 |

This option is only allowed with BANDWIDTH.

SmarTest does not issue any error message. If a channel of a group on which recording was aborted is queried for result data, all its cycles will be reported as failing.

This option can be used in a production environment if the result data is recorded in acquire failure mode, since if any data is recorded with this recording mode, the device must in fact have failed. Actually, recording will only be aborted in case of a massive fail on several pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQIB  SQIB  -  SeQuencer Interrupt Behavior）

```
SQIB BANDWIDTH FLrQ
```

This example suppresses all error messages in case of a recording abort.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQIT  -  SeQuencer InterRupt）

|

context

 |

The name of an execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`）.

 |
 |

NO

 |

No interrupt occurred during execution of the last test.

 |
 |

BANDWIDTH

 |

An interrupt occurred due to a bandwidth error.

 |
 |

TIMEOUT

 |

An interrupt occurred due to a timeout error.

 |
 |

OTHER

 |

An interrupt occurred due to an error that was neither a bandwidth nor a timeout error..

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins on which the specified interrupt was observed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQIT  -  SeQuencer InterRupt）

```
> SQSL "test1"
> SQST RUN
> SQIT?
< SQIT TIMEOUT, (pin1)
```

In this example, a timeout was observed on `pin1`.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQLA  SQLA  -  SeQuencer Label Attribute）

|

type

 |

Currently, LBL is the only possible value. This is also the default.

 |
 |

name

 |

A sequencer label. If ALL is specified in the query, then all labels of the specified port are returned together with their attributes.

 |
 |

attr_key_i=

attr_val_i

 |

Attribute-value pairs. Valid attribute names are:

 |
 |

PARA_MEM

 |

Specifies the memory type for parallel vectors. Possible values are:

SM = standard memory (default for MAIN and SVEC)

NONE = no memory for parallel vectors (default for all label types except MAIN and SVEC)

SHMEM = memory shared for different sites of the same pin (only for 7.x, for details see `Selecting the memory type`（raw: `02.06.07.01.04.01_Selecting_the_memory_type.md`）.

HSER = memory for SmartLoop鈩? initialization patterns (see `Defining a compliance pattern for pattern鈥慴ased SmartLoop testing`（raw: `02.06.17.04.01_Defining_a_compliance_pattern_for_pattern__ased_SmartLoop_testing.md`）)

An empty value will delete the attribute definition. This attribute can only be changed if the sequencer program of the label contains no GENV or RPTV instructions.

 |
 |

PARA_MCTX

 |

Specifies the mode context that is associated with the label. A mode context defines a type (I, O, or IO) and a mode (std or fast) for every configured pin. You define mode contexts in the Pin Configuration tool. The default mode context, which sets the mode of every pin to std, has the name DEFAULT.

Note that within a test setup, the label must have the same mode context as the associated timing and level data.

 |
 |

If ALL is specified in the query, all attributes for the given labels are returned. If SAVE or an attribute name is specified in the query, only attributes explicitly defined for the given labels are returned.

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter is only evaluated if you specify ALL for the second parameter in the query. In this case, SQLA? will return the attributes of those labels that are associated with the ports specified here. The default for this parameter is the default port @ to which all pins belong.

Specify @@ to display attributes for all labels of all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQLA  SQLA  -  SeQuencer Label Attribute）

```
> APTS LBL,"test","table1"
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,16,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
> SQLA ,"test","PARA_MEM=SHMEM"
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
```

This example changes the PARA_MEM attribute of the new label test from SM to SHMEM. Note the change of the address in command line 4.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example defines a burst label for the default port.

Display the whole sequencer area:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< ...
< SQPG 8,STOP,,,,(@)
```

The sequencer area comprises nine command lines. Three further lines are required for the rudimentary burst label. Thus, issue:

```
> DMAS SQPG,SM,12,(@)
```

Define the label:

```
> SQLB "burst_1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb",(@)
```

Display the whole sequencer area again:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< ...
< SQPG 8,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 9,NOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 10,NOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 11,BEND,,,,(@)
```

You can now replace the NOP instructions in command lines 9 and 10 by CALL instructions with the SQPG command.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example queries all labels of all types for the default port.

```
> SQLB? ALL,ALL
< SQLB "test_1",MAIN,0,4,"spec_search_wtb"
< SQLB "test_2",MAIN,5,8,"spec_search_wtb"
< SQLB "burst_1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb"
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example renames the burst label `burst_1`, defined in example 1, to "BURST1".

```
> SQLB "BURST1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb"
> SQLB? ALL,BRST
< SQLB "BURST1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb"
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example illustrates the relative numbering of the command lines in SAOF APP mode.

```
> SAOF?
< SAOF ZERO
> SQLB? ALL,ALL
< SQLB "L_1",MAIN,0,2,"wf1"
> SAOF APP
> DMAS SQPG,SM,3,(@)
> SQLB "L_2",MAIN,0,2,"wf1"
> SAOF ZERO
> SQLB? ALL,ALL
< SQLB "L_1",MAIN,0,2,"wf1"
< SQLB "L_2",MAIN,3,5,"wf1"
```

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQPG  SQPG  -  SeQuencer ProGramming）

The following is a simple example of a counted match loop:

```
SQPG 3,MACT,256,CONTINUE,,(@)
SQPG 4,GENV,5,,,(@)
SQPG 5,MRPT,5,,,(@)
```

Note that only the GENV or RPTV instruction is allowed immediately before the MACT instruction. CONTINUE, which is optional, tells SmarTest to continue the surrounding test even if the match loop failed.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQPG  SQPG  -  SeQuencer ProGramming）

The following example shows that inserting a GENV instruction into a label with SQPG disturbs the sequencer constructs and must be accompanied by an appropriate adjustment of the vector areas (see also `Inserting a sequencer instruction`（raw: `02.06.07.01.07.03.01_Inserting_a_sequencer_instruction.md`）).

Display the sequencer area of the default port:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< ...
< SQPG 4,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 7,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 8,STVA,520,,,(@)
< ...
```

The vector area segment of the label starting at command 4 comprises 2 memory words, as shown by the start address of the following label (command line 8).

Now display the vector area segment of pin S0_1 for the label starting at command 4, and also the first memory word of the following label:

```
> $VECD? PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1)
< VECD PARA,SM,504,16,(S0_1),
 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001
 0000 0001 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000
 0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000
```

The GENV instruction is associated with the first two memory words. The last 7 bytes of the second word are padding vectors. This is shown by making the first label the start label and then displaying the active vectors of command 6 for pin `S0_1`:

```
> SQSL "test_1"
> $VCYC? 0,9,(S0_1)
< VCYC 0,9,GENV,F160,(S0_1),
 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001
 0000 0001
```

Now insert a GENV instruction before command 6:

```
> TSTL "test_1",
> INSI 6,1
> SQPG 6,GENV,1,,,(@)
```

Display the active vectors for the two GENV instructions:

```
> $VCYC? 0,10,(S0_1)
< VCYC 0,1,GENV,F160,(S0_1), 0000 0001
< VCYC 1,9,GENV,F160,(S0_1),
 0000 0001 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000
 0000 0010
```

The first memory word is now associated with the new instruction. The first of its vectors is active, the others are inactive. The previous command 6 (now command 7) is now associated with the second and the third block. Thus the third memory word is illegally shared between two labels.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQRC -  SeQuencer Remove execution Context）

|

context_name

 |

The name of the context to be removed.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

With this option, all existing contexts will be removed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQRC -  SeQuencer Remove execution Context）

```
> SQRC "c1"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQRP  SQRP  -  SeQuencer Reference Port）

|

port

 |

This parameter specifies the reference port.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQRP  SQRP  -  SeQuencer Reference Port）

The following example synchronizes two ports RX and TX, each of which is the only port in its sequencing group. The RX port does not admit any changes of primary sets, the TX port must change its primary sets several times during the testflow. This is implemented by the `FTCG`（raw: `02.06.02.02.125_FTCG__FTCG__-__Functional_Test_ConfiGure.md`） command as follows:

```
> FTCG SKPR,OFF,(@@)
> FTCG SKPR,ON,(RX)
```

In order to synchronize both ports, the time span used up by the activation sequences in TX must be filled with break vectors in RX. If both ports operate with the same period length, and the PHASE flag is set for both of them in the multi-port timing specification, then the number of break vectors that compensates the different types of activation sequences will always be a multiple of 8. The exact number must be determined by empirical tests. The required numbers could then be passed to SQBV as follows:

```
> SQBV ,1504,TIM,(RX)
> SQBV ,22048,TIM_LEV,(RX)
> SQBV ,31784,ALL,(RX)
```

The reference port is TX. This is specified by

```
> SQRP (TX)
```

Finally, the timing changes in TX may include moving receive edges across cycle boundaries, and this in turn can (in rare cases) prolong the activation sequence for the next functional test. But this is not acceptable, because only one value can be passed to SQBV for every activation sequence type. In order to secure that the length of an activation sequence is not affected by the timing of the preceding test, break vectors can be inserted in TX before the last activation of the respective sequence type, so that the sequence as a whole has the extended length even if no cycle crossing takes place in the previous test.

The required number of break vectors must again be determined by measurements. The required number of vectors could then be defined as follows:

```
> SQBV 128,,TIM,(TX)
> SQBV 128,,TIM_LEV,(TX)
> SQBV 128,,ALL,(TX)
```

Note that in this case the insertion port is identical with the reference port.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQSL  SQSL  -  SeQuencer Start Label）
