```
> SQSL "test_1"
> SQSL? TYPE
< SQSL "test_1",MAIN,(@)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQSL  SQSL  -  SeQuencer Start Label）

```
> PSFC 2
> SQSL "test_1"
> SQSL? ALL
< SQSL "test_1","11",MAIN,(@)
> SQSL "test_2", "10"
> SQSL "test_3", 2
> SQSL? ALL
< SQSL "test_2","10",MAIN,(@)
< SQSL "test_3","01",MAIN,(@)
> SQSL?
< SQSL "test_2"
> PQFC 2
> SQSL?
< SQSL "test_3"
```

This example illustrates the definition of different start labels for different sites. Note that the restriction of the setup focus has no influence on the command, but that the setting of the query focus does affect SQSL?.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQST  SQST  -  SeQuencer STate）

|

seq_state

 |

Gives the state of the sequencer:

 |
 |

OFF

 |

In the OFF state, both the sequencers and the clock are off. All pins go into the high-z state.

This option can only be applied to all execution contexts.

 |
 |

HALT

 |

In the HALT state, both the sequencer and the clock are off, and the drivers keep their last level or remain in high-z state if already in high-z state.

Note that you cannot pass directly from HALT to OFF or from OFF to HALT. You must first pass to BRK in both cases.

This option can only be applied to all execution contexts.

 |
 |

BRK

 |

In the BRK state, the clock is on and the break waveform is applied to the DUT.

This option can only be applied to all execution contexts.

 |
 |

ABRT

 |

This is not a sequencer state, but an instruction to change the state of an execution context from RUN to BRK. ABRT requires that an execution context is specified.

 |
 |

CBRK

 |

This is not a sequencer state, but a conditional instruction. If no context is in BRK or RUN state, the state of the global context will be changed to BRK. If any context is in BRK or RUN state, nothing will be done.

 |
 |

RUN

 |

In the RUN state, the clock is on and the sequencer applies vectors to the DUT. This option can be applied to a specified execution context.

 |
 |

Note that if the sequencer state changes from OFF or BRK to RUN, the sequencer runs with the global settings that have previously been defined with `SQGB, SQGB? - (SeQuencer GloBal)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.232_SQGB__SQGB__-__SeQuencer_GloBal.md`）.

 |
 |

exec_context

 |

An execution context. In the command, this parameter can only be added to the sequencer state RUN and the instruction ABRT. It must be added if ABRT is specified. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） .

If the query is issued without a context, then RUN will be returned if there is at least one context that is in the RUN state.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQST  SQST  -  SeQuencer STate）

```
SQST RUN
```

This example starts a global sequencer run.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQTO  SQTO  -  SeQuencer TimeOut）

|

timeout

 |

Defines the time (in seconds) that the sequencer runs. The default value is 900 and the range is 0.001 to 2147483.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SQTO  SQTO  -  SeQuencer TimeOut）

```
SQTO 3000
```

This example programs the sequencer to exit after 50 minutes.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SREC  SREC  -  Set RECeiver mask）

|

mask_value

 |

The mask value parameter specifies whether a pin mask will be applied:

 |
 |

ACT

 |

If ACT is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list become active (not masked).

 |
 |

X

 |

If X is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are masked.

 |
 |

STOR

 |

If STOR is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are stored.

 |
 |

RSTO

 |

If RSTO is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are restored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be masked. This parameter may also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） or by `DFGE, DFGE? - (DeFine Group Expressions)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.59_DFGE__DFGE__-__DeFine_Group_by_Expressions.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pins in pinlist can be O or IO pin types. The @ character sets the mask for all pins of these types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SREC  SREC  -  Set RECeiver mask）

```
SREC X, (D1, D2, D3, D4)
```

This example masks the pins D1, D2, D3 and D4.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SRPR  SRPR  -  Set Routing PRimary）

set

An identification number of the routing set. This is an integer from 1 to the maximum number defined by the DSCP command.

If the NONE specifier is specified, no routing statements will be executed by the next command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSAC  SSAC  -  Source Synchronous testing  Add Configuration）

|

read_mode

 |

Possible read modes are:

 |
 |

NORM

 |

Channel data is processed as it is stored in the source channels. This is the default.

 |
 |

INV

 |

Channel data is inverted internally before it is processed. The channel data itself is not changed.

 |
 |

nr_of_results

 |

Specifies the size of the area to be used for buffering cycle/edge data for source synchronous testing. If this parameter is omitted you must specify a reference pin.

The number to be specified here must be calculated as

result_granularity * number_of_cycles.

The result granularity is the number of results per cycle. It can be 1 (one global result), in which case you must specify the number of cycles, or 8 (one result for every edge), in which case you must specify 8 * number_of_cycles.

The number of bytes required to store the specified number of results must be a multiple of 8. If this requirement is not satisfied, the number of results will be auto-corrected.

 |
 |

ref_pin

 |

The pin that defines the size of the buffer area. If this parameter is omitted, you must specify the number of results. If a reference pin is defined, the nr_of_results parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins that are to be configured as buffer pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSAC  SSAC  -  Source Synchronous testing  Add Configuration）

The following example shows how the buffer channels are configured by using a reference pin:

```
> DCGM ALL,STRT,NONE
> DCRT RAM,(@)
> SSRC (@)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.4
> FTST?
> SSAC INV,,(D1),(SB)
> SSAC NORM,,(D1),(G1,G2)
> SSCT IMM,NORM,,(SB),(D1,D2,D3,CL)
> SSCT ACC,NORM,,(G1),(SB)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.5
> FTST?
. . .
```

First the detailed Error Map is configured for source synchronous testing (recording mode ALL, location in RDRAM). Next the existing buffer configurations are removed. Then the sweep variable is set, and the first functional test executed. Subsequently the buffer channels are configured using D1 as the reference pin. Then the results of the first functional test are processed. Finally, the sweep variable is incremented and the next functional test executed.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSCT  SSCT  -  Source Synchronous data  Combine and Transfer）

The following example shows a typical start sequence of a source synchronous test:

```
> DCGM ALL,STRT,NONE
> DCRT RAM,(@)
> SSRC (@)
> SSAC INV,128,,(SB)
> SSAC NORM,128,,(G1,G2)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.4
> FTST?
> SSCT IMM,NORM,128,(SB),(D1,D2,D3,CL)
> SSCT ACC,NORM,128,(G1),(SB)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.5
> FTST?
> SSCT IMM,NORM,128,(SB),(D1,D2,D3,CL)
> SSCT ACC,NORM,128,(G2),(SB,G1)
. . .
```

At first, the detailed Error Map is configured for the requirements of result buffering (error map located in RDRAM, recording mode ALL). After the first functional test the results of the data pins D1 through D3 and the output clock pin CL are immediately combined and transferred into the source buffer SB. The subsequent transfer into the first global buffer is delayed and will only be triggered by the next FTST? call. After the second functional test, the SSCT ACC call combines the results of the source buffer and the first global buffer into the second global buffer.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSRC -  Source Synchronous testing  Remove Configurations）

```
SSRC {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSRC -  Source Synchronous testing  Remove Configurations）

|

pinlist

 |

The pins whose buffer configurations are to be removed. Pins for which no buffer configuration exists are ignored.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSRC -  Source Synchronous testing  Remove Configurations）

```
> SSRC (@)
```

This example removes all buffer configurations. Pins for which no buffer has been configured are ignored.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSTR  -  Source Synchronous Testing  Result query）

```
SSTR? [ALL_SITES,] {GLO|INV},{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
SSTR {GLO|INV},{(pinlist)},{glob_res}
```

Or:

```
SSTR? {DET},{(pin)}
```

returns:

```
SSTR {DET},{(pin)},{#spec(data)}}
```

Parameters
 |

ALL_SITES

 |

This parameter causes SSTR? to return a global result for all sites. If it is omitted, the result for that site is returned that currently has the result focus.

 |
 |

GLO

 |

One global result is returned for all buffers of the pin list. The result is calculated by combining first all cycle results of the individual buffers with AND, and then the combined buffer results of all buffers again with AND. PASS will be returned if the final result is 1.

This option must be selected if PASS is represented by 1 and FAIL by 0 in all buffer pins.

 |
 |

INV

 |

One global result is returned for all pins of the pin list. The result is calculated in 3 steps:

- The cycle results of the individual channels are inverted.
- The inverted cycle results are combined with AND.
- The global results of the individual channels are again combined with AND

PASS will be returned if the final result is 1.

This option must be selected if PASS is represented by 0 and FAIL by 1 in all buffer pins. A possible application is that one global result is to be returned for one or more global buffers.

 |
 |

DET

 |

The cycle results of the specified buffer pin are returned as they are stored in the buffer.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The buffer pins whose results are to be accumulated. More than one pin can only specified for options GLO and INV.

 |
 |

pin

 |

If DET is specified as the first parameter, only one pin may be specified.

 |
 |

glob_res

 |

The global result that is returned for options GLO and INV. "P" signifies PASS, and "F" signifies FAIL.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that is returned for option DET. It has a header which specifies the length of the data in the following format:

#Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream,

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

If you record 8 results per cycle (every edge is recorded) then one bit represents one edge. If only one global result per cycle is recorded, two bits represent one cycle.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SSTR  -  Source Synchronous Testing  Result query）

The following example assumes that the global buffer pins G2 and G4 contain the total results of two source synchronous tests that were run in parallel:

```
> SSTR? INV,(G2)
< SSTR INV,(G2),P
> SSTR? INV,(G4)
< SSTR INV,(G4),F
> $SSTR? DET,(G4)
< SSTR DET,(G4),#9000000008,0000 0000  0001 0000  0000 0000  0000 0100  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000
> SSTR? INV,(G2,G4)
< SSTR INV,(G2,G4),F
```

Note that the result granularity has been set to 8, so that every bit of the SSTR DET reply represents one receive edge. Note also that SSTR DET simply returns the buffer content. Since the global buffers must represent FAIL by 1 and PASS by 0, the reply indicates that one edge in the second cycle and one edge in the fourth cycle have failed in all shots for one of the two tests. All other edges have passed at least in one shot.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STDE -  Save Test Data Entity）

STDE

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STDE -  Save Test Data Entity）

```
STDE
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STME  STME  -  SiTe Match Enable）

|

ON

 |

Turns the site match function on.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Turns the site match function off.

 |
 |

AUTO

 |

Starting the sites successively affects the test negatively if the pin configuration contains at least one shared digital channel for triggering an analog module. The AUTO option checks if such a shared channel exists. If it does, the match site function is set to OFF; if not, it is set to ON. AUTO is the default.

 |
 |

FAST

 |

Activates the `Fast Sync`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.03_Fast_Sync.md`） feature (local synchronization) of the test processor. After setting this option," STME ON" is required to turn on the site match function.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STME  STME  -  SiTe Match Enable）

```
> STME AUTO,
> STME?
< STME ON,
```

This example sets the site match function to AUTO, then reads the actual setting. Since the actual setting is ON, the pin configuration cannot contain a shared digital channel.

```
>SQST OFF
>NIFE 2
>STME FAST,
>STME ON,
```

This example configures the Fast Sync feature, and sets two independent Fast Sync ports on each test processor.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

```
STRS? ["exec_context",] [start], [stop], {mode}, [(pinlist)], {spec_type}, {"spec_name[@port[@UNCHANGED]]"}, [stepwidth], {resolution}
```

returns:

```
STRS {res_spec}, [pass_meas_value], [fail_meas_value], [(pinlist)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

|

exec_context

 |

An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） .

 |
 |

start

 |

Double float with up to 5 digits after the decimal point defining the value of spec_name at the start of the search. The maximum valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647, though this may be limited by the maximum and minimum values defined with the spec. If the parameter is omitted, the minimum value as defined in the spec set will be used.

The start value can be greater than the stop value. In this case the search will be in the negative direction.

 |
 |

stop

 |

Double float with up to 5 digits after the decimal point defining the value of spec_name where you want the search to end. The maximum valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647, though this may be limited by the maximum and minimum values defined with the spec. If the parameter is omitted, the maximum value as defined in the spec set will be used.

The stop value can be smaller than the start value. In this case the search will be in the negative direction.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Search mode. Use:

L to specify a linear search,

LB to specify linear/binary search,

B to specify a binary search.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the value of the spec variable is to be modified. This parameter may also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

The @ character indicates all pins. This is the default.

 |
 |

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use :

LEV to specify levels, or

TIM to specify timing.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

A string of up to 64 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

If you use the option @port`[`@UNCHANGED`]`, (see the port parameter), you must include this extension in the double quotes, too.

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can add a port name to the spec variable. This will have the effect that the value of the variable will be modified only for pins belonging to this port. This holds even if the variable has global scope for this port in the timing specification.

If you specify the spec variable without a port in a multi-port setup, its value will only be modified for a pin whose port has the spec variable set to global scope.

For more information on the scope of a variable see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）.

Note that if a port that is specified with the name of the variable it is this port on which the value of the variable will be modified. The setup pins have no influence on this.

On a Pin Scale system, the specification of a port will have an additional effect:

If spec_name is used in the definition of the port period, this port will be temporarily used as the primary port. For more information see `Modifying the period for a search or shmoo in a multi-port setup`（raw: `02.06.09.01.01.01_Modifying_the_period_for_a_search_or_shmoo_in_a_multi-port_setup__Pin_Sc.md`）.

This switch can be suppressed by adding @UNCHANGED to the port name.

 |
 |

stepwidth

 |

The search step width in the unit specified with the corresponding spec. This is optional if mode is B.

 |
 |

resolution

 |

The smallest step size to be used in the search. Especially useful in a binary search of a range of floating point numbers, where the number of values between start and stop is infinite. The unit must be the same as defined with the spec.

 |
 |

res_spec

 |

LT (less than)

LE (less than or equal to)

EQ (equal to)

GE (greater than or equal to)

GT (greater than).

 |
 |

pass_meas_value

 |

A double float defining the passed measured value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

This parameter contains the last (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the first (in a FAIL/PASS transition) value where the test passed.

 |
 |

fail_meas_value

 |

A double float defining the failed measured value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

This parameter contains the first (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the last (in a FAIL/PASS transition) value where the test failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

```
STRS? 0.5,2.0,LB,,LEV,"aclk_vo_swing",0.1,0.1
```

returns

```
STRS GE,2,,
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

|

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use:

 |
 |

LEV

 |

to specify levels, or

 |
 |

TIM

 |

to specify timing.

 |
 |

equation_set_no

 |

Equation set number. An integer in the range 1 to 99.

Use PRM to specify the primary equation set, or, in a multi-port setup, the primary specification as defined with SPRM. In this case, the specset_no parameter is ignored.

In the query, use ALL to display all equation sets.

This parameter must be omitted if a multi-port specification is specified for the thirdparameter.

 |
 |

specset_no

 |

Specset number. An integer in the range of 1 to 99. In the query, use ALL to select all defined specsets.

If specset_no is not set, and equation_set_no is set to ALL or a number, only the spec names in the specified equation sets, but no values are returned.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, enter the name of a specification instead of a spec set number. In this case, the secondparameter must be left empty.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

The name of a base (spec) variable. In a multi-port setup, the same variable name can occur among the spec variables of more than one port within the same specification. In this case, you can qualify the variable name by a port name in the following format

<spec_name>@<port_name>,

if you want to modify the variable on that port only.

Note, however, that the scope of the variable will be set to local for the port in question after such a modification (even if it is set to global in the setup), until the setup is downloaded again.

Note also that in a multi-port setup, you cannot change the value of a variable globally (that is, without specifying a port) unless at least one of the variable instances has its scope set to global in the setup. For basic information on the local and global scope of spec variables in a multi-port setup see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）.

 |
 |

spec_or_equ_name

 |

The name of a base (spec) or derived (equation) variable. An equation variable cannot be specified in the command or in a query which uses the extra parameter.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Requires that the actual values of both base and derived variables are returned.

 |
 |

EQUA

 |

Requires that the actual values of only the derived (equation) variables are returned.

 |
 |

MAX

 |

Requires that the maximum values of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the maximum value of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

MIN

 |

Requires that the maximum of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the minimum value of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

SPEC

 |

Requires that the actual values of only the base (spec) variables are returned.

 |
 |

UNIT

 |

Requires that the units of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the unit of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

value

 |

Float with 5 possible decimal places.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

By this extra parameter, you can modify the runtime definitions for an individual pin. Note that you cannot retrieve the pin specific values with SVLR?.

 Note You can use the pinlist parameter to modify the value of a spec variable of an individual pin, temporarily. If you make a new modification on a different spec variable, only the last modification is kept while the previous spec variable is reset to the setup value defined in the spec file. To make a permanent modification on a spec variable, specify all pins (that is, @) as the pinlist. Otherwise, to change the value of a spec variable of an individual pin permanently, you have to use a specset for each pin and modify the spec variable in that specset. |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

The following example queries the values of the spec variable f in a setup where both single-port and multi-port specifications occur:

```
> SVLR? TIM,ALL,ALL,"f"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",35
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_2",33
< SVLR TIM,1,1,"f",37
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

The next example queries in which equation sets the spec variable f occurs:

```
> SVLR? TIM,ALL,,"f"
< SVLR TIM,1,,"f",
< SVLR TIM,2,,"f",
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

For this example assume that the primary timing is a multi-port specification which contains the two ports p_1 and p_2, and that p_1 and p_2 share the spec variable f in this specification. Assume further that f has been set to scope global for the port p_1. Now query the current value of f for p_1, change it globally, and query it again:

```
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",33
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f",43
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",43
```

Since f is global for p_1, its value has been modified. Now change the value a second time, but this time locally, and then try to change it globally again:

```
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1",53
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f",43
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",53
```

The second global command has no effect because f has only local scope after issuing the local command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TCMT  TCMT  -  Test CoMment Transfer）

|

vect_addr

 |

The logical number of the vector at which the comment is to be inserted or read. The specified number range must not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

text

 |

A string of up to 250 characters. The string must be enclosed with double quotes.

Comments can contain any characters with ASCII codes from 32 to 126, that is, all printable ASCII characters. To put a double quote character (", ASCII 34) into a comment, enter two double quote characters.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The vector range forwards from vect_addr.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TCMT  TCMT  -  Test CoMment Transfer）

```
TCMT 2063,"Start of test 2".
```

This example inserts the comment "Start of test 2" at the logical vector address 2063.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TDEX  Test Data Extension）

Italic text in the syntax descriptions below indicates meta-syntax, as described in `Syntax conventions`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.01.02_Syntax_conventions.md`）.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TDEX  Test Data Extension）

The attributes used in the XML data, grouped by element (elements are in alphabetical order):

 |

apgFile

 |

name: <apgFilePath>, a string, is the path to the compiled `APG program file`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.03_APG_program_file.md`）.

 |
 |

bitInversion

 |

name: <bitInversionName>, a string, is the name of the bit inversion setting used.

See the discussion of :bitInversion: in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details.

 |
 |

bitOrdering

 |

name: <bitOderingName>, a string, is the name of the bit oderingsetting used.

See the discussion of :bitOrdering: in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details.

 |
 |

crc

 |

name: <crcName>, a string, is the name of the cyclic redundancy check setting used.

See the discussion of :crc: in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details.

 |
 |

dbi

 |

name: <dbiName>, a string, is the name of the data bus inversion setting used.

See the discussion of :dbi: in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details.

 |
 |

digital

 |

refInsertionCtrl: <refreshType>, a string, is the type of refresh insertion control on the pin. Supported types include:

- SEQ
- SEQUENCER
- VEC
- VECTOR

For an explanation of the refresh insertion control types, see the discussion of using interrupCtrl in `Pin mapping file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.06.01_Pin_mapping_file_syntax.md`）.

 |
 |

layer

 |

- id: <layerId>, an integer, is the unique ID of the layer being defined.
- type: <layerType>, a string, is the type of operation applied by the layer, crc (cyclic redundancy check) or dbi (data bus inversion).

See `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details.

The order of the layer elements within the errorCorrection element determines the order in which the error correction operations are applied.

 |
 |

options

 |

- expansionSize: <expansionSize>, an integer, is the expansion size setting used for the compilation.

See the description of the -e option in `apgc command syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.02.05.01_apgc_command_syntax.md`） for details.

- limitVariableScope: <limitScope>, a boolean, is the setting of the variable scope limitation:

  - "true": Limited variable scope was active for compilation.
  - "false": Extended variable scope was active for compilation.

See the description of the -evs and -lvs options in `apgc command syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.02.05.01_apgc_command_syntax.md`） for details.

- reconstructionLevel: <reconstructionLevel>, a string, is the reconstruction level with which the label was compiled.

See the description of the -r0, r1, and r2 options in `apgc command syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.02.05.01_apgc_command_syntax.md`） for details.

- reusableMaintenance: <reuse>, a boolean, is the setting whether the label has been compiled as a reusable maintenance operation.

See the description of the -m option in `apgc command syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.02.05.01_apgc_command_syntax.md`） for details.

- wavetableGeneration: <generateWavetable>, a boolean, is the setting whether new waveforms have been generated during the compilation.

See the description of the -w option in `apgc command syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.02.05.01_apgc_command_syntax.md`） for details.

 |
 |

pin

 |

- id: <pinId>, an integer, is the unique ID of the pin being defined or referenced. If this <pin> element is a reference, the value of the id attribute must match one of the pins defined in the <pinMap> element.
- name: <pinName>, a string, is the name of the pin being defined. This attribute is optional.
- xmode: <pinXmode>, a string, is the xmode of the pin being defined. This attribute is optional.

See the description of the xmode pin attribute in `Pin mapping file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.06.01_Pin_mapping_file_syntax.md`） for details.

- system: <value> can be true or false. The default value is false. If system = true, SmarTest will generate corresponding programs for those pins (system generated). No vector data will be generated for those pins by MTP.
- optional: <value> can be true or false. The default value is false. If optional = true, even this pin is not defined in the pin configuration file, SmarTest will skip this pin and run the relative MTL patterns without warning.
 |
 |

scramble

 |

name: <scrambleName>, a string, is the name of the scrambling setting used.

See the discussion of :scramble: in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details.

 |
 |

sequencerProgram

 |

checkSum: <checkSum>, an integer, contains the checksum of the label as calculated by the MTL compiler.

 |
 |

timer

 |

- id: <timerId>, an integer, is the unique ID of the maintenance settings being defined.
- timerMode: <timerMode>, a string, is the name of the pin being defined. This attribute is optional.

See the description of the :timerMode: keyword in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details

- intervalMode: <intervalMode>, a string, is the interval mode defined for this refresh operation setting.

See the description of the :intervalMode: keyword in `Device architecture file syntax`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.05.01_Device_architecture_file_syntax.md`） for details

- refreshCtrl: <refreshCtrl>, a string, reflects the refresh control settings with which the label has been compiled:

  - start: The REFRESH_CTRL(START) command has been used.
  - none: The REFRESH_CTRL(START) command has not been used, but refresh is enabled.

If refresh has been disabled and the REFRESH_CTRL(START) command has not been used, there is no refreshCtrl attribute at all.

The REFRESH_CTRL function is described in `Macros and functions in program files`（raw: `../02.12_Memory_Test_Plus_7.10.2/02.12.03.03.03.01.08_Macros_and_functions_in_program_files.md`）.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TDEX  Test Data Extension）

```
TDEX "::pattern::mtl::hsm","myLabel",#9000003254<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO8859-1" standalone="no" ?>
<testDataExtension
                   xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="TestDataExtension.xsd">

  <pinMap>
    <pin id="0" name="pin0" xmode="2">
      <capabilities>
        <digital refInsertionCtrl="VEC"/>
      </capabilities>
    </pin>
    <pin id="1" name="pin1" xmode="4">
      <capabilities>
        <digital refInsertionCtrl="SEQ"/>
      </capabilities>
    </pin>
    <pin id="2" name="pin2" xmode="6">
      <capabilities>
        <digital refInsertionCtrl="SEQ"/>
      </capabilities>
    </pin>
    <pin id="3" name="pin3" xmode="8">
      <capabilities>
        <digital refInsertionCtrl="VEC"/>
      </capabilities>
    </pin>
    <pin id="4" name="pin4">
      <capabilities>
        <digital refInsertionCtrl="SEQ"/>
      </capabilities>
    </pin>
    <pin id="5" name="pin5" xmode="4">
      <capabilities>
        <digital refInsertionCtrl="SEQ"/>
      </capabilities>
    </pin>
  </pinMap>

  <mtlPattern>
    <sourceFiles>
      <apgFile name="/data/device/mts/pattern_defs/apg_file_name_create.apg"/>
    </sourceFiles>
    <setupConfiguration>
      <scramble name="scramble_1"/>
      <bitInversion name="bitInversion_1"/>
      <bitOrdering name="bitOrdering_1"/>
      <dbi name="dbi_1"/>
      <crc name="crc_1"/>
    </setupConfiguration>
    <deviceMaintenance>
      <refresh>
        <timer id="0" intervalMode="accumulated" refreshCtrl="none" timerMode="dynamic"/>
        <timer id="1" intervalMode="compensated" refreshCtrl="start" timerMode="static"/>
        <timer id="2" intervalMode="accumulated" refreshCtrl="none" timerMode="static"/>
        <timer id="3" intervalMode="unknown" refreshCtrl="start" timerMode="unknown"/>
      </refresh>
    </deviceMaintenance>
    <consistencyCheck>
      <sequencerProgram checkSum="21845"/>
    </consistencyCheck>
    <reconstruction>
      <pins>
        <pin id="0"/>
        <pin id="1"/>
        <pin id="2"/>
      </pins>
    </reconstruction>
    <errorCorrection>
      <layer id="0" type="dbi">
        <bus>
          <pins>
            <pin id="0"/>
            <pin id="1"/>
            <pin id="2"/>
          </pins>
          <flags>
            <pin id="3"/>
          </flags>
        </bus>
        <bus>
          <pins>
            <pin id="10"/>
            <pin id="11"/>
            <pin id="12"/>
          </pins>
          <flags>
            <pin id="13"/>
          </flags>
        </bus>
      </layer>
      <layer id="1" type="other">
        <bus>
          <pins>
            <pin id="100"/>
            <pin id="101"/>
          </pins>
          <flags>
            <pin id="103"/>
          </flags>
        </bus>
        <bus>
          <pins>
            <pin id="110"/>
            <pin id="111"/>
          </pins>
          <flags>
            <pin id="113"/>
          </flags>
        </bus>
      </layer>
    </errorCorrection>
    <compilation>
      <options expansionSize="100"
               limitVariableScope="false"
               reconstructionLevel="2"
               reusableMaintenance="true"
               wavetableGeneration="false"/>
    </compilation>
  </mtlPattern>

</testDataExtension>
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TEMP  -  read TEMPerature）

```
TEMP? [cardType]
```

returns:

```
TEMP {cardType}, {cardId}, {temperature}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TEMP  -  read TEMPerature）

| cardType  | Specifies the card type for which temperature is read |
 | DIGIO  | Digital IO card (including DC Scale cards) |
 | ANAIO  | Analog IO card |
 | CLK  | Clock Board |
 | cardId  | Returns

- the card number (or pogo block number) of the logical channel board (three digits)
- or the Clock Board number (11, 12, 21, 22, ..., 41, 42),
- or an identification number of the DPS card (101 to 108).
 |
 | temperature |

Returns the temperature (in Kelvin) for each card.

Default value in offline mode is 292.3 K.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TEMP  -  read TEMPerature）

```
TEMP? DIGIO
TEMP DIGIO,101,292.3
TEMP DIGIO,102,292.3
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

|

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the definitions to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）) and the level sets used (as defined by `LSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.155_LSUS__LSUS__-__Level_Sets_USed.md`）). Entering ALL in this field sets the termination mode for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Entering PRM in this field defines the termination mode for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number > 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for digital pins in high-Z state. For more information see `Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF`（raw: `02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md`）.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no`

 |
 |

term_mode

 |

The termination mode has dependencies to pin types and to the parameters (term_pulldown and param_1 to param_3 - see the syntax). The allowed combinations are shown in the Termination modes table, below.

Level set 0 only supports the termination modes OFF (the default), T, C, and A.

 |
 |

term_pulldown

 |

Extra parameter that defines the pull down mode. For more information refer to column term_mode of table Termination modes below.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

param_1

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_1 gives the termination voltage, active load commutation voltage, or the clamp low level voltage. The units are mV.

 |
 |

param_2

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_2 defines the active load Iol current, or the clamp high level voltage. The units are mA or mV respectively.

When used, param_2 defines either

- the active load Iol current in 碌A,
- the clamp high level voltage in mV, or
- the receiver swing voltage in mV.

For the NP termination modes SP, SM, SEP, or SEM, param_2 defines the receiver threshold in mV.

 |
 |

param_3

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below:

- For term_mode = A, param_3 defines the active load Ioh current. The units are 碌A.
- For term_mode = CT, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.
- For term_mode = bidir_receiver, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.
 |
 |

l_range

 |

For term_mode `=`A the low level current range.

This parameter can be

- I5E3: Defines the low current range of 0 to 5 mA.
- I3E4: Defines the high current range of 0 to 30 mA.
- AUTO: Lets the firmware automatically select the correct range. Whenever possible, the system selects the lower range.

This parameter is not supported for AVI64.

 |
 |

h_range

 |

For term_mode `=`A the high level current range.

This parameter can be

- I5E3: Defines the low current range of 0 to 5 mA.
- I3E4: Defines the high current range of 0 to 30 mA.
- AUTO: Lets the firmware automatically select the correct range. Whenever possible, the system selects the lower range.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names of those power supply outputs which have already been defined. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured power supply pins.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 1,T,-1500,,,,,(Q1)
```

This example terminates the output pin Q1 to -1500 mV in level set 1.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 3,A,3000,1500,1000,I3E4,I3E4,(out)
```

This example sets the active load level of the pin group out to 3V, and sets Iol and Ioh current to 1.5 and 1.0 mA respectively. The 0 to 30 mA range is used for both the low and the high range.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 1,CT,2000,,,,,(o1,o1-)
```

This example terminates the differential output pair (the o1 and o1- pins) to 2000 mV with center tap termination in level set 1.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 1,OFF,PULLDOWN,,,,,,(Q1,Q2)
```

On a PS1600 card, this example switches on the pulldown resistor on the specified pins.

```
TERM 1,OFF,NONE,,,,,,(Q1,Q2)
```

On a PS1600 card, this example switches off the pulldown resistor on the specified pins.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TMUD  Tester Memory Utilization set Default values）

```
TMUD {client}, [logState],{(portlist)}
```

Parameter
 |

Parameter

 |

Description

 |
 |

client

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

PROTOCOLTEST

 |

Logging of memory usage will be switched on or off for protocol tests.

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

Logging of memory usage will be switched on or off for all supported clients.

 |
 |

logState

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

ON

 |

Starts logging of memory usage. The values recorded in the previous logging session will be reset to 0.

The values of the current logging session can be retrieved with the TMUL? query.

 |
 |

 |

OFF

 |

Stops logging of memory usage including the DEBUG_WATERMARK and DEBUG_SEQUENCES options.

The values that were determined are kept until logging is started again with option ON.

 Note When logging is stopped, all protocol patterns for the specified ports will be deleted. |
 |

 |

DEBUG_WATERMARK

 |

This option causes TMUD to write all changes of the maximum used memory to the report window (in bytes). If necessary, it also activates logging of memory usage (the ON state).

 |
 |

 |

DEBUG_SEQUENCES

 |

This option causes TMUD to write the cache management type (standard or volatile) of any new transaction sequence to the report window. If necessary, it also activates logging of memory usage (the ON state).

 |
 |

 |

DEBUG_ALL

 |

This option combines DEBUG_WATERMARK and DEBUG_SEQUENCES. If necessary, it also activates logging of memory usage (the ON state). Both these activities are also stopped by setting logState to OFF.

 |
 |

 |

If the parameter is omitted, the current counter values will be reset to 0, but the log state will not be changed.

 |
 |

portList

 |

Is a comma separated list of ports.

To apply the command to all ports, use @@.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TMUD  Tester Memory Utilization set Default values）

```
> TMUD PROTOCOLTEST,ON,(mdioPort)

> TMUL? ALL,ALL,(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"0,0,0",(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,SIZE,"0,0,AUTO",(mdioPort)
```

In this example the TMUD resets the memory utilization logs of the mdioPort of the PROTOCOLTEST client. It also sets logging to ON in case it was disabled previously.

The TMUL? query is used to display that TMUD has reset all memory utilization counters to default values.

```
> TMUD ALL,ON,(@@)

> TMUL? ALL,ALL,(@@)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"0,0,0",(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"0,0,0",(otherPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,SIZE,"0,0,65536",(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,SIZE,"0,0,AUTO",(otherPort)
```

In this example the TMUD resets the memory utilization logs of all ports (@@) of all clients. It also sets logging to ON in case it was disabled previously for all ports and clients.

The TMUL? query is used to display that TMUD has reset all memory utilization counters to default values.

Note If the memory size was specified by `PROTOCOL_TEST::reserveTransactionMemory()` the according limit will be displayed, else AUTO is shown.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TMUL   Tester Memory Utilization Log）

TMUL? {client}, {type},{(portlist)}

returns

TMUL {client}, {type}, {"reportString"}, {(portlist)}

Parameter
 |

Name

 |

Description

 |
 |

client

 |

Use either of:

PROTOCOLTEST - to query protocol test clients only

ALL - to query all supported clients

 |
 |

type

 |

Use either of:

CACHE - to query cache related information only

SIZE - to query size related information only

ALL - to query all supported types

 |
 |

portList

 |

Is a comma separated list of ports.

To query all ports, use @@

 |
 |

reportString

 |

Contains the information queried in string format.

The output will differ depending on the type queried:

- Output for type CACHE: {number of hits}, {number of misses}, {number of removed entries}

  - number of hits: Number of times an entry had been found in the cache.
  - number of misses: Number of times a new entry had been added to cache because the entry was not found in cache already.
  - number of removed entries: Number of entries removed from cache because an entry should be added, but no sufficient space was available

- Output for type SIZE in bytes: {min memory mark}, {high memory mark}, {limit}

  - min memory mark: The minimum memory size (in bytes) required to store generated data.
  - high memory mark: The maximum memory size (in bytes) that has been utilized during testing.
  - limit: Specified size limit (in bytes).

If no limit is specified, the system will either return "AUTO", if no limit had been specified at all, or the limit specified by `PROTOCOL_TEST::reserveTransactionMemory()`.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TMUL   Tester Memory Utilization Log）

The following example queries the `mdioPort` for details about the CACHE of the PROTOCOLTEST client. The returned string shows that entries have been found 1560 times in the cache (number of hits). It also shows that 28 entries had been added (number of misses) to the cache and no entry has been removed.

```
> TMUL? PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"1560,28,0",(mdioPort)
```

The next example queries the `mdioPort` for ALL details of ALL clients. The returned strings shows the results for CACHE  and SIZE. With regards to SIZE, one can see that the minimum memory size required to store the generated data is 7488 bytes. It also shows that the maximum memory size utilized during testing was 10314 bytes and that there is no limit set, thus AUTO is displayed.

```
> TMUL? ALL,ALL,(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"1560,28,0",(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,SIZE,"7488,10314,AUTO",(mdioPort)
```

This example queries all ports (@@)`` for ALL details of ALL client.

```
> TMUL? ALL,ALL,(@@)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"1560,28,0",(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,CACHE,"0,0,0",(otherPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,SIZE,"7488,10314,AUTO",(mdioPort)
< TMUL PROTOCOLTEST,SIZE,"0,0,AUTO",(otherPort)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TOCF  TOCF  -  Timing Level Offset search ConFiguration）

|

search_type

 |

This parameter defines which value of the search result is to be stored as an offset to the edge positions of the current primary timing. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

EYE

 |

The middle of the pass area is stored as the offset. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

LB

 |

The left boundary of the pass area is stored as the offset.

 |
 |

 |

RB

 |

The right boundary of the pass area is stored as the offset.

 |
 |

resource_type

 |

This parameter selects the timing or level resource. Possible values are:

 |
 |

Timing resources

 |

R

 |

Receive edges are moved.

 |
 |

F

 |

Fast drive edges are moved.

 |
 |

S

 |

Slow drive edges are moved.

 |
 |

D

 |

Both kinds of drive edges are moved.

 |
 |

Level resources

 |

VIH

 |

High driver levels are moved

 |
 |

VIL

 |

Low driver levels are moved

 |
 |

VISWING

 |

Driver swings are moved.

 |
 |

VOH

 |

High receiver levels are moved.

 |
 |

VOL

 |

Low receiver levels are moved.

 |
 |

VIOFFSET

 |

Driver offsets. Both the driver high and low levels will be moved by the same values.

 |
 |

VOOFFSET

 |

Receiver offsets. Both the receiver high and low levels will be moved by the same values.

 |
 |

VTH

 |

Receiver thresholds are moved.

 |
 |

VOSWING

 |

Receiver swings are moved.

 |
 |

start

 |

This parameter defines the start of the search range relative to the edge or level positions as defined in the current primary timing or level. Negative values are allowed.

Units for timing and level searches are ns and mV.

 |
 |

number_of_steps

 |

This parameter defines the number of steps for the linear search.

 |
 |

step_width

 |

This parameter defines the step width for the linear search. The search range is number_of_steps * step_width.

step_width can be negative. Therefore, a negative search is possible.

Units for timing and level searches are ns and mV.

 |
 |

resolution

 |

This parameter defines the resolution of the binary search. The binary search is stopped when the distance between the last two binary search steps is 鈮?resolution.

Units for timing and level searches are ns and mV.

 |
 |

min_pass_count

 |

The PASS area determined by the binary search may still contain isolated FAIL results at its start or end. This parameter activates an additional check that is intended to exclude this. It specifies how many consecutive PASS results must be present at the start (before the end) of the putative PASS region. If this requirement is not satisfied, the left boundary of the area is moved to the right (the right boundary moved to the left) until the required number of consecutive PASS results is found.

The default for min_pass_count is 1.

 |
 |

min_stable_error_count

 |

This and the histogram_step_width parameter define a histogram based search, which is performed after the binary search. It moves the left boundary of the PASS area to the left (the right boundary to the right) until the number of errors is the same for the number of search steps specified with min_stable_error_count.

 |
 |

histogram_step_width

 |

This parameter defines the step width of the histogram search.

 |
 |

transition_detection

 |

This parameter controls the criterion for a test to be considered as PASSED. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

PF

 |

The test is considered to have passed only if no errors occurred at all. This is the default

 |
 |

 |

ECL

 |

The test is considered to have passed if the number of errors is smaller than error_count_limit.

 |
 |

 |

PF_FASTSTOP

 |

Like PF but, using the FASTSTOP mode, stops the linear search after the first PASS area is detected (see `Linear search modes`（raw: `02.06.09.01.02.01_Linear_search_modes.md`）).

 |
 |

 |

ECL_FASTSTOP

 |

Like ECL but, using the FASTSTOP mode, stops the linear search after the first PASS area is detected (see `Linear search modes`（raw: `02.06.09.01.02.01_Linear_search_modes.md`）).

 |
 |

error_count_limit

 |

This parameter defines the minimum number of errors that are not tolerated if transition_detection is set to ECL.

 |
 |

restore_flag

 |

The restore_flag parameter enables or disables the restore process after a search was executed: It allows you to suppress storing of the search result.

 |
 |

 |

YES

 |

Restores the timing / level offsets to the values it had before the offset search was executed.

 |
 |

 |

NO

 |

The new measured offset values are used in the edge position calculation.

This is the default configuration.

 |
 |

setup_pinlist

 |

This parameter defines the pins the edge positions of which are to be changed. If an input pin is specified, the O or IO pins on which the outcome of a search step is to depend must be defined with TOCR.

Note also that the edge type specified with the edge_type parameter must be in line with the pin type.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TOCF  TOCF  -  Timing Level Offset search ConFiguration）

```
TOCF EYE,R,1,100,1,0.1,5,PF,,NO,(Pin1)
```

This example appends a check for 5 consecutive pass results to the result of the binary search.

```
TOCF EYE,R,1,100,1,0.1,1,10,0.1,ECL,7,NO,(Pin1)
```

This example appends a histogram based search to the binary search. The histogram based search is terminated if the error count is stable for 10 consecutive search steps. A test is considered passed if the number of errors is smaller than 7.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TOCR  TOCR  -  Timing level Offset Configure Result pins）

|

result_pinlist

 |

In the command, this parameter specifies the result pins for the setup pin specified with setup_pin. It can be omitted for O or IO setup pins. In this case the result pin will be identical with the setup pin.

In the query, it lists the result pins for which the associated setup pins are to be retrieved.

 |
 |

setup_pin

 |

The setup pin for which the result pins are to be defined.

 |
 |

setup_pinlist

 |

This query parameter lists the setup pins, for which the associated result pins are to be retrieved.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TOCR  TOCR  -  Timing level Offset Configure Result pins）

```
TOCR (Pin2,Pin3),(Pin1)
```

This example defines `Pin2` and `Pin3` as the result pins for `Pin1`.

```
> TOCR? ,(Pin1,Pin5)
< TOCR (Pin2,Pin3),(Pin1)
```

This example queries the result pins for Pin1 and Pin5. No reply is given for setup pin Pin5, because its result pin is also Pin5.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORC -  Timing level Offset Result Copy）

|

source_waveform_set

 |

Number of the source waveform set. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query, you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

source_specset_id

 |

The source specification ID (single port). It is derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

source_multi-port_spec

 |

Name of the source multi-port specification.

Note that the multi-port specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multi-port specification.

 |
 |

source_level_set_id

 |

The source level set ID. It can be:

- A fixed level set ID, which is an integer in the range of 1 to the maximum number of level sets allowed, which is defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command.
- An equation based level set ID, which derived as follows:

eqnset * 100000 + specset * 1000 + level_set_no

 |
 |

source_timing_set

 |

The source timing set.

 |
 |

dest_waveform_set

 |

Number of the destination waveform set. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query, you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

dest_specset_id

 |

The destination specification ID (single port). It is derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

dest_multi-port_spec

 |

Name of the destination multi-port specification.

Note that the multi-port specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multi-port specification.

 |
 |

dest_timing_set

 |

The destination timing set.

 |
 |

dest_level_set_id

 |

The destination level set ID. It can be:

- A fixed level set ID, which is an integer in the range of 1 to the maximum number of level sets allowed, which is defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command.
- An equation based level set ID, which derived as follows:

eqnset * 100000 + specset * 1000 + level_set_no

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This refers to the primary waveform set/specification or to the primary timing set or to the primary level set, all as defined with `SPRM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.228_SPRM__SPRM__-__Set_PRiMary_sets.md`）.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

The specified source offsets are copied to all specifications or timing sets or level sets.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins on which the copy action is to be executed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORC -  Timing level Offset Result Copy）

Example 1: copies the offsets of timing set 2 of single port specification 102 to the primary timing set of the primary specification.

```
TORC 102,2,PRM,PRM,(Pin1,Pin2)
```

Example 2: copies all level_set offsets of level set 1 to all the other level sets for all pins (@).

```
> TORC 1,,ALL,,(@)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORN  -  Timing level Offset search RuN）

```
TORN? {(pinlist)} [,"exec_context"]
```

Returns:

```
TORN {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORN  -  Timing level Offset search RuN）

|

pinlist

 |

The pins for which the embedded search is to be executed. You can specify @ for all pins.

Note the difference between a list of pins and @ in a multi-site setup. In the former case, all channels that are associated with these pins must have the embedded timing/level search capability and must have been configured with TOCF. If this is not the case, TORN? will return the status FAILED. But if @ is specified, channels that do not fulfill both these conditions will simply be ignored.

 |
 |

exec_context

 |

An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） .

 |
 |

status

 |

TORN? returns one of the following three status codes:

 |
 |

 |

SUCCEEDED

 |

The search was successfully finished for all active sites.

 |
 |

 |

FAILED

 |

The search failed for at least one channel.

 |
 |

 |

ABORTED

 |

The search was canceled by the user.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORN  -  Timing level Offset search RuN）

```
> TORN? (Pin1,Pin2)
< TORN SUCCEEDED
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORR  Timing level Offset Reset Result）

|

waveform_set

 |

Number of a waveform set. Enter PRM for the primary waveform set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

The source specification ID (single port). It is derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

Name of a multiport specification.

Note that the multi-port specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multi-port specification.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

A level set ID. It can be:

- A fixed level set ID, which is an integer in the range of 1 to the maximum number of level sets which is defined with the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command.
- An equation based level set ID, which is derived as follows:

eqnset * 100000 + specset * 1000 + level_set_no

 |
 |

timing_set

A timing set number.

 |
 |

 |

 |

ALL

pinlist

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORR  Timing level Offset Reset Result）

|

waveform_set

 |

specset_id

 |

- VIH: High driver levels
- VIL: Low driver levels
- VISWING: Driver swings
- VOH: High receiver levels
- VOL: Low receiver levels
- VTH: Receiver thresholds
- VIOFFSET: Driver offsets (Both the driver high and low levels will be moved by the same values.)
- VOOFFSET: Receiver offsets (Both the receiver high and low levels will be moved by the same values.)
- VOSWING: Receiver swings
 |
 |

offset

 |

The offset for the respective type (edge type or level type) and pin. The offset is 0 if no search was executed or no value stored.

The units for voltage resources are [mV].

The units for timing resources are [ns].

 |
 |

pin

 |

A reply parameter. The pin for which the offsets are returned

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

A query parameter. The pins for which the offsets are to be retrieved.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORS  -  Timing level Offset ReSult）

```
> TORS? PRM,PRM,R,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,R,0,(p1)

> TORS? PRM,PRM,S,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,S,0,(p1)

> TORS? PRM,PRM,F,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,F,0,(p1)

> TORS? PRM,PRM,D,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,F,0,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,S,0,(p1)

> TORS? PRM,PRM,ALL,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,R,0,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,F,0,(p1)
< TORS 1,1,S,0,(p1)

> TORS? PRM,,VIL,(@)
<TORS 1,,VIL,750,(p1)
<TORS 1,,VIL,750,(p2)

> TORS? PRM,,VISWING,(@)
< TORS 1,,VIH,-450,(p1,p2)
< TORS 1,,VIL,450,(p1,p2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORT  -  Timing Level Offset search Result Transitions）

```
TORT? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TORT {left_boundary|NOT_FOUND}, {right_boundary|NOT_FOUND}, {(pinlist)}
```

Note The returned transition value is the latest passing value near to the transition.

Parameters
 |

left_boundary

 |

The offet of the left boundary or lower level of the pass area found by the last timing or level search, where the fail-pass transition was found.

Units for timing searches are [ns].

Units for voltage searches are [mV].

 |
 |

right_boundary

 |

The offset of the right boundary or upper level of the pass area found by the last timing or level search, where the pass-fail transition was found.

Units for timing searches are [ns].

Units for voltage searches are [mV].

 |
 |

NOT_FOUND

 |

This is returned if no search was executed, the search results were reset, or the search was aborted.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins for which the offsets are to be returned.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TORT  -  Timing Level Offset search Result Transitions）

```
TORT? (@)
TORT NOT_FOUND,NOT_FOUND, (p1,p2)
```
