```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TPSE  TPSE  -  Test Point SEquence）

|

testdata_name

 |

Specifies the test data collection from which the test events are to be selected. The collection must have been defined with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.

 |
 |

labelType

 |

The following types are supported:

 |
 |

 |

MAIN

 |

requires a label name defined with `SQLB`（raw: `02.06.02.02.236_SQLB__SQLB__-__SeQuencer_LaBel_definition.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

SVEC

 |

requires a label name defined with SQLB.

 |
 |

 |

PPSQ

 |

Per pin subroutine defined with `DPPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.81_DPPS__DPPS__-__Define_Per_Pin_Subroutine_label.md`）. This type is only used for memory tests. You should not define a test point sequence for a per pin subroutine manually. Note also that the anchor of a per pin subroutine is an address, not a vector number.

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

reports the test points of all label types (query only).

 |
 |

label_name

 |

The name of the pattern to which the test point sequence belongs.

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

returns the test points of all labels (query only)

 |
 |

edit_mode

 |

Possible modes are:

- REPLACE: All existing test point definitions are replaced with the new definitions.
- UPDATE: Existing test points can be modified, that is, you can associate a different test event with the given vector position. You cannot add new test points or remove existing ones.
- INSERT: Additional test points can be defined. The existing setups are unchanged. Existing test points cannot be replaced.
- DELETE: All specified test points are removed. If a group does no longer contain a test point, it will be removed as well.

The TPSE? query always responds with REPLACE mode.

 |
 |

anchor_number

 |

Selects a single test point for the query. In the command, the anchor numbers are specified within the XML code (anchor attribute of the tp element).

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Only pins with test point capability (DC Scale DPS32 and VI32 pins) are considered.

 |
 |

#spec(test_points)

 |

The binary data stream that contains the test points. The general format is:

`#`Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The general format of the XML string is explained above. The two attributes of the tp element must take the following values:

 |
 |

 |

anchor

 |

The value of this attribute must be a logical vector number of the specified pattern. This is the vector at which the test point becomes active. At least 32 vectors must be generated before the first anchor and between any two anchors. These vectors are needed to download data to the hardware.

 |
 |

 |

td

 |

The value of this attribute must be the identifier of a td element in the test data block specified with the testdata_name parameter.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TPSE  TPSE  -  Test Point SEquence）

This example sets up a test label that generates a ramp of 4 samples on pin `vdd` in the default port.

```
DFTD "ramp_events",REPLACE,(vdd),#3628<?xml version="1.0"?>
<testdata>
  <td id="init" type="dcset">
    <setMeasureRange type="voltage" minValue="0" maxValue="3.0"/>
  </td>
  <td id="1" type="dcset">
    <setForceValue type="voltage" value="0.0"/>
  </td>
  <td id="2" type="dcset">
    <setForceValue type="voltage" value="0.5"/>
  </td>
  <td id="3" type="dcset">
    <setForceValue type="voltage" value="1.0"/>
    <measure    type="current" samples="4"/>
  </td>
  <td id="4" type="dcset">
    <setForceValue type="voltage" value="1.5"/>
  </td>
</testdata>

SQLB "ramp4",SVEC,0,3,"wavetable",(@)
. . .
SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
SQPG 2,GENV,512,,,(@)
SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)

TPSE "ramp_events",SVEC,"ramp4",REPLACE,(vdd),#3226<?xml version="1.0"?>
<sequence>
  <tp anchor="64" td="init"/>
    <tp anchor="120" td="1"/>
    <tp anchor="200" td="2"/>
    <tp anchor="300" td="3"/>
    <tp anchor="400" td="4"/>
</sequence>
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TPSP  TPSP  -  TestPoint SuPpression）

|

suppression_type

 |

Defines which types of test point operations are suppressed. Possible values are:

 |
 | OFF  | No operations are suppressed. This is the default. |
 | I  | Operations that change the DUT input signal are suppressed. |
 | O  | Operations that record DUT output signals are suppressed. |
 | IO  | Both operation types are suppressed. |
 |

pin_list

 |

The pin or pins to which this command is applied. To specify multiple pins, separate the names with a comma, or use @ to specify all pins. Pin groups can also be specified. Only pins that are associated with DCScale channels are taken into account.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TPSP  TPSP  -  TestPoint SuPpression）

```
TPSP I,(dps1)
FTST?
TPSP OFF,(dps1)
```

In this example, input operations for `dps1` are suppressed for the following functional test. After completion of the test, the suppression is canceled.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSCF  TSCF  -  TMU Set ConFiguration）

|

ts_name

 |

Specifies the name of a TMU set that must have been defined with TSDF.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the TMU test. For a list see the table below. If this parameter is omitted in the query, all defined properties will be returned.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all TMU sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified to modify or retrieve the configuration of the current primary TMU set.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified property. The values that are admitted for the individual properties are listed in the table below.

 |
 |

RESET

 |

If you specify this keyword instead of a property value, the property will be deleted in the specified TMU set.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which this configuration is to be applied.

 |

Properties and their values
 |

Property

 |

Explanation and values

 |
 |

DATA_RATE

 |

This property defines the data rate which is the smallest distance between two events. The unit is bits per second.

 |
 |

EDGE_SELECT

 |

This mandatory property defines which edges are the events to be sampled. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

RISE

 |

The events are rising edges.

 |
 |

 |

FALL

 |

The events are falling edges.

 |
 |

 |

RISE_FALL

 |

The events are alternately rising and falling edges. This option is used for pulse and jitter measurements. If this option is selected, the PRESCALER property must be set to a value > 1 and < 17.

 |
 |

INITIAL_DISCARD

 |

This optional property defines how many events are to be discarded before the first sample of a measurement set. This refers to the events as they occur in the output signal of the prescaler. The default is 0.

If EDGE_SELECT is set to RISE_FALL, and INITIAL_DISCARD is set to an even number, the first sampled event will be a rising edge if INITIAL_DISCARD is set to an odd number, the first sampled event will be a falling edge.

Note: Parameter INITIAL_DISCARD must be 0 for DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD

 |

This optional property defines how many events are to be discarded between two samples of a measurement set. This refers to the events as they occur in the output signal of the prescaler. The default is 0.

If EDGE_SELECT is set to RISE_FALL, this property must be set to an even number (including 0). If it is set to an odd number, all sampled edges will be of the same type, all rising or all falling.

Note: Parameter INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD must be 0 for DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

MEAS_PER_SHOT

 |

This mandatory property must equal the number of armings in the pattern. A shot is one execution of the pattern. For certain measurements, two executions are required; see the NUM_SHOTS parameter.

This is one of the three parameters by which the required size of the result area is determined. The others are SAMPLES_PER_MEAS and NUM_SHOTS.

 |
 |

NUM_SHOTS

 |

This optional property defines the number of shots (sequencer runs). It is used to calculate the size of the result area and to determine how the measurements are to be processed. The possible values are 1 or 2. Two shots are needed for rise time and fall time measurements. The default is 1.

 |
 |

PRESCALER

 |

This mandatory property defines how much the frequency of the signal is to be reduced before it is passed on to the event discarding block. This is required if the minimal distance of two consecutive events in the DUT signal can be smaller than the minimal distance that the event discarding block supports.

Possible values for Smart Scale pins are 1 through 17. 1 means no prescaling. If EDGE_SELECT is set to RISE_FALL, the prescaler value must be < 17 and > 1.

 |
 |

SAMPLES_PER_MEAS

 |

This mandatory property defines the number of samples per measurement (arming). This is another parameter that contributes to the calculation of the result area size.

 |
 |

THRESHOLD_A

 |

This optional property defines a voltage threshold for the event to be sampled. It is only needed for (two shot) rise time and fall time measurements. The default is the voltage level as defined in the level setup.

Note that if this property is defined, the level setup must be changed, and if the pins specified by pinlist are tested functionally in parallel with the TMU measurement, they will be tested with the modified voltage level.

Note also that the original level setup is automatically restored after the measurement has been finished.

 |
 |

THRESHOLD_B

 |

This optional property defines the voltage threshold for a second shot. It is only needed for (two shot) rise time and fall time measurements.

It must not be defined if NUM_SHOTS is set to 1.

Note that the original level setup is automatically restored after the measurement has been finished.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSCF  TSCF  -  TMU Set ConFiguration）

```
> TSCF? "TMU_set1",,(Pin1)

< TSCF "TMU_set1",PRESCALER,3,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",INITIAL_DISCARD,0,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD,500,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",SAMPLES_PER_MEAS,2,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",NUM_SHOTS,1,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",MEAS_PER_SHOT,5,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",EDGE_SELECT,RISE,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",DATA_RATE,50000000,(Pin1)
```

This example queries a period measurement definition. Typically, only two samples are taken for such a measurement, and these at a great distance (see the INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD property in the example). The period resulting from this measurement can be retrieved with the `TSRS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.278_TSRS__-__TMU_Set_ReSults.md`） query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSDF  TSDF  -  TMU Set DeFinition）

|

TMU_set_name

 |

In the command, this is the name of a new TMU set. In the query, it is a name of an existing TMU set. If you omit this parameter in the query, TSDF? will return the names of all user defined TMU sets.

 |
 |

mode_context

 |

The mode context with which the TMU set is associated. If this parameter is omitted, the DEFAULT context is assumed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSDF  TSDF  -  TMU Set DeFinition）

```
> TSDF   "TMU_set1"
> TSDF   "TMU_set2"
> TSDF   "TMU_set3"

> TSDF?
< TSDF   "TMU_set1"
< TSDF   "TMU_set2"
< TSDF   "TMU_set3"

```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSER  -  TMU Set ERror）

```
TSER? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSER {VDL_OVERRUN|ARM_OVERRUN|OUT_OF_MEMORY|GLITCH_OVERRUN|NOT_FINISHED}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSER  -  TMU Set ERror）

|

VDL_OVERRUN

 |

The sample rate of the TMU is exceeded.

 |
 |

ARM_OVERRUN

 |

The TMU is re-armed before all the requested samples have been taken in the preceding measurement execution.

 |
 |

OUT_OF_MEMORY

 |

The embedded processor has run out of memory.

 |
 |

GLITCH_OVERRUN

 |

An event that should appear in the prescaler output occurs before the positive pulse representing the previous such event is terminated. See `Dealing with very high frequencies`（raw: `02.06.13.01.05_Dealing_with_very_high_data_rates.md`）.

 |
 |

NOT_FINISHED

 |

The measurement has not been finished.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins for which the state of the TMU measurement is to be returned.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSER  -  TMU Set ERror）

```
> TSER? (Pin1)
< TSER ARM_OVERRUN,(Pin1)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSHA  -  Timing Setup Has Arming）

|

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port timing specification, specify the name of the specification.

 |
 |

TRUE

 |

The wavetable of at least one of the pins in the pin list contains the ARM action.

 |
 |

FALSE

 |

No wavetable of any pin in the pin list contains the ARM action.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins whose associated wavetable is to be checked.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSHA  -  Timing Setup Has Arming）

```
> TSHA? "MP_1",(pin1)
< TSHA "MP_1",FALSE,(pin1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRH  -  TMU Set Result Handle）

```
TSRH? {REQUEST|SELECT|RELEASE}, {"handle_name"}
```

returns:

TSRH {REQUEST|SELECT|RELEASE}, {"handle_name"}, {SUCCEED|FAILED}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRH  -  TMU Set Result Handle）

|

REQUEST

 |

Defines a handle. If the request is successful, the new handle will be the active handle.

 |
 |

SELECT

 |

Selects an existing handle as the active handle.

 |
 |

RELEASE

 |

Releases (deletes) an existing handle.

 |
 |

handle_name

 |

The name of the handle to be requested, selected, or released.

 |
 |

SUCCEED

 |

The requested action was successful.

 |
 |

FAILED

 |

The requested action failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRH  -  TMU Set Result Handle）

```
> TSRH? REQUEST, "area1"
< TSRH REQUEST,"area1",SUCCEED
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRC  -  Time Stamping Results Computed）

```
TSRC? [(sitesToBeDone),] [measurement_id], {result_type}, [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(execution_control),] [(site_selector),] [(resultAreaName),] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSRC [shotcount],{result_type}, {successinfo}, {(pin)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRC  -  Time Stamping Results Computed）

| sitesToBeDone |

An extra string parameter, defining the sites to be uploaded. i.e. "01110011".

This option needs parameter `site_selector`（raw: `02.06.02.02.277_TSRC__-__Time_Stamping_Results_Computed.md#_141847__r_site_selector`） to be set to ALL.

 |
 | measurement_id |

The optional number of the measurement block (identified by the ARM keyword within a waveform that is executed in the pattern) for which the computation is performed. If no measurement block is specified, all measurement blocks will be computed.

 |
 | result_type |

The mandatory result type. Currently, the only supported result type is PERIOD.

 |
 | first_sample |

NOT USED

 |
 | no_of_samples |

NOT USED

 |
 | execution_control |

With this extra parameter, you can modify the default action sequence of TSRC?. Possible values are:

 | NOT_FINISHED |

Default. All three steps described above will be executed. If not all required samples have been actually taken, the query will not stop, it issues warning and continues to analyze and compute the available samples.

 |
 | FINISHED |

Completeness check will be skipped. TSRC? assumes that all required samples have been taken. It will analyze and compute the available samples. It starts from step 2, above.

 |
 | ANALYZED |

Samples will not be analyzed. TSRC? assumes that all required samples were taken and analyzed in a previous step. It computes the available samples. It starts from step 3, above.

   | |
 | site_selector |

This extra query parameter allows you to compute the results for a specific site or all sites. Possible values are:

 | ONE |

Only the values of the site which has the query focus are processed (the default).

 |
 | ALL |

The values of all sites or the sites defined by parameter `sitesToBeDone`（raw: `02.06.02.02.277_TSRC__-__Time_Stamping_Results_Computed.md#_141847__r_sitesToBeDone`） are processed.

 |
 | <N> |

The results of the site with this number are processed.

   | |
 | resultAreaName |

The extra parameter defines the name of the result area from which the samples should be computed. If this parameter is omitted, the default result area is used.

 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory list of pins for which the time stamps are to be computed.

 |
 | pin |

The pin to which the computed results belong.

 |
 | shotcount |

The parameter returns the number of shots that have been computed.

 |
 | successinfo |

The parameter indicates whether the computation succeeded.

Possible return values:

-

SUCCEEDED

-

FAILED.

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRS  -  TMU Set ReSults）

```
TSRS? [(sitesToBeDone),] [measurement_id], {result_type}, [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(execution_control),] [(site_selector),] [(resultAreaName),] [(mode),] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSRS [measurement_id], [(sitenumber),] {result_type}, [sample_id|aggregation_type|first_sample], {result|no_of_samples}, {(pin)} [,#spec(binary_results)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRS  -  TMU Set ReSults）

| sitesToBeDone |

An extra string parameter, defining the sites to be uploaded. i.e. "01110011".

This option needs parameter `site_selector`（raw: `02.06.02.02.278_TSRS__-__TMU_Set_ReSults.md#_125500__r_site_selector`） to be set to ALL.

 |
 | measurement_id |

The optional number of the measurement block (identified by the ARM keyword within a waveform that is executed in the pattern) for which periods or statistics to be returned. If no measurement block is specified, the periods or statistics of all measurement blocks are returned.

 |
 | result_type |

The mandatory result type. Currently, the only supported result type is PERIOD.

 |
 | first_sample |

The optional parameter specifies the first sample in the query (TSRS?) for which the period is to be returned. In the return (TSRS) of the query it specifies the first sample that is returned if the mode is set to ON. Samples are counted from 0.

 |
 | no_of_samples |

The optional parameter defines in the query (TSRS?) the number of samples for which the periods are to be returned. In the return (TSRS) of the query it specifies the number of samples that are returned if the mode is set to ON.

Depending on the value of parameter first_sample, fewer samples than specified may be returned. For example, if there are 9 samples in total, first_sample is 7 and no_of_samples is 4, only two samples are returned (the last two), not four.

 |
 | execution_control |

With this extra parameter, you can modify the default action sequence of TSRS?. Possible values are:

 | NOT_FINISHED |

All four steps described above will be executed. If not all required samples have been actually taken, the query will not stop, it will continue to analyze,compute and upload the available samples.

This is the default value.

 |
 | FINISHED  | Completeness check will be skipped. TSRS? assumes that all required samples have been taken. It will analyze, compute, and upload the available samples. It starts from step 2. |
 | ANALYZED  | Samples will not be analyzed. TSRS? assumes that all required samples were taken and analyzed in a previous step. It computes the available samples. It starts from step 3. |
 | COMPUTED  | Samples will not be computed. TSRS? assumes that all required samples were taken, analyzed, and computed in a previous step. It retrieves the periods and their statistics to the system controller. It starts from step 4.  | |
 | site_selector |

This extra query parameter allows you to request the results for all sites or a specific site. Possible values:

 | ONE |

Only the values of the site which has the query focus are processed (the default).

 |
 | ALL |

The values of all sites or the sites defined by parameter `sitesToBeDone`（raw: `02.06.02.02.278_TSRS__-__TMU_Set_ReSults.md#_125500__r_sitesToBeDone`） are processed.

 |
 | <N> |

The results of the site with this number are processed.

   | |
 | resultAreaName |

The extra parameter defines the name of the result area from which the samples should be retrieved. If this parameter is omitted, the default result area is used.

 |
 | mode  | This extra parameter controls the format of the reply when a range is specified with parameters first_sample and no_of_samples:

- If mode is set to OFF, a separate line is returned for every period value within the range.
- If mode is set to ON, the values are returned in a binary format in one line.
OFF is the default value. |
 | pinlist  | The mandatory list of pins for which the time stamps are to be returned. |
 | sitenumber |

Extra reply parameter. The site the samples belong to if the site_selector parameter has been set to ALL.

 |
 | sample_id |

This reply parameter identifies the sample. It is only returned if a range was specified in the query and mode was set to OFF.

 |
 | aggregation_type |

This reply parameter specifies an aggregation type. If a range was specified in the query, TSRS? returns not only the individual period values but also a number of statistics. These are:

-

STDDEV (standard deviation)

-

MEAN

-

MAX

-

MIN

-

MEDIAN

-

PP (peak to peak), the PP is same as MINMAX in the TMU ORE firmware.

 |
 | result |

The reply parameter specifies the period related to sample n or a value of the descriptive statistics. The unit is seconds.

It is not returned if a range was specified in the query and mode was set to ON.

 |
 | pin |

The pin to which the returned results belong.

 |
 | #spec(raw_results) |

The binary data that are returned if a range is specified with parameters first_sample and no_of_samples, and parameter mode is set to ON. The general format is:

`n1n2...nNdata_stream`

Where the decimal digit N defines the number of the decimal digits ni (1 = i = N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The values are specified as seconds.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRS  -  TMU Set ReSults）

This example returns the descriptive statistics for the measurement blocks individually.

```
> TSRS? ,PERIOD, , , (pin_a)

    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , STDDEV ,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MEAN 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MAX, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MIN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MEDIAN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , PP, 1.36,(pin_a)

    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , STDDEV ,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEAN 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MAX, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MIN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEDIAN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , PP, 1.36,(pin_a)
```

This example returns the individual samples 100 through 119 in measurement block 2, and also the statistical values.

```
> TSRS? 2,PERIOD,100,20,(pin_a)

    < TSRS  2,PERIOD ,100,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD ,101,1.37,(pin_a)
    ...
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD ,119,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , STDDEV ,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEAN 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MAX, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MIN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEDIAN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , PP, 1.36,(pin_a)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRW  -  TMU Set RaW results）

```
TSRW? [(sitesToBeDone),] [shot], [measurement_id], [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(execution_control),] [(site_selector),][(resultAreaName),] [(mode),] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSRW [shot], [measurement_id], [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(sitenumber),] {(pin)}, {#spec(raw_results)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRW  -  TMU Set RaW results）

| sitesToBeDone |

An extra string parameter, defining the sites to be uploaded. i.e. "01110011".

This option needs parameter `site_selector`（raw: `02.06.02.02.279_TSRW__-__TMU_Set_RaW_results.md#_125519__r_site_selector`） to be set to ALL.

 |
 | shot |

The optional parameter specifies the number of the shot for which the time stamps are to be uploaded. If no shot number is specified, the time stamps for all shots are uploaded.

 |
 | measurement_id |

The optional number of the measurement block (identified by the ARM keyword within a waveform that is executed in the pattern) from which time stamps are to be uploaded. If no measurement block is specified, results from all measurement blocks are uploaded.

 |
 | first_sample |

The optional parameter specifies the first sample to be uploaded. Samples are counted from 0.

 |
 | no_of_samples |

The optional parameter specifies the number of samples that are to be uploaded. Depending on the value of parameter first_sample, fewer samples than specified may be uploaded. For example, if there are nine samples in total, first_sample is 7 and no_of_samples is 4, only two samples are returned (the last two), not four.

 |
 | execution_control |

With this extra parameter, you can modify the default actions sequence of TSRW?. Possible values are.

 |

NOT_FINISHED

 |

All three steps described above will be executed. If not all required samples have been actually taken, the query will not stop, it issues a warning and continues to analyze and upload the available samples.

This is the default value.

 |
 | FINISHED  | The completeness check will be skipped. TSRW? assumes that all required samples have been taken. It will analyze and upload the available samples. It starts from step 2, above. |
 | ANALYZED  | Samples will not be analyzed. TSRW? assumes that all required samples were taken and analyzed in a previous step. It uploads the available samples. It starts from step 3, above.  | |
 | site_selector |

This extra query parameter allows you to request the results for a specific site or all sites. Possible values:

 | ONE |

Only the values of the site which has the query focus are uploaded (the default).

 |
 | ALL |

The values of all sites or the sites defined by parameter `sitesToBeDone`（raw: `02.06.02.02.279_TSRW__-__TMU_Set_RaW_results.md#_125519__r_sitesToBeDone`） are computed.

 |
 | <N> |

The results of the site with this number are computed.

   | |
 | resultAreaName |

The extra parameter defines the name of the result area from which the samples should be retrieved. If this parameter is omitted the default result area is used.

 |
 | mode |

This extra parameter has two functions. It defines the format of the reply, and it controls the behavior of the TMU if the distance of a sample from the arming point exceeds the maximum of about 15 s.

By default, there will be an internal wrap-around in this case, and the following time stamps will no longer be correct. You can choose to let the software correct the results, but this will increase the testing time.

There are four options:

-

OFF

The time stamps are returned in ASCII format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are wrapped around.

-

ON

The time stamps are returned in binary format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are wrapped around.

-

LTOFF

The time stamps are returned in ASCII format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are corrected.

-

LTON

The time stamps are returned in binary format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are corrected.

 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory list of pins for which the time stamps are to be uploaded.

 |
 | pin |

The pin to which the uploaded results belong.

 |
 | sitenumber |

Extra reply parameter. The site to which the samples belong.

 |
 | #spec(raw_result) |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

`n1n2...nNdata_stream`

Where the decimal digit N defines the number of the decimal digits ni (1 = i = N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSRW  -  TMU Set RaW results）

```
> TSRW? 1,1,0,3,(std_i)

    < TSRW 1,1,0,3,(std_i),#2470.0000524107368,0.0000525147428,0.0000526187385
```

This example uploads the time stamps 0 through 2 of measurement block 1 of the first shot. The unit is seconds.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSST  -  TeSt STatus）

```
TSST? {ALL|test_result_mask}, {ALL|test_status_mask}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSST {test_result}, {test_status}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSST  -  TeSt STatus）

|

test_result_mask

 |

In order to mask some of the result bits, enter an integer not greater than 2047. The bits of the corresponding binary number will be combined with the respective bits of the result bytes by AND.

 |

ALL

 |

By this option, the information of the result bytes is returned as an integer. This integer must be translated into a binary number and then be interpreted as follows:

- Bit 0 (LSB): Upper limit

Set to 1 if all these conditions are true for at least one measurement:

  - A high limit is both specified and activated with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.
  - The measurement is not masked with DFTD.
  - The measurement value was greater than the high limit.

- Bit 1: Lower limit

Set to 1 if all these conditions are true for at least one measurement:

  - A low limit is both specified and activated with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.
  - The measurement is not masked with DFTD.
  - The measurement value was smaller than the low limit.

- Bit 2: Global status

Set to 1 if at least one of the bits 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 is set to 1.

- Bit 3: Low clamp violation

Set to 1 if all these conditions are true for at least one measurement:

  - Checking low clamp violations is activated with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.
  - The measurement is not masked with DFTD.
  - The low clamp was violated (status bit 0 is set to 1).

- Bit 4: High clamp violation

Set to 1 if all these conditions are true for at least one measurement:

  - Checking high clamp violations is activated with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.
  - The measurement is not masked with DFTD.
  - The high clamp was violated (status bit 1 is set to 1).

- Bit 5: Range underflow

Set to 1 if all these conditions are true for at least one measurement:

  - Checking measurement ranges is activated with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.
  - The measurement is not masked with DFTD.
  - An underflow occurred (status bit 4 is set to 1).

- Bit 6: Range overflow

Set to 1 if all these conditions are true for at least one measurement:

  - Checking measurement ranges is activated with `DFTD`（raw: `02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md`）.
  - The measurement is not masked with DFTD.
  - An overflow occurred (status bit 5 is set to 1).

- Bit 7: Distance too small or internal buffer overflow

Set to 1 if the distance between two consecutive test points (for example, between definition of the range and measurement) is too small, and measurements were interrupted.

AVI64 and FVI16 only: The bit is also set to 1 in case too many commands were issued causing internal buffer overflow.

- Bit 8: Lost measurements

Set to 1 if not all measurement results were recorded because the test stopped earlier than expected.

- Bit 9: Type mismatch

Set to 1 if at least one measurement has been executed in a range that does not match the requested measurement type.

- Bit 10: Wrong hardware state

Set to 1 if the hardware switched into an unexpected state that caused the test to fail (for example, a disconnect for safety reasons). Detailed information can be queried with `PSAS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`）.

   | |
 |

test_status_mask

 |

In order to mask some of the result bits, enter an integer not greater than 15. The bits of the corresponding binary number will be combined with the respective bits of the status byte by AND.

 |

ALL

 |

By this option, the information of the status byte is returned as an integer. This integer must be translated into a binary number, and then be interpreted as follows:

- Bit 0 (LSB): Current sink limit is reached

Set to 1 if current sink limit is reached (Clamp low) for at least one measurement.

- Bit 1: Current source limit

Set to 1 if current source limit is reached (Clamp high) for at least one measurement.

- Bit 2: Clamp low was reached

Set to 1 if clamp low was reached during the test for a DC Scale pin where no measurement was executed.

- Bit 3: Clamp high was reached

Set to 1 if clamp high was reached during the test for a DC Scale pin where no measurement was executed.

- Bit 4: Range underflow

Set to 1 in case of a range underflow has been detected for at least one measurement.

- Bit 5: Range overflow

Set to 1 in case of a range overflow has been detected for at least one measurement.

- Bit 6-7: Reserved
   | |
 |

test_result

 |

If you specify `ALL` for the test_result_mask parameter, the result byte is returned as a decimal value.

If you specify a mask, P or F is returned according to the result of combining the mask and the test result bytes by AND.

- P: The result of the AND operation is 0 for all bit pairs.
- F: The result of the AND operation is 1 for at least 1 bit pair.
 |
 |

test_status

 |

If you specify ALL for the test_result_mask parameter, the status byte is returned as a decimal value.

If you specify a mask, P or F is returned according to the result of combining the mask and the test result byte by AND.

- P: The result of the AND operation is 0 for all bit pairs.
- F: The result of the AND operation is 1 for at least 1 bit pair.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Results are provided only for the pins specified in pinlist. If you specify more than one pin, the names must be separated by commas. All pins in pinlist must have test point capability.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSST  -  TeSt STatus）

```
> TSST? ALL,ALL,(@)
< TSST 1,0,(dpsPin1)
> TSST? 0,256,(@)
< TSST P,P,(dpsPin1)
```

This example shows the effect of a mask. As shown by the first query, the only error was that at least one pin has failed the limit check. In the second query, bit 0 of the result byte is masked, and consequently TSST? returns P for both result and status.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSTL  TSTL  -  TeST Label）

|

label

 |

Defines the label you wish to edit. Enter an alphanumeric string, 1 to 128 characters long, enclosed in double quotes. You can deactivate the currently selected label by specifying an empty string ("").

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter is ignored in the command. In the query reply, it specifies the port to which the active label belongs.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSTL  TSTL  -  TeST Label）

```
TSTL "new",
```

This example selects the label "new" for editing.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSUD -  TMU Set UnDefine）

```
TSUD {"TMU_set_name"|ALL}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSUD -  TMU Set UnDefine）

|

TMU_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing TMU set.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This option removes all defined TMU sets.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSUD -  TMU Set UnDefine）

```
> TSUD   "TMU_set1"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSUS  TSUS  -  Timing Sets USed）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows: `100 * `equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a timing set or the highest number of timing set you want to associate with a given waveform set. The number you enter must be less than or equal to the maximum number of timing sets allowed (as defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command). This number is automatically updated to include any new timing set as it is created. At power-on only one timing set (containing the default values and belonging to the single waveform set) is available.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

For multiport specifications, you can specify a list of the ports for which the number of the timing sets used is to be displayed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSUS  TSUS  -  Timing Sets USed）

```
TSUS 3,7
```

This example defines a maximum of 7 timing sets in waveform set 3.

```
TSUS? "spefc",(ARMPort)
TSUS "spefc",3,(ARMPort)
```

This example queries the number of timing sets defined for port ARMPort in the multiport specification spefc.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSUX  TSUX  -  Timing Sets Used eXtended）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter ALL for all waveform sets in the query command.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. In the command, TSUX is set to this value for the specified waveform set, if the number is smaller than the current value of `TSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`） for this set. Otherwise, it is set to the current value of TSUS.

 |
 |

SWAP

 |

This command parameter causes the values set by `TSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）and TSUX to be switched, that is, TSUS is set to the current value of TSUX , and TSUX to that of TSUS for the specified waveform set.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

This command parameter sets the value of TSUX back to 1 for the specified waveform set.

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSVD  -  TimStamper ValiD）

```
TSVD? {waveform_set|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|PRM}, {"TMU_set"|PRM}
```

returns:

```
TSVD? {waveform_set|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|PRM}, {"TMU_set"|PRM}, {VALID|ERROR}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSVD  -  TimStamper ValiD）

|

waveform_set

 |

Specifies a waveform set number for a fixed timing setup.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Specifies a spec set ID for an equation based setup. The spec set ID is derived from an equation set number and a spec set number as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

Specifies the name of a multiport specification for a multi-port setup.

 |
 |

TMU_set

 |

The TMU set that is to be checked.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

Refers to the current primary timing specification or the current primary TMU set.

 |
 |

VALID

 |

Timing specification and TMU set are consistent.

 |
 |

ERROR

 |

Timing specification and TMU set are not consistent.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TSVD  -  TimStamper ValiD）

```
> TSVD? PRM, "TMU_set1"
< TSVD PRM, "TMU_set1",VALID
```

This example queries if the current primary timing is consistent to the TMU set `TMU_set1`.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTCF  TTCF  -  Transition Test ConFiguration）

|

tt_name

 |

Specifies the name of a transition test set that must have been defined with `TTDF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.288_TTDF__TTDF__-__Transition_Test_set_DeFinition.md`）.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the transition test set. For a list, see the Properties and their values table below.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all transition test sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified to modify or retrieve the configuration of the current primary transition test set.

 |
 |

DEFAULT

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration of the predefined transition test set DEFAULT. Note that the DEFAULT set cannot be changed, it can only be queried.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified property. The values that are admitted for the individual properties are listed in the table below.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which this configuration is to be applied.

 |

Properties and their values
 |

Property

 |

Explanation and values

 |
 |

ALL_PATTERN_ERR

 |

This is a collective switch for all pattern matching errors. The possible values are ON and OFF. There is no default.

 |
 |

ALL_TRACKING_ERR

 |

This is a collective switch for all tracking errors. The possible values are ON and OFF. There is no default.

 |
 |

DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED

 |

This property only applies if X-tokens are removed (REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE set to ON) and the token size is > 0. It defines the maximum number of UI by which the received data are allowed to exceed the expected data under these circumstances. The received data exceeds the expected data in length if the number of idle tokens in the received data is greater than the number of X-tokens in the expected data. See `Skipping idle tokens`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.02_Skipping_idle_tokens.md`）.

The default is 0. The specified value must be 鈮?256.

 |
 |

DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT

 |

This property only applies if X-tokens are removed (REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE set to ON) and the token size is > 0. It defines the maximum number of UI by which the expected data are allowed to exceed the received data under these circumstances. The expected data exceeds the received data in length if the number of X-tokens in the expected data is greater than the number of idle tokens in the received data. See `Skipping idle tokens`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.02_Skipping_idle_tokens.md`）.

The default is 0. The specified value must be 鈮?256.

 |
 |

DISPARITY_MODE

 |

This property determines whether disparity is taken into account when comparing expected tokens with received tokens. This only applies to token size 10.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_BADTRAN

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if an illegal sequence of transitions occurred.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTADJOVR

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if an adjustment overflow occurs. This means that the observation window was adjusted more than 1 UI in one direction within 24 UI. Note that adjustments in opposite direction cancel each other out. Thus if '+' indicates an adjustment to the right, and '-' an adjustment to the left,

`- + - + - + - +`

is acceptable, but

`+ + + + + - + +`

creates an overflow.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTLMT

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the maximum drift of 7.75 UI for the entire pattern is exceeded.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_COMPARE

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if compare errors are detected.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_FTO

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the number of UI that are skipped for synchronization at test start exceeds the maximum defined with FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_JMP2

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if an unrecoverable BC transition (jump by 2) is detected.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_PULSE

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if a bit was sampled only once. If pulse stretching is enabled, the error will refer to the stretched pulse (see `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.03_Stretching_the_pulse.md`）).

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_STO

 |

This property defines whether the test fails when the number of consecutive skipped bits after initial synchronization exceeds the maximum defined with SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

This can happen in two cases:

- at synchronization of an IO pin that has been switched from drive to receive mode, or
- when too many consecutive idle tokens have been skipped, that is, if

no_of_tokens * token_size > SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_STOP

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the sequencer stops too early, that is, before all compare actions have been completed. This error can be avoided by adding an appropriate number of break vectors (at least 400) at the end of the test.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE0

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if no reference transition occurs, that is, the observation window could not be adjusted successfully.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE2

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if a BC transition occurs in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LLHH HHHH

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE3

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if two different transitions occur within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LHHH LLLH

Here the second UI contains an AB transition, and the third UI contains a CD transition.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE4

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if three transitions occur within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

HHLL LHHH LLLH

Here the first UI contains a BC transition, the second contains an AB transition, and the third a CD transition.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TRK

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the maximum drift for the entire pattern as defined with TRACKING_LIMIT is exceeded.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TRMCNT

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the skipped idle bits are not a multiple of the token size.

 |
 |

ERR_XMAX

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the length of the received data exceeds the length of the expected data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_XMIN

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the length of the expected data exceeds the length of the received data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT

 |

This property defines how many bits are allowed to be skipped by initial synchronization at test start. The maximum value is 2^32. This is also the default.

 |
 |

FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE

 |

This property activates or deactivates initial synchronization at test start.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

IDLE_TOKEN_i

 |

With this property, you can specify idle tokens whose occurrences in the received data are to be counted. i can be 1 through 6. This property only applies to token sizes > 0 and < 18.

 |
 |

PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_1BIT

 |

This property defines if and how much pulses that are sampled only once are to be stretched. For more information see `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.03_Stretching_the_pulse.md`）.

Possible values are:

 |
 |

NONE

 |

No stretching takes place.

 |
 |

STRETCH_1TO3

 |

1 sample bits are stretched to 3 samples.

 |
 |

STRETCH_1TO4

 |

1 sample bits are stretched to 4 samples.

 |
 |

PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_2BIT

 |

This property defines if and how much pulses that are sampled only twice are to be stretched. For more information see `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.01_Startup_latency_and_initial_synchronization.md`）.

Possible values are:

 |
 |

NONE

 |

No stretching takes place.

 |
 |

STRETCH_2TO3

 |

2 sample bits are stretched to 3 samples.

 |
 |

STRETCH_2TO4

 |

2 sample bits are stretched to 4 samples.

 |
 |

REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE

 |

This property activates or deactivates removal of tokens consisting entirely of X from the expected data. The possible values are ON and OFF. For more information see `Skipping idle tokens`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.02_Skipping_idle_tokens.md`）.

This property only takes effect if the token size is > 0.

 |
 |

SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT

 |

This property defines how many bits are allowed to be skipped by subsequent initial synchronization. The maximum value is 2^32. This is also the default.

This property also limits the maximum number of consecutive idle tokens that can be skipped after synchronization, by the following inequality:

number_of_skipped_tokens * token_size 鈮? SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT

 |
 |

SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE

 |

This property activates or deactivates subsequent initial synchronization, for example after the switch of an IO pin from drive to receive mode. The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default. This property only takes effect if FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE is set to ON.

For more information see `Startup latency and initial synchronization`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.01_Startup_latency_and_initial_synchronization.md`）.

 |
 |

TOKEN_SIZE

 |

This property defines the token size for the pattern matching block. The allowed values are:

0, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 32, 34, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 64, 66.

0 is the default. For more information see `Pattern matching`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02_Pattern_matching.md`）.

 |
 |

TRACKING_LIMIT

 |

This property defines how much the device is to be allowed to drift during the whole pattern. The maximum value that still allows a reliable tracking is 7.75 UI. This is also the default.

The step width for this parameter is 1/4 UI.

 |
 |

TRACKING_MODE

 |

This property defines the operation mode of the transition tracker. For more information see `Controlling the tracking behavior`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.01_Controlling_the_tracking_behavior.md`）.

The possible values are:

 |
 |

ACTIVE

 |

If necessary, the observation window is adjusted after every 3 UI.

 |
 |

FREEZE_AFTER_SYNC

 |

If necessary, the observation window is adjusted once at test start and once after every switch of a IO pin from drive to receive mode.

 |
 |

FREEZE_ALWAYS

 |

The observation window is never adjusted.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTCF  TTCF  -  Transition Test ConFiguration）

```
> TTCF? "my_TT_SET",ALL,(PIN1)

< TTCF "my_TT_SET",DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED,100,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT,100,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",DISPARITY_MODE,OFF,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_BADTRAN,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_CNTADJOVR,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_CNTLMT,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_COMPARE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_FTO,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_JMP2,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_PULSE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_STO,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_STOP,OFF,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE0,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE2,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE3,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE4,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TRK,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TRMCNT,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_WRCMP,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_XMAX,ON,(PIN1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_XMIN,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT,10,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_1,"LLLLLHHHHH",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_2,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_3,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_4,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_5,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_6,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_1BIT,STRETCH_2TO4,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_2BIT,STRETCH_1TO3,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE,OFF,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT,10,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",TOKEN_SIZE,10,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",TRACKING_LIMIT,4,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",TRACKING_MODE,ACTIVE,(Pin1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTDB  -  Transition Test DeBug information）

```
TTDB? {type|ALL}, [sub_type], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TTDB {type}, [sub_type], {value}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTDB  -  Transition Test DeBug information）

|

type

 |

Specifies the information type. For a list, see the Information types and subtypes table below.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All information types are returned.

 |
 |

sub_type

 |

Specifies a subtype of the information type. The subtypes for every type are listed in the Information types and subtypes table below.

 |
 |

value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified combination of type and subtype. For more explanation see the Information types and subtypes table below.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which debug information is to be retrieved.

 |

Information types and subtypes
 |

Information type

 |

Explanation and values

 |
 |

MAX_DEVIATION

 |

If the token size was > 0 during the last sequencer run, this item returns for this sequencer run:

- The maximum number of UI by which the received data has fallen behind the exceeded the expected data (subtype DUT_BEHIND_ED)
- The maximum number of UI by which the expected data has fallen behind the received data (subtype ED_BEHIND_DUT)

The received data is shortened by skipping idle tokens, the expected data by removing X-tokens.

 |
 |

TRK_FIRST_ADJUSTMENT

 |

This item returns the adjustment that was determined by the first transition after test start.

 |
 |

TRK_FIRST_ERR

 |

This item returns the number of expected bits that had been processed when the first tracking error occurred.

 |
 |

TRK_VALUES

 |

This item returns information about the adjustment of the observation window. The unit is 0.25 UI (= 1 sample).

There are three subtypes:

- ACT returns the actual adjustment at the end of the test.
- MIN returns the maximum adjustment to the left during the last test.
- MAX returns the maximum adjustment to the right during the last test.
 |
 |

TRK_STATUS

 |

This item returns the transition patterns that were observed during the last test as a sequence of four-digit blocks.

In order to understand this information, you must take into account that the observation window can only be adjusted after every three UI (see the discussion of the implementation parameters in `Drift and transition tracking`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01_Drift_and_transition_tracking.md`）). Thus, the observation window actually consists of three successive UI.

The four-digit blocks encode the accumulated transitions for one such 3-UI window (subtype TRANS_COMPOSITE) or for two such windows (subtype TRANS_X). "1" indicates a transition, "0" indicates no transition. Every block starts with "1". This indicates that the observation window was adjusted successfully.

As an example for the one window case, consider

LLLL LHHH LLLH,

where the second UI has an AB transition, and the third has a CD transition. This is encoded by

1101,

which says that an AB transition (second digit) and a CD transition (fourth digit), but no BC transition was observed in the 3-UI window.

TRK_STATUS has three subtypes:

- TRANS_X returns the transition patterns that occurred in the last 24 UI (= 8 windows, each of 3 UI). Each of the four blocks accumulates two windows (= 6 UI). The order of the blocks corresponds to the order of the test.
- TRANS_COMPOSITE returns the transition patterns that occurred by accumulating the 3 UI of one window during the last sequencer run up to the first error. Since the first digit is always 1 (except when the window could not be adjusted) there are 8 possible patterns between 1000 (best) and 1111 (worst). The patterns that occurred are displayed.
- TRANS_R returns 0 if the observation window could always be adjusted successfully. It returns 1 if this is not the case. This error should only occur if the observation window was adjusted more than 1 UI in the same direction within 24 UI (see the ERR_CNTADJOVR property of the TTCF command).
 |
 |

LOCATION_FIRST_FAIL

 |

This item returns the number of expected bits that had been processed when the first error of any kind occurred.

 |
 |

REMOVED_IDLE

 |

This item returns how often one of the 6 idle tokens that had been defined with TTCF IDLE_TOKEN_i occurred during the last sequencer run. The sub_type parameter specifies the number of the token.

 |
 |

REMOVED_XTOKEN

 |

This item returns how many X-tokens were removed. This only applies if X-token removal is activated with TTCF REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE.

REMOVED_XTOKEN has one subtype:

- SEQUENCER_RUN returns the number of X-tokens that were removed on the last sequencer run
 |
 |

STATUS

 |

This item returns information about the state of the tracker after the test as a bit sequence. Most of these status bits can also be queried with TTST?. The individual bits stand for:

 |
 |

- Bit1: An interrupt was generated.
- Bit2: Break vectors entered the formatting block.
- Bit3: The first match between expected and received data has occurred.
- Bit4: Expected and received data are prepared for the first compare.
- Bit5: The FIFO between tracking and pattern matching block is empty.
- Bit6: The FIFO between expected data and pattern matching block is empty.
- Bit7: The expected data window FIFO is empty.
- Bit8: The expected data FIFO is empty.
- Bit9: EXPECTED_FIFO_DUT_OVERFLOW
- Bit10: ADJUSTMENT_ERROR
- Bit11: Always 1
- Bit12: DRIVE_BIT_IN_COMPARE_DATA
- Bit13: DUT_FIFO_OVERFLOW
- Bit14: ERR_XCNT
 |

- Bit15: ERR_XMIN
- Bit16: ERR_XMAX
- Bit17: ERR_TRMCNT
- Bit18: ERR_WRCMP
- Bit19: ERR_COMPARE
- Bit20: ERR_STO
- Bit21: ERR_FTO
- Bit22: ERR_STOP
- Bit23: ERR_CNTLMT
- Bit24: ERR_CNTADJOVR
- Bit25: ERR_BADTRAN
- Bit26: ERR_PULSE
- Bit27: ERR_TRK
- Bit28: ERR_JMP2
- Bit29: ERR_TE4
- Bit30: ERR_TE0
- Bit31: ERR_TE2
- Bit32: ERR_TE3
 |
 |

The names specified for bits 9 through 32 refer to the possible errors returned by `TTST?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.292_TTST__-__Transition_Test_STatus_information.md`）. For more explanations see this query and the `TTCF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.286_TTCF__TTCF__-__Transition_Test_ConFiguration.md`） command.

 |
 |

REMOVED_XTOKEN_EMAP

 |

This item returns how many x-tokens were removed with respect to start and stop of the error map.

REMOVED_XTOKEN_EMAP has two subtypes:

- START returns the number of removed X-tokens at the start of the error map.
- STOP returns the number of removed X-tokens at the end of error map recording.
 |
 |

SYNC_VALUES

 |

This item returns how many received bits were skipped for initial synchronization at test start (subtype INITIAL) or after a switch of an IO pin from drive to receive mode (subtype SUBSEQUENT).

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTDB  -  Transition Test DeBug information）

```
> TTDB? IDLE_TOKEN, 1, (Pin1)

< TTDB IDLE_TOKEN, 1, 1234,(Pin1)
```

This example queries how often the first special idle token was removed in the last sequencer run.

```
> TTDB? TRK_STATUS,ALL, (Pin1)

< TTDB TRK_STATUS,TRANS_X,"1000 1001 1101 1000", (Pin1)
< TTDB TRK_STATUS,TRANS_R,0, (Pin1)
< TTDB TRK_STATUS,TRANS_COMPOSITE,"1000 1001 1101", (Pin1)
```

The first line of the reply reports the transitions of the last 24 UI, accumulated in blocks of 6. The third line reports which accumulated transition patterns occurred in one window (= 3 UI) during the last sequencer run. Three of the 8 possible patterns were observed.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTDF  TTDF  -  Transition Test set DeFinition）

```
> TTDF   "myTTTrckSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTPatTSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTRCTLSet1"

TTDF?
> TTDF   "myTTTrckSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTPatTSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTRCTLSet1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTMD  -  Transition Test MoDe query）

```
TTMD? {specset_id|"multi-port_spec"}, {timing_set}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TTMD {specset_id|"multi-port_spec"}, {timing_set}, {tt_mode}, [clk_fwd], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTMD  -  Transition Test MoDe query）

|

specset_id

 |

Number of a single-port timing specification. Derived as follows:

`100 *`equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

For a multiport setup, specify the name of a multiport specification.

Note that the multiport specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multiport specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. Enter PRM for the primary timing set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by TSUS.

 |
 |

tt_mode

 |

Specifies the protocol engine test mode. Possible values are:

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Protocol engine is inactivated

 |
 |

X4

 |

X4-mode is activated.

 |
 |

X6

 |

X6-mode is activated.

 |
 |

clk_fwd

 |

Not used.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the protocol engine mode is to be retrieved. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma.

In a multiport setup, every pin must belong to a port of the specified specification.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTMD  -  Transition Test MoDe query）

```
> TTMD 101,1,(PIN1)
< TTMD 101,1,X4,,(PIN1)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTPR  TTPR  -  Transition Test PRimary set）

|

tt_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing transition test set.

 |
 |

DEFAULT

 |

This is a predefined transition test set.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTPR  TTPR  -  Transition Test PRimary set）

```
> TTPR   "myTTTrckSet1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTRS  -  Time TRansition Search）

```
TTRS? {start}, {stop}, {search_type}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TTRS {value_specifier}, [pass_value], [fail_value], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTRS  -  Time TRansition Search）

|

start

 |

The start parameter defines the point in time (in ns), relative to the start of the cycle, where you want the search to begin.

 |
 |

stop

 |

The stop parameter defines the point in time (in ns), relative to the start of the cycle, where you want the search to end.

 |
 |

search_type

 |

The search type is one of the following:

 |
 |

L

 |

Specifies a linear search from the start of the window, at intervals defined by the ESGB command. The search will terminate after the first failed test or after the search limit specified by the stop parameter has been reached.

 |
 |

LB

 |

Specifies a combined linear and binary search using the step width defined by the ESGB command. A linear search is performed, with an additional binary search carried out in the interval between the last passed and the first failed test.

 |
 |

B

 |

Specifies a binary search carried out between the start and the stop positions.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins on which the search is to take place. This parameter may also include groups previously created using `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pinlist must only contain pins configured as outputs.

 |
 |

value_

specifier

 |

This parameter can be:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned if the first functional test of a search in the positive direction failed.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned if all the functional tests performed between start and stop pass. LE is only returned for a search in the negative direction.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

(equal to) is returned if the first failure of the search occurs between the start and the stop positions.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned if all the tests carried out between start and stop pass. GE can only be returned for a search in the positive direction.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned if the first functional test performed during a search in the negative direction fails.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The pass_value is the time (in ns) at which the last passed test occurs. A pass value is only returned for if value_specifier is EQ, LE, or GE.

 |
 |

fail_value

 |

The fail_value is the time (in ns) at which the last failed test occurs. A fail value is only returned for if value_specifier is EQ, LT, or GT.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTRS  -  Time TRansition Search）

```
TTRS? 10,80,L,(Q0)
TTRS EQ,70,80,(Q0)
```

This example executes a global search test on pin Q0. A linear sweep takes place between 10 ns and 80 ns relative to the start of the period. The system returned a pass at 70 ns and a fail at 80 ns.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTST  -  Transition Test STatus information）

```
TTST? {status_type}, {filter}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

TTST {status_type}, {property}, {state}, {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTST  -  Transition Test STatus information）

|

status_type

 |

Specifies the status type. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ERR_STATUS

 |

Returns information about possible errors per pin. These are exactly the properties that can be activated as errors with TTCF, and whose names start with "ERR_".

Note that each of the states contained in this status type is reported when it is observed, regardless of whether it is actually activated with TTCF. TTCF only controls whether the specific error condition contributes to the pass/fail result of a pin.

The possible errors are:

 |
 |

ERR_BADTRAN

 |

An illegal sequence of transitions occurred.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTADJOVR

 |

An adjustment overflow occurred. This means that the observation window was adjusted more than 1 UI in one direction within 24 UI. Note that adjustments in opposite direction cancel each other out. Thus if '+' indicates an adjustment to the right, and '-' an adjustment to the left,

- + - + - + - +

is acceptable, but

+ + + + + - + +

creates an overflow.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTLMT

 |

The maximum drift of 7.75 UI for the entire pattern was exceeded.

 |
 |

ERR_COMPARE

 |

Compare errors were detected.

 |
 |

ERR_FTO

 |

The number of bits that were skipped for synchronization at test start exceeds the maximum defined with FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

 |
 |

ERR_JMP2

 |

An unrecoverable BC transition (jump by 2) was detected.

 |
 |

ERR_PULSE

 |

A bit was sampled only once. If pulse stretching was enabled this error refers to the stretched pulse. See `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.03_Stretching_the_pulse.md`）.

 |
 |

ERR_STO

 |

The number of consecutive skipped bits after initial synchronization exceeds the maximum defined with SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

This can happen in two cases:

- at synchronization of an IO pin that has been switched from drive to receive mode, or
- when too many consecutive idle tokens have been skipped, that is, if

no_of_tokens * token_size >

SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

 |
 |

ERR_STOP

 |

The sequencer stopped too early, that is, before all compare actions have been completed. This error can be avoided by adding an appropriate number of break vectors (at least 400) at the end of the test.

 |
 |

ERR_TE0

 |

No reference transition occurred, that is, the observation window could not be adjusted successfully.

 |
 |

ERR_TE2

 |

A BC transition occurred in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LLHH HHHH

 |
 |

ERR_TE3

 |

Two different transitions occurred within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LHHH LLLH

Here the second UI contains an AB transition, and the third UI contains a CD transition.

 |
 |

ERR_TE4

 |

Three transitions occurred within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

HHLL LHHH LLLH

Here the first UI contains a BC transition, the second contains an AB transition, and the third a CD transition.

 |
 |

ERR_TRK

 |

The maximum drift for the entire pattern as defined with TRACKING_LIMIT was exceeded.

 |
 |

ERR_TRMCNT

 |

The removed idle bits were not a multiple of the token size.

 |
 |

ERR_XMAX

 |

The length of the received data exceeds the length of the expected data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED.

This only applies when X-token removal is activated with the REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE property.

 |
 |

ERR_XMIN

 |

The length of the expected data exceeds the length of the received data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT.

This only applies when X-token removal is activated with the REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE property.

 |
 |

ERR_STATUS_COMBINED

 |

Returns combined information about possible errors for all specified pins.

Note that each of the states contained in this status type is reported when it is observed, regardless of whether it is actually activated as an error with `TTCF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.286_TTCF__TTCF__-__Transition_Test_ConFiguration.md`）.

 |
 |

INTR_STATUS

 |

Returns information per pin about interrupts during the last sequencer run.

 |
 |

INTR_STATUS_COMBINED

 |

Returns combined information about interrupts for all specified pins.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All status types are returned.

 |
 |

filter

 |

Specifies which subset of the available information is to be returned. The possible values depend on the selected status type.

Possible values for ERR_STATUS and ERR_STATUS_COMBINED are:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

The state of all possible errors is returned.

 |
 |

ALL_HEX

 |

The state of all possible errors is returned as a hexadecimal number.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Only the possible errors that were not observed are returned.

 |
 |

ON

 |

Only the possible errors that were observed are returned.

 |
 |

property

 |

The reply is whether the possible error identified by this property was observed. For the meaning of the properties see the `TTCF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.286_TTCF__TTCF__-__Transition_Test_ConFiguration.md`） command.

 |
 |

The values ALL, ALL_HEX, OFF, and ON can also be specified for INTR_STATUS and INTR_STATUS_COMBINED.

The individual properties for these two types are:

 |
 |

ADJUSTMENT_ERROR

 |

This is a hardware error.

 |
 |

DRIVE_BIT_IN_COMPARE_DATA

 |

This can only happen when APG mode is enabled and a drive bit was found in the received data.

 |
 |

DUT_FIFO_OVERFLOW

 |

This can happen when X-token removal is enabled and the number of removed X-tokens exceeds the number of skipped idle tokens.

 |
 |

EXPECTED_FIFO_DUT_OVERFLOW

 |

This is a hardware error.

 |
 |

state

 |

Specifies the state of a selected property. Possible values are:

 |
 |

OFF

 |

The state was not observed.

 |
 |

ON

 |

The state was observed.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which status information is to be retrieved.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › TTST  -  Transition Test STatus information）

```
> TTST? ALL,ALL,(p1)

< TTST INTR_STATUS,DRIVE_BIT_IN_COMPARE_DATA,OFF,(p1)
< TTST INTR_STATUS,ADJUSTMENT_ERROR,OFF,(p1)
< TTST INTR_STATUS,DUT_FIFO_OVERFLOW,OFF,(p1)
< TTST INTR_STATUS,EXPECTED_FIFO_OVERFLOW,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_XMAX,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_XMIN,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_FTO,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_STO,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TRMCNT,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_COMPARE,ON,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE4,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE3,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE2,ON,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE0,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_JMP2,ON,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TRK,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_PULSE,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_BADTRAN,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_CNTADJOVR,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_CNTLMT,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_STOP,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_WRCMP,OFF,(p1)
```

This example returns all properties of the ERR_STATUS type. ON indicates that the respective state was observed, OFF indicates that it was not observed. Note that ON does not imply that the test failed. For this, the respective property must also be activated as an error with TTCF. In this example compare errors (ERR_COMPARE) and a jump by 2 (ERR_TE2, ERR_JMP2) were observed.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UDPR -  UnDefine Pin Role）

```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UDPR -  UnDefine Pin Role）

|

alias_set_name

The alias set name.

The alias of the pin (specified by the pin name parameter) defined in this alias set is deleted.

The symbol @ can be used to list all the required alias set names.

 |
 |

pin_alias

 |

The pin alias.

 |
 |

package_pin_name

 |

The package pin name.

 |

This example deletes the pair of package pin name CP and the pin alias CLK from the alias set FUNC.
