### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UHCM  UHCM  -  Ultra High Current power supply Modes）

| set_nr  | The mandatory identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify:

 | ALL  | Modifies all existing DPS sets. |
 | PRM  | Modifies the primary DPS set. |
 | ACT  | Only for the query: Displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.  | |
 | time_to_alarm |

The extra parameter specifies the time (in milliseconds) from constant current clamp until an alarm flag is raised. See also ms_const_curr_time_to_alarm in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

Range: 0 ... 1270 ms.

This parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | reserved_param  | The optional parameter is reserved and required for compatibility. |
 | clamp_mode  | The optional parameter defines the clamp mode:

 | limit |

The clamp is active forever (the delay value is ignored).

This is the default value.

 |
 | `<delay>` |

Switch off at overcurrent after a delay.

<delay> is a time in milliseconds [ms].

For `<delay>`, the clamp is active until the channel switches off.

In case the channel is switched off, a disconnect/connect sequence is required (`PSST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） OFF/ON).

 |

See also `ms_const_curr_disconnect`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__ms_const_curr_disconnect`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

 |
 | fast_preload |

The optional parameter defines the preload time in milliseconds (ms).

To be used to charge large capacities for a programmable time. It does not make sense to set a shorter delay for clamp_mode than for fast_preload. A delay of zero (0) switches the fast_preload feature off.

See also `ms_fast_preload`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__ms_fast_preload`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

 |
 | openLoopProtection  |  The extra parameter defines the status of the internal force to sense connections.

The internal force to sense connections are available between the P# pin and the PS# pin and between the GS# pin and the common GND pin.

The following options are supported:

 | DIODE |

The internal force to sense connections are made via anti鈥憄arallel diodes.

This is the default state if the parameter is not defined.

This is the recommended setting if both parameters `force_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_force_drop`） and `return_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_return_drop`） are set to a value < 0.5 V.

 |
 | NONE |

The internal force to sense connections are open.

The output stage no longer has any voltage feedback if the force to sense connection on the DUT or the DUT board is (unintentionally) open.

 The following rules apply to this option:

- The `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`）.
- This is the required setting if one of the parameters `force_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_force_drop`） or `return_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_return_drop`） is set to a value 鈮?nbsp;0.5 V.
 |

This parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | force_drop |

The optional parameter forces a channel to be disconnected if a user鈥慸efined voltage drop on the force lines is reached, which means that the absolute voltage is higher than the defined threshold.

The `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`） can measure the voltage drop of the force line on the DUT board.

Card specific behavior:

-

UHC4T: A comparator defines if the voltage drop is small enough or not. This means to measure the drop of the pogo cable (see specifications) plus the drop of the DUT board. Value/flag available for all channels ganged.

The range is 0 to 0.5 V with a resolution of 1 mV. Default is 0.25 V.

Two rules have to be respected for the two parameters force_drop and return_drop and the programmed force voltage:

  - Both force_drop and return_drop must be between 0.0 V and 0.5 V.
  - The sum of force_drop and return_drop is limited by the programmed force voltage according to the diagram below. Only values within the red area are allowed.

- XPS256: force_drop can be an integer or string. In the string representation it is possible to also add a user-defined warning level for the voltage force drop. If this level is exceeded, a flag is raised, see `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`）.

The range is 0 to 1.0 V with a resolution of 1 mV. The total of theforce_drop and the return_drop must not exceed 1.0 V.

For a maximum voltage drop > 0.5 V, the `openLoopProtection`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_openLoopProtection`） parameter must be set to none and in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`） the `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON.

In case the channel is switched off, a disconnect/connect sequence is required (`PSST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） OFF/ON).

See also `max_voltage_drop_force`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__max_voltage_drop_force`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

This optional parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | return_drop |

The optional parameter forces a channel to be disconnected if a user-defined voltage drop on the return lines is reached, which menas that the absolute voltage is higher than the defined threshold.

The `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`） can measure the voltage drop of the return line on the DUT board.

Card specific behavior:

-

UHC4T: A comparator defines if the voltage drop is small enough or not. This means to measure the drop of the pogo cable (see specifications) plus the drop of the DUT board. Value/flag available for all channels ganged. The range is 0 to 0.5 V with a resolution of 1 mV. Default is 0.25 V.

Two rules have to be respected for the two parameters force_drop and return_drop and the programmed force voltage:

  - Both force_drop and return_drop must be between 0 and 0.5 V.
  - The sum of force_drop and return_drop is limited by the programmed force voltage according to the diagram below. Only values within the red area are allowed.

- XPS256: See `force_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_force_drop`）.

In case the channel is switched off, a disconnect/connect sequence is required (`PSST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） OFF/ON).

See also `max_voltage_drop_return`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__max_voltage_drop_return`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

This optional parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | pulldown |

The extra parameter specifies whether a pulldown resistor is active after disconnect.

 Supported values:

- OFF
- ON (default)
 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory comma鈥憇eparated list of pins.

The @ character can be used to specify all applicable pins.

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UHCM  UHCM  -  Ultra High Current power supply Modes）

```
UHCM PRM,,,,0.4,0.1,(Vee)
```

This example sets the voltage drop force to 0.4 V, and the voltage drop return to 0.1 V.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPAS  UPAS  -  Utility Purpose ASsignment for multi-site）

| site |

The site parameter is an integer that defines the number of the site where the channels are to be defined.

The integer must be greater than 1.

When specified as part of the UPAS? query, you can use the parameter ALL to read the standard output states for all sites.

 |
 | setting |

Output states for each member of the utility purpose on the specified site.

Set the output state of each utility line with the following specifiers:

- 0: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)
- 1: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to low
- X (x): No action

The number and order of characters must correspond to the ch_No_list parameter of the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command.

If this parameter is omitted, the specified site is set to the same states as site 1.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of a utility purpose defined by the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command.

In the query, the symbol @ can be used to list all defined utility purposes.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPAS  UPAS  -  Utility Purpose ASsignment for multi-site）

```
> DFUP (101,102,103,104),"11XX",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPAS 2,"XX11",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "11XX", (AWG_CNCT)
> PSFC 2
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "XX11", (AWG_CNCT)
```

In this example, the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command defines a utility purpose AWG_CNCT and output states for site 1. The UPAS command defines the output states of AWG_CNCT for site 2. First the settings of site 1 are activated. Then the setup focus is restricted to site 2, and the output states for site 2 are activated.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPST  UPST  -  Utility Purpose STate）

| setting |

The optional parameter specifies the status of the utility lines in the utility purpose.

The status is determined with the following specifiers:

-

0: Sets the output state of the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)

-

1: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to low

-

X (x): No action

Specify the setting values corresponding to the definition order of the utility lines in the specified utility purpose.

If this parameter is omitted, the settings defined by the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） or UPAS commands (depending on the setup focus as set with `PSFC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.191_PSFC__PSFC__-__Parallel_Setup_FoCus.md`）) are set to the utility lines of the specified utility purpose.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of the utility purpose to be set or read.

For the query, you can specify multiple names, which must be separated by a comma.

Specifying the symbol @ returns the definitions of all utility purposes.

   | Note All utility lines that are set with `UTST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.313_UTST__UTST__-__UTility_line_STate.md`） or UPST will be switched in parallel when the `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command is performed. If the `WSDN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.341_WSDN_-__Wait_Setup_DoNe.md`） command is used immediately after FLSH, the time span during which execution will pause equals the longest settling time that is defined for any of the switched utility lines (with `UTTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.314_UTTI__UTTI__-__UTility_line_settling_TIme.md`）) or purposes (with `UPTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.307_UPTI__UPTI__-__Utility_Purpose_settling_TIme.md`）).

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPST  UPST  -  Utility Purpose STate）

```
UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
FLSH
WSDN
UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
```

returns

```
UPST "0110",(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example sets the utility purpose "AWG_CNCT" to the hardware, then reads the state of the utility purpose.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPTD  UPTD  -  UP To Date）

```
UPTD? CONF
```

This example requests if the pin configuration data has been changed since the file was last loaded or saved. If the data has not changed, the response is:

```
UPTD CONF,1
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPTI  UPTI  -  Utility Purpose settling TIme）

| time |

Specifies the wait time to change the utility line status using the `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） commands (in ms).

0 ... 2鈥?47鈥?83.646 [ms]

 |
 | purpose_name |

Specifies the utility purpose name or names for which the settling time is to be set.

The symbol @ is used for all utility purposes.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UPTI  UPTI  -  Utility Purpose settling TIme）

```
UPTI 2.5,(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example sets the settling time of the utility purpose "AWG_CNCT" to 2.5 ms.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTDE -  Unload Test Data Entity）

|

file_name

 |

The specified TDE must belong to the directory specified with the `PTDE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.200_PTDE__PTDE__-__Path_for_Test_Data_Entities.md`） `` command.

 |

ALL

 |

Unloads all test data entities.

Only test data entities belonging to the directory specified with the `PTDE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.200_PTDE__PTDE__-__Path_for_Test_Data_Entities.md`） `` command will be unloaded.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIN  -  UTility line INputs）

```
UTIN?
```

returns:

```
UTIN {data}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIN  -  UTility line INputs）

| data |

This parameter returns a decimal number that you must translate to binary.

Ignore the most significant bit. The other bits give the state of the seven lines.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIN  -  UTility line INputs）

```
UTIN?
```

returns:

```
UTIN 6
```

This example returns a decimal value of 6, which is 0000 0110b.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

```
UTIX? [utility_group]
```

returns

```
UTIX {utility_group}, {value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

|

utility_group

 |

This parameter specifies the utility pogo block.

The pogo block is defined by a three鈥慸igit number. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy single鈥慸igit format 1 ... 8 is also supported, but the query always returns the three鈥慸igit format.

For the query, ALL can be entered to specify all utility blocks.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）.

 |
 |

value

 |

The returned integer word.

This integer word must be translated to binary code to get the state of each utility line in the utility line block specified in the query.

The range is 0 ... 4鈥?94鈥?67鈥?95 for a 4鈥憆ow utility block.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

Assuming that the first 16 utility lines of block 165 are high, then

```
UTIX? 165
```

returns

```
UTIX 165,65535
```

In this example the first 16 utility lines of block 165 were set to 0 by the `UTOT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.311_UTOT__UTOT__-__UTility_line_OuTputs.md`） command and no external device has pulled down any of the utility lines.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

```
UTIX? 165
```

returns

```
UTIX 165,65534
```

In this example the first 16 utility lines of block 165 were either set to FFFEh by UTOT or they were set to FFFFh and an external device has pulled down line 00, or both occurrences have taken place.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

| utility_group |

This parameter specifies the utility pogo block.

The pogo block is defined by a three鈥慸igit number. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy single鈥慸igit format 1 ... 8 is also supported, but the query always returns the three 鈥慸igit format.

For the UTOT? query, the parameter can be set to ALL to specify all utility blocks.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）.

 |
 | mask |

The optional parameter masks the utility lines in the block selected by the utility_group parameter.

Enter a decimal equivalent of a 32 bit binary number (0 ... 4鈥?94鈥?67鈥?95), to mask the required line.

The mask value is defined as follows:

- 1: A bit value of 1 causes the selected line to be programmed to the value specified in the parameter value.
- 0: A bit value of 0 masks the line, that is, the line remains unchanged.

If the mask parameter is not specified, then all the utility lines in the selected block are programmed.

 |
 | value |

This parameter can be entered either as string in the form of a hex word (0 ... FFFF鈥疐FFF), or in the form of an integer word (0 ... 4鈥?94鈥?67鈥?95).

Utility lines are basically low side switches. Therefore, the utility lines are set to the inverse of the binary equivalent of the specified value. For example, let us assume the value is 12. This equals to 1100 in binary, its inverse is 0011. Therefore, the first and the second utility line (URW00 and URW01) will be set to high, while all others on this block are set to low.

You can pulse the output utility lines by entering several hex words one after another (not decimal integers) enclosed in double quotes.

- Thus to produce a single pulse on the sixth line of the second utility pogo block, you would enter: `UTOT 166, "0040, 0000, 0040"`.
- You can use this facility for instance to produce a trigger pulse for a certain measurement.
- The specified hex data is sequentially written to the utility lines.Note Such pulses on the utility lines can in no way be synchronized to the execution of test vectors and are meant to enable you to switch slow devices such as relays. If you need to switch utility lines in synchronism with test vectors you must use the command `UTSC, UTSC? - (UTility line Serial Configuration)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.312_UTSC__UTSC__-__UTility_line_Serial_Configuration.md`） and set up serial control of utility lines as described in `Sequencer-controlled utility lines`（raw: `../../03_Use_cases_and_application_papers/03.09_How_to_set_up_sequencer__ontrolled_utility_lines/03.09.01_Sequencer-controlled_utility_lines.md`）.
 |
 | word |

This is an integer value returned by the system, informing you of the setting of the utility output lines. For each utility block you enter, the system returns a reading.

The query returns the value the utility lines were set to by `UTOT`. Use the `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`） command to read back the actual state of the utility lines.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT 165,16383,12345
```

This code sets the first sixteen utility lines of the first block, except those used for the addressing of EEPROMs related to the DUT interface. These are URW14 and URW15. URW0 to URW13 are set to the inverse of 12345. 12345 in decimal equals 0011000000111001 in binary. Inverted, this is 53190 in decimal or 1100111111000110 in binary. Thus the lines will have these states:

 |

URW00 = low

 |

URW04 = low

 |

URW08 = high

 |

URW12 = low

 |
 |

URW01 = high

 |

URW05 = low

 |

URW09 = high

 |

URW13 = low

 |
 |

URW02 = high

 |

URW06 = high

 |

URW10 = high

 |

URW14 = high

 |
 |

URW03 = low

 |

URW07 = high

 |

URW11 = high

 |

URW15 = high

 |

For the utility lines required to address EEPROMs related to the DUT interface see `Utility lines and DUT board EEPROMs`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.06_Utility_lines_and_DUT_board_EEPROMs.md`）.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT? 165
```

returns:

```
UTOT 165,,12345
```

The query returns the value that was written by UTOT. If you have previously executed Example 1, then the returned value will be the written value, but bits 14 and 15 may be different. This is because these lines retain the values that have been written previously.

Use the `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`） command to read back the actual state of the utility lines.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT 166,65535,"5555,AAAA,0,FFFF"
```

writes the sequence AAAAh, 5555h, FFFFh, 0000h to the first sixteen utility lines of the second utility block.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT? 166
```

returns the last written values. If you have just executed example 3, the result would be:

```
UTOT 166,,65535
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTSC  UTSC  -  UTility line Serial Configuration）

| word |

One unique utility pogo block number or a list enclosed in brackets containing utility pogo blocks separated by commas.

The pogo block or the list of pogo blocks uses three鈥慸igit numbers. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy single鈥慸igit format 1 ... 8 is also supported, but the query always returns the three鈥慸igit format.

 |
 | ALL  | Keyword to use all available utility blocks with the given mode. |
 | mode |

Mode to be applied to a single block or the ganged utility blocks.

Available modes are:

 |
 | RD  | Parallel output (with `UTOT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.311_UTOT__UTOT__-__UTility_line_OuTputs.md`）), parallel input (with `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`）) or serial input (via serial interface pin SOUT), turns ganging on, if off. |
 | RW  | Serial output (via serial interface pin SINP), parallel input (with `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`）) or serial input (via serial interface pin SOUT), turns ganging on, if off. |
 | OFF  | Parallel output (with `UTOT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.311_UTOT__UTOT__-__UTility_line_OuTputs.md`）), parallel input (with `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`）), turns ganging off. |
 | maskMode |

The extra parameter sets the mask mode for the defined utility blocks.

Available modes are:

 |
 | MASK  | Enables the mask mode. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTSC  UTSC  -  UTility line Serial Configuration）

The following example shows how to reset the mode for all utility blocks to static:

```
UTSC ALL, OFF
```

The following example shows how to gang utility blocks 1 to 4 setting the mode to serial out:

```
UTSC (165,166,167,168),RW
```

The following example shows how to change the mode of the previously set up gang to parallel out:

```
UTSC (165,166,167,168),RD
```

The following example, based on the previous setup, will lead to an error, because the fourth utility pogo block is missing:

```
UTSC (165,166,167),OFF
```

The following example shows how to turn off ganging by changing the mode of the previously set up gang to off:

```
UTSC (165,166,167,168),OFF
```

The following example shows how to set up a new gang with the second, third and fourth utility pogo block in serial out mode:

```
UTSC (166,167,168),RW
```

The following example shows how to use the UTSC? query to display the entire gang and the mode if a single utility block of a gang is given:

```
UTSC? 166
```

results in:

```
UTSC (166,167,168),RW
```

The following example shows how to use the UTSC? query to display all gangs and modes of all utility blocks:

```
UTSC? ALL
```

results in:

```
UTSC 1,OFF
UTSC (166,167,168),RW
UTSC 169,OFF
UTSC 170,OFF
UTSC 171,OFF
UTSC 172,OFF
```

The following example shows how to change the existing gang with utility blocks 2 to 4 in serial out mode to the masked mode:

```
UTSC (166,167,168),RW,MASK
```

The following example shows the query result of UTSC? with mask mode set for the second to fourth utility pogo block:

```
UTSC? ALL
```

results in:

```
UTSC 165,OFF
UTSC (166,167,168),RW,MASK
UTSC 169,OFF
UTSC 170,OFF
UTSC 171,OFF
UTSC 172,OFF
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTST  UTST  -  UTility line STate）

| value |

Specifies the output (desired) status of the utility line with the specifier 0 or 1.

- 0: High output
- 1: Low output
 |
 | type |

This parameter is used to specify whether the output (desired) state or the input (actual) state is to be returned. Possible values are:

- w: Returns the output (desired) state.
- r: Returns the input (actual) state

For pure output utility lines, this parameter is ignored.

 |
 | util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names to be set or read.

In the query, specifying @ returns all utility lines.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated by commas.

   | Note All utility lines that are set with UTST or `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） will be switched in parallel when the `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command is performed. If the `WSDN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.341_WSDN_-__Wait_Setup_DoNe.md`） command is used immediately after FLSH, the time span during which execution will pause equals the longest settling time that is defined for any of the switched utility lines (with `UTTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.314_UTTI__UTTI__-__UTility_line_settling_TIme.md`）) or purposes (with `UPTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.307_UPTI__UPTI__-__Utility_Purpose_settling_TIme.md`）).

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTST  UTST  -  UTility line STate）

```
UTST 1,(Filt1,Filt2)
UTST 0,(Filt3,Filt4)
FLSH
WSDN
UTST? w,(Filt1,Filt2,Filt3,Filt4)
```

will return:

```
UTST 1,(Filt1,Filt2)
UTST 0,(Filt3,Filt4)
```

This example sets the utility lines "Filt1" and "Filt2" to high output, and "Filt3" and "Filt4" to low output.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTTI  UTTI  -  UTility line settling TIme）

| time  | Specifies the wait time to change the utility line status using the `UTST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.313_UTST__UTST__-__UTility_line_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command (in ms). |
 | util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names for which the settling time is to be set.

The symbol @ is used for all utility lines.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › UTTI  UTTI  -  UTility line settling TIme）

```
UTTI 2.5,(filter)
```

This example sets the settling time of the utility line "filter" to 2.5 ms.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALC  -  VALid Cycle range）

```
VALC? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VALC {map_state}, {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALC  -  VALid Cycle range）

|

map_state

 |

Returns the current state of the error map. The state can be:

- INVL: Invalid - no error map details are available. (The setup has been changed, but no functional test has been performed.)
- INCS: Inconsistent - the contents of the error map are inconsistent with the current setup.
- CONS: Consistent - a functional test has been performed and the contents of the error map are consistent with the current setup.
 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

The first recorded cycle.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

The number of recorded cycles.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of DC Scale pins. The pins must belong to the same port.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALC  -  VALid Cycle range）

```
> VALC? (dpsPin)
< VALC CONS,0,700,(dpsPin)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALD  -  VALid Data）

```
VALD? {map_id}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VALD {map_state}, {map_id}, {start}, {number}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALD  -  VALid Data）

|

map_id

   | Determines the type of Error Map for which data is to be read out: |
 |

ERRM

 |

The error map option reads the error map.

 |
 |

OVEM

 |

The overview error map option reads the overview error map in FCM mode (defined by DCRM). If the Overview Error Map was in LMAP mode for the last executed test, an error message will be issued.

 |
 |

LMAP

 |

The label map option reads the overview error map in LMAP mode (defined by DCRM). If the overview error map was in FCM mode for the last executed test, an error message will be issued if LMAP is selected.

 Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 |

RECD

 |

The receive data option reads the error map (compatibility with the `ERMP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.114_ERMP__-__ERror_MaP.md`） query). Equivalent to ERRM.

 |
 |

DERR

 |

The per pin detailed error map option reads the detailed error map. Equivalent to ERRM.

 |
 |

EOLY

 |

The errors only map option reads the per pin errors only in the error map. Equivalent to ERRM.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Error map information will only be returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO pin types.

 |
 |

map_state

 |

Returns the current state of the error map. The state can be:

 |
 |

INVL

 |

Invalid is returned if no error map details are available (the setup has been changed, but no functional test has been performed).

 |
 |

INCS

 |

This is returned if the contents of the error map are inconsistent with the current setup.

 |
 |

CONS

 |

This is returned after a functional test has been performed and indicates that the contents of the error map are consistent with the current setup.

 |
 |

start

 |

This is an integer that indicates the first cycle that was recorded, or, for the LMAP option of map_id, the first label call that was recorded. start will be a value between 0 and 2^48.

 |
 |

number

 |

This is an integer that indicates the number of cycles recorded, or for the LMAP option of map_id, the number of label calls recorded. If ERRM, RECD or DERR have been selected, the range for this parameter depends on whether the internal or the external error map is used. For the internal error map, it is 0 to 8191; for the external error map the upper limit can be higher. When EOLY has been selected, the upper limit is 2^48.

For the `Pin Scale 5000 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.04.02_Pin_Scale_5000_card.md`）, the upper limit is 4096.

In the reply, this parameter indicates the number of cycles (or label calls) which have been read. If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALD  -  VALid Data）

```
VALD? ERRM, (Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

returns:

```
VALD CONS, ERRM, 0, 1024, (Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

This example queries the error map and returns data between the cycles of 0 and 1024. The error map data is consistent with the current setup.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALR  -  VALid Range）

```
VALR? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VALR {map_state}, {no_of_results}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALR  -  VALid Range）

|

map_state

 |

Returns the current state of the error map. The state can be:

- INVL: Invalid - no error map details are available. (The setup has been changed, but no functional test has been performed.)
- INCS: Inconsistent - the contents of the error map are inconsistent with the current setup.
- CONS: Consistent - a functional test has been performed and the contents of the error map are consistent with the current setup.
 |
 |

no_of_results

 |

Integer indicating the number of results recorded.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of DC Scale pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VALR  -  VALid Range）

```
> VALR? (dpsPin)
< VALR CONS,10,(dpsPin)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCAT  VCAT  -  VeCtor ATtachment）

|

label_name

 |

The label must be of type MAIN or SVEC.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

In the query, you can specify ALL provided that you also specify @@ for the port parameter. The query will then return the data for all labels of all ports.

 |
 |

port

 |

Specifies the port to which the label belongs. In the query, you can specify @@ in combination with ALL in the first parameter to retrieve the DUT views for all labels of all ports.

 |
 |

attachment_type

 |

Defines the attachment type. Possible values are:

- AreaPatternAttachment, which defines the DUT view of a label for the Pattern Debug tool.
- ScanInstanceAttachment, which describes a scan test instance generated by the STIL Reader or the ASCII Interface.
- MarkerPatternAttachment, defines that synchronization points used with protocols will be specified and add to the sequencer label.
 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The general format of the parameter is as follows:

#Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream

where the decimal digit N defines the number of the decimal digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) which in their turn specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The format of the data stream depends on the attachment type:

 |
 |

AreaPatternAttachment consists of one or more statements in the following format:

logical_vector_nr, list_of_pins_with_associated_formats

In the query, the individual statements are separated by linefeed characters for better readability. The list of pins with associated formats consists of one or more triples

(pinlist), x_mode, selector;

Note that fractional x-modes are coded by negative integers.

 |
 |

ScanInstanceAttachment identifies one or more scan instance definitions in the following format:

first_vector, x_vector, test_type, length, "scan_test_name", "struct_block_name";

where:

 |
 |

first_vector

 |

The logical tester vector within which the scan test instance begins, counted from 0.

 |
 |

X_vector

 |

The X-vector within first_vector at which the scan instance begins, counted from 0.

 |
 |

test_type

 |

scan tests: test_type = 1

functional test: test_type = 0

 |
 |

length

 |

Length of the scan instance, that is, the number of X-vectors. If the command was generated by the ASCII Interface, length equals the template length.

 |
 |

scan_test_name

 |

Name of the scan instance. If the command was generated by the ASCII Interface, the name has the format

<template_name>_<instance_number>

 |
 |

struct_block_name

 |

Name of the active structure block, empty for the default block. The structure block configures the scan chain.

 |
 |

MarkerPatternAttachment defines one or more synchronization markers for a protocol pattern in the following format:

tester_vector, sync_point_name, x_vector, pin_name

where:

 |
 |

tester_vector

 |

The logical tester vector within which the synchronization point is located, counted from 0.

 |
 |

sync_point_name

 |

The name of the synchronization point. To activate the synchronization point, this name must be specified with the setSynchronization() member function of the SYNCHRONIZED_TEST API. See also `Protocol wrapper API`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.172_Protocol_wrapper_API.md`）.

 |
 |

X_vector

 |

The X-vector within tester_vector to which the synchronization marker is assigned.

 |
 |

pin_name

 |

The pin on which the marker is (to be) defined. This information is required if the pins of the specified port (port parameter) are assigned different x-modes in the STATEMAP section of their base wavetable.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCAT  VCAT  -  VeCtor ATtachment）

```
> vcat? "example",(@),"AreaPatternAttachment"
< VCAT "example", (@), "AreaPatternAttachment", #31190,(CP,I1,O1),1,std;
 1,(CP,I1,O1),-3,slow;
 4,(CP,I1,O1),2,fast;
 6,(CP,I1,O1),-3,slow;
 9,(CP,I1,O1),std,1;
```

The pattern of the example comprises 9 vectors (0 through 8). The last line refers to a virtual vector 9 which is needed for internal reasons. This vector need not be specified in the command, it is added internally.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCAT  VCAT  -  VeCtor ATtachment）

```
> VCAT "scan_test",(@),"ScanInstanceAttachment", #2303,0,1,24,"chain_pattern 0","";
```

This example identifies a scan instance in the `scan_test` pattern, which is associated with the default port @. The length of the data stream is 30 bytes. The scan instance starts at the first X-vector of the fourth tester vector, its length is 24 X-vectors, the name of the scan test instance is `chain_pattern 0`, and the default scan structure block is used.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCAT  VCAT  -  VeCtor ATtachment）

```
> VCAT? "myMainLabel", (myPort), "MarkerPatternAttachment"
< VCAT "myMainLabel", (myPort), "MarkerPatternAttachment", #250
 38, mySyncPoint,2,Pin1;
 71, mySecondSyncPoint,1,Pin1;
```

In this example, VCAT has attached two synchronization markers to pin Pin1 of the sequencer label `myMainLabel` at port `myPort`.

The two synchronization markers are `mySyncPoint` which is attached to the tester vector with the logical vector number 38 and `mySecondSyncPoint` which is attached to the vector with the logical vector number 71.

Synchronization takes account of place on the X-vector level. Therefore the specification of a marker contains an offset in X-vectors. If an x4-mode in assumed for the above example, the actual positions of the two markers in terms of X-vectors would be 38*4+2 = 154 and 71*4+1=285, respectively.

As the modification of the pattern is restricted to whole tester vectors the X-vector offset within the marker specification is fixed, but the tester vector offset will be updated if the pattern is modified.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCLK  -  Verify CLocK）

```
VCLK? {waveform_set}, {timing_set}, {period}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VCLK {autocorrect}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCLK  -  Verify CLocK）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter PRM for the primary waveform set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To enter a multi-port specification is only possible if the specification is associated with the default port and if no other ports are configured.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. Enter PRM for the primary timing set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

period

 |

Enter the test system period in ns for which you wish to check whether auto-correction will take place or not. period must be within the maximum and minimum test system periods of the model.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose period you want to check. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ symbol can be used to check all configured pins.

 |
 |

autocorrect

 |

The auto-correction flag returned by the system. It can be:

 |
 |

0

 |

No auto-correction will occur.

 |
 |

1

 |

Auto-correction will occur.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCLK  -  Verify CLocK）

```
VCLK? 1,1,20,(@)
```

This example checks if a period of 20 ns will cause auto-correction to the edge placements in Timing Set 1 of Waveform Set 1 on any pin. If no auto-correction will occur the following string is returned:

```
VCLK 0
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCYC  -  Valid CYCle）

```
VCYC? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VCYC {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {seq_status}, {pin_oper_mode}, {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCYC  -  Valid CYCle）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. The scanning method and the range of values this parameter can take depend on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the label and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the label at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. It is the cycle length from the specified start_cycle to the last cycle resulting from the seq_status specified by a sequencer instruction. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2,147,483,648 (2^31).

 |
 |

seq_status

 |

Returns the sequencer status that was current when the cycle range was generated. The status is expressed on most occasions in the form of the sequencer instruction that was used to generate the vectors in the requested cycle range. Otherwise it is expressed in terms of a sequencer activity. Note that seq_status is not the same as the sequencer state determined by the command `SQST, SQST? - (SeQuencer STate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.241_SQST__SQST__-__SeQuencer_STate.md`）. Sequencer instructions are parameters to `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）. For additional information on sequencer programming see `Vector Setup Commands`（raw: `02.06.07_Vector_Setup_Commands.md`）.

The seq_status parameter is required for the reconstruction of received data. Some of the values it returns signify that vectors are being generated, others inform of sequencer status changes, which can cause some break vectors to be generated.

 |
 |

 |

GENV

 |

This is returned if GENV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range.

 |
 |

 |

SRCV

 |

This is returned if SRCV is the sequencer instruction that generates vectors in the reported cycle range.

For non-source pins the reported cycle range is generated by the parallel vectors exactly the same way as from RPTV. This means that no_of_vectors parallel vectors are repeated for a repeating count (equal to no_of_cycles divided by no_of_vectors) to generate no_of_cycles cycles on the test system.

For source pins the reported cycle range is generated by the vectors stored in the source memory. This means that no_of_cycles vectors are generated from the source memory to produce no_of_cycles cycles on the test system, and the information of no_of_vectors has no meaning to source pins.

 |
 |

 |

RPTV

 |

This is returned if RPTV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range.

You can stop a repeat loop by hitting BREAK in the user interface. The seq_status may then still be RPTV because the BREAK occurs asynchronously to the execution of the loop.

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |

JPPS

 |

This is returned if the parallel vectors for the reported cycles were generated by a per-pin subroutine.

 |
 |

 |

CTIM

 |

This is returned if a change timing instruction has been issued in the queried cycle range. Each timing change generates break vectors.

The real number of break cycles depends on the test system period and will not be shown in the cycle reconstruction.

Between 0 to 7 break cycles will be recorded during a CTIM instruction, the exact number depends on the number of vectors loaded.

 |
 |

 |

CLEV

 |

The CLEV (change levels) parameter indicates that unrecorded break cycles, due to a change of level set, exist in the specified cycle range.

 |
 |

 |

BRK

 |

This is returned if break cycles are being generated during the reported cycle range - for example, if a timed match loop is in progress. Between 0 and 7 break cycles will be recorded.

Additionally, the following sequencer instructions also generate break vectors:

 |
 |

 |

 |

sequencer instruction

 |

 reported as

 |
 |

 |

 |

CTIM

 |

CTIM

 |
 |

 |

 |

CLEV

 |

CLEV

 |
 |

 |

 |

WTER

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

 |

FLQU

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

 |

STOP

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

MTCH

 |

This is returned if

- the test contains a counted match loop,
- the test has been executed online, and
- the last cycle of the match loop is not the last cycle of a 8-cycle block.

In this case the last match loop cycles belonging to this block (up to 7) are recorded in the Error Map and reported by VCYC?. For details see `Adjusting the junctions between match loop and surrounding label`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01.01_Adjusting_the_junctions_between_match_loop_and_surrounding_label.md`）.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included in the query, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to obtain data for all pins.

The response is provided for each pin separately.

 |
 |

pin_oper_mode

 |

Reports the operating mode of each pin in the pin list. This can be:

 |
 |

F160

 |

Specifies Standard operating mode.

 |
 |

F330

 |

Not valid.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Vector data in binary format. The parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the binary data. The data is returned for each pin separately, on a sequencer construct basis (see `Addressing the vector areas`（raw: `02.06.07.01.04_Addressing_the_vector_areas.md`）). The system returns one byte for each cycle and pin. If the requested cycles are break cycles, then no data is returned.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VCYC  -  Valid CYCle）

```
VCYC? 0, 5, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
VCYC 0,5,GENV,F160,(pin1),#9000000005\x0E\x0E\x0E\x0F\x0D\x0A
```

This example returns the physical waveform DC/DC power units in hex notation in the range of 0 to 5 cycles.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

```
VDCG? {waveform_set}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {waveform_set}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

Or:

```
VDCG? {specset_id}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {specset_id}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

Or:

```
VDCG? {wavetable_name}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {wavetable_name}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter PRM for the primary waveform set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

Alternatively, you can enter:

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

With this specifier the command checks that:

- The pins in pinlist have exactly the same device cycle names.
- For each device cycle, each pin defines the device cycle with the same length.
 |
 |

 |

FDC

 |

With this specifier the command checks that the first device cycle in the device cycle definition table for each pin in the pinlist has the same length.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names whose device cycles are to be checked. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured pins.

 |
 | dev_cyc_len  | Always 1 for SmarTest 7.10. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

```
VDCG? 1,ALL,(inputs)
```

returns:

```
VDCG 1,ALL,SLEN
```

This example checks the consistency of all device cycles for pins in the pin group "inputs" in waveform set 1. The test system replies that all device cycles for the specified group are consistently defined.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCN -  Vector Device Cycle Name）

VDCN {vec_No}, {"dev_cyc_name"}, {dev_cyc_len}, {repeat_count}, {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCN -  Vector Device Cycle Name）

|

vec_No

 |

A logical vector number of the selected label. Logical vector numbers count the active vectors of one label. The first active vector of a label has the logical vector number 0 (zero).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

Alternatively, enter FDC for the first device cycle name in the device cycle table.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

Length of the device cycle that is being downloaded.

This is always 1. (For SmarTest 7.10, only 1 waveform per device cycle is possible.)

 |
 |

repeat_count

 |

Determines how many times the device cycle is to be downloaded.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which vectors are to be downloaded. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to download to all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCN -  Vector Device Cycle Name）

```
VDCN 93, "EXAMPL", 1, 15, (@)
```

This example downloads vector data resulting from the default values for the EXAMPL device cycle to all pins, starting at active vector 93. The download is repeated 15 times.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCP  VDCP   Vector Device Cycle Parameter）

|

vec_No

 |

A logical vector number of the selected label. For the command, it determines the first active vector that will be overwritten.

For the query, this parameter specifies the vector at which analysis of the vector area starts (see also the description of the strt_disp parameter below).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

Possible values are:

- The name of a defined device cycle.
- FDC: The first device cycle specifier. It indicates that the first device cycle in the device cycle table for the pins in pinlist is to be taken. If the length of this device cycle is not equal to the length parameter dev_cyc_len, an error is reported in the report window and the pins with this error are not set.

This specifier should be used only if you are working with device cycles consisting of just one test system cycle. The specifier gives you a shortcut to a device cycle name, where all device cycles have the same length (of 1).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

The length of the specified device cycle.

For the query, the length specifies the analyzed range of active vectors, starting at the vector number vec_No. Enter an integer in the range 0 to 256 (see also the description of the disp_length parameter below).

 |
 |

ed_comp

 |

The edit component. This parameter is optional. It specifies which direction parameter (either Dx for drive or EDx for expected data, where x is 1 or 2) is being edited. The direction parameter being edited is fixed, and the system can, if necessary, auto-correct the other direction parameter.

The edit component can take the following values:

- dd1d: Drive data 1, drive value
- dd1z: Drive data 1, high-Z value
- dd2d: Drive data 2, drive value
- dd2z: Drive data 2, high-Z value
- ed1: Expected data 1 value
- ed2: Expected data 2 value

If the edit component is one of dd1d, dd1z, dd2d, or dd2z, then both the DD1 and DD2 parameters are fixed, and the ED1 and ED2 parameters can be auto-corrected to yield a consistent physical waveform sequence.

If the edit component is ed1 or ed2, then the ED1 and ED2 parameters are fixed, and the DD1 and DD2 parameters can be auto-corrected.

If no edit component parameter is specified, then all four direction parameters are fixed.

 |
 |

DD1

DD2

 |

Drive data parameters. They contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values you can define are:

- F00: Drive 0, tri-state off
- F10: Drive 1, tri-state off
- F0Z: Drive 0, tri-state on
- F1Z: Drive 1, tri-state on
- N: Not used. Enter it if you do not want to set a drive data parameter to a drive and tri-state value.
- UC: Unclear. You must not enter this parameter value. The system may return this value as an answer to your query, to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle. This response from the system is possible only if you do not use the Timing Setup to generate your device cycles.

The drive data parameters F0N, F1N, FN0, and FNZ, which set just the drive value or just the tri-state value (as is the case with the WAVE command), cannot be used here

 |
 |

ED1

ED2

 |

Expected data parameters. The values you can define are:

- F0: Compare to 0
- F1: Compare to 1
- FI: Compare to intermediate
- FX: Compare to mask
- FU: Compare to unstable
- N: Not used. Enter it if you do not want to set an expected data parameter to a compare value.
- UC: Unclear. You must not enter this parameter value. The system may return this value as an answer to your query, to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle. This response from the system is possible only if you do not use the Timing Setup to generate your device cycles.
 |
 |

strt_disp

 |

This parameter defines the offset of your range of interest from vec_No. The actual display starts with the last device cycle that does not begin before vec_No and does not end before vec_No + strt_disp.

The purpose of this construction is to enable a correct device cycle reconstruction even if the first vector you are interested in does not lie at a device cycle boundary (a device cycle can span up to 16 vectors).

 |
 |

disp_length

 |

Specifies the display length in vectors. This parameter determines the end of your range of interest. The actual display ends with the last device cycle that starts before vec_No + strt_disp + disp_length.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which a vector data transfer is to be made. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. Pins that do not belong to the port of the label are ignored.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VDCP  VDCP   Vector Device Cycle Parameter）

```
> VDCP? 0,8,0,8,(S0_1)
< VDCP 0,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 1,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 2,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 3,"MYDC",2,,F00,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 5,"MYDC",2,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
> VDCP? 2,6,4,2,(S0_1)
< VDCP 5,"MYDC",2,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
```

In the second call of VDCP? (the first call just serves to display the underlying situation) the range of interest starts at vector 6. Note that the reply starts with vector 5, and that the first occurrence of MYDC, which lies between vector 2 and vector 6, is not displayed.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VECC  VECC  -  VECtor download Compressed）

```
VECC? PARA,ALL,0,,(S0)
```

returns:

```
size: 21
data:
VECC PARA,ALL,0,,(S0)\x0A
size: 75
data:
VECD PARA,SM,0,56,(S0),#9000000016\x02Ee\x80\x02Ee\x814VX\x13Eu\x90\x00\x0A
status: 0
```

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VECD  VECD  -  VECtor Download）

```
> VECD? PARA,SM,0,16,(OUT1)
< VECD PARA,SM,0,16,(OUT1),#9000000024\x0E\x0C\x0E\x0E\x0D\x0E\x0E\x0D\x0E\x0E\x0E\x0E
  \x0C\x0D\x0E\x0E
```

This example shows the answer as it is recorded in the MCDLog.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VNEC  -  Valid Number of Executed Cycles）

```
VNEC? {site_sel}, {value_format}, {(pin)}
```

Returns:

```
VNEC {site_sel}, {(pin)}, {value_data}
```

Parameters
 | site_sel  | Select sites. It can be a string of 1's and 0's; or "ALL" to specify all sites. The response is a string of 1's and 0's. |
 | value_format |

Specify a data format. It can be ASC or BIN.

SmarTest 7.5.0 supports the ASC mode only.

 |
 | pin  | Specify a pin. Only one pin is supported. It can be any pin that has been configured to I, O, IO, DC, and DPS types. |
 | value_data  | Hold the returned cycle numbers in ASCII format. The ASCII data consists of a list of cycle numbers separated by comma. Each cycle number is for each active and requested site. |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VNEC  -  Valid Number of Executed Cycles）

```
VNEC? ALL, ASC, ("pin1")
```

Returns:

```
VNEC "11",("pin1"),#138,8
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VPAR  -  Vectors in PARallel）

```
VPAR? {start_vec_No}, {stop_vec_No}
```

returns:

```
VPAR {cmd_No}, [frst_used_vec]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VPAR  -  Vectors in PARallel）

|

start_vec_No

 |

Defines the offset of the first vector to be searched from the start vector of the currently selected label. The specified address must not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

stop_vec_No

 |

Defines the last vector in the search range. The specified address must not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

cmd_No

 |

In the reply, the number of the command within the sequencer area, or NISQ - see below.

 |
 |

frst_used_vec

 |

Returns the logical address of the first vector affected by the sequencer instruction.

 |

NISQ (Non-Interpretable SeQuence) indicates that the sequencer program does not respect its context conditions. This means, there is non-linear use of vectors, or there are partial "Match Begin" or "Match End" sequences (for example a WTER without its MBGN, a MJPE without its MEND - see the SQPG command). The label is no longer displayable by the Vector Setup in this case. No frst_used_vec parameter is returned when the parameter cmd_No is NISQ.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VPAR  -  Vectors in PARallel）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,10,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> VPAR? 0,15
< VPAR 0,0
< VPAR 1,0
< VPAR 2,0
< VPAR 3,10
```

This example displays the sequencer instructions of the selected label before calling VPAR? in order to make its reply understandable.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VRCS  -  Valid ReConStruction）

```
VRCS? {reconstr_type}, [reconstr_cond,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VRCS [reconstr_cond,] {reconstr_state}, [reconstr_oper,] {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

reconstr_type

 |

The reconstruction type determines how test cycles are counted.

 |
 |

STRT

 |

Start analysis. Specifies that cycles are counted from the start of the test.

 |
 |

STOP

 |

Stop analysis. Specifies that cycles are counted from the end of the test.

 |
 |

reconstr_cond

 |

The reconstruction condition defines how VRCS? reacts to ambiguous sequencer instructions, that is, instructions that may generate a varying number of cycles from one test execution to the next. Examples for such instructions are JMPE or multiple counted match loops.

 |
 |

 |

STRD

 |

Reconstruction stops at the first ambiguous instruction. The result may be incomplete, but is reliable.

 |
 |

 |

FULL

 |

Reconstruction continues even if ambiguous instructions are present. The maximum possible number of cycles is assumed for the ambiguous instructions. The result may be complete, but possible not completely reliable.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. pinlist can include pins configured as I, O and IO types.

 |
 |

reconstr_state

 |

This parameter returns the state of the reconstruction.

 |
 |

 |

INVL

 |

If INVL is returned, no valid cycles exist. This occurs if you have hit BREAK before any vectors are generated.

 |
 |

 |

PRED

 |

If PRED is returned, all returned values are predicted (a change to the setup has been made, but a test has not yet been executed).

 |
 |

 |

REAL

 |

If REAL is returned, all values given are values from the last executed test.

 |
 |

reconstr_oper

 |

OKAY

 |

The reconstruction was successful, no problems encountered.

 |
 |

 |

MMRV

 |

Multiple Matchloop Restriction Violation:

The reconstruction stopped at the first match loop because there are multiple match loops in the pattern, and the match loop execution counter, which is needed for the reconstruction, can only hold the count from the last match loop execution.

 |
 |

 |

JMPE

 |

The reconstruction stopped at a jump on error instruction because execution path of the sequencer is unknown (for example, whether the jump was taken or not).

 |
 |

 |

RETC

 |

The reconstruction stopped at a return conditional instruction because execution path of the sequencer is unknown (for example, whether the jump was taken or not).

 Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 |

 |

ABRT

 |

The pattern was empty or there was an unspecified problem during the reconstruction.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

The start cycle is an integer which identifies the first cycle for which results exist.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This parameter is an integer which defines the total number of valid cycles.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VRCS  -  Valid ReConStruction）

```
VRCS? STRT, (@)
```

returns:

```
VRCS? REAL, 0, 437621, (@)
```

This example queries the number of reconstructed cycles, counting the cycles from the start of the test. The system replies that 437,621 cycles, starting from zero have been reconstructed, based on the last performed test.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VTIM  -  Verify TIMing）

```
VTIM? {waveform_set},{timing_set},{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VTIM {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VTIM  -  Verify TIMing）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Specifies the timing sets to be checked. Enter PRM for the Primary Timing Set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）.

In a multi-port setup, the check is performed for those pins from pinlist that belong to the same port. If you specify a number, a timing set with this number must be present in every equation set that is associated with a port of the multi-port specification.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be checked. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to check all configured pins.

In a multi-port setup, the pins can belong to more than one port. Only those pins are considered that belong to one of the ports of the specification.

 |
 |

status

 |

The system returns:

 |
 |

0

 |

The timing is not the same.

 |
 |

1

 |

The timing is the same.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VTIM  -  Verify TIMing）

The following example illustrates the working of VTIM? in a multi-port setup. The pins S1_1 and DS0_1 belong to the same port, and S1_2 belongs to another one.

```
> ETDS? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",1,,"d1:0 d2:30",(S1_1,DS0_1)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",2,,"d1:0 d2:12",(S1_1)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",2,,"d1:1 d2:12",(DS0_1)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",1,,"d1:-0.67 d2:1.33 d3:9.3",(S1_2)
```

This call of `ETDS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.117_ETDS__ETDS__-__Edge_Timing_Definition_String.md`） shows that the edge timings of S1_1 and DS0_1 are the same in timing set 1, but not in timing set 2 of the port to which these pins belong.

```
> PCLK? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",1,50,(S1_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",2,20,(S1_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",1,50,(DS0_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",2,20,(DS0_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",1,16.667,(S1_2)
```

This call of `PCLK?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.175_PCLK__PCLK__-__Pin_CLocK.md`） shows that the periods of S1_1 and DS0_1 are the same in the two timing sets of the port.

```
> VTIM? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< VTIM 0
```

VTIM? returns 0 because of the different timings for S1_1 and DS0_1 in timing set 2.

```
> ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",2,,"d1:0 d2:12",(DS0_1)
> VTIM? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< VTIM 1
```

After changing the edge timing of DS0_1 in timing set 2 to the values of S1_1 with a call of `ETDS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.117_ETDS__ETDS__-__Edge_Timing_Definition_String.md`）, VTIM? returns 1 although DS0_1 has a different timing in timing set 1 and in timing set 2, and S1_2, which belongs to another port, has different values altogether.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VWFG  -  Verify WaveForms in Groups）

There are three different ways to call VWFG?:

```
VWFG? {waveform_set}, ["dev_cyc_name"], {(pinlist)}
VWFG? {specset_id},["dev_cyc_name"],{(pinlist)}
VWFG? {wavetable_name}, ["dev_cyc_name"], {(pinlist)}
```

All three forms return:

```
VWFG {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VWFG  -  Verify WaveForms in Groups）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

If you specify the name of a device cycle, only this device cycle will be checked. Enter ALL for all device cycle names in the device cycle table.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose definitions you want to check. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to check all configured pins.

 |
 |

status

 |

The system returns:

0: The definitions are not the same.

1: The definitions are the same.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VWFG  -  Verify WaveForms in Groups）

```
> VWFG? "spec_search_wtb","SBC",(ser_in)
< VWFG 1
> VWFG? "spec_search_wtb",,(ser_in)
< VWFG 0
```

According to this example, the waveform and device cycle definition for device cycle SBC are the same for the pins in the group ser_in within the wavetable spec_search_wtb, but this does not hold for all device cycles that are defined for the pins of this group.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VWFS  -  Verify WaveForm Sets）

```
VWFS? {waveform_set_1},{waveform_set_2},{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VWFS {status}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VWFS  -  Verify WaveForm Sets）

|

waveform_set_x

 |

Waveform set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which you wish to check waveform set compatibility. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to check all configured pins.

 |
 |

status

 |

The system returns:

 |
 |

 |

0

 |

The waveform sets are not compatible.

 |
 |

 |

1

 |

The waveform sets are compatible.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › VWFS  -  Verify WaveForm Sets）

```
VWFS? 1,2,(DATA)
```

This example checks whether waveform sets 1 and 2 are the same for the pins in the group DATA. If they are the same the following string is returned:

```
VWFS 1,(DATA)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › WAIT -  WAIT）

```
WAIT {time}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › WAIT -  WAIT）

|

time

 |

Enter a time in 碌s.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › WAIT -  WAIT）

```
RLYC DC,PMU,(outputs); WAIT 1000; FTST?
```

This example causes the MCD to wait 1 ms (1000 碌s) for the PMU relay to close before executing a functional test.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › WAVE  WAVE  -  WAVEform）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveforms set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed by double quotes.

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To change or query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

wfIndex

 |

Logical waveform index. This index identifies the logical waveform for which a physical waveform is to be created. The values specified for the DD1, DD2, ED1, and ED2 parameters must be in accordance with the format of this logical waveform.

 |
 |

DD1 and DD2

 |

First and second drive data parameter. These are optional parameters and contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values you can define are:

 |
 |

F0N

 |

drive 0

 |
 |

F1N

 |

drive 1

 |
 |

FN0

 |

tri-state off

 |
 |

FNZ

 |

tri-state on

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

ED1 and ED2

 |

First and second receive data parameter. These are optional parameters. The values you can define are:

 |
 |

F0

 |

compare to 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

compare to 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

compare to intermediate

 |
 |

FX

 |

compare to mask

 |
 |

FU

 |

compare to unstable

 |
 |

C

 |

capture digital data

 |
 |

D

 |

do not capture digital data

 |
 |

The values C and D are used for selective digital capture. The following rules apply to these values:

- A waveform that is used for selective digital capture cannot contain more than one compare action. Therefore, if you specify C or D for one of ED1 or ED2, you cannot specify a value for the other Expected Data parameter.
