### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › OPT  -  hardware OPTions）

```
*OPT?
```

returns:

```
*OPT {`hardware_type`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_hardware_type`）}, {`board_no`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_board_no`）}, {`board_type`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_board_type`）}, {`board_id`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_board_id`）}, `[phys_location`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_phys_location`）], `[clk_board`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_clk_board`）], `[chan_1_info_1`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_chan_x_info_y`）], [chan_1_info_2], ... [chan_16_info_1], [chan_16_info_2]
```

Parameters
 | hardware_type  | Returns type of the test head:

- PS_2CC or CS_2CC

  - Compact test head containing two card cages.

- PS_4CC or CS_4CC

  - Small test head containing four card cages.

- PS_8CC or CS_8CC

  - Large test head containing eight card cages.

- JN_S

  - 256 pin test head (MCU)

 |
 | board_no  | Returns the position of the installed card or the logical board number:

- The position of the card is determined by the slot in which the card is installed.
The following ranges are applicable for board_no:

- Control board:

  - Control segment number; two digits (CS); 1 to 16

- Clock board:

  - Board number of the clock board; two digits (CSCLK): 11, 12, 21, 22, ..., 41, 42

- Pin Scale 1600 channel cards and all DC Scale cards:

  - Board number (physical or virtual pogo block number) of the logical board; triple digit; range for physical pogo blocks 101 to 132, 201 to 232, 301 to 332, and 401 to 432.

- PPS modules:

  - Board number (pogo block number or slot number) of the PPS module; triple digit; range 101 to 132 and 201 to 232

- DPS cards:

  - DPS card number (DPS pogo block number) of the DPS card; single digit; 1 to 8

 |
 | board_type |

Returns the type of board or card. This may be:

- CNTR: Control board
- CLK: Clock board
- CPIO: Channel card - Pin Scale 1600
- JNIO: Channel board - MCU
- PPS: Precision Parallel Source
- HVP: High-Voltage PMU
- SWA: Switch matrix

DPS-slot device power supplies:

- SE-UDPS: Internal Utility Power Supply

DC Scale cards:

- DPS128HC: DC Scale DPS128/64-HC
- UHC4T: DC Scale UHC4T
- XPS256 DC Scale XPS256
 |
 | board_id |

As defined in the file /opt/hp93000/soc/pws/data/board_ids.

 |
 | phys_location |

Returns the physical location of the board. Format: TCSS.

- T: Test head (Always 1 for V93000 systems)
- C: Card cage; single digit; range 1 to 8
- SS: Slot in the card cage; two digits; range 01 to 14.

For details on the mapping of card slots see Mapping of physical resources.

 |
 | clk_board  | Board number of the clock board in the card cage to which the board belongs. |
 | chan_x_info_y |

Channel information. For each channel on the board, the system can return two terms: chan_x_info_1 and chan_x_info_2, where x is the channel number in the range 1 to 16 decimal.

- Digital channels

  - chan_x_info_1: For each of the 16 channels on the channel card, chan_x_info_1 returns the sequencer memory (SM) depth in blocks of 128K vectors (or 0.125M vectors).
  - chan_x_info_2: For each of the 16 channels on the channel card, chan_x_info_2 returns the vector memory (VM) depth in blocks of 128K vectors (or 0.125M vectors).

- Fast differential channels

chan_x_info_1:

I: Input channel

O: Output channel

- PPS channels

  - chan_x_info_1: Returns the size of installed pattern memory in blocks of 1K words (16 bit).

- HVP channels

  - chan_x_info_1: Returns the size of installed DAC/ADC RAM in blocks of 1K words (16 bit).

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › OPT  -  hardware OPTions）

```
> *OPT?
< *OPT JN_S,1,CNTR,254,1100,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
< *OPT JN_S,11,CLK,254,1115,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
< *OPT JN_S,101,JNIO,254,1102,11,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,
< *OPT JN_S,102,JNIO,254,1102,11,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,
```

The reply from the *OPT? query has been generated in offline mode. The board IDs are set to 254.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RST -  ReSeT）

```
*RST [type]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RST -  ReSeT）

|

type

 |

not used

 |

- Enforces a disconnect (AC relay is open)
- All DPS sets, except the default set, will be deleted.
- All resources (for example objects defined with RDEF) will be deleted
- All pin definitions (for example pins defined with DFAN) will be deleted.
- All instruments will be deleted from the instrument registry and recreated.
- The instrument will have its reset bit toggled.
- The instrument will be set to its default state.
 |
 |

 SWR

 |

- All resources will be deleted
- All pin definitions will be deleted.
- The instrument will have its reset bit toggled.
- The instrument will be set to its default state.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands in alphabetical order › List of commands › RST -  ReSeT）

```
*RST
```

Resets the software and the hardware.

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › Concepts of Configuration setup › Defining pin groups）

The following example contains both fixed and expression based pin group definitions:

```
> DFGP X,(SI1,SI2,SO1,SO2),(SCAN)
> DFGP O,(O1,SO1,SO2),(OUT)
> DFGE O,"SCAN * OUT",(SCAN_OUT)
> DFGE? (SCAN_OUT)
< DFGE O,"SCAN * OUT",(SCAN_OUT)
> DFGP? (SCAN_OUT)
< DFGP O,(SO1,SO2),(SCAN_OUT)
```

The DFGE command defines SCAN_OUT as the intersection of SCAN and OUT.

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › Concepts of Configuration setup › Defining ports）

See the `DFPT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.66_DFPT__DFPT__-__DeFine_PorT.md`） command.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CHIN  -  CHannel INformation）

```
CHIN? {channel_nr|ALL}
```

returns:

CHIN {channel_nr}, {channel_type}, [phys_location], {board_no}, [clk_board], [chan_info_1], [chan_info_2]

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CHIN  -  CHannel INformation）

|

channel_nr

 |

The number that identifies the channel.

Specify ALL if you want information about all channels.

For a digital channel, specify it with the test system channel number, which is five digits (see `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name) for the number)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`）.

For a DPS channel, specify it with the test system channel number, which is two digits (see `DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） for the number).

 |
 |

channel_type

 |

Returns the type of the channel. It can be:

 |
 |

CPIO

 |

Pin Scale 1600 digital channel

 |
 | PYIO  | Pin Scale 5000 digital channel |
 |

WZ_FDIFF_I

 |

Fast differential input channel

 |
 |

WZ_FDIFF_O

 |

Fast differential output channel

 |
 |

PPS

 |

Precision Parallel Source channel

 |
 |

HVP

 |

High Voltage PMU

 |
 |

DPS128HC

 |

DC Scale DPS128-HC or DPS64-HC

 |
 | XPS256  | DC Scale XPS256 |
 |  UHC4T  | DC Scale UHC4T |
 |

phys_location

 |

The channel's physical location.

NOTE: For PS1600 and DPS128 SmarTest returns always "-1"!

This format is TCSSPP.

Where:

 |
 |

T

 |

test head (1)

 |
 |

C

 |

card cage (1 - 8)

 |
 |

SS

 |

slot (01 - 18) in the card cage

 |
 |

PP

 |

hardware pin number of the digital channel

For DPS, this is the channel number in the DPS board.

 |
 |

board_no

 |

Board number of the board to which the channel belongs. For the DPS, this is the DPS board number. For details, see the board_no parameter in `*OPT? - (hardware OPTions)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md`）.

 |
 |

clk_board

 |

Board number of the clock board in the card cage to which the channel belongs.

 |
 |

chan_info_1

 |

First information of the channel.

 |
 |

For digital channels:

Sequencer memory (SM) depth in blocks of 128k vectors (or 0.125M vectors).

DC Scale DPS channels behave like a digital channel and return the sequencer memory depth.

 |
 |

For PPS channels:

Pattern memory depth in blocks of 1k words (16 bit).

 |
 |

For HVP channels:

DAC/ADC RAM depth in blocks of 1k words (16 bit).

 |
 |

chan_info_2

 |

Second information of the channel.

 |
 |

For digital channels:

Sequencer memory (SM) depth in blocks of 128k vectors (or 0.125M vectors).

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CHIN  -  CHannel INformation）

```
CHIN? 10901
```

returns:

```
CHIN 10901,PSIO,120601,109,21,512,0
```

```
CHIN? ALL
```

  Return (for example):

```
CHIN 10101,PYIO,110301,101,11,3551,0
CHIN 10102,PYIO,110302,101,11,3551,0

CHIN 21701,DPS128HC,-1,217,31,191,0
CHIN 21702,DPS128HC,-1,217,31,191,0

```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CONF  CONF  -  CONFiguration）

| context |

This extra parameter specifies a mode context. If it is omitted, the default mode context DEFAULT is set or read. If DEFAULT is the only context defined, the parameter is omitted in the query reply.

The default mode context is predefined. All other mode contexts must be defined with the CTXT command.

If you specify ALL in the query, CONF? will display all mode contexts.

 |
 | pin_type |

The mandatory parameter assigns channel resources to the pin. This can be:

 | I  | Configures a drive pin. |
 | O  | Configures a receive pin. |
 | IO  | Configures a bidirectional pin. |
 | DC |

Configures a pin for DC measurements. The pin is only connected to the PMU, and no driver or receiver resources are allocated to it.

For DC Scale channels (power or signal pins) the mode is always DC.

This option is not allowed for Smart Scale pins.

 |
 | OFF  | The pin is not available for measurements.  | |
 |

pin_oper_mode

 |

The mandatory parameter defines or indicates the operating mode of the pins in pinlist. The operation mode can be:

 | DCSIGNAL  | In the query this indicates that the pin is associated with a DC Scale channel and has been configured in PMU mode with DFPN. |
 | POWER  | In the query this indicates that the pin is associated with a DC Scale channel and has been configured in DPS mode with DFPS. |
 | CMON  | Configures the pin as current monitor output. For more information, refer to `XPS256 current monitor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.03.02_XPS256_current_monitor.md`）. |
 | F160 |

Specifies Standard operating mode. This is the default. It must be selected for pins on PS1600 boards.

 |
 | F330  | Not valid. |
 | FAST |

This operation mode must be selected for fast pins. Note that no pin can be set to FAST in the default mode context DEFAULT, and that no IO pin can be set to FAST.

For Smart Scale pins this mode will be mapped to F160.

   | |
 | pinlist |

The name of the pin or pins to be configured or listed. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

The symbol @ can be used in the query to list all pins that were previously either explicitly configured with the CONF command, or (in the case of DC Scale pins) implicitly with the DFPN or DFPS command.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CONF  CONF  -  CONFiguration）

```
> CONF IO,F160,(D0,D1)
```

This example configures pins `D0` and `D1` as bidirectional pins operating in Standard Mode for the default mode context.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CONF  CONF  -  CONFiguration）

```
> CONF? (sdd,vdd)
< CONF DC,DCSIGNAL,(sdd)
< CONF DC,POWER,(vdd)
```

This example queries the DC Scale channels `sdd` and `vdd`, which were set with `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） to PMU mode (`DCSIGNAL`) and with `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） to DPS mode (`POWER`), respectively.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CTXT  CTXT  -  ConTeXT）

|

action

 |

Specifies the action. Possible values are:

 |
 |

DEFINE

 |

Defines a new mode context

 |
 |

DELETE

 |

Deletes a mode context

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Displays all existing mode contexts (only in the query).

 |
 |

name

 |

The name of the mode context. If the action parameter is set to DELETE, you can also specify ALL to delete all mode contexts.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › CTXT  CTXT  -  ConTeXT）

```
> CTXT? ALL
< CTXT DEFINE,"DEFAULT"
< CTXT DEFINE,"differential"
< CTXT DEFINE,"PdrvNPrcv"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFGE  DFGE  -  DeFine Group by Expressions）

|

group_type

 |

Defines the type of pins in the group. This can be:

 |
 |

I

 |

Identifies a group of device input pins.

 |
 |

O

 |

Identifies a group of device output pins.

 |
 |

IO

 |

Identifies a group of bidirectional pins.

 |
 |

DC

 |

Identifies a group of DC type pins.

 |
 |

group_expression

 |

The expression that describes the pins to be included in the group. The expression must be built up from pin or pin group names which serve as arguments for the following operators:

 |
 |

 |

+

 |

returns the union of its arguments, that is, all pins that are contained in one of its arguments.

 |
 |

 |

*

 |

returns the intersection of its arguments, that is, all pins that are contained in both of its arguments.

 |
 |

 |

-

 |

returns the difference of its arguments, that is, all pins that are contained in the first argument, but not in the second.

 |
 |

 |

You can also use parentheses to force a certain processing order.

 |
 |

pin_group

 |

The name assigned to the pin group. You can use the same name for groups of different type.

The symbol @ can be used with the DFGE? query to list all groups previously defined using the DFGP and DFGE command. If you query a non-existent group, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFGE  DFGE  -  DeFine Group by Expressions）

```
> DFGP? (SCAN)
< DFGP X,(SI1,SI2,SO1,SO2),(SCAN)
> DFGP? (OUT)
< DFGP O,(O1,SO1,SO2),(OUT)
> DFGE O,"SCAN * OUT",(SCAN_OUT)
> DFGE? (SCAN_OUT)
< DFGE O,"SCAN * OUT",(SCAN_OUT)
> DFGP? (SCAN_OUT)
< DFGP O,(SO1,SO2),(SCAN_OUT)
```

This example defines a group called SCAN_OUT which contains the pins that occur both in pin groups OUT and SCAN. Note that you must use the DFGP? query to display the pins of SCAN_OUT. DFGE? returns the group definition.

The same result would be obtained with the definition

```
> DFGE O,"OUT - O1",(SCAN_OUT)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFGP  DFGP  -  DeFine GrouP）

|

pin_type

 |

Defines the type of pins in the group. This can be:

 |
 |

I

 |

Identifies a group of device input pins.

 |
 |

O

 |

Identifies a group of device output pins.

 |
 |

DC

 |

Identifies a group of DC type pins.

 |
 |

X

 |

Identifies a group that may contain pins of any type.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The names of the pins to be included in the group. All pin names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

pin_group

 |

The name assigned to the pin group. You can use the same name for groups of different type.

The symbol @ can be used with the DFGP? query to list all groups previously defined using the DFGP command. If you query a non-existent group, the system returns nothing.

Maximum number of characters is 16 for 32-bit SmarTest and 64 for 64-bit SmarTest.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFGP  DFGP  -  DeFine GrouP）

```
DFGP O,(Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3),(outputs)
```

This example defines a group called outputs which contains pins Q0, Q1, Q2 and Q3.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

| resourceSpecifier |

The extra parameter specifies the resource to be set or queried.

The following resources are supported:

 | Resource specifier  | Description |
 | VIL and VIH  | Input (drive) voltage definition for I and I/O pins. |
 | VIHH  | High voltage level definition for I and I/O pins. |
 | VOL and VOH  | Output threshold voltage definition for O and I/O pins. |
 | VOL_DIFF and VOH_DIFF  | Output threshold voltage definition for O and I/O pins in differential mode. |
 | VT  | Termination voltage definition. |
 | VCOM  | Commutation voltage of the active load. |
 | REC_SWING  | The receiver swing for a differential comparator. |
 | REC_OFFSET  | The receiver offset for a differential comparator. |
 | ALL  | Keyword ALL selects all resources.  | |
 | mode |

The extra parameter specifies for which operation mode parameter value should be applied or queried.

Supported operation modes:

- STD
- ALL

Keyword ALL selects all operating modes.

Extra parameter resourceSpecifier must also be defined if mode is specified.

If the parameter is not defined, mode STD is taken as default value. In this case the specified value is applied to STD values only and default values used in STDDIFF mode will not be affected.

Note: There is an exception when setting parameter value to RESET. In this case, an omitted mode parameter will be counted as ALL.

 |
 | value |

The mandatory parameter defines the default value for the selected resource and operating mode.

 This parameter is to be defined as

- voltage (in mV) or
- as keyword RESET.

With the parameter set to RESET, the affected values will be set to the system-defined default values of the selected cmos or ecl device technology.

 |

### Example 1: Resource and mode specified（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV VIL,STD,100

```

This example sets the default value for the VIL resource in STD mode to 100 mV. Other default values are not modified.

### Example 2: Resource specified, mode omitted（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV VIL,100
DFLV VIH,200
```

This example sets the default value for the VIL resource to 100 mV, and VIH to 200 mV. As no operating mode is specified, the values are applied only for the STD mode.

### Example 3: Reset single resource（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV VIL, RESET
```

Sets the default value for the VIL resources to the technology defined default value for all operating modes. This overwrites potential user-defined values by the initial system value.

### Example 4: Reset all default values to the technology defined values and query all values（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFLV  DFLV  -  DeFaultLeVel）

```
DFLV RESET
DFLV? ALL, ALL
```

returns

```
DFLV VIL,STD,2250
DFLV VIH,STD,2500
DFLV VIHH,STD,0
DFLV VOL,STD,2250
DFLV VOH,STD,2500
DFLV VOL_DIFF,STD,0
DFLV VOH_DIFF,STD,0
DFLV VT,STD,2500
DFLV VCOM,STD,2500
DFLV REC_OFFSET,STD,1200
DFLV REC_SWING,STD,3200
```

for the cmos technology.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPC  DFPC  -  DeFine Pin Comment）

|

pin

 |

In the command, this is the pin to which a comment is to be added. In the query reply, it is the pin whose comment is returned.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

A query parameter that specifies the pins for which the comments are to be returned. You can also specify @ for all configured pins.

Pins for which no comments have been defined are ignored.

 |
 |

comment

 |

The comment to the pin. The maximal length of the comment string is 2048 characters.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPC  DFPC  -  DeFine Pin Comment）

```
> DFPC (pin1), "This is a comment to pin1"
> DFPC? (pin1,pin2)
< DFPC (pin1), "This is a comment to pin1"
```

Since no comment has been defined for pin `pin2`, it is ignored in the reply.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPN  DFPN  -  DeFine Pin Name）

|

connectionSet

 |

This parameter is currently not used.

This extra string parameter adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC Scale channel in PMU mode. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as single pin or in ganging groups. Note: The documentation for supported DC Scale cards knows this feature also as "Ganging on the fly".

Default connection set: The default connection set is defined if this extra parameter is not used or if an empty string is programmed. A DC Scale pin can be defined in only one default connection set.

All traces that are needed for a cross-card ganging group and are defined by the `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`） command and the DFPN command must have the same connectionSet defined. Recommendation: If the DUT trace can be activated by utility lines, name it like the utility line (see DFUP command).

There can be several pin definitions containing the same channel:

Adding a different ganging combination (new pin), does not invalidate the setups for the existing pins.

The different pins containing the same channel must be part of the same ports.

The patterns, events and DC-setups of these pins do not overlap.

 |
 | channelNo_1 |

The test system channel number of the channel to which the specified device pin is connected (five digits), or the utility block number of the specified card cage (three digit).

Digital or DC Scale channel

For a digital channel this is a five digit number. The first three digits specify the pogo block number, and the fourth and fifth digits specify the pin number in the pogo block. The first digit is 1 to 4, the second and third digits is 01 to 32, and the final two digits is 01 to 16. For example, 10105 is the digital channel whose pogo pin number is 05 in the pogo block 101.

Each pogo block contains 16 digital channels. The pogo block numbers are determined by the slots in which the channel boards are installed.

The first three digits are also called the board number of the logical channel board, and the last two digits are a channel number in the logical channel board, where each logical channel board contains 16 channels

Utility DC channel

For the utility DC pins, this is a three digit number, specifying the utility block of the card cage. The referenced utility pogo must be one which can be connected to the DC rail of the card-cage. To get the utility block number, add 164 (264 for the second utility line card on EXA Scale test systems) to the desired utility line block, such that for example utility block 4 has number 168. For compatibility with SmarTest 7.6x, "HPMU1" now maps to "UTIDC165" and so on (for Smart Scale test systems only).

For more information, see subtopics in `Pogo pin assignment - Utility pogo blocks`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08_Pogo_pin_assignment_-_Utility_pogo_blocks.md`）.

The hardware knows 4 Utility DC channels (pogo pins): DC-force, DC-sense, ground-sense, and guard. But because they are referenced as a group, one pin name is sufficient to reflect all 4 channels.

 |
 |

DC_channel_list

 |

You can define ganging for a set of DC Scale channels in PMU mode by specifying a list of DC Scale channels, separated by commas and enclosed by parentheses. The channels must be physically adjacent on the same board.

Before cross-card ganging can be used, the connection must be enabled by command `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`）.

 |
 |

pinNo

 |

This is the device pin number which is allocated to the specified channel. The number must be enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

pinName

 |

The name to be allocated to the pin. Maximum number of characters is 16 for 32-bit SmarTest and 64 for 64-bit SmarTest.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This query parameter specifies the pins whose definitions are to be retrieved. The symbol @ can be used with the DFPN? query to list all pins previously defined by the DFPN command. If a list of more than one pin is required, the pin names must be separated by a comma. If you query a non-existent pin, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPN  DFPN  -  DeFine Pin Name）

```
> DFPN 10101,"1",(Clock)
> DFPN 10102,"2",(D0)
> DFPN? (@)
< DFPN 10101,"1",(Clock)
< DFPN 10102,"2",(CD0)
```

The above example allocates the `Clock` pin to channel 10101 and allocates pin `D0` to channel 10102, and then queries these definitions. The device pin numbers allocated are 1 and 2 respectively.

```
DFPN (11901, 11902),,(vee)
```

This example defines ganging for DC Scale channels in PMU mode.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

|

dps_channel

 |

The test system channel number of the DPS channel to be configured.

The channel is to be defined as follows:

- For `external device power supplies`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.06_External_device_power_supply__external_GPIB_DPS.md`）, this is a three鈥慸igit or four鈥慸igit integer.

The first one or two digits define an external supply. To avoid a conflict with the internal supplies, we recommend using values above 8. The maximum supported value is 16.

The last two digits define the channel number of the DPS. If the channel number is less than 10, a leading "0" must be used.

-

For DC Scale channels (in DPS mode) this is a five digit number in the same format as for digital I/O channels.

 |
 |

DC_scale_channel_list

 |

To gang DC Scale channels, you must specify a consecutive number of channels enclosed by parentheses, either as comma separated list or as range, for example 10105-10106.

- DPS128/64: Ganging is possible for any number of successive channels within a card, but not across cards.

DPS128/DPS64 channels must be of the same type (HC or HV).

The maximum number of ganging groups per DPS128/64 is half the number of channels. The maximum current per card cannot be exceeded.

- XPS256: Only channels on the same HLA can be ganged.
- UHC4, UHC4T: For UHC4 or UHC4T ganging is possible for any number of successive channels within a card and any number of cards within a test head. The combination of UHC4 and UHC4T within the same ganging group is not supported. The maximum current per card cannot be exceeded.

Before cross-card ganging can be used, the connection must be enabled by command `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`）.

 |
 |

polarity

 |

Gives the polarity of the DPS which has to be applied to the selected channel.

 |
 |

POS

 |

Enter POS only if the DPS connections on the DUT board are as follows: The force is connected to power; the sink is connected to ground. The voltage supplied to the device will then be exactly as entered in the Level Setup, but the entry made there must be positive, otherwise the system returns an error.

For DC scale channels, only POS is allowed.

 |
 |

NEG

 |

NEG is not allowed for DC Scale channels.

 |
 |

pin

 |

Defines the pin name for the DPS channel.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names of those power supply outputs which have already been defined. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured power supply pins.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DFPS 11,POS,(Vee)
```

This example connects device pin Vee to channel 1 of DPS board 1. The DPS output polarity is positive.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

|

```
DFPS (10101, 10102),POS,(vee)
```

 |
 |

```
DFPS (10101-10102),POS,(vee)
```

 |

Both lines define the same master/slave configuration for DC Scale channels in DPS mode. They just use different notations. Note the five digit channel numbers.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DDIC CONN, (104GO, 105GI)
DFPS (10403, 10404, 10501, 10502),POS,(vee)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale UHC4 channels in DPS mode across two boards.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DDIC CONN, (104GO, 105GI, 105GO, 106GI)
DFPS (10403, 10404, 10502, 10503, 10504, 10601),POS,(vee)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale UHC4 channels in DPS mode across three boards.

### Example 5（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPS  DFPS  -  DeFine Power Supply）

```
DDIC CONN,(230GO, 227GI)
DFPS (23004, 22701),POS,(VDDCI)
```

This example specifies the ganging of channels across two DC Scale UHC4 cards.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPT  DFPT  -  DeFine PorT）

|

pinlist

 |

Pin name or names. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to refer to all configured pins. The pin list can contain digital or DC Scale pins, or a combination of both.

 |
 |

port

 |

The name of the port to which the pins are associated. The maximum number of characters is 16 for 32-bit SmarTest and 64 for 64-bit SmarTest.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

List of ports for which the associated pins are to be displayed. Specify `(@@)` to retrieve the definitions of all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFPT  DFPT  -  DeFine PorT）

```
DFPT? (port_1, port_2)
```

returns:

```
DFPT (CP_1,DS7_1,DS0_1,I/O7_1,...,I/O0_1,Q7_1,
Q0_1,S1_1,S0_1,_MR_1),(port_1)
DFPT (CP_2,DS7_2,DS0_2,I/O7_2,...,I/O0_2,Q7_2,
Q0_2,S1_2,S0_2,_MR_2),(port_2)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFUP  DFUP  -  DeFine Utility Purpose）

| ch_No_list |

Utility line channel numbers to be defined as the members of a utility purpose and specified with five digits. The channels must be separated with a comma.

In the five鈥慸igit format, the first three digits of the channel numbers specify the utility pogo block. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy three鈥慸igit format is also supported: The first digit (1 ... 8) specifies the utility pogo block UTIL鈥? ... UTIL鈥?.

The last two digits specify the channel number 01 ... 32 of the utility line.

On the utility pogo blocks, an offset of -1 is to be considered and the channel number is URW00 ... URW31.

When reading the defined utility lines with the DFUP? command, the data returned always have the five鈥慸igit format. The same applies to the `PALS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.173_PALS__PALS__-__Pin_ALlocation_for_multiple_Sites.md`） command.

The channel numbers 16515 and 16516 should not be used. They should only be accessed with the `I2CA`（raw: `02.06.02.02.142_I2CA__I2CA__-__I2CA_bus.md`）or the `BDID`（raw: `02.06.02.02.09_BDID__BDID__-__BoarD_ID.md`）firmware command.

 |
 | setting |

Output states for each channel in the ch_No_list. Specify the setting of each utility line with the following specifiers:

- 0: sets the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)
- 1: sets the corresponding (write) channel to low
- X (x): no action

Specify the setting values corresponding to the definition order of the ch_No_list parameter.

The number of characters must be equal to the number of the utility line channels in the ch_No_list parameter.

Note that the settings must be explicitly activated with `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`）.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of the utility purpose. In the query you can use the symbol @ to list all defined utility purposes.

This parameter can have up to 16 alphanumeric characters and must not contain blank spaces, or any of the following characters: `# ; ( ' ' ) ? @ ,`

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFUP  DFUP  -  DeFine Utility Purpose）

```
> DFUP (16501,16502,16503,16504),"0110",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "0110",(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example defines a utility purpose AWG_CNCT and activates its standard settings.

The members and the setting values are as follows:

```
Member:      16501  16502  16503  16504
---------------------------------------
Setting:     0      1      1      0
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFUT  DFUT  -  DeFine UTility line）

| ch_No |

Channel number of the utility line specified with five or three digits.

In the five鈥慸igit format, the first three digits specify the utility pogo block. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

In the legacy three鈥慸igit format, the first digit (1 ... 8) specifies the utility pogo block UTIL鈥? ... UTIL鈥?.

The last two digits specify the channel number 01 ... 32 of the utility line.

On the utility pogo blocks, an offset of -1 is to be considered and the channel number is URW00 ... URW31.

When reading the defined utility lines with the DFUT? command, the data returned always have the five鈥慸igit format. The same applies to the `PALS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.173_PALS__PALS__-__Pin_ALlocation_for_multiple_Sites.md`） command.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）

 |
 | type |

Specifies the operating mode of the utility line with the following specifiers:

- W: Write-Only
- R: Read-Only
- RW: Read-Write

Utility lines of the optional `Utility Card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.04_Utility_Card.md`） can also be configured as safety lines or as global shutdown line for hardware鈥慶ontrolled shutdown of XPS256 pins:

- TRIGGER_IF_HIGH: Safety line
- TRIGGER_IF_LOW: Safety line
- TRIGGER_SITE_IF_HIGH: Global shutdown line
- TRIGGER_SITE_IF_LOW: Global shutdown line

For more information, refer to `XPS256 safety line and DUT board disconnect`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.03.06_XPS256_safety_line_and_DUT_board_disconnect.md`）.

 |
 | util_name |

Name of the utility line. For the query, it specifies the utility line name to be retrieved. @ can be used to list all defined utility lines.

This parameter can have up to 16 alphanumeric characters and must not contain blank spaces, or any of the following characters: `# ; ( ' ' ) ? @ ,`

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DFUT  DFUT  -  DeFine UTility line）

```
DFUT 16504,w,(filter)
```

This example assigns the name `filter` and operating mode w to utility line 4 of the first utility pogo block.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

| device_cycle  | The device_cycle parameter is an integer that defines the absolute maximum number of device cycles that you can create for one pin.

Default: 256

Maximum: 16384

Note that the total number of device cycles gets evenly divided between the combined number of waveform sets and wavetables. If you use the default values, then 256 device cycles divides into the total number of 32 `waveform sets and wavetables`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） to give you 8 device cycles per waveform set/wavetable. If you choose values that do not divide evenly, then the number of device cycles will be rounded up to the next multiple of the `waveform_set`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） parameter.

 |
 | devicecycle_set |

The devicecycle_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of device cycle sets that you can create. Device cycle sets are needed for selective digital capture.

Default: 1

Maximum: 128

 |
 | dps_set |

The dps_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of DPS sets you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | level_set |

The level_set parameter is an integer that defines the combined total of level sets for fixed and equation based levels that you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | period_res_prec |

This parameter defines the precision with which the period resolution is calculated by the system. It has no effect on a user defined period resolution (using, for example, the period_res keyword in the equation set).

The default is 4, if the .technology file does not contain this parameter.

If it does, the value of the .technology file is the default.

This value is set to 9, the greatest possible value, when a device is created.

 |
 |

pmu_set

 |

The pmu_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of actions that can be contained in all measurement sets of all PPMU DC sets.

Default: 1024

Maximum: 12800

 |
 | routing_set |

Defines the number of routing sets managed by the firmware, provided by the MCD.

Default: 256

Maximum: 512

 |
 | timing_set |

The timing_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum combined total of timing sets for fixed and equation based timing you can create.

Default: 256

Maximum: 999

The number of timing sets must be equal to or greater than the number of waveform sets, as there must be at least one timing set per waveform set.

 |
 | waveform_set |

The waveform_set parameter defines the maximum combined total of waveform sets (fixed timing) and wavetables (equation based timing) you can create. Thus, if you specify a value of 32, you could, for example, create 10 waveform sets and 22 wavetables.

Default: 32

Maximum: 128

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

```
DSCP 256,16,256,32,32,1024,16,1,256,
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › GCTX  -  Get ConTeXt）

```
GCTX? {setup_type},[setup_comp]
```

returns:

GCTX {setup_type}{,setup_nr|"name"},"[context_name]"

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › GCTX  -  Get ConTeXt）

|

setup_type

 |

The type of the setup component for which the mode context is queried. Possible values are:

 |
 |

TIM

 |

Timing equation set

 |
 |

LEV

 |

Level equation set

 |
 |

WAVE

 |

Wavetable

 |
 |

LBL

 |

Sequencer label

 |
 |

SPCF

 |

Multi-port specification

 |
 |

CURR

 |

The mode context for the current primary sets (as defined with the SPRM command) and the current start label (as defined with the SQSL command).

 |
 |

setup_nr

 |

The number of a setup component. This parameter is ignored for setup type CURR.

 |
 |

name

 |

The name of a wavetable, or the name of a multi-port specification. This parameter is ignored for setup type CURR.

 |
 |

context_name

 |

The name of the mode context. If you specified CURR for the setup_type parameter, and the current mode context is not correct, GCTX? returns an empty string.

The context is only correct when all primary sets (defined by SPRM) and the current start label (defined by SQSL) are associated with the same mode context. Furthermore, if there exists a primary multi-port specification, the mode context must be the same for all ports of this specification.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › GCTX  -  Get ConTeXt）

```
> GCTX? TIM,101
< GCTX TIM,101,"High-Speed"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › HWTY  -  HardWare TYpe）

```
HWTY?
```

returns:

```
HWTY {machine}, {testhead}, {dut_if}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › HWTY  -  HardWare TYpe）

|

machine

 |

Returns PS

 |
 |

testhead

 |

Returns type of the test head. Options are:

TH_1CC for the A-test head or CX test head (containing one card cage)

TH_2CC for the compact test head or SX test head (containing two card cages)

TH_3CC for the LX test head (containing three card cages)

TH_4CC for the small test head (containing four card cages)

TH_8CC for the large test head (containing eight card cages).

 |
 |

dut_if

 |

Specifies the DUT interface type

 |
 |

SOC

 |

SOC

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › HWTY  -  HardWare TYpe）

```
> HWTY?
< HWTY VS,TH_4CC,SOC
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PACT  PACT  -  Parallel ACTivities control）

|

control

 |

The control parameter is:

 |
 |

 |

ACTIVE

 |

When a site is ACTIVE it receives all test data, and generates results for the tests.

 |
 |

 |

MASKED

 |

When a site is MASKED, it receives all test data, as with the ACTIVE parameter. However, the receivers for the site are disabled and no result information is available.

 |
 |

site

 |

A single integer representing a site number.

 |
 |

site_string

 |

A string consisting of "0" and "1". One character must be given for every site that is configured in the pin configuration. "0" indicates that the respective site is (to be) masked. "1" indicates that the respective site is (to be) activated.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

means that all configured sites that are available for testing (that is, do not use a channel that is inactivated in the MCDIgnore file) are to be activated or masked.

For the MCDIgnore file see MCDIgnore usage and restrictions in Service Guide Part 1.

 |
 |

STR

 |

forces the query to return a site string instead of a single line for every site.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PACT  PACT  -  Parallel ACTivities control）

```
> PACT ACTIVE, 1
> PACT MASKED, 2
> PACT MASKED, 3
```

This example masks site 2 and site 3, and makes site 1 active.

```
> PACT?
< PACT ACTIVE,1
< PACT MASKED,2
< PACT MASKED,3
> PACT? STR
< PACT "100"
```

This example shows the impact of the optional STR parameter for the query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PALS  PALS  -  Pin ALlocation for multiple Sites）

|

site

 |

The site parameter is an integer that defines the number of the site where the channels are to be defined.

The integer must be greater than 1 (channels for site 1 are defined by the command `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`）.

When specified as part of the PALS? query, you can use the parameter ALL to read the channel allocation for all sites or the parameter PEND to read the pending channel allocation.

 |
 |

channel_1

 |

This parameter specifies the test system channel used in the specified site for the pin.

For a digital or DC Scale channel, specify it with the test system channel number, which is five digits.

See `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for the channel number.

For utility lines, see `DFUT, DFUT? - (DeFine UTility line)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.70_DFUT__DFUT__-__DeFine_UTility_line.md`） for the channel number.

 |
 |

DC_scale_channels_list

 |

You can define a Master/Slave configuration for DC Scale channels by specifying a list of DC Scale channels, separated by commas and enclosed by parentheses. The first channel is the master.

For UHC4 / UHC4T the channels must be physically adjacent on the same board, or be the last (the 4th) channel of a board and the first of another UHC4 / UHC4T board. You cannot gang UHC4 and UHC4T boards. Before ganging between boards can be used, the connection must be enabled by `DDIC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md`）.

 |
 |

channel_2

 |

The optional parameter is currently not used.

 |
 |

pin

 |

This defines the name of the pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The names of the pins to be allocated to the pin.

The query returns the name of the pin allocated to each channel. The symbol @ can be used with the PALS? command to list all pins previously defined by the PALS command. If a list of more than one pin is required, the pin names must be separated with a comma. If you query a non-existent pinlist, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PALS  PALS  -  Pin ALlocation for multiple Sites）

```
PALS 2,10201,,(Clock)
PALS 2,10202,,(D0)
```

The above example allocates the Clock pin for site 2 to channel 10201 and allocates pin D0 for site 2 to channel 10202.

```
PALS 2,(10101, 10102),,(dc1)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale channels. The first channel is the master.

```
DDIC CONN, (104GO, 105GI)
DDIC CONN, (105GO, 107GI)
PALS 2,(10403, 10404, 10501, 10502, 10503, 10504, 10701, 10702),,(dc1)
```

This example defines a master/slave configuration for DC Scale UHC4 channels across boards. The first channel is the master.

```
DFAN "MCE231,2,i","",(av8_bbrx_b+)
DFAN "MCE231,6,i","",(av8_bbrx_b-)
PALS 2,"MCE231,1,i",,(av8_bbrx_b+)
PALS 3,"MCE231,3,i",,(av8_bbrx_b+)
PALS 4,"MCE231,4,i",,(av8_bbrx_b+)
PALS 2,"MCE231,5,i",,(av8_bbrx_b-)
PALS 3,"MCE231,7,i",,(av8_bbrx_b-)
PALS 4,"MCE231,8,i",,(av8_bbrx_b-)
```

This example defines a pair of differential pins av8_bbrx_b+ and av8_bbrx_b- using the MCE card in 4 sites.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PFND  -  Pin FiND）

```
PFND? [group_type,] {(pin)}
```

returns:

```
PFND {group_type}, {(list)}, {(pin)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PFND  -  Pin FiND）

|

group_type

 |

The group type can be PRT (for "port") or DIFF (for "differential pair"). PRT is the default.

 |
 |

pin

 |

The name of the pin about which information is to be retrieved.

 |
 |

list

 |

List of the ports that contain the pin, or the differential pair to which the specified pin belongs.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PFND  -  Pin FiND）

```
> PFND? (I/O1_1)
< PFND PRT,(port_1,port_1.CP_1),(I/O1_1)
> PFND? DIFF,(P+)
< PFND DIFF,(P+,P-),(P+)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PQFC  PQFC  -  Parallel Query FoCus）

|

site

 |

The site parameter is single integer representing the number of the site that has or shall have the query focus.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PQFC  PQFC  -  Parallel Query FoCus）

```
PQFC 2
```

This example sets the query focus to site 2.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PRLT  -  request Parallel ResuLTs）

```
PRLT? ["exec_context",] {site}
```

returns:

```
PRLT {site}, {"result"}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PRLT  -  request Parallel ResuLTs）

| exec_context  | An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`）. |
 | site  | The site parameter is number A single integer representing the site number. ALL Means that all the results of all configured sites are returned. |
 | result  | The result parameter is a string containing one character for every site. The nth character stands for site n. Possible characters are: P If the last test passed on all pins. F If the last test failed at any pin. 0 If the site was masked during the last test. |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PRLT  -  request Parallel ResuLTs）

```
PRLT? ALL
```

returns:

```
PRLT ALL, "PF0"
```

In this example, site 1 passed the last test, site 2 failed it, and site 3 was masked during the test.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PSSL  PSSL   Power Supply Safety Limits）

|

min_voltage

 |

Lowest allowed voltage in V. Must be 鈮?0.

 |
 |

max_voltage

 |

Highest allowed voltage in V. Must be 鈮?0.

 |
 |

max_source_current

 |

Highest allowed source current in A. Must be > 0.

 |
 |

max_sink_current

 |

Highest allowed sink current in A. Must be > 0.

 |
 |

pin_list

 |

Comma separated list of DPS power pins, previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command, and of DC signal (PMU) pins defined by the `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） command.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PSSL  PSSL   Power Supply Safety Limits）

```
PSSL OFF,OFF,OFF,OFF,(DPS_1)
PSSL -2,5,0.5,0.5,(DPS_2)
PSSL -1.5,3,0.5,0.5,(SIG_1A)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PSTE  PSTE  -  Parallel SiTe Enable）

| sites |

The sites parameter is an integer that specifies the number of sites (to be) configured. The maximum is 1024.

For more information, refer to `Number of sites`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits.md#_116532__r_numberOfSites`） in `SmarTest system parameters - default values and limits`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits/01.04_SmarTest_system_parameters_-_default_values_and_limits.md`）.

 |
 | site_string |

A string consisting of "0" and "1". The length of the string corresponds to the number of the configured sites. The nth character of this string stands for site n.

"0" indicates that the respective site uses a channel that is listed in the MCDIgnore file, and that this site therefore cannot be used for testing. "1" indicates that the site can be used.

 |
 | STR |

If you specify this optional keyword in the query, PSTE? will return a site string.

If this parameter is omitted, PSTE? will return the number of sites that are configured in the pin configuration.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › PSTE  PSTE  -  Parallel SiTe Enable）

```
> PSTE 3
```

This example configures three sites (site 1, site 2, and site 3).

```
> PSTE? STR
< PSTE "101"
```

This example says that three sites are configured, but that only two of them (site 1 and site 3) are available for testing. Site 2 uses a channel that is listed in the MCDIgnore file, and therefore cannot be used for testing.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › STME  STME  -  SiTe Match Enable）

|

ON

 |

Turns the site match function on.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Turns the site match function off.

 |
 |

AUTO

 |

Starting the sites successively affects the test negatively if the pin configuration contains at least one shared digital channel for triggering an analog module. The AUTO option checks if such a shared channel exists. If it does, the match site function is set to OFF; if not, it is set to ON. AUTO is the default.

 |
 |

FAST

 |

Activates the `Fast Sync`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.03_Fast_Sync.md`） feature (local synchronization) of the test processor. After setting this option," STME ON" is required to turn on the site match function.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › STME  STME  -  SiTe Match Enable）

```
> STME AUTO,
> STME?
< STME ON,
```

This example sets the site match function to AUTO, then reads the actual setting. Since the actual setting is ON, the pin configuration cannot contain a shared digital channel.

```
>SQST OFF
>NIFE 2
>STME FAST,
>STME ON,
```

This example configures the Fast Sync feature, and sets two independent Fast Sync ports on each test processor.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDEF -  UnDEFine pin）

```
UDEF {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDEF -  UnDEFine pin）

|

pinlist

 |

Consists of single or multiple pin names or the symbol @ which removes all pins. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDEF -  UnDEFine pin）

```
UDEF (Q3)
```

This example causes pin Q3 to be removed from the current configuration. If you subsequently redefine the channel using the same or a different name, it assumes its former operating mode and the pin type OFF.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDGP -  UnDefine GrouP）

```
UDGP {(group)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDGP -  UnDefine GrouP）

|

group

 |

Defines the name of the group of pins to be removed. The symbol @ can be used to dismantle all groups. If more than one group is to be removed, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDGP -  UnDefine GrouP）

```
UDGP (Qout)
```

This command dismantles the group entitled Qout.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDPS -  Undefine DPS pin）

```
UDPS {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDPS -  Undefine DPS pin）

|

pinlist

 |

Consists of single or multiple pin names or the symbol @ which undefines all DPS pins. If more than one pin is to be removed, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDPS -  Undefine DPS pin）

```
UDPS (Vee)
```

This example removes pin Vee from the setup. The software saves the level data associated with the DPS channel. Therefore if you redefine the channel using the same or a different name, the DPS settings are immediately restored.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDUP -  UnDefine Utility Purpose）

```
UDUP {(purpose_name)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDUP -  UnDefine Utility Purpose）

| purpose_name |

Specifies the utility purpose name or names to be undefined.

The symbol @ removes all utility purpose definitions.

If more than one name is to be removed, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDUP -  UnDefine Utility Purpose）

```
UDUP (@)
```

This command undefines all defined utility purpose names.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDUT -  UnDefine UTility line）

```
UDUT {(util_name)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDUT -  UnDefine UTility line）

| util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names to be undefined.

The symbol @ removes all utility line definitions.

If more than one name is to be removed, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDUT -  UnDefine UTility line）

```
UDUT (@)
```

This command undefines all defined utility line names.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDVP -  UnDefine Virtual Pin）

|

pinlist

 |

The names of the pins to undefine. The @ symbol can be used to undefine all pins that were previously defined by the VPIN command.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UDVP -  UnDefine Virtual Pin）

- To undefine a virtual pin:

```
> UDVP (VPIN1)
```

- To undefine multiple virtual pins:

```
> UDVP (VPIN2,VPIN3)
```

- To undefine all virtual pins:

```
> UDVP (@)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UPAS  UPAS  -  Utility Purpose ASsignment for multi-site）

| site |

The site parameter is an integer that defines the number of the site where the channels are to be defined.

The integer must be greater than 1.

When specified as part of the UPAS? query, you can use the parameter ALL to read the standard output states for all sites.

 |
 | setting |

Output states for each member of the utility purpose on the specified site.

Set the output state of each utility line with the following specifiers:

- 0: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)
- 1: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to low
- X (x): No action

The number and order of characters must correspond to the ch_No_list parameter of the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command.

If this parameter is omitted, the specified site is set to the same states as site 1.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of a utility purpose defined by the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command.

In the query, the symbol @ can be used to list all defined utility purposes.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UPAS  UPAS  -  Utility Purpose ASsignment for multi-site）

```
> DFUP (101,102,103,104),"11XX",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPAS 2,"XX11",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "11XX", (AWG_CNCT)
> PSFC 2
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "XX11", (AWG_CNCT)
```

In this example, the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command defines a utility purpose AWG_CNCT and output states for site 1. The UPAS command defines the output states of AWG_CNCT for site 2. First the settings of site 1 are activated. Then the setup focus is restricted to site 2, and the output states for site 2 are activated.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UPST  UPST  -  Utility Purpose STate）

| setting |

The optional parameter specifies the status of the utility lines in the utility purpose.

The status is determined with the following specifiers:

-

0: Sets the output state of the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)

-

1: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to low

-

X (x): No action

Specify the setting values corresponding to the definition order of the utility lines in the specified utility purpose.

If this parameter is omitted, the settings defined by the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） or UPAS commands (depending on the setup focus as set with `PSFC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.191_PSFC__PSFC__-__Parallel_Setup_FoCus.md`）) are set to the utility lines of the specified utility purpose.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of the utility purpose to be set or read.

For the query, you can specify multiple names, which must be separated by a comma.

Specifying the symbol @ returns the definitions of all utility purposes.

   | Note All utility lines that are set with `UTST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.313_UTST__UTST__-__UTility_line_STate.md`） or UPST will be switched in parallel when the `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command is performed. If the `WSDN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.341_WSDN_-__Wait_Setup_DoNe.md`） command is used immediately after FLSH, the time span during which execution will pause equals the longest settling time that is defined for any of the switched utility lines (with `UTTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.314_UTTI__UTTI__-__UTility_line_settling_TIme.md`）) or purposes (with `UPTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.307_UPTI__UPTI__-__Utility_Purpose_settling_TIme.md`）).

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UPST  UPST  -  Utility Purpose STate）

```
UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
FLSH
WSDN
UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
```

returns

```
UPST "0110",(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example sets the utility purpose "AWG_CNCT" to the hardware, then reads the state of the utility purpose.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UPTI  UPTI  -  Utility Purpose settling TIme）

| time |

Specifies the wait time to change the utility line status using the `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） commands (in ms).

0 ... 2鈥?47鈥?83.646 [ms]

 |
 | purpose_name |

Specifies the utility purpose name or names for which the settling time is to be set.

The symbol @ is used for all utility purposes.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UPTI  UPTI  -  Utility Purpose settling TIme）

```
UPTI 2.5,(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example sets the settling time of the utility purpose "AWG_CNCT" to 2.5 ms.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UTST  UTST  -  UTility line STate）

| value |

Specifies the output (desired) status of the utility line with the specifier 0 or 1.

- 0: High output
- 1: Low output
 |
 | type |

This parameter is used to specify whether the output (desired) state or the input (actual) state is to be returned. Possible values are:

- w: Returns the output (desired) state.
- r: Returns the input (actual) state

For pure output utility lines, this parameter is ignored.

 |
 | util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names to be set or read.

In the query, specifying @ returns all utility lines.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated by commas.

   | Note All utility lines that are set with UTST or `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） will be switched in parallel when the `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command is performed. If the `WSDN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.341_WSDN_-__Wait_Setup_DoNe.md`） command is used immediately after FLSH, the time span during which execution will pause equals the longest settling time that is defined for any of the switched utility lines (with `UTTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.314_UTTI__UTTI__-__UTility_line_settling_TIme.md`）) or purposes (with `UPTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.307_UPTI__UPTI__-__Utility_Purpose_settling_TIme.md`）).

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UTST  UTST  -  UTility line STate）

```
UTST 1,(Filt1,Filt2)
UTST 0,(Filt3,Filt4)
FLSH
WSDN
UTST? w,(Filt1,Filt2,Filt3,Filt4)
```

will return:

```
UTST 1,(Filt1,Filt2)
UTST 0,(Filt3,Filt4)
```

This example sets the utility lines "Filt1" and "Filt2" to high output, and "Filt3" and "Filt4" to low output.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UTTI  UTTI  -  UTility line settling TIme）

| time  | Specifies the wait time to change the utility line status using the `UTST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.313_UTST__UTST__-__UTility_line_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command (in ms). |
 | util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names for which the settling time is to be set.

The symbol @ is used for all utility lines.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › UTTI  UTTI  -  UTility line settling TIme）

```
UTTI 2.5,(filter)
```

This example sets the settling time of the utility line "filter" to 2.5 ms.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › VPIN  VPIN  -  Virtual PIN）

|

pinlist

 |

The name to be allocated to the pin. The query returns the name of the virtual pins that have been defined. The @ symbol can be used with the VPIN? query to list all pins previously defined by the VPIN command. If you query a non-existent pin name, the system returns nothing.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › VPIN  VPIN  -  Virtual PIN）

- To define a virtual pin:

```
> VPIN (VPIN1)
```

- To define multiple virtual pins:

```
> VPIN (VPIN2,VPIN3)
```

- To list all defined virtual pins:

```
> VPIN? (@)
```

Returns:

```
< VPIN (VPIN1,VPIN2,VPIN3)
```

- To check for the existence of specific virtual pins:

```
> VPIN? (VPIN2,VPIN4,VPIN6)
```

Returns:

```
< VPIN (VPIN2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › OPT  -  hardware OPTions）

```
*OPT?
```

returns:

```
*OPT {`hardware_type`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_hardware_type`）}, {`board_no`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_board_no`）}, {`board_type`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_board_type`）}, {`board_id`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_board_id`）}, `[phys_location`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_phys_location`）], `[clk_board`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_clk_board`）], `[chan_1_info_1`（raw: `02.06.02.02.344_OPT__-__hardware_OPTions.md#_98881__r_chan_x_info_y`）], [chan_1_info_2], ... [chan_16_info_1], [chan_16_info_2]
```

Parameters
 | hardware_type  | Returns type of the test head:

- PS_2CC or CS_2CC

  - Compact test head containing two card cages.

- PS_4CC or CS_4CC

  - Small test head containing four card cages.

- PS_8CC or CS_8CC

  - Large test head containing eight card cages.

- JN_S

  - 256 pin test head (MCU)

 |
 | board_no  | Returns the position of the installed card or the logical board number:

- The position of the card is determined by the slot in which the card is installed.
The following ranges are applicable for board_no:

- Control board:

  - Control segment number; two digits (CS); 1 to 16

- Clock board:

  - Board number of the clock board; two digits (CSCLK): 11, 12, 21, 22, ..., 41, 42

- Pin Scale 1600 channel cards and all DC Scale cards:

  - Board number (physical or virtual pogo block number) of the logical board; triple digit; range for physical pogo blocks 101 to 132, 201 to 232, 301 to 332, and 401 to 432.

- PPS modules:

  - Board number (pogo block number or slot number) of the PPS module; triple digit; range 101 to 132 and 201 to 232

- DPS cards:

  - DPS card number (DPS pogo block number) of the DPS card; single digit; 1 to 8

 |
 | board_type |

Returns the type of board or card. This may be:

- CNTR: Control board
- CLK: Clock board
- CPIO: Channel card - Pin Scale 1600
- JNIO: Channel board - MCU
- PPS: Precision Parallel Source
- HVP: High-Voltage PMU
- SWA: Switch matrix

DPS-slot device power supplies:

- SE-UDPS: Internal Utility Power Supply

DC Scale cards:

- DPS128HC: DC Scale DPS128/64-HC
- UHC4T: DC Scale UHC4T
- XPS256 DC Scale XPS256
 |
 | board_id |

As defined in the file /opt/hp93000/soc/pws/data/board_ids.

 |
 | phys_location |

Returns the physical location of the board. Format: TCSS.

- T: Test head (Always 1 for V93000 systems)
- C: Card cage; single digit; range 1 to 8
- SS: Slot in the card cage; two digits; range 01 to 14.

For details on the mapping of card slots see Mapping of physical resources.

 |
 | clk_board  | Board number of the clock board in the card cage to which the board belongs. |
 | chan_x_info_y |

Channel information. For each channel on the board, the system can return two terms: chan_x_info_1 and chan_x_info_2, where x is the channel number in the range 1 to 16 decimal.

- Digital channels

  - chan_x_info_1: For each of the 16 channels on the channel card, chan_x_info_1 returns the sequencer memory (SM) depth in blocks of 128K vectors (or 0.125M vectors).
  - chan_x_info_2: For each of the 16 channels on the channel card, chan_x_info_2 returns the vector memory (VM) depth in blocks of 128K vectors (or 0.125M vectors).

- Fast differential channels

chan_x_info_1:

I: Input channel

O: Output channel

- PPS channels

  - chan_x_info_1: Returns the size of installed pattern memory in blocks of 1K words (16 bit).

- HVP channels

  - chan_x_info_1: Returns the size of installed DAC/ADC RAM in blocks of 1K words (16 bit).

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Pin configuration setup commands › List of configuration commands › OPT  -  hardware OPTions）

```
> *OPT?
< *OPT JN_S,1,CNTR,254,1100,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
< *OPT JN_S,11,CLK,254,1115,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
< *OPT JN_S,101,JNIO,254,1102,11,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,
< *OPT JN_S,102,JNIO,254,1102,11,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,,8,
```

The reply from the *OPT? query has been generated in offline mode. The board IDs are set to 254.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Routing Setup Commands › List of routing setup commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

| device_cycle  | The device_cycle parameter is an integer that defines the absolute maximum number of device cycles that you can create for one pin.

Default: 256

Maximum: 16384

Note that the total number of device cycles gets evenly divided between the combined number of waveform sets and wavetables. If you use the default values, then 256 device cycles divides into the total number of 32 `waveform sets and wavetables`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） to give you 8 device cycles per waveform set/wavetable. If you choose values that do not divide evenly, then the number of device cycles will be rounded up to the next multiple of the `waveform_set`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） parameter.

 |
 | devicecycle_set |

The devicecycle_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of device cycle sets that you can create. Device cycle sets are needed for selective digital capture.

Default: 1

Maximum: 128

 |
 | dps_set |

The dps_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of DPS sets you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | level_set |

The level_set parameter is an integer that defines the combined total of level sets for fixed and equation based levels that you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | period_res_prec |

This parameter defines the precision with which the period resolution is calculated by the system. It has no effect on a user defined period resolution (using, for example, the period_res keyword in the equation set).

The default is 4, if the .technology file does not contain this parameter.

If it does, the value of the .technology file is the default.

This value is set to 9, the greatest possible value, when a device is created.

 |
 |

pmu_set

 |

The pmu_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of actions that can be contained in all measurement sets of all PPMU DC sets.

Default: 1024

Maximum: 12800

 |
 | routing_set |

Defines the number of routing sets managed by the firmware, provided by the MCD.

Default: 256

Maximum: 512

 |
 | timing_set |

The timing_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum combined total of timing sets for fixed and equation based timing you can create.

Default: 256

Maximum: 999

The number of timing sets must be equal to or greater than the number of waveform sets, as there must be at least one timing set per waveform set.

 |
 | waveform_set |

The waveform_set parameter defines the maximum combined total of waveform sets (fixed timing) and wavetables (equation based timing) you can create. Thus, if you specify a value of 32, you could, for example, create 10 waveform sets and 22 wavetables.

Default: 32

Maximum: 128

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Routing Setup Commands › List of routing setup commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

```
DSCP 256,16,256,32,32,1024,16,1,256,
```

set

set

An identification number of the routing set. This is an integer from 1 to the maximum number defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command.

| mode  | Selects the activation mode: |
 | FRC  | Forced activation. Primary sets are always activated. |
 | CNL  | Conditional activation, depends on previous activation performed by APRM or by any of the commands in the second list above. |
