### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › CLMP  CLMP  -  CLaMP level）

|

level_set

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by the DSCP command). Specifying ALL sets the clamp levels for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Specifying PRM sets the clamp levels for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number > 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for the high-Z state of digital pins. For more information see `Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF`（raw: `02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md`）.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

 |
 |

clamp_mode

 |

ON | OFF

For the Pin Scale 3600, the clamps can be set to ON when std/fast mode is set to std, and termination mode is set to OFF or A (active load).

Pin Scale 9G cards do not have clamps. Setting clamp levels will be ignored.

For termination mode, see `TERM, TERM? - (TERMination mode)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.257_TERM__TERM__-__TERMination_mode.md`）.

 |
 |

low_clamp_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the low clamp level.

For the Pin Scale 800, the range is -1800 to 6800. At power-on this parameter assumes a default value of -250.

 |
 |

high_clamp_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the high clamp level. For the Pin Scale 800, the range is -1800 to 6800, and the difference of high_clamp_level - low_clamp_level must be in the range 0 to 8.6 V.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pins for which the clamp levels are to be set. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the DFGP (DeFine GrouP) command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. The symbol @ refers to all pins. You can include O and IO pin types in pinlist.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › CLMP  CLMP  -  CLaMP level）

```
CLMP 1,ON,-10,5100,(Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

This example sets the clamp levels for level set 1 for pins Q0, Q1, Q2 and Q3. The low clamp level is set to -10 mV, and the high clamp level is set to 5100 mV.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › DFSP  DFSP  -  DeFine Sampling Profile）

| meas_resource  | The measurement resource. It can be:

- PMU - The default value
 |
 | measure_type  | The measurement type. It can be:

- VOLT - for voltage measurements, or
- CURR - for current measurements.
 |
 | measure_range  | This parameter corresponds to the voltage/current measure range. |
 | sampling_rate  | Specifies the sampling rate in microseconds. |
 | average_factor  | The number of measurements per sample. |
 | keep_range  | Specifies whether the range used by current profiling should be kept. Default is to restore last measure range before doing the profiling. |
 | pinlist  | This parameter specifies the pins to be used for the measurements. |

### Example 1: Current measurements（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › DFSP  DFSP  -  DeFine Sampling Profile）

```
DFSP CURR,0.5,2048,2,(@)
```

or

```
DFSP CURR,40,2048,,KEEP,(dps1)
```

### Example 2: Voltage measurements（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › DFSP  DFSP  -  DeFine Sampling Profile）

```
DFSP VOLT,2,50,8,(dps1)
```

or

```
DFSP VOLT,2,50,,(@)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › DRLV  DRLV  -  DRive LeVel）

|

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set (fixed levels) in which you want the levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command). Typing ALL in this field sets the levels for all existing level sets. Typing PRM sets the drive voltage levels for the primary level set.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

 |
 |

logic_0_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the low level voltage for the drive amplifier.

 |
 |

logic_1_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the high level voltage for the drive amplifier.

 |
 |

v3h_level

 |

Input (drive) 3rd level definition (high level voltage shift). The expression of this extra parameter must define a value in millivolts (mV).

This parameter is no longer used.

 |
 |

range

 |

This extra parameter selects the drive range in mV:

- -8000.0 ... 8000.0 selects the 8 V range
- -30000.0 ... 30000.0 selects the 30 V range
- all other values select the -40 V ... +80 V range

If not specified the best fit range will be selected based on logic_0_level and logic_1_level.

This parameter is currently not available.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose levels you want to set. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） (DeFine GrouP) command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ sets or reads the drive levels of all input pins in the level set. You can include I and IO pin types in pinlist.

 |

For card specifications, like level ranges, see `Digital Cards`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04_Digital_Cards.md`）, for example:

- `Pin Scale 1600`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.01.03_PS1600_driver.md`）
- `Pins Scale 5000`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.03.04_Pin_Scale_5000_driver.md`）

### Example 1（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › DRLV  DRLV  -  DRive LeVel）

```
DRLV 1,-1750,-850,(Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

This example sets the driver levels for level set 1 for pins Q0, Q1, Q2 and Q3. The logic 0 level is set to -1750 mV and the logic 1 level to -850 mV.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › DRLV  DRLV  -  DRive LeVel）

```
DRLV 1,-1750,-850,8000,(avi64Pin1)
```

This example shows how the 8 V drive range of an AVI64 pin is selected.

ds_No

 |

DPS Set Number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a DPS set, or the highest number of set you want to load. The number you type must not exceed the maximum number of DPS sets allowed (defined by the DSCP command).

This number is automatically updated to include any new DPS set as it is created. At power-on only one DPS set (containing the default values) is available.

 |

DSUS 2

This example defines a maximum of 2 DPS sets.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › EQFC  EQFC  -  EQualization and Filter Configuration）

| level_set_no |

The identification number of the level set (fixed levels) in which you want the filter/equalization values to be included. ### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › EQFS -  EQuation FileS command transfer）

|

spec_type

to specify levels, or

to specify timing.

to specify specs.

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › EQSP  EQSP  -  EQuation SPecification transfer）

The following example queries the current wavetables:

```
> EQSP? TIM,WVT

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › FTCG  FTCG  -  Functional Test ConfiGure）

FTCG

```
FTCG {parameter}, {mode}, {(portlist)}
```

  FTCG?

```
FTCG? {parameter}, {(@@)}
```

returns:

```
FTCG {parameter}, {mode}, {(portlist)}
```

  Parameters

 |

parameter

 |

The parameter to be used is SKPR (SKip PRimaries).

 |
 |

mode

 |

Specifies different activation conditions. This option can take the following values:

 |
 |

ON

 |

Suppresses activation of all primary sets at the start of a functional test for the sequencing groups of the ports specified by the portlist parameter. This option serves to keep a PLL alive across functional tests.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Allows activation for the ports specified by the portlist parameter. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

NEVER

 |

By this option, the primary sets will always be loaded at the start of a test for all ports of the sequencing groups to which the ports specified by the portlist parameter belong.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

In the command, specify a list of ports, separated by commas. Note that the ports are treated as representatives of their sequencing groups. Activation will be suppressed, allowed, or enforced not only for the specified ports, but for all member ports of the sequencing groups to which the specified ports belong in the current setup.

In the query, specify @@, which stands for all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › FTCG  FTCG  -  Functional Test ConfiGure）

The following example illustrates the dependence of the FTCG command on the current sequencing group definitions.

```
> SQLB "MP_burst1",MPBU,28,31,"SG1",(clock)
> SQLB "MP_burst1",MPBU,28,29,"SG2",(data1)
> SQLB "MP_burst1",MPBU,31,32,"SG2",(data2)
> SQLB "MP_burst2",MPBU,32,33,"SG1",(clock)
> SQLB "MP_burst2",MPBU,30,31,"SG1",(data1)
> SQLB "MP_burst2",MPBU,33,34,"SG2",(data2)
> FTCG SKPR,ON,(clock)
> FTCG SKPR,NEVER,(data2)
> SPRM "cont_clock",,,
> SQSL "MP_burst1"
> SQGB ACQF,0
> FTST?
...
> SQSL "MP_burst2"
> FTST?
...
```

In the first functional test, sequencing group `SG1` only contains the port `clock`, and therefore activation of primary sets is suppressed at the start of `MP_burst1` only for `clock`, whereas it is enforced for ports `data1` and `data2`. In the second test, `SG1` contains both `clock` and `data1`, and therefore activation is suppressed for both these ports at the start of `MP_burst2`, and enforced only for `data2`.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › LSUS  LSUS  -  Level Sets USed）

|

level_set_no

 |

Level Set Number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a level set or the highest number of set you want to load. The number you type must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command).

This number is automatically updated to include any new level set as it is created. At power-on only one level set (containing the default values) is available.

 |
 |

equation_set_no

 |

The level equation set number for which the number of currently defined level sets is to be determined. Enter an integer in the range 1 to 99. Valid for Equation based testing only.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › LSUS  LSUS  -  Level Sets USed）

```
LSUS 4
```

This example defines a maximum of 4 level sets.

|

level_set_no

Level Set Number. If the number is smaller than the current value of LSUS then LSUX is set to this value. Otherwise it is set to the current value of LSUS.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › PSLV  PSLV  -  Power Supply LeVel）

Note The settling time parameter (setup_time) of the PSLV command and the rise_... and fall_... parameters of the `PSSR, PSSR? -(Power Supply Slew Rate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.197_PSSR__PSSR__-_Power_Supply_Slew_Rate.md`） command exclude each other. This also applies to the t_ms equation parameter (see `DPSPINS`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07_DPSPINS.md`） and `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）).

 |

dps_No

 |

Needed for non-equation-based setup.

 |
 |

dps_No

 |

The identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify. The number must not exceed the maximum number allowed (as defined by the DSCP (Define System Control Parameter) command.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Modifies all the existing fixed DPS sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

Modifies the primary DPS set.

 |
 |

ACT

 |

(Only for PSLV?) Displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Needed for equation-based setup.

This parameter is derived as follows:

`100000*equation_set_no + 1000*specset_no+1`

 |
 |

voltage

 |

The optional parameter voltage defines the output voltage (in V) of the DPS. Applicable value depends on the DPS type.

 |
 |

source_current

 |

The optional parameter defines the source current limit (ilimit_source) in [A]. The applicable value depends on the DPS type.

The parameter defines the source and the sink current limit if both values are equal.

The parameter defines only the source current limit if the sink_current parameter is used.

 |
 | sink_current |

The extra parameter defines the sink current limit (ilimit_sink) in [A].

The parameter is required only if the source and sink current limits are set to different values. This parameter defines then the sink current limit while the source current limit is defined by the above source_current parameter.

The parameter is not required if the current limits are programmed symmetrically to the same (absolute) value. Both, the source and the sink value are then defined by the source_current parameter.

The query answer shows the sink_current parameter only if the programmed sink current limit is not symmetrical to the source current limit.

 |
 |

impedance

 |

The optional parameter sets the DPS output impedance. You can select:

- LOZ sets the DPS output impedance to low when the test system is in the disconnect state. The current limit remains at the same level as in the active state, while the force voltage is set to 0 V.
- HIZ sets the DPS output to high impedance when the test system is in the disconnect state. This sets the channel to the minimum possible current limit. HIZ is the default state for DPS-slot types. If it is applied to DC Scale cards, HIZ_R is used instead of HIZ.
- HIZ_R sets the DPS output to high impedance by switching the output relay off when the test system is in the disconnect state.

Note that relay switching is slower than with HIZ.

- LOZ_HIZ combines LOZ with HIZ. First, the DPS is switched to 0 V with an unchanged current limit (just like in LOZ mode). After the output voltage has reached 0 V (卤50 mV) or after a timeout of 1 second, the DPS pin is switched to high impedance. This combines the advantages of both modes. A capacitor on the load board is quickly discharged and then the DPS pin is switched to high impedance. This is safer when changing the DUT or DUT board after a disconnect.
- LOZ_HIZ_R combines LOZ with HIZ_R. First, the DPS is switched to 0 V with an unchanged current limit (just like in LOZ mode). After the output voltage has reached 0 V (卤50mV) or after a timeout of 1 second, the DPS pin is switched to open. This combines the advantages of both modes. A capacitor on the DUT board is quickly discharged and then the DPS pin is switched to high impedance. This is safer when changing the DUT or the DUT board after a disconnect.
 |
 |

setup_time

 |

The optional parameter is an integer which specifies the settling time (in ms) of the DPS. All DPS's are synchronized so that they finish their settling periods at the same point in time. This is the point when the system is switched to the connect state. If there are, for example, two DPS's, one with a settling time of 10 ms, and the other with a settling time of 4 ms, then the second DPS will be started 6 ms after the first:

   !`Synchronizing Different DPS Settling Times`（raw: `../../../../raw/93235.png`）

The range is from -2147483647 up to 2147483646 ms.

 The default value is 0.Note setup_time has a resolution of ms (floating point values are rounded to nearest integer). |
 |

pinlist

 |

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command. If more than one pin is specified, the names must be separated by commas. The character @ can be used to set the levels for all DPS pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › PSLV  PSLV  -  Power Supply LeVel）

```
PSLV 1,5.2,0.5,HIZ,15,(Vee)
```

This example sets the following parameters for device pin Vee:

- DPS set 1
- A voltage of 5.2 V
- A current limit of 0.5 A
- Minimum current limit when the test system is disconnected
- A setup time of 15 ms

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › PSSR  PSSR  - Power Supply Slew Rate）

Note The rise_... and fall_... parameters of the PSSR command and the settling time parameter (setup_time) of the `PSLV`（raw: `02.06.02.02.195_PSLV__PSLV__-__Power_Supply_LeVel.md`） command exclude each other. This also applies to the t_ms equation parameter (see `DPSPINS`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07_DPSPINS.md`） and `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）). Note All time values have a resolution of microseconds (floating point values are rounded to three decimal places).

 |

dps_No

 |

Needed for non-equation-based setup.

The identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify. The number must not exceed the maximum number allowed (as defined by the DSCP (Define System Control Parameter) command). Entering ALL modifies all the existing fixed DPS sets. Entering PRM modifies the primary DPS set. Entering ACT (only for PSSR?) displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Needed for equation-based setup.

This parameter is derived as follows:

`100000*equation_set_no + 1000*specset_no+1`

 |
 |

rise_tm_per_v

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the rising edge in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

 |
 |

rise_settm

 |

Sets the settling time for the rising edge in ms.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms.

 |
 |

fall_tm_per_v

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the falling edge in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

 |
 |

fall_settm

 |

Sets the settling time for the falling edge in ms.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms.

 |
 |

rise_t_per_v_c2c

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the rising edge. expression must define a value in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect-" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_rise_t_ms_per_volt parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

rise_setup_t_c2c

 |

Sets the settling time for the rising edge. expression must define a value in ms.

The allowed range is -10000 to 10000 ms.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect-" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_rise_settling_t_ms parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

fall_t_per_v_c2c

 |

Sets the inverse slew rate for the falling edge. expression must define a value in ms/V.

The allowed range is 0 to 10000 ms/V.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect-" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_fall_t_ms_per_volt parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

fall_setup_t_c2c

 |

Sets the settling time for the falling edge. expression must define a value in ms.

The allowed range is -10000 to 10000 ms.

The parameter is optional. If specified, it is used for "connect-to-connect" cases, that is for level changes caused by a reprogramming of the output voltage within one DPS set, or by a switch to another DPS set while the DPS is connected. If omitted, the above vout_fall_settling_t_ms parameter is used instead.

This parameter is for both DPS-slot DPS and DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command. If a pin is associated with a DPS-slot DPS, it is ignored. @ refers to all pins that are associated with a DC Scale channel.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › PSSR  PSSR  - Power Supply Slew Rate）

```
PSSR PRM,10,50,20,70,(Vcc)
```

This example sets the following parameters for the primary set of DPS pin Vcc:

- rise_tm_per_v = 10 ms/V
- rise_settm = 50 ms
- fall_tm_per_v = 20 ms/V
- fall_settm = 70 ms

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

```
RCLS? {test}, {pass_value}, [limit], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
RCLS {value_specifier}, {result_value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

|

test

 |

This parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

H

 |

to determine the high level threshold for the DUT output pins.

 |
 |

L

 |

to determine the low level threshold for the DUT output pins.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The pass_value parameter defines the expected pass value (in mV) for the threshold measurement.

pass_value must be in the range of the comparator threshold level in the channel board (see `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`）).

 |
 |

limit

 |

The limit parameter specifies the limit (in mV) of the measurement window for value measurements. The range for this parameter is as follows:

- If you want to determine the high level threshold, the value entered must be between the maximum comparator threshold level of the channel board (see `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`）) and the specified pass value
- If you want to determine the low level threshold, the value entered must be between the pass value and the minimum comparator threshold level of the channel board.

If a pass/fail test is to be performed, this parameter must be omitted. For both high and low level threshold measurements, the search is performed by varying the comparator threshold from the limit you specify, to the hardware limit.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be tested. This parameter may also include groups previously created using the DFGP command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. pinlist must only contain pins configured as outputs.

 |
 |

value_specifier

 |

This parameter contains one of the following:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned after a high level test to indicate that the first functional test (performed at the value defined by the limit parameter) failed. LT is only returned after a value test.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned, after a low level test, if all the tests carried out within the window pass. LE is only returned during value measurements.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

Equal to is returned if the first failure of the level test occurs within the measurement window. EQ is only returned after a value measurement.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned, after a high level test, if all the tests carried out within the window pass. GE is only returned after a value measurement.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned after a low level test to indicate that the first functional test (performed at the value defined by the limit parameter) failed. GT is only returned after a value test.

 |
 |

P

 |

A P is returned if the functional test passes. A P can only be returned if the limit parameter has been omitted.

 |
 |

F

 |

An F is returned if the functional test fails. An F can only be returned if the limit parameter has been omitted.

 |
 |

result_value

 |

The result value is the level (in mV) of the last passed test.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

```
RCLS? H,3000,6000,(Q0)
```

returns:

```
RCLS EQ,5300
```

In this example a search was made to find the high level threshold between 3V and 6V. The pass/fail transition was located at 5.3V.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RCLV  RCLV  -  ReCeive LeVel）

|

level_set

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the low and high threshold levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP, DSCP? - (Define System Control Parameter)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）). If you enter a level set number that is outside the used range of sets defined by the LSUS command, a new level set is created. Typing ALL in this field sets the low and high threshold levels for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Typing PRM sets the low and high threshold levels for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number greater than 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for sequencer state OFF. For more information see `Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF`（raw: `02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md`）.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

 |
 |

vth

 |

Output threshold for FAST comparator (single threshold as opposed to high and low). The expression must define a value in millivolts (mV).

 |
 |

logic_0_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the logic 0 threshold level of the comparator. This parameter represents the point where the comparator distinguishes between logic 0 and an intermediate level.

 |
 |

logic_1_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the logic 1 threshold level of the comparator. This parameter represents the point where the comparator distinguishes between logic 1 and an intermediate level.

 |
 |

range

 |

This extra parameter selects the receive range in mV.

This parameter is currently not available.

Ranges of the high-speed voltage comparator:

- -8000.0 ... 8000.0 selects the 8 V range
- -40000.0 ... 80000.0 selects the -40 V ... +80 V range

Ranges of the high-resolution voltage comparator:

- -3000.0 ... 3000.0 selects the 3 V range
- -10000.0 ... 10000.0 selects the 10 V range
- -30000.0 ... 30000.0 selects the 30 V range
- -40000.0 ... 80000.0 selects the -40 V ... +80 V range

If not specified the best fit range will be selected based on logic_0_level and logic_1_level if a voltage comparator is selected.

Range of the high-resolution current comparator:

- A fixed range of 200 mA is set.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose threshold level you want to set. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the command `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ sets or reads the threshold levels for all output pins. You can include O or IO pins in pinlist.

 |

For card specifications, like level ranges, see `Digital Cards`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04_Digital_Cards.md`）, for example:

- `Pin Scale 1600`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.01.03_PS1600_driver.md`）
- `Pins Scale 5000`（raw: `../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.03.04_Pin_Scale_5000_driver.md`）

### Example 1（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RCLV  RCLV  -  ReCeive LeVel）

```
RCLV 1,-1300,-750,(Q0)
```

This example sets the low level compare threshold for pin Q0 to -1300 mV and the high level compare threshold to -750 mV.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RCLV  RCLV  -  ReCeive LeVel）

```
TERM 1,,,,,,HRV,(avi64Pin1)
RCLV 1,-1300,-750,3000,(avi64Pin1)
```

This example for an AVI64 pin sets the low level compare threshold to -1300 mV, the high level compare threshold to -750 mV, and the range to the 3 V range.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RSET -  ReSET）

```
RSET {specifier}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RSET -  ReSET）

|

specifier

 |

The specifier can be:

 |
 |

DPS

 |

Loads the default power supply setup for standard DPSs.

 |
 |

FCR

 |

Loads the default clock routing.

 |
 |

LEV

 |

Loads the default power supply setup for standard DPSs.

Level: 0 V

Current: 50 mA

Off state: minimum current

Setup time: 0 ms

This default states are:

UHC4T

- Connect state: normal
- Level: 0 V
- Range: 4 V
- Clamp: 4 A
- Clamp-Range: 40 A
- Disconnect state: HIZ
- Voltage drop force: 250 mV
- Voltage drop return: 250 mV
- Clamp mode: limit (see `UHCM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md`）)
- DUT capacitor mode: off

Fast preload: 0 ms

 |
 |

TIM

 |

Loads the default timing setup. The settings are:

Timing Sets

- Defined Timing Sets: 1
- Allowed Timing Sets: 256

Waveform Sets

- Defined Waveform Sets: 1
- Allowed Waveform Sets: 16

Waveforms: not defined

Breakwaveform: defined

Events

- Action: NOP
- Timing: 0 ns

Min Period: 4 ns

- This is dependent on the test system hardware configuration.

Device Cycles: not defined

Default Device Cycle: ""

 |
 |

VEC

 |

Loads the default vector setup. The Vector Memory contains:

No vectors

No tests (and therefore no labels)

No comments

No sequencer programs (no instructions)

 |
 |

ATR

 |

Loads the default edge attributes.

Pin attribute: set to 0

 |
 |

PDL

 |

Loads the default path delay attributes.

Cable assembly delay attribute: set to 0

Fixture delay attribute: set to 0

System attribute: set to 0

 |
 |

CAL

 |

Loads the default calibration data.

Level calibration data

Timing calibration data

 |
 |

MTPP

 |

Resets memory test and per-pin sequencer subroutine data.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RSET -  ReSET）

```
RSET TIM
```

This example resets all waveform sets and timing sets and loads the hardware with the default vector rate and edge placement values. Only waveform set 1 and timing set 1 in waveform set 1 is active.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SDSC  -  Set number DeSCriptions）

```
SDSC? {spec_type}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], [setup_comp_2], ["description"]
```

returns:

```
SDSC {spec_type}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], [setup_comp_2], {"description"}
```

Alternatively, for multiport specifications:

```
SDSC? {TIM}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], {"multi-port_spec"}, ["description"][, (portlist)]
```

returns:

```
SDSC {TIM}, {type}, [setup_comp_1], {"multi-port_spec"}, {"description"}, {(port)}
```

Parameters
 |

spec_type

Which specification type to use. Use:

 |

LEV

to specify levels

TIM

to specify timing. This is the only possible value for multi-port specifications.

 |
 |

ANA

 |

to specify analog setup

 |

type

The possible values and their meaning are as follows:

 |

EQN

equation sets

specsets

wavetables (equation based)

digital sets

analog sets (for analog setup)

routing sets (for analog setup)

 |

An integer in the range 1 to 99 that refers to a setup component of a certain type (for example, an equation set or waveform set). The component type is determined by the values of spec_type and type according to the table below. If no value is specified, all components of the respective type are processed.

If you specify the name of a multi-port specification for the setup_comp_2 parameter, the setup_comp_1 parameter will be ignored.

 |

setup_comp_2

An integer that refers to a setup component of a certain type (for example, a timing set or spec set). The component type is determined by the values of spec_type and type according to the table below. If no value is specified, all components of the respective type are processed.

 |

multi-port_spec

In a multi-port setup, enter the name of a specification instead of a component number, but only for spec_type TIM. In this case, the setup_comp_1 parameter will be ignored.

description

Maximum 60 characters. Can be also a substring of a description, in which case all components containing this string in their description are returned.

With multi-port specifications, you can specify a list of ports. If you do, only those components will be displayed that are associated with one of the specified ports.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SDSC  -  Set number DeSCriptions）

```
> SDSC? TIM,EQN,,,
< SDSC TIM,EQN,1,,"gross_func_eqn"
< SDSC TIM,EQN,2,,"specs_search_eqn"
< SDSC TIM,EQN,3,,"speed_eqn"
```

This example returns all defined equation sets.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SDSC  -  Set number DeSCriptions）

```
> SDSC? TIM,EQN,2,"spec_port_1_port_2",,(port_1)
< SDSC TIM,EQN,1,"spec_port_1_port_2",
     "gross_func_eqn",(port_1)
```

This example returns the equation set that is associated with port port_1 in the multiport specification

spec_port_1_port_2. Note that the setup_comp_1 parameter is ignored.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SLDO -  Switch Level and Dps Order）

|

order

 |

This parameter sets the switching order mode:

 |
 |

FDSL

 |

First DPS, second levels. If this parameter is specified, the DPS voltage values are always switched before the voltage values of the levels.

 |
 |

CVDL

 |

There are three possibilities:

1. If DPS voltage values are increasing or stable, DPS voltages are switched before level voltages.

2. If DPS voltage values are decreasing or stable, level voltages are switched before DPS voltages.

3. If the voltages of some DPS pins are decreasing while the voltages of others are increasing (ambiguous case), DPS voltages are always switched first.

 |
 |

report

 |

This parameter sets the report mode, which can be one of the following:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Reports a change in the switching order from DPS voltages (first) to level voltages (first) and vice versa.

 |
 |

FLSD

 |

First levels, second DPS. Reports a change in the switching order to switching level voltages first.

 |
 |

AMBI

 |

Ambiguous case. Reports an ambiguous case.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

Nothing is reported. This is the default report mode.

 |
 |

operation

 |

This is the mode of operation. SAVE returns values for everything that can be set.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SLDO -  Switch Level and Dps Order）

```
SLDO CVDL, AMBI
```

This example switches either the DPS voltage values or the level voltage values first when changing from one DPS or level set to the next depending on which of the three above mentioned cases occur and reports any ambiguous case.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SPRM  SPRM  -  Set PRiMary sets）

|

waveform_set_no

 |

The identification number of the waveform set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of waveform sets allowed - as defined by `CONF, CONF? - (CONFiguration)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.31_CONF__CONF__-__CONFiguration.md`）.

 |
 |

timing_specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

Note that the spec set ID also identifies the primary wavetable in equation based testing.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

For a multi-port setup, specify a primary multi-port specification.

 |
 |

timing_set_no

 |

The identification number of the timing set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets (of the selected waveform set or timing specification). The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of timing sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）).

In a multiport setup, the timing set number applies to all ports of the specification if you do not specify a port. If you do, the number applies to the specified port.

 |
 |

timing_set_list

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can specify primary timing sets for all ports of the specification by entering a list of numbers separated by commas. The order of the timing sets must correspond to the order of the ports in the multi-port timing specification.

In the query, the numbers of the primary timing sets are returned in a list for all ports of the primary specification unless the numbers are identical for all ports or a port has been specified in the query.

 |
 |

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed level sets. The maximum number is determined by `LSUS, LSUS? - (Level Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.155_LSUS__LSUS__-__Level_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）).

 |
 |

dps_set_no

 |

The identification number of the DPS set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed DPS sets. The maximum number is determined by `DSUS, DSUS? - (Dps Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.91_DSUS__DSUS__-__Dps_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must be less than or equal to the maximum number of DPS sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）).

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no`

 |
 |

dps_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + 1`

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multiport setup, you can specify a port of the specification that was entered as the first parameter. In this case, the timing set number specified as the second parameter will only be applied to the specified port. The port parameter is ignored if a timing set list is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SPRM  SPRM  -  Set PRiMary sets）

The following example shows how to define and query primary timing sets for the multi-port specification spec_ClockP_P1_P2, which contains three ports:

```
> SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2","2,1,2",,
> SPRM?
< SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2","2,1,2",101002,101003
> SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2",2,,,(port_1.CP_1)
> SPRM?
< SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2",2,101002,101003
> SPRM? (port_1.CP_1)
< SPRM "spec_ClockP_P1_P2",2,101002,101003,(port_1.CP_1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
SPST? {spec_type}, {equation_set_no}, {specset_no}
```

returns:

```
SPST {spec_type}, {equation_set_no}, {specset_no}, {status}
```

or, for multiport specifications:

```
SPST? {spec_type}, , {"multi-port_spec"}
```

or

```
SPST? {spec_type}, PRM,
```

returns:

```
SPST {spec_type},, {"multi-port_spec"}, {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

|

to specify levels, or

TIM

to specify timing.

equation_set_no

Equation set number. An integer in the range 0 to 256.

Use ALL to refer to all defined equation sets. Use PRM to specify the primary equation set. In the latter case, the specset_no parameter is ignored.

Equation set 0 is used for compatibility with a non-equation based testing environment. In this case, when equation set 0 is used and spec_type is LEV, specset_no is meaningless, while when equation set 0 is used and spec_type is TIM, specset_no is interpreted as the number of a waveform set.

```

In this last example, a multi-port specification is queried. The answer says that bits 1 and 2 have been set. This has the effect that a drive or receive period 1 limit violation will be ignored, and only a period 2 limit violation will be recorded.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

|

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use:

 |
 |

LEV

 |

to specify levels, or

 |
 |

TIM

 |

to specify timing.

 |
 |

equation_set_no

 |

Equation set number. An integer in the range 1 to 99.

Use PRM to specify the primary equation set, or, in a multi-port setup, the primary specification as defined with SPRM. In this case, the specset_no parameter is ignored.

In the query, use ALL to display all equation sets.

This parameter must be omitted if a multi-port specification is specified for the thirdparameter.

 |
 |

specset_no

 |

Specset number. An integer in the range of 1 to 99. In the query, use ALL to select all defined specsets.

If specset_no is not set, and equation_set_no is set to ALL or a number, only the spec names in the specified equation sets, but no values are returned.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, enter the name of a specification instead of a spec set number. In this case, the secondparameter must be left empty.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

The name of a base (spec) variable. In a multi-port setup, the same variable name can occur among the spec variables of more than one port within the same specification. In this case, you can qualify the variable name by a port name in the following format

<spec_name>@<port_name>,

if you want to modify the variable on that port only.

Note, however, that the scope of the variable will be set to local for the port in question after such a modification (even if it is set to global in the setup), until the setup is downloaded again.

Note also that in a multi-port setup, you cannot change the value of a variable globally (that is, without specifying a port) unless at least one of the variable instances has its scope set to global in the setup. For basic information on the local and global scope of spec variables in a multi-port setup see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）.

 |
 |

spec_or_equ_name

 |

The name of a base (spec) or derived (equation) variable. An equation variable cannot be specified in the command or in a query which uses the extra parameter.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Requires that the actual values of both base and derived variables are returned.

 |
 |

EQUA

 |

Requires that the actual values of only the derived (equation) variables are returned.

 |
 |

MAX

 |

Requires that the maximum values of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the maximum value of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

MIN

 |

Requires that the maximum of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the minimum value of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

SPEC

 |

Requires that the actual values of only the base (spec) variables are returned.

 |
 |

UNIT

 |

Requires that the units of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the unit of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

value

 |

Float with 5 possible decimal places.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

By this extra parameter, you can modify the runtime definitions for an individual pin. Note that you cannot retrieve the pin specific values with SVLR?.

 Note You can use the pinlist parameter to modify the value of a spec variable of an individual pin, temporarily. If you make a new modification on a different spec variable, only the last modification is kept while the previous spec variable is reset to the setup value defined in the spec file. To make a permanent modification on a spec variable, specify all pins (that is, @) as the pinlist. Otherwise, to change the value of a spec variable of an individual pin permanently, you have to use a specset for each pin and modify the spec variable in that specset. |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

The following example queries the values of the spec variable f in a setup where both single-port and multi-port specifications occur:

```
> SVLR? TIM,ALL,ALL,"f"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",35
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_2",33
< SVLR TIM,1,1,"f",37
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

The next example queries in which equation sets the spec variable f occurs:

```
> SVLR? TIM,ALL,,"f"
< SVLR TIM,1,,"f",
< SVLR TIM,2,,"f",
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

For this example assume that the primary timing is a multi-port specification which contains the two ports p_1 and p_2, and that p_1 and p_2 share the spec variable f in this specification. Assume further that f has been set to scope global for the port p_1. Now query the current value of f for p_1, change it globally, and query it again:

```
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",33
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f",43
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",43
```

Since f is global for p_1, its value has been modified. Now change the value a second time, but this time locally, and then try to change it globally again:

```
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1",53
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f",43
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",53
```

The second global command has no effect because f has only local scope after issuing the local command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

|

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the definitions to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`）) and the level sets used (as defined by `LSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.155_LSUS__LSUS__-__Level_Sets_USed.md`）). Entering ALL in this field sets the termination mode for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Entering PRM in this field defines the termination mode for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number > 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for digital pins in high-Z state. For more information see `Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF`（raw: `02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md`）.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no`

 |
 |

term_mode

 |

The termination mode has dependencies to pin types and to the parameters (term_pulldown and param_1 to param_3 - see the syntax). The allowed combinations are shown in the Termination modes table, below.

Level set 0 only supports the termination modes OFF (the default), T, C, and A.

 |
 |

term_pulldown

 |

Extra parameter that defines the pull down mode. For more information refer to column term_mode of table Termination modes below.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

param_1

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_1 gives the termination voltage, active load commutation voltage, or the clamp low level voltage. The units are mV.

 |
 |

param_2

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_2 defines the active load Iol current, or the clamp high level voltage. The units are mA or mV respectively.

When used, param_2 defines either

- the active load Iol current in 碌A,
- the clamp high level voltage in mV, or
- the receiver swing voltage in mV.

For the NP termination modes SP, SM, SEP, or SEM, param_2 defines the receiver threshold in mV.

 |
 |

param_3

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below:

- For term_mode = A, param_3 defines the active load Ioh current. The units are 碌A.
- For term_mode = CT, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.
- For term_mode = bidir_receiver, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.
 |
 |

l_range

 |

For term_mode `=`A the low level current range.

This parameter can be

- I5E3: Defines the low current range of 0 to 5 mA.
- I3E4: Defines the high current range of 0 to 30 mA.
- AUTO: Lets the firmware automatically select the correct range. Whenever possible, the system selects the lower range.

This parameter is not supported for AVI64.

 |
 |

h_range

 |

For term_mode `=`A the high level current range.

This parameter can be

- I5E3: Defines the low current range of 0 to 5 mA.
- I3E4: Defines the high current range of 0 to 30 mA.
- AUTO: Lets the firmware automatically select the correct range. Whenever possible, the system selects the lower range.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names of those power supply outputs which have already been defined. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured power supply pins.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 1,T,-1500,,,,,(Q1)
```

This example terminates the output pin Q1 to -1500 mV in level set 1.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 3,A,3000,1500,1000,I3E4,I3E4,(out)
```

This example sets the active load level of the pin group out to 3V, and sets Iol and Ioh current to 1.5 and 1.0 mA respectively. The 0 to 30 mA range is used for both the low and the high range.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 1,CT,2000,,,,,(o1,o1-)
```

This example terminates the differential output pair (the o1 and o1- pins) to 2000 mV with center tap termination in level set 1.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › TERM  TERM  -  TERMination mode）

```
TERM 1,OFF,PULLDOWN,,,,,,(Q1,Q2)
```

On a PS1600 card, this example switches on the pulldown resistor on the specified pins.

```
TERM 1,OFF,NONE,,,,,,(Q1,Q2)
```

On a PS1600 card, this example switches off the pulldown resistor on the specified pins.

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › UPTD  UPTD  -  UP To Date）

```
UPTD? CONF
```

This example requests if the pin configuration data has been changed since the file was last loaded or saved. If the data has not changed, the response is:

```
UPTD CONF,1
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › WAIT -  WAIT）

```
WAIT {time}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › WAIT -  WAIT）

|

time

 |

Enter a time in 碌s.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › WAIT -  WAIT）

```
RLYC DC,PMU,(outputs); WAIT 1000; FTST?
```

This example causes the MCD to wait 1 ms (1000 碌s) for the PMU relay to close before executing a functional test.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RST -  ReSeT）

```
*RST [type]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RST -  ReSeT）

|

type

 |

not used

 |

- Enforces a disconnect (AC relay is open)
- All DPS sets, except the default set, will be deleted.
- All resources (for example objects defined with RDEF) will be deleted
- All pin definitions (for example pins defined with DFAN) will be deleted.
- All instruments will be deleted from the instrument registry and recreated.
- The instrument will have its reset bit toggled.
- The instrument will be set to its default state.
 |
 |

 SWR

 |

- All resources will be deleted
- All pin definitions will be deleted.
- The instrument will have its reset bit toggled.
- The instrument will be set to its default state.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Level Setup Commands › List of level setup commands › RST -  ReSeT）

```
*RST
```

Resets the software and the hardware.

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › Concepts of timing setup › Data organization of equation based timing）

The following figure exemplifies the structure of equation based timing by a schematic setup:

 !`Timing Specifications`（raw: `../../../../raw/10596.png`）

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › Concepts of timing setup › Defining the timing specification）

The following is a simple example of a `single-port timing specification`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.34.04.01_Single-port_timing_setup.md`）:

```
EQNSET 1 "default"

WAVETBL "table1"
CHECK all

SPECSET 1 "sp1"

# SPECNAME *****ACTUAL***** *****MINIMUM**** *****MAXIMUM**** UNITS COMMENT
f          100                                                [MHz]
```

This specification uses spec set 1 for equation set 1. It will be identified to the firmware commands by 101. The base variable f is set to 100. The `CHECK all statement`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.34.04.03.05.01_CHECK_Statement_Options.md`） activates all consistency checks (see `Consistency checks for edge delays`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.01_Consistency_checks_for_edge_delays.md`）).

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › APRM -  Activate PRiMary sets）

```
APRM {mode}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › APRM -  Activate PRiMary sets）

| mode  | Selects the activation mode: |
 | FRC  | Forced activation. Primary sets are always activated. |
 | CNL  | Conditional activation, depends on previous activation performed by APRM or by any of the commands in the second list above. |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › APRM -  Activate PRiMary sets）

```
APRM CNL
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › BWDF  BWDF  -  Break Waveform DeFinition）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter ALL for all waveform sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *` equation_set_no `+ ` specset_no

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

a1..a6

 |

Edge action. The actions you can define are:

 |
 |

N

 |

no action

 |
 |

F0N

 |

drive 0, no tri-state action

 |
 |

F1N

 |

drive 1, no tri-state action

 |
 |

FN0

 |

no drive action, tri-state off

 |
 |

FNZ

 |

no drive action, tri-state on

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which break waveform definitions are to be made or read back. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured input and IO pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › BWDF  BWDF  -  Break Waveform DeFinition）

```
BWDF 1,N,N,N,F1N,F0N,N,(D0,D1,D2,D3)
```

This example defines a pulse for waveform set 1, and for pins D0 to D3, driving to 1 at edge action 4 and to 0 at edge action 5. The tri-state formatter is not used.

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › BWDS  BWDS  -  Break Waveform Definition String）

```
> BWDS? 1,,,(@)
< BWDS 1,,,"",(io)
< BWDS 1,,,"d1:F00 d5:F10",(clk)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

```
CDCP? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {strt_disp}, {disp_length}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CDCP {cycle}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}, {DD1}, {DD2}, {ED1}, {ED2}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle to be analyzed. The range of values for this parameter depends on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

cycle

 |

In the query, the consecutive number of the displayed cycle.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles to be analyzed. The range for this parameter is 0 to 1000.

 |
 |

strt_disp

 |

This parameter defines the offset of your range of interest from start_cycle. The actual display starts with the last device cycle that does not begin before start_cycle and does not end before start_cycle + strt_disp.

The purpose of this construction is to enable a correct device cycle reconstruction even if the first cycle you are interested in does not lie at a device cycle boundary (a device cycle can generate up to 16 cycles).

 |
 |

disp_length

 |

Specifies the display length in cycles. This parameter determines the end of your range of interest. The actual display stops with the last device cycle that starts before start_cycle + strt_disp + disp_length.

If this parameter is larger than no_of_cycles, it is ignored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which a device cycle data transfer is to be made. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to download data for all configured pins.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

A reply parameter, giving the name of the reconstructed device cycle.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

A reply parameter, giving the length of the reconstructed device cycle. For SmarTest 7.10 this is always 1.

 |
 |

DD1 and DD2

 |

Drive Data parameters. They contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values the system returns are:

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

N

 |

Not used. Returned if no drive data parameter is set to a drive and tri-state value.

 |
 |

UC

 |

Unclear. The system may return this value to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle.

 |
 |

ED1 and ED2

 |

Expected Data Parameters. The values the system returns are:

 |
 |

F0

 |

compare to 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

compare to 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

compare to intermediate

 |
 |

FX

 |

compare to mask

 |
 |

FU

 |

compare to unstable

 |
 |

N

 |

Not used. Returned if no expected data parameter is set to a compare value.

 |
 |

UC

 |

Unclear. The system may return this value to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

```
> CDCP? 0,8,0,8,(S0_1)
< CDCP 0,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 1,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 2,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 3,"MYDC",2,F00,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 5,"MYDC",2,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
> CDCP? 2,6,4,2,(S0_1)
< CDCP 5,"MYDC",2,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
```

In the second call of CDCP? (the first call just serves to display the underlying situation) the range of interest starts at vector 6. Note that the reply starts with vector 5, and that the first occurrence of MYDC, which lies between vector 2 and vector 6, is not displayed.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › CLKR  CLKR  -  CLocK Resolution）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To set or query the resolution of a multi-port timing specification, specify the name of the specification.

 |
 |

ref_period

 |

Not used. (Ignored)

 |
 |

period_res

 |

The period resolution (in ns) for the specified specification or waveform set.

If necessary, period_res is rounded to nine digits after the decimal point. The allowable maximum period resolution is the maximum tester period value. The minimum period resolution is determined by the hardware (see `Automatic calculation of period resolution for single-port setups`（raw: `02.06.06.01.04.01.02.01_Automatic_calculation_of_period_resolution_for_single-port_setups.md`）).

 |
 |

type

 |

In the query, the type parameter specifies which resolution is queried. The allowed values are:

VIRTUAL: The period resolution (period_res) is queried. This is the default.

EXACT: The clock resolution (clock_res) is queried.

 |
 |

clock_res

 |

In the answer to the query, the clock resolution is returned if type is set to EXACT in the query.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › CLKR  CLKR  -  CLocK Resolution）

```
> CLKR 1,,10
> CLKR? 1
< CLKR 1,1000,10

```

This example sets and queries the period resolution (10 ns) for waveform set 1. Ignore the returned value of the ref_period parameter.

```
> CLKR? "spec_port_1_port_2"
< CLKR "spec_port_1_port_2",50,5.555555556
```

This example queries the period resolution for the multi-port specification `spec_port_1_port_2`.

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DCDT  DCDT  -  Device Cycle DefaulT）

```
DCDT 1,"HOLD"
```

This example defines the default device cycle name HOLD for Waveform Set 1.

```
DCDT? "fast_ARM",(ARMPort)
DCDT "fast_ARM","Cycle",(ARMPort)
```

This example queries the default device cycle name for the ARMPort port in the multi-port specification fast_ARM.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DCUD -  Device Cycle UnDefine）

```
DCUD {waveform_set},{"dev_cyc_name"},{(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DCUD -  Device Cycle UnDefine）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes. Enter ALL for the removal of all device cycles from the device cycle table.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which device cycle definitions are to be deleted. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DCUD -  Device Cycle UnDefine）

```
DCUD 1,"WRITE"
```

This example deletes the device cycle `WRITE` for waveform set 1 from the device cycle table.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DFCR  DFCR  -  DeFine Clock Routing）

|

source_group

 |

specifies the hardware group whose local clock is to be routed to dest_group. The format is Gx, where x is the group number.

 |
 |

dest_group

 |

specifies the hardware group whose inherited clock is to be changed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DFCR  DFCR  -  DeFine Clock Routing）

```
> DFCR?
<
> DFCR G1,G8
> DFCR?
< DFCR G4,G3
< DFCR G4,G1
< DFCR G4,G5
< DFCR G1,G6
< DFCR G1,G2
< DFCR G1,G8
< DFCR G1,G7
```

This example changes the default routing (DFCR? gives an empty reply). Note that the inherited clocks of G6 and of all successors of G6 are also changed.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DPRT  DPRT  -  Default PRimary Timing sets）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + spec_set_no

Note that the spec set ID identifies the primary wavetable in equation based testing.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, a primary multiport specification can be specified.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

The identification number of the timing set. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets (of the selected waveform set or timing specification). The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）. The number you enter must also be less than or equal to the maximum number of timing sets allowed (as defined by DSCP).

In a multiport setup, the timing set number applies to all ports of the specification if no port is specified. Otherwise, the number applies to the specified port.

 |
 |

timing_set_list

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can specify primary timing sets for all ports of the specification by entering a list of numbers separated by commas.

In the query, the numbers of the primary timing sets are returned in a list for all ports of the primary specification unless the numbers are identical for all ports or a port has been specified in the query.

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can specify a port of the specification that was entered as the first parameter. In this case, the timing set number specified as the second parameter will only be applied to the specified port. The port parameter is ignored if a timing set list is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DPRT  DPRT  -  Default PRimary Timing sets）

```
DPRT?
```

returns:

```
DPRT 3,4
```

On sending a query the system reports that the default primary waveform set is 3 and the default primary timing set is 4.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

| device_cycle  | The device_cycle parameter is an integer that defines the absolute maximum number of device cycles that you can create for one pin.

Default: 256

Maximum: 16384

Note that the total number of device cycles gets evenly divided between the combined number of waveform sets and wavetables. If you use the default values, then 256 device cycles divides into the total number of 32 `waveform sets and wavetables`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） to give you 8 device cycles per waveform set/wavetable. If you choose values that do not divide evenly, then the number of device cycles will be rounded up to the next multiple of the `waveform_set`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set`） parameter.

 |
 | devicecycle_set |

The devicecycle_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of device cycle sets that you can create. Device cycle sets are needed for selective digital capture.

Default: 1

Maximum: 128

 |
 | dps_set |

The dps_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of DPS sets you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | level_set |

The level_set parameter is an integer that defines the combined total of level sets for fixed and equation based levels that you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |
 | period_res_prec |

This parameter defines the precision with which the period resolution is calculated by the system. It has no effect on a user defined period resolution (using, for example, the period_res keyword in the equation set).

The default is 4, if the .technology file does not contain this parameter.

If it does, the value of the .technology file is the default.

This value is set to 9, the greatest possible value, when a device is created.

 |
 |

pmu_set

 |

The pmu_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of actions that can be contained in all measurement sets of all PPMU DC sets.

Default: 1024

Maximum: 12800

 |
 | routing_set |

Defines the number of routing sets managed by the firmware, provided by the MCD.

Default: 256

Maximum: 512

 |
 | timing_set |

The timing_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum combined total of timing sets for fixed and equation based timing you can create.

Default: 256

Maximum: 999

The number of timing sets must be equal to or greater than the number of waveform sets, as there must be at least one timing set per waveform set.

 |
 | waveform_set |

The waveform_set parameter defines the maximum combined total of waveform sets (fixed timing) and wavetables (equation based timing) you can create. Thus, if you specify a value of 32, you could, for example, create 10 waveform sets and 22 wavetables.

Default: 32

Maximum: 128

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › DSCP  DSCP  -  Define System Control Parameter）

```
DSCP 256,16,256,32,32,1024,16,1,256,
```
