### Example 1（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
> SPST? lev,all,all
< SPST LEV,1,1,0
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
> SPST? tim,all,all
<  SPST TIM,1,1,0
< SPST TIM,2,22,0
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SPST  -  SPecset STatus）

```
> SPST? TIM,,"mu_burst"
< SPST TIM,,"mu_burst",6
```

In this last example, a multi-port specification is queried. The answer says that bits 1 and 2 have been set. This has the effect that a drive or receive period 1 limit violation will be ignored, and only a period 2 limit violation will be recorded.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

```
STRS? ["exec_context",] [start], [stop], {mode}, [(pinlist)], {spec_type}, {"spec_name[@port[@UNCHANGED]]"}, [stepwidth], {resolution}
```

returns:

```
STRS {res_spec}, [pass_meas_value], [fail_meas_value], [(pinlist)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

|

exec_context

 |

An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） .

 |
 |

start

 |

Double float with up to 5 digits after the decimal point defining the value of spec_name at the start of the search. The maximum valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647, though this may be limited by the maximum and minimum values defined with the spec. If the parameter is omitted, the minimum value as defined in the spec set will be used.

The start value can be greater than the stop value. In this case the search will be in the negative direction.

 |
 |

stop

 |

Double float with up to 5 digits after the decimal point defining the value of spec_name where you want the search to end. The maximum valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647, though this may be limited by the maximum and minimum values defined with the spec. If the parameter is omitted, the maximum value as defined in the spec set will be used.

The stop value can be smaller than the start value. In this case the search will be in the negative direction.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Search mode. Use:

L to specify a linear search,

LB to specify linear/binary search,

B to specify a binary search.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the value of the spec variable is to be modified. This parameter may also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

The @ character indicates all pins. This is the default.

 |
 |

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use :

LEV to specify levels, or

TIM to specify timing.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

A string of up to 64 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

If you use the option @port`[`@UNCHANGED`]`, (see the port parameter), you must include this extension in the double quotes, too.

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can add a port name to the spec variable. This will have the effect that the value of the variable will be modified only for pins belonging to this port. This holds even if the variable has global scope for this port in the timing specification.

If you specify the spec variable without a port in a multi-port setup, its value will only be modified for a pin whose port has the spec variable set to global scope.

For more information on the scope of a variable see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）.

Note that if a port that is specified with the name of the variable it is this port on which the value of the variable will be modified. The setup pins have no influence on this.

On a Pin Scale system, the specification of a port will have an additional effect:

If spec_name is used in the definition of the port period, this port will be temporarily used as the primary port. For more information see `Modifying the period for a search or shmoo in a multi-port setup`（raw: `02.06.09.01.01.01_Modifying_the_period_for_a_search_or_shmoo_in_a_multi-port_setup__Pin_Sc.md`）.

This switch can be suppressed by adding @UNCHANGED to the port name.

 |
 |

stepwidth

 |

The search step width in the unit specified with the corresponding spec. This is optional if mode is B.

 |
 |

resolution

 |

The smallest step size to be used in the search. Especially useful in a binary search of a range of floating point numbers, where the number of values between start and stop is infinite. The unit must be the same as defined with the spec.

 |
 |

res_spec

 |

LT (less than)

LE (less than or equal to)

EQ (equal to)

GE (greater than or equal to)

GT (greater than).

 |
 |

pass_meas_value

 |

A double float defining the passed measured value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

This parameter contains the last (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the first (in a FAIL/PASS transition) value where the test passed.

 |
 |

fail_meas_value

 |

A double float defining the failed measured value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

This parameter contains the first (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the last (in a FAIL/PASS transition) value where the test failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

```
STRS? 0.5,2.0,LB,,LEV,"aclk_vo_swing",0.1,0.1
```

returns

```
STRS GE,2,,
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

|

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use:

 |
 |

LEV

 |

to specify levels, or

 |
 |

TIM

 |

to specify timing.

 |
 |

equation_set_no

 |

Equation set number. An integer in the range 1 to 99.

Use PRM to specify the primary equation set, or, in a multi-port setup, the primary specification as defined with SPRM. In this case, the specset_no parameter is ignored.

In the query, use ALL to display all equation sets.

This parameter must be omitted if a multi-port specification is specified for the thirdparameter.

 |
 |

specset_no

 |

Specset number. An integer in the range of 1 to 99. In the query, use ALL to select all defined specsets.

If specset_no is not set, and equation_set_no is set to ALL or a number, only the spec names in the specified equation sets, but no values are returned.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multi-port setup, enter the name of a specification instead of a spec set number. In this case, the secondparameter must be left empty.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

The name of a base (spec) variable. In a multi-port setup, the same variable name can occur among the spec variables of more than one port within the same specification. In this case, you can qualify the variable name by a port name in the following format

<spec_name>@<port_name>,

if you want to modify the variable on that port only.

Note, however, that the scope of the variable will be set to local for the port in question after such a modification (even if it is set to global in the setup), until the setup is downloaded again.

Note also that in a multi-port setup, you cannot change the value of a variable globally (that is, without specifying a port) unless at least one of the variable instances has its scope set to global in the setup. For basic information on the local and global scope of spec variables in a multi-port setup see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）.

 |
 |

spec_or_equ_name

 |

The name of a base (spec) or derived (equation) variable. An equation variable cannot be specified in the command or in a query which uses the extra parameter.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Requires that the actual values of both base and derived variables are returned.

 |
 |

EQUA

 |

Requires that the actual values of only the derived (equation) variables are returned.

 |
 |

MAX

 |

Requires that the maximum values of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the maximum value of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

MIN

 |

Requires that the maximum of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the minimum value of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

SPEC

 |

Requires that the actual values of only the base (spec) variables are returned.

 |
 |

UNIT

 |

Requires that the units of all the base (spec) variables are returned.

This keyword can also be specified as an extra parameter in combination with the spec_name parameter to retrieve only the unit of the specified spec variable.

 |
 |

value

 |

Float with 5 possible decimal places.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

By this extra parameter, you can modify the runtime definitions for an individual pin. Note that you cannot retrieve the pin specific values with SVLR?.

 Note You can use the pinlist parameter to modify the value of a spec variable of an individual pin, temporarily. If you make a new modification on a different spec variable, only the last modification is kept while the previous spec variable is reset to the setup value defined in the spec file. To make a permanent modification on a spec variable, specify all pins (that is, @) as the pinlist. Otherwise, to change the value of a spec variable of an individual pin permanently, you have to use a specset for each pin and modify the spec variable in that specset. |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

The following example queries the values of the spec variable f in a setup where both single-port and multi-port specifications occur:

```
> SVLR? TIM,ALL,ALL,"f"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",35
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_2",33
< SVLR TIM,1,1,"f",37
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

The next example queries in which equation sets the spec variable f occurs:

```
> SVLR? TIM,ALL,,"f"
< SVLR TIM,1,,"f",
< SVLR TIM,2,,"f",
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › SVLR  SVLR  -  Spec VaLues at Runtime）

For this example assume that the primary timing is a multi-port specification which contains the two ports p_1 and p_2, and that p_1 and p_2 share the spec variable f in this specification. Assume further that f has been set to scope global for the port p_1. Now query the current value of f for p_1, change it globally, and query it again:

```
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",33
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f",43
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",43
```

Since f is global for p_1, its value has been modified. Now change the value a second time, but this time locally, and then try to change it globally again:

```
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1",53
> SVLR TIM,PRM,,"f",43
> SVLR? TIM,PRM,,"f@p_1"
< SVLR TIM,,"spec_p_1_p_2","f@p_1",53
```

The second global command has no effect because f has only local scope after issuing the local command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › TSUS  TSUS  -  Timing Sets USed）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows: `100 * `equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a timing set or the highest number of timing set you want to associate with a given waveform set. The number you enter must be less than or equal to the maximum number of timing sets allowed (as defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command). This number is automatically updated to include any new timing set as it is created. At power-on only one timing set (containing the default values and belonging to the single waveform set) is available.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

For multiport specifications, you can specify a list of the ports for which the number of the timing sets used is to be displayed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › TSUS  TSUS  -  Timing Sets USed）

```
TSUS 3,7
```

This example defines a maximum of 7 timing sets in waveform set 3.

```
TSUS? "spefc",(ARMPort)
TSUS "spefc",3,(ARMPort)
```

This example queries the number of timing sets defined for port ARMPort in the multiport specification spefc.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › TSUX  TSUX  -  Timing Sets Used eXtended）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter ALL for all waveform sets in the query command.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. In the command, TSUX is set to this value for the specified waveform set, if the number is smaller than the current value of `TSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`） for this set. Otherwise, it is set to the current value of TSUS.

 |
 |

SWAP

 |

This command parameter causes the values set by `TSUS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）and TSUX to be switched, that is, TSUS is set to the current value of TSUX , and TSUX to that of TSUS for the specified waveform set.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

This command parameter sets the value of TSUX back to 1 for the specified waveform set.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › UPTD  UPTD  -  UP To Date）

```
UPTD? CONF
```

This example requests if the pin configuration data has been changed since the file was last loaded or saved. If the data has not changed, the response is:

```
UPTD CONF,1
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VCLK  -  Verify CLocK）

```
VCLK? {waveform_set}, {timing_set}, {period}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VCLK {autocorrect}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VCLK  -  Verify CLocK）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter PRM for the primary waveform set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To enter a multi-port specification is only possible if the specification is associated with the default port and if no other ports are configured.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. Enter PRM for the primary timing set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

period

 |

Enter the test system period in ns for which you wish to check whether auto-correction will take place or not. period must be within the maximum and minimum test system periods of the model.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose period you want to check. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ symbol can be used to check all configured pins.

 |
 |

autocorrect

 |

The auto-correction flag returned by the system. It can be:

 |
 |

0

 |

No auto-correction will occur.

 |
 |

1

 |

Auto-correction will occur.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VCLK  -  Verify CLocK）

```
VCLK? 1,1,20,(@)
```

This example checks if a period of 20 ns will cause auto-correction to the edge placements in Timing Set 1 of Waveform Set 1 on any pin. If no auto-correction will occur the following string is returned:

```
VCLK 0
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

```
VDCG? {waveform_set}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {waveform_set}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

Or:

```
VDCG? {specset_id}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {specset_id}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

Or:

```
VDCG? {wavetable_name}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {wavetable_name}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter PRM for the primary waveform set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

Alternatively, you can enter:

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

With this specifier the command checks that:

- The pins in pinlist have exactly the same device cycle names.
- For each device cycle, each pin defines the device cycle with the same length.
 |
 |

 |

FDC

 |

With this specifier the command checks that the first device cycle in the device cycle definition table for each pin in the pinlist has the same length.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names whose device cycles are to be checked. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured pins.

 |
 | dev_cyc_len  | Always 1 for SmarTest 7.10. |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

```
VDCG? 1,ALL,(inputs)
```

returns:

```
VDCG 1,ALL,SLEN
```

This example checks the consistency of all device cycles for pins in the pin group "inputs" in waveform set 1. The test system replies that all device cycles for the specified group are consistently defined.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VTIM  -  Verify TIMing）

```
VTIM? {waveform_set},{timing_set},{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VTIM {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VTIM  -  Verify TIMing）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Specifies the timing sets to be checked. Enter PRM for the Primary Timing Set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by `TSUS, TSUS? - (Timing Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.283_TSUS__TSUS__-__Timing_Sets_USed.md`）.

In a multi-port setup, the check is performed for those pins from pinlist that belong to the same port. If you specify a number, a timing set with this number must be present in every equation set that is associated with a port of the multi-port specification.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be checked. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to check all configured pins.

In a multi-port setup, the pins can belong to more than one port. Only those pins are considered that belong to one of the ports of the specification.

 |
 |

status

 |

The system returns:

 |
 |

0

 |

The timing is not the same.

 |
 |

1

 |

The timing is the same.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VTIM  -  Verify TIMing）

The following example illustrates the working of VTIM? in a multi-port setup. The pins S1_1 and DS0_1 belong to the same port, and S1_2 belongs to another one.

```
> ETDS? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",1,,"d1:0 d2:30",(S1_1,DS0_1)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",2,,"d1:0 d2:12",(S1_1)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",2,,"d1:1 d2:12",(DS0_1)
< ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",1,,"d1:-0.67 d2:1.33 d3:9.3",(S1_2)
```

This call of `ETDS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.117_ETDS__ETDS__-__Edge_Timing_Definition_String.md`） shows that the edge timings of S1_1 and DS0_1 are the same in timing set 1, but not in timing set 2 of the port to which these pins belong.

```
> PCLK? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",1,50,(S1_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",2,20,(S1_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",1,50,(DS0_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",2,20,(DS0_1)
< PCLK "spec_port_1_port_2",1,16.667,(S1_2)
```

This call of `PCLK?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.175_PCLK__PCLK__-__Pin_CLocK.md`） shows that the periods of S1_1 and DS0_1 are the same in the two timing sets of the port.

```
> VTIM? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< VTIM 0
```

VTIM? returns 0 because of the different timings for S1_1 and DS0_1 in timing set 2.

```
> ETDS "spec_port_1_port_2",2,,"d1:0 d2:12",(DS0_1)
> VTIM? "spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,(S1_1,DS0_1,S1_2)
< VTIM 1
```

After changing the edge timing of DS0_1 in timing set 2 to the values of S1_1 with a call of `ETDS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.117_ETDS__ETDS__-__Edge_Timing_Definition_String.md`）, VTIM? returns 1 although DS0_1 has a different timing in timing set 1 and in timing set 2, and S1_2, which belongs to another port, has different values altogether.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VWFG  -  Verify WaveForms in Groups）

There are three different ways to call VWFG?:

```
VWFG? {waveform_set}, ["dev_cyc_name"], {(pinlist)}
VWFG? {specset_id},["dev_cyc_name"],{(pinlist)}
VWFG? {wavetable_name}, ["dev_cyc_name"], {(pinlist)}
```

All three forms return:

```
VWFG {status}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VWFG  -  Verify WaveForms in Groups）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

If you specify the name of a device cycle, only this device cycle will be checked. Enter ALL for all device cycle names in the device cycle table.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins whose definitions you want to check. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to check all configured pins.

 |
 |

status

 |

The system returns:

0: The definitions are not the same.

1: The definitions are the same.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VWFG  -  Verify WaveForms in Groups）

```
> VWFG? "spec_search_wtb","SBC",(ser_in)
< VWFG 1
> VWFG? "spec_search_wtb",,(ser_in)
< VWFG 0
```

According to this example, the waveform and device cycle definition for device cycle SBC are the same for the pins in the group ser_in within the wavetable spec_search_wtb, but this does not hold for all device cycles that are defined for the pins of this group.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VWFS  -  Verify WaveForm Sets）

```
VWFS? {waveform_set_1},{waveform_set_2},{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VWFS {status}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VWFS  -  Verify WaveForm Sets）

|

waveform_set_x

 |

Waveform set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which you wish to check waveform set compatibility. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. The symbol @ can be used to check all configured pins.

 |
 |

status

 |

The system returns:

 |
 |

 |

0

 |

The waveform sets are not compatible.

 |
 |

 |

1

 |

The waveform sets are compatible.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › VWFS  -  Verify WaveForm Sets）

```
VWFS? 1,2,(DATA)
```

This example checks whether waveform sets 1 and 2 are the same for the pins in the group DATA. If they are the same the following string is returned:

```
VWFS 1,(DATA)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WAVE  WAVE  -  WAVEform）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveforms set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query command you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed by double quotes.

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To change or query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

wfIndex

 |

Logical waveform index. This index identifies the logical waveform for which a physical waveform is to be created. The values specified for the DD1, DD2, ED1, and ED2 parameters must be in accordance with the format of this logical waveform.

 |
 |

DD1 and DD2

 |

First and second drive data parameter. These are optional parameters and contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values you can define are:

 |
 |

F0N

 |

drive 0

 |
 |

F1N

 |

drive 1

 |
 |

FN0

 |

tri-state off

 |
 |

FNZ

 |

tri-state on

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

ED1 and ED2

 |

First and second receive data parameter. These are optional parameters. The values you can define are:

 |
 |

F0

 |

compare to 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

compare to 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

compare to intermediate

 |
 |

FX

 |

compare to mask

 |
 |

FU

 |

compare to unstable

 |
 |

C

 |

capture digital data

 |
 |

D

 |

do not capture digital data

 |
 |

The values C and D are used for selective digital capture. The following rules apply to these values:

- A waveform that is used for selective digital capture cannot contain more than one compare action. Therefore, if you specify C or D for one of ED1 or ED2, you cannot specify a value for the other Expected Data parameter.
- If you issue more than one instance of the WAVE command for the same logical waveform, the values you specify for the same Expected Data parameter in these different WAVE instances must be homogeneous; that is, either all or none of them must be C or D. You cannot, for instance, set ED1 to C in one of these WAVE instances, and set it to F1 in another.
 |
 |

pwfIndex

 |

Physical waveform index. Enter an integer between 0 and 31 (0 and 255 on the Pin Scale Digital systems) for each physical waveform . The index is stored in the vector area and references the physical waveform in the physical waveform table.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which physical waveform states are to be defined or read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by commas.

 |
 |

ALLOW_EQ

 |

This extra parameter allows you to define physical waveforms for an equation based timing. Note that only the runtime settings are affected; the definitions in the wavetable are not changed.

Note also the following:

- Every runtime change will affect all specifications that use the respective wavetable.
- Since the new waveform must be evaluated and downloaded for every specification that uses the respective wavetable, the change tends to be rather slow.
- The runtime definitions are not checked for consistency. It is up to the user to ensure this.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WAVE  WAVE  -  WAVEform）

```
> WFDS 1,2,,"d1:D11 d3:0 d4:C11",(pin1,pin2,pin3,pin4)
> WAVE 1,2,F00,,,,4,(pin1,pin2,pin3,pin4)
> WAVE 1,2,F10,,,,5,(pin1,pin2,pin3,pin4)
```

This example first defines a logical waveform with the index 2 for waveform set 1. The waveform uses the data parameter D11, the fixed action 0, and the complement C11 of D11. Then two physical waveforms are defined for logical waveform 2, which are referenced by the physical waveform DC/DC power units 4 and 5. Waveform 4 drives to 0 at edge d1, to 0 at d3, and to 1 at d4. Waveform 5 drives to 1 at edge d1, to 0 at d3, and to 0 at d4.

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WFDF  WFDF  -  WaveForm DeFinition）

```
> WFDF 1,2,N,N,D11,N,N,N,(D0,D2,D2,D3)
```

This example defines a waveform referenced by waveform index 2. The waveform uses the drive data and tri-state parameter 1. Edge number 3 provides the timing for this waveform. The definitions are made for waveform set 1 and for pins D0 to D3.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WFDS  WFDS  -  WaveForm Definition String）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）. For the query you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets. Enter PRM to select the primary waveform set.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed by double quotes.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

wfIndex

 |

Waveform index. Enter an integer between 0 and 255. The index references a waveform in a device cycle. For the query you can also enter ALL for all waveform DC/DC power units. The waveform index is also used by the `WAVE, WAVE? - (WAVEform)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.333_WAVE__WAVE__-__WAVEform.md`） command.

Note that the index must be specified decimally here, whereas in the wavetable, it is coded hexadecimally.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Not used.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

Edge action definition string which consists of drive actions for the drive/ bidirectional edges only. On Pin Scale systems, there is only one drive edge type, which is denoted by di (1 鈮? i 鈮?8).

With these edges you can associate the following actions:

- N: No action
- F0N: Drive 0, no tri-state action
- F1N: Drive 1, no tri-state action
- FN0: No drive action, tri-state off
- FNZ: No drive action, tri-state on
- F00: Drive 0, tri-state off
- F0Z: Drive 0, tri-state on
- F10: Drive 1, tri-state off
- F1Z: Drive 1, tri-state on
- D1N: Drive parameter 1 (DD1), no tri-state action
- D1N: Drive parameter 2 (DD2), no tri-state action
- C1N: Drive complement of parameter 1 (DD1), no tri-state action
- C2N: Drive complement of parameter 2 (DD2), no tri-state action
- DN1: No drive action, tri-state parameter 1 (DD1)
- DN2: No drive action, tri-state parameter 2 (DD2)
- D11: Drive parameter 1 (DD1), tri-state parameter 1 (DD1)
- C11: Drive complement of parameter 1 (DD1), tri-state parameter 1 (DD1)
- D22: Drive parameter 2 (DD2), tri-state parameter 2 (DD2)
- C22: Drive complement of parameter 2 (DD2), tri-state parameter 2 (DD2)

All edges which are not explicitly set are set to N. In the query only those edges that are used are printed.

The following table shows which data-dependent drive actions use the driver formatter, which use the tri-state formatter, and which use both. You have to consider this when assigning parameters to the `WAVE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.333_WAVE__WAVE__-__WAVEform.md`） command. See also `Specifying the actions`（raw: `02.06.06.01.03.01.01_Specifying_the_actions.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

Data-dependent Drive Action

 |

Driver

 |

Tri-state

 |
 |

D1N, D2N, C1N, C2N

 |

yes

 |

no

 |
 |

DN1, DN2

 |

no

 |

yes

 |
 |

D11, C11, D22, C22

 |

yes

 |

yes

 |
 |

 |

On Smart Scale systems, there are two types of drive edges, denoted by fi and si (1 鈮?i 鈮?8). For both of them, only the action codes 0, 1, and N are admitted. But the Smart Scale systems also support the old di syntax. For more information see `Defining waveforms for Smart Scale pins`（raw: `02.06.06.01.03.02_Defining_waveform_shapes_for_Smart_Scale_pins.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

On the expected data side the actions you can define are:

- N: No action
- E0: Edge compare to 0
- E1: Edge compare to 1
- EI: Edge compare to intermediate
- EX: Edge compare to mask
- EU: Edge compare to unstable
- C: Capture digital data (selective digital capture)
- D: Do not capture digital data (selective digital capture)

Note that waveforms that are to be used for selective digital capture must contain exactly one compare action.

- W0: Window open with compare to 0
- W1: Window open with compare to 1
- WI: Window open with compare to intermediate
- WX: Window open with compare to mask
- WU: Window open with compare to unstable
- WC: Window close
- EE1: Edge compare to parameter 1 (ED1)
- EE2: Edge compare to parameter 1 (ED2)
- WE1: Window open with compare to parameter 1 (ED1)
- WE2: Window open with compare to parameter 1 (ED2)
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the waveform is to be defined or read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. The @ symbol can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

ALLOW_EQ

 |

This extra parameter allows you to define or change logical waveforms for an equation based timing. Note that only the runtime settings are affected; the definitions in the wavetable are not changed.

Note also the following:

- Every runtime change will affect all specifications that use the respective wavetable.
- Since the new or changed waveform must be evaluated and downloaded for every specification that uses the respective wavetable, the change tends to be rather slow.
- The runtime definitions are not checked for consistency. It is up to the user to ensure this.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WFDS  WFDS  -  WaveForm Definition String）

```
> WFDS 1,0,,"e1:F00 e2:D1N e3:F00",(io)
> WFDS 1,1,,"r4:EE1",(io)
> WFDS 1,0,,"d1:F00 d2:F10 d3:F10 d4:F00 d5:F10 d6:F00 d7:F10 d8:F00",(clk)

> WFDS? 1,ALL,,(@)
< WFDS 1,0,,"d1:F00 d2:D1N d3:F00",(io)
< WFDS 1,1,,"r4:EE1",(io)
< WFDS 1,0,,"d1:F00 d2:F10 d3:F10 d4:F00 d5:F10 d6:F00 d7:F10 d8:F00",(clk)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WFUD -  WaveForm UnDefine）

```
WFUD {wvf_set},{wfIndex},{(pinlist)}
WFUD {specset_id|"multiport_spec"}, {wfIndex}, [mode], {definition_string}, {(pinlist)}, ALLOW_EQ
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WFUD -  WaveForm UnDefine）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *`equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To change or query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

wfIndex

 |

Logical waveform index. Enter an integer between 0 and 31 (255 on Pin Scale systems).

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the waveform is to be deleted. This parameter can also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. The @ symbol can be used to specify all configured input pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

ALLOW_EQ

 |

This extra parameter allows you to delete a logical waveform for an equation based timing. Note that only the runtime settings are affected; the definitions in the wavetable are not changed.

Note also the following:

- Every runtime change will affect all specifications that use the respective wavetable.
- Since the new or changed waveform must be evaluated and downloaded for every specification that uses the respective wavetable, the change tends to be rather slow.
 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WFUD -  WaveForm UnDefine）

```
WFUD 1,2,(D0,D2,D2,D3)
```

This example deletes a logical waveform defined for waveform set 1 and for pins `D0` to `D3`, referenced by waveform index 2.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WRST -  Waveform ReSeT）

```
WRST {waveform_set}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WRST -  Waveform ReSeT）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WRST -  Waveform ReSeT）

```
WRST 3
```

This example resets all waveform and timing entries for all pins for waveform set 3.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WSDM  WSDM  -  Waveform Set Display Mode）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter ALL for all waveform sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

`Derived as follows:`

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

To query a multiport specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

display_mode

 |

Sets the Vector Setup display mode. This can be:

 |
 |

0

 |

The "classic" display mode. A device cycle has the length of one test system cycle.

 |
 |

1

 |

The "single column" display mode. All pins use the same device cycles.

 |
 |

2

 |

The "multi column" display mode. All pins do not use the same device cycles, the device has two or more separate ports with independent signals.

 |
 |

portlist

 |

For multiport specifications, you can specify the ports for which the vector setup display mode is to be returned.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WSDM  WSDM  -  Waveform Set Display Mode）

```
> WSDM? "spec_1", (port_1)
< WSDM  "spec_1", 0
```

This example queries the display mode of port port_1 in the multiport specification spec_1. The reply shows that it is set to the "classic" display mode.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WSUS  WSUS  -  Waveform Sets USed）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. This is the highest number currently allocated to a waveform set or the highest number of a set you want to load. The number you enter must not exceed the maximum number of waveform sets allowed (defined by the `DSCP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md`） command).

This number is automatically updated to include any new waveform set as it is created. At power-on, only one waveform set (containing one timing set and default values) is available.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Timing Setup Commands › List of timing setup commands › WSUS  WSUS  -  Waveform Sets USed）

```
WSUS 3
```

This example sets the number of used waveform sets to 3.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › Concepts of vector setup › Label definition  sequencer program  and sequencer area）

The following figure shows the label definitions of the standard example and the corresponding sections of the sequencer area for the default port @:

 !`Label Definitions and Sequencer Area`（raw: `../../../../raw/120222.png`）

Since the default port contains all configured pins, the sequencer area on the right side of this figure is stored in the memory of all pins.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › Concepts of vector setup › Sequencer areas and vector areas）

The following figure illustrates the case where one pin belongs to more than one port:

 !`Vector areas for pin belonging to two ports`（raw: `../../../../raw/114615.png`）

Observe the following points in this figure:

- port1 comprises the pins Pin1 and Pin2, while port2 only contains Pin2.
- The arrows indicate which vector area segments belong to which labels. Pin2 has two vector areas, one for the labels of port1 and one for the labels of port2.
- The numbers above the arrow heads are the start addresses of the vector area segments for the respective label (as defined by STVA).
- The association of the vector generating instructions to vector area sub-segments is exemplified by Pin1 and Test 1.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › Concepts of vector setup › Addressing the vector areas）

The following figure displays the relations between the sequencer program and the vector areas of the standard example, and also illustrates the various concepts introduced to describe the structure of these areas:

 !`Vector areas`（raw: `../../../../raw/120207.png`）

The left side of the figure shows a section of the sequencer area for the default port @. It contains the sequencer programs for two labels (command line 4 through 8 and line 9 through 12). The right side displays the associated segments of the vector areas for the pins IN1 and OUT1.

Notice the following points in the figure:

- An instance of the sequencer area for @ is contained in the memory of both pin IN1 and pin OUT1.
- Each of the rows on the right side represents one memory word.
- Every cell of a row represents 8 bits. Every active vector contains one physical waveform index (which is displayed in hexadecimal notation).
- The padding (inactive) vectors are left blank in the figure.
- The numbers to the left of the memory words specify the absolute start addresses of the words within the vector areas.
- The numbers above the memory words are the logical vector numbers.
- The first label contains two sequencer constructs:

  - The first construct consists of the RPTV instruction and the single words starting at address 408 in the vector areas of both pins. Only the first 7 data cells of this block contain waveform DC/DC power units.
  - The second construct consists of the GENV instruction and the two words starting at addresses 416 and 424. The last 7 cells of the second word contain no user data.

The second label contains one sequencer construct (framed by a dotted line), which comprises two words.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › Concepts of vector setup › The pattern master file）

The syntax of the pattern master file is as follows:

hp93000,pattern_master_file,0.1

[path:

 [<relative_or_absolute_path_1 >]]

files:

 <file_name_1_1>

 <file_name_1_2>

 ...

 <file_name_1_m>

[[path:

 [<relative_or_absolute_path_2>]]

files:

 <file_name_2_1>

 <file_name_2_2>

 ...

 <file_name_2_n>

...]

The default for the path is the vectorssubdirectory of the current device. But if you specify a path, note that the reference directory for relative paths is the waste subdirectory of the device. Therefore, if your pattern files are in the subdirectory sample of the vectors directory, you must specify the relative path to this directory as ./vectors/sample.

You can add comments to a pattern master file after "-- " (2 times the minus sign followed by a space) at the beginning of a line.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › Concepts of vector setup › The pattern master file）

Both the usage of relative paths and the insertion of comments are illustrated by the following example file:

```

hp93000,pattern_master_file,0.1

-- The following file must reside in <device>/vectors:
files:
   sample1.binl

-- The following path points to <device>/vectors/pmfl_test:
path: ../vectors/pmfl_test

files:
  sample2.binl.gz
  sample3.binl.gz
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APDV -  APpenD Vectors）

```
APDV {cmd_No}, {vect_length}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APDV -  APpenD Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

A number that identifies the command within the sequencer area of the port to which the label belongs. Enter the command number of a GENV or RPTV instruction within the selected label.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The number of vectors you wish to append. Enter an integer in the range 0 to the maximum vector length.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APDV -  APpenD Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,520,,,(@)
< ...
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> APDV 2,25
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,34,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,544,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example appends 25 vectors to the end of the sequencer construct with the command number 2. Note the change of the start address in command line 4.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

```
APTS {"label"}, {type}, {base_wf_set|"wavetable"|specset_id|"multiport_spec"} [,(port)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

|

label

 |

Defines the name of the new label. Enter an alphanumeric string in double quotes containing 1 to 128 characters.

 |
 |

type

 |

The label type. It has the following options:

 |
 |

MAIN

 |

The MAIN program. You can make calls to both types of subroutine (SJMP and SVEC), execute commands and sequencer instructions, generate vectors and use SSRC and SRCV instructions.

 |
 |

SVEC

 |

Vector subroutine. A subroutine where you can execute commands and sequencer instructions and generate vectors. You can nest SVEC subroutines up to 7 levels deep.

 |
 |

DSRC

 |

The digital source label. A type of label used only by SSRC and SRCV (see `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）). A DSRC label is not executable. The contents of the DSRC label are determined by the DVCU command. See `DVCU, DVCU? - (Define Vector variable Configuration Usage)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.96_DVCU__DVCU__-__Define_Vector_variable_Configuration_Usage.md`）

 |
 |

base_wf_set

 |

Defines a base waveform set. Enter an integer in the range of 1 to the number of used waveform sets as defined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

wavetable

 |

The name of the base wavetable. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *` equation_set_no `+ ` specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_

spec

 |

In a multiport setup, you can also specify the name of a multiport specification.

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter fulfills two functions. It primarily determines the port with which the label is to be associated. If you do not specify a port, the label is associated with the default port @.

If you have entered a multiport specification as the third parameter, the parameter also serves to identify uniquely the base wavetable for the label.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

```
> APTS "test_2",MAIN,"gross_func_wtb"
> SQLB? ALL,ALL,(@)
< SQLB "test_1",MAIN,0,3,"gross_func_wtb"
< SQLB "test_2",MAIN,4,6,"gross_func_wtb"
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,12,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,520,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
```

This example appends a label to the sequencer area of the default port @. The label has the name `test_2`, is of type MAIN and is configured with the base wavetable `gross_func_wtb`. The following two queries display the result of the call. The STVA instruction of the new label points to the actual end of the vector areas.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › APTS -  APpend TeSt）

```
APTS "NEW",MAIN,"spec_port_1_port_2",(port_1)
```

This example appends the label `NEW` to the sequencer area of port `port_1`. The base wavetable is identified uniquely by specifying the multi-port specification `spec_port_1_port_2` and the port `port_1`, which belongs to `spec_port_1_port_2`.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › BCMT  BCMT  -  Binary CoMmenT）

```
> BCMT?
< BCMT 0,49,#9000000078&!This is the first vector
  of test_2&0This is the first vector of test_3
```

This call of BCMT? displays the comments of the default port. The `&` character (with the decimal ASCII value 38) indicates the (identical) length of the two comments. The first comment is at vector 33 (decimal ASCII value of the ! character), the second at vector 48 (decimal ASCII value of the 0 character).

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › BLUP -  BLock UP to date）

|

name

 |

The name of a label.

 |
 |

type

 |

The only allowed option is:

 |
 |

 |

LBL

 |

This comprises labels of types MAIN, BRST, SVEC, and MPBU.

 |
 |

state

 |

This parameter defines the status and can be one of the following:

 |
 |

 |

UPTD

 |

Label is up to date.

 |
 |

 |

CHNG

 |

Label was changed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › BLUP -  BLock UP to date）

```
BLUP "test",LBL,UPDT,
```

This example sets the state of label `test` to up to date.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CMNT  CMNT  -  CoMmeNT）

|

act_vect_of_port

 |

Specifies the active vector of the referenced port at which the comment is to be inserted, or, in the query, the first vector of which the comment is to be displayed.

Note that you must count the active vectors of the port consecutively across all of its labels, starting from 0. Suppose, for example, that two labels, test_1 and test_2, are associated with the port, where test_1 has 8 active vectors, and test_2 has 3. Then, to insert a comment at the second vector of test_2, you must enter 9.

 |
 |

text

 |

A string of up to 250 characters. The string must be enclosed with double quotes.

Comments can contain any characters with ASCII codes from 32 to 126, that is, all printable ASCII characters. To put a double quote character (", ASCII 34) into a comment, enter two double quote characters.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

In the query, the range of active vectors to be displayed, starting from act_vect_of_port. It can cross label boundaries.

 |
 |

port

 |

Specifies the port to which the active vectors associated with the comments belong. If you do not specify a port, the comments to the active vectors of the default port @ are set or read.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CMNT  CMNT  -  CoMmeNT）

Display the sequencer area of the default port:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,528,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 7,GENV,12,,,(@)
< SQPG 8,STOP,,,,(@)
```

Add the comment "Start of test_2" to the active vector 15 of the default port @, that is, to the first active vector of the second label:

```
> CMNT 15,"Start of test_2"
```

Activate test_2 for editing and display the comments for its vectors with the label specific TCMT? query:

```
> TSTL "test_2",(@)
> TCMT? 0,11
< TCMT 0,"Start of test_2"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CMVC -  Clear and MoVe Comments）

CMVC {src_vec_No}, {dst_vec_No}, {vect_length}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CMVC -  Clear and MoVe Comments）

|

src_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the source range.

 |
 |

dst_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the destination range.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The vector range from which comments are to be moved. Specify 0 in order to simply delete the vectors between the source and the destination number.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CMVC -  Clear and MoVe Comments）

```
> CMNT? 0,6
< CMNT 0,"0"
< CMNT 1,"1"
< CMNT 2,"2"
< CMNT 3,"3"
< CMNT 4,"4"
< CMNT 5,"5"
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> CMVC 0,4,2
> CMNT? 0,6
< CMNT 4,"0"
< CMNT 5,"1"
```

This example moves comments in the vector range 0 to 1 to the range 4 to 5. The previous comments for vectors 4 and 5 are overwritten, the comments for vector 2 and 3 are cleared.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CNGV -  CoNnect Generate Vectors）

```
CNGV {(cmd_No)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CNGV -  CoNnect Generate Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number which references the first of the two consecutive GENV sequencer constructs.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CNGV -  CoNnect Generate Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,8,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> CNGV 2
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,17,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CPYV -  CopY Vectors）

```
CPYV {src_vec_No}, {dst_vec_No}, {vect_length}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

src_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the source range.

 |
 |

dst_vec_No

 |

The logical vector number that determines the start of the destination range.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The length of the vector range to be copied.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins for which vectors are to be copied. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to modify the vectors of all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › CPYV -  CopY Vectors）

```
> SQPG? all,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> $VECD? PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1)
< VECD PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1),
  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0001
  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000
  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000
```

The first three active vectors of the RPTV instruction (with the logical vector numbers 9 to 11) are set to 0 for pin S0_1. Now activate the label for editing and copy vectors 12 to 14 to position 9 for S0_1:

```
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> CPYV 12,9,3,(S0_1)
```

Display the result:

```
> $VECD? PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1)
< VECD PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1),
  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0001
  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000
  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0001  0000 0011  0000 0001  0000 0000  0000 0000
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DELI -  DELete Instruction）

```
DELI {cmd_No}, {count}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DELI -  DELete Instruction）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number which references the first sequencer instruction to be deleted.

 |
 |

count

 |

This parameter defines the total number of instructions to be deleted.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DELI -  DELete Instruction）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,27,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,7,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,544,,,(@)
< ...
> DELI 2,1
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,7,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,544,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example deletes the sequencer instruction with command number 2 from the sequencer area of the default port @. Note that since the vectors of the instruction are not deleted, the start address of the following label (STVA instruction at command number 4) does not change.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DELV -  DELete Vectors）

```
DELV {cmd_No}, {vect_length}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DELV -  DELete Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number which references the sequencer construct where vectors are to be deleted. The instruction of the construct must be GENV (GENerate Vectors) or RPTV (RePeaT Vectors)

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The number of active vectors to be deleted at the end of the referenced sequencer construct.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DELV -  DELete Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,34,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,544,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> DELV 2,25
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,520,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
```

This example deletes 25 vectors from the end of the sequencer construct referenced by command number 2. Three memory words become inactive in the process and are deleted. The start address of the following label (command line 4) is adjusted.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DLTS -  DeLete TeSt）

```
DLTS {"label"}[, (port)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DLTS -  DeLete TeSt）

|

label

 |

Specifies the label to be deleted.

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter is only relevant for multi-port burst labels. If you call DLTS with a multi-port burst label and you do not specify a port, the label is deleted for all ports. If you specify a port, the label is only deleted for this port.

 |


This example deletes the label referenced by `MPBU_port_1_port_2` from the port `port_1`.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DMAS  DMAS  -  Define Memory Area Size）

|

area

 |

The area parameter specifies the type of data for which a memory area is to be set or read. It can be one of the following:

 |
 |

 |

PARA

 |

Only the DMAS? PARA (PARAllel vector area) query is supported. It returns the current end of the vector areas for the different memory types. Note that in case of a multiport setup, values are only returned if the PER_PORT option is explicitly set as the third parameter.

 |
 |

 |

PPSQ

 |

Only the DMAS? PPSQ (Per Pin SeQuencer subroutine) query is supported. It returns the space currently used for per pin sequencer subroutines. It can only be applied to the default port @.

 |
 |

 |

RSLT

 |

The DMAS? RSLT(ReSuLT area) query returns how much memory is available for result data (Error Map in the external memory or digital capture data).

 |
 |

 |

SAVE

 |

The DMAS? SAVE query returns the size of the currently used memory for the area types PARA, PPSQ, and SQPG.

Note that in case of a multiport setup, PARA values are only returned if the PER_PORT option is set explicitly as the third parameter.

 |
 |

 |

SQPG

 |

The SQPG (Sequencer ProGramming area) option allocates memory for a number of sequencer instructions. The allocated command lines are filled with NOP instructions.

The DMAS? SQPG query returns the current end of the sequencer areas for the specified ports.

 |
 |

 |

MFRE

 |

The MFRE (Memory Free RangE) option can only be used in the query. It reports the actual maximum number of vectors that can be added to each of the specified ports, pins or channels.

 |
 |

 |

MFRP

 |

The MFRP (Memory Free Range per Pool) option can only be used in the query. It reports the free memory space for the specified ports from the pool (test processor, channel group) perspective.

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

The ALL (ALL areas) option can only be used in a query. It returns the size of the currently used memory for the area types PARA, PPSQ, and SQPG, and in addition also the space that is free for result data (area type RSLT).

Note that in case of a multiport setup, PARA values are only returned if the PER_PORT option is set explicitly as the third parameter.

 |
 |

size

 |

In the command, the size parameter defines the number of sequencer instructions for which memory is to be allocated on the specified port (area type SQPG). One sequencer instruction requires the space of 8 vectors. Enter a number of instructions between 0 and MAX_FREE_MEM/ 8 vectors.

In the query replies, this parameter either specifies the used space (for example, with area type PARA) or the available free space (with area types RSLT, MFRE, and MFRP).

 |
 |

size_1

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the amount of free vector memory at the end of a specified channel for the PER_CHANNEL option of MFRE and MFRP.

 |
 |

size_2

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the largest block of free vector memory on a specified channel for the PER_CHANNEL option of MFRE and MFRP.

 |
 |

size_3

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the total amount of free vector memory on a specified channel for the PER_CHANNEL option of MFRE and MFRP.

 |
 |

pool_size

 |

This query reply parameter specifies the total amount of free vector memory on a pool (channel group, test processor) which shares a channel with a specified port for the PER_POOL option of MFRP.

 |
 |

memory

 |

Specifies the type of memory which is acted upon:

 |
 |

 |

SM

 |

Sequencer memory. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

SHMEM

 |

A special kind of SM for memory sharing in multisite setups. For details see `Selecting the memory type`（raw: `02.06.07.01.04.01_Selecting_the_memory_type.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

HSER

 |

A special kind of SM for patterns used in SmartLoop testing. For details see `Defining a compliance pattern for pattern鈥慴ased SmartLoop testing`（raw: `02.06.17.04.01_Defining_a_compliance_pattern_for_pattern__ased_SmartLoop_testing.md`）.

 |
 |   | SMEXT  | A special kind of memory for vectors, used only when himem is enabled in the .technology file. See `Technology file for a device - himem`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.07.02.01.02_Technology_file_for_a_device.md#_49363__row_himem`） for details. This option can only be used in the query with MFRE or MFRP. |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

All types of memory. This option can only be used in the query.

 |
 |

PER_PORT

 |

This query option requires the answer to be given per port. This is the default.

Note however that this option must be specified for area type PARA; otherwise DMAS? will return no answer. This also applies to the PARA values for area types SAVE and ALL.

 |
 |

PER_PIN

 |

This query option is only supported by area types MFRE and RSLT, Its point is that the amount of free vector space or result space can be different for different pins of the same port.

 |
 |

PER_CHANNEL

 |

This option is only supported by the MFRE and the MFRP area types. With area type MFRE, it causes DMAS? to return three values for each specified channel in the following order:

- size_1: The amount of memory that is available at the end of the vector memory
- size_2: The size of the largest free vector memory block
- size_3: The sum of all free blocks

With area type MFRP, the same three values are returned, but for all channels of any pool that supplies channels to one of the specified ports.

 |
 |

PER_POOL

 |

This option is only supported by the MFRP area type. It causes DMAS? to return the total free space of all pools (channel groups, test processors) that supply channels for the specified ports.

 |
 |

port

 |

The port for which areas are to be defined or for which information is requested. The default port, to which all pins belong, is denoted by the @ character.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

The ports for which information is to be retrieved.

 |
 |

pin, pin_list

 |

The pins for which information is requested or returned.

 |
 |

channel, channel_list

 |

The channels for which information is requested or returned.

 |
 |

pool_channels

 |

The channels of the pool to which the channels of those ports belong that are specified in the query.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DMAS  DMAS  -  Define Memory Area Size）

The following example illustrates the various options of the MFRE and MFRP queries. First, the free memory range of the `port12` port is queried on the port level:

```
> DMAS? MFRE,,(port12)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,84288,(port12)
```

On the pin level, the corresponding query and reply look as follows:

```
> DMAS? MFRE,,PER_PIN,(port12)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,84288,(Pin1)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,88288,(Pin2)
```

Note that the query per port returns the smaller of the two values.

`Pin1` is mapped to channel 10101, `Pin2` to channel 10102. Thus the corresponding channel related query and its reply are

```
> DMAS? MFRE,,PER_CHANNEL,(10101,10102)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,84212,84312,84640,(10101)
< DMAS MFRE,SM,88312,88312,88640,(10102)
```

The figures are slightly different, because the query per channel only considers the hardware.

Finally, the two possible options for MFRP, applied to `port12`, produce

```
> DMAS? MFRP,,PER_CHANNEL,(port12)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,84212,84312,84640,(10101)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,88312,88312,88640,(10102)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,84212,84312,84640,(10103)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,90464,90464,90736,(10104)
```

 for the PS9G pool 10101 through 10104, and

```
> DMAS? MFRP,,PER_POOL,(port12)
< DMAS MFRP,SM,347400,(10101,10102,10103,10104)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DPPC -  Define Per Pin subroutine Configuration）

|

name

 |

Name of the Pin-Per Sequencer Subroutine label. For the query, you can enter ALL to return all PPSS labels.

 |

parameter

There are various parameters for the PPSS labels:

SMLEN

 |
 |

RELOC

specifies that the subroutine is relocatable.

 |
 |

MWAIT

 |

Used internally.

 |
 |

MAXLEN

 |

Used internally.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

In the query, to display information about all parameters.

 |
 |

value

 |

Value for the parameter specified as parameter.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Pins for which a per-pin subroutine is valid.

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › DPPS  DPPS  -  Define Per Pin Subroutine label）

|

name

 |

Per-pin Subroutine name. This parameter can be used to call the subroutine from a parallel sequencer program.

For the query, you can also enter ALL to return all per pin subroutine label names

 |

cycle_len

Per-pin cycle length.

|

name

address

pinlist
