### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › FTSM  FTSM  -  Functional Test Set Mask）

```
FTSM {mode}, [run_to], [mask_before], [mask_after][,(ref_port)]
FTSM?
FTSM?
```

returns:

```
FTSM CLEAR, , ,
```

or

```
FTSM SET, [run_to], [mask_before], [mask_after][,(ref_port)]
```

  Parameters

 | mode  | Lets you set the mode of the FTSM command. The mode can be: |
 | SET  | In this mode the parameters run_to, mask_before, and mask_after are set and used in the next sequencer run. The original SQGB values are saved and restored with the next FTSM CLEAR command. |
 | CLEAR  | The FTSM parameters run_to, mask_before, and mask_after will be ignored by subsequent sequencer runs. Instead, the original SQGB values are restored. Original values are the values that had been active before execution of the FTSM SET command to set a specific mask. |
 | run_to |

The pattern is executed up to the specified cycle, including this cycle. This parameter cannot be used together with the mask_before or mask_after parameter except for two cases:

- If the mask_before parameter is set to 0.
- If the run_to parameter is set to N and the mask_after parameter to N + 1.

The cycle number must be within the range [0 ... 2^48 - 2]

 |
 | mask_before |

All cycles before the specified cycle are masked and do not contribute to the pass/fail result. The specified cycle is not masked.

If mask_before is not a multiple of 8, cycles will be recorded starting from the next lowest multiple of 8, but those up to the specified cycle will be discarded afterwards.

 |
 | mask_after  | All cycles after the specified cycle are masked and do not contribute to the pass/fail result. The specified cycle is not masked. (Recording will run to the end of the test, but the cycles following the specified one will be discarded afterwards.) |
 | ref_port |

For a multi-port burst, this parameter specifies the reference port to which the cycle numbers of the run_to, mask_before, and mask_after parameters refer.

If you have set the run_to parameter, then the sequencers will be stopped for all ports after the reference port has completed the requested number of cycles. The mask_before, and mask_after parameters are only applied to the specified port. The other ports will not be masked,

Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

   |  Application Used in the parametric functional test. Errors and warnings

An error is generated if:

- A value (run_to, mask_before, mask_after) is not in the valid range of [0... 2^48 - 2].
- The run_to and mask_before parameters are specified, and run_to is equal or bigger than mask_before.
- The run_to and the mask_after parameters are specified, and run_to is bigger than mask_after.

A warning is generated if:

- The run_to parameter and the mask_before parameter are specified and run_to < mask_before. In this case the pattern executed will always pass as all cycles executed are masked out for result evaluation.
- The run_to parameter and the mask_after parameter are specified and run_to <= mask_after. In this case the entry for the mask_after parameter can be omitted as the sequencer will not even execute the cycles that are masked out.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › FTSM  FTSM  -  Functional Test Set Mask）

```
FTSM?
```

returns:

```
FTSM CLEAR, , ,
FTSM SET, ,10,20
```

The FTSM? query returns the current FTSM settings.

The FTSM SET command masks all cycles except for those in the range from cycle 10 to cycle 20.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › GETA  -  GET vector memory Address information）

GETA? {type}, [param_1], {param_2}, {(pinlist)}

returns:

GETA {type}, {param_1}, {param_2}, {applic}, {start_addr}, {length}, {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › GETA  -  GET vector memory Address information）

|

type

 |

Specifies the type of test for which vector area address information is required. The only allowed value is VEC (for VECtors).

 |
 |

param_1

 |

param_1 requires a label name. The present implementation always takes the label currently activated with the TSTL command, so you must leave this parameter blank in the query. The reply specifies the currently activated label.

 |
 |

param_2

 |

param_2 requires a logical vector number.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to obtain data for all pins.

 |
 |

applic

 |

A reply parameter. Returns the type of the test application:

 |
 |

PARA

 |

Parallel test.

 |
 |

start_addr

 |

A reply parameter. It returns the absolute address of the queried vector in the vector area.

 |
 |

length

 |

A reply parameter. It returns an integer giving the remaining active vectors of the sequencer construct starting from the queried vector.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › GETA  -  GET vector memory Address information）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> GETA? VEC,,9,(S0_1)
< GETA VEC,"test_1",9,PARA,520,6,(S0_1)
```

This example queries the absolute address of the parallel vector with the logical vector number 9 (the first active vector of the RPTV instruction) in the label test_1 for pin S0_1. Note that 7 padding vectors exist between the last active vector of the GENV instruction and the first active vector of the RPTV instruction.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › INGV -  INsert Generate Vectors）

```
INGV{cmd_No}, {num_vec}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › INGV -  INsert Generate Vectors）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number before which the GENV instruction is to be inserted.

 |
 |

num_vec

 |

The number of vectors that are to be generated by the GENV sequencer instruction.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › INGV -  INsert Generate Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,16,,,(@)
< ...
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> INGV 3,11
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,11,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,32,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example inserts a GENV instruction for 11 vectors before command 2. Note that the memory type is SM, as in command 0, and that the address of command 5 has been increased.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › INSI -  INsert Instructions）

```
INSI {cmd_No}, {count}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › INSI -  INsert Instructions）

|

cmd_No

 |

The command number before which instructions are to be inserted.

 |
 |

count

 |

This parameter defines the number of NOP instructions to be inserted.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › INSI -  INsert Instructions）

```
TSTL "test_1",(@)
INSI 358, 12
```

This example inserts 12 NOP sequencer instructions before command number 358.

returns:

```
NODV {num_vec}
```

num_vec

returns the number of active vectors.

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › RSET -  ReSET）

```
RSET {specifier}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › RSET -  ReSET）

|

specifier

 |

The specifier can be:

 |
 |

DPS

 |

Loads the default power supply setup for standard DPSs.

 |
 |

FCR

 |

Loads the default clock routing.

 |
 |

LEV

 |

Loads the default power supply setup for standard DPSs.

Level: 0 V

Current: 50 mA

Off state: minimum current

Setup time: 0 ms

This default states are:

UHC4T

- Connect state: normal
- Level: 0 V
- Range: 4 V
- Clamp: 4 A
- Clamp-Range: 40 A
- Disconnect state: HIZ
- Voltage drop force: 250 mV
- Voltage drop return: 250 mV
- Clamp mode: limit (see `UHCM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md`）)
- DUT capacitor mode: off

Fast preload: 0 ms

 |
 |

TIM

 |

Loads the default timing setup. The settings are:

Timing Sets

- Defined Timing Sets: 1
- Allowed Timing Sets: 256

Waveform Sets

- Defined Waveform Sets: 1
- Allowed Waveform Sets: 16

Waveforms: not defined

Breakwaveform: defined

Events

- Action: NOP
- Timing: 0 ns

Min Period: 4 ns

- This is dependent on the test system hardware configuration.

Device Cycles: not defined

Default Device Cycle: ""

 |
 |

VEC

 |

Loads the default vector setup. The Vector Memory contains:

No vectors

No tests (and therefore no labels)

No comments

No sequencer programs (no instructions)

 |
 |

ATR

 |

Loads the default edge attributes.

Pin attribute: set to 0

 |
 |

PDL

 |

Loads the default path delay attributes.

Cable assembly delay attribute: set to 0

Fixture delay attribute: set to 0

System attribute: set to 0

 |
 |

CAL

 |

Loads the default calibration data.

Level calibration data

Timing calibration data

 |
 |

MTPP

 |

Resets memory test and per-pin sequencer subroutine data.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › RSET -  ReSET）

```
RSET TIM
```

This example resets all waveform sets and timing sets and loads the hardware with the default vector rate and edge placement values. Only waveform set 1 and timing set 1 in waveform set 1 is active.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SAOF  SAOF  -  Set Alternating Operation Features）

|

mode

 |

The operation mode which can take the following values:

 |
 |

ZERO

 |

Editing mode. This is the default.

 |
 |

APP

 |

This mode serves to append data to the sequencer and vector areas. In order to do that, you must first allocate memory for the respective area with the DMAS command. Now,in editing mode, the DMAS command defines the size of the area (it starts from address 0). If, however, the system is in APP mode, the existing area will be expanded by the size specified in the DMAS command.

Note that you cannot iterate this step. If you allocate memory in APP mode for a second time, the first expansion will be redefined. In order to further expand the area, you must first issue SAOFAPP again.

 |
 |

LOAD

 |

Load vectors. This mode improves performance of a vector download.

 |
 |

TMLD

 |

Load timing and/or pin attributes. This mode improves performance of a timing download.

 |
 |

EGRP

 |

Edit group definitions.

 |
 |

label

 |

If you call SAOF with a label name, you can generate a vector file for this label only.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SAOF  SAOF  -  Set Alternating Operation Features）

The following example illustrates the effects of the APP mode:

```
> SAOF?
< SAOF ZERO
> DMAS SQPG,SM,4,(@)
> DMAS SQPG,SM,3,(@)
> DMAS? SQPG,SM,(@)
< DMAS SQPG,SM,3,(@)
> SAOF APP
> DMAS SQPG,SM,4,(@)
> SAOF ZERO
> DMAS? SQPG,SM,(@)
< DMAS SQPG,SM,7,(@)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SPGV -  SPlit Generate Vectors）

```
SPGV {vec_No}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SPGV -  SPlit Generate Vectors）

|

vec_No

 |

The logical vector number at which a GENV sequencer construct is to be split.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SPGV -  SPlit Generate Vectors）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,16,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STVA,528,,,(@)
< ...
> SPGV 7
> TSTL "test_1",(@)
> SQPG ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,7,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STVA,536,,,(@)
< ...
```

This example splits a GENV sequencer construct at command number 2 before vector 7. Note the adjustment of the start address in command 6.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

|

mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

ACQF

 |

ACQuire Failure mode. Only failed cycles are recorded, starting after analyze_delay cycles. If analyze_delay is not a multiple of 8, recording starts after the nearest smaller multiple of 8. In this mode the Error Map is called the Acquire Failure Map.

As the test proceeds the Acquire Failure Map is filled with failure data until the test stops or the map becomes completely full, whichever occurs first. If the map stops recording before the test has finished, the sequencer, which is in standard mode, continues executing the test until the end.

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of ACQF is reproduced by:

DCGM FAIL,STRT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

ACFF

 |

This mode is functionally identical to ACQF. It is obsolete and should not be used in new applications.

 |
 |

EL

 |

EndLess. The sequencer repeats the complete test, including primaries and multiport synchronization, in an endless loop and can only be stopped by Break.

The analyze_delay parameter is ignored. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented mode.

This mode is used for oscilloscope tests. The Error Map functions as a rolling buffer. After stopping the sequencer, the Error Map shows the last "buffer-full" of recorded cycles.

 |
 |

ELPT

 |

EndLess PaTtern. The sequencer repeats only the user program. This avoids critical holds during measurement.

In case of multiport testing, ports may run with different frequencies. Using the ELPT mode in this case, can lead to the situation, that for loop counts >1 the synchronization is no longer executed.

 |
 |

EMPS

 |

Error Map PoSitioning. The Error Map is in cycle oriented mode, the sequencer in default mode. The analyze_delay parameter specifies the end of the recorded area. If it is not a multiple of 8, the last cycle to be displayed is the largest multiple of 8 that is smaller than analyze_delay. The first cycle to be displayed is determined by the size of the Error Map (8k cycles).

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of EMPS is reproduced by:

DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

SE

 |

Stop on Error. The sequencer runs from the beginning of the test and stops when an error is encountered. If no errors occur, the sequencer runs to the end of the test and stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. The analyze_delay parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

SEEL

 |

Stop on Error and EndLess. The sequencer repeats the test in an endless loop, unless an error is encountered, whereupon it stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode. This mode is used to locate sporadic failures.

 |
 |

STSQ

 |

STop SeQuencer. Stops the sequencer after analyze_delay cycles. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. See also the query `GETC? - (GET Cycles)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.131_GETC__-__GET_Cycles.md`） for the analyze_delay count.

 |
 |

STRD

 |

In the query reply, this mode is displayed if the current combination of recording mode, as set with DCGM, and interpretation of the Error Map position, as set with DCRP, is different from all the other SQGB modes. For example, the Error Map can be in cycle oriented recording mode, and analyze_delay be interpreted as a start value.

In the command, this option leaves it to SmarTest to select the appropriate recording mode (cycle oriented or acquire failure), unless the recording mode has been explicitly set with DCGM.

 |
 |

STSV

 |

STop Sequencer on Vector. Stops the sequencer at the logical vector number specified in the analyze_delay parameter before executing the vector. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM.

Note that the STSV option cannot be used if no start label has been defined with SQSL, or if the start label is a burst or multi-port burst label.

 |
 |

analyze_delay

 |

Sets the analyze delay. This parameter is mandatory for the STSQ and STSV modes. Its interpretation depends on the selected mode parameter. The number must be between 1 (0 for ACQF) and 281,474,976,710,655 = 2^48 - 1 (2^48 - 2 for ACQF).

If the mode parameter is set to STSV, three cases must be distinguished:

- If analyze_delay is an existing logical vector number of the actual start label, the sequencer will be stopped at this logical vector before executing the vector.
- If analyze_delay specifies the total number of logical vectors (= greatest logical vector number of the test + 1) the sequencer stops at the last valid vector.
- If analyze_delay is greater than the total number of logical vectors, an error message is issued.
 |
 |

ref_port

 |

This parameter accepts a single port. It must be specified in the following situation:

- The selected mode requires an analyze delay (but is different from STSV), and
- the start label is a multi-port burst.

It specifies the port which is used for counting the cycles specified with the analyze_delay parameter. When this reference port has completed the specified number of cycles, the sequencers will be stopped, or cycle recording started or stopped, for all ports. Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

 |
 |

port_list

 |

If the current mode requires an analyze delay, you can specify a port list in the query. The reply will give the calculated analyze delays for those ports that are not used as the reference port. These delays are derived from the analyze delay of the reference port and the ratio between the period lengths of the reference port and the other port in the primary timing setup. If you specify @@, SQGB will return the settings for all ports of the current start label.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

```
> PCLK? "mu_burst",1,(@@)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,20,(P1)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,10,(P2)
> SPRM "mu_burst",1,,
> SQSL "mu_burst"
> SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
> SQGB? (@@)
< SQGB STSQ,15,(P1)
< SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
```

This example configures the sequencers to stop when port P2 has completed 30 cycles. Port P1, whose period length is twice the period length of P2, will be stopped after 15 cycles. Note that P1 and P2 must belong to the same sequencing group.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQLA  SQLA  -  SeQuencer Label Attribute）

|

type

 |

Currently, LBL is the only possible value. This is also the default.

 |
 |

name

 |

A sequencer label. If ALL is specified in the query, then all labels of the specified port are returned together with their attributes.

 |
 |

attr_key_i=

attr_val_i

 |

Attribute-value pairs. Valid attribute names are:

 |
 |

PARA_MEM

 |

Specifies the memory type for parallel vectors. Possible values are:

SM = standard memory (default for MAIN and SVEC)

NONE = no memory for parallel vectors (default for all label types except MAIN and SVEC)

SHMEM = memory shared for different sites of the same pin (only for 7.x, for details see `Selecting the memory type`（raw: `02.06.07.01.04.01_Selecting_the_memory_type.md`）.

HSER = memory for SmartLoop鈩? initialization patterns (see `Defining a compliance pattern for pattern鈥慴ased SmartLoop testing`（raw: `02.06.17.04.01_Defining_a_compliance_pattern_for_pattern__ased_SmartLoop_testing.md`）)

An empty value will delete the attribute definition. This attribute can only be changed if the sequencer program of the label contains no GENV or RPTV instructions.

 |
 |

PARA_MCTX

 |

Specifies the mode context that is associated with the label. A mode context defines a type (I, O, or IO) and a mode (std or fast) for every configured pin. You define mode contexts in the Pin Configuration tool. The default mode context, which sets the mode of every pin to std, has the name DEFAULT.

Note that within a test setup, the label must have the same mode context as the associated timing and level data.

 |
 |

If ALL is specified in the query, all attributes for the given labels are returned. If SAVE or an attribute name is specified in the query, only attributes explicitly defined for the given labels are returned.

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter is only evaluated if you specify ALL for the second parameter in the query. In this case, SQLA? will return the attributes of those labels that are associated with the ports specified here. The default for this parameter is the default port @ to which all pins belong.

Specify @@ to display attributes for all labels of all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQLA  SQLA  -  SeQuencer Label Attribute）

```
> APTS LBL,"test","table1"
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,16,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
> SQLA ,"test","PARA_MEM=SHMEM"
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,RPTV,10,5,,(@)
< SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,STOP,,,,(@)
```

This example changes the PARA_MEM attribute of the new label test from SM to SHMEM. Note the change of the address in command line 4.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example defines a burst label for the default port.

Display the whole sequencer area:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< ...
< SQPG 8,STOP,,,,(@)
```

The sequencer area comprises nine command lines. Three further lines are required for the rudimentary burst label. Thus, issue:

```
> DMAS SQPG,SM,12,(@)
```

Define the label:

```
> SQLB "burst_1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb",(@)
```

Display the whole sequencer area again:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< ...
< SQPG 8,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 9,NOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 10,NOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 11,BEND,,,,(@)
```

You can now replace the NOP instructions in command lines 9 and 10 by CALL instructions with the SQPG command.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example queries all labels of all types for the default port.

```
> SQLB? ALL,ALL
< SQLB "test_1",MAIN,0,4,"spec_search_wtb"
< SQLB "test_2",MAIN,5,8,"spec_search_wtb"
< SQLB "burst_1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb"
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example renames the burst label `burst_1`, defined in example 1, to "BURST1".

```
> SQLB "BURST1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb"
> SQLB? ALL,BRST
< SQLB "BURST1",BRST,9,11,"gross_func_wtb"
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQLB  SQLB  -  SeQuencer LaBel definition）

This example illustrates the relative numbering of the command lines in SAOF APP mode.

```
> SAOF?
< SAOF ZERO
> SQLB? ALL,ALL
< SQLB "L_1",MAIN,0,2,"wf1"
> SAOF APP
> DMAS SQPG,SM,3,(@)
> SQLB "L_2",MAIN,0,2,"wf1"
> SAOF ZERO
> SQLB? ALL,ALL
< SQLB "L_1",MAIN,0,2,"wf1"
< SQLB "L_2",MAIN,3,5,"wf1"
```

### Example 1（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQPG  SQPG  -  SeQuencer ProGramming）

The following is a simple example of a counted match loop:

```
SQPG 3,MACT,256,CONTINUE,,(@)
SQPG 4,GENV,5,,,(@)
SQPG 5,MRPT,5,,,(@)
```

Note that only the GENV or RPTV instruction is allowed immediately before the MACT instruction. CONTINUE, which is optional, tells SmarTest to continue the surrounding test even if the match loop failed.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQPG  SQPG  -  SeQuencer ProGramming）

The following example shows that inserting a GENV instruction into a label with SQPG disturbs the sequencer constructs and must be accompanied by an appropriate adjustment of the vector areas (see also `Inserting a sequencer instruction`（raw: `02.06.07.01.07.03.01_Inserting_a_sequencer_instruction.md`）).

Display the sequencer area of the default port:

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< ...
< SQPG 4,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,GENV,9,,,(@)
< SQPG 7,STOP,,,,(@)
< SQPG 8,STVA,520,,,(@)
< ...
```

The vector area segment of the label starting at command 4 comprises 2 memory words, as shown by the start address of the following label (command line 8).

Now display the vector area segment of pin S0_1 for the label starting at command 4, and also the first memory word of the following label:

```
> $VECD? PARA,SM,504,24,(S0_1)
< VECD PARA,SM,504,16,(S0_1),
 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001
 0000 0001 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000
 0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000
```

The GENV instruction is associated with the first two memory words. The last 7 bytes of the second word are padding vectors. This is shown by making the first label the start label and then displaying the active vectors of command 6 for pin `S0_1`:

```
> SQSL "test_1"
> $VCYC? 0,9,(S0_1)
< VCYC 0,9,GENV,F160,(S0_1),
 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000 0001
 0000 0001
```

Now insert a GENV instruction before command 6:

```
> TSTL "test_1",
> INSI 6,1
> SQPG 6,GENV,1,,,(@)
```

Display the active vectors for the two GENV instructions:

```
> $VCYC? 0,10,(S0_1)
< VCYC 0,1,GENV,F160,(S0_1), 0000 0001
< VCYC 1,9,GENV,F160,(S0_1),
 0000 0001 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000
 0000 0010
```

The first memory word is now associated with the new instruction. The first of its vectors is active, the others are inactive. The previous command 6 (now command 7) is now associated with the second and the third block. Thus the third memory word is illegally shared between two labels.

### Example 1（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQSL  SQSL  -  SeQuencer Start Label）

```
> SQSL "test_1"
> SQSL? TYPE
< SQSL "test_1",MAIN,(@)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQSL  SQSL  -  SeQuencer Start Label）

```
> PSFC 2
> SQSL "test_1"
> SQSL? ALL
< SQSL "test_1","11",MAIN,(@)
> SQSL "test_2", "10"
> SQSL "test_3", 2
> SQSL? ALL
< SQSL "test_2","10",MAIN,(@)
< SQSL "test_3","01",MAIN,(@)
> SQSL?
< SQSL "test_2"
> PQFC 2
> SQSL?
< SQSL "test_3"
```

This example illustrates the definition of different start labels for different sites. Note that the restriction of the setup focus has no influence on the command, but that the setting of the query focus does affect SQSL?.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQST  SQST  -  SeQuencer STate）

|

seq_state

 |

Gives the state of the sequencer:

 |
 |

OFF

 |

In the OFF state, both the sequencers and the clock are off. All pins go into the high-z state.

This option can only be applied to all execution contexts.

 |
 |

HALT

 |

In the HALT state, both the sequencer and the clock are off, and the drivers keep their last level or remain in high-z state if already in high-z state.

Note that you cannot pass directly from HALT to OFF or from OFF to HALT. You must first pass to BRK in both cases.

This option can only be applied to all execution contexts.

 |
 |

BRK

 |

In the BRK state, the clock is on and the break waveform is applied to the DUT.

This option can only be applied to all execution contexts.

 |
 |

ABRT

 |

This is not a sequencer state, but an instruction to change the state of an execution context from RUN to BRK. ABRT requires that an execution context is specified.

 |
 |

CBRK

 |

This is not a sequencer state, but a conditional instruction. If no context is in BRK or RUN state, the state of the global context will be changed to BRK. If any context is in BRK or RUN state, nothing will be done.

 |
 |

RUN

 |

In the RUN state, the clock is on and the sequencer applies vectors to the DUT. This option can be applied to a specified execution context.

 |
 |

Note that if the sequencer state changes from OFF or BRK to RUN, the sequencer runs with the global settings that have previously been defined with `SQGB, SQGB? - (SeQuencer GloBal)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.232_SQGB__SQGB__-__SeQuencer_GloBal.md`）.

 |
 |

exec_context

 |

An execution context. In the command, this parameter can only be added to the sequencer state RUN and the instruction ABRT. It must be added if ABRT is specified. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） .

If the query is issued without a context, then RUN will be returned if there is at least one context that is in the RUN state.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQST  SQST  -  SeQuencer STate）

```
SQST RUN
```

This example starts a global sequencer run.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQTO  SQTO  -  SeQuencer TimeOut）

|

timeout

 |

Defines the time (in seconds) that the sequencer runs. The default value is 900 and the range is 0.001 to 2147483.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SQTO  SQTO  -  SeQuencer TimeOut）

```
SQTO 3000
```

This example programs the sequencer to exit after 50 minutes.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SREC  SREC  -  Set RECeiver mask）

|

mask_value

 |

The mask value parameter specifies whether a pin mask will be applied:

 |
 |

ACT

 |

If ACT is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list become active (not masked).

 |
 |

X

 |

If X is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are masked.

 |
 |

STOR

 |

If STOR is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are stored.

 |
 |

RSTO

 |

If RSTO is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are restored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be masked. This parameter may also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） or by `DFGE, DFGE? - (DeFine Group Expressions)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.59_DFGE__DFGE__-__DeFine_Group_by_Expressions.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pins in pinlist can be O or IO pin types. The @ character sets the mask for all pins of these types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › SREC  SREC  -  Set RECeiver mask）

```
SREC X, (D1, D2, D3, D4)
```

This example masks the pins D1, D2, D3 and D4.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › TCMT  TCMT  -  Test CoMment Transfer）

|

vect_addr

 |

The logical number of the vector at which the comment is to be inserted or read. The specified number range must not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

text

 |

A string of up to 250 characters. The string must be enclosed with double quotes.

Comments can contain any characters with ASCII codes from 32 to 126, that is, all printable ASCII characters. To put a double quote character (", ASCII 34) into a comment, enter two double quote characters.

 |
 |

vect_length

 |

The vector range forwards from vect_addr.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › TCMT  TCMT  -  Test CoMment Transfer）

```
TCMT 2063,"Start of test 2".
```

This example inserts the comment "Start of test 2" at the logical vector address 2063.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › TSTL  TSTL  -  TeST Label）

|

label

 |

Defines the label you wish to edit. Enter an alphanumeric string, 1 to 128 characters long, enclosed in double quotes. You can deactivate the currently selected label by specifying an empty string ("").

 |
 |

port

 |

This parameter is ignored in the command. In the query reply, it specifies the port to which the active label belongs.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › TSTL  TSTL  -  TeST Label）

```
TSTL "new",
```

This example selects the label "new" for editing.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

```
VDCG? {waveform_set}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {waveform_set}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

Or:

```
VDCG? {specset_id}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {specset_id}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

Or:

```
VDCG? {wavetable_name}, {dev_cyc_name}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VDCG {wavetable_name}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform set number. Enter PRM for the primary waveform set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

Alternatively, you can enter:

 |
 |

 |

ALL

 |

With this specifier the command checks that:

- The pins in pinlist have exactly the same device cycle names.
- For each device cycle, each pin defines the device cycle with the same length.
 |
 |

 |

FDC

 |

With this specifier the command checks that the first device cycle in the device cycle definition table for each pin in the pinlist has the same length.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names whose device cycles are to be checked. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to read all configured pins.

 |
 | dev_cyc_len  | Always 1 for SmarTest 7.10. |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCG  -  Verify Device Cycle for Group）

```
VDCG? 1,ALL,(inputs)
```

returns:

```
VDCG 1,ALL,SLEN
```

This example checks the consistency of all device cycles for pins in the pin group "inputs" in waveform set 1. The test system replies that all device cycles for the specified group are consistently defined.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCN -  Vector Device Cycle Name）

VDCN {vec_No}, {"dev_cyc_name"}, {dev_cyc_len}, {repeat_count}, {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCN -  Vector Device Cycle Name）

|

vec_No

 |

A logical vector number of the selected label. Logical vector numbers count the active vectors of one label. The first active vector of a label has the logical vector number 0 (zero).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

The device cycle name. Enter a string of up to 16 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

Alternatively, enter FDC for the first device cycle name in the device cycle table.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

Length of the device cycle that is being downloaded.

This is always 1. (For SmarTest 7.10, only 1 waveform per device cycle is possible.)

 |
 |

repeat_count

 |

Determines how many times the device cycle is to be downloaded.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which vectors are to be downloaded. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to download to all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCN -  Vector Device Cycle Name）

```
VDCN 93, "EXAMPL", 1, 15, (@)
```

This example downloads vector data resulting from the default values for the EXAMPL device cycle to all pins, starting at active vector 93. The download is repeated 15 times.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCP  VDCP   Vector Device Cycle Parameter）

|

vec_No

 |

A logical vector number of the selected label. For the command, it determines the first active vector that will be overwritten.

For the query, this parameter specifies the vector at which analysis of the vector area starts (see also the description of the strt_disp parameter below).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

Possible values are:

- The name of a defined device cycle.
- FDC: The first device cycle specifier. It indicates that the first device cycle in the device cycle table for the pins in pinlist is to be taken. If the length of this device cycle is not equal to the length parameter dev_cyc_len, an error is reported in the report window and the pins with this error are not set.

This specifier should be used only if you are working with device cycles consisting of just one test system cycle. The specifier gives you a shortcut to a device cycle name, where all device cycles have the same length (of 1).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

The length of the specified device cycle.

For the query, the length specifies the analyzed range of active vectors, starting at the vector number vec_No. Enter an integer in the range 0 to 256 (see also the description of the disp_length parameter below).

 |
 |

ed_comp

 |

The edit component. This parameter is optional. It specifies which direction parameter (either Dx for drive or EDx for expected data, where x is 1 or 2) is being edited. The direction parameter being edited is fixed, and the system can, if necessary, auto-correct the other direction parameter.

The edit component can take the following values:

- dd1d: Drive data 1, drive value
- dd1z: Drive data 1, high-Z value
- dd2d: Drive data 2, drive value
- dd2z: Drive data 2, high-Z value
- ed1: Expected data 1 value
- ed2: Expected data 2 value

If the edit component is one of dd1d, dd1z, dd2d, or dd2z, then both the DD1 and DD2 parameters are fixed, and the ED1 and ED2 parameters can be auto-corrected to yield a consistent physical waveform sequence.

If the edit component is ed1 or ed2, then the ED1 and ED2 parameters are fixed, and the DD1 and DD2 parameters can be auto-corrected.

If no edit component parameter is specified, then all four direction parameters are fixed.

 |
 |

DD1

DD2

 |

Drive data parameters. They contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values you can define are:

- F00: Drive 0, tri-state off
- F10: Drive 1, tri-state off
- F0Z: Drive 0, tri-state on
- F1Z: Drive 1, tri-state on
- N: Not used. Enter it if you do not want to set a drive data parameter to a drive and tri-state value.
- UC: Unclear. You must not enter this parameter value. The system may return this value as an answer to your query, to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle. This response from the system is possible only if you do not use the Timing Setup to generate your device cycles.

The drive data parameters F0N, F1N, FN0, and FNZ, which set just the drive value or just the tri-state value (as is the case with the WAVE command), cannot be used here

 |
 |

ED1

ED2

 |

Expected data parameters. The values you can define are:

- F0: Compare to 0
- F1: Compare to 1
- FI: Compare to intermediate
- FX: Compare to mask
- FU: Compare to unstable
- N: Not used. Enter it if you do not want to set an expected data parameter to a compare value.
- UC: Unclear. You must not enter this parameter value. The system may return this value as an answer to your query, to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle. This response from the system is possible only if you do not use the Timing Setup to generate your device cycles.
 |
 |

strt_disp

 |

This parameter defines the offset of your range of interest from vec_No. The actual display starts with the last device cycle that does not begin before vec_No and does not end before vec_No + strt_disp.

The purpose of this construction is to enable a correct device cycle reconstruction even if the first vector you are interested in does not lie at a device cycle boundary (a device cycle can span up to 16 vectors).

 |
 |

disp_length

 |

Specifies the display length in vectors. This parameter determines the end of your range of interest. The actual display ends with the last device cycle that starts before vec_No + strt_disp + disp_length.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which a vector data transfer is to be made. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. Pins that do not belong to the port of the label are ignored.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VDCP  VDCP   Vector Device Cycle Parameter）

```
> VDCP? 0,8,0,8,(S0_1)
< VDCP 0,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 1,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 2,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 3,"MYDC",2,,F00,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 5,"MYDC",2,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
> VDCP? 2,6,4,2,(S0_1)
< VDCP 5,"MYDC",2,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< VDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
```

In the second call of VDCP? (the first call just serves to display the underlying situation) the range of interest starts at vector 6. Note that the reply starts with vector 5, and that the first occurrence of MYDC, which lies between vector 2 and vector 6, is not displayed.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VECC  VECC  -  VECtor download Compressed）

```
VECC? PARA,ALL,0,,(S0)
```

returns:

```
size: 21
data:
VECC PARA,ALL,0,,(S0)\x0A
size: 75
data:
VECD PARA,SM,0,56,(S0),#9000000016\x02Ee\x80\x02Ee\x814VX\x13Eu\x90\x00\x0A
status: 0
```

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VECD  VECD  -  VECtor Download）

```
> VECD? PARA,SM,0,16,(OUT1)
< VECD PARA,SM,0,16,(OUT1),#9000000024\x0E\x0C\x0E\x0E\x0D\x0E\x0E\x0D\x0E\x0E\x0E\x0E
  \x0C\x0D\x0E\x0E
```

This example shows the answer as it is recorded in the MCDLog.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VPAR  -  Vectors in PARallel）

```
VPAR? {start_vec_No}, {stop_vec_No}
```

returns:

```
VPAR {cmd_No}, [frst_used_vec]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VPAR  -  Vectors in PARallel）

|

start_vec_No

 |

Defines the offset of the first vector to be searched from the start vector of the currently selected label. The specified address must not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

stop_vec_No

 |

Defines the last vector in the search range. The specified address must not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

cmd_No

 |

In the reply, the number of the command within the sequencer area, or NISQ - see below.

 |
 |

frst_used_vec

 |

Returns the logical address of the first vector affected by the sequencer instruction.

 |

NISQ (Non-Interpretable SeQuence) indicates that the sequencer program does not respect its context conditions. This means, there is non-linear use of vectors, or there are partial "Match Begin" or "Match End" sequences (for example a WTER without its MBGN, a MJPE without its MEND - see the SQPG command). The label is no longer displayable by the Vector Setup in this case. No frst_used_vec parameter is returned when the parameter cmd_No is NISQ.

### Example（取自子主题 Vector Setup Commands › List of vector setup commands › VPAR  -  Vectors in PARallel）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,504,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,10,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,RPTV,6,5,,(@)
< SQPG 4,STOP,,,,(@)
> VPAR? 0,15
< VPAR 0,0
< VPAR 1,0
< VPAR 2,0
< VPAR 3,10
```

This example displays the sequencer instructions of the selected label before calling VPAR? in order to make its reply understandable.

### Examples（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › Concepts of AC test functions › Using embedded timing and level search on a Smart Scale system）

### Binary search for the left boundary

The following example shows a binary search for the left boundary (FAIL/PASS transition) with a minimal pass count of 5 (a dot denotes PASS):

 !`Embedded timing search`（raw: `../../../../raw/124091.png`）

Note the following points in the graphic:

- It is to be understood that the largest PASS area of the linear search starts with the dot in the Linear Search line.
- To make the graphic more perspicuous, it is assumed that every transition occurs at a multiple of the binary search resolution.
- The required 5 consecutive PASS values are found after three additional steps.

### Level search

In general, the embedded level search works according to the same principles as the timing search. In particular, you can also restrict the level search to individual pins. The firmware commands and test method APIs with which the search is configured and executed are also the same for both level and timing search.

Note that a positive step width means that the level is increased, and a negative step width that it is diminished.

You can combine level searches with timing searches, but not on the same pin at the same time: If you define, for example, first a level search for a pin with TOCF, and then a timing search for the same pin, the timing search configuration will overwrite the level configuration.

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › CYRM  CYRM  -  CYcle Resolution Mode）

|

resolution_mode

 |

Defines the resolution mode. This can be:

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the normal operation mode. In spite of its name (which was coined at a time when the normal operation mode was one result per cycle), it simply means that the result resolution as defined with DCRM is to be applied. This is the default.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

This option

- activates a mechanism by which a test that failed on the cycle level is re-executed in order to enable error map recording on the edge level. For details see `Retrieving edge information by repeating the test`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.02.01_Retrieving_edge_information_by_repeating_the_test.md`）.

Note also that re-execution of the test can be blocked with the CYRP command.

- prevents acceptance of any DCRM configuration that combines more than one edge result into one recorded result, except DCRM 1,PFC.

Note that the EDGE option is not available for pins which take part in a match loop.

 |
 |

error_limit

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin or pins to which this mode will be applied. You can also specify one or more pin groups or ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › CYRM  CYRM  -  CYcle Resolution Mode）

```
CYRM CYCL,,(@)
CYRM CYCL,,(MatchLoopPin)
```

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › DPSR  DPSR  -  Define Parallel SeaRch）

```
> PSFC ALL
> DPSR 3,,,FUNC,#219,TIM,"f",B,30,130,,
> PSFC 2
> DPSR 3,(IN1),,FUNC,#220,TIM,"del",B,0,110,,
> PQFC 1
> DPSR? 3,(@)
< DPSR 3,(@),(@),FUNC,#9000000019,TIM,"f",B,30,130,,
> PQFC 2
> DPSR? 3,(@)
< DPSR 3,(OUT1),(@),FUNC,#9000000019,TIM,"f",B,30,130,,
< DPSR 3,(IN1),(@),FUNC,#9000000020,TIM,"del",B,0,110,,
```

This example illustrates:

- How the same search can be defined differently for different sites.
- How an existing condition is partially overwritten when a new condition is partially inconsistent with it.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

```
DRLS? {test}, {pass_value}, [limit], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
DRLS {value_specifier}, {result_value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

|

test

 |

This parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

H

 |

This parameter must be entered to determine the high input voltage threshold (VIH,min). VIH,min is the minimum input level which is recognized as logic 1 by the DUT.

 |
 |

L

 |

This parameter must be entered to determine the low input voltage threshold (VIL,max). VIL,max is the maximum input level which is recognized as logic 0 by the DUT.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

For a simple pass or fail test (limit parameter omitted), the pass value defines the expected pass level (in mV) for the test. For value measurements, this parameter defines the start value of the measurement window; set it to a value that ensures a pass result for the functional test. pass_value must be in the range of the drive level in the channel board (see `DRLV, DRLV? - (DRive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.89_DRLV__DRLV__-__DRive_LeVel.md`）).

 |
 |

limit

 |

The limit parameter is an integer which defines the upper (for a low level search) and lower (for a high level search) limits for the measurement window of a value measurement. The limit must be specified in mV. This parameter must be omitted if only a pass/fail result for the test is required. The range limitations for this parameter are as follows:

- when checking the high threshold, the limit parameter must be between the minimum drive level of the channel board (see `DRLV, DRLV? - (DRive LeVel`（raw: `02.06.02.02.89_DRLV__DRLV__-__DRive_LeVel.md`）) and the specified pass value;
- when checking the low level threshold, the limit parameter must be between the specified pass value and the maximum drive level of the channel board.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins that you want to test. This parameter may also include groups previously created using the DFGP command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. pinlist must only contain pins configured as inputs.

 |
 |

value_specifier

 |

This reply parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned if a VIL,max measurement was performed and already the first test (with the pass_value parameter) failed.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned if a VIH,min measurement was performed and all the functional tests performed within the measurement window passed.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

(equal to) is returned if a value measurement was performed and the first failed functional test occurred within the measurement window.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned if a VIL,max measurement was performed and all tests performed within the measurement window passed.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned if a VIH,min measurement has been performed and the first functional test performed within the measurement window failed.

 |
 |

P

 |

This indicates that the functional test performed passed. This is only returned if the limit parameter is omitted.

 |
 |

F

 |

This indicates that the functional test performed failed. This is only returned if the limit parameter is omitted.

 |
 |

result_value

 |

The result value is the level (in mV) of the last passed test.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

```
DRLS? H,5000,,(Q0_1)
```

returns:

```
DRLS P,5000
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › DRLS  -  DRive Level Sensitivity）

```
DRLS? H,5000,-1000,(Q0_1)
```

returns:

```
DRLS EQ,-490
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › EDDC  -  EDge in Device Cycle）

```
EDDC? [waveform_set], [timing_set], {edge_spec},
[dev_cyc_name], [dc_ref], [direction], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EDDC {edge_number}, {dev_cyc_name}, [reuse_flag], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › ESGB  ESGB  -  Edge Search GloBal）

|

lin_step

 |

The lin_step parameter defines the step width (in ns) to be used for the linear searches which can be initiated by the TTRS? query. Any negative number entered in this parameter results in tests only being performed at the specified start and stop values. The default value for the linear_step is -1.000.

 |
 |

lin_bin_step

 |

The lin_bin_step parameter defines the step width (in ns) to be used for the combined linear and binary searches which can be initiated by the TTRS?, and TSUP? command queries. Any negative number entered in this parameter results in tests only being performed at the specified start and stop values. The default value for the lin_bin_step is 0.500.

 |
 |

min_pulse

 |

The min_pulse parameter defines the minimum pulse width (in ns) which can be used for the input pin searches initiated by the TSUP? and THLD? queries. The default value for the min_pulse is 0.000.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › ESGB  ESGB  -  Edge Search GloBal）

```
ESGB 20,30,0
```

This example defines a 20 ns step width for linear search and a 30 ns step width for the combined linear/binary search. The minimum allowed pulse width is 0 ns.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › EXSR -  EXecute SeaRch）

```
EXSR{set_nr}
```

Parameter
 |

set_nr

 |

Specifies the number of the search set which is to be executed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › EXSR -  EXecute SeaRch）

```
> EXSR 1
> EXSR 2
```

Note that the results for search set 1 are still extant after execution of search set 2.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › FTSM  FTSM  -  Functional Test Set Mask）

```
FTSM {mode}, [run_to], [mask_before], [mask_after][,(ref_port)]
FTSM?
FTSM?
```

returns:

```
FTSM CLEAR, , ,
```

or

```
FTSM SET, [run_to], [mask_before], [mask_after][,(ref_port)]
```

  Parameters

 | mode  | Lets you set the mode of the FTSM command. The mode can be: |
 | SET  | In this mode the parameters run_to, mask_before, and mask_after are set and used in the next sequencer run. The original SQGB values are saved and restored with the next FTSM CLEAR command. |
 | CLEAR  | The FTSM parameters run_to, mask_before, and mask_after will be ignored by subsequent sequencer runs. Instead, the original SQGB values are restored. Original values are the values that had been active before execution of the FTSM SET command to set a specific mask. |
 | run_to |

The pattern is executed up to the specified cycle, including this cycle. This parameter cannot be used together with the mask_before or mask_after parameter except for two cases:

- If the mask_before parameter is set to 0.
- If the run_to parameter is set to N and the mask_after parameter to N + 1.

The cycle number must be within the range [0 ... 2^48 - 2]

 |
 | mask_before |

All cycles before the specified cycle are masked and do not contribute to the pass/fail result. The specified cycle is not masked.

If mask_before is not a multiple of 8, cycles will be recorded starting from the next lowest multiple of 8, but those up to the specified cycle will be discarded afterwards.

 |
 | mask_after  | All cycles after the specified cycle are masked and do not contribute to the pass/fail result. The specified cycle is not masked. (Recording will run to the end of the test, but the cycles following the specified one will be discarded afterwards.) |
 | ref_port |

For a multi-port burst, this parameter specifies the reference port to which the cycle numbers of the run_to, mask_before, and mask_after parameters refer.

If you have set the run_to parameter, then the sequencers will be stopped for all ports after the reference port has completed the requested number of cycles. The mask_before, and mask_after parameters are only applied to the specified port. The other ports will not be masked,

Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

   |  Application Used in the parametric functional test. Errors and warnings

An error is generated if:

- A value (run_to, mask_before, mask_after) is not in the valid range of [0... 2^48 - 2].
- The run_to and mask_before parameters are specified, and run_to is equal or bigger than mask_before.
- The run_to and the mask_after parameters are specified, and run_to is bigger than mask_after.

A warning is generated if:

- The run_to parameter and the mask_before parameter are specified and run_to < mask_before. In this case the pattern executed will always pass as all cycles executed are masked out for result evaluation.
- The run_to parameter and the mask_after parameter are specified and run_to <= mask_after. In this case the entry for the mask_after parameter can be omitted as the sequencer will not even execute the cycles that are masked out.

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › FTSM  FTSM  -  Functional Test Set Mask）

```
FTSM?
```

returns:

```
FTSM CLEAR, , ,
FTSM SET, ,10,20
```

The FTSM? query returns the current FTSM settings.

The FTSM SET command masks all cycles except for those in the range from cycle 10 to cycle 20.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

| exec_context  | An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`）. |
 | result_flag  | This is returned by the system when the functional test has finished. It can be:

 |   | P  | is returned if the functional test passes. |
 |   | F  | is returned if the functional test fails.  | |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

