### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

```
RCLS? {test}, {pass_value}, [limit], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
RCLS {value_specifier}, {result_value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

|

test

 |

This parameter is one of the following:

 |
 |

H

 |

to determine the high level threshold for the DUT output pins.

 |
 |

L

 |

to determine the low level threshold for the DUT output pins.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The pass_value parameter defines the expected pass value (in mV) for the threshold measurement.

pass_value must be in the range of the comparator threshold level in the channel board (see `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`）).

 |
 |

limit

 |

The limit parameter specifies the limit (in mV) of the measurement window for value measurements. The range for this parameter is as follows:

- If you want to determine the high level threshold, the value entered must be between the maximum comparator threshold level of the channel board (see `RCLV, RCLV? - (ReCeive LeVel)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.204_RCLV__RCLV__-__ReCeive_LeVel.md`）) and the specified pass value
- If you want to determine the low level threshold, the value entered must be between the pass value and the minimum comparator threshold level of the channel board.

If a pass/fail test is to be performed, this parameter must be omitted. For both high and low level threshold measurements, the search is performed by varying the comparator threshold from the limit you specify, to the hardware limit.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be tested. This parameter may also include groups previously created using the DFGP command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. pinlist must only contain pins configured as outputs.

 |
 |

value_specifier

 |

This parameter contains one of the following:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned after a high level test to indicate that the first functional test (performed at the value defined by the limit parameter) failed. LT is only returned after a value test.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned, after a low level test, if all the tests carried out within the window pass. LE is only returned during value measurements.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

Equal to is returned if the first failure of the level test occurs within the measurement window. EQ is only returned after a value measurement.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned, after a high level test, if all the tests carried out within the window pass. GE is only returned after a value measurement.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned after a low level test to indicate that the first functional test (performed at the value defined by the limit parameter) failed. GT is only returned after a value test.

 |
 |

P

 |

A P is returned if the functional test passes. A P can only be returned if the limit parameter has been omitted.

 |
 |

F

 |

An F is returned if the functional test fails. An F can only be returned if the limit parameter has been omitted.

 |
 |

result_value

 |

The result value is the level (in mV) of the last passed test.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › RCLS  -  ReCeive Level Sensitivity）

```
RCLS? H,3000,6000,(Q0)
```

returns:

```
RCLS EQ,5300
```

In this example a search was made to find the high level threshold between 3V and 6V. The pass/fail transition was located at 5.3V.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › RSSR  -  Retrieve Spec Search Results）

```
RSSR? {set_nr},[(setup_pinlist)]
```

returns:

```
RSSR {set_nr},(search_result),[pass_value],[fail_value],(setup_pinlist)
```

Parameters
 |

set_nr

 |

Specifies the number of the search set for which results are to be returned.

 |
 |

setup_pinlist

 |

The specified setup pins identify the search conditions for which the results are to be returned. For conditions with several setup pins, only one of them needs to be specified.

If this parameter is omitted, results are returned for all search conditions for which a valid result exists.

 |
 |

search_result

 |

Specifies whether a transition was found.

Possible values are:

 |
 |

P

 |

Transition found

 |
 |

 |

F

 |

No transition found

 |
 |

 |

E

 |

No result found for the specified pins. Search was not executed or had errors.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The last (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the first (in a FAIL/PASS transition) spec value or edge position where the test passed.

If only a pass value is returned, the test always passed.

 |
 |

fail_value

 |

The first (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the last (in a FAIL/PASS transition) spec value or edge position where the test failed.

If only a fail value is returned, the test always failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › RSSR  -  Retrieve Spec Search Results）

```
> PQFC 2
> RSSR? 3,(@)
< RSSR 3,P,90.1,90.2,(OUT1)
< RSSR 3,P,33.1,33,(IN1)
```

In this example, RSSR? returns the results of all setup pins in search set 3 for site 2. For OUT1, a pass/fail transition was found, for IN1 a fail/pass transition.

### Example 1（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SHSP  SHSP  -  SHmoo SPecs）

```
> SHSP LEV, "aclk_vil",(aclkout), LEV, "adata_vil", (adata3)
> SHSP?
< SHSP LEV, "aclk_vil",(aclkout), LEV, "adata_vil", (adata3)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SHSP  SHSP  -  SHmoo SPecs）

In the following Pin Scale example, both spec variables occur in the period definitions associated with the two ports:

```
> CLKR? "MP_spec",(Port1)
< CLKR "MP_spec",17,3.4,(Port1)
> PRPT? "MP_spec","shmsp@Port1";
< PRPT "MP_spec",(Port2)
> SHSP TIM, "shmsp@Port1",,TIM,"shmsp@Port2",
> SHVL 17,30
> PRPT? "MP_spec","shmsp@Port1"
< PRPT "MP_spec",(Port1)
> CLKR? "MP_spec",(Port1)
< CLKR "MP_spec",17,4.25,(Port1)
```

Since `shmsp` is used in the period definitions for both port `Port1` and `Port2`, the one that is specified first in the SHSP command will be used to derive the period resolution. Note that the primary port is only changed after issuing the SHVL command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SHVL  SHVL  -  SHmoo spec VaLues）

|

value_1

 |

A double float defining the new value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

Or use RSTO to restore the original value.

 |
 |

value_2

 |

A double float defining the new value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

Or use RSTO to restore the original value.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SHVL  SHVL  -  SHmoo spec VaLues）

```
> SHSP TIM, "shmsp@Port1",, TIM, "shmsp@Port2",
> SHVL 2,3
> SHVL?
< SHVL 2,3
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

|

mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

ACQF

 |

ACQuire Failure mode. Only failed cycles are recorded, starting after analyze_delay cycles. If analyze_delay is not a multiple of 8, recording starts after the nearest smaller multiple of 8. In this mode the Error Map is called the Acquire Failure Map.

As the test proceeds the Acquire Failure Map is filled with failure data until the test stops or the map becomes completely full, whichever occurs first. If the map stops recording before the test has finished, the sequencer, which is in standard mode, continues executing the test until the end.

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of ACQF is reproduced by:

DCGM FAIL,STRT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

ACFF

 |

This mode is functionally identical to ACQF. It is obsolete and should not be used in new applications.

 |
 |

EL

 |

EndLess. The sequencer repeats the complete test, including primaries and multiport synchronization, in an endless loop and can only be stopped by Break.

The analyze_delay parameter is ignored. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented mode.

This mode is used for oscilloscope tests. The Error Map functions as a rolling buffer. After stopping the sequencer, the Error Map shows the last "buffer-full" of recorded cycles.

 |
 |

ELPT

 |

EndLess PaTtern. The sequencer repeats only the user program. This avoids critical holds during measurement.

In case of multiport testing, ports may run with different frequencies. Using the ELPT mode in this case, can lead to the situation, that for loop counts >1 the synchronization is no longer executed.

 |
 |

EMPS

 |

Error Map PoSitioning. The Error Map is in cycle oriented mode, the sequencer in default mode. The analyze_delay parameter specifies the end of the recorded area. If it is not a multiple of 8, the last cycle to be displayed is the largest multiple of 8 that is smaller than analyze_delay. The first cycle to be displayed is determined by the size of the Error Map (8k cycles).

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of EMPS is reproduced by:

DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

SE

 |

Stop on Error. The sequencer runs from the beginning of the test and stops when an error is encountered. If no errors occur, the sequencer runs to the end of the test and stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. The analyze_delay parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

SEEL

 |

Stop on Error and EndLess. The sequencer repeats the test in an endless loop, unless an error is encountered, whereupon it stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode. This mode is used to locate sporadic failures.

 |
 |

STSQ

 |

STop SeQuencer. Stops the sequencer after analyze_delay cycles. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. See also the query `GETC? - (GET Cycles)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.131_GETC__-__GET_Cycles.md`） for the analyze_delay count.

 |
 |

STRD

 |

In the query reply, this mode is displayed if the current combination of recording mode, as set with DCGM, and interpretation of the Error Map position, as set with DCRP, is different from all the other SQGB modes. For example, the Error Map can be in cycle oriented recording mode, and analyze_delay be interpreted as a start value.

In the command, this option leaves it to SmarTest to select the appropriate recording mode (cycle oriented or acquire failure), unless the recording mode has been explicitly set with DCGM.

 |
 |

STSV

 |

STop Sequencer on Vector. Stops the sequencer at the logical vector number specified in the analyze_delay parameter before executing the vector. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM.

Note that the STSV option cannot be used if no start label has been defined with SQSL, or if the start label is a burst or multi-port burst label.

 |
 |

analyze_delay

 |

Sets the analyze delay. This parameter is mandatory for the STSQ and STSV modes. Its interpretation depends on the selected mode parameter. The number must be between 1 (0 for ACQF) and 281,474,976,710,655 = 2^48 - 1 (2^48 - 2 for ACQF).

If the mode parameter is set to STSV, three cases must be distinguished:

- If analyze_delay is an existing logical vector number of the actual start label, the sequencer will be stopped at this logical vector before executing the vector.
- If analyze_delay specifies the total number of logical vectors (= greatest logical vector number of the test + 1) the sequencer stops at the last valid vector.
- If analyze_delay is greater than the total number of logical vectors, an error message is issued.
 |
 |

ref_port

 |

This parameter accepts a single port. It must be specified in the following situation:

- The selected mode requires an analyze delay (but is different from STSV), and
- the start label is a multi-port burst.

It specifies the port which is used for counting the cycles specified with the analyze_delay parameter. When this reference port has completed the specified number of cycles, the sequencers will be stopped, or cycle recording started or stopped, for all ports. Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

 |
 |

port_list

 |

If the current mode requires an analyze delay, you can specify a port list in the query. The reply will give the calculated analyze delays for those ports that are not used as the reference port. These delays are derived from the analyze delay of the reference port and the ratio between the period lengths of the reference port and the other port in the primary timing setup. If you specify @@, SQGB will return the settings for all ports of the current start label.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

```
> PCLK? "mu_burst",1,(@@)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,20,(P1)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,10,(P2)
> SPRM "mu_burst",1,,
> SQSL "mu_burst"
> SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
> SQGB? (@@)
< SQGB STSQ,15,(P1)
< SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
```

This example configures the sequencers to stop when port P2 has completed 30 cycles. Port P1, whose period length is twice the period length of P2, will be stopped after 15 cycles. Note that P1 and P2 must belong to the same sequencing group.

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SREC  SREC  -  Set RECeiver mask）

|

mask_value

 |

The mask value parameter specifies whether a pin mask will be applied:

 |
 |

ACT

 |

If ACT is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list become active (not masked).

 |
 |

X

 |

If X is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are masked.

 |
 |

STOR

 |

If STOR is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are stored.

 |
 |

RSTO

 |

If RSTO is selected, the output components of the pins specified in the pin list are restored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins to be masked. This parameter may also include groups previously created by `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） or by `DFGE, DFGE? - (DeFine Group Expressions)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.59_DFGE__DFGE__-__DeFine_Group_by_Expressions.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pins in pinlist can be O or IO pin types. The @ character sets the mask for all pins of these types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › SREC  SREC  -  Set RECeiver mask）

```
SREC X, (D1, D2, D3, D4)
```

This example masks the pins D1, D2, D3 and D4.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

```
STRS? ["exec_context",] [start], [stop], {mode}, [(pinlist)], {spec_type}, {"spec_name[@port[@UNCHANGED]]"}, [stepwidth], {resolution}
```

returns:

```
STRS {res_spec}, [pass_meas_value], [fail_meas_value], [(pinlist)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

|

exec_context

 |

An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） .

 |
 |

start

 |

Double float with up to 5 digits after the decimal point defining the value of spec_name at the start of the search. The maximum valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647, though this may be limited by the maximum and minimum values defined with the spec. If the parameter is omitted, the minimum value as defined in the spec set will be used.

The start value can be greater than the stop value. In this case the search will be in the negative direction.

 |
 |

stop

 |

Double float with up to 5 digits after the decimal point defining the value of spec_name where you want the search to end. The maximum valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647, though this may be limited by the maximum and minimum values defined with the spec. If the parameter is omitted, the maximum value as defined in the spec set will be used.

The stop value can be smaller than the start value. In this case the search will be in the negative direction.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Search mode. Use:

L to specify a linear search,

LB to specify linear/binary search,

B to specify a binary search.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the value of the spec variable is to be modified. This parameter may also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） command. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

The @ character indicates all pins. This is the default.

 |
 |

spec_type

 |

Which specification type to use. Use :

LEV to specify levels, or

TIM to specify timing.

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

A string of up to 64 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

If you use the option @port`[`@UNCHANGED`]`, (see the port parameter), you must include this extension in the double quotes, too.

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can add a port name to the spec variable. This will have the effect that the value of the variable will be modified only for pins belonging to this port. This holds even if the variable has global scope for this port in the timing specification.

If you specify the spec variable without a port in a multi-port setup, its value will only be modified for a pin whose port has the spec variable set to global scope.

For more information on the scope of a variable see `Global and local scope of base variables`（raw: `02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md`）.

Note that if a port that is specified with the name of the variable it is this port on which the value of the variable will be modified. The setup pins have no influence on this.

On a Pin Scale system, the specification of a port will have an additional effect:

If spec_name is used in the definition of the port period, this port will be temporarily used as the primary port. For more information see `Modifying the period for a search or shmoo in a multi-port setup`（raw: `02.06.09.01.01.01_Modifying_the_period_for_a_search_or_shmoo_in_a_multi-port_setup__Pin_Sc.md`）.

This switch can be suppressed by adding @UNCHANGED to the port name.

 |
 |

stepwidth

 |

The search step width in the unit specified with the corresponding spec. This is optional if mode is B.

 |
 |

resolution

 |

The smallest step size to be used in the search. Especially useful in a binary search of a range of floating point numbers, where the number of values between start and stop is infinite. The unit must be the same as defined with the spec.

 |
 |

res_spec

 |

LT (less than)

LE (less than or equal to)

EQ (equal to)

GE (greater than or equal to)

GT (greater than).

 |
 |

pass_meas_value

 |

A double float defining the passed measured value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

This parameter contains the last (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the first (in a FAIL/PASS transition) value where the test passed.

 |
 |

fail_meas_value

 |

A double float defining the failed measured value, with up to 5 digits after the decimal point. Valid range is -21474.83648 to +21474.83647.

This parameter contains the first (in a PASS/FAIL transition) or the last (in a FAIL/PASS transition) value where the test failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › STRS  -  Spec TRansition Search）

```
STRS? 0.5,2.0,LB,,LEV,"aclk_vo_swing",0.1,0.1
```

returns

```
STRS GE,2,,
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › TOCF  TOCF  -  Timing Level Offset search ConFiguration）

|

search_type

 |

This parameter defines which value of the search result is to be stored as an offset to the edge positions of the current primary timing. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

EYE

 |

The middle of the pass area is stored as the offset. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

LB

 |

The left boundary of the pass area is stored as the offset.

 |
 |

 |

RB

 |

The right boundary of the pass area is stored as the offset.

 |
 |

resource_type

 |

This parameter selects the timing or level resource. Possible values are:

 |
 |

Timing resources

 |

R

 |

Receive edges are moved.

 |
 |

F

 |

Fast drive edges are moved.

 |
 |

S

 |

Slow drive edges are moved.

 |
 |

D

 |

Both kinds of drive edges are moved.

 |
 |

Level resources

 |

VIH

 |

High driver levels are moved

 |
 |

VIL

 |

Low driver levels are moved

 |
 |

VISWING

 |

Driver swings are moved.

 |
 |

VOH

 |

High receiver levels are moved.

 |
 |

VOL

 |

Low receiver levels are moved.

 |
 |

VIOFFSET

 |

Driver offsets. Both the driver high and low levels will be moved by the same values.

 |
 |

VOOFFSET

 |

Receiver offsets. Both the receiver high and low levels will be moved by the same values.

 |
 |

VTH

 |

Receiver thresholds are moved.

 |
 |

VOSWING

 |

Receiver swings are moved.

 |
 |

start

 |

This parameter defines the start of the search range relative to the edge or level positions as defined in the current primary timing or level. Negative values are allowed.

Units for timing and level searches are ns and mV.

 |
 |

number_of_steps

 |

This parameter defines the number of steps for the linear search.

 |
 |

step_width

 |

This parameter defines the step width for the linear search. The search range is number_of_steps * step_width.

step_width can be negative. Therefore, a negative search is possible.

Units for timing and level searches are ns and mV.

 |
 |

resolution

 |

This parameter defines the resolution of the binary search. The binary search is stopped when the distance between the last two binary search steps is 鈮?resolution.

Units for timing and level searches are ns and mV.

 |
 |

min_pass_count

 |

The PASS area determined by the binary search may still contain isolated FAIL results at its start or end. This parameter activates an additional check that is intended to exclude this. It specifies how many consecutive PASS results must be present at the start (before the end) of the putative PASS region. If this requirement is not satisfied, the left boundary of the area is moved to the right (the right boundary moved to the left) until the required number of consecutive PASS results is found.

The default for min_pass_count is 1.

 |
 |

min_stable_error_count

 |

This and the histogram_step_width parameter define a histogram based search, which is performed after the binary search. It moves the left boundary of the PASS area to the left (the right boundary to the right) until the number of errors is the same for the number of search steps specified with min_stable_error_count.

 |
 |

histogram_step_width

 |

This parameter defines the step width of the histogram search.

 |
 |

transition_detection

 |

This parameter controls the criterion for a test to be considered as PASSED. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

PF

 |

The test is considered to have passed only if no errors occurred at all. This is the default

 |
 |

 |

ECL

 |

The test is considered to have passed if the number of errors is smaller than error_count_limit.

 |
 |

 |

PF_FASTSTOP

 |

Like PF but, using the FASTSTOP mode, stops the linear search after the first PASS area is detected (see `Linear search modes`（raw: `02.06.09.01.02.01_Linear_search_modes.md`）).

 |
 |

 |

ECL_FASTSTOP

 |

Like ECL but, using the FASTSTOP mode, stops the linear search after the first PASS area is detected (see `Linear search modes`（raw: `02.06.09.01.02.01_Linear_search_modes.md`）).

 |
 |

error_count_limit

 |

This parameter defines the minimum number of errors that are not tolerated if transition_detection is set to ECL.

 |
 |

restore_flag

 |

The restore_flag parameter enables or disables the restore process after a search was executed: It allows you to suppress storing of the search result.

 |
 |

 |

YES

 |

Restores the timing / level offsets to the values it had before the offset search was executed.

 |
 |

 |

NO

 |

The new measured offset values are used in the edge position calculation.

This is the default configuration.

 |
 |

setup_pinlist

 |

This parameter defines the pins the edge positions of which are to be changed. If an input pin is specified, the O or IO pins on which the outcome of a search step is to depend must be defined with TOCR.

Note also that the edge type specified with the edge_type parameter must be in line with the pin type.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › TOCF  TOCF  -  Timing Level Offset search ConFiguration）

```
TOCF EYE,R,1,100,1,0.1,5,PF,,NO,(Pin1)
```

This example appends a check for 5 consecutive pass results to the result of the binary search.

```
TOCF EYE,R,1,100,1,0.1,1,10,0.1,ECL,7,NO,(Pin1)
```

This example appends a histogram based search to the binary search. The histogram based search is terminated if the error count is stable for 10 consecutive search steps. A test is considered passed if the number of errors is smaller than 7.

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › TORN  -  Timing level Offset search RuN）

The pins for which the embedded search is to be executed. You can specify @ for all pins.

Note the difference between a list of pins and @ in a multi-site setup. In the former case, all channels that are associated with these pins must have the embedded timing/level search capability and must have been configured with TOCF. If this is not the case, TORN? will return the status FAILED. But if @ is specified, channels that do not fulfill both these conditions will simply be ignored.

 |
 |

 |

TORN? returns one of the following three status codes:

 |
 |

 |

SUCCEEDED

 |

The search was successfully finished for all active sites.

 |
 |

 |

FAILED

 |

The search failed for at least one channel.

 |
 |

 |

ABORTED

 |

The search was canceled by the user.

waveform_set

### Syntax（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › TTRS  -  Time TRansition Search）

```
TTRS? {start}, {stop}, {search_type}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TTRS {value_specifier}, [pass_value], [fail_value], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › TTRS  -  Time TRansition Search）

|

start

 |

The start parameter defines the point in time (in ns), relative to the start of the cycle, where you want the search to begin.

 |
 |

stop

 |

The stop parameter defines the point in time (in ns), relative to the start of the cycle, where you want the search to end.

 |
 |

search_type

 |

The search type is one of the following:

 |
 |

L

 |

Specifies a linear search from the start of the window, at intervals defined by the ESGB command. The search will terminate after the first failed test or after the search limit specified by the stop parameter has been reached.

 |
 |

LB

 |

Specifies a combined linear and binary search using the step width defined by the ESGB command. A linear search is performed, with an additional binary search carried out in the interval between the last passed and the first failed test.

 |
 |

B

 |

Specifies a binary search carried out between the start and the stop positions.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins on which the search is to take place. This parameter may also include groups previously created using `DFGP, DFGP? - (DeFine GrouP)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`）. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pinlist must only contain pins configured as outputs.

 |
 |

value_

specifier

 |

This parameter can be:

 |
 |

LT

 |

(less than) is returned if the first functional test of a search in the positive direction failed.

 |
 |

LE

 |

(less than or equal to) is returned if all the functional tests performed between start and stop pass. LE is only returned for a search in the negative direction.

 |
 |

EQ

 |

(equal to) is returned if the first failure of the search occurs between the start and the stop positions.

 |
 |

GE

 |

(greater than or equal to) is returned if all the tests carried out between start and stop pass. GE can only be returned for a search in the positive direction.

 |
 |

GT

 |

(greater than) is returned if the first functional test performed during a search in the negative direction fails.

 |
 |

pass_value

 |

The pass_value is the time (in ns) at which the last passed test occurs. A pass value is only returned for if value_specifier is EQ, LE, or GE.

 |
 |

fail_value

 |

The fail_value is the time (in ns) at which the last failed test occurs. A fail value is only returned for if value_specifier is EQ, LT, or GT.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 AC Testing Commands › List of AC test function commands › TTRS  -  Time TRansition Search）

```
TTRS? 10,80,L,(Q0)
TTRS EQ,70,80,(Q0)
```

This example executes a global search test on pin Q0. A linear sweep takes place between 10 ns and 80 ns relative to the start of the period. The system returned a pass at 70 ns and a fail at 80 ns.

The amount of required waiting time must be optimized manually. It depends on the application (settling time, capacitors) and on the type of DC operation.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

```
CSAS? [msMode,] {mask}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CSAS {status}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

| msMode  | The extra parameter controls how the return value is created.

The value of the parameter can be PQFC:

- PQFC specified: The current query focus is respected and allows status query per site without affecting status bits of other sites.
- PQFC not specified: The command reads (and clears) status bits of all enabled and active sites at a glance, ignoring the actual query focus.
The parameter applies only to use of parameter mask as integer value. |
 |

mask

   | Integer bit mask or ALL.

-

Integer bit mask: Integer value is used to mask out individual status bits. Each bit of mask is logically AND-ed with the corresponding bit of the DPS status. If one of the resulting bits is set, then F (Fail) is returned, otherwise P (Pass).

It is used to check for an error condition. All bit positions of the status flags that should be checked, must be set to 1 in mask. If one of the selected status bits is set, then CSAS? returns F.

- ALL: Hex value (hexadecimal representation of all status bits) is returned.
For setting the integer bit mask or interpreting a returned hex value, refer to the `status`（raw: `02.06.02.02.33_CSAS__-__Channel_Slot_Accumulated_Status.md#_144688__r_status`） parameter below. |
 |

pinlist

 |

Comma separated list of DPS128/64 or XPS256 pins. The @ character can be used to read the status for all DPS pins.

 |
 |

status

   | If mask is ALL, you need to translate the hex value (hexadecimal representation of the status bits) to its binary form as follows:

 | Bit 0:  | High voltage or current of surge tracker exceeded |
 | Bit 1:  | Low voltage or current of surge tracker exceeded |
 | Bit 2:  | 0 |
 | Bit 3:  | Measurement range change failed |
 | Bit 4:  | Clamp current correction failed |
 | Bit 5:  | Battery full |
 | Bit 6:  | Power budget 1 |
 | Bit 7:  | Power budget 2 |
 | Bit 8:  | Power budget 3 |
 | Bit 9:  | High voltage of surge tracker reached |
 | Bit 10:  | Low voltage of surge tracker reached |
 | Bit 11:  | High current of surge tracker reached |
 | Bit 12:  | Low current of surge tracker reached |

If mask is specified as an integer bit-mask:

- Pass: P
- Fail: F
 |

### Example 1:（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

```
CSAS? 3,(VCC)
```

returns either

```
CSAS P,(VCC)
```

or

```
CSAS F,(VCC)
```

The example uses the integer bitmask and checks whether a spike on the `VCC` pin exceeded the low or high limit.

- P = Pass

No spike occurred since the last CSAS? query.

- F = Fail

Either the low or high limit or both were exceeded.

### Example 2:（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › CSAS  -  Channel Slot Accumulated Status）

```
CSAS? ALL,(Vaux)
```

returns

```
CSAS #H10,(Vaux)
```

The example uses the ALL specifier and checks for an error condition on the `Vaux` pin.

- Bit 3 = 0

No "Measurement range change failed" error. All set current measurement range requests were successful.

- Bit 4 = 1

The "Clamp current correction failed". A high-accuracy clamp current correction for a DCVH setup with execution mode SER_HAC or PAR_HAC was not successful.

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › CTXT  CTXT  -  ConTeXT）

|

action

 |

Specifies the action. Possible values are:

 |
 |

DEFINE

 |

Defines a new mode context

 |
 |

DELETE

 |

Deletes a mode context

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Displays all existing mode contexts (only in the query).

 |
 |

name

 |

The name of the mode context. If the action parameter is set to DELETE, you can also specify ALL to delete all mode contexts.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › CTXT  CTXT  -  ConTeXT）

< CTXT DEFINE,"DEFAULT"

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DDIC  DDIC  -  Define DUT Interface Connection）

|

connectionSet

 |

This parameter is currently not used.

This extra string parameter adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC Scale channel in PMU mode. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as single pin or in ganging groups. Note: The documentation for supported DC Scale cards knows this feature also as "Ganging on the fly".

Default connection set: The default connection set is defined if this extra parameter is not used or if an empty string is programmed. A DC Scale pin can be defined in only one default connection set.

It's possible to specify several DDIC commands which differ in the name parameter, but have identical (cp1, cp2) combination.

 |
 |

circuitry_type

 |

The following circuitry types are supported:

 |
 |

CONN

 |

A simple direct connection between the given pogo pins.

Two pogo pins on one or two DC Scale cards (UHC4T) must be given: One GANG_IN (pppGI) pogo and one GANG_OUT pogo (pppGO).

 |
 |

CLR

 |

Clears all previously defined circuitry.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Only for queries:

Returns all previously defined circuitry.

 |
 |

cp1,cp2

 |

The parameters define the ganging or stacking connections:

- Format pppxx defines a pogo block and a ganging connection.

Only pogo pin in/out pairs are allowed as connection points.

 |
 |

ppp

 |

The three digits specify the pogo block number.

 |
 |

xx

 |

Alpha numeric code for specifying the ganging connections:

 |
 |

GO

 |

Ganging Output

 |
 |

GI

 |

Ganging Input

 |
 | cc  | The two digits define the channel number from 01 to 16. |
 | -  | Low force (LF#) / Return of the upper channel |
 | +  | High force (HF#) / Force of the lower channel |
 |  CAUTION "Upper channel" in this context means towards the DUT while the "lower channel" means towards a stable reference like ground or the supply voltage of the DUT. This applies to both positive and negative voltages. |

### Example 1: Ganging（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DDIC  DDIC  -  Define DUT Interface Connection）

```
DDIC CONN, (207GO,209GI)
DDIC? ALL
```

returns

```
DDIC CONN, (207GO,209GI)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DFCT -  DeFine Continuity Test）

|

force_current

 |

The force_current parameter specifies the current (in [micro ]A) that the active load sources or sinks. The range is 0 to 35 mA for the Pin Scale 800 and P-/Ce- channel boards. The direction of the current is determined by the polarity of the commutation voltage and the pass range.

 |
 |

commutation_voltage

 |

This parameter defines the commutation voltage (in mV) that the active load requires to source/sink the force_current. For the Pin Scale 800, the range is -1.5 V to 5.5 V. For the P-/Ce-channel boards, the range is -2 V to +6 V.

 |

 |

pass_volt_min

 |

This parameter specifies (in mV) the minimum pass value of the test. It defines the low level threshold for the comparator during the measurement.

 |
 |

pass_volt_max

 |

This parameter specifies (in mV) the maximum pass value of the test. It defines the high level threshold for the comparator during the measurement.

   | Note If pass_volt_min > pass_volt_max, the two parameters are swapped around internally.

 |

polarity

 |

The polarity is as follows:

 |
 |

SPOL

 |

Selecting the SPOL (single polarity) option causes the measurement to be taken with the specified polarity. The specified polarities are set for the commutation voltage and the pass limits.

 |
 |

BPOL

 |

Selecting the BPOL (both polarities) option causes measurements to be taken with both polarities; a pass result is returned if the pin passes the test in both directions.

For using this option, the range of commutation_voltage is -1.5 V to +1.5 V for the Pin Scale 800, and -2 V to +2 V for the P-/Ce-channel boards.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The parameters defined by the DFCT command are applied to all the pins named in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. Pinlist can contain pins configured as O, I, IO, or DC pin types. The @ character can be used to specify all relevant pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DFCT -  DeFine Continuity Test）

```
DFCT 10000,1700,200,700,SPOL,(p1,p2,p3,p4)
CTST? GPF
```

This example sets up the parameters needed to execute a continuity test on pins `p1` to `p4`. The parameters are as follows:

-  Force current = 10 mA
-  Commutation voltage = 1.7 V
-  Voltage minimum pass value = 200 mV
-  Voltage maximum pass value = 700 mV
-  Single polarity measurement selected

The example also includes the CTST? (Continuity TeST) query used to execute the test.

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

|

setnr

 |

This number defines the set number for the measurement. The number must be an integer from 1 to 256.

In the query, you can specify ALL to retrieve the data of all sets.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This parameter specifies the pins to be used for the measurements.

 |
 |

binary_data

 |

This is a binary data string. The string starts with the '#' character, followed by a digit in the range 1 to 9 which stipulates how many digits are used in the data length specifier. The data length specifier is next: up to 9 digits determine how many bytes of data will follow. The actual data string follows last.

 Note If the binary data string is empty, the definition for the pins specified in pinlist will be deleted from the set.

The first character or value of the data stream determines the format for the remainder of the data stream (characters '0' through '3' are for current measurements, '4' through '11' for voltage measurements):

 | 0: Waveform template |
 | |

If the first character is a '0', it is followed by a waveform template. The values are given first for the low value and then for the high value. The values are separated by a ',' (comma).

This template is for the PASS/FAIL results from the `PSER?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） query. The current range in which the measurements will be executed is determined by the maximum/ minimum value of the template. The values have the unit Amps [A].

This option can only be combined with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 1: Number of measurement points followed by low and high values |
 |   | If the first character is a '1', a number and two values follow. The first number gives the number of measurement points. The second and third define the low and high values. These are separated by a "," (comma). The current range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Amps [A].

This option can only be combined with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 2: Low and high value |
 |   | If the first character is a '2', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The current range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Amps [A]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 3: Low and high value |
 |   | If the first character is a '3', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The current range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Amps [A]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option can only be selected for DC Scale channel DPS's and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command. If the channels belong to a Master/Slave configuration, they are unganged during the measurement as far as possible, that is, as far this can be done without affecting the goal of the measurement.

 |
 | 4: Waveform template |
 |   | If the first character is a '4', it is followed by a waveform template. The values are given first for the low value and then for the high value. The values are separated by a ',' (comma). This template is for the PASS/FAIL results from the `PSER?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） query. The voltage range in which the measurements will be executed is determined by the maximum/ minimum value of the template. The values have the unit Volt [V].

This option can only be selected for DC Scale channel DPS's and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 5: Number of measurement points followed by the low and high values |
 |   | If the first character is a '5', a number and two values follow. The first number gives the number of measurement points. The second and third define the low and high values. These are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V].

This option can only be selected for DC Scale channel DPS's and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 6: Low and high value |
 |   | If the first character is a '6', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 7: Voltage waveform template for the high speed digitizer |
 |   | If the first character is a '7', it is followed by a voltage waveform template for the high speed digitizer (connect state *HDIG). An error message occurs if another connect state is used. The values are given first for the low value and then for the high value. The values are separated by a ',' (comma). This template is for the PASS/FAIL results from the `PSER?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） query. The voltage range in which the measurements will be executed, is determined by the maximum/ minimum value of the template. The values have the unit Volt [V]. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command. See also `DPS_PIN_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.50.01_DPS_PIN_TASK.md`）. |
 | 8: Number of measurement points followed by the low and high values for high speed digitizer measurements |
 |   | If the first character is an '8', a number and two values follow. The first number gives the number of measurement points. The second and third define the low and high values. These are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. This template is for high speed digitizer measurements only, that means connect state *HDIG. An error message occurs if another connect state is used. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels and can be combined only with the `PSEE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.189_PSEE_-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Execute.md`） command. See also `DPS_PIN_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.50.01_DPS_PIN_TASK.md`）. |
 | 9: Low and high value for high speed digitizer measurements |
 |   | If the first character is a '9', two values follow. They define the low and high value (in this order) and are separated by a "," (comma). The voltage range for the measurements is determined by the maximum and minimum value of the template. The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1. This template is for high speed digitizer measurements only, that means connect state *HDIG. An error message occurs if another connect state is used. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command. See also `DPS_PIN_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.50.01_DPS_PIN_TASK.md`）. |
 | 10: Force voltage-drop measurement |
 | |

If the first value is a '10', two values follow. They define the low/high P/F limits of a force (voltage-)drop measurement and are separated by a "," (comma). The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option can be selected only for the HC variant of `DC Scale DPS128`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01_DC_Scale_DPS128_DPS64_cards.md`） channels and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

 |
 | 11: Return voltage-drop measurement |
 | |

If the first value is an '11', two values follow. They define the low/high P/F limits of a return (voltage-)drop measurement and are separated by a "," (comma). The values are given in the unit Volt [V]. The number of measurement points is 1.

This option can be selected only for the HC variant of `DC Scale DPS128`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.01_DC_Scale_DPS128_DPS64_cards.md`） channels and requires that the measurement is executed with the `PSIE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.192_PSIE_-__Power_Supply_Internal_trigger_Execute.md`） command.

   | |

### Example 1（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000170,0.1,0.2,0.2,0.3
```

This example defines a template which consists of 2 points (0.1, 0.2) and (0.2, 0.3). If the first measured value is in the range (0.1, 0.2) and the second value is in the range (0.2, 0.3), then the result will be a pass.

### Example 2（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000121,15,0.1,0.2
```

This example defines a template which is 15 points long and is constant.

### Example 3（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DFPS 11,pos,(Vcc)
DFPS 12,pos,(Vdd)
DPSE 1,(@),#10 <- Delete set 1
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#152,1,2 <- Vcc min=1A, max=2A
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#152,2,3 <- Vdd min=2A, max=3A
PSST ON <- Measurement requires connect state
PSIE 1,,,(@) <- Measure both pins in parallel
PSER? 1,pval
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000006,1.501 <- value within range
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000006,3.173 <- value outside range
PSER? 1,ppf
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000000
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000000
PSER? 1,gpf
PSER 1,F,(),#9000000000
```

This example performs a measurement with format 2 and PSIE for two different pins in parallel.

### Example 4（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › DPSE  DPSE  -  Define Power Supply External trigger measurement）

```
DFPS (10101),pos,(Vcc) <- DC Scale pin
DFPS (10102,10103),pos,(Vdd) <- DC Scale pin (Gang of two channels)
DPSE 1,(@),#10 <- Delete set 1
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#153,0.5,1.5 <- Vcc min=0.5A, max=1.5A
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#153,20,30 <- Vdd min=20A, max=30A
PSST ON <- Measurement requires connect state
PSIE 1,,,(@) <- Measure both pins in parallel
 Vcc: High Precision Mode is used
 Vdd: Only one channel of the gang is used
PSER? 1,pval
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000006,1.301 <- value within range
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000006,31.73 <- value outside range
PSER? 1,ppf
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000000
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000000
PSER? 1,gpf
PSER 1,F,(),#9000000000
```

This example performs a measurement with format 3 and PSIE for two different pins in parallel.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › MEAS -  execute a MEASurement set）

```

```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › MEAS -  execute a MEASurement set）

|

id_dc

The DC set identification number to be executed.

id_mset

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › MEAS -  execute a MEASurement set）

```
MEAS 1,2
```

This example executes the measurement set 2 of the DC set 1.

See also an example in `MSET, MSET? - (definition of Measurement SET)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.164_MSET__MSET__-__definition_of_Measurement_SET.md`）.

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › MSET  MSET  -  definition of Measurement SET）

Setting up PPMUs:

```
MSET 1,DC,1,LEN,6,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,1,WAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 1,DC,1,ACT,,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,1,SEL,0,CURR,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,SEL,0,VOLT,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,IRNG,1,IRA,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,IRNG,1,90,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,UFOR,2,500,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,IFOR,2,-40,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUL,3,-5,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUL,3,3000,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUH,4,5,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,1,PMUH,4,3000,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,1,ACTI,5,,(p1,p2)
```

On PS5000:

```
MSET? 3,DC,1,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,LEN,7,,(@)
MSET 3,DC,1,WAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 3,DC,1,SWAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 3,DC,1,ACT,,,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,SEL,0,CURR,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,IRNG,1,10000,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,UFOR,2,3300,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,PMUL,3,-10,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,PMUH,4,30,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,ACTI,5,,(dig1)
MSET 3,DC,1,SYNC,6,,(dig1)
```

Setting up the relays:

```
MSET 1,DC,2,LEN,2,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,2,WAIT,,1.3,(@)
MSET 1,DC,2,ACT,,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,2,OPM,0,ON,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,2,PPMU,0,ON,(p2)
MSET 1,DC,2,ACTI,1,,(p1,p2)
```

Setting up the measurement mode:

```
MSET 1,DC,3,LEN,1,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,3,WAIT,,0,(@)
MSET 1,DC,3,ACT,,,(@)
MSET 1,DC,3,PMUM,0,I,(p1)
MSET 1,DC,3,PMUM,0,H,(p2)
```

This example illustrates the internal structure of a measurement set as well as the requirement to define different measurement sets for different tasks. Note that no ACTI action is required (or even permitted) for measurement set 3 which contains only the PMUM action.

To execute this example, use the MEAS command as shown below:

```
MEAS 1,1
MEAS 1,2
MEAS 1,3
```

These commands sequentially execute measurement sets 1, 2 and 3 of DC set 1.

To retrieve the result of this measurement, use the `PMUR?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.179_PMUR___retrieve_PPMU_result.md`） command as shown below:

```
PMUR? GPF,(@)
```

This command retrieves the global pass/fail result of all pins.

Defining a DC set for value measurement

```
MSET 2,DC,1,VMUM,0,I,1,ADC,4000,0.0004,(p1)
```

In this example, 4000 measurements will be taken with the sampling period 400 us on the pin p1.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? [PRLT,] {spec},[averages,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
PDMM {spec},, [ident], {result}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 | PRLT  | The extra parameter controls how the measurement is performed.

The value of the parameter can be: PRLT

 |
 | PRLT specified: |
 |   | The specified test is performed for all active sites and for all pins that are defined in the pinlist. The command returns individual results only for the site in focus.

The command additionally stores a global pass/fail result for all active sites. The global pass/fail result can be retrieved by a following `PRLT?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.183_PRLT__-__request_Parallel_ResuLTs.md`） query.

 |
 | PRLT not specified: |
 |   |   | If not specified, the measurement results are returned only for the site in result focus. The command returns individual results for the measurements defined by parameter spec and for the pins defined by pinlist. A following PRLT? query will return an error message. |
 | spec  | The mandatory parameter defines the test specification that can be: |
 | Fo_Se  | to check that the force/sense lines are correctly wired on your DUT board. This measurement must be made in disconnected state. |
 | Ma_S1  | to check the force connections on the ganging line. The force of master and all forces of slaves must be connected within a resistant of 20 惟. PASS is returned if pin is not in ganging mode.

Only supported with the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | averages |

The extra parameter defines the number of averaged measurements to be performed.

The valid range of the integer parameter is 1 鈥?128.

The default value is 1.

 |
 | pinlist  | pinlist must contain the names of DPS previously defined by the DFPS command (and used in DPS operating mode) or the names of DPS previously defined by the DFPN command (and used in PMU operating mode).

See `DFPS, DFPS? - (DeFine Power Supply)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） and `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for more information.

If more than one pin is specified, the names must be separated by a comma. The character @ can be used to specify all DPS pins.

 |
 | ident  | The identifier is: |
 | POS  | for positive power lines |
 | NEG  | for negative power lines |
 | result  | The result is P (pass), or F (fail) for a Fo_Se specification. |

### Example 1: Test of the site in query focus（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? Fo_Se, (@)
```

returns:

```
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vee)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vee)
```

This example checks that the force/sense connections on the DUT board are correctly wired for positive and negative lines. For the pin Vee the master channel and the slave channel show a pass for both lines.

### Example 2: Test of all active sites（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? PRLT, Fo_Se, (Vcc,Vee)
PRLT? ALL
```

returns:

```
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vcc)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vcc)
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vee)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vee)

PRLT ALL,"PF0P"
```

The returned pass/fail result of PRLT? presumes that four sites are defined and sites 1, 2, and 4 are active. Sites 1 and 4 have passed the test. Site 2 shows the result for an open force to sense connection.

### Example 3: Averaging（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? Fo_Se, 10, (@)
```

returns:

```
PDMM Fo_Se,,POS,P,(Vee)
PDMM Fo_Se,,NEG,P,(Vee)
```

The returned go/no-go results are built from the average of ten measurements to improve the stability of the measurement in noisy environments.

### Example 4: Ganging（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PDMM  -  PDps Miscellaneous Measurement）

```
PDMM? Ma_Sl,32,(@)
```

  returns:

```
PDMM Ma_Sl,,POS,P,(Vee1)
PDMM Ma_Sl,,POS,P,(Vee2)

```

This example checks the master and slave connections for ganged pins with an average of 32 measurements to improve the stability of the measurements in noisy environments.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

```
PMUR?{type}, [mode,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns

```
PMUR {judge}, [voltage], [current], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

|

type

 |

Data type to be retrieved. The following specifiers can be set:

VMUM: Returns the measurement value from the PPMU measurement (successive approximation) for the pins in pinlist.

VAL: Returns the per pin measurement value or values for the pins in pinlist.

PF: Per pin pass fail result for the pins in pinlist.

GPF: Global pass fail result for all tested pins. The pinlist is ignored.

 |
 |

mode

 |

This parameter controls the behavior of PMUR? if the type parameter is set to VAL. The allowed values are:

 |
 |

 |

FORCE_MEASURE

 |

PMUR? performs a value measurement for type VAL.

 |
 |

 |

USE_CACHE

 |

PMUR? performs a value measurement only if necessary, that is, if a result for the same measurement set is not present in the cache.

 |
 |

judge

 |

This parameter indicates a judgment of the pin with the following specifiers:

P: Pass

F: Fail

 |
 |

voltage

 |

Measured voltage in mV. This parameter is only returned when type = VAL.

 |
 |

current

 |

Measured current in uA. This parameter is only returned when type = VAL.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Target pin or pins to retrieve result

   | Note For the VAL type, either voltage or current will be returned depending on the measurement mode (I-force V-measure or V-force I-measure).

### Example 1（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

```
> PMUR? VAL,(p1,p2)
< PMUR P,,2,(p1)
< PMUR F,-2100,,(p2)
```

This example retrieves the measurement value of "p1" and "p2" for the site that has the query focus.

### Example 2（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PMUR   retrieve PPMU result）

```
> PMUR? GPF,(@)
< PMUR P,,,()
```

In this example, PMUR? returns the global pass/fail result for all tested pins of the site that has the query focus.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

```
PSAS? [msMode ,] {mask}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns

```
PSAS {status}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 | msMode  | The extra parameter controls how the return value is created.

The value of the parameter can be PQFC:

- PQFC specified: The current query focus is respected and allows status query per site without affecting status bits of other sites.
- PQFC not specified: The command reads (and clears) status bits of all enabled and active sites at a glance, ignoring the actual query focus.
The parameter applies only to use of parameter mask as integer value. |
 | mask  | Integer bit mask or ALL.

-

Integer bit mask: Integer value is used to mask out individual status bits. Each bit of mask is logically AND-ed with the corresponding bit of the DPS status. If one of the resulting bits is set, then F (Fail) is returned, otherwise P (Pass).

It is used to check for an error condition. All bit positions of the status flags that should be checked, must be set to 1 in mask. If one of the selected status bits is set, then PSAS? returns F.

- ALL: Hex value (hexadecimal representation of all status bits) is returned.
For setting the integer bit mask or interpreting a returned hex value, refer to the `status`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md#_98691__r_status`） parameter below. |
 | pinlist  | Comma separated list of DPS128/64 or XPS256 pins. The @ character can be used to read the status for all DPS pins. |
 | status  | If parameter mask is ALL, you need to translate the hex value (hexadecimal representation of the status bits) to its binary form as follows:

 | Bit 0 (LSB):  | Constant voltage |
 | Bit 1:  | Constant current |
 | Bit 2:  | Unregulated |
 | Bit 3:  | Overvoltage |
 | Bit 4:  | Overpower / Overcurrent / Power budget exceeded |
 | Bit 5:  | Overtemperature |
 | Bit 6:  | Voltage drop force |
 | Bit 7:  | Voltage drop return |
 | Bit 8:  | DUT board disconnect  | For the special mapping of bit 9 and 8 on UHC4 and UHC4T, refer to table `DPS flag description`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md#_98691__s_DPS_flag_description`） below. |
 | Bit 9:  | Safety line |
 | Bit 10:  | Current limit disconnect |
 | Bit 11:  | Low headroom |
 | Bit 12:  | Current limiter protection detected |
 | Bit 13:  | Range overflow |
 | Bit 14 (MSB):  | Clamp distance too low |
 | Bit 15:  | Voltage drop force warning |
 | Bit 16:  | Voltage drop return warning  |  If parameter mask is specified as an integer bit-mask:

- Pass: P
- Fail: F

Refer to table `DPS flag implementation`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md#_98691__s_DPS_flag_implementation_710`） below for information regarding the card specific implementation of the bits or flags.

 |

### Description（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

For the following examples (1 to 4), the assumed binary value of the status of the UHC4 pin Vcc is 10000110 (Voltage drop return, Unregulated, Constant Current).

### Example 1（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To get all flags:

```
PSAS? ALL,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS #86,(Vcc)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To check if Unregulated (bit 2) is set:

```
PSAS? 4,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS F,(Vcc)
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To check if Constant Current (bit 1) or Overpower (bit 4) is set:

```
PSAS? 18,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS F,(Vcc)
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

To check if Voltage Drop Force (bit 6) or DUT Board Disconnect (bit 8) is set:

```
PSAS? 320,(Vcc)
```

returns

```
PSAS P,(Vcc)
```

### Example 5（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

```
PSAS? ALL,(Vee)
```

returns

```
PSAS 2,(Vee)
```

This example for device pin Vee shows the DPS is working in constant current mode.

### Example 6（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSAS  -  Power Supply Accumulated Status）

```
PSAS? ALL,(Vee)
```

returns

```
PSAS 64,(Vee)
```

This example for device pin Vee shows the DPS has hit the voltage drop force threshold.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSEE -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Execute）

```
PSEE [setnr], [current_range], [samples], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSEE -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Execute）

|

setnr

 |

The set number of the external trigger measurement. (The range is 1 to 256). When this parameter is specified the corresponding set must have already been defined.

 |
 |

current_range

 |

If the setnr parameter is specified, the range in which the executed measurement will be made will be determined from the maximum value of the limits defined with the `DPSE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.85_DPSE__DPSE__-__Define_Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement.md`） command, and this parameter will be ignored.

If the setnr parameter is not specified, you must specify the range with a value. In this case, the measurement will be executed in the smallest range that can measure the given value. The unit is Ampere [A].

 |
 |

samples

 |

This parameter specifies the number of measurements. After the measurements are completed, the average of the measurements will be calculated.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

This parameter will be ignored if setnr is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSEE -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Execute）

```
DFPS 11,pos,(Vcc)
DFPS 12,pos,(Vdd)
DPSE 1,(@),#10          <- Delete set 1
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#150,1,2   <- Vcc min=1A, max=2A
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#150,2,3   <- Vdd min=2A, max=3A
PSST ON      <- Measurement requires connect state
PSEE 1,,,(@)   <- Measure both pins in parallel
PSER? 1,pval
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000006,1.501 <- value within range
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000006,3.173 <- value outside range
```

This example performs a measurement with format 2 and PSEE for two different pins in parallel.

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? [setnr], {mode}
```

returns:

```
PSER [setnr], [result], {(pinlist)}, {binary_data}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

|

setnr

 |

The set number of the external trigger measurement. (The range is 1 to 256). If this parameter is omitted, this command returns the result of previous execution of the PSEE or PSIE command.

 |
 |

mode

 |

This parameter defines the type of result.

 |
 |

PVAL

 |

Binary data for each pin defined in the measurement will be returned.

 |
 |

PPF

 |

A per-pin pass/fail result will be returned. Only valid when a setnr is given.

 |
 |

BVAL

 |

Binary data mode.

4 Bytes header for the sample count

4 Byte for test points count

Test points (8 bytes per test point)

Sampler (channel count) is set to 1.

 |
 |

GPF

 |

A global pass/fail result will be returned. Only valid when a setnr is given. Data will be evaluated for all sites of a multi-site test.

 |
 |

result

 |

The result given when setnr is specified. The result parameter contains a P (pass) or an F (fail) if the GPF or PPF option has been selected.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Only DPS pins and DC Scale pins configured with `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） are supported.

 |
 |

binary_data

 |

The binary data result string. The string starts with the '#' character, followed by a digit in the range 1 to 9 which stipulates how many digits are used in the data length specifier. The data length specifier is next - up to 9 digits determine how many bytes of data will follow. Then comes the actual data string which appears as a list of values separated by a "," (comma). The first byte of data is an identifier which defines the format of the following data. For a waveform the first byte is '\x00' with the waveform represented as FLOAT64 values. Each value is in Amps [A].

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000170,0.1,0.2,0.2,0.3
DPSE 1,(Vdd),#90000000121,2,0.1,0.2
PSEE 1,,,()
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? 1,PVAL
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000010,0.15,0.25
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000010,0.3,0.3
```

### Example 3（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? 1,PPF
PSER 1,P,(Vcc),#9000000000
PSER 1,F,(Vdd),#9000000000
```

### Example 4（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSER? 1,GPF
PSER 1,F,(),#9000000000
PRLT? ALL // get multisite results
PRLT "FPP" // site 1 fail, sites 2 & 3 are pass
```

### Example 5（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
PSEE, I_300mA, 32, (Vee)
PSER? ,PVAL
```

returns:

```
PSER,,(Vee),#90000000120,0001923451
```

### Example 6（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSER  -  Power Supply External trigger measurement Read results）

```
DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000096,0.1,0.2
PSIE 1,,all_sampler,,,(Vcc)
PSER? ,PVAL
```

returns:

```
PSER ,,(Vcc),#90000000190.15,0.25,0.35,0.45
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSIE -  Power Supply Internal trigger Execute）

PSIE [setnr], [current_range] [,{keep_range|"RSTO"}] [,{all_sampler|"CH_ALL"}] [,{primary_act|"NPRM"}], [samples] [,settl_time], {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSIE -  Power Supply Internal trigger Execute）

|

setnr

 |

The set number defined by the `DPSE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.85_DPSE__DPSE__-__Define_Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement.md`） command. (The range is 1 to 256). This set contains the limits of the measurement point for pass/fail judgment. When this parameter is specified, the corresponding set must already have been defined.

When the setnr parameter is omitted, the current and the pinlist parameters must be specified.

 |
 |

current_range

 |

If the setnr parameter is specified, this parameter will be ignored.

If the setnr parameter is not specified, you must specify the range with a value. In this case, the measurement will be executed in the smallest range that can measure the given value. The unit is Ampere [A].

 |
 |

keep_range

 |

No longer supported.

The measurement range is kept per default.

For DPS128 and XPS256, the parameter is silently ignored and the measurement range is restored to the force or clamp range.

 |
 |

all_sampler

 |

To upload the results of all channels in the gang with sampler connected, and store them, specify CH_ALL. This option can be selected only for DC Scale UHC4 / UHC4T channels.

If called without the all_sampler parameter, the command will upload only the value of the master channel, even if the measurement was done over the sampler, or if a voltage drop on DUT was measured.

 |
 |

primary_act

 |

The conditional primary activation is default.

To avoid the conditional primary activation, specify NPRM.

 |
 |

samples

 |

(Optional) This parameter specifies how often the measurement will be performed under the same test conditions. The default is 1.

For details see the table above.

The value that will be stored is the average of all these measurements.

This parameter can be used both for measurements defined with DPSE and for measurements defined directly with PSIE.

 |
 |

settl_time

 |

The system must wait the settling time before the measurement is executed. If the force range is switched, for example, "unganging during measurement", to avoid glitches the settling time is waited before the small force range is active.

The unit is milliseconds (ms).

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Names of pins to which this command is applied. The character @ can be used to specify all DPS pins. This parameter will be ignored if setnr is specified.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSIE -  Power Supply Internal trigger Execute）

```
> DPSE 1,(Vcc),#90000000112,0.09,0.11
> PSIE 1,,,(Vcc)
> PSER? 1,PVAL
< PSER 1,F,(Vcc),#9000000006,0.155
```

In this example, the `DPSE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.85_DPSE__DPSE__-__Define_Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement.md`） command specifies a current limit of 0.9 A to 0.11 A for Vcc. Then the PSIE command starts measurements for the measurement set 1. In this case, the pin name is ignored because the set number is specified with the first parameter. After the measurement, the `PSER`（raw: `02.06.02.02.190_PSER__-__Power_Supply_External_trigger_measurement_Read_results.md`） command retrieves the measurement value for Vcc. In this case, the 300 mA range that is determined by using the specified limit value, is automatically selected for the measurement.

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSST  PSST  -  Power Supply STatus）

|

state

 |

The device power supply state:

 |
 |

 |

ON

 |

Switches the DPS on.

 |
 |

 |

OFF

 |

Switches the DPS off.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which the DPS is switched on/off.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSST  PSST  -  Power Supply STatus）

```
PSST ON
```

This example turns the DPS on.

### Example 2（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › PSST  PSST  -  Power Supply STatus）

The following example shows the use of the PSST command in conjunction with multisite:

```
PSFC ALL ; PSST ON   # turn on all supplies of all sites

PSFC "01"              # focus on one site only of the dual-site

PSST OFF,(vcc)         # turn off vcc of one site only!
PQFC 1 ; PSST? (vcc)   # these last two commands return different
PQFC 2 ; PSST? (vcc)   # answers, since one site should have vcc
                       # connected, whereas the other site does not
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › UHCM  UHCM  -  Ultra High Current power supply Modes）

| set_nr  | The mandatory identification number of the DPS set which you want to modify:

 | ALL  | Modifies all existing DPS sets. |
 | PRM  | Modifies the primary DPS set. |
 | ACT  | Only for the query: Displays the settings of the actual enabled DPS set.  | |
 | time_to_alarm |

The extra parameter specifies the time (in milliseconds) from constant current clamp until an alarm flag is raised. See also ms_const_curr_time_to_alarm in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

Range: 0 ... 1270 ms.

This parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | reserved_param  | The optional parameter is reserved and required for compatibility. |
 | clamp_mode  | The optional parameter defines the clamp mode:

 | limit |

The clamp is active forever (the delay value is ignored).

This is the default value.

 |
 | `<delay>` |

Switch off at overcurrent after a delay.

<delay> is a time in milliseconds [ms].

For `<delay>`, the clamp is active until the channel switches off.

In case the channel is switched off, a disconnect/connect sequence is required (`PSST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） OFF/ON).

 |

See also `ms_const_curr_disconnect`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__ms_const_curr_disconnect`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

 |
 | fast_preload |

The optional parameter defines the preload time in milliseconds (ms).

To be used to charge large capacities for a programmable time. It does not make sense to set a shorter delay for clamp_mode than for fast_preload. A delay of zero (0) switches the fast_preload feature off.
