See also `ms_fast_preload`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__ms_fast_preload`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

 |
 | openLoopProtection  |  The extra parameter defines the status of the internal force to sense connections.

The internal force to sense connections are available between the P# pin and the PS# pin and between the GS# pin and the common GND pin.

The following options are supported:

 | DIODE |

The internal force to sense connections are made via anti鈥憄arallel diodes.

This is the default state if the parameter is not defined.

This is the recommended setting if both parameters `force_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_force_drop`） and `return_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_return_drop`） are set to a value < 0.5 V.

 |
 | NONE |

The internal force to sense connections are open.

The output stage no longer has any voltage feedback if the force to sense connection on the DUT or the DUT board is (unintentionally) open.

 The following rules apply to this option:

- The `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`）.
- This is the required setting if one of the parameters `force_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_force_drop`） or `return_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_return_drop`） is set to a value 鈮?nbsp;0.5 V.
 |

This parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | force_drop |

The optional parameter forces a channel to be disconnected if a user鈥慸efined voltage drop on the force lines is reached, which means that the absolute voltage is higher than the defined threshold.

The `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`） can measure the voltage drop of the force line on the DUT board.

Card specific behavior:

-

UHC4T: A comparator defines if the voltage drop is small enough or not. This means to measure the drop of the pogo cable (see specifications) plus the drop of the DUT board. Value/flag available for all channels ganged.

The range is 0 to 0.5 V with a resolution of 1 mV. Default is 0.25 V.

Two rules have to be respected for the two parameters force_drop and return_drop and the programmed force voltage:

  - Both force_drop and return_drop must be between 0.0 V and 0.5 V.
  - The sum of force_drop and return_drop is limited by the programmed force voltage according to the diagram below. Only values within the red area are allowed.

- XPS256: force_drop can be an integer or string. In the string representation it is possible to also add a user-defined warning level for the voltage force drop. If this level is exceeded, a flag is raised, see `PSAS? - (Power Supply Accumulated Status)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.188_PSAS__-__Power_Supply_Accumulated_Status.md`）.

The range is 0 to 1.0 V with a resolution of 1 mV. The total of theforce_drop and the return_drop must not exceed 1.0 V.

For a maximum voltage drop > 0.5 V, the `openLoopProtection`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_openLoopProtection`） parameter must be set to none and in the `DC Scale Safety editor`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__s_DC_Scale_Safety_editor`） the `Vdrop Disco`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.10.05_XPS256_programming_-_Default_values.md#_354611__r_Vdrop_Disco`） parameter must be set to ON.

In case the channel is switched off, a disconnect/connect sequence is required (`PSST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） OFF/ON).

See also `max_voltage_drop_force`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__max_voltage_drop_force`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

This optional parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | return_drop |

The optional parameter forces a channel to be disconnected if a user-defined voltage drop on the return lines is reached, which menas that the absolute voltage is higher than the defined threshold.

The `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`） can measure the voltage drop of the return line on the DUT board.

Card specific behavior:

-

UHC4T: A comparator defines if the voltage drop is small enough or not. This means to measure the drop of the pogo cable (see specifications) plus the drop of the DUT board. Value/flag available for all channels ganged. The range is 0 to 0.5 V with a resolution of 1 mV. Default is 0.25 V.

Two rules have to be respected for the two parameters force_drop and return_drop and the programmed force voltage:

  - Both force_drop and return_drop must be between 0 and 0.5 V.
  - The sum of force_drop and return_drop is limited by the programmed force voltage according to the diagram below. Only values within the red area are allowed.

- XPS256: See `force_drop`（raw: `02.06.02.02.303_UHCM__UHCM__-__Ultra_High_Current_power_supply_Modes.md#_106910__r_force_drop`）.

In case the channel is switched off, a disconnect/connect sequence is required (`PSST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.198_PSST__PSST__-__Power_Supply_STatus.md`） OFF/ON).

See also `max_voltage_drop_return`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md#_16887__max_voltage_drop_return`） in `DPSPINS resources`（raw: `../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.14.02.03.07.01_DPSPINS_resources.md`）.

This optional parameter is supported only by the `DC Scale UHC4T card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.02_DC_Scale_UHC4T_card.md`） and the `DC Scale XPS256 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03_DC_Scale_XPS256_card.md`）.

 |
 | pulldown |

The extra parameter specifies whether a pulldown resistor is active after disconnect.

 Supported values:

- OFF
- ON (default)
 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory comma鈥憇eparated list of pins.

The @ character can be used to specify all applicable pins.

pinlist must contain the names of pins previously defined by the `DFPS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.65_DFPS__DFPS__-__DeFine_Power_Supply.md`） command.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 DC Measurement Commands › List of DC measurement commands › UHCM  UHCM  -  Ultra High Current power supply Modes）

```
UHCM PRM,,,,0.4,0.1,(Vee)
```

This example sets the voltage drop force to 0.4 V, and the voltage drop return to 0.1 V.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

```
CDCP? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {strt_disp}, {disp_length}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CDCP {cycle}, {dev_cyc_name}, {dev_cyc_len}, {DD1}, {DD2}, {ED1}, {ED2}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle to be analyzed. The range of values for this parameter depends on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

cycle

 |

In the query, the consecutive number of the displayed cycle.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles to be analyzed. The range for this parameter is 0 to 1000.

 |
 |

strt_disp

 |

This parameter defines the offset of your range of interest from start_cycle. The actual display starts with the last device cycle that does not begin before start_cycle and does not end before start_cycle + strt_disp.

The purpose of this construction is to enable a correct device cycle reconstruction even if the first cycle you are interested in does not lie at a device cycle boundary (a device cycle can generate up to 16 cycles).

 |
 |

disp_length

 |

Specifies the display length in cycles. This parameter determines the end of your range of interest. The actual display stops with the last device cycle that starts before start_cycle + strt_disp + disp_length.

If this parameter is larger than no_of_cycles, it is ignored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which a device cycle data transfer is to be made. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to download data for all configured pins.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

A reply parameter, giving the name of the reconstructed device cycle.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

A reply parameter, giving the length of the reconstructed device cycle. For SmarTest 7.10 this is always 1.

 |
 |

DD1 and DD2

 |

Drive Data parameters. They contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values the system returns are:

 |
 |

F00

 |

drive 0, tri-state off

 |
 |

F10

 |

drive 1, tri-state off

 |
 |

F0Z

 |

drive 0, tri-state on

 |
 |

F1Z

 |

drive 1, tri-state on

 |
 |

N

 |

Not used. Returned if no drive data parameter is set to a drive and tri-state value.

 |
 |

UC

 |

Unclear. The system may return this value to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle.

 |
 |

ED1 and ED2

 |

Expected Data Parameters. The values the system returns are:

 |
 |

F0

 |

compare to 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

compare to 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

compare to intermediate

 |
 |

FX

 |

compare to mask

 |
 |

FU

 |

compare to unstable

 |
 |

N

 |

Not used. Returned if no expected data parameter is set to a compare value.

 |
 |

UC

 |

Unclear. The system may return this value to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CDCP  -  Cycle Device Cycle Parameter）

```
> CDCP? 0,8,0,8,(S0_1)
< CDCP 0,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 1,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 2,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 3,"MYDC",2,F00,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 5,"MYDC",2,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
> CDCP? 2,6,4,2,(S0_1)
< CDCP 5,"MYDC",2,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
< CDCP 7,"DNRZ",1,F10,N,N,N,(S0_1)
```

In the second call of CDCP? (the first call just serves to display the underlying situation) the range of interest starts at vector 6. Note that the reply starts with vector 5, and that the first occurrence of MYDC, which lies between vector 2 and vector 6, is not displayed.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CHER  -  CHeck ERrors）

```
CHER? [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CHER {res_flag}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CHER  -  CHeck ERrors）

|

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the result returned for this Pin Scale pin will be combined from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to the HXA pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Results will be provided only for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO pins.

 |
 |

res_flag

 |

The result flag is returned by the system. It can be:

 |
 |

F

 |

The last functional test performed on the specified pins failed.

 |
 |

P

 |

The last functional test performed on the specified pins passed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CHER  -  CHeck ERrors）

After a functional test has been performed, sending CHER? returns the result for each pin in pinlist.

```
CHER? (@)
```

returns:

```
CHER F,(Q0,Q1)
CHER P,(Q2)
CHER F,(Q3)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CHFA  -  CHannel FAil flag）

```
CHFA? [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
CHFA {res_flag}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CHFA  -  CHannel FAil flag）

|

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the combined result from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to the HXA pin will be used to determine the answer.

 |
 |

res_flag

 |

The result flag can be:

 |
 |

F

 |

The pin failed in the last match loop cycle.

 |
 |

P

 |

The pin passed in the last match loop cycle.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of pins. If more than one pin is included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be of O or IO type.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CHFA  -  CHannel FAil flag）

```
CHFA? (D1)
```

returns:

```
CHFA F, (D1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYCI  -  get CYCle Information）

CYCI? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {resolution_mode} [,MUX] [,(port)]

returns:

CYCI {cycle}, [res_mode] [, (port)], {vector_number}, [label], [type], [seq_status], [comment], [no_of_waveforms] [,MUX], {#spec(data)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYCI  -  get CYCle Information）

|

start_cycle

 |

The start cycle is an integer that defines the first cycle to be reported. The start cycle is in the range 0 to 2^48 when the sequencer runs in the Start Analysis mode, and -2^48 to -1 when the sequencer is in the Stop Analysis mode. If a positive number is entered, cycles are counted from 0 upwards. If a negative number is entered, the cycles are counted from the end of the test to -1. In both cases the reported start cycles are in Start Analysis mode.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

Defines the number of cycles to be reported. The integer must be in the range 0 to 256.

 |
 |

resolution_mode

 |

Defines the answer format of the binary data.

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the default value.

 |
 |

CYRM

 |

This option lets the result granularity depend on the CYRM command. If CYRM is set to EDGE, then CYCI? will supply information on the edge level (receive events).

 |
 |

port

 |

If you specify a port, information is returned for this port. If you do not specify any port, the default port @, to which all pins belong, is reported.

 |
 |

cycle

 |

In the reply, this is the consecutive number of the reported cycle. The numbering starts with the value of start_cycle.

 |
 |

res_mode

 |

This has the same values as defined in the CYRM mode parameter.

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the answer if the CYRM command mode is CYCL.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

If CYRM is set to EDGE and resolution_mode was set to CYRM, then EDGE will be returned for this parameter.

 |
 |

vector_number

 |

Returns the logical number of the first vector of the instruction that generated the cycle. The logical vector number counts the active vectors within one label, starting from 0. If the vectors generated by the instruction are break vectors, then -1 is returned.

 |
 |

label

 |

Returns the label name. It references the label to which the reported cycle belongs.

 |
 |

type

 |

Returns the label type. The following types are reported:

 |
 |

MAIN

 |

The MAIN program.

 |
 |

SJMP

 |

A JuMP Subroutine.

 |
 |

SVEC

 |

A VECtor Subroutine.

 |
 |

BRST

 |

BuRST mode.

 |
 |

 |

MPBU

 |

Multi-Port BUrst mode

 |
 |

seq_status

 |

Returns the current sequencer status. The status is expressed on most occasions in the form of the sequencer instruction that was used to generate the vectors in the requested cycle range. Otherwise it is expressed in terms of the current sequencer activity. Note that seq_status is not the same as the sequencer state determined by `SQST, SQST? - (SeQuencer STate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.241_SQST__SQST__-__SeQuencer_STate.md`）. Sequencer instructions are parameters to `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）. For additional information on sequencer programming see also see `Vector Setup Commands`（raw: `02.06.07_Vector_Setup_Commands.md`）.

The seq_status parameter is required for the reconstruction of received data. Some of the values it returns signify that vectors are being generated, others inform of sequencer status changes, which cause some or no break vectors to be generated.

 |
 |

GENV

 |

This is returned if GENV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vector for the reported cycle.

 |
 |

SRCV

 |

This is returned if SRCV is the sequencer instruction that generates vectors in the reported cycle range.

For "non-source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the parallel vectors exactly the same way as RPTV. That means "no_of_vectors" parallel vectors are repeated for a repeating count (equal to no_of_cycles divided by no_of_vectors) to generate "no_of_cycles" cycles on the test system.

For "source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the vectors stored in the source memory. It means "no_of_cycles" vectors are generated from the source memory to produce "no_of_cycles" cycle on the test system, and the information of "no_of_vectors" has no meaning to "source pin".

 |
 |

RPTV

 |

This is returned if RPTV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vector for the reported cycle.

 |
 |

JPPS

 |

This keyword indicates that a per pin subroutine is executed that cannot be reconstructed because it is too complex. In this case, PP is returned for the drive data and expected data parameters in the result data (#spec(data) parameter).

 |
 |

CTIM

 |

This is returned if a change timing instruction has been issued in the queried cycle range. Each timing change generates break vectors.

The real number of break cycles depends on the test system period and will not be shown in the cycle reconstruction.

Between 0 to 7 break cycles will be recorded during a CTIM instruction, the exact number depends on the number of vectors loaded previously. For instance, if the previous number of cycles was a multiple of 8, then no break vectors are issued during the reload.

 |
 |

CLEV

 |

The CLEV (change levels) parameter indicates that unrecorded break cycles, due to a change of level set, exist in the specified cycle range.

 |
 |

BRK

 |

This is returned if break cycles are being generated during the reported cycle range - for example, if a timed match loop is in progress. Between 0 and 7 break cycles will be recorded.

Additionally, the following sequencer instructions also generate break vectors:

 |
 |

 |

Sequencer instruction

 |

reported as

 |
 |

 |

CTIM

 |

CTIM

 |
 |

 |

CLEV

 |

CLEV

 |
 |

 |

WTER

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

FLQU

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

MEAS

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

STOP

 |

BRK

 |
 |

MTCH

 |

This is returned if

- the test contains a counted match loop,
- the test has been executed online, and
- the last cycle of the match loop is not the last cycle of a 8-cycle block.

In this case the last match loop cycles belonging to this block (up to 7) are recorded in the Error Map and reported by CYCI?. For details see `Adjusting the junctions between match loop and surrounding label`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01.01_Adjusting_the_junctions_between_match_loop_and_surrounding_label.md`）.

 |
 |

comment

 |

Returns the comment text inserted at vector_number. (See also `TCMT, TCMT? - (Test CoMment Transfer)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.254_TCMT__TCMT__-__Test_CoMment_Transfer.md`）)

 |
 |

no_of_waveforms

 |

This parameter will always be 1.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the Pin Scale pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Returns result data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the data for each pin. The pins are ordered by ascending channel numbers from the first site.

The format of the pin specific output data is controlled by the res_mode parameter: Cycle resolution format is used if res_mode was set to CYCL, edge resolution format is used if res_mode was set to CYRM. Both formats agree for the first 23 bytes, which contain the following information:

 |
 |

 |

byte 0-16:

 |

Device cycle name or 'BREAK' in case of break cycles, zero terminated. The reserved device cycle name 'JPPS' can be returned if the reconstructed data belongs to a Per-Pin subroutine.

 |
 |

 |

byte 17:

 |

HXA information

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 0-3: NOT USED (always 0).

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 4-5: channel selector for pins mapped to a HXA pin. Indicates the logical position of the pin in the multiplexing order. Set to 0 for standard pins.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 6-7: pin multiplexing factor for HXA pins. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

 |

0

 |

Pin not mapped to HXA pin

 |
 |

 |

 |

1

 |

One of two Pin Scale pins that are mapped to HXA pin

 |
 |

 |

 |

3

 |

One of 4 Pin Scale pins that are mapped to HXA pin

 |
 |

 |

 |

Information relating to HXA multiplexing is only returned if the MUX flag is set.

 |
 |

 |

byte 18, 19:

 |

NOT USED (always set to 4).

 |
 |

 |

byte 20, 21:

 |

NOT USED (always set to 15).

 |
 |

 |

byte 22:

 |

Received data. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

 |

0

 |

No error

 |
 |

 |

 |

FF

 |

This means that an error has occurred, but that it is not reconstructible for one of the following reasons:

- The waveform contains more than 1 edge.
- The waveform contains a window compare.
- Only 1 bit results are recorded.
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bits 0-2 contain the received value:

 |
 |

 |

 |

1

 |

Received high

 |
 |

 |

 |

2

 |

Received intermediate

 |
 |

 |

 |

4

 |

Received low

 |
 |

 |

 |

5

 |

Received unstable

 |
 |

 |

 |

7

 |

Failed but not reconstructible

This value will be returned for single-ended standard mode if only one bit results are recorded and the edge failed.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 3 - 5: number of failing compare edge or failing window close. If the edge was not reconstructible (bits 6-7 set to 3) the value is set to 7.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 6-7:

 |
 |

 |

 |

0

 |

This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

 |

3

 |

The failing edge is not reconstructible.

 |
 |

 |

The cycle resolution format consists of the 23 bytes described above. If the data is returned in edge resolution format, CYCI? provides additional information about receive events.

 |
 |

 |

byte 23:

 |

Number of the following receive events. Note that only used receive events will be reported.

Every receive event consists of three bytes (A, B, C), that are to be read as follows:

 |
 |

 |

byte A:

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED (Always 0).

 |
 |

 |

byte B:

 |

Receive event index

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 0-2: edge index (0 through 7)

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 3-4: channel selector for HXA pins.

If the multiplexing factor in byte 17 is > 0, and the channel selector in byte 17 is set to 0, then CYCI? will add the edges of all the other channels for the same HXA pin to the binary data. This field indicates to which of these channels the edge belongs. It specifies the position number of the respective channel in the logical multiplexing order.

 |
 |

 |

 |

Information relating to HXA multiplexing is only returned if the MUX flag is set.

 |
 |

 |

byte C:

 |

Receive data

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 0 - 3: compare method

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 4 - 6: received value

 |
 |

 |

For details see the tables below.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYCI  -  get CYCle Information）

CYCI? 20,2,CYCL

returns:

CYCI 20,11,"TEST1",SVEC,RPTV,"comment",1,

#9000000046

 dvc_01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x04\x99

 dvc_02\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x04\x0F\x0F\x00

CYCI 21,12,"TEST1",SVEC,GENV,,1,

#9000000046

 dvc_03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x04\x04\x05\x0F\x6C

 dvc_04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x04\x04\x0F\x0F\x0D

This example returns result information (on the cycle level) for 2 cycles and 2 output pins of the label `TEST1`, which is of type SVEC. The first cycle was generated by a RPTV instruction from logical vector 11 and has an associated comment, the second cycle was generated by a GENV instruction for logical vector 12.

The binary data reports the device cycle names, which in this example are different for each pin and cycle. The waveform offsets are zero. The reported drive/expected/received data are:

 |

dvc_01:

 |

DD1 = F00, DD2 = F10, ED1 = FX, ED2 = F0

error: high received on edge 3 (param E2)

 |
 |

dvc_02:

 |

DD1 = F00, DD2 = N, ED1 = N, ED2 = N

no error

 |
 |

dvc_03:

 |

DD1 = N, DD2 = N, ED1 = FU, ED2 = N

error: high received on edge 5 (param E1)

 |
 |

dvc_04:

 |

DD1 = N, DD2 = N, ED1 = N, ED2 = N

error: unstable received on edge 1 (FIX)

 |

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRM  CYRM  -  CYcle Resolution Mode）

|

resolution_mode

 |

Defines the resolution mode. This can be:

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

This is the normal operation mode. In spite of its name (which was coined at a time when the normal operation mode was one result per cycle), it simply means that the result resolution as defined with DCRM is to be applied. This is the default.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

This option

- activates a mechanism by which a test that failed on the cycle level is re-executed in order to enable error map recording on the edge level. For details see `Retrieving edge information by repeating the test`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.02.01_Retrieving_edge_information_by_repeating_the_test.md`）.

Note also that re-execution of the test can be blocked with the CYRP command.

- prevents acceptance of any DCRM configuration that combines more than one edge result into one recorded result, except DCRM 1,PFC.

Note that the EDGE option is not available for pins which take part in a match loop.

 |
 |

error_limit

 |

CURRENTLY NOT USED.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin or pins to which this mode will be applied. You can also specify one or more pin groups or ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRM  CYRM  -  CYcle Resolution Mode）

```
CYRM CYCL,,(@)
CYRM CYCL,,(MatchLoopPin)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRP  -  CYcle Resolution Parameter）

```
CYRP [recovery],[shots]
CYRP?
```

returns:

```
CYRP {recovery},{shots}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRP  -  CYcle Resolution Parameter）

|

recovery

 |

Specifies whether the test is repeated with all receive edges enabled after the last fine granularity shot. This serves to reset the hardware registers into the state in which they were before the first fine granularity shot. Possible values are:

 |
 |

RCRY

 |

The test is repeated at the end with all receive edges enabled. This is the default.

 |
 |

NRCR

 |

The test is not repeated.

 |
 |

shots

 |

Specifies whether additional shots are allowed. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ONE

 |

No additional shots are allowed. This option allows execution of a test only if CYRM is set to CYCLE, or the mode parameter of DCRM is set to 8.

ONE can be used to prevent execution of a test in fine granularity mode (EDGE option of CYRM) with several shots if this would lead to erroneous results.

 |
 |

MULT

 |

Additional shots are allowed. This is the default.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRP  -  CYcle Resolution Parameter）

```
CYRP NRCR,ONE
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRS  -  CYcle Resolution State）

```
CYRS? {(pinlist)}
CYRS {result_state}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRS  -  CYcle Resolution State）

|

result_state

 |

Specifies the result state of the selected pins. Possible values are:

 |
 |

INVL

 |

No functional test has been executed, so that no test results are available.

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

Test results are available for all selected pins, but they are not edge specific for at least one of them.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

Edge specific test results are available for all selected pins.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin or pin list for which the result state is to be returned. Only O or IO pins will be taken into consideration.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › CYRS  -  CYcle Resolution State）

```
CYRS? (Out1,Out2)
CYRS CYCL,(Out1,Out2)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCEL  DCEL  -  Digital Compare Exception List）

| DCRT  | The command for which an exception list is to be created. Currently, DCRT is the only allowed command. |
 | TP   | The option of the command specified in the first parameter. Currently TP is the only allowed value. |
 | parameter  | This query parameter can be TP or ALL. |
 | action  | This can be one of the following: |
 | SET  | Add the specified pins to the exception list related to the command in the first parameter. |
 | DEL  | Delete the specified pins from the exception list related to the command in the first parameter. |
 | pinlist  | In the command, these are the pins that are to be added to or deleted from the exception list. In the query, DCEL? returns the subset of the specified pins that is included in the exception list. Instead of a pin list, you can also specify one or more pin groups. |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCEL  DCEL  -  Digital Compare Exception List）

```
> DCRT RAM,(portA)
> DFPT? (portA)
< DFPT (p1,p2,p3),(portA)
> DCEL DCRT,TP,(p2)
> DCEL? DCRT,TP,(portA)
< DCEL DCRT,TP,SET,(p2)
> DCEL DCRT,TP,(p1,p3)
> DCEL? DCRT,TP,(portA)
< DCEL DCRT,TP,SET,(p1,p2,p3)
> DCRT? (portA)
< DCRT RAM,(portA)
```

Note that you can add further pins to the exception list, and that the settings of DCRT are not changed even if all three pins of `portA` are in the exception list.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCGM  DCGM  -  Digital Compare Global Mode）

|

acqu_mode

 |

Specifies the recording mode for the detailed Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All cycles are recorded (cycle oriented mode). In this mode, recording will wrap around to the start when the error map is full before the specified stop position or the end of the test.

In this mode, the response time of the result queries EMAP? and ERMP? will be better than in the FAIL mode.

 |
 |

FAIL

 |

Only failed cycles are recorded (failure acquire mode). In this mode, recording for the detailed Error Map will always stop when the map is full. Note that this may happen before the area of interest is reached.

In this mode, more data can be stored in the detailed Error Map.

 |
 |

STRD

 |

SmarTest is to decide whether ALL or FAIL is selected.

 |
 |

emap_pos_int

 |

Specifies how the Error Map position, as set with `DCRP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.47_DCRP__DCRP__-__Digital_Compare_Result_Positioning.md`） or `SQGB`（raw: `02.06.02.02.232_SQGB__SQGB__-__SeQuencer_GloBal.md`）, is interpreted for the detailed Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

STRT

 |

The Error Map position is interpreted as a start value. If the start position is greater than the total number of test cycles, no data will be recorded.

 |
 |

HALT

 |

The Error Map position is interpreted as a stop value. Recording will stop at this position at the latest. If the stop position is greater than the total number of test cycles, recording will stop at the end of the test.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

The Error Map position is ignored. Recording will stop at the end of the test or (if the recording mode is FAIL) when the Error Map is full.

 |
 |

Note that the options STRT and HALT cannot be used with the sequencer modes EL, SE, SEEL, STSQ, and STSV (as set with `SQGB`（raw: `02.06.02.02.232_SQGB__SQGB__-__SeQuencer_GloBal.md`）). If one of these sequencer modes is active, DCGM will issue a warning, and `FTST?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.127_FTST__-__Functional_TeST.md`） will refuse to run.

 |
 |

ovem_pos_int

 |

Specifies how the Error Map position is interpreted for the overview Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

HALT

 |

The Error Map position is interpreted as a stop value. Recording will stop at this position. When the error map is full before this position is reached, recording will wrap around. If the stop position is greater than the total number of test cycles, recording will stop at the end of the test.

This value is only allowed if the emap_pos parameter is also set to HALT.

 |
 |

NONE

 |

The Error Map position is ignored. Recording will stop at the end of the test.When the error map is full before the test ends, recording will wrap around.

 |
 |

answer_type

 |

This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |
 |

exec_context

 |

An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`） . This parameter is only accepted when answer_type is set to EXEC.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCGM  DCGM  -  Digital Compare Global Mode）

```
DCGM FAIL,STRT,NONE
```

This example sets the error map into acquire failure mode and specifies that the error map position is to be interpreted as a start value for the detailed error map, and to be ignored for the overview error map.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

DCRM

```
DCRM {map},{mode},[bits],["sub_cycles",] {(port_list)}
```

 DCRM?

```
DCRM? [answer_type,] {map},{(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
DCRM {map},{mode},[bits],[sub_cycles,] {(port)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

| map  | Specifies which error map will be configured. Possible values are: |
 | EMAP  | Detailed Error Map |
 | OVEM  | Overview Error Map |
 | mode  | The meaning of this parameter depends on the map parameter.

- map is set to EMAP:

In this case mode specifies the maximum number of results that are recorded per cycle. The possible values are 1, 2, 4, 6, 8; 6 is only supported by Smart Scale cards. 1 is the default.

Note that not all these values are supported on all hardware types. Furthermore certain of these values are only available with one option of the bits parameter. The details can be found in `Possible combinations of CYRM, CYRP, and DCRM`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.01.02.05_Possible_combinations_of_CYRM__CYRP__and_DCRM.md`）.

The number of results can be reduced with the sub_cycles parameter, but not for mode values of 6 and 8.

- map is set to OVEM:

In this case the mode parameter controls the compression mode and the compression factor. The following values are allowed:

 | FCM  | A fixed number of cycles is combined into one result. The number can be defined by a second call of DCRM, where the number is specified as the mode parameter. |
 | LMAP  | All cycles of one pattern in a (single-port or multi-port) burst are combined into one result. Note that with this option, 8 鈥?nbsp;15 break cycles are inserted between the patterns of the burst. In the error map, 0 .. 7 additional cycles are recorded.Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 | BFLM  | All cycles of one pattern in a (single-port or multi-port) burst are combined into one result. With this option, which is only available for Smart Scale, no break cycles are inserted between the patterns of the burst. Note In BFLM mode, each pattern in the burst must generate 8 or more cycles. |
 | cycles |

The number of cycles to be compressed in FCM mode. It must be divisible by 16.

Note that this number is not affected by a switch to LMAP. If you switch back to FCM the compression factor will be the same as before the switch to LMAP.

The default is 4096.

 |
 |
 | bits  |  Only valid if map is set to EMAP. Specifies how detailed the recorded error code is to be in case of failure. Possible values are: |
 | PF  | Only a one bit Pass/Fail result will be returned. |
 | PFC  | In case of failure, a more detailed two bit code will be recorded. This is the default. |
 | The meaning of the 2 bit error codes depends on the expected result as follows:

 |   | Received |
 | Expected  | L  | I  | H  | U |
 | L  | 00  | 01  | 10  | 11 |
 | I  | 10  | 00  | 01  | 11 |
 | H  | 01  | 10  | 00  | 11 |
 | U  | 01  | 10  | 11  | 00 |

"I" stands for "Intermediate", and "U" stands for "Unstable". Note that you can reconstruct the received result from the expected result and the error code.

 |
 | Note that only one error code format is supported for some result granularities. See `Possible combinations of CYRM, CYRP, and DCRM`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.01.02.05_Possible_combinations_of_CYRM__CYRP__and_DCRM.md`）. |
 | sub_cycles |

This parameter, which is only valid if map is set to EMAP, defines the sub-cycles. The format is

c1: edge_list1 [c2: edge_list2 [c3: edge_list3 [c4: edge_list4]]]

where every edge list is a comma separated list of edge numbers.

The number of sub-cycles must not be larger than the number specified with the mode parameter. A sub-cycle can contain only one edge, numbering gaps are allowed, and the same edge may occur in more than one sub-cycle.

User defined sub-cycle definitions are not supported for all combinations of mode and bits, and some combinations are only supported for certain recording modes and certain hardware types. For details see `Possible combinations of CYRM, CYRP, and DCRM`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.01.02.05_Possible_combinations_of_CYRM__CYRP__and_DCRM.md`）.

The default with mode set to 2 is:

```
"c1:1,2,3,4 c2:5,6,7,8"
```

The default with mode set to 4 is:

```
"c1:1,2 c2:3,4 c3:5,6 c4:7,8"
```

 |
 | port_list  | Specifies the ports for which the recording mode is to be defined. If you specify @@, DCRM will set the recording mode, or return the current settings, for all ports. |
 | answer_type  | This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are: |
 | CONF  | The current configuration is returned. This is the default. |
 | EXEC  | The configuration of the last executed test is returned. |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

```
DCRM EMAP,4,PF,"c1:1,3 c2:5,7 c3:2,4 c4:6,8",(P1,P2)
```

This example configures the detailed Error Map of port `P1` and `P2` to record 1 bit results for 4 sub-cycles, each of which combines two different edges.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

```
DCRM EMAP,1,PFC,(P1,P2)
```

This example configures the Error Map to record one global detailed two bit result combining all edges of a cycle at every test execution.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRM  DCRM  -  Digital Compare Result Mode）

```
DCRM OVEM,6000,,(@)
```

This example defines that 6000 cycles will be compressed into one Overview Error Map bit when the next test will be executed.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRP  DCRP  -  Digital Compare Result Positioning）

|

error_map_pos

 |

Specifies the start or stop position for Error Map recording. The interpretation of the value is determined by DCGM independently for both error maps:

- If the current interpretation mode is STRT, the value specifies the first cycle to be recorded. This applies only to the detailed Error Map.
- If the current interpretation mode is HALT, the value specifies the first cycle that will not be recorded any more.
- If the current interpretation mode is NONE, the value can also be specified, but it is ignored until the interpretation mode is changed.

The range of the value must be between 0 and 2^48 - 1

If the value is interpreted as a start (stop) value, recording will start (stop) at the largest multiple of 8 smaller than error_map_pos.

 |
 |

ref_port

 |

This parameter specifies the single port which is used for counting the cycles specified with the error_map_pos parameter. When this reference port has completed the specified number of cycles, cycle recording will be started or stopped for all ports. Note that the reference port must belong to the start label. In particular, you must specify the default @ for single port start labels.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

In the query, you can specify a port list. For the ports that are not used as the reference port, the reply will return the calculated Error Map positions. These are derived from the Error Map position of the reference port and the ratio between the period lengths of the reference port and the other port in the primary timing setup. If you specify @@, DCRM? will return the settings for all ports of the current start label.

 |
 |

answer_type

 |

This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRP  DCRP  -  Digital Compare Result Positioning）

```
> PCLK? "mu_burst",1,(@@)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,20,(P1)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,10,(P2)
> DCGM ALL,STRT,NONE
> DCRP 20,(P2)
> DCRP? (@@)
< DCRP 10,(P1)
< DCRP 20,(P2)
```

This example illustrates the calculation of the cycle numbers for the ports that are not used as the reference port. For interpretation mode STRT, recording will start for the reference port `P2` with cycle 16 (largest multiple of 8 smaller than 20). Since the period length for `P1` is twice the period length of `P2`, recording for `P1` will start with cycle 8 (largest multiple of 8 smaller than 10).

### Example 2（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRP  DCRP  -  Digital Compare Result Positioning）

```
> SQGB STSQ,14,(P2)
> DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE
> DCRP 20,(P2)
> DCRP? (@@)
< DCRP 7,(P1)
< DCRP 14,(P2)
> SQGB STRD,
> DCRP? (@@)
< DCRP 10,(P1)
< DCRP 20,(P2)
```

This example shows that a definition of the Error Map position with DCRP is ignored when the sequencer mode is STSQ, but that it can subsequently be activated. Note that the DCGM command only serves to make the initial ineffectiveness of the definition visible. It is not possible to execute a functional test with these settings when the sequencer mode is STSQ.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRS  -  Digital Compare Result Size）

```
DCRS? [answer_type,] {map},[mode],[bits],{(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
DCRS {map},{x-mode},{bits},{no_of_cycles},{(port)}
```

Parameters
 |

answer_type

 |

This parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |
 |

map

 |

The only allowed value is EMAP (for the detailed error map).

 |
 |

mode

 |

Specifies the level of granularity with which the receive edges of one cycle are recorded. The allowed values are 1, 2, 4, and 8; for Smart Scale, 6 is also possible. If you omit this parameter, the mode set with DCRM is used.

 |
 |

bits

 |

Specifies how detailed the recorded error code is to be in case of failure. If you omit this parameter, the value set with DCRM is used. Possible values are:

 |
 |

PF

 |

Only a one bit Pass/Fail result will be returned. This value is not allowed for Pin Scale cards if mode is set to 1.

 |
 |

PFC

 |

In case of failure, a more detailed two bit code will be returned. PFC is not allowed if mode is set to 8.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

Returns the number of test system cycles that can be stored in the Error Map.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

Specifies the ports for which the capacity of the Error Map is to be returned. If you specify @@, DCRS? will return the capacity for all ports.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRS  -  Digital Compare Result Size）

```
> DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE
> DCRT TP,(P1)
> DCRM EMAP,8,PF,(P1)
> CYRM CYCL,,(P1)
> DCRS? EMAP,,,(P1)
< DCRS EMAP,8,PF,2048,(P1)
> DCRP 3360,(P1)
> FTST?
> EMAP? PPIN,1312,2048,EDGE,8,PF,ALL,BYTE,(P1)
```

This example shows how to get hold of the first cycles of your area of interest under the following conditions:

- The area of interest is greater than the capacity of the error map.
- The acquire mode is set to ALL with DCGM, so that the first recorded cycles will be overwritten when the error map is full before the end of the test.

The solution is to interpret the error map position defined with DCRP as a stop value (by setting the second parameter of DCGM to HALT), and to calculate the last cycle to be recorded as:

```
first_cycle_of_interest + capacity_of_the_Error_Map
```

In the example, the first addend is 1312. The second addend is determined with the DCRS? query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRT  DCRT  -  Digital Compare Result Target）

|

target

 |

Specifies the target area for the error map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

TP

 |

The error map data is stored within the test processor. This is the default.

 |
 |

RAM

 |

The error map data is stored in the external memory as the vector memory.

Note that if you select the external memory as the location of the detailed error map on a P/Ce system, the parallel vector areas must be located in the Sequencer Memory.

 |
 |

port_list

   | Specifies the ports for which the target is to be defined:

- If you specify @@ (all ports, multi-port label), the DCRT command will set the specified target area for all configured ports.
- If you specify @ (all pins, non-multiport label), the DCRT command will set the specified target area for the default port (all pins).
- If you specify the name of a specific port (multi-port label), the DCRT command will set the specified target area for that port only.
 |
 |

answer_type

 |

This query parameter specifies whether the current configuration or the configuration of the last executed test is to be returned. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

CONF

 |

The current configuration is returned. This is the default.

 |
 |

 |

EXEC

 |

The configuration of the last executed test is returned.

 |

### Examples（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › DCRT  DCRT  -  Digital Compare Result Target）

### Querying the location of the error map for all ports and setting it for specific ones (multi-port label)

This example queries the location of the error map for all ports. Then, it sets the location of the error map in the test processor for port `P2`, and in RDRAM for `P1`:

```
DCRT? (@@) // Note: this is equivalent to specifying DCRT? CONF,(@@)
DCRT RAM,(P1) // Set location of error map for port P1 in RDRAM
DCRT TP,(P2) // Set location of error map for port P2 in Test Processor
```

### Querying and setting the location of the result map for the default port (non multi-port label)

To query or set the location of the error map for the default port, you need to specify @ as the port_list of the DCRT? and DCRT commands, respectively:

```
DCRT? (@) // Query location of error map for the default port
DCRT TP,(@) // Set location of error map for the default port to Test Processor
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EAEX  -  Edge Action EXpected data）

```
EAEX? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EAEX {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, [err_type], {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EAEX  -  Edge Action EXpected data）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. The scanning method and the range of values this parameter can take depend on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode, enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis mode, enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range. If the timing set was changed within the requested cycle range, more than one answer is returned.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. You can use the @ character to read the edge actions for all pins.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is optional and specifies what type of error information is available. It is always NOER since this query only reports expected data.

 |
 |

NOER

 |

Error information is not available. The reported range lies outside the range covered by the Error Map.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. Edges without action are not reported.

 |
 |

 |

The data is to be decoded as follows:

Each cycle of the reported cycle range is preceded by a two byte header information:

- First byte, bits 7, 6, 5, 4: Always zero, reserved for future use.
- First byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0: Always 1: number of waveforms contained in the device cycle.
- Second byte: Number of edge actions following (0 - 140)
 |
 |

 |

Each of the following edge actions is described by two bytes:

- First byte, bit 7: Channel selector for differential pins. The first channel has the value 0, the second the value 1.
- First byte, bits 6, 5, 4, 3: Waveform index (0 - 9)
- First byte, bits 2, 1, 0: Edge index (0 - 7)
- Second byte, bit 7: Error flag

0: No error on receive edge, or a drive edge

1: Cannot occur since only expected data are reported

- Second byte, bits 6, 5: Data parameter

00: Fixed value

10: Data parameter 1

11: Data parameter 2

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bit 4: Edge direction

0: Drive/tri-state edge

1: Receive edge

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 0, then drive/tri-state data:

Bits 3, 2: Tri-state data

00: Not used

10: Tri-state off

11: Tri-state on

01: Reserved for future use

Bits 1, 0: Drive data

00: Not used

10: Drive 0

11: Drive 1

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 1, then receive data compare method:

0001: Edge compare to intermediate

0010: Edge compare to 0

0011: Edge compare to 1

0100: Edge compare to mask

0101: Edge compare to unstable

1001: Window compare to intermediate

1010: Window compare to 0

1011: Window compare to 1

1100: Window compare to mask

1101: Window compare to unstable

1111: Window close

0000: Reserved for future use

0111: Reserved for future use

1000: Reserved for future use

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EAEX  -  Edge Action EXpected data）

```
EAEX? 0, 1, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
EAEX 0,1,3,,(pin1),#9000000010\x01\x04\x00\x0B\x01\x0A\x02\x19\x03\x1F\x0A
```

This example returns edge action drive and expected data (in hex notation) for one cycle. To decode the data, convert it into binary notation and use the lists above.

The data in binary format is:

```
0000 0001 0000 0100 0000 0000 0000 1011 0000 0001
0000 1010 0000 0010 0001 1001 0000 0011 0001 1111
```

The device cycle contains 1 waveform with 4 edge actions. The edge actions are RZ on the drive edges 1 and 2 and a window compare to intermediate on the receive edges 3 and 4.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

```
EARD? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {type}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EARD {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {type}, [err_type], {(pinlist)}, [MUX,] {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. You can enter a value between 0 and 2^48.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2^48.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

type

 |

This parameter specifies which actions will be reported. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

RCV

 |

Only receive edges are reported

 |
 |

 |

DRV

 |

Only drive edge actions are reported.

 |
 |

 |

BOTH

 |

Both drive and receive edge actions are reported. This is the default.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is used in the reply to inform about the recording mode, or if the specified cycle range is not included in the error map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

NOER

 |

Indicates that the part of the requested cycle range specified in the reply is outside the recorded error map.

 |
 |

 |

PF

 |

Indicates that the requested cycle range is included in the recorded error map, and that 1 bit results have been recorded.

 |
 |

 |

PFC

 |

Indicates that the requested cycle range is included in the recorded error map, and that 2 bit results have been recorded.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can use the @ character to read the error data for all pins.

For an HXA pin, specify one of the Pin Scale pins to which it is mapped.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. The format of the reconstructed data supports expanded device cycles with up to 10 waveforms and 16 edges per waveform. Edges without action are not reported.

 |
 |

 |

The data is to be decoded as follows:

 |
 |

 |

Byte 0:

 |

Contains multiplexing information for HXA pins. This byte is returned only once in the reply.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 7-4: Pin multiplexing factor. Specifies the number of Pin Scale pins that are mapped to one HXA pin or differential pin. 1 stands for differential pins or 2-multiplexed HXA pins, 3 for 4-multiplexed HXA pins.

The parameter is set to 0 for normal pins.

 |
 |

 |

 |

bits 3-0: Channel selector. If the pin multiplexing factor is > 0, this field specifies the logical position of the pin in the multiplexing order.

 |
 |

 |

 |

Information relating to HXA multiplexing is only returned if the MUX flag is set.

 |
 |

 |

Byte 1:

 |

Always 1. This byte is returned for every cycle.

 |
 |

 |

Byte 2,3:

 |

The number of actions to follow. The maximum, for an HXA pin mapped to 4 Pin Scale pins, is 640. This byte is returned for every cycle.

 |
 |

 |

Every edge action is described in 3 bytes.

 |
 |

 |

Byte A:

 |

Normal action or OOB action. Possible values are:

0: Normal action

1: OOB action

 |
 |

 |

Byte B:

 |

Edge index (0-7 for normal pins, up to 31 for HXA pins).

 |
 |

 |

Byte C:

 |

Action data

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 7: Action type. The following values can occur:

0: Drive action

1: Receive action

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 6-4: Received value, 0 for drive actions. For receive actions, the following codes can occur:

000: No error (expected = received)

001: Intermediate

010: 0

011: 1

101: Unstable

110: Reconstruction not possible

 |
 |

 |

 |

bit 3-0: Expected compare/drive action.

The following values can occur for drive actions:

1010: Drive to 0, tri-state off

1011: Drive to 1, tri-state off

1110: Drive to 0, tri-state on

1111: Drive to 1, tri-state on

The following values can occur for receive actions:

0001: Edge compare to intermediate

0010: Edge compare to 0

0011: Edge compare to 1

0100: Edge compare to mask

0101: Edge compare to unstable

0110: Edge compare, reconstruction not possible

1001: Window compare to intermediate

1010: Window compare to 0

1011: Window compare to 1

1100: Window compare to mask

1101: Window compare to unstable

1110: Window compare, reconstruction not possible

1111: Window close

 |
 |

 |

 |

The codes for "reconstruction not possible" are only returned if the edge failed in single-ended standard mode with one bit results.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

```
> EARD? 2,1,BOTH,(TX1_d0)
< EARD 2,1,BOTH,PF,MUX,(TX1_d0),#9000000052
      \x10\x01\x00\x10
      \x00\x00\x82\x00\x01\x82\x00\x02\x82\x00\x03\x82\x00\x04\x82\x00\x05\x82\x00\x06\x82\x00\x07\x82
 \x00\x08\x82\x00\x09\x82\x00\x0a\x82\x00\x0b\x82\x00\x0c\x82\x00\x0d\x82\x00\x0e\x82\x00\x0f\x82
```

This example shows the results for a Pin Scale pin TX1_d0, which is multiplexed together with one other Pin Scale pin to an HXA pin. Since the MUX flag is set, the combined results of both these pins are returned in the reply.

Byte 0 indicates that TX1_d0 is one of two multiplexed Pin Scale pins, and that it has the logical position 0 in the multiplexing order. Byte 2 and 3 contain the information that the cycle contains 16 edges.

Byte A is the same for all edges and says that the edge is associated with a fixed value (not a data parameter), and that the waveform to which it belongs occupies position 0 in the device cycle. The edges of the two Pin Scale pins are interleaved according to the logical position in the multiplexing order. The edges of TX1_d0, which has position 0, are those with an even edge index (byte B), starting from 0. The edges of the other multiplexed Pin Scale pin (position 1) have an odd index. The actions (byte C) are also the same for all edges, namely an edge compare to 0 where expected = received value (that is, no error).

### Example 2（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARD  -  Edge Action Result Data）

The EARD? answer will be split if the requested cycle range is greater than the available error map information, as shown below:

 !`Example`（raw: `../../../../raw/11910.png`）

```
> EARD? 0,15000, (pin1)
< EARD 0, 100, BOTH, NOER, (pin1), BinData        (a)
< EARD 100, 9900, BOTH, PF, (pin1), BinData       (b)
< EARD 10000, 5000, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData      (c)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARE  -  Edge Action REceived data）

```
EARE? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EARE? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, [err_type],{(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARE  -  Edge Action REceived data）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. You can enter a value between 0 and 2^48.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2^48.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can use the @ character to read the error data for all pins.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is optional and specifies what type of error information is available. The system returns a status only for O or IO pins:

 |
 |

ERON

 |

Error information is available. The cycle range where error information is available is reported by the query `VALD? - (VALid Data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.316_VALD__-__VALid_Data.md`）.

 |
 |

NOER

 |

Error information is not available. The reported range lies outside the range covered by the Error Map.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. The format of the reconstructed data supports expanded device cycles with up to 10 waveforms and 14 edges per waveform. Edges without action are not reported.

 |
 |

 |

The data is to be decoded as follows:

Each cycle of the reported cycle range is preceded by a two byte header information:

- First byte, bits 7, 6, 5, 4: Always zero, reserved for future use.
- First byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0: Always 1: number of waveforms contained in the device cycle.
- Second byte: Number of edge actions following (0 - 140)
 |
 |

 |

Each of the following edge actions is described by two bytes:

- First byte, bit 7: Channel selector for differential pins. The first channel has the value 0, the second the value 1.
- First byte, bits 6, 5, 4, 3: Waveform index (always 0)
- First byte, bits 2, 1, 0: Edge index (0 - 7)
- Second byte, bit 7: Error flag

0: No error on receive edge, or a drive edge

1: Error on receive edge. (The system returns this only if err_type is ERON.) In case of a failing window compare, both the window open edge and the window close edge are marked.

- Second byte, bits 6, 5: Data parameter

00: Fixed value

10: Data parameter 1

11: Data parameter 2

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bit 4: Edge direction

0: Drive/tri-state edge

1: Receive edge

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 0, then drive/tri-state data:

Bits 3, 2: Tri-state data

00: Not used

10: Tri-state off

11: Tri-state on

01: Reserved for future use

Bits 1, 0: Drive data

00: Not used

10: Drive 0

11: Drive 1

01: Reserved for future use

- Second byte, bits 3, 2, 1, 0

If bit 4 is a 1, then receive data compare method:

0001: Edge compare to intermediate

0010: Edge compare to 0

0011: Edge compare to 1

0100: Edge compare to mask

0101: Edge compare to unstable

0110: Edge compare, reconstruction not possible

1001: Window compare to intermediate

1010: Window compare to 0

1011: Window compare to 1

1100: Window compare to mask

1101: Window compare to unstable

1110: Window compare, reconstruction not possible

1111: Window close

0000: Reserved for future use

0111: Reserved for future use

1000: Reserved for future use

 |

If reconstruction is not possible (code 110 on bits 2, 1, 0), there has been more than one edge or window compare within a single test system cycle.

If error bit 7 is set, an error has occurred on at least one of these edge or window compares.

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EARE  -  Edge Action REceived data）

```
EARE? 0, 1, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
EARE 0,1,3,ERON,(pin1),#9000000010\x01\x04\x00\x0B\x01\x0A\x02\x9A\x03\x9F\x0A
```

This example returns edge action drive and received data (in hex notation) for one cycle. To decode the data, convert it into binary notation and use the lists above.

The data in binary format is:

```
0000 0001 0000 0100 0000 0000 0000 1011 0000 0001
0000 1010 0000 0010 1001 1010 0000 0011 0001 1111
```

The device cycle contains 1 waveform with 4 edge actions. The edge actions are RZ on the drive edges 1 and 2 and a failing window compare (received value: 0) on the receive edges 3 and 4.

The EARE? answer will be split if the requested cycle range is greater than the available error map information, as shown below:

 !`Example`（raw: `../../../../raw/11910.png`）

```
EARE? 0,15000, (pin1)
EARE 0, 100, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData (a)
EARE 100, 9900, 1, ERON, (pin1), BinData (b)
EARE 10000, 5000, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData (c)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EDGE  -  EDGE errors）

```
EDGE? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EDGE {fail_string},{(pinlist)}
```

for each group of consecutive pins having the same result.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EDGE  -  EDGE errors）

|

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which edge direction definitions are to be read back. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the DFGP (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

fail_string

 |

One character per edge. F means failed and . means not failed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EDGE  -  EDGE errors）

```
> EDGE? (pin1, pin2, pin3, pin4)
< EDGE ...F.... (pin1,pin2)
< EDGE .F..F... (pin3)
< EDGE ..F..... (pin4)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

```
EMAP? {pin_res},{start_cycle},{no_of_cycles},{resolution_mode},[results_per_cycle],[bits],{rep_mode},{results_align},[byte_max], [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
EMAP {pin_res},{start_cycle},{no_of_cycles},{resolution_mode},{results_per_cycle},{bits},{rep_mode},{results_align},[byte_max],{(pinlist)}, [MUX,] {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

pin_res

 |

Specifies the pin granularity. Possible values are:

 |
 |

PPIN

 |

Separate results will be reported for every pin of the pin list.

 |
 |

COMB

 |

Only one global result will be reported for all pins of the pin list.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

In the query, this is an integer that defines the first test cycle to be reported.

In the reply, this is the first cycle that is returned. If the requested cycle range exceeds the capacity of the Error Map, the index of the first returned cycle may be greater than that of the first requested cycle.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of test cycles to be reported. The range for this parameter is 0 to2^48 - 1. In the reply, this parameter indicates the number of cycles which have been read. If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the requested range.

 |
 |

resolution_mode

 |

Defines how the recorded results are combined. Possible values are:

 |
 |

CYCL

 |

In this mode all recorded results are combined into one result per cycle.

 |
 |

SCYC

 |

In this mode the results are reported as they were recorded.

 |
 |

EDGE

 |

This mode requests error information for each recorded receive edge. If the results_per_cycle parameter is omitted, the reply will return all 8 edges, even if only 2 or 4 edges were recorded; the edges that were not recorded will be represented as passed. In this way, the edge number of the failing recorded edges will be indicated by their position within the result data stream.

The EDGE option requires one of the following two sets of conditions to be satisfied:

- The mode parameter of DCRM is > 1.
- No result combination, as specified with the sub_cycles parameter of DCRM, contains more than 1 edge.

Note that this requires that result combinations are specified with DCRM.

- The edges in the sub_cycles string are in ascending order.

or (see `Retrieving edge information by repeating the test`（raw: `02.06.11.01.02.02.01_Retrieving_edge_information_by_repeating_the_test.md`）):

- DCRM is set to 1,PFC.
- CYRM is set to EDGE.
- CYRP is set to MULT (the default).
 |
 |

results_per_cycle

 |

This parameter is only relevant for resolution mode EDGE. If you are only interested in an initial segment of the 8 edge sequence that is returned by default, you can specify the length of this segment here. In certain situations, this allows you to reduce the size of the reply.

If the MUX flag is set, and one of the specified PS (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the edges of the PS pins that are multiplexed to this HXA pin will be returned interleaved as follows:

r1 of PS pin 1, ..., r1 of PS pin n, r2 of PS pin 1, ..., r2 of PS pin n,...,

r8 of PS pin 1, ..., r8 of PS pin n

Here, n is 2 or 4, and the PS pins are ordered as defined in the BOARDCONF section of the model file.

Accordingly, if the multiplexing factor of the HXA pin is 4, and 5 edges per cycle are requested, then the first edge of every PS pin plus the second edge of the first PS pin will be returned.

 |
 |

bits

 |

Specifies how detailed the reported error code is to be in case of failure. Possible values are:

 |
 |

PF

 |

Only a 1 bit Pass/Fail result will be returned.

 |
 |

PFC

 |

In case of failure, a more detailed two bit code will be returned.

The received data can be reconstructed from the expected data and the error code as follows:

  !`Parameters`（raw: `../../../../raw/57171.png`）

"I" stands for "Intermediate" and "U" for "Unstable".

Note that 2 bit codes can only be reported if 2 bit codes were recorded (bits parameter of `DCRM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.46_DCRM__DCRM__-__Digital_Compare_Result_Mode.md`） set to PFC).

 |
 |

rep_mode

 |

Specifies the reporting mode for the Error Map. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All cycles within the selected area are reported. If the data was recorded in acquire failure mode, EMAP? will expand the reply accordingly.

 |
 |

EOLY

 |

As far as is feasible, only failed cycles are reported.

 |
 |

results_align

 |

Specifies how the results, as defined by the resolution_mode, results_per_cycle and bits parameters, are aligned within the returned data stream. The supported values are:

 |
 |

BYTE

 |

By this option, no byte will contain results of more than one cycle. If the results returned per cycle do not make up exactly one or two bytes, they will be padded accordingly.

Note that if two bit codes are requested for resolution mode EDGE, and results_per_cycle is set to a value < 8, the results will always be padded to two bytes, even if results_per_cycle is 鈮?4.

 |
 |

 |

PACK

 |

This option is mainly relevant for resolution modes CYCL and SCYC. It will have the effect that the results are not padded, but follow one another immediately. Thus, the results of 8 or 4 cycles (depending on the bits setting) will be packed into one byte in CYCL mode, and the results of 4 or 2 cycles (depending on the bits setting) will be packed into one byte in SCYC mode.

PACK will have an effect on resolution mode EDGE only, if the initial segment defined with results_per_cycle already makes up a complete byte. This would be the case, for example, if two bit codes are recorded for all 8 edges, and results_per_cycle is set to 4.

 |
 |

byte_max

 |

In the query, this parameter specifies the maximum number of bytes that may be returned. This option is primarily intended for the reporting mode EOLY, where the size of the data that will be returned cannot be calculated beforehand.

In the answer, the following codes can be returned:

 |
 |

EOB

 |

The cycle range of the query exceeds the specified maximum number of bytes.

 |
 |

EOF

 |

The cycle range of the query exceeds the cycle range to be recorded (as defined with `DCGM`（raw: `02.06.02.02.44_DCGM__DCGM__-__Digital_Compare_Global_Mode.md`） and `DCRP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.47_DCRP__DCRP__-__Digital_Compare_Result_Positioning.md`）).

 |
 |

EOM

 |

The cycle range of the query exceeds the actual content of the Error Map.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

In particular, if information on the edge level is requested, then the edges of all multiplexed Pin Scale pins will be returned interleaved as follows:

r1 of PS pin 1, ..., r1 of PS pin n,

r2 of PS pin 1, ..., r2 of PS pin n,

...

r8 of PS pin 1, ..., r8 of PS pin n

Here, n is 2 or 4, and the order of the PS pins is that defined in the BOARDCONF section of the model file.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins or pin groups for which information is returned. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in the pin list must have type O or IO. They must also all belong to the same port in the current start label.

If the MUX flag is set, then each pin in the pin list should represent a different HXA pin, and all HXA pins should have the same multiplexing factor.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

Nn1n2...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The data stream itself consists of blocks each of which contains result data for every cycle (passed as well as failed) within a contiguous cycle range. Every block has a header that specifies

- the number of the first cycle of the block (8 bytes, big-endian encoded), and
- the block size in bytes (4 bytes, big-endian encoded).

The result data is also big-endian encoded.

If the rep_mode parameter has been set to ALL, only one block is returned, which contains the whole selected result range.

If rep_mode has been set to EOLY, then EMAP? will close a block after a failed cycle, and start a new block at the next failed cycle, if the passed cycles in-between occupy at least as much space as a block header (12 bytes). See the first example below.

If you are working with HXA pins note that the block size specifies bytes, not cycles. Thus, a block of size 32 contains 4 cycles of a HXA pin with 4 multiplexed Pin Scale pins.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

```
> EMAP? COMB,0,42,EDGE,8,,EOLY,BYTE,,(dut_tx3)
< EMAP COMB,0,42,EDGE,8,PF,EOLY,BYTE,,(dut_tx3),#9000000038
  \x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x0F
  \x00\x00\x00\x03
  \x03\x00\x80
  \x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x1F
  \x00\x00\x00\x0B
  \x80\x00\x00\x80\xA0\x00\x80\xA0\x00\x00\x0A
```
