This example shows the format of the binary data that is returned by EMAP?. The data stream has been broken up to make it more readable. Two data blocks are returned. The information is to be decoded as follows:

 |

Block

 |

Start cycle

 |

Number of cycles

 |

Failing edges

 |
 |

 |

Hex

 |

Dec

 |

Hex

 |

Dec

 |

 |
 |

1. block

 |

0F

 |

15

 |

3

 |

3

 |

edges 7,8 (03 = 00000011) in cycle 15

edge 1 (80 = 1000000) in cycle 17

 |
 |

2. block

 |

1F

 |

31

 |

0B

 |

11

 |

For example:

edge 1 (80 = 10000000) in cycle 31

edges 1,3 (A0 = 10100000) in cycle 35

 |

For each cycle, all 8 edges are reported. The first block is closed because 13 passing cycles (= 13 bytes) lie between the failed cycle 17 and the next failed cycle 31.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

```
> FTST?
< FTST F
> EMAP? COMB,0,50000000,EDGE,8,PF,EOLY,BYTE,3500000,(O1,O2)
< EMAP COMB,0,12000000,EDGE,8,PF,EOLY,BYTE,EOB,(O1,O2),#90003500000
```

This example illustrates the use of the byte_max parameter. The test comprises 50 million cycles. The Error Map is located in the RDRAM. If the number of errors exceeds 0.5% of the cycles, that is, as soon as more than 250,000 errors have been found, the device is to be rejected offhand. Therefore, EMAP? is called with the EOLY option, so that only failed cycles are returned, and the maximum length of the reply is restricted to 3,500,000. This is based on the worst case assumption that every error occupies 13 bytes. The answer indicates that in fact more than 0.5% of the cycles have failed. Note that only 7% of the 50 million test cycles have to be uploaded to the system controller.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

The following example illustrates the difference between the resolution modes EDGE and SCYC.

```
> DCRM? EMAP,(@)
< DCRM EMAP,4,PFC,"c1:1 c2:2 c3:7 c4:8",(@)
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,EDGE,,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,12,EDGE,8,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out),#224
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00001100   11000011   10000011   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000011   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000

> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,SCYC,,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,12,SCYC,4,PF,ALL,BYTE,,(out),#224
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00001100   11110000   10110000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00110000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
```

The first failing cycle is cycle 0 (fifth byte in the second line of the EMAP? reply); in this cycle, edges 1,2,7,8 have failed. In addition, cycle 1 (edges 1,3,4) and 7 (edges 3,4) contain errors. With the PACK option, resolution mode SCYC compresses 12 bytes into 6:

```
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,SCYC,,PF,ALL,PACK,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,12,SCYC,4,PF,ALL,PACK,,(out),#218
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000110   11111011   00000000   00000000   00000011
     00000000   00000000
```

But the following call of EMAP? will produce an error message:

```
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,12,EDGE,4,PF,ALL,PACK,,(out)
```

The reason for this is that the results per cycle are only 4 bits long.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › EMAP  -  Error MAP）

The following example shows the expanded format for 2 bit error codes (2 bytes per cycle):

```
> DCRM? EMAP,(@)
< DCRM EMAP,4,PFC,"c1:1 c2:2 c3:3 c4:4",(@)
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,7,EDGE,,PFC,ALL,BYTE,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,7,EDGE,8,PFC,ALL,BYTE,,(out),#228
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00001110   11110011   00000000   00001111   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00001100   00000000
```

In cycle 0, edges 1, 2, and 4 have failed. In cycle 1, edges 3 and 4 have failed. In cycle 6, edge 3 has failed.

```
> $EMAP? PPIN,0,7,EDGE,4,PFC,ALL,PACK,,(out)
< EMAP PPIN,0,7,EDGE,4,PFC,ALL,PACK,,(out),#220
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00000000   00000111   11110011   00001111   00000000   00000000
     00000000   00000000   00001100
```

In this case, the PACK option is accepted because the initial segment of 4 two bit codes already makes up one byte.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCC  -  ERror in Cycle range Count）

ERCC? {type}, {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}

returns:

ERCC {type}, {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles} [, granularity], {valid_code}, {no_of_errors}, [map_mode], [MUX,] {(pin)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCC  -  ERror in Cycle range Count）

|

type

 |

The type parameter can be:

 |
 |

ERCP

 |

Error count per pin. Each pin returns a separate answer.

 |
 |

ERCG

 |

Error count global, which requests the sum of all error counts reported by ERCP. Only one answer is generated.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

An integer that defines the cycle following which failures are to be counted. If the queried range starts before the analyze delay (see SQGB command) then the returned value will be corrected to a later cycle number.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

An integer that defines the cycle range in which failures are to be counted. If the queried start_cycle has to be corrected or the amount of failures causes an overflow of the error map then the returned value will be corrected to a smaller number of cycles.

 |
 |

granularity

 |

This parameter specifies how errors are condensed. Possible values are:

 |
 |

CYCL

   | The number of failing cycles is returned. |
 |

EDGE

   | The number of failing edges is returned. |
 |

valid_code

 |

This parameter tells you if the error count that the system returns is valid. The system may return:

 |
 |

VALD

 |

The error count is valid. This reply is always returned in offline mode.

 |
 |

OVFL

 |

This signifies an Error Map overflow. no_of_errors contains the number of errors that occurred until this happened.

 |
 |

LESS

 |

Either the start of the cycle range was before the error map error acquisition started or the end was after the test has ended or both. If an overflow condition and the less condition are both true, LESS is reported.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the errors from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to this HXA pin will be used to calculate the total number of errors.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which errors are to be counted. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to retrieve the data for all configured pins.

 |
 |

no_of_errors

 |

An integer that contains the number of errors found in the queried range of cycles. If the reported range of cycles is smaller than the queried range then this value represents only the number of errors in the reported range and not in the requested range. It should be regarded as the minimum number of errors in the requested range, and could be higher.

 |
 |

map_mode

 |

The system returns the current Error Map mode. This is:

 |
 |

F160

 |

The pin operating mode is Standard mode

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCC  -  ERror in Cycle range Count）

```
> ERCC? ERCP, 1000, 200, (pin1,pin2)
< ERCC ERCP, 1000, 200, VALD, 5, F160, (pin1)
< ERCC ERCP, 1000, 200, VALD, 1, F160, (pin2)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCT  -  ERror CounT）

```
ERCT? {type}, [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERCT {type}, {valid_code}, {no_of_errors}, [map_mode], [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCT  -  ERror CounT）

|

type

 |

The type parameter can be:

 |
 |

ERCP

 |

Error count per pin, as delivered by the hardware error counter. The map_mode is always F160. For differential pins, the maximum of the specified pin and its counterpart is returned.

 |
 |

ERCG

 |

Error count global, which requests a sum of all error counts reported by ERCP. No map_mode information is returned.

 |
 |

EOLY

 |

The Errors OnLY option delivers the numbers of failed cycles per pin from the detailed Error Map. The map_mode is F160. For differential pins, the numbers of those cycles will be returned where at least one of the pins produced an error.

 |
 |

valid_code

 |

This parameter tells you if the error count the system returns is valid. The system may return:

 |
 |

VALD

 |

The error count is valid. (This reply is always returned in offline mode.)

 |
 |

OVFL

 |

Signifies error counter overflow. The hardware error counter has a range of 2^31.

 |
 |

no_of_errors

 |

This parameter returns the total number of results containing errors for one of the specified pins. For the ERCG type, it returns the sum of all the error counts for the individual pins.

 |
 |

map_mode

 |

The system returns the Error Map mode. The only possible value is:

 |
 |

F160

 |

The pin is operating in standard mode

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the errors from all Pin Scale pins multiplexed to this HXA pin will be used to calculate the total number of errors.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The command returns the error count only for pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCT  -  ERror CounT）

```
> ERCT? ERCP, (Q0)
< ERCT ERCP, VALD, 1, F160, (Q0)
```

This example requests the error count for pin Q0. The system returns one error, the error count is valid, the map mode is F160.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCY  -  ERror CYcle）

```
ERCY? {type}, {start_cyc_no}, [no_of_cycles], [no_of_errors], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERCY {type}, {cycle_no}, [window_len], [expected_data], [received_data], [data_type], {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

type

 |

Selects the type of error data to be returned. The parameter can be:

 |
 |

CYC

 |

Only Error Cycles are returned.

 |
 |

EXP

 |

Error Cycles with expected data is returned.

 |
 |

REC

 |

Error Cycles with received data is returned.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Error Cycles with expected and received data is returned.

 |
 |

start_cyc_no

 |

An integer that defines the cycle following which failures are to be returned.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

An integer that defines the cycle range in which failures are to be reported. This parameter must be entered if the no_of_errors parameter has not been included.

 |
 |

no_of_errors

 |

This parameter determines how many cycles containing errors are to be returned for every pin, starting from start_cycle. This parameter must be entered if the no_of_cycles parameter has not been included.

 |
 |

cycle_no

 |

Specifies the cycle where an error has occurred.

 |
 |

window_len

 |

Window length is an optional parameter returned only if you have specified the error type EXP, REC or ALL and the cycle containing an error occurred during a window compare. The parameter window_len delivers the length of the compare window. A length of one test system cycle returns a 0. A length of two cycles returns a -1, and so on. An error occurring during a window compare is reported in the cycle where the compare window closes. The number of cycles making up the window is therefore negative.

In cases where cycle-boundary crossing takes place, the window_len parameter is useful when re-constructing in which cycle the error actually occurred.

 |
 |

expected_data

 |

Expected Data optional parameter. Returned only if the selected data type is EXP or ALL. The values returned can be:

 |
 |

F0

 |

expected data is 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

expected data is 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

expected data is intermediate

 |
 |

FU

 |

expected data is unstable

 |
 |

FN

 |

No reconstruction possible due to multiple compare edges in a single cycle. This will usually be the case when testing in X mode.

 |
 |

received_data

 |

Received Data optional parameter. Returned only if the selected data type is REC or ALL. The values returned can be:

 |
 |

F0

 |

received data is 0

 |
 |

F1

 |

received data is 1

 |
 |

FI

 |

received data is intermediate

 |
 |

FU

 |

received data is unstable

 |
 |

FN

 |

No reconstruction possible due to multiple compare edges in a single cycle. This will usually be the case when testing in X mode.

 |
 |

data_type

 |

Data Type optional parameter. Returned only if the selected data type is EXP, REC or ALL. The values returned can be:

 |
 |

FIX

 |

The edge or window compare was made to a fixed state.

 |
 |

E1

 |

The edge or window compare was made to the E1 parameter.

 |
 |

E2

 |

The edge or window compare was made to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

FE1

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to a fixed state, and one edge or window compare to the E1 parameter.

 |
 |

FE2

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to a fixed state, and one edge or window compare to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

E1E2

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to the E1 parameter and one edge or window compare to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

FE1E2

 |

Multiple compare. Contains at least one edge or window compare to a fixed state, one edge or window compare to the E1 parameter and one edge or window compare to the E2 parameter.

 |
 |

See also the `WAVE`（raw: `02.06.02.02.333_WAVE__WAVE__-__WAVEform.md`） command for an explanation of the expected data parameters.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which error cycles are to be retrieved. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. The @ character can be used to retrieve the data for all configured pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERCY  -  ERror CYcle）

```
> ERCY? ALL,0,,2,(pin1,pin2)
< ERCY ALL,215,-2,F1,F0,E1,(pin1)
< ERCY ALL,240,,F0,FI,FIX,(pin1)
< ERCY ALL,17,,F0,F1,FIX,(pin2)
```

This example queries the system for the first two error cycles of pin1 and of pin2, starting from cycle 0. Expected and received data are also to be returned. The system returns the first two error cycles of pin1. For pin2 only one error cycle exists, therefore only one cycle can be returned.

There is an error on pin1 in cycle 215 which was a window compare 3 cycles long. The expected data was a 1, the receive data was a 0. The window compare was made to the E1 parameter.

There is an error on pin1 in cycle 240 which was an edge compare to a fixed state. The expected data was a 0, the received data was intermediate.

There is an error on pin2 in cycle 17 which was an edge compare to a fixed state. The expected data was 0, the received data was 1.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERMP  -  ERror MaP）

```
ERMP? {map_id}, {start_unit}, {no_of_units}, [map_mode],[edges,] [MUX,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
ERMP {map_id}, {start_unit}, {no_of_units}, {map_mode},[edges,] [MUX,] {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

map_id

 |

Determines the type of Error Map for which data is to be read out. Note that the allowed values depend on the settings of the DCRM command. Options that request two bit values can only be specified if the bits parameter of DCRM is set to PFC.

The possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

DERR

 |

This option provides per pin pass/fail results and full error codes per test cycle for all pins in the pinlist. The system returns values for the error codes PASS, FAIL1, FAIL2 and FAIL3 using a two-bit code as follows:

PASS 00

FAIL1 01

FAIL2 10

FAIL3 11

The received data can be reconstructed from the expected data and from the error code values in the following table:

 |
 |

 |

 |

 |

Expected Data

 |

FAIL1

 |

FAIL2

 |

FAIL3

 |
 |

Low

 |

Intermediate

 |

High

 |

Unstable

 |
 |

Intermediate

 |

High

 |

Low

 |

Unstable

 |
 |

High

 |

Low

 |

Intermediate

 |

Unstable

 |
 |

Unstable

 |

Low

 |

Intermediate

 |

High

   | |

 |
 |

 |

 |

Note that this mode requires that the DCRM command has been set to 1,PFC, and that the map_mode parameter of ERMP? is set to F160.

 |
 |

 |

EDGE

 |

This option reads the error map and returns an overall one bit Pass/Fail result (combining the results of all selected pins) of the edges selected by DCRM. The reply will not only return the results, but will also indicate the numbers of the recorded edges.

Note that this mode is only applicable if

- no result combination, as specified with the sub_cycles parameter of DCRM, contains more than 1 edge,
- the edges parameter is omitted or set to 8.
 |
 |

 |

EOLY

 |

The errors only error map delivers errors per pin. With this option, a two bit error code and the address of all those cycles will be returned at which errors have occurred. For more information on the error codes see the DERR option.

Note that this mode requires that the DCRM command has been set to 1,PFC.

 |
 |

 |

ERRM

 |

The error map option reads the Error Map and provides a single one-bit result per test system cycle for all pins in the pinlist. The result is:

0: Pass

1: Fail

 |
 |

 |

OVEM

 |

This option reads the Overview Error Map and provides a single result according to the compression factor set with DCRM. The returned pass/fail result is of the same type as for the ERRM option (one bit pass/fail). This option is only allowed if if the over view Error Map was set to FCM with DCRM in the last executed test.

 |
 |

 |

LMAP

 |

This option returns the results for the specified range of label calls within a burst. It is only allowed if the overview Error Map was set to LMAP with DCRM in the last executed test.

 Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 |

 |

RECD

 |

The receive data option reads the Error Map and provides per pin pass/fail result per test cycle for all pins in the pinlist. The returned pass/fail information is of the same type as for the ERRM option (one bit pass/fail).

 |
 |

start_unit

 |

For most values of map_id, this parameter defines the first recorded cycle that is to be reported. Note that depending on the selected map_id, the returned start cycle can be an earlier cycle than the requested start cycle.

If map_id is set to LMAP, then start_unit specifies the first label call of a burst that is to be reported. For this map_id option, only positive numbers are allowed.

 |
 |

no_of_units

 |

For most values of map_id, this parameter defines the number of cycles to be reported. The range for this parameter depends on the compression factor if OVEM has been selected. The specified number of cycles is adjusted to the existing cycles. If no existing cycle is included in the specified range, an error message is issued. It is recommended that you first determine the available cycle range with the VALD? query.

Note that depending on the selected map_id, the returned number of cycles can be greater than the requested number.

If map_id is set to LMAP, then no_of_units specifies the number of label calls within a burst that are to be reported.

 |
 |

map_mode

 |

Specifies how detailed the displayed error code is to be in case of failure. Note that the parameter is ignored for all values of map_id except EDGE. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

PF

 |

A one bit Pass/Fail result will be returned. This value is only allowed if DCRM has been set to 8,PF.

 |
 |

 |

F160

 |

This is equivalent to PF for the map_id value EDGE.

 |
 |

edges

 |

Specifies the number of edges for the EDGE option of the map_id parameter.

 |
 |

MUX

 |

If this flag is set, and one of the specified (Pin Scale) pins is multiplexed to an HXA pin, then the reply for this pin will combine the results of all Pin Scale pins that are multiplexed to the respective HXA pin.

In particular, if information on the edge level is requested, then the edges of all multiplexed Pin Scale pins will be returned interleaved as follows:

r1 of PS pin 1, ..., r1 of PS pin n, r2 of PS pin 1, ..., r2 of PS pin n, ..., r8 of PS pin 1, ..., r8 of PS pin n

Here, n is 2 or 4, and the order of the PS pins is that defined in the BOARDCONF section of the model file.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO pin types. They must also all belong to the same port of the current start label.

If the MUX flag is set, then each pin in the pin list should represent a different HXA pin, and all HXA pins should have the same multiplexing factor.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that is returned. The general format is:

#Nn1n2...nNdata_stream

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The structure of the data stream depends on the selected map_id value.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › ERMP  -  ERror MaP）

```
> ERMP? OVEM, 0, 16, F160,(Q0)
< ERMP OVEM,0,16,F160,(Q0),#9000000001 0x80
```

This example requests Overview Error Map data for the output pin Q0 in the Start Analysis mode between vectors 0 and 15.

```
> $ERMP? EDGE,0,7,F160,3,(Q0,Q7)
< ERMP EDGE,0,7,F160,3,(Q0,Q7),
  1100 0000  0000 0000  0010 0000  1100 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000 0000 0000
```

This example uses the "$" prefix, by which the binary data stream is represented bitwise by an ASCII "1" or "0" (see `Storing and Retrieving Binary Data`（raw: `02.06.01.03.04_Storing_and_Retrieving_Binary_Data.md`）). The call requests edge specific data for the output pins Q0, Q7. The first three receive edges of each of the first 7 cycles are queried. One byte is returned for every cycle. The result is that there are errors at edges 1 and 2 in cycle 0 and cycle 3, and an error at edge 3 in cycle 2. The other cycles contain no errors at the first three edges.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

```
FFCI? {(no_ffcyc)} [,(port)]
```

returns:

```
FFCI {(no_ffcyc)}, {no_pins}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

| no_ffcyc  | Number of first failed cycles to be reported. |
 | port  | Specifies the port for the pins for which information is to be returned. If you omit this parameter information will be returned for the default port @ to which all configured pins belong. |
 | no_pins  | The number of O and IO pins. |
 | #spec(data) |

Prefix and pin error data in binary format:

- The prefix is defined as follows:

  - The number sign # marks the start of the data block.
  - One digit follows, indicating how many digits make up the following data length specifier.
  - A number of digits indicating the length (in bytes) of the data to follow.

- Binary data are available per reported cycle. The data for each cycle consists of two parts, the number of the failing cycle and the pin data, which indicates the failing pins of that cycle:

  - Cycle number:

The length of the cycle number is always 8 bytes.

  - Pin data:

The pin data consists of one byte per eight pins that belong to the specified port:

    - Each pin is represented by one bit.
    - An error on a particular pin is denoted by a 1, an error free pin by a 0.
    - Bits of the pin data are filled starting from the left (MSB) side.
    - If the number of configured channels of the specified port is not divisible by 8, the last byte of pin data contains unused bits on the right (LSB) side.

Mapping of the bits in the pin data block to the individual pins:

- The I / IO pins are sorted based on their pogo number defined for the first site.
- The sorted pins are mapped starting on the left (MSB) side of the first byte of the pin data block.
- The information how the pins are mapped can be read by command `FFPM? (First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping)`（raw: `02.06.11.02.24_FFPM___First_Failing_cycle_information_Pin_Mapping.md`）.
 |

### Example 1: Firmware view（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

```
$FFCI? 2
FFCI 2,7,#218
  00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000011
  01100000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  00010000 00010000
```

This example for `Firmware view`（raw: `../../01_Getting_started/01.01_SmarTest_Work_Center/01.01.08.08_Firmware_view.md`） queries the first two cycles where failures have occurred on an output pin of the default port, that is, on any configured output pin. Note: For the query, you must use the prefix $ so that the binary data are represented by ASCII 1 or 0.

The answer is to be interpreted as follows:

- `FFCI 2,7` means that 2 cycles are reported and 7 output pins are configured. Since this entails that one byte is sufficient for the pin data, the binary data needs only one byte for the pin data consists of 2 * 9 bytes.
- `#218` defines the size of the following binary data: 2 digits for the length specifier followed by the length specifier itself that indicates a length of 18 for the binary data.
- The Firmware view displays the cycle numbers and pin data as groups of eight bytes that must be evaluated as follows:

  - Failed cycle # 3:

    - The cycle number 3 is defined by the first eight address bytes `0000000` 鈥? `00000011`.
    - The 9th byte `01100000` shows failures on the 2nd and 3rd pin: Value 0 of the MSB on the left represents the passing 1st pin.

  - Failed cycle # 16:

    - The next eight bytes 10 鈥?17 (`00000000` 鈥? `00010000`) define the cycle number 16.
    - The last byte 18 (`00010000`) shows that the fourth pin failed.

For the assignment from bits of the pin data bytes to the configured pins, refer to `#spec(data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__r_specData`）, the `following example`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__d_Example_2`） and to firmware command `FFPM? (First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping)`（raw: `02.06.11.02.24_FFPM___First_Failing_cycle_information_Pin_Mapping.md`）.

The FFCI? command can also be executed using API `FW_TASK`（raw: `../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.77_FW_TASK.md`）. You must use the syntax `FWTASK_STATUS FW_TASK(const STRING& command, FW_ResultData & resultdata);` to retrieve the binary data.

### Example 2: Sort order of pins（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFCI  -  First Failed Cycle Information）

The pogo numbers of the following example setup are assigned in descending order to emphasize that the order of the pogo numbers and not the order of the definition by `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） matters.

```
DFPN 11105,"",(pinA)
DFPN 11104,"",(pinB)
DFPN 11103,"",(pinC)
DFPN 11102,"",(pinD)
DFPN 11101,"",(pinE)
CONF IO,F160,(pinA)
CONF I,F160,(pinB,pinC)
CONF O,F160,(pinD,pinE)
```

The FFCI? command will sort I / IO pins based on their pogo number defined for the first site resulting in the pin list pinE, pinD, pinA. The two pins pinB and pinC have no output capability and, therefore, will not be included in the FFCI? answer.

Assuming a test has been executed where pinA passes, but pinD and pinE fail for every cycle, the FFCI? answer for the first two failing cycles now would look like this:

```
FFCI? 2
FFCI 2,3,#218
  00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  11000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  00000001 11000000
```

 The binary data of the answer is to be interpreted as follows:

- Byte 1 鈥?8: Address of the first cycle (`00000000` 鈥? `00000000` = 0)
- Byte 9: Pin data `11000000`
- Byte 10 鈥?17: Address of the second cycle (`00000000` 鈥? `00000001` = 1)
- Byte 18: Pin data `11000000`

Byte 9 and 18 show that the first two pins on the left side (MSB) are failing. According to the sorting scheme that is defined in the FFCI parameter description for `#spec(data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__r_specData`）, the failed pins are pinE (Channel 11101 and pinD (Channel 11102).

The `FFPM?`（raw: `02.06.11.02.24_FFPM___First_Failing_cycle_information_Pin_Mapping.md`） firmware command will return `FFPM 3,(pinE,pinD,pinA)` as pinE, pinD and pinA are configured for the I / IO mode. The pin list is sorted by the pogo number defined for the first site.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFPM   First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping）

```
FFPM? [port]
```

returns:

```
FFPM {no_pins}, {Pinlist}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFPM   First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping）

| port  | Specifies the port for the pins for which information is to be returned. If you omit this parameter information will be returned for the default port @ to which all configured pins belong. |
 | no_pins  | The number of pins, which belong to the specified port. |
 | PinList |

List of pin names, corresponding to the order in the `FFCI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md`） pin result block (from MSB of first byte to LSB in the last byte).

For more information, refer to the FFCI parameter description for `#spec(data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__r_specData`）.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FFPM   First Failing cycle information Pin Mapping）

The pogo numbers of the following example setup are assigned in descending order to emphasize that the order of the pogo numbers and not the order of the definition by `DFPN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） matters.

```
DFPN 11105,"",(pinA)
DFPN 11104,"",(pinB)
DFPN 11103,"",(pinC)
DFPN 11102,"",(pinD)
DFPN 11101,"",(pinE)
CONF IO,F160,(pinA)
CONF I,F160,(pinB,pinC)
CONF O,F160,(pinD,pinE)
```

The FFCI? command will sort I / IO pins based on their pogo number defined for the first site resulting in the pin list pinE, pinD, pinA. The two pins pinB and pinC have no output capability and, therefore, will not be included in the FFCI? answer.

Assuming a test has been executed where pinA passes, but pinD and pinE fail for every cycle, the FFCI? answer for the first two failing cycles now would look like this:

```
FFCI? 2
FFCI 2,3,#218
  00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  11000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
  00000001 11000000
```

 The binary data of the answer is to be interpreted as follows:

- Byte 1 鈥?8: Address of the first cycle (`00000000` 鈥? `00000000` = 0)
- Byte 9: Pin data `11000000`
- Byte 10 鈥?17: Address of the second cycle (`00000000` 鈥? `00000001` = 1)
- Byte 18: Pin data `11000000`

Byte 9 and 18 show that the first two pins on the left side (MSB) are failing. According to the sorting scheme that is defined in the FFCI parameter description for `#spec(data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.122_FFCI__-__First_Failed_Cycle_Information.md#_98603__r_specData`）, the failed pins are pinE (Channel 11101 and pinD (Channel 11102).

For the configuration defined above, the `FFPM?` command will return the following data:

```
FFPM 3,(pinE,pinD,pinA)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

```
FTST? ["exec_context"]
```

returns:

```
FTST {result_flag}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

| exec_context  | An execution context. For more information on execution contexts see `Using execution contexts`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md`）. |
 | result_flag  | This is returned by the system when the functional test has finished. It can be:

 |   | P  | is returned if the functional test passes. |
 |   | F  | is returned if the functional test fails.  | |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › FTST  -  Functional TeST）

```
FTST?
```

returns:

```
FTST P
```

This example returns a pass result for the functional test.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETC  -  GET Cycles）

```
GETC? {(vector_no)}
```

returns:

```
GETC {(cycle_no)}
```

Parameters
 |

vector_no

 |

The vector number for which you want to obtain the matching cycle number. vector_no must be a positive integer that does not exceed the maximum vector address allowed by the system.

 |
 |

cycle_no

 |

The number of the cycle that results when the vector at vector_no is executed. The cycle numbers do not always linearly follow the vector numbers. The relationship between the two depends on the sequencer program. The system returns a cycle_no in the range of 0 to 2^48.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETC  -  GET Cycles）

```
> SQPG? ALL,(@)
< SQPG 0,STVA,0,,,(@)
< SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(@)
< SQPG 2,GENV,103,,,(@)
< SQPG 3,GENV,7,,,(@)
< SQPG 4,MACT,256,,,(@)
< SQPG 5,GENV,1,,,(@)
< SQPG 6,MRPT,1,,,(@)
< SQPG 7,RPTV,1544,100,,(@)
< SQPG 8,GENV,1,,,(@)
< SQPG 9,STOP,,,,(@)
> GETC? 112
< GETC 104
> GETC? 1656
< GETC 154504
```

In this example, the cycle numbers are calculated from the expected values. Vector 112 is the first vector after the match loop. The last 6 vectors before the match loop are not recorded in the Error Map, because the sequencers consider them to be part of the match loop (see `Counted match loops`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01_Counted_match_loops.md`）). The two match loop vectors proper are also not recorded in the Error Map. Since no other loop has occurred before vector 112, the cycle number corresponding to vector 112 is calculated as 112 - 8 = 104.

The cycle number of vector 1656, the last vector of the label, is calculated as 104 + 100 * 1544 = 154504.

The calculation is more complicated if it is based on the received data, because the last match loop cycles may be recorded in the Error Map (see again `Counted match loops`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01_Counted_match_loops.md`）).

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETS  -  GET Sets）

```
GETS? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
GETS {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, {level_set}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

start_cycle

 |

The start cycle is an integer that defines the first cycle to be reported. The start cycle is in the range 0 to 2^48 when the sequencer runs in the Start Analysis mode, or -2^48 to -1 when the sequencer runs in the Stop Analysis mode. If a positive number is entered, cycles are counted from 0 upwards. If a negative value is entered, the cycles are counted from the end of the test at -1. The start cycle returned by the system may be different from the start cycle entered for the query.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

In the command, this parameter defines the number of cycles to be reported. The integer must be in the range 0 to 2147483648.

In the reply, the parameter specifies the number of cycles that are generated with the timing and levels sets specified by the timing_set and level_set parameters. 0 is returned if a CLEV and a CTIM instruction follow each other immediately.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to return the sequencer instructions for all pins.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

level_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the level set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

level_set_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100000 *`equation_set_no `+ 1000 * `specset_no `+ `level_set_no

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETS  -  GET Sets）

```
GETS? 0,2000,(Q0)
```

This example requests the timing and level set information for the first 2000 test cycles of pin `Q0`. The response may be as follows:

```
GETS 0,160,2,1,(Q0)
GETS 160,704,1,1,(Q0)
GETS 864,1136,2,1,(Q0)
```

The first 160 cycles were generated with timing set 2 and level set 1, the next 704 cycles with timing set 1 and level set 1, and the last 1136 cycles with timing set 2 and level set 1 again.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETV  -  GET Vectors）

```
GETV? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
GETV {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {start_vector}, {no_of_vectors}, {seq_status}, {"label"|"scan_template"}, [instance], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETV  -  GET Vectors）

|

start_cycle

 |

An integer that defines the first cycle to be reported. It is in the range 0 to 2^48 when the sequencer runs in the Start Analysis mode, or -2^48 to -1 when the sequencer runs in the Stop Analysis mode. If a positive number is entered, cycles are counted from 0 upwards. If a negative value is entered, the cycles are counted from the end of the test at -1.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

Defines the number of cycles to be reported. The integer must be in the range 0 to 2147483648 (2^31).

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |
 |

start_vector

 |

Returns the logical number of the start vector for the instruction specified by the seq_status parameter within the test specified by the label parameter.

The logical vector number counts the active vectors within one label, starting from 0. If the vectors generated by the instruction are break vectors, then -1 is returned.

 |
 |

no_of_vectors

 |

Returns the vector length of the instruction specified by the seq_status parameter. If the vectors generated in the requested range are break vectors, then the parameter returns -1.

 |
 |

seq_status

 |

Returns the current sequencer status. The status is expressed on most occasions in the form of the sequencer instruction that was used to generate a segment of the vectors in the requested cycle range. Otherwise it is expressed in terms of the current sequencer activity. Note that seq_status is not the same as the sequencer state determined by `SQST, SQST? - (SeQuencer STate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.241_SQST__SQST__-__SeQuencer_STate.md`）. Sequencer instructions are parameters to `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）. For additional information on sequencer programming see also `Vector Setup Commands`（raw: `02.06.07_Vector_Setup_Commands.md`）.

 |
 |

 |

The seq_status parameter is required for the reconstruction of received data. Some of the values it returns signify that vectors are being generated, others inform of sequencer status changes, which cause some or no break vectors to be generated.

 |
 |

 |

GENV

 |

This is returned if GENV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range. The number of vectors generated equals the no_of_vectors.

 |
 |

 |

SRCV

 |

This is returned if SRCV is the sequencer instruction that generates vectors in the reported cycle range.

For "non-source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the parallel vectors exactly the same way as RPTV. That means "no_of_vectors" parallel vectors are repeated for a repeating count (equal to no_of_cycles divided by no_of_vectors) to generate "no_of_cycles" cycles on the test system.

For "source pin" the reported cycle range is generated by the vectors stored in the source memory. It means "no_of_cycles" vectors are generated from the source memory to produce "no_of_cycles" cycle on the test system, and the information of "no_of_vectors" has no meaning to "source pin".

 |
 |

 |

RPTV

 |

This is returned if RPTV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range. In order to obtain the number of repetitions divide no_of_cycles by no_of_vectors.

You can stop a repeat loop by hitting BREAK in the user interface. The seq_status may then still be RPTV because the BREAK occurs asynchronously to the execution of the loop.

 |
 |

 |

JPPS

 |

This is returned if the parallel vectors for the reported cycles were generated by a per-pin subroutine.

 |
 |

 |

CTIM

 |

This is returned if a change timing instruction has been issued in the queried cycle range. Each timing change generates break vectors.

The actual number of break cycles depends on the test system period and will not be shown in the cycle reconstruction.

Between 0 to 7 break cycles will be recorded during a CTIM instruction, the exact number depends on the number of vectors loaded previously. For instance, if the previous number of cycles was a multiple of 8, then no break vectors are issued during the reload.

 |
 |

 |

CLEV

 |

The CLEV (change levels) parameter indicates that unrecorded break cycles, due to a change of level set, exist in the specified cycle range.

 |
 |

 |

BRK

 |

This is returned if break cycles are being generated during the reported cycle range - for example, if a timed match loop is in progress. Between 0 and 7 break cycles will be recorded.

Additionally, the following sequencer instructions also generate break vectors:

 |

sequencer instruction

 |

reported as

 |
 |

CTIM

 |

CTIM

 |
 |

CLEV

 |

CLEV

 |
 |

WTER

 |

BRK

 |
 |

FLQU

 |

BRK

 |
 |

MEAS

 |

BRK

 |
 |

STOP

 |

BRK

 |

 |
 |

 |

MTCH

 |

This is always returned if the test contains a counted match loop. The specified vectors are those that are associated with the MRPT instruction. The specified number of cycles is greater than 0 if the test has been executed online, and the last cycle that was generated from these vectors is not the last cycle of a block. For details see `Adjusting the junctions between match loop and surrounding label`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01.01_Adjusting_the_junctions_between_match_loop_and_surrounding_label.md`）.

MTCH is also returned for a timed match loop, but only if the test has been executed online, and the number of cycles will always be 0.

 |
 |

label

 |

This parameter returns the label to which the instruction belongs.

 |
 |

instance

 |

This parameter is blank for all sequencer instructions.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETV  -  GET Vectors）

```
> GETV? 0,50,(S0_1)
< GETV 0,9,0,9,GENV,"test_1",,(S0_1)
< GETV 9,30,9,6,RPTV,"test_1",,(S0_1)
< GETV 39,1,-1,-1,BRK,"test_1",,(S0_1)
```

The vectors for cycles 9 through 38 were generated by an RPTV instruction that generated 6 waveforms 5 times.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETX  -  GET eXtended vector information）

```
GETX? [type], [label], [vector], [cycle], [index], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
GETX {type}, {label}, {vector}, {cycle}, [index], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETX  -  GET eXtended vector information）

|

type

 |

The label type. You can supply one of the following options:

 |
 |

MAIN

 |

The MAIN program.

 |
 |

SJMP

 |

A JuMP Subroutine.

 |
 |

SVEC

 |

A VECtor Subroutine.

 |
 |

BRST

 |

BuRST mode.

 |
 |

MPBU

 |

Multi-Port BUrst mode

 |
 |

ALL

 |

reads the configurations for all label types (query only).

 |
 |

label

 |

The label name. It references the label for which you require vector information. Enter a string enclosed in double quotes. The string can have a length of between 1 and 128 alpha-numeric characters.

 |
 |

vector

 |

The logical number of a vector within the label specified by label. The logical vector number counts the active vectors within one label, starting from 0.

 |
 |

cycle

 |

A cycle number. If this parameter is specified, the label and vector parameters are ignored.

 |
 |

index

 |

This parameter is reserved for future use. In this implementation it must be left blank!

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to obtain data for all pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › GETX  -  GET eXtended vector information）

```
> GETX? ,,,4,,(CP)
< GETX MAIN,"multi",4,4,,(CP)
```

This example asks for vector data at cycle 4 on pin CP. The system replies that cycle 4 was generated by vector 4 in a main label called multi.

Note that this type of query where only a cycle number is supplied is similar to the GETV? query requesting information on just a single cycle - see `GETV? - (GET Vectors)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.135_GETV__-__GET_Vectors.md`）.

```
> GETX? MAIN,"multi",10,,,(CP)
< GETX MAIN,"multi",10,10,,(CP)
```

This example requests the number of the cycle that was generated by vector 10 in the main label called multi. The system replies with cycle 10.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

```
PASS? {(pin_list)}
```

or

```
PASS? {(port_list)}
```

returns:

```
PASS {res_flag}, {(pin_list)}
```

or

```
PASS {res_flag}, {(port)}
```

respectively.

Note port_list mode returns the pass or fail result per port. This is different than the case when using pin_list mode.

To report the last test result per individual pin , the PPIN command is used.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

```
PASS?PPIN,{(pins)}
```

returns

```
PASS PPIN,{res_flag}, {(pin}
```

Note The result (pass or fail) is returned for each pin specified in pins individually.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

|

pin_list

 |

The last test result is provided for the pins specified in pin_list. If more than one pin list is included, the names must be separated by a comma.

Normally, only O or IO pins in the list are taken into account; I pins are ignored. However, if any sequencer program of the setup contains a`MEAS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.160_MEAS_-__execute_a_MEASurement_set.md`） instruction (see the `SQPG`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`） command), and the measurement set that is executed by this instruction is defined for an I pin, then the measurement result for this pin will be included in the reply of PASS? if the I pin is specified in pin_list.

 |
 |

port_list

 |

The last test result is provided for the pins of a port specified in port_list. If more than one port is included, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |
 |

Pins

 |

The last test result is provided per each pin specified in pins individually. If more than one pin is included , the names must be separated by a comma.

 |
 |

res_flag

 |

F

 |

If this result is returned, at least one pin in pin_list or port failed the last test. In the case of per pin query (using PPIN command), a fail is returned if the individual pin specified in pins failed the last test.

 |
 |

P

 |

If this result is returned, all pins in pin_list or port passed the last test. In the case of per pin query (using PPIN command) , a pass is returned if the individual pin specified in pins passed the last test.

 |

Application

Test results, see `Test Result Commands`（raw: `02.06.11_Test_Result_Commands.md`） and `Multi-Port Testing`（raw: `../../03_Use_cases_and_application_papers/03.03_How_to_use_Multiport_for_specific_Applications/03.03.01.02_General_Overview_of_Multi-Port_Testing__Cover.md`）.

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › PASS  -  PASS or fail result）

After a functional test has been performed, sending PASS? returns one result for the whole test.

```
PASS? (@)
```

returns:

```
PASS P, (@)
```

or

```
PASS F, (@)
```

for a passed or a failed test result respectively.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

|

mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

ACQF

 |

ACQuire Failure mode. Only failed cycles are recorded, starting after analyze_delay cycles. If analyze_delay is not a multiple of 8, recording starts after the nearest smaller multiple of 8. In this mode the Error Map is called the Acquire Failure Map.

As the test proceeds the Acquire Failure Map is filled with failure data until the test stops or the map becomes completely full, whichever occurs first. If the map stops recording before the test has finished, the sequencer, which is in standard mode, continues executing the test until the end.

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of ACQF is reproduced by:

DCGM FAIL,STRT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

ACFF

 |

This mode is functionally identical to ACQF. It is obsolete and should not be used in new applications.

 |
 |

EL

 |

EndLess. The sequencer repeats the complete test, including primaries and multiport synchronization, in an endless loop and can only be stopped by Break.

The analyze_delay parameter is ignored. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented mode.

This mode is used for oscilloscope tests. The Error Map functions as a rolling buffer. After stopping the sequencer, the Error Map shows the last "buffer-full" of recorded cycles.

 |
 |

ELPT

 |

EndLess PaTtern. The sequencer repeats only the user program. This avoids critical holds during measurement.

In case of multiport testing, ports may run with different frequencies. Using the ELPT mode in this case, can lead to the situation, that for loop counts >1 the synchronization is no longer executed.

 |
 |

EMPS

 |

Error Map PoSitioning. The Error Map is in cycle oriented mode, the sequencer in default mode. The analyze_delay parameter specifies the end of the recorded area. If it is not a multiple of 8, the last cycle to be displayed is the largest multiple of 8 that is smaller than analyze_delay. The first cycle to be displayed is determined by the size of the Error Map (8k cycles).

This mode is only supported for compatibility reasons. Instead, you should use DCGM and DCRP to configure the Error Map. The effect of EMPS is reproduced by:

DCGM ALL,HALT,NONE

DCRP EMAP,<error_map_pos>,<ref_port>

 |
 |

SE

 |

Stop on Error. The sequencer runs from the beginning of the test and stops when an error is encountered. If no errors occur, the sequencer runs to the end of the test and stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. The analyze_delay parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

SEEL

 |

Stop on Error and EndLess. The sequencer repeats the test in an endless loop, unless an error is encountered, whereupon it stops. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode. This mode is used to locate sporadic failures.

 |
 |

STSQ

 |

STop SeQuencer. Stops the sequencer after analyze_delay cycles. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM. See also the query `GETC? - (GET Cycles)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.131_GETC__-__GET_Cycles.md`） for the analyze_delay count.

 |
 |

STRD

 |

In the query reply, this mode is displayed if the current combination of recording mode, as set with DCGM, and interpretation of the Error Map position, as set with DCRP, is different from all the other SQGB modes. For example, the Error Map can be in cycle oriented recording mode, and analyze_delay be interpreted as a start value.

In the command, this option leaves it to SmarTest to select the appropriate recording mode (cycle oriented or acquire failure), unless the recording mode has been explicitly set with DCGM.

 |
 |

STSV

 |

STop Sequencer on Vector. Stops the sequencer at the logical vector number specified in the analyze_delay parameter before executing the vector. The Error Map is set to cycle oriented recording mode, but this can be changed with DCGM.

Note that the STSV option cannot be used if no start label has been defined with SQSL, or if the start label is a burst or multi-port burst label.

 |
 |

analyze_delay

 |

Sets the analyze delay. This parameter is mandatory for the STSQ and STSV modes. Its interpretation depends on the selected mode parameter. The number must be between 1 (0 for ACQF) and 281,474,976,710,655 = 2^48 - 1 (2^48 - 2 for ACQF).

If the mode parameter is set to STSV, three cases must be distinguished:

- If analyze_delay is an existing logical vector number of the actual start label, the sequencer will be stopped at this logical vector before executing the vector.
- If analyze_delay specifies the total number of logical vectors (= greatest logical vector number of the test + 1) the sequencer stops at the last valid vector.
- If analyze_delay is greater than the total number of logical vectors, an error message is issued.
 |
 |

ref_port

 |

This parameter accepts a single port. It must be specified in the following situation:

- The selected mode requires an analyze delay (but is different from STSV), and
- the start label is a multi-port burst.

It specifies the port which is used for counting the cycles specified with the analyze_delay parameter. When this reference port has completed the specified number of cycles, the sequencers will be stopped, or cycle recording started or stopped, for all ports. Note that the reference port must belong to the current start label (as defined by SQSL).

 |
 |

port_list

 |

If the current mode requires an analyze delay, you can specify a port list in the query. The reply will give the calculated analyze delays for those ports that are not used as the reference port. These delays are derived from the analyze delay of the reference port and the ratio between the period lengths of the reference port and the other port in the primary timing setup. If you specify @@, SQGB will return the settings for all ports of the current start label.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › SQGB  SQGB  -  SeQuencer GloBal）

```
> PCLK? "mu_burst",1,(@@)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,20,(P1)
< PCLK "mu_burst",1,10,(P2)
> SPRM "mu_burst",1,,
> SQSL "mu_burst"
> SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
> SQGB? (@@)
< SQGB STSQ,15,(P1)
< SQGB STSQ,30,(P2)
```

This example configures the sequencers to stop when port P2 has completed 30 cycles. Port P1, whose period length is twice the period length of P2, will be stopped after 15 cycles. Note that P1 and P2 must belong to the same sequencing group.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › SQIB  SQIB  -  SeQuencer Interrupt Behavior）

|

BANDWIDTH

 |

This refers to the behavior when the detailed error map is located in the external memory, and result recording was aborted due to a bandwidth overflow of the memory.

 |
 |

TIMEOUT

 |

This refers to the behavior in case of a sequencer timeout.

 |
 |

ERIM

 |

SmarTest issues an error message immediately after completion of the test. In case of a recording abort, this message reports the channels, pins, and sites of all channel groups on which recording was aborted.

In case of a sequencer timeout, a list of those channels is returned on which the timeout occurred.

 |
 |

FLIM

 |

This option is only allowed with TIMEOUT.

SmarTest reports the test as failed, that is, FTST? returns F. This is the default for TIMEOUT.

 |
 |

ERRQ

 |

This option is only allowed with BANDWIDTH.

SmarTest does not issue an error message immediately after completion of the test, but only if a channel which is involved in a recording abort is queried for result data. In this case again, the channels, pins, and sites of all channel groups on which recording was aborted will be reported. This is the default for BANDWIDTH.

 |
 |

FLRQ

 |

This option is only allowed with BANDWIDTH.

SmarTest does not issue any error message. If a channel of a group on which recording was aborted is queried for result data, all its cycles will be reported as failing.

This option can be used in a production environment if the result data is recorded in acquire failure mode, since if any data is recorded with this recording mode, the device must in fact have failed. Actually, recording will only be aborted in case of a massive fail on several pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › SQIB  SQIB  -  SeQuencer Interrupt Behavior）

```
SQIB BANDWIDTH FLrQ
```

This example suppresses all error messages in case of a recording abort.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VALD  -  VALid Data）

```
VALD? {map_id}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VALD {map_state}, {map_id}, {start}, {number}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VALD  -  VALid Data）

|

map_id

   | Determines the type of Error Map for which data is to be read out: |
 |

ERRM

 |

The error map option reads the error map.

 |
 |

OVEM

 |

The overview error map option reads the overview error map in FCM mode (defined by DCRM). If the Overview Error Map was in LMAP mode for the last executed test, an error message will be issued.

 |
 |

LMAP

 |

The label map option reads the overview error map in LMAP mode (defined by DCRM). If the overview error map was in FCM mode for the last executed test, an error message will be issued if LMAP is selected.

 Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 |

RECD

 |

The receive data option reads the error map (compatibility with the `ERMP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.114_ERMP__-__ERror_MaP.md`） query). Equivalent to ERRM.

 |
 |

DERR

 |

The per pin detailed error map option reads the detailed error map. Equivalent to ERRM.

 |
 |

EOLY

 |

The errors only map option reads the per pin errors only in the error map. Equivalent to ERRM.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Error map information will only be returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. All pins in pinlist must be O or IO pin types.

 |
 |

map_state

 |

Returns the current state of the error map. The state can be:

 |
 |

INVL

 |

Invalid is returned if no error map details are available (the setup has been changed, but no functional test has been performed).

 |
 |

INCS

 |

This is returned if the contents of the error map are inconsistent with the current setup.

 |
 |

CONS

 |

This is returned after a functional test has been performed and indicates that the contents of the error map are consistent with the current setup.

 |
 |

start

 |

This is an integer that indicates the first cycle that was recorded, or, for the LMAP option of map_id, the first label call that was recorded. start will be a value between 0 and 2^48.

 |
 |

number

 |

This is an integer that indicates the number of cycles recorded, or for the LMAP option of map_id, the number of label calls recorded. If ERRM, RECD or DERR have been selected, the range for this parameter depends on whether the internal or the external error map is used. For the internal error map, it is 0 to 8191; for the external error map the upper limit can be higher. When EOLY has been selected, the upper limit is 2^48.

For the `Pin Scale 5000 card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.04.02_Pin_Scale_5000_card.md`）, the upper limit is 4096.

In the reply, this parameter indicates the number of cycles (or label calls) which have been read. If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VALD  -  VALid Data）

```
VALD? ERRM, (Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

returns:

```
VALD CONS, ERRM, 0, 1024, (Q0,Q1,Q2,Q3)
```

This example queries the error map and returns data between the cycles of 0 and 1024. The error map data is consistent with the current setup.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VALR  -  VALid Range）

```
VALR? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VALR {map_state}, {no_of_results}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VALR  -  VALid Range）

|

map_state

 |

Returns the current state of the error map. The state can be:

- INVL: Invalid - no error map details are available. (The setup has been changed, but no functional test has been performed.)
- INCS: Inconsistent - the contents of the error map are inconsistent with the current setup.
- CONS: Consistent - a functional test has been performed and the contents of the error map are consistent with the current setup.
 |
 |

no_of_results

 |

Integer indicating the number of results recorded.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

List of DC Scale pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VALR  -  VALid Range）

```
> VALR? (dpsPin)
< VALR CONS,10,(dpsPin)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VCYC  -  Valid CYCle）

```
VCYC? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VCYC {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {seq_status}, {pin_oper_mode}, {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VCYC  -  Valid CYCle）

|

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. The scanning method and the range of values this parameter can take depend on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the label and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the label at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. It is the cycle length from the specified start_cycle to the last cycle resulting from the seq_status specified by a sequencer instruction. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2,147,483,648 (2^31).

 |
 |

seq_status

 |

Returns the sequencer status that was current when the cycle range was generated. The status is expressed on most occasions in the form of the sequencer instruction that was used to generate the vectors in the requested cycle range. Otherwise it is expressed in terms of a sequencer activity. Note that seq_status is not the same as the sequencer state determined by the command `SQST, SQST? - (SeQuencer STate)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.241_SQST__SQST__-__SeQuencer_STate.md`）. Sequencer instructions are parameters to `SQPG, SQPG? - (SeQuencer ProGramming)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.237_SQPG__SQPG__-__SeQuencer_ProGramming.md`）. For additional information on sequencer programming see `Vector Setup Commands`（raw: `02.06.07_Vector_Setup_Commands.md`）.

The seq_status parameter is required for the reconstruction of received data. Some of the values it returns signify that vectors are being generated, others inform of sequencer status changes, which can cause some break vectors to be generated.

 |
 |

 |

GENV

 |

This is returned if GENV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range.

 |
 |

 |

SRCV

 |

This is returned if SRCV is the sequencer instruction that generates vectors in the reported cycle range.

For non-source pins the reported cycle range is generated by the parallel vectors exactly the same way as from RPTV. This means that no_of_vectors parallel vectors are repeated for a repeating count (equal to no_of_cycles divided by no_of_vectors) to generate no_of_cycles cycles on the test system.

For source pins the reported cycle range is generated by the vectors stored in the source memory. This means that no_of_cycles vectors are generated from the source memory to produce no_of_cycles cycles on the test system, and the information of no_of_vectors has no meaning to source pins.

 |
 |

 |

RPTV

 |

This is returned if RPTV is the sequencer instruction that generated the parallel vectors in the reported cycle range.

You can stop a repeat loop by hitting BREAK in the user interface. The seq_status may then still be RPTV because the BREAK occurs asynchronously to the execution of the loop.

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |
 |

 |

JPPS

 |

This is returned if the parallel vectors for the reported cycles were generated by a per-pin subroutine.

 |
 |

 |

CTIM

 |

This is returned if a change timing instruction has been issued in the queried cycle range. Each timing change generates break vectors.

The real number of break cycles depends on the test system period and will not be shown in the cycle reconstruction.

Between 0 to 7 break cycles will be recorded during a CTIM instruction, the exact number depends on the number of vectors loaded.

 |
 |

 |

CLEV

 |

The CLEV (change levels) parameter indicates that unrecorded break cycles, due to a change of level set, exist in the specified cycle range.

 |
 |

 |

BRK

 |

This is returned if break cycles are being generated during the reported cycle range - for example, if a timed match loop is in progress. Between 0 and 7 break cycles will be recorded.

Additionally, the following sequencer instructions also generate break vectors:

 |
 |

 |

 |

sequencer instruction

 |

 reported as

 |
 |

 |

 |

CTIM

 |

CTIM

 |
 |

 |

 |

CLEV

 |

CLEV

 |
 |

 |

 |

WTER

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

 |

FLQU

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

 |

STOP

 |

BRK

 |
 |

 |

MTCH

 |

This is returned if

- the test contains a counted match loop,
- the test has been executed online, and
- the last cycle of the match loop is not the last cycle of a 8-cycle block.

In this case the last match loop cycles belonging to this block (up to 7) are recorded in the Error Map and reported by VCYC?. For details see `Adjusting the junctions between match loop and surrounding label`（raw: `02.06.07.01.08.04.03.01.01_Adjusting_the_junctions_between_match_loop_and_surrounding_label.md`）.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included in the query, the names must be separated with a comma. You can type the character @ to obtain data for all pins.

The response is provided for each pin separately.

 |
 |

pin_oper_mode

 |

Reports the operating mode of each pin in the pin list. This can be:

 |
 |

F160

 |

Specifies Standard operating mode.

 |
 |

F330

 |

Not valid.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Vector data in binary format. The parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the binary data. The data is returned for each pin separately, on a sequencer construct basis (see `Addressing the vector areas`（raw: `02.06.07.01.04_Addressing_the_vector_areas.md`）). The system returns one byte for each cycle and pin. If the requested cycles are break cycles, then no data is returned.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VCYC  -  Valid CYCle）

```
VCYC? 0, 5, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
VCYC 0,5,GENV,F160,(pin1),#9000000005\x0E\x0E\x0E\x0F\x0D\x0A
```

This example returns the physical waveform DC/DC power units in hex notation in the range of 0 to 5 cycles.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VNEC  -  Valid Number of Executed Cycles）

```
VNEC? {site_sel}, {value_format}, {(pin)}
```

Returns:

```
VNEC {site_sel}, {(pin)}, {value_data}
```

Parameters
 | site_sel  | Select sites. It can be a string of 1's and 0's; or "ALL" to specify all sites. The response is a string of 1's and 0's. |
 | value_format |

Specify a data format. It can be ASC or BIN.

SmarTest 7.5.0 supports the ASC mode only.

 |
 | pin  | Specify a pin. Only one pin is supported. It can be any pin that has been configured to I, O, IO, DC, and DPS types. |
 | value_data  | Hold the returned cycle numbers in ASCII format. The ASCII data consists of a list of cycle numbers separated by comma. Each cycle number is for each active and requested site. |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VNEC  -  Valid Number of Executed Cycles）

```
VNEC? ALL, ASC, ("pin1")
```

Returns:

```
VNEC "11",("pin1"),#138,8
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VRCS  -  Valid ReConStruction）

```
VRCS? {reconstr_type}, [reconstr_cond,] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
VRCS [reconstr_cond,] {reconstr_state}, [reconstr_oper,] {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

Parameters
 |

reconstr_type

 |

The reconstruction type determines how test cycles are counted.

 |
 |

STRT

 |

Start analysis. Specifies that cycles are counted from the start of the test.

 |
 |

STOP

 |

Stop analysis. Specifies that cycles are counted from the end of the test.

 |
 |

reconstr_cond

 |

The reconstruction condition defines how VRCS? reacts to ambiguous sequencer instructions, that is, instructions that may generate a varying number of cycles from one test execution to the next. Examples for such instructions are JMPE or multiple counted match loops.

 |
 |

 |

STRD

 |

Reconstruction stops at the first ambiguous instruction. The result may be incomplete, but is reliable.

 |
 |

 |

FULL

 |

Reconstruction continues even if ambiguous instructions are present. The maximum possible number of cycles is assumed for the ambiguous instructions. The result may be complete, but possible not completely reliable.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. pinlist can include pins configured as I, O and IO types.

 |
 |

reconstr_state

 |

This parameter returns the state of the reconstruction.

 |
 |

 |

INVL

 |

If INVL is returned, no valid cycles exist. This occurs if you have hit BREAK before any vectors are generated.

 |
 |

 |

PRED

 |

If PRED is returned, all returned values are predicted (a change to the setup has been made, but a test has not yet been executed).

 |
 |

 |

REAL

 |

If REAL is returned, all values given are values from the last executed test.

 |
 |

reconstr_oper

 |

OKAY

 |

The reconstruction was successful, no problems encountered.

 |
 |

 |

MMRV

 |

Multiple Matchloop Restriction Violation:

The reconstruction stopped at the first match loop because there are multiple match loops in the pattern, and the match loop execution counter, which is needed for the reconstruction, can only hold the count from the last match loop execution.

 |
 |

 |

JMPE

 |

The reconstruction stopped at a jump on error instruction because execution path of the sequencer is unknown (for example, whether the jump was taken or not).

 |
 |

 |

RETC

 |

The reconstruction stopped at a return conditional instruction because execution path of the sequencer is unknown (for example, whether the jump was taken or not).

 Note If you use the LMAP error map mode, `FLBL`（raw: `02.06.02.02.123_FLBL__-__Failing_LaBeLs.md`） ignores the RETC clearing flag for failures. |
 |

 |

ABRT

 |

The pattern was empty or there was an unspecified problem during the reconstruction.

 |
 |

start_cycle

 |

The start cycle is an integer which identifies the first cycle for which results exist.

 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This parameter is an integer which defines the total number of valid cycles.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › VRCS  -  Valid ReConStruction）

```
VRCS? STRT, (@)
```

returns:

```
VRCS? REAL, 0, 437621, (@)
```

This example queries the number of reconstructed cycles, counting the cycles from the start of the test. The system replies that 437,621 cycles, starting from zero have been reconstructed, based on the last performed test.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › WFEX  -  WaveForm EXpected data）

```
WFEX? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
WFEX {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, [err_type], {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. The scanning method and the range of values this parameter can take depend on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode, enter a positive value between 0 and 2^48. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis mode, enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for stop-on-error tests.
 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2^48.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma. You can use the @ character to read the error data for all pins.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is always of the type NOER since this query only reports expected data.

 |
 |

NOER

 |

Error information is not available. The reported range lies outside the range covered by the Error Map.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. For each cycle of the reported cycle range 6 bytes are returned. Each byte of reconstructed data is to be decoded as follows:

 |
 |

bit 7: Error flag.

 |
 |

0

 |

No error on receive edge, or a drive / unused edge

 |
 |

1

 |

Cannot occur since only expected data are reported.

 |
 |

bits 6, 5: Data parameter

 |
 |

00

 |

Fixed value

 |
 |

10

 |

Data parameter 1

 |
 |

11

 |

Data parameter 2

 |
 |

bit 4: Edge direction

 |
 |

0

 |

Drive / tri-state edge

 |
 |

1

 |

Receive edge

 |
 |

bits 3, 2, 1, 0: Edge action

 |
 |

If bit 4 is a 0, then drive / tri-state data:

 |
 |

bits 3, 2: Tri-state data

 |
 |

10

 |

Tri-state off

 |
 |

11

 |

Tri-state on

 |
 |

00

 |

Not used

 |
 |

bits 1, 0: Drive data

 |
 |

10

 |

Drive 0

 |
 |

11

 |

Drive 1

 |
 |

00

 |

Not used

 |
 |

If bit 4 is a 1, then expected data:

 |
 |

bit 3: Compare type

 |
 |

0

 |

Edge compare

 |
 |

1

 |

Window compare

 |
 |

bits 2, 1, 0: Compare method

 |
 |

010

 |

Compare to 0

 |
 |

011

 |

Compare to 1

 |
 |

001

 |

Compare to intermediate

 |
 |

100

 |

Compare to mask

 |
 |

101

 |

Compare to unstable

 |
 |

000

 |

Not used

 |
 |

111

 |

Window close

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › WFEX  -  WaveForm EXpected data）

```
WFEX? 0, 1, (pin1)
```

returns:

