WFEX 0,1,3,NOER,(pin1),#9000000006\x0B\x0A\x1A\x1F\x00\x00\x0A
```

This example returns edge action drive and expected data (in binary notation) for one cycle. To decode the data, convert it into binary notation and use the lists above.

The data in binary format is:

```
0000 1011  0000 1010  0001 1010
0001 1111  0000 0000  0000 0000
```

The edge actions are RZ on the drive edges 1 and 2 and a window compare to 0 on the receive edges 3 and 4. Edges 5 and 6 are unused.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › WFRE  -  WaveForm REceived data）

```
WFRE? {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
WFRE {start_cycle}, {no_of_cycles}, {timing_set}, [err_type], {(pinlist)}, {#spec(data)}
```

Parameters
 |

start_cycle

 |

This is an integer that defines the first cycle for which information is to be returned. The scanning method and the range of values this parameter can take depend on the analysis mode:

- In the Start Analysis mode, enter a positive value between 0 and 248. The system responds by counting cycles forwards from the first cycle of the test and returns a positive number. The Start Analysis mode is the default setting.
- In the Stop Analysis mode, enter a negative number between -2^48 and -1. The system responds by counting cycles backwards relative to the end of the test at -1 cycle and returns a negative number. This mode is used by the system for Stop-on-Error tests.
 |
 |

no_of_cycles

 |

This is an integer that defines the number of cycles for which information is to be returned. The range for this parameter is 0 to 2^48.

If a 0 is returned, no data is available for the given range.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

This parameter is an integer that represents the timing set used in the given cycle range.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Information is only returned for the pins specified in pinlist. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma. You can use the @ character to read the error data for all pins.

 |
 |

err_type

 |

This parameter is optional and specifies what type of error information is available. The system returns a status only for O or IO pins:

 |
 |

ERON

 |

Error information is available. The cycle range where error information is available is reported by the query `VALD? - (VALid Data)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.316_VALD__-__VALid_Data.md`）.

 |
 |

NOER

 |

Error information is not available. The reported range lies outside the range covered by the Error Map.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

Edge action data in binary format. This parameter reports the length of data (in bytes) being transferred, followed by the reconstructed data. The data is returned for each pin separately. For each cycle of the reported cycle range 6 bytes are returned. Each of these bytes has to be decoded as follows:

 |
 |

bit 7: Error flag.

 |
 |

0

 |

No error on receive edge, or a drive or unused edge

 |
 |

1

 |

Error on receive edge. (The system returns this only if err_type is ERON). In case of a failing window compare, both the window open edge and the window close edge are marked.

 |
 |

bits 6, 5: Data parameter

 |
 |

00

 |

Fixed value

 |
 |

10

 |

Data parameter 1

 |
 |

11

 |

Data parameter 2

 |
 |

bit 4: Edge direction

 |
 |

0

 |

Drive / tri-state edge

 |
 |

1

 |

Receive edge

 |
 |

bits 3, 2, 1, 0: Edge action

 |
 |

If bit 4 is a 0, then drive / tri-state data:

 |
 |

bits 3, 2: Tri-state data

 |
 |

10

 |

Tri-state off

 |
 |

11

 |

Tri-state on

 |
 |

00

 |

Not used

 |
 |

bits 1, 0: Drive data

 |
 |

10

 |

Drive 0

 |
 |

11

 |

Drive 1

 |
 |

00

 |

Not used

 |
 |

If bit 4 is a 1, then receive data:

 |
 |

bit 3: Compare type

 |
 |

0

 |

Edge compare

 |
 |

1

 |

Window compare

 |
 |

bits 2, 1, 0: Compare method

 |
 |

010

 |

Compare to 0

 |
 |

011

 |

Compare to 1

 |
 |

001

 |

Compare to intermediate

 |
 |

100

 |

Compare to mask

 |
 |

101

 |

Compare to unstable

 |
 |

000

 |

Not used

 |
 |

110

 |

Reconstruction not possible

 |
 |

111

 |

Window close

 |

If reconstruction is not possible (code 110 on bits 2, 1, 0), there has been more than one edge or window compare within a single test system cycle.

If error bit 7 is set, an error has occurred on at least one of these edge or window compares.

### Example（取自子主题 Test Result Commands › List of test result commands › WFRE  -  WaveForm REceived data）

```
WFRE? 0, 1, (pin1)
```

returns:

```
WFRE 0,1,3,ERON,(pin1),#9000000006\x0B\x0A\x9B\x9F\x00\x00\x0A
```

This example returns edge action drive and expected data (in binary notation) for one cycle. To decode the data, convert it into binary notation and use the lists above.

The data in binary format is:

```
0000 1011  0000 1010  1001 1011
1001 1111  0000 0000  0000 0000
```

The edge actions are RZ on the drive edges 1 and 2 and a failed window compare (received value: 1) on the receive edges 3 and 4. Edges 5 and 6 are unused.

The WFRE? answer will be split if the requested cycle range is greater than the available error map information, as shown below:

 !`Example`（raw: `../../../../raw/23378.png`）

```
WFRE? 0,15000, (pin1)
WFRE 0, 100, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData           (a)
WFRE 100, 9900, 1, ERON, (pin1), BinData        (b)
WFRE 10000, 5000, 1, NOER, (pin1), BinData      (c)
```

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › Accessing Utility Lines）

For an example see the `UPAS`（raw: `02.06.02.02.304_UPAS__UPAS__-__Utility_Purpose_ASsignment_for_multi-site.md`） command.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › DFUP  DFUP  -  DeFine Utility Purpose）

| ch_No_list |

Utility line channel numbers to be defined as the members of a utility purpose and specified with five digits. The channels must be separated with a comma.

In the five鈥慸igit format, the first three digits of the channel numbers specify the utility pogo block. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy three鈥慸igit format is also supported: The first digit (1 ... 8) specifies the utility pogo block UTIL鈥? ... UTIL鈥?.

The last two digits specify the channel number 01 ... 32 of the utility line.

On the utility pogo blocks, an offset of -1 is to be considered and the channel number is URW00 ... URW31.

When reading the defined utility lines with the DFUP? command, the data returned always have the five鈥慸igit format. The same applies to the `PALS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.173_PALS__PALS__-__Pin_ALlocation_for_multiple_Sites.md`） command.

The channel numbers 16515 and 16516 should not be used. They should only be accessed with the `I2CA`（raw: `02.06.02.02.142_I2CA__I2CA__-__I2CA_bus.md`）or the `BDID`（raw: `02.06.02.02.09_BDID__BDID__-__BoarD_ID.md`）firmware command.

 |
 | setting |

Output states for each channel in the ch_No_list. Specify the setting of each utility line with the following specifiers:

- 0: sets the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)
- 1: sets the corresponding (write) channel to low
- X (x): no action

Specify the setting values corresponding to the definition order of the ch_No_list parameter.

The number of characters must be equal to the number of the utility line channels in the ch_No_list parameter.

Note that the settings must be explicitly activated with `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`）.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of the utility purpose. In the query you can use the symbol @ to list all defined utility purposes.

This parameter can have up to 16 alphanumeric characters and must not contain blank spaces, or any of the following characters: `# ; ( ' ' ) ? @ ,`

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › DFUP  DFUP  -  DeFine Utility Purpose）

```
> DFUP (16501,16502,16503,16504),"0110",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "0110",(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example defines a utility purpose AWG_CNCT and activates its standard settings.

The members and the setting values are as follows:

```
Member:      16501  16502  16503  16504
---------------------------------------
Setting:     0      1      1      0
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › DFUT  DFUT  -  DeFine UTility line）

| ch_No |

Channel number of the utility line specified with five or three digits.

In the five鈥慸igit format, the first three digits specify the utility pogo block. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

In the legacy three鈥慸igit format, the first digit (1 ... 8) specifies the utility pogo block UTIL鈥? ... UTIL鈥?.

The last two digits specify the channel number 01 ... 32 of the utility line.

On the utility pogo blocks, an offset of -1 is to be considered and the channel number is URW00 ... URW31.

When reading the defined utility lines with the DFUT? command, the data returned always have the five鈥慸igit format. The same applies to the `PALS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.173_PALS__PALS__-__Pin_ALlocation_for_multiple_Sites.md`） command.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）

 |
 | type |

Specifies the operating mode of the utility line with the following specifiers:

- W: Write-Only
- R: Read-Only
- RW: Read-Write

Utility lines of the optional `Utility Card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.04_Utility_Card.md`） can also be configured as safety lines or as global shutdown line for hardware鈥慶ontrolled shutdown of XPS256 pins:

- TRIGGER_IF_HIGH: Safety line
- TRIGGER_IF_LOW: Safety line
- TRIGGER_SITE_IF_HIGH: Global shutdown line
- TRIGGER_SITE_IF_LOW: Global shutdown line

For more information, refer to `XPS256 safety line and DUT board disconnect`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.05.03.03.06_XPS256_safety_line_and_DUT_board_disconnect.md`）.

 |
 | util_name |

Name of the utility line. For the query, it specifies the utility line name to be retrieved. @ can be used to list all defined utility lines.

This parameter can have up to 16 alphanumeric characters and must not contain blank spaces, or any of the following characters: `# ; ( ' ' ) ? @ ,`

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › DFUT  DFUT  -  DeFine UTility line）

```
DFUT 16504,w,(filter)
```

This example assigns the name `filter` and operating mode w to utility line 4 of the first utility pogo block.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UDUP -  UnDefine Utility Purpose）

```
UDUP {(purpose_name)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UDUP -  UnDefine Utility Purpose）

| purpose_name |

Specifies the utility purpose name or names to be undefined.

The symbol @ removes all utility purpose definitions.

If more than one name is to be removed, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UDUP -  UnDefine Utility Purpose）

```
UDUP (@)
```

This command undefines all defined utility purpose names.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UDUT -  UnDefine UTility line）

```
UDUT {(util_name)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UDUT -  UnDefine UTility line）

| util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names to be undefined.

The symbol @ removes all utility line definitions.

If more than one name is to be removed, the names must be separated by a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UDUT -  UnDefine UTility line）

```
UDUT (@)
```

This command undefines all defined utility line names.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPAS  UPAS  -  Utility Purpose ASsignment for multi-site）

| site |

The site parameter is an integer that defines the number of the site where the channels are to be defined.

The integer must be greater than 1.

When specified as part of the UPAS? query, you can use the parameter ALL to read the standard output states for all sites.

 |
 | setting |

Output states for each member of the utility purpose on the specified site.

Set the output state of each utility line with the following specifiers:

- 0: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)
- 1: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to low
- X (x): No action

The number and order of characters must correspond to the ch_No_list parameter of the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command.

If this parameter is omitted, the specified site is set to the same states as site 1.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of a utility purpose defined by the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command.

In the query, the symbol @ can be used to list all defined utility purposes.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPAS  UPAS  -  Utility Purpose ASsignment for multi-site）

```
> DFUP (101,102,103,104),"11XX",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPAS 2,"XX11",(AWG_CNCT)
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "11XX", (AWG_CNCT)
> PSFC 2
> UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
> FLSH
> UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
< UPST "XX11", (AWG_CNCT)
```

In this example, the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） command defines a utility purpose AWG_CNCT and output states for site 1. The UPAS command defines the output states of AWG_CNCT for site 2. First the settings of site 1 are activated. Then the setup focus is restricted to site 2, and the output states for site 2 are activated.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPOW  UPOW  -  Utility POWer）

| mode |

The mandatory parameter defines the new state of the supply.

Available options of the parameter:

- ON: Switches the supply on
- OFF: Switches the supply off
 |
 | supplyId |

The extra parameter defines the utility power supply to be set.

Available options of the parameter:

- UP5V: The `+5 V supply on UP5V pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.01_Utility_power_supply_-_UP5V_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the optional Utility Card or the internal utility resources.
- XPP5V: The `+5 V supply on XPP5V pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.02_Utility_power_supply_-_XP_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- XPM5V: The `-5 V supply on XPM5V pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.02_Utility_power_supply_-_XP_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- XPP3V3: The `+3.3 V supply on XPP3V3 pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.02_Utility_power_supply_-_XP_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- P15V: The `+15 V supply on UPP15V pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.03_Utility_power_supply_-_UPP15V___UPM15V___F24V_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_sys.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- M15V: The `-15 V supply on UPM15V pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.03_Utility_power_supply_-_UPP15V___UPM15V___F24V_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_sys.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- F24VA: The `floating 24 V supply on F24VA pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.03_Utility_power_supply_-_UPP15V___UPM15V___F24V_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_sys.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- F24VB: The `floating 24 V supply on F24VB pins`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.03_Utility_power_supply_-_UPP15V___UPM15V___F24V_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_sys.md`） of the optional Utility Card.
- UDPS: The `Internal Utility Power Option`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.04_Internal_Utility_Power_Option__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the internal utility resources that replaces the legacy `SE-UDPS`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.07_Internal_Utility_Power_Supply__SE-UDPS___V93000_systems.md`）.
The extra parameter must always be set in combination with the resourceID parameter. |
 | resourceID |

The extra parameter defines the utility power resource to be set.

Available options of the parameter:

- 1: First `optional Utility Card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.04_Utility_Card.md`） or the `Internal utility power supplies`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.03.02_Internal_utility_power_supplies.md`） of the first card cage.
- 2: Second `optional Utility Card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.04_Utility_Card.md`） or the `Internal utility power supplies`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.03.02_Internal_utility_power_supplies.md`） of the second card cage.
The extra parameter must always be set in combination with the supplyId parameter. |
 |

state

 |

The returned state of the queried supply.

 Possible values are:

- ON: The supply is switched on.
- OFF: The supply is switched off.
- TRIP: Returned in case of a power fail, for example: overcurrent or DUT board undocking.Note To switch on the supply again after such power fail events have occurred, you need to use `UPOW ON` followed by the extra parameters defining the supply and the resource.
   |  Some hints and restrictions for setting the extra supplyId and resourceID parameters:

- For compatibility with the `Internal utility power supply (V93000 systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.05_Internal_utility_power_supply__V93000_systems.md`）, the UP5V supply of the first Utility Card or the internal UP5V supply of the first card cage is always switched on. The supply can be programmed by this FW command but it has no effect on the hardware.
- For compatibility with PinScale and SmartScale systems, the `Utility power supply - XP pins (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.02_Utility_power_supply_-_XP_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the first Utility Card can be programmed only using the short syntax `UPOW {state}` without the extra parameters defined. The supplyId parameter set to XPP5V, XPM5V, or XPP3V3 in combination with the resourceID parameter set to 1 is not supported.
- Independently switching the XPP5V, XPM5V, and XPP3V3 supplies is supported only for the second Utility Card with resourceID parameter set to 2.
- The supplyId parameter set to UDPS is supported only in combination with the resourceID parameter set to 1: Since, the second `optional Utility Card`（raw: `../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.08.04_Utility_Card.md`） occupies all (legacy) DPS pogo blocks, the `Internal Utility Power Option`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.04_Internal_Utility_Power_Option__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） cannot be used if a second Utility Card is installed.

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPOW  UPOW  -  Utility POWer）

```
UPOW ON
```

Switches on the `Utility power supply - XP pins (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.05.02_Utility_power_supply_-_XP_pins__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`） of the first Utility Card.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPST  UPST  -  Utility Purpose STate）

| setting |

The optional parameter specifies the status of the utility lines in the utility purpose.

The status is determined with the following specifiers:

-

0: Sets the output state of the corresponding (write) channel to high (high impedance state)

-

1: Sets the corresponding (write) channel to low

-

X (x): No action

Specify the setting values corresponding to the definition order of the utility lines in the specified utility purpose.

If this parameter is omitted, the settings defined by the `DFUP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.69_DFUP__DFUP__-__DeFine_Utility_Purpose.md`） or UPAS commands (depending on the setup focus as set with `PSFC`（raw: `02.06.02.02.191_PSFC__PSFC__-__Parallel_Setup_FoCus.md`）) are set to the utility lines of the specified utility purpose.

 |
 | purpose_name |

Name of the utility purpose to be set or read.

For the query, you can specify multiple names, which must be separated by a comma.

Specifying the symbol @ returns the definitions of all utility purposes.

   | Note All utility lines that are set with `UTST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.313_UTST__UTST__-__UTility_line_STate.md`） or UPST will be switched in parallel when the `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command is performed. If the `WSDN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.341_WSDN_-__Wait_Setup_DoNe.md`） command is used immediately after FLSH, the time span during which execution will pause equals the longest settling time that is defined for any of the switched utility lines (with `UTTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.314_UTTI__UTTI__-__UTility_line_settling_TIme.md`）) or purposes (with `UPTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.307_UPTI__UPTI__-__Utility_Purpose_settling_TIme.md`）).

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPST  UPST  -  Utility Purpose STate）

```
UPST ,(AWG_CNCT)
FLSH
WSDN
UPST? (AWG_CNCT)
```

returns

```
UPST "0110",(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example sets the utility purpose "AWG_CNCT" to the hardware, then reads the state of the utility purpose.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPTI  UPTI  -  Utility Purpose settling TIme）

| time |

Specifies the wait time to change the utility line status using the `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） commands (in ms).

0 ... 2鈥?47鈥?83.646 [ms]

 |
 | purpose_name |

Specifies the utility purpose name or names for which the settling time is to be set.

The symbol @ is used for all utility purposes.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UPTI  UPTI  -  Utility Purpose settling TIme）

```
UPTI 2.5,(AWG_CNCT)
```

This example sets the settling time of the utility purpose "AWG_CNCT" to 2.5 ms.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIN  -  UTility line INputs）

```
UTIN?
```

returns:

```
UTIN {data}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIN  -  UTility line INputs）

| data |

This parameter returns a decimal number that you must translate to binary.

Ignore the most significant bit. The other bits give the state of the seven lines.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIN  -  UTility line INputs）

```
UTIN?
```

returns:

```
UTIN 6
```

This example returns a decimal value of 6, which is 0000 0110b.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

```
UTIX? [utility_group]
```

returns

```
UTIX {utility_group}, {value}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

|

utility_group

 |

This parameter specifies the utility pogo block.

The pogo block is defined by a three鈥慸igit number. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy single鈥慸igit format 1 ... 8 is also supported, but the query always returns the three鈥慸igit format.

For the query, ALL can be entered to specify all utility blocks.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）.

 |
 |

value

 |

The returned integer word.

This integer word must be translated to binary code to get the state of each utility line in the utility line block specified in the query.

The range is 0 ... 4鈥?94鈥?67鈥?95 for a 4鈥憆ow utility block.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

Assuming that the first 16 utility lines of block 165 are high, then

```
UTIX? 165
```

returns

```
UTIX 165,65535
```

In this example the first 16 utility lines of block 165 were set to 0 by the `UTOT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.311_UTOT__UTOT__-__UTility_line_OuTputs.md`） command and no external device has pulled down any of the utility lines.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTIX  -  UTility line Inputs eXtended）

```
UTIX? 165
```

returns

```
UTIX 165,65534
```

In this example the first 16 utility lines of block 165 were either set to FFFEh by UTOT or they were set to FFFFh and an external device has pulled down line 00, or both occurrences have taken place.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

| utility_group |

This parameter specifies the utility pogo block.

The pogo block is defined by a three鈥慸igit number. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy single鈥慸igit format 1 ... 8 is also supported, but the query always returns the three 鈥慸igit format.

For the UTOT? query, the parameter can be set to ALL to specify all utility blocks.

For more information, see `Utility line assignments`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.01_Utility_line_assignments.md`） and `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`）.

 |
 | mask |

The optional parameter masks the utility lines in the block selected by the utility_group parameter.

Enter a decimal equivalent of a 32 bit binary number (0 ... 4鈥?94鈥?67鈥?95), to mask the required line.

The mask value is defined as follows:

- 1: A bit value of 1 causes the selected line to be programmed to the value specified in the parameter value.
- 0: A bit value of 0 masks the line, that is, the line remains unchanged.

If the mask parameter is not specified, then all the utility lines in the selected block are programmed.

 |
 | value |

This parameter can be entered either as string in the form of a hex word (0 ... FFFF鈥疐FFF), or in the form of an integer word (0 ... 4鈥?94鈥?67鈥?95).

Utility lines are basically low side switches. Therefore, the utility lines are set to the inverse of the binary equivalent of the specified value. For example, let us assume the value is 12. This equals to 1100 in binary, its inverse is 0011. Therefore, the first and the second utility line (URW00 and URW01) will be set to high, while all others on this block are set to low.

You can pulse the output utility lines by entering several hex words one after another (not decimal integers) enclosed in double quotes.

- Thus to produce a single pulse on the sixth line of the second utility pogo block, you would enter: `UTOT 166, "0040, 0000, 0040"`.
- You can use this facility for instance to produce a trigger pulse for a certain measurement.
- The specified hex data is sequentially written to the utility lines.Note Such pulses on the utility lines can in no way be synchronized to the execution of test vectors and are meant to enable you to switch slow devices such as relays. If you need to switch utility lines in synchronism with test vectors you must use the command `UTSC, UTSC? - (UTility line Serial Configuration)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.312_UTSC__UTSC__-__UTility_line_Serial_Configuration.md`） and set up serial control of utility lines as described in `Sequencer-controlled utility lines`（raw: `../../03_Use_cases_and_application_papers/03.09_How_to_set_up_sequencer__ontrolled_utility_lines/03.09.01_Sequencer-controlled_utility_lines.md`）.
 |
 | word |

This is an integer value returned by the system, informing you of the setting of the utility output lines. For each utility block you enter, the system returns a reading.

The query returns the value the utility lines were set to by `UTOT`. Use the `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`） command to read back the actual state of the utility lines.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT 165,16383,12345
```

This code sets the first sixteen utility lines of the first block, except those used for the addressing of EEPROMs related to the DUT interface. These are URW14 and URW15. URW0 to URW13 are set to the inverse of 12345. 12345 in decimal equals 0011000000111001 in binary. Inverted, this is 53190 in decimal or 1100111111000110 in binary. Thus the lines will have these states:

 |

URW00 = low

 |

URW04 = low

 |

URW08 = high

 |

URW12 = low

 |
 |

URW01 = high

 |

URW05 = low

 |

URW09 = high

 |

URW13 = low

 |
 |

URW02 = high

 |

URW06 = high

 |

URW10 = high

 |

URW14 = high

 |
 |

URW03 = low

 |

URW07 = high

 |

URW11 = high

 |

URW15 = high

 |

For the utility lines required to address EEPROMs related to the DUT interface see `Utility lines and DUT board EEPROMs`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.04.06_Utility_lines_and_DUT_board_EEPROMs.md`）.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT? 165
```

returns:

```
UTOT 165,,12345
```

The query returns the value that was written by UTOT. If you have previously executed Example 1, then the returned value will be the written value, but bits 14 and 15 may be different. This is because these lines retain the values that have been written previously.

Use the `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`） command to read back the actual state of the utility lines.

### Example 3（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT 166,65535,"5555,AAAA,0,FFFF"
```

writes the sequence AAAAh, 5555h, FFFFh, 0000h to the first sixteen utility lines of the second utility block.

### Example 4（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTOT  UTOT  -  UTility line OuTputs）

```
UTOT? 166
```

returns the last written values. If you have just executed example 3, the result would be:

```
UTOT 166,,65535
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTSC  UTSC  -  UTility line Serial Configuration）

| word |

One unique utility pogo block number or a list enclosed in brackets containing utility pogo blocks separated by commas.

The pogo block or the list of pogo blocks uses three鈥慸igit numbers. For valid pogo blocks, refer to `DUT interface layout`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.03.01_DUT_interface_layout.md`） and to `Utility pogo block mapping`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md#_347642__s_Utility_pogo_block_mapping`） in `Utility pogo block - Utility Card (V93000 EXA Scale systems)`（raw: `../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08.02_Utility_pogo_block_-_Utility_Card__V93000_EXA_Scale_systems.md`）.

The legacy single鈥慸igit format 1 ... 8 is also supported, but the query always returns the three鈥慸igit format.

 |
 | ALL  | Keyword to use all available utility blocks with the given mode. |
 | mode |

Mode to be applied to a single block or the ganged utility blocks.

Available modes are:

 |
 | RD  | Parallel output (with `UTOT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.311_UTOT__UTOT__-__UTility_line_OuTputs.md`）), parallel input (with `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`）) or serial input (via serial interface pin SOUT), turns ganging on, if off. |
 | RW  | Serial output (via serial interface pin SINP), parallel input (with `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`）) or serial input (via serial interface pin SOUT), turns ganging on, if off. |
 | OFF  | Parallel output (with `UTOT`（raw: `02.06.02.02.311_UTOT__UTOT__-__UTility_line_OuTputs.md`）), parallel input (with `UTIX?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.310_UTIX__-__UTility_line_Inputs_eXtended.md`）), turns ganging off. |
 | maskMode |

The extra parameter sets the mask mode for the defined utility blocks.

Available modes are:

 |
 | MASK  | Enables the mask mode. |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTSC  UTSC  -  UTility line Serial Configuration）

The following example shows how to reset the mode for all utility blocks to static:

```
UTSC ALL, OFF
```

The following example shows how to gang utility blocks 1 to 4 setting the mode to serial out:

```
UTSC (165,166,167,168),RW
```

The following example shows how to change the mode of the previously set up gang to parallel out:

```
UTSC (165,166,167,168),RD
```

The following example, based on the previous setup, will lead to an error, because the fourth utility pogo block is missing:

```
UTSC (165,166,167),OFF
```

The following example shows how to turn off ganging by changing the mode of the previously set up gang to off:

```
UTSC (165,166,167,168),OFF
```

The following example shows how to set up a new gang with the second, third and fourth utility pogo block in serial out mode:

```
UTSC (166,167,168),RW
```

The following example shows how to use the UTSC? query to display the entire gang and the mode if a single utility block of a gang is given:

```
UTSC? 166
```

results in:

```
UTSC (166,167,168),RW
```

The following example shows how to use the UTSC? query to display all gangs and modes of all utility blocks:

```
UTSC? ALL
```

results in:

```
UTSC 1,OFF
UTSC (166,167,168),RW
UTSC 169,OFF
UTSC 170,OFF
UTSC 171,OFF
UTSC 172,OFF
```

The following example shows how to change the existing gang with utility blocks 2 to 4 in serial out mode to the masked mode:

```
UTSC (166,167,168),RW,MASK
```

The following example shows the query result of UTSC? with mask mode set for the second to fourth utility pogo block:

```
UTSC? ALL
```

results in:

```
UTSC 165,OFF
UTSC (166,167,168),RW,MASK
UTSC 169,OFF
UTSC 170,OFF
UTSC 171,OFF
UTSC 172,OFF
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTST  UTST  -  UTility line STate）

| value |

Specifies the output (desired) status of the utility line with the specifier 0 or 1.

- 0: High output
- 1: Low output
 |
 | type |

This parameter is used to specify whether the output (desired) state or the input (actual) state is to be returned. Possible values are:

- w: Returns the output (desired) state.
- r: Returns the input (actual) state

For pure output utility lines, this parameter is ignored.

 |
 | util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names to be set or read.

In the query, specifying @ returns all utility lines.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated by commas.

   | Note All utility lines that are set with UTST or `UPST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.305_UPST__UPST__-__Utility_Purpose_STate.md`） will be switched in parallel when the `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command is performed. If the `WSDN`（raw: `02.06.02.02.341_WSDN_-__Wait_Setup_DoNe.md`） command is used immediately after FLSH, the time span during which execution will pause equals the longest settling time that is defined for any of the switched utility lines (with `UTTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.314_UTTI__UTTI__-__UTility_line_settling_TIme.md`）) or purposes (with `UPTI`（raw: `02.06.02.02.307_UPTI__UPTI__-__Utility_Purpose_settling_TIme.md`）).

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTST  UTST  -  UTility line STate）

```
UTST 1,(Filt1,Filt2)
UTST 0,(Filt3,Filt4)
FLSH
WSDN
UTST? w,(Filt1,Filt2,Filt3,Filt4)
```

will return:

```
UTST 1,(Filt1,Filt2)
UTST 0,(Filt3,Filt4)
```

This example sets the utility lines "Filt1" and "Filt2" to high output, and "Filt3" and "Filt4" to low output.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTTI  UTTI  -  UTility line settling TIme）

| time  | Specifies the wait time to change the utility line status using the `UTST`（raw: `02.06.02.02.313_UTST__UTST__-__UTility_line_STate.md`） and `FLSH`（raw: `02.06.02.02.124_FLSH_-__FLuSH_buffered_commands.md`） command (in ms). |
 | util_name |

Specifies the utility line name or names for which the settling time is to be set.

The symbol @ is used for all utility lines.

If more than one name is required, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Utility Line Commands › List of utility line commands › UTTI  UTTI  -  UTility line settling TIme）

```
UTTI 2.5,(filter)
```

This example sets the settling time of the utility line "filter" to 2.5 ms.

### Description（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › Concepts of the TMU per pin › TMU per Pin overview）

The following figures show the basic principles for period and pulse width measurements. Note that the sample rate of the TMU is 20 ns, and that the minimum distance between two events required by the event discarding block is about 4 ns (for this latter requirement see also `Dealing with very high data rates`（raw: `02.06.13.01.05_Dealing_with_very_high_data_rates.md`）).

### Example 2: Pulse width measurement（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › Concepts of the TMU per pin › TMU per Pin overview）

The second example illustrates a measurement where rising and falling edges are sampled alternately. This is the basis for measurements of the positive or negative pulse width. No discard before the first measurement has been defined. The graphic only illustrates the case of the positive pulse width.

 !`Pulse width measurement with the ppTMU`（raw: `../../../../raw/127185.png`）

Note the following points with respect to alternate sampling of rising and falling edges:

- The event discarding block only considers the rising edges of the prescaler output; the falling edges are ignored. Therefore all selected events (that is, also the falling edges) are represented by the prescaler as rising edges.
- If in this case the prescaler is set to n, then after selecting an edge, it skips the next n edges of the same type, and then selects the next edge of the opposite type. Thus in the example, after selecting a rising edge, it skips the next 3 rising edges and then selects the next falling edge; and after selecting a falling edge, it skips the next 3 falling edges, and then selects the next rising edge.
- If an even number (including 0) of events is to be discarded before the first sample, the first sampled event will be a rising edge. If you discard an odd number of events before the first sample, the first sampled event will be a falling edge. In this case the formulas for PW+ and PW-, as specified in the graphic, must be interchanged.
- If you specify an odd number of events to be discarded between samples (for example, only one event in the figure above), the sampled events will all be of the same type, that is, they will be either all rising or all falling edges. Therefore, if you want to measure the pulse width, the number of events to be discarded between two samples must be even.
- With alternate sampling of rising and falling edges, the period length can be calculated from the samples by the formula

 (ti+1 - ti-1) / ((prescaling_factor + 0.5) * (inter_meas_discard + 1) * 2).

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › Concepts of the TMU per pin › Storing the results of more than one TMU measurement）

```
> TSPR "TMU_set1"
> TSRH? REQUEST,"area1"
< TSRH REQUEST,"area1",SUCCEED
> FTST?
> FTST P
> TSPR "TMU_set2"
> TSRH? REQUEST,"area2"
< TSRH REQUEST,"area2",SUCCEED
> FTST?
< FTST P
> TSRS? ,PERIOD,,,(pin_a)
< TSRS ,PERIOD,,1.36,(pin_a)
> TSRH? SELECT,"area1"
< TSRH SELECT,"area1",SUCCEED
> TSRS? ,PERIOD,,,(pin_a)
< TSRS ,PERIOD,,1.38,(pin_a)
```

This example makes successively `TMU_set1` and `TMU_set2` the primary TMU set, and executes a test with each of these primary TMU sets. The results of the first measurement are stored in `area1`, those of the second in `area2`. Afterwards, the global means of both measurements are retrieved with TSRS?.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSCF  TSCF  -  TMU Set ConFiguration）

|

ts_name

 |

Specifies the name of a TMU set that must have been defined with TSDF.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the TMU test. For a list see the table below. If this parameter is omitted in the query, all defined properties will be returned.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all TMU sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified to modify or retrieve the configuration of the current primary TMU set.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified property. The values that are admitted for the individual properties are listed in the table below.

 |
 |

RESET

 |

If you specify this keyword instead of a property value, the property will be deleted in the specified TMU set.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which this configuration is to be applied.

 |

Properties and their values
 |

Property

 |

Explanation and values

 |
 |

DATA_RATE

 |

This property defines the data rate which is the smallest distance between two events. The unit is bits per second.

 |
 |

EDGE_SELECT

 |

This mandatory property defines which edges are the events to be sampled. Possible values are:

 |
 |

 |

RISE

 |

The events are rising edges.

 |
 |

 |

FALL

 |

The events are falling edges.

 |
 |

 |

RISE_FALL

 |

The events are alternately rising and falling edges. This option is used for pulse and jitter measurements. If this option is selected, the PRESCALER property must be set to a value > 1 and < 17.

 |
 |

INITIAL_DISCARD

 |

This optional property defines how many events are to be discarded before the first sample of a measurement set. This refers to the events as they occur in the output signal of the prescaler. The default is 0.

If EDGE_SELECT is set to RISE_FALL, and INITIAL_DISCARD is set to an even number, the first sampled event will be a rising edge if INITIAL_DISCARD is set to an odd number, the first sampled event will be a falling edge.

Note: Parameter INITIAL_DISCARD must be 0 for DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD

 |

This optional property defines how many events are to be discarded between two samples of a measurement set. This refers to the events as they occur in the output signal of the prescaler. The default is 0.

If EDGE_SELECT is set to RISE_FALL, this property must be set to an even number (including 0). If it is set to an odd number, all sampled edges will be of the same type, all rising or all falling.

Note: Parameter INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD must be 0 for DC Scale pins.

 |
 |

MEAS_PER_SHOT

 |

This mandatory property must equal the number of armings in the pattern. A shot is one execution of the pattern. For certain measurements, two executions are required; see the NUM_SHOTS parameter.

This is one of the three parameters by which the required size of the result area is determined. The others are SAMPLES_PER_MEAS and NUM_SHOTS.

 |
 |

NUM_SHOTS

 |

This optional property defines the number of shots (sequencer runs). It is used to calculate the size of the result area and to determine how the measurements are to be processed. The possible values are 1 or 2. Two shots are needed for rise time and fall time measurements. The default is 1.

 |
 |

PRESCALER

 |

This mandatory property defines how much the frequency of the signal is to be reduced before it is passed on to the event discarding block. This is required if the minimal distance of two consecutive events in the DUT signal can be smaller than the minimal distance that the event discarding block supports.

Possible values for Smart Scale pins are 1 through 17. 1 means no prescaling. If EDGE_SELECT is set to RISE_FALL, the prescaler value must be < 17 and > 1.

 |
 |

SAMPLES_PER_MEAS

 |

This mandatory property defines the number of samples per measurement (arming). This is another parameter that contributes to the calculation of the result area size.

 |
 |

THRESHOLD_A

 |

This optional property defines a voltage threshold for the event to be sampled. It is only needed for (two shot) rise time and fall time measurements. The default is the voltage level as defined in the level setup.

Note that if this property is defined, the level setup must be changed, and if the pins specified by pinlist are tested functionally in parallel with the TMU measurement, they will be tested with the modified voltage level.

Note also that the original level setup is automatically restored after the measurement has been finished.

 |
 |

THRESHOLD_B

 |

This optional property defines the voltage threshold for a second shot. It is only needed for (two shot) rise time and fall time measurements.

It must not be defined if NUM_SHOTS is set to 1.

Note that the original level setup is automatically restored after the measurement has been finished.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSCF  TSCF  -  TMU Set ConFiguration）

```
> TSCF? "TMU_set1",,(Pin1)

< TSCF "TMU_set1",PRESCALER,3,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",INITIAL_DISCARD,0,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD,500,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",SAMPLES_PER_MEAS,2,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",NUM_SHOTS,1,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",MEAS_PER_SHOT,5,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",EDGE_SELECT,RISE,(Pin1)
< TSCF "TMU_set1",DATA_RATE,50000000,(Pin1)
```

This example queries a period measurement definition. Typically, only two samples are taken for such a measurement, and these at a great distance (see the INTER_SAMPLE_DISCARD property in the example). The period resulting from this measurement can be retrieved with the `TSRS?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.278_TSRS__-__TMU_Set_ReSults.md`） query.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSDF  TSDF  -  TMU Set DeFinition）

|

TMU_set_name

 |

mode_context

 |

The mode context with which the TMU set is associated. If this parameter is omitted, the DEFAULT context is assumed.

|

 |
 |

ARM_OVERRUN

 |
 |

 |
 |

NOT_FINISHED

 |

The measurement has not been finished.

pinlist

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRC  -  Time Stamping Results Computed）

```
TSRC? [(sitesToBeDone),] [measurement_id], {result_type}, [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(execution_control),] [(site_selector),] [(resultAreaName),] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSRC [shotcount],{result_type}, {successinfo}, {(pin)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRC  -  Time Stamping Results Computed）

| sitesToBeDone |

An extra string parameter, defining the sites to be uploaded. i.e. "01110011".

This option needs parameter `site_selector`（raw: `02.06.02.02.277_TSRC__-__Time_Stamping_Results_Computed.md#_141847__r_site_selector`） to be set to ALL.

 |
 | measurement_id |

The optional number of the measurement block (identified by the ARM keyword within a waveform that is executed in the pattern) for which the computation is performed. If no measurement block is specified, all measurement blocks will be computed.

 |
 | result_type |

The mandatory result type. Currently, the only supported result type is PERIOD.

 |
 | first_sample |

NOT USED

 |
 | no_of_samples |

NOT USED

 |
 | execution_control |

With this extra parameter, you can modify the default action sequence of TSRC?. Possible values are:

 | NOT_FINISHED |

Default. All three steps described above will be executed. If not all required samples have been actually taken, the query will not stop, it issues warning and continues to analyze and compute the available samples.

 |
 | FINISHED |

Completeness check will be skipped. TSRC? assumes that all required samples have been taken. It will analyze and compute the available samples. It starts from step 2, above.

 |
 | ANALYZED |

Samples will not be analyzed. TSRC? assumes that all required samples were taken and analyzed in a previous step. It computes the available samples. It starts from step 3, above.

   | |
 | site_selector |

This extra query parameter allows you to compute the results for a specific site or all sites. Possible values are:

 | ONE |

Only the values of the site which has the query focus are processed (the default).

 |
 | ALL |

The values of all sites or the sites defined by parameter `sitesToBeDone`（raw: `02.06.02.02.277_TSRC__-__Time_Stamping_Results_Computed.md#_141847__r_sitesToBeDone`） are processed.

 |
 | <N> |

The results of the site with this number are processed.

   | |
 | resultAreaName |

The extra parameter defines the name of the result area from which the samples should be computed. If this parameter is omitted, the default result area is used.

 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory list of pins for which the time stamps are to be computed.

 |
 | pin |

The pin to which the computed results belong.

 |
 | shotcount |

The parameter returns the number of shots that have been computed.

 |
 | successinfo |

The parameter indicates whether the computation succeeded.

Possible return values:

-

SUCCEEDED

-

FAILED.

 |

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRS  -  TMU Set ReSults）

```
TSRS? [(sitesToBeDone),] [measurement_id], {result_type}, [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(execution_control),] [(site_selector),] [(resultAreaName),] [(mode),] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSRS [measurement_id], [(sitenumber),] {result_type}, [sample_id|aggregation_type|first_sample], {result|no_of_samples}, {(pin)} [,#spec(binary_results)]
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRS  -  TMU Set ReSults）

| sitesToBeDone |

An extra string parameter, defining the sites to be uploaded. i.e. "01110011".

This option needs parameter `site_selector`（raw: `02.06.02.02.278_TSRS__-__TMU_Set_ReSults.md#_125500__r_site_selector`） to be set to ALL.

 |
 | measurement_id |

The optional number of the measurement block (identified by the ARM keyword within a waveform that is executed in the pattern) for which periods or statistics to be returned. If no measurement block is specified, the periods or statistics of all measurement blocks are returned.

 |
 | result_type |

The mandatory result type. Currently, the only supported result type is PERIOD.

 |
 | first_sample |

The optional parameter specifies the first sample in the query (TSRS?) for which the period is to be returned. In the return (TSRS) of the query it specifies the first sample that is returned if the mode is set to ON. Samples are counted from 0.

 |
 | no_of_samples |

The optional parameter defines in the query (TSRS?) the number of samples for which the periods are to be returned. In the return (TSRS) of the query it specifies the number of samples that are returned if the mode is set to ON.

Depending on the value of parameter first_sample, fewer samples than specified may be returned. For example, if there are 9 samples in total, first_sample is 7 and no_of_samples is 4, only two samples are returned (the last two), not four.

 |
 | execution_control |

With this extra parameter, you can modify the default action sequence of TSRS?. Possible values are:

 | NOT_FINISHED |

All four steps described above will be executed. If not all required samples have been actually taken, the query will not stop, it will continue to analyze,compute and upload the available samples.

This is the default value.

 |
 | FINISHED  | Completeness check will be skipped. TSRS? assumes that all required samples have been taken. It will analyze, compute, and upload the available samples. It starts from step 2. |
 | ANALYZED  | Samples will not be analyzed. TSRS? assumes that all required samples were taken and analyzed in a previous step. It computes the available samples. It starts from step 3. |
 | COMPUTED  | Samples will not be computed. TSRS? assumes that all required samples were taken, analyzed, and computed in a previous step. It retrieves the periods and their statistics to the system controller. It starts from step 4.  | |
 | site_selector |

This extra query parameter allows you to request the results for all sites or a specific site. Possible values:

 | ONE |

Only the values of the site which has the query focus are processed (the default).

 |
 | ALL |

The values of all sites or the sites defined by parameter `sitesToBeDone`（raw: `02.06.02.02.278_TSRS__-__TMU_Set_ReSults.md#_125500__r_sitesToBeDone`） are processed.

 |
 | <N> |

The results of the site with this number are processed.

   | |
 | resultAreaName |

The extra parameter defines the name of the result area from which the samples should be retrieved. If this parameter is omitted, the default result area is used.

 |
 | mode  | This extra parameter controls the format of the reply when a range is specified with parameters first_sample and no_of_samples:

- If mode is set to OFF, a separate line is returned for every period value within the range.
- If mode is set to ON, the values are returned in a binary format in one line.
OFF is the default value. |
 | pinlist  | The mandatory list of pins for which the time stamps are to be returned. |
 | sitenumber |

Extra reply parameter. The site the samples belong to if the site_selector parameter has been set to ALL.

 |
 | sample_id |

This reply parameter identifies the sample. It is only returned if a range was specified in the query and mode was set to OFF.

 |
 | aggregation_type |

This reply parameter specifies an aggregation type. If a range was specified in the query, TSRS? returns not only the individual period values but also a number of statistics. These are:

-

STDDEV (standard deviation)

-

MEAN

-

MAX

-

MIN

-

MEDIAN

-

PP (peak to peak), the PP is same as MINMAX in the TMU ORE firmware.

 |
 | result |

The reply parameter specifies the period related to sample n or a value of the descriptive statistics. The unit is seconds.

It is not returned if a range was specified in the query and mode was set to ON.

 |
 | pin |

The pin to which the returned results belong.

 |
 | #spec(raw_results) |

The binary data that are returned if a range is specified with parameters first_sample and no_of_samples, and parameter mode is set to ON. The general format is:

`n1n2...nNdata_stream`

Where the decimal digit N defines the number of the decimal digits ni (1 = i = N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

The values are specified as seconds.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRS  -  TMU Set ReSults）

This example returns the descriptive statistics for the measurement blocks individually.

```
> TSRS? ,PERIOD, , , (pin_a)

    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , STDDEV ,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MEAN 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MAX, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MIN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , MEDIAN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  1,PERIOD , PP, 1.36,(pin_a)

    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , STDDEV ,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEAN 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MAX, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MIN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEDIAN, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , PP, 1.36,(pin_a)
```

This example returns the individual samples 100 through 119 in measurement block 2, and also the statistical values.

```
> TSRS? 2,PERIOD,100,20,(pin_a)

    < TSRS  2,PERIOD ,100,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD ,101,1.37,(pin_a)
    ...
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD ,119,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , STDDEV ,1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MEAN 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MAX, 1.36,(pin_a)
    < TSRS  2,PERIOD , MIN, 1.36,(pin_a)

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRW  -  TMU Set RaW results）

```
TSRW? [(sitesToBeDone),] [shot], [measurement_id], [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(execution_control),] [(site_selector),][(resultAreaName),] [(mode),] {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TSRW [shot], [measurement_id], [first_sample], [no_of_samples], [(sitenumber),] {(pin)}, {#spec(raw_results)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRW  -  TMU Set RaW results）

| sitesToBeDone |

An extra string parameter, defining the sites to be uploaded. i.e. "01110011".

This option needs parameter `site_selector`（raw: `02.06.02.02.279_TSRW__-__TMU_Set_RaW_results.md#_125519__r_site_selector`） to be set to ALL.

 |
 | shot |

The optional parameter specifies the number of the shot for which the time stamps are to be uploaded. If no shot number is specified, the time stamps for all shots are uploaded.

 |
 | measurement_id |

The optional number of the measurement block (identified by the ARM keyword within a waveform that is executed in the pattern) from which time stamps are to be uploaded. If no measurement block is specified, results from all measurement blocks are uploaded.

 |
 | first_sample |

The optional parameter specifies the first sample to be uploaded. Samples are counted from 0.

 |
 | no_of_samples |

The optional parameter specifies the number of samples that are to be uploaded. Depending on the value of parameter first_sample, fewer samples than specified may be uploaded. For example, if there are nine samples in total, first_sample is 7 and no_of_samples is 4, only two samples are returned (the last two), not four.

 |
 | execution_control |

With this extra parameter, you can modify the default actions sequence of TSRW?. Possible values are.

 |

NOT_FINISHED

 |

All three steps described above will be executed. If not all required samples have been actually taken, the query will not stop, it issues a warning and continues to analyze and upload the available samples.

This is the default value.

 |
 | FINISHED  | The completeness check will be skipped. TSRW? assumes that all required samples have been taken. It will analyze and upload the available samples. It starts from step 2, above. |
 | ANALYZED  | Samples will not be analyzed. TSRW? assumes that all required samples were taken and analyzed in a previous step. It uploads the available samples. It starts from step 3, above.  | |
 | site_selector |

This extra query parameter allows you to request the results for a specific site or all sites. Possible values:

 | ONE |

Only the values of the site which has the query focus are uploaded (the default).

 |
 | ALL |

The values of all sites or the sites defined by parameter `sitesToBeDone`（raw: `02.06.02.02.279_TSRW__-__TMU_Set_RaW_results.md#_125519__r_sitesToBeDone`） are computed.

 |
 | <N> |

The results of the site with this number are computed.

   | |
 | resultAreaName |

The extra parameter defines the name of the result area from which the samples should be retrieved. If this parameter is omitted the default result area is used.

 |
 | mode |

This extra parameter has two functions. It defines the format of the reply, and it controls the behavior of the TMU if the distance of a sample from the arming point exceeds the maximum of about 15 s.

By default, there will be an internal wrap-around in this case, and the following time stamps will no longer be correct. You can choose to let the software correct the results, but this will increase the testing time.

There are four options:

-

OFF

The time stamps are returned in ASCII format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are wrapped around.

-

ON

The time stamps are returned in binary format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are wrapped around.

-

LTOFF

The time stamps are returned in ASCII format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are corrected.

-

LTON

The time stamps are returned in binary format. Values that exceed the maximum distance from the arming point are corrected.

 |
 | pinlist |

The mandatory list of pins for which the time stamps are to be uploaded.

 |
 | pin |

The pin to which the uploaded results belong.

 |
 | sitenumber |

Extra reply parameter. The site to which the samples belong.

 |
 | #spec(raw_result) |

The binary data that are returned. The general format is:

`n1n2...nNdata_stream`

Where the decimal digit N defines the number of the decimal digits ni (1 = i = N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the TMU per pin › List of commands for the TMU per pin › TSRW  -  TMU Set RaW results）

```
> TSRW? 1,1,0,3,(std_i)

    < TSRW 1,1,0,3,(std_i),#2470.0000524107368,0.0000525147428,0.0000526187385
```

This example uploads the time stamps 0 through 2 of measurement block 1 of the first shot. The unit is seconds.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › Concepts of source synchronous testing  html › Principles of source synchronous testing）

The following figure illustrates the principle by a very simple example with deterministic phase distortion (common mode drift):

 !`Pattern iteration for source-synchronous testing`（raw: `../../../../raw/84881.png`）

In this example, the pattern is repeated eight times. This is a certain redundancy since every cycle has passed at least in one shot already after the third shot. If unnecessary shots are to be avoided, the overall result would have to be checked after each shot.

So far, it has been assumed that only one data change occurs in every cycle, so that only one result per cycle is required. But you can also check several changes in one cycle. In this case you would have to record results on the edge level (all eight edges are recorded in one shot). In this case the whole pattern would be considered as passed if every edge passes at least in one shot.

The above discussion centers on validation of a given requirement. But you can also measure the actual setup time by setting the distance between the data edge and the clock edge to 0. The setup time will then be the time between the first and the last point where the expected values are received for both data and clock.

A group of output data pins and the associated output clock pin is called a synchronization group. One source synchronous device may contain several synchronization groups.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSAC  SSAC  -  Source Synchronous testing  Add Configuration）

|

read_mode

 |

Possible read modes are:

 |
 |

NORM

 |

Channel data is processed as it is stored in the source channels. This is the default.

 |
 |

INV

 |

Channel data is inverted internally before it is processed. The channel data itself is not changed.

 |
 |

nr_of_results

 |

Specifies the size of the area to be used for buffering cycle/edge data for source synchronous testing. If this parameter is omitted you must specify a reference pin.

The number to be specified here must be calculated as

result_granularity * number_of_cycles.

The result granularity is the number of results per cycle. It can be 1 (one global result), in which case you must specify the number of cycles, or 8 (one result for every edge), in which case you must specify 8 * number_of_cycles.

The number of bytes required to store the specified number of results must be a multiple of 8. If this requirement is not satisfied, the number of results will be auto-corrected.

 |
 |

ref_pin

 |

The pin that defines the size of the buffer area. If this parameter is omitted, you must specify the number of results. If a reference pin is defined, the nr_of_results parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pins that are to be configured as buffer pins.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSAC  SSAC  -  Source Synchronous testing  Add Configuration）

The following example shows how the buffer channels are configured by using a reference pin:

```
> DCGM ALL,STRT,NONE
> DCRT RAM,(@)
> SSRC (@)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.4
> FTST?
> SSAC INV,,(D1),(SB)
> SSAC NORM,,(D1),(G1,G2)
> SSCT IMM,NORM,,(SB),(D1,D2,D3,CL)
> SSCT ACC,NORM,,(G1),(SB)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.5
> FTST?
. . .
```

First the detailed Error Map is configured for source synchronous testing (recording mode ALL, location in RDRAM). Next the existing buffer configurations are removed. Then the sweep variable is set, and the first functional test executed. Subsequently the buffer channels are configured using D1 as the reference pin. Then the results of the first functional test are processed. Finally, the sweep variable is incremented and the next functional test executed.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSCT  SSCT  -  Source Synchronous data  Combine and Transfer）

The following example shows a typical start sequence of a source synchronous test:

```
> DCGM ALL,STRT,NONE
> DCRT RAM,(@)
> SSRC (@)
> SSAC INV,128,,(SB)
> SSAC NORM,128,,(G1,G2)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.4
> FTST?
> SSCT IMM,NORM,128,(SB),(D1,D2,D3,CL)
> SSCT ACC,NORM,128,(G1),(SB)
> SVLR TIM,1,1,"sweep",2.5
> FTST?
> SSCT IMM,NORM,128,(SB),(D1,D2,D3,CL)
> SSCT ACC,NORM,128,(G2),(SB,G1)
. . .
```

At first, the detailed Error Map is configured for the requirements of result buffering (error map located in RDRAM, recording mode ALL). After the first functional test the results of the data pins D1 through D3 and the output clock pin CL are immediately combined and transferred into the source buffer SB. The subsequent transfer into the first global buffer is delayed and will only be triggered by the next FTST? call. After the second functional test, the SSCT ACC call combines the results of the source buffer and the first global buffer into the second global buffer.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSRC -  Source Synchronous testing  Remove Configurations）

```
SSRC {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSRC -  Source Synchronous testing  Remove Configurations）

|

pinlist

 |

The pins whose buffer configurations are to be removed. Pins for which no buffer configuration exists are ignored.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSRC -  Source Synchronous testing  Remove Configurations）

```
> SSRC (@)
```

This example removes all buffer configurations. Pins for which no buffer has been configured are ignored.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSTR  -  Source Synchronous Testing  Result query）

```
SSTR? [ALL_SITES,] {GLO|INV},{(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
SSTR {GLO|INV},{(pinlist)},{glob_res}
```

Or:

```
SSTR? {DET},{(pin)}
```

returns:

```
SSTR {DET},{(pin)},{#spec(data)}}
```

Parameters
 |

ALL_SITES

 |

This parameter causes SSTR? to return a global result for all sites. If it is omitted, the result for that site is returned that currently has the result focus.

 |
 |

GLO

 |

One global result is returned for all buffers of the pin list. The result is calculated by combining first all cycle results of the individual buffers with AND, and then the combined buffer results of all buffers again with AND. PASS will be returned if the final result is 1.

This option must be selected if PASS is represented by 1 and FAIL by 0 in all buffer pins.

 |
 |

INV

 |

One global result is returned for all pins of the pin list. The result is calculated in 3 steps:

- The cycle results of the individual channels are inverted.
- The inverted cycle results are combined with AND.
- The global results of the individual channels are again combined with AND

PASS will be returned if the final result is 1.

This option must be selected if PASS is represented by 0 and FAIL by 1 in all buffer pins. A possible application is that one global result is to be returned for one or more global buffers.

 |
 |

DET

 |

The cycle results of the specified buffer pin are returned as they are stored in the buffer.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The buffer pins whose results are to be accumulated. More than one pin can only specified for options GLO and INV.

 |
 |

pin

 |

If DET is specified as the first parameter, only one pin may be specified.

 |
 |

glob_res

 |

The global result that is returned for options GLO and INV. "P" signifies PASS, and "F" signifies FAIL.

 |
 |

#spec(data)

 |

The binary data that is returned for option DET. It has a header which specifies the length of the data in the following format:

#Nn1n2n...nNdata_stream,

where the digit N defines the number of the digits ni (1 鈮?i 鈮?N) that specify the length of data_stream in bytes.

If you record 8 results per cycle (every edge is recorded) then one bit represents one edge. If only one global result per cycle is recorded, two bits represent one cycle.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing › List of commands for source synchronous testing › SSTR  -  Source Synchronous Testing  Result query）

The following example assumes that the global buffer pins G2 and G4 contain the total results of two source synchronous tests that were run in parallel:

```
> SSTR? INV,(G2)
< SSTR INV,(G2),P
> SSTR? INV,(G4)
< SSTR INV,(G4),F
> $SSTR? DET,(G4)
< SSTR DET,(G4),#9000000008,0000 0000  0001 0000  0000 0000  0000 0100  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000  0000 0000
> SSTR? INV,(G2,G4)
< SSTR INV,(G2,G4),F
```

Note that the result granularity has been set to 8, so that every bit of the SSTR DET reply represents one receive edge. Note also that SSTR DET simply returns the buffer content. Since the global buffers must represent FAIL by 1 and PASS by 0, the reply indicates that one edge in the second cycle and one edge in the fourth cycle have failed in all shots for one of the two tests. All other edges have passed at least in one shot.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › Overview of the protocol engine per pin › Drift and transition tracking）

!`Transition tracking`（raw: `../../../../raw/146398.png`）

This example picks up the example of `Overview of the protocol engine per pin`（raw: `02.06.15.01_Overview_of_the_protocol_engine_per_pin.md`）. Five observation windows are shown. There are last CD transitions in the first and third window. The fourth window has its last internal transition between A and B in the third sub-window.
