### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTCF  TTCF  -  Transition Test ConFiguration）

|

tt_name

 |

Specifies the name of a transition test set that must have been defined with `TTDF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.288_TTDF__TTDF__-__Transition_Test_set_DeFinition.md`）.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the transition test set. For a list, see the Properties and their values table below.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all transition test sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified to modify or retrieve the configuration of the current primary transition test set.

 |
 |

DEFAULT

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration of the predefined transition test set DEFAULT. Note that the DEFAULT set cannot be changed, it can only be queried.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified property. The values that are admitted for the individual properties are listed in the table below.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which this configuration is to be applied.

 |

Properties and their values
 |

Property

 |

Explanation and values

 |
 |

ALL_PATTERN_ERR

 |

This is a collective switch for all pattern matching errors. The possible values are ON and OFF. There is no default.

 |
 |

ALL_TRACKING_ERR

 |

This is a collective switch for all tracking errors. The possible values are ON and OFF. There is no default.

 |
 |

DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED

 |

This property only applies if X-tokens are removed (REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE set to ON) and the token size is > 0. It defines the maximum number of UI by which the received data are allowed to exceed the expected data under these circumstances. The received data exceeds the expected data in length if the number of idle tokens in the received data is greater than the number of X-tokens in the expected data. See `Skipping idle tokens`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.02_Skipping_idle_tokens.md`）.

The default is 0. The specified value must be 鈮?256.

 |
 |

DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT

 |

This property only applies if X-tokens are removed (REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE set to ON) and the token size is > 0. It defines the maximum number of UI by which the expected data are allowed to exceed the received data under these circumstances. The expected data exceeds the received data in length if the number of X-tokens in the expected data is greater than the number of idle tokens in the received data. See `Skipping idle tokens`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.02_Skipping_idle_tokens.md`）.

The default is 0. The specified value must be 鈮?256.

 |
 |

DISPARITY_MODE

 |

This property determines whether disparity is taken into account when comparing expected tokens with received tokens. This only applies to token size 10.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_BADTRAN

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if an illegal sequence of transitions occurred.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTADJOVR

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if an adjustment overflow occurs. This means that the observation window was adjusted more than 1 UI in one direction within 24 UI. Note that adjustments in opposite direction cancel each other out. Thus if '+' indicates an adjustment to the right, and '-' an adjustment to the left,

`- + - + - + - +`

is acceptable, but

`+ + + + + - + +`

creates an overflow.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTLMT

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the maximum drift of 7.75 UI for the entire pattern is exceeded.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_COMPARE

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if compare errors are detected.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_FTO

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the number of UI that are skipped for synchronization at test start exceeds the maximum defined with FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_JMP2

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if an unrecoverable BC transition (jump by 2) is detected.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_PULSE

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if a bit was sampled only once. If pulse stretching is enabled, the error will refer to the stretched pulse (see `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.03_Stretching_the_pulse.md`）).

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_STO

 |

This property defines whether the test fails when the number of consecutive skipped bits after initial synchronization exceeds the maximum defined with SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

This can happen in two cases:

- at synchronization of an IO pin that has been switched from drive to receive mode, or
- when too many consecutive idle tokens have been skipped, that is, if

no_of_tokens * token_size > SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_STOP

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the sequencer stops too early, that is, before all compare actions have been completed. This error can be avoided by adding an appropriate number of break vectors (at least 400) at the end of the test.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE0

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if no reference transition occurs, that is, the observation window could not be adjusted successfully.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE2

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if a BC transition occurs in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LLHH HHHH

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE3

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if two different transitions occur within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LHHH LLLH

Here the second UI contains an AB transition, and the third UI contains a CD transition.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TE4

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if three transitions occur within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

HHLL LHHH LLLH

Here the first UI contains a BC transition, the second contains an AB transition, and the third a CD transition.

The possible values are ON and OFF. OFF is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TRK

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the maximum drift for the entire pattern as defined with TRACKING_LIMIT is exceeded.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_TRMCNT

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the skipped idle bits are not a multiple of the token size.

 |
 |

ERR_XMAX

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the length of the received data exceeds the length of the expected data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

ERR_XMIN

 |

This property defines whether the test fails if the length of the expected data exceeds the length of the received data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT

 |

This property defines how many bits are allowed to be skipped by initial synchronization at test start. The maximum value is 2^32. This is also the default.

 |
 |

FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE

 |

This property activates or deactivates initial synchronization at test start.

The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default.

 |
 |

IDLE_TOKEN_i

 |

With this property, you can specify idle tokens whose occurrences in the received data are to be counted. i can be 1 through 6. This property only applies to token sizes > 0 and < 18.

 |
 |

PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_1BIT

 |

This property defines if and how much pulses that are sampled only once are to be stretched. For more information see `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.03_Stretching_the_pulse.md`）.

Possible values are:

 |
 |

NONE

 |

No stretching takes place.

 |
 |

STRETCH_1TO3

 |

1 sample bits are stretched to 3 samples.

 |
 |

STRETCH_1TO4

 |

1 sample bits are stretched to 4 samples.

 |
 |

PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_2BIT

 |

This property defines if and how much pulses that are sampled only twice are to be stretched. For more information see `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.01_Startup_latency_and_initial_synchronization.md`）.

Possible values are:

 |
 |

NONE

 |

No stretching takes place.

 |
 |

STRETCH_2TO3

 |

2 sample bits are stretched to 3 samples.

 |
 |

STRETCH_2TO4

 |

2 sample bits are stretched to 4 samples.

 |
 |

REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE

 |

This property activates or deactivates removal of tokens consisting entirely of X from the expected data. The possible values are ON and OFF. For more information see `Skipping idle tokens`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.02_Skipping_idle_tokens.md`）.

This property only takes effect if the token size is > 0.

 |
 |

SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT

 |

This property defines how many bits are allowed to be skipped by subsequent initial synchronization. The maximum value is 2^32. This is also the default.

This property also limits the maximum number of consecutive idle tokens that can be skipped after synchronization, by the following inequality:

number_of_skipped_tokens * token_size 鈮? SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT

 |
 |

SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE

 |

This property activates or deactivates subsequent initial synchronization, for example after the switch of an IO pin from drive to receive mode. The possible values are ON and OFF. ON is the default. This property only takes effect if FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE is set to ON.

For more information see `Startup latency and initial synchronization`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02.01_Startup_latency_and_initial_synchronization.md`）.

 |
 |

TOKEN_SIZE

 |

This property defines the token size for the pattern matching block. The allowed values are:

0, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 32, 34, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 64, 66.

0 is the default. For more information see `Pattern matching`（raw: `02.06.15.01.02_Pattern_matching.md`）.

 |
 |

TRACKING_LIMIT

 |

This property defines how much the device is to be allowed to drift during the whole pattern. The maximum value that still allows a reliable tracking is 7.75 UI. This is also the default.

The step width for this parameter is 1/4 UI.

 |
 |

TRACKING_MODE

 |

This property defines the operation mode of the transition tracker. For more information see `Controlling the tracking behavior`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.01_Controlling_the_tracking_behavior.md`）.

The possible values are:

 |
 |

ACTIVE

 |

If necessary, the observation window is adjusted after every 3 UI.

 |
 |

FREEZE_AFTER_SYNC

 |

If necessary, the observation window is adjusted once at test start and once after every switch of a IO pin from drive to receive mode.

 |
 |

FREEZE_ALWAYS

 |

The observation window is never adjusted.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTCF  TTCF  -  Transition Test ConFiguration）

```
> TTCF? "my_TT_SET",ALL,(PIN1)

< TTCF "my_TT_SET",DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED,100,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT,100,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",DISPARITY_MODE,OFF,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_BADTRAN,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_CNTADJOVR,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_CNTLMT,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_COMPARE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_FTO,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_JMP2,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_PULSE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_STO,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_STOP,OFF,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE0,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE2,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE3,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TE4,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TRK,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_TRMCNT,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_WRCMP,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_XMAX,ON,(PIN1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",ERR_XMIN,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT,10,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_1,"LLLLLHHHHH",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_2,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_3,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_4,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_5,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",IDLE_TOKEN_6,"",(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_1BIT,STRETCH_2TO4,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",PULSE_STRETCHING_MODE_2BIT,STRETCH_1TO3,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE,OFF,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT,10,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_MODE,ON,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",TOKEN_SIZE,10,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",TRACKING_LIMIT,4,(Pin1)
< TTCF "my_TT_SET",TRACKING_MODE,ACTIVE,(Pin1)
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTDB  -  Transition Test DeBug information）

```
TTDB? {type|ALL}, [sub_type], {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TTDB {type}, [sub_type], {value}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTDB  -  Transition Test DeBug information）

|

type

 |

Specifies the information type. For a list, see the Information types and subtypes table below.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All information types are returned.

 |
 |

sub_type

 |

Specifies a subtype of the information type. The subtypes for every type are listed in the Information types and subtypes table below.

 |
 |

value

 |

Specifies the value for the specified combination of type and subtype. For more explanation see the Information types and subtypes table below.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which debug information is to be retrieved.

 |

Information types and subtypes
 |

Information type

 |

Explanation and values

 |
 |

MAX_DEVIATION

 |

If the token size was > 0 during the last sequencer run, this item returns for this sequencer run:

- The maximum number of UI by which the received data has fallen behind the exceeded the expected data (subtype DUT_BEHIND_ED)
- The maximum number of UI by which the expected data has fallen behind the received data (subtype ED_BEHIND_DUT)

The received data is shortened by skipping idle tokens, the expected data by removing X-tokens.

 |
 |

TRK_FIRST_ADJUSTMENT

 |

This item returns the adjustment that was determined by the first transition after test start.

 |
 |

TRK_FIRST_ERR

 |

This item returns the number of expected bits that had been processed when the first tracking error occurred.

 |
 |

TRK_VALUES

 |

This item returns information about the adjustment of the observation window. The unit is 0.25 UI (= 1 sample).

There are three subtypes:

- ACT returns the actual adjustment at the end of the test.
- MIN returns the maximum adjustment to the left during the last test.
- MAX returns the maximum adjustment to the right during the last test.
 |
 |

TRK_STATUS

 |

This item returns the transition patterns that were observed during the last test as a sequence of four-digit blocks.

In order to understand this information, you must take into account that the observation window can only be adjusted after every three UI (see the discussion of the implementation parameters in `Drift and transition tracking`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01_Drift_and_transition_tracking.md`）). Thus, the observation window actually consists of three successive UI.

The four-digit blocks encode the accumulated transitions for one such 3-UI window (subtype TRANS_COMPOSITE) or for two such windows (subtype TRANS_X). "1" indicates a transition, "0" indicates no transition. Every block starts with "1". This indicates that the observation window was adjusted successfully.

As an example for the one window case, consider

LLLL LHHH LLLH,

where the second UI has an AB transition, and the third has a CD transition. This is encoded by

1101,

which says that an AB transition (second digit) and a CD transition (fourth digit), but no BC transition was observed in the 3-UI window.

TRK_STATUS has three subtypes:

- TRANS_X returns the transition patterns that occurred in the last 24 UI (= 8 windows, each of 3 UI). Each of the four blocks accumulates two windows (= 6 UI). The order of the blocks corresponds to the order of the test.
- TRANS_COMPOSITE returns the transition patterns that occurred by accumulating the 3 UI of one window during the last sequencer run up to the first error. Since the first digit is always 1 (except when the window could not be adjusted) there are 8 possible patterns between 1000 (best) and 1111 (worst). The patterns that occurred are displayed.
- TRANS_R returns 0 if the observation window could always be adjusted successfully. It returns 1 if this is not the case. This error should only occur if the observation window was adjusted more than 1 UI in the same direction within 24 UI (see the ERR_CNTADJOVR property of the TTCF command).
 |
 |

LOCATION_FIRST_FAIL

 |

This item returns the number of expected bits that had been processed when the first error of any kind occurred.

 |
 |

REMOVED_IDLE

 |

This item returns how often one of the 6 idle tokens that had been defined with TTCF IDLE_TOKEN_i occurred during the last sequencer run. The sub_type parameter specifies the number of the token.

 |
 |

REMOVED_XTOKEN

 |

This item returns how many X-tokens were removed. This only applies if X-token removal is activated with TTCF REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE.

REMOVED_XTOKEN has one subtype:

- SEQUENCER_RUN returns the number of X-tokens that were removed on the last sequencer run
 |
 |

STATUS

 |

This item returns information about the state of the tracker after the test as a bit sequence. Most of these status bits can also be queried with TTST?. The individual bits stand for:

 |
 |

- Bit1: An interrupt was generated.
- Bit2: Break vectors entered the formatting block.
- Bit3: The first match between expected and received data has occurred.
- Bit4: Expected and received data are prepared for the first compare.
- Bit5: The FIFO between tracking and pattern matching block is empty.
- Bit6: The FIFO between expected data and pattern matching block is empty.
- Bit7: The expected data window FIFO is empty.
- Bit8: The expected data FIFO is empty.
- Bit9: EXPECTED_FIFO_DUT_OVERFLOW
- Bit10: ADJUSTMENT_ERROR
- Bit11: Always 1
- Bit12: DRIVE_BIT_IN_COMPARE_DATA
- Bit13: DUT_FIFO_OVERFLOW
- Bit14: ERR_XCNT
 |

- Bit15: ERR_XMIN
- Bit16: ERR_XMAX
- Bit17: ERR_TRMCNT
- Bit18: ERR_WRCMP
- Bit19: ERR_COMPARE
- Bit20: ERR_STO
- Bit21: ERR_FTO
- Bit22: ERR_STOP
- Bit23: ERR_CNTLMT
- Bit24: ERR_CNTADJOVR
- Bit25: ERR_BADTRAN
- Bit26: ERR_PULSE
- Bit27: ERR_TRK
- Bit28: ERR_JMP2
- Bit29: ERR_TE4
- Bit30: ERR_TE0
- Bit31: ERR_TE2
- Bit32: ERR_TE3
 |
 |

The names specified for bits 9 through 32 refer to the possible errors returned by `TTST?`（raw: `02.06.02.02.292_TTST__-__Transition_Test_STatus_information.md`）. For more explanations see this query and the `TTCF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.286_TTCF__TTCF__-__Transition_Test_ConFiguration.md`） command.

 |
 |

REMOVED_XTOKEN_EMAP

 |

This item returns how many x-tokens were removed with respect to start and stop of the error map.

REMOVED_XTOKEN_EMAP has two subtypes:

- START returns the number of removed X-tokens at the start of the error map.
- STOP returns the number of removed X-tokens at the end of error map recording.
 |
 |

SYNC_VALUES

 |

This item returns how many received bits were skipped for initial synchronization at test start (subtype INITIAL) or after a switch of an IO pin from drive to receive mode (subtype SUBSEQUENT).

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTDB  -  Transition Test DeBug information）

```
> TTDB? IDLE_TOKEN, 1, (Pin1)

< TTDB IDLE_TOKEN, 1, 1234,(Pin1)
```

This example queries how often the first special idle token was removed in the last sequencer run.

```
> TTDB? TRK_STATUS,ALL, (Pin1)

< TTDB TRK_STATUS,TRANS_X,"1000 1001 1101 1000", (Pin1)
< TTDB TRK_STATUS,TRANS_R,0, (Pin1)
< TTDB TRK_STATUS,TRANS_COMPOSITE,"1000 1001 1101", (Pin1)
```

The first line of the reply reports the transitions of the last 24 UI, accumulated in blocks of 6. The third line reports which accumulated transition patterns occurred in one window (= 3 UI) during the last sequencer run. Three of the 8 possible patterns were observed.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTDF  TTDF  -  Transition Test set DeFinition）

```
> TTDF   "myTTTrckSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTPatTSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTRCTLSet1"

TTDF?
> TTDF   "myTTTrckSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTPatTSet1"
> TTDF   "myTTRCTLSet1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTMD  -  Transition Test MoDe query）

```
TTMD? {specset_id|"multi-port_spec"}, {timing_set}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
TTMD {specset_id|"multi-port_spec"}, {timing_set}, {tt_mode}, [clk_fwd], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTMD  -  Transition Test MoDe query）

|

specset_id

 |

Number of a single-port timing specification. Derived as follows:

`100 *`equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multiport_spec

 |

For a multiport setup, specify the name of a multiport specification.

Note that the multiport specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multiport specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing set number. Enter PRM for the primary timing set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by TSUS.

 |
 |

tt_mode

 |

Specifies the protocol engine test mode. Possible values are:

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Protocol engine is inactivated

 |
 |

X4

 |

X4-mode is activated.

 |
 |

X6

 |

X6-mode is activated.

 |
 |

clk_fwd

 |

Not used.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the protocol engine mode is to be retrieved. This parameter can also include groups previously created by the `DFGP`（raw: `02.06.02.02.60_DFGP__DFGP__-__DeFine_GrouP.md`） (DeFine GrouP) command. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated by a comma.

In a multiport setup, every pin must belong to a port of the specified specification.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTMD  -  Transition Test MoDe query）

```
> TTMD 101,1,(PIN1)
< TTMD 101,1,X4,,(PIN1)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTPR  TTPR  -  Transition Test PRimary set）

|

tt_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing transition test set.

 |
 |

DEFAULT

 |

This is a predefined transition test set.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTPR  TTPR  -  Transition Test PRimary set）

```
> TTPR   "myTTTrckSet1"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTST  -  Transition Test STatus information）

```
TTST? {status_type}, {filter}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

TTST {status_type}, {property}, {state}, {(pinlist)}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTST  -  Transition Test STatus information）

|

status_type

 |

Specifies the status type. Possible values are:

 |
 |

ERR_STATUS

 |

Returns information about possible errors per pin. These are exactly the properties that can be activated as errors with TTCF, and whose names start with "ERR_".

Note that each of the states contained in this status type is reported when it is observed, regardless of whether it is actually activated with TTCF. TTCF only controls whether the specific error condition contributes to the pass/fail result of a pin.

The possible errors are:

 |
 |

ERR_BADTRAN

 |

An illegal sequence of transitions occurred.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTADJOVR

 |

An adjustment overflow occurred. This means that the observation window was adjusted more than 1 UI in one direction within 24 UI. Note that adjustments in opposite direction cancel each other out. Thus if '+' indicates an adjustment to the right, and '-' an adjustment to the left,

- + - + - + - +

is acceptable, but

+ + + + + - + +

creates an overflow.

 |
 |

ERR_CNTLMT

 |

The maximum drift of 7.75 UI for the entire pattern was exceeded.

 |
 |

ERR_COMPARE

 |

Compare errors were detected.

 |
 |

ERR_FTO

 |

The number of bits that were skipped for synchronization at test start exceeds the maximum defined with FIRST_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

 |
 |

ERR_JMP2

 |

An unrecoverable BC transition (jump by 2) was detected.

 |
 |

ERR_PULSE

 |

A bit was sampled only once. If pulse stretching was enabled this error refers to the stretched pulse. See `Stretching the pulse`（raw: `02.06.15.01.01.03_Stretching_the_pulse.md`）.

 |
 |

ERR_STO

 |

The number of consecutive skipped bits after initial synchronization exceeds the maximum defined with SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

This can happen in two cases:

- at synchronization of an IO pin that has been switched from drive to receive mode, or
- when too many consecutive idle tokens have been skipped, that is, if

no_of_tokens * token_size >

SUBSEQUENT_INITIAL_SYNC_LIMIT.

 |
 |

ERR_STOP

 |

The sequencer stopped too early, that is, before all compare actions have been completed. This error can be avoided by adding an appropriate number of break vectors (at least 400) at the end of the test.

 |
 |

ERR_TE0

 |

No reference transition occurred, that is, the observation window could not be adjusted successfully.

 |
 |

ERR_TE2

 |

A BC transition occurred in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LLHH HHHH

 |
 |

ERR_TE3

 |

Two different transitions occurred within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

LLLL LHHH LLLH

Here the second UI contains an AB transition, and the third UI contains a CD transition.

 |
 |

ERR_TE4

 |

Three transitions occurred within a UI (not between two UI) in a block of three UI, for example

HHLL LHHH LLLH

Here the first UI contains a BC transition, the second contains an AB transition, and the third a CD transition.

 |
 |

ERR_TRK

 |

The maximum drift for the entire pattern as defined with TRACKING_LIMIT was exceeded.

 |
 |

ERR_TRMCNT

 |

The removed idle bits were not a multiple of the token size.

 |
 |

ERR_XMAX

 |

The length of the received data exceeds the length of the expected data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_DUT_BEFORE_ED.

This only applies when X-token removal is activated with the REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE property.

 |
 |

ERR_XMIN

 |

The length of the expected data exceeds the length of the received data by more than the value defined with DEVIATION_LIMIT_ED_BEFORE_DUT.

This only applies when X-token removal is activated with the REMOVE_XTOKEN_MODE property.

 |
 |

ERR_STATUS_COMBINED

 |

Returns combined information about possible errors for all specified pins.

Note that each of the states contained in this status type is reported when it is observed, regardless of whether it is actually activated as an error with `TTCF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.286_TTCF__TTCF__-__Transition_Test_ConFiguration.md`）.

 |
 |

INTR_STATUS

 |

Returns information per pin about interrupts during the last sequencer run.

 |
 |

INTR_STATUS_COMBINED

 |

Returns combined information about interrupts for all specified pins.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

All status types are returned.

 |
 |

filter

 |

Specifies which subset of the available information is to be returned. The possible values depend on the selected status type.

Possible values for ERR_STATUS and ERR_STATUS_COMBINED are:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

The state of all possible errors is returned.

 |
 |

ALL_HEX

 |

The state of all possible errors is returned as a hexadecimal number.

 |
 |

OFF

 |

Only the possible errors that were not observed are returned.

 |
 |

ON

 |

Only the possible errors that were observed are returned.

 |
 |

property

 |

The reply is whether the possible error identified by this property was observed. For the meaning of the properties see the `TTCF`（raw: `02.06.02.02.286_TTCF__TTCF__-__Transition_Test_ConFiguration.md`） command.

 |
 |

The values ALL, ALL_HEX, OFF, and ON can also be specified for INTR_STATUS and INTR_STATUS_COMBINED.

The individual properties for these two types are:

 |
 |

ADJUSTMENT_ERROR

 |

This is a hardware error.

 |
 |

DRIVE_BIT_IN_COMPARE_DATA

 |

This can only happen when APG mode is enabled and a drive bit was found in the received data.

 |
 |

DUT_FIFO_OVERFLOW

 |

This can happen when X-token removal is enabled and the number of removed X-tokens exceeds the number of skipped idle tokens.

 |
 |

EXPECTED_FIFO_DUT_OVERFLOW

 |

This is a hardware error.

 |
 |

state

 |

Specifies the state of a selected property. Possible values are:

 |
 |

OFF

 |

The state was not observed.

 |
 |

ON

 |

The state was observed.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which status information is to be retrieved.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for the protocol engine per pin › List of commands for protocol engine tests › TTST  -  Transition Test STatus information）

```
> TTST? ALL,ALL,(p1)

< TTST INTR_STATUS,DRIVE_BIT_IN_COMPARE_DATA,OFF,(p1)
< TTST INTR_STATUS,ADJUSTMENT_ERROR,OFF,(p1)
< TTST INTR_STATUS,DUT_FIFO_OVERFLOW,OFF,(p1)
< TTST INTR_STATUS,EXPECTED_FIFO_OVERFLOW,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_XMAX,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_XMIN,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_FTO,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_STO,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TRMCNT,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_COMPARE,ON,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE4,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE3,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE2,ON,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TE0,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_JMP2,ON,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_TRK,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_PULSE,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_BADTRAN,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_CNTADJOVR,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_CNTLMT,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_STOP,OFF,(p1)
< TTST ERR_STATUS,ERR_WRCMP,OFF,(p1)
```

This example returns all properties of the ERR_STATUS type. ON indicates that the respective state was observed, OFF indicates that it was not observed. Note that ON does not imply that the test failed. For this, the respective property must also be activated as an error with TTCF. In this example compare errors (ERR_COMPARE) and a jump by 2 (ERR_TE2, ERR_JMP2) were observed.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for jitter injection › Principles of jitter injection）

!`Predefined jitter modulation waveforms`（raw: `../../../../raw/117826.png`）

These are three of the four predefined jitter modulation waveforms that are available on a Smart Scale system.

This example defines a simple sawtooth waveform with a peak-to-peak value of 200ps for a STDDIFF or STD pin.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for jitter injection › List of commands for jitter injection › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

```
JSWF? {"jitter_set_name"}, {clock_resolution}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
JSWF {"jitter_set_name"}, {"offset_sequence"}, {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for jitter injection › List of commands for jitter injection › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

|

jitter_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of a jitter set that must have been defined with JSDF.

 |
 |

clock_resolution

 |

Specifies the clock resolution on which the calculation will be based. The admitted range is between 880 and 1750 ps.

You can retrieve the clock resolution for a specification with the CLKR? EXACT query.

Note that the unit is pico seconds, not nano seconds.

 |
 |

offset_sequence

 |

The list of the calculated offsets that is returned.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which the offset sequence is calculated.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands for jitter injection › List of commands for jitter injection › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

```
> jscf? "test",,(IO0)
< JSCF "test",WAVEFORM,SINUS,(IO0)
< JSCF "test",PERIOD,20,(IO0)
< JSCF "test",AMPLITUDE,100,(IO0)
> CLKR? EXACT,101,(@)
< CLKR 101,2.4,1.2,(@)
> jswf? "test",1200,(IO0)
< JSWF "test","0,29,47,47,29,0,-30,-48,-48,-30,-1,29,47,47,29,0,
  . . .
  -1,-30,-48,-48,-30,0,29,47,47,29,0,-30,-48,-48,-30",(IO0)
```

This example first queries the jitter waveform for pin `IO0`, and also the clock resolution for timing specification 101. It then calculates the offset sequence for this waveform and clock resolution. Note that CLKR? returns the clock resolution as nano seconds, but that JSWF? expects it to be specified as pico seconds. The reply is displayed in abbreviated form. The total length of the sequence is about 500 items.

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands for jitter injection › List of commands for jitter injection › JSWF  -  Jitter Set WaveForm）

```
> JSCF? "test",WAVEFORM,(IO1)
< JSCF "test",WAVEFORM,"150,110,80,70,0"
> JSWF? "test",880,(IO1)
< JSWF "test","150,120,90,70,40",(IO1)
```

This example shows how JSWF? corrects the offset list if the second of two consecutive items is smaller than the first, and the maximum difference is exceeded.

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › Overview of pseudo random bit sequences）

The following example shows a Fibonacci and a Galois LFSR for the same connection polynomial 1 + x + x3 (which corresponds to the recurrence relation sn+3 = sn+2 + sn), and also the PRBSs that they create from the seed 001. The rightmost column displays the output sequence in both cases.

 !`Fibonacci and Galois LFSR`（raw: `../../../../raw/118399.png`）

Both LFSRs create basically the same periodic PRBS. But in order to generate the same sequence right from the start, they must be initialized with different seeds. If the seed of the Fibonacci LFSR is 100 (in the output order), the seed of the Galois LFRS must be 110 in the output order.

Observe that the period of the PRBS resulting from 1 + x + x3 is maximal: The LFSR assumes each of its 2^3 = 8 possible states except 000 before the same state is reached again.

It is also obvious that if any segment on, on+1, on+2 of the output sequence is taken as the seed of the Fibonacci LFSR in the order on+2, on+1, on, the resulting PRBS will be identical with the original output sequence from on onwards.

### Examples（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › Executing a pattern  ased SmartLoop test › Defining a compliance pattern for pattern  ased SmartLoop testing）

### Model file entry

```
IOCHANNEL
10101-10108: HW=PS9G, speed= 3600Mbps, smem = 112M, loopback = 6800Mbps
...
```

### Pin configuration

```
>  DFPN? (PortD)
<  DFPN 10101,"4",(Pin4)
<  DFPN 10105,"5",(Pin5)
```

### Equation set

```
EQNSET 1 "equation set 1"

DEFINES  PortD

SPECS
p      [ns]

compliance

TIMINGSET 1 "eq 1 ts 1"
period=1.5

PINS  Pin4
d1=0 #DU

PINS  Pin5
r1=16 #RU
```

### Pattern

```
>  SQLB? ALL,MAIN,(PortD)
<  SQLB "compl",MAIN,0,3,"wavetable 1",(PortD)
>  SQLA? ALL,ALL,ALL,(PortD)
<  SQLA LBL,"compl","PARA_MEM=HSER,PARA_MCTX=DEFAULT",(PortD)
<  SQLA LBL,"burst","PARA_MEM=NONE",(PortD)
>  SQPG? ALL,(PortD)
<  SQPG 0,STVA,,0,,(PortD)
<  SQPG 1,STSA,,,,(PortD)
<  SQPG 2,GENV,100501,,,(PortD)
<  SQPG 3,STOP,,,,(PortD)
<  SQPG 4,CALL,,"compl",,(PortD)
<  SQPG 5,BEND,,,,(PortD)
```

Note that the compliance pattern `compl` comprises 100501 vectors. This is possible because channels 10101 through 10104 and 10105 through 10108 are all licensed for SmartLoop鈩? but only 10101 and 10105 are associated with a pin.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › LBMD  -  LoopBack MoDe）

LBMD? {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|PRM}, {(pinlist)}

returns:

LBMD {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi-port_spec"|PRM}, {lpbk_mode}, {(pinlist)}

Parameters
 |

wvf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number (range 1 to maximum). Enter ALL for all waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

This option is needed by some GUIs that use this query. A SmartLoop鈩?test can only be defined in equation based timing.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case).

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

The SmartLoop鈩?configuration of the primary wavetable(s) is returned.

 |
 |

lpbk_mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

LOOP_I

 |

The pin is enabled for resending the received data to the DUT.

 |
 |

LOOP_O

 |

The pin is enabled for routing received data to the corresponding input pin.

 |
 |

LOOP_OFF

 |

The pin is not configured for SmartLoop鈩?testing.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the SmartLoop鈩?configuration is to be retrieved. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured input and IO pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › LBMD  -  LoopBack MoDe）

```
> LBMD? PRM,(@)
< LBMD 101,LOOP_OFF,,(pin1,pin2)
> SPRM 103,1,1,1
> LBMD? PRM,(@)
< LBMD 103,LOOP_I,2,(pin1)
< LBMD 103,LOOP_O,8,(pin2)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › LBMD  -  LoopBack MoDe）

```
> LBMD? "lpbk_1",(@)
< LBMD "lpbk_1",LOOP_O,(pin1,pin2)
```

This example queries a wavetable.

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › LBRT  -  LoopBack RouTing）

```
LBRT? {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
LBRT {(pin1)}, {(pin2)}
```

Parameters
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins for which the partner pin is to be retrieved.

 |
 |

pin1

 |

Specifies a pin of pinlist.

 |
 |

pin2

 |

Specifies the pin which is mapped to the partner channel of the channel for pin1.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › LBRT  -  LoopBack RouTing）

```
> LBRT? (@)
< LBRT (pin1),(pin2)
< LBRT (pin2),(pin1)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRCF  PRCF  -  Pseudo Random bit sequence ConFiguration）

|

PRBS_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of a PRBS set that must have been defined with PRDF.

 |
 |

property

 |

Specifies a property of the PRBS set. There are two properties to be configured:

 |
 |

POLYNOMIAL

 |

This property defines the connection polynomial of the LFSR. It is coded as a bit string where the position of the bit identifies the degree of the addend, and its value defines the coefficient of this addend. The constant term of the polynomial, which is always 1, must be omitted. The last bit is supposed to determine the degree n of the polynomial. Therefore, the length of the string must be n, and its last bit must be "1".

 |
 |

SEED

 |

This property defines the seed for the LFSR in the order in which it is output. This property is only required for PRBS generation. The seed for the PRBS check is taken from the received data.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

This value can be specified in the query to retrieve the configuration data of all PRBS sets.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

This value can be specified to modify or retrieve the configuration of the current primary PRBS set.

 |
 |

property_value

 |

Specify a bit string for this parameter. Its meaning depends on the selected property. For POLYNOMIAL it encodes the connection polynomial. For SEED, it defines the initial state of the LFSR. The maximum length is 32 in both cases.

- The default for the polynomial is

11111110111010110011110000100101,

which is the polynomial

1+x+x2+x3+x4+x5+x6+x7+x9+x10+x11+x13+x15+x16+x19+x20+x21+x22+x27+x30+x32.

- The default for the seed is

00110010011011110001001101100111.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

Specifies the pins to which pin this configuration is to be applied.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRCF  PRCF  -  Pseudo Random bit sequence ConFiguration）

```
> PRCF? "PRBS_1",ALL,(Pin1)
< PRCF "PRBS_1",POLYNOMIAL,"101",(Pin1)
< PRCF "PRBS_1",SEED,"100",(Pin1)
```

This example defines 1 + x1 + x3 as the connection polynomial, and 100 as the initial segment for Pin1. This is the example which is also used in `Overview of pseudo random bit sequences`（raw: `02.06.17.01_Overview_of_pseudo_random_bit_sequences.md`）.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRDF  PRDF  -  PRBS set DeFinition）

|

prbs_set_name

 |

In the command, this is the name of a new PRBS set. In the query, it is a name of an existing PRBS set. If you omit this parameter in the query, PRDF? will return the names of all user defined PRBS sets.

 |
 |

mode_context

 |

The mode context with which the PRBS set is associated. If this parameter is omitted, the DEFAULT context is assumed.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRDF  PRDF  -  PRBS set DeFinition）

```
> PRDF   "prbs_set1"
> PRDF   "prbs_set2"
> PRDF   "prbs_set3"
```

```
> PRDF?
< PRDF   "prbs_set1"
< PRDF   "prbs_set2"
< PRDF   "prbs_set3"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

```
PRMD? {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi_port_spec"|PRM}, {(pinlist)}
```

returns:

```
PRMD {wvf_set|"wavetable_name"|specset_id|"multi_port_spec"|PRM}, {prbs_mode}, [x_mode], {(pinlist)}
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

|

wvf_set

 |

Waveform Set Number (range 1 to maximum). Enter ALL for all waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by the command `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

This option is needed by some GUI tools that use this query. A PRBS test can only be defined in equation based timing.

 |
 |

wavetable_name

 |

The wavetable name. Enter a string of up to 40 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case).

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

100 * equation_set_no + specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

To query a multi-port specification, enter the name of the specification.

 |
 |

PRM

 |

The PRBS configuration of the primary wavetable(s) is returned.

 |
 |

prbs_mode

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

PRBS_I

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS generation.

 |
 |

PRBS_I_INV

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS generation and is the negative connection of a differential pair.

 |
 |

PRBS_O_INV

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS checking and is the negative connection of a differential pair.

 |
 |

PRBS_O

 |

The pin is enabled for PRBS checking.

 |
 |

PRBS_OFF

 |

The pin is not configured for PRBS testing.

 |
 |

x_mode

 |

Specifies the x-mode for PRBS enabled pins. Left empty if prbs_mode is PRBS_OFF.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The name of the pin or pins for which the PRBS configuration is to be retrieved. The symbol @ can be used to specify all configured input and IO pins. If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

 |

### Example 1（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

```
> PRMD? PRM,(@)
< PRMD 101,PRBS_OFF,,(pin1,pin2)
> SPRM 103,1,1,1
> PRMD? PRM,(@)
< PRMD 103,PRBS_I,2,(pin1)
< PRMD 103,PRBS_O,8,(pin2)
```

### Example 2（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRMD  -  PRBS MoDe）

```
> PRMD? "prbs_2",(@)
< PRMD "prbs_2",PRBS_O,4,(pin1,pin2)
```

This example queries a wavetable.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRPR  PRPR  -  PRBS PRimary set）

|

prbs_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing PRBS set. If you specify "", the defaults will be restored.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRPR  PRPR  -  PRBS PRimary set）

```
> PRPR   "PRBS_set"
```

### Syntax（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRUD -  PRBS set UnDefine）

PRUD {"prbs_set_name"|ALL}

### Parameters（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRUD -  PRBS set UnDefine）

|

prbs_set_name

 |

Specifies the name of an existing PRBS set.

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Remove all existing transition tests sets

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests › List of commands for PRBS per pin and loopback tests › PRUD -  PRBS set UnDefine）

```
> PRUD   "prbs_set1"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › ASWE  ASWE  -  Auto SWing Enable）

|

waveform_set

 |

Specifies the number of a waveform set for non-equation based testing. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, ALL for all waveform sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by `WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md`）.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Specifies a spec set ID for equation based testing. The specset_id is derived as follows:

`100 *` equation_set_no `+ ` specset_no

 |
 |

enable_status

 |

Enter ON to switch automatic swing modification on. Enter OFF to switch automatic swing modification off.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › ASWE  ASWE  -  Auto SWing Enable）

```
ASWE 1,ON
```

This example enables the automatic swing adjustment for waveform set 1.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › ASWM  ASWM  -  Auto SWing Mode）

|

command

 |

This parameter is used to set the specified mode:

 |
 |

SET

 |

Sets the mode specified regardless of the previous mode.

 |
 |

MIN

 |

Sets the 'minimum' mode of either the mode specified or the previous mode. Minimum refers to minimum time consumption.

The following order applies:

FREEZE, SEARCH, AUTO. For example, SEARCH is the minimum mode of the two modes SEARCH and AUTO.

 |
 |

MAX

 |

Sets the 'maximum' mode of either the mode specified or the previous mode. Maximum refers to maximum time consumption.

The following order applies:

AUTO, SEARCH, FREEZE. For example, SEARCH is the maximum mode of the two modes SEARCH and FREEZE.

 |
 |

mode

 |

The mode can take one of the following values:

 |
 |

AUTO

 |

Automatic level swing adjustment is done for all waveform sets. Any change of waveforms or levels triggers an automatic swing adjustment.

 |
 |

FREEZE

 |

No swing adjustment is performed. The actual swing adjustment settings are used. As soon as primary sets change, the mode is switched back to AUTO.

 |
 |

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › ASWM  ASWM  -  Auto SWing Mode）

```
ASWM SET,AUTO
```

This example sets the swing adjustment mode AUTO.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › FXDL  FXDL  -  FiXture DeLay）

|

channel

 |

The test system channel number of the digital channel. This is a five digit field. See `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for the number. You can type ALL to set the attributes for all installed channels. For the query, you can type CFG to query only configured channels.

 |
 |

fixture_delay

 |

The fixture_delay represents the delay (in ns) of the lines on the DUT board. The range of the admissible values depends on the test system type as follows:

- PS1600: Between -0.015 and +26.4 ns

The default value is 0. The maximum number of digits after the decimal point is 3.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › FXDL  FXDL  -  FiXture DeLay）

```
FXDL 10101,2.5
```

This example sets the fixture delay of channel 10101 to 2.5 ns.

### Parameters（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › PADS  PADS  -  Pin Attributes Definition String）

|

mode

 |

Currently not used.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

Edge delay definition string which consists of delay adjustments for up to all available edges. The valid range (in ns) is from -8 to 8.

All edges which are not explicitly set are not changed but stay at the same value as before.

 |
 |

drv_adj

 |

The driver adjustment contains the sum of any additional driver offset delays that you want to include. The delay (in ns) must be between -5 and +5 and contain a maximum of three digits after the decimal point. The default value is 0.

 |
 |

rec_adj

 |

The receiver adjustment contains the sum of any additional receiver offset delays that you want to include. The delay (in ns) must be between -5 and +5 and contain a maximum of three digits after the decimal point. The default value is 0.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pinlist must include all pins to which the given attributes apply. If more than one pin is to be entered, the names must be separated with a comma. All pins in pinlist must be I, O, or IO pin types.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › PADS  PADS  -  Pin Attributes Definition String）

```
> PADS ,"d1:0.1 d2:0.2 d3:0.3 d4:0.1 d5:0.2 d6:0.3 d7:0.1 d8:0.2",2,,(clk)

> PADS? ,(@)
< PADS ,"d1:0.1 d2:0.2 d3:0.3 d4:0.1 r1:0.1 r2:0.2 r3:0.3 r4:0.1",,-1,(io)
< PADS ,"d1:0.1 d2:0.2 d3:0.3 d4:0.1 d5:0.2 d6:0.3 d7:0.1 d8:0.2",2,,(clk)
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › PTDS  PTDS  -  Pin attributes Tweaking Definition String）

|

channelNo

 |

This is a five digit field which defines the channel to which the pin is connected. See also the command `DFPN, DFPN? - (DeFine Pin Name)`（raw: `02.06.02.02.63_DFPN__DFPN__-__DeFine_Pin_Name.md`） for this parameter.

 |
 |

You can also enter:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Sets, or returns information on, all channels.

 |
 |

EBT_specifier

 |

The Equation Based Timing specifier can be:

 |
 |

eqn_set

 |

Equation Set number in the range of 1 to 256.

 |
 |

0

 |

Causes the next parameter (set_specifier) to be interpreted as waveform_set instead of spec_set.

 |
 |

If you specify the name of a multi-port specification for the set_specifier parameter, the EBT_specifier parameter will be ignored.

You can also enter:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Sets delay for, or returns information on, all Equation Sets.

 |
 |

set_specifier

 |

Possible values are:

 |
 |

1 to 256

 |

The number is interpreted as a waveform set number if EBT_specifier is set to 0. Otherwise, it is taken as a specset number.

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

In a multiport setup, you can specify the name of a multi-port specification in double quotes. In this case, the EBT_specifier parameter will be ignored. The pin attributes will be associated with the specified timing set (timing_set parameter) in every port of the specification.

 |
 |

You can also enter:

 |
 |

ALL

 |

Sets delay for, or returns information on, all Spec Sets or Waveform Sets.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing Set number in the range of 1 to 256. You can also enter ALL to select information on all timing sets.

Note that ALL is the only allowed option if EBT_specifier or set_specifier is also set to ALL.

 |
 |

tweaking_set

 |

Tweaking Set number. Currently not used.

 |
 |

mode

 |

Currently not used.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

Definition string for the logical edges.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › PTDS  PTDS  -  Pin attributes Tweaking Definition String）

```
PTDS 10812,0,4,5,,1,1,"d1:2,d2:0.003, d8:5, r1:-1, r2:-2"
PTDS? 10101,,all,all,,
```

The following example defines pin attributes for timing sets of the multi-port specification spec_port_1_port_2.

```
> PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",1,,,"d1:1 d3:3"
> PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",2,,,"d1:2 d2:3"
> PTDS? 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",ALL,,
< PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",1,,,"d1:1 d3:3"
< PTDS 10101,,"spec_port_1_port_2",2,,,"d1:2 d2:3"
```

### Parameters（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › SATR  SATR  -  System ATtRibutes）

|

comm_rec_delay

 |

The common receiver delay represents the adjustment to the round-trip delay between the drivers and receivers. The delay is in [ns] and must be in the range -50 to +50. Three digits are allowed after the decimal point. The default value is 0.

 |

### Example（取自子主题 Calibration and Attributes Commands › List of calibration and attributes commands › SATR  SATR  -  System ATtRibutes）

```
SATR 20
```

This example sets the common receiver delay to 20 ns.

## 是什么

**这一页是「firmware 命令」的总入口。**
它自己不定义任何命令——**它做两件事**：分流（该不该用 firmware 命令）
和分门别类（18 个类别）。

### 一、先用什么、最后才用什么：一条明确的优先级

原文把这个放在最前面，是一段**排序建议**，不是一个「也可以」：

> 「Firmware commands are used for **low level control of the test system**. In general it is
> recommended to use instead
> - **SmartRDI**
> - **Testmethod API**
> when possible, **and in that order**, and **only work with firmware commands if none of these
> meets your need**.」

**顺序是有意义的**，`and in that order` 明说了：

| 优先级 | 用什么 |
|---|---|
| 1 | **[[smartrdi]]** |
| 2 | **Testmethod API** |
| 3 | **firmware 命令**（前两个都满足不了时） |

**所以本页的定位是「退路」，不是起点。**

### 二、什么情况下退路是必须的：pin 特定的测试结果

原文给了一个**具体的例子**，而这条例子恰好是本页存在的理由：

> 「Examples for when firmware commands can be necessary are **queries** like
> **`CHFA?` - (CHannel FAil flag)** or **`CHER?` - (CHeck ERrors)** which can be used to
> **get pin specific test results**.」

**两个特征值得注意：**

| 特征 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **是 `?` 结尾的查询** | `CHFA?` / `CHER?` ——**`?` 表示这是问句，不是设置** |
| **拿的是 pin 特定的结果** | `pin specific test results` ——**这正是前两级覆盖不到的地方** |

> **括号里的展开读法**：`CHFA?` = `CHannel FAil flag`，`CHER?` = `CHeck ERrors`。
> **原文用「大写字母组词」的方式解释缩写**——这是本语料里解释命令名的固定写法。

### 三、⚠️ 全页最要紧的一条限制：只看当前 focus 的那个 site

> 「**Any firmware queries report setup and results for the site currently in focus only.**」

**只说了一遍、只有一行，但它是本页的边界条件。**

**这条限制的后果**（本页按它的字面意思列出，**（推断）**部分已标注）：

- **multiport / multisite 下，一次查询只回答一个 site 的情况**——想拿全部 site 的结果，
  **得自己逐个 site 换 focus 再查**（**（推断）**：「只看 focus」的字面推论，
  **原文没有明说怎么遍历**）。
- **它和 [[site-focus-required-before-command]] 是同一件事的两面**：
  那一页讲「某条命令要求先聚焦 site」（**约束侧**），
  本页讲「查询只报当前聚焦 site 的结果」（**行为侧**）。
- **`Any` 和 `queries` 两个词的范围**：原文写的是 **`Any firmware queries`**——
  **限定在「查询」这一类**。**设置类的命令是否也受这条限制，原文没说。**

### 四、18 个类别

原文的 `Subtopics` 就是它的目录，**18 个类别**。本页按原文顺序列，**每类的具体命令本页都没读**：

| # | 类别 | 本页对它的了解 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Introduction to firmware commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 2 | `Commands in alphabetical order` | **只知道标题**（**按字母序的总清单**） |
| 3 | `Pin configuration setup commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 4 | `Routing Setup Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 5 | `Level Setup Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 6 | `Timing Setup Commands` | **只知道标题**（[[timing-setup-commands]] 是它在 wiki 里的页） |
| 7 | `Vector Setup Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 8 | `Relays and Control Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 9 | `AC Testing Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 10 | `DC Measurement Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 11 | `Test Result Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 12 | `Utility Line Commands` | **只知道标题** |
| 13 | `Commands for the TMU per pin` | **只知道标题** |
| 14 | `Commands for Processing Results of Source Synchronous Testing` | **只知道标题** |
| 15 | `Commands for the protocol engine per pin` | **只知道标题** |
| 16 | `Commands for jitter injection` | **只知道标题** |
| 17 | `Commands for PRBS per pin tests and loopback tests` | **只知道标题** |
| 18 | `Calibration and Attributes Commands` | **只知道标题** |

**这张清单本身有一个结构信息**：**第 3–12 类是按「测试资源/阶段」分的**
（pin 配置、routing、level、timing、vector、relay、AC、DC、结果、utility line），
**第 13–18 类是按「特殊硬件能力」分的**（TMU、source synchronous、protocol engine、
jitter、PRBS、calibration）。**（推断）**：依据是两组标题的命名方式不同，
**原文没有把这层分组说出来。**

### 五、语法节：**63,000 行，本 wiki 里最大的一页**

`## 语法 / 参数` 一节有 **63,395 行**——因为脚本沿 `Subtopics` 往下抽，
把 18 个类别里的命令语法和例子**逐字**抄了进来。

**这一页的读法**：

- **散文这一节（就是你现在读的）只讲「该不该用、分几类」**；
- **真正的命令表和参数在脚本那一节**，**逐字来自 18 篇本页没读的子主题**；
- **要找某条命令，用 `Commands in alphabetical order` 那一支的字母序**
  （第 2 类），而不是从头翻。

## 典型用法

**原文这篇没有 `## Procedure` / `## Before you begin` / `## What to do next`**，
也没有任何步骤。**本页按原文能支撑的内容列三条：**

**1. 该不该用 firmware 命令（原文唯一一条决策建议）**：

```
要用某个能力
  ├─ SmartRDI 能做吗？      → 能就用它
  ├─ Testmethod API 能做吗？ → 能就用它
  └─ 都不行？               → 才用 firmware 命令
```

**2. 什么时候会走到第 3 步**：原文给的例子是**要拿 pin 特定的测试结果**时的查询
（`CHFA?`、`CHER?`）。

**3. 用查询前必须先确认一件事**：**当前 focus 的 site 是不是你要问的那个 site**
——因为 `Any firmware queries report setup and results for the site currently in focus only`。
**multisite 下这一条决定了你要不要先换 focus。**

## 和谁有关

- [[smartrdi]] — **原文推荐的第一顺位**：能用它就别用 firmware 命令
- [[testmethod]] — **原文推荐的第二顺位**（Testmethod API）；
  **注意原文用的是 `Testmethod API`，而第三顺位才是 firmware 命令**
- [[pin]] — **本页唯一给了例子的场景是「pin 特定的测试结果」**

  那页讲「命令要求先聚焦」，本页讲「查询只报聚焦的那个」
- [[timing-setup-commands]] — **18 类里第 6 类的 wiki 页**；本页是它的父页
- [[flag]] / [[alphabetical-list-of-flags]] — **firmware 命令和 flag 是两套不同的东西**；

- `Introduction to firmware commands` / `Commands in alphabetical order` /
  `Pin configuration setup commands` / `Routing Setup Commands` / `Level Setup Commands` /
  `Vector Setup Commands` / `Relays and Control Commands` / `AC Testing Commands` /

  （**均未建**）— **本页 `Subtopics` 的 18 篇，本页一篇没读**；
